Where the names meet

Kāmeśa (28, 30, 39) is kāma + īśa joined by guṇa; the name cannot be hyphenated across the e.

The names

29 अनाकलितसादृश्यचिबुकश्रीविराजिता an-ākalita-sādṛśya-cibuka-śrī-virājitā

She who shines with the beauty of a chin for which no likeness can be conceived

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, karmadhāraya, bahuvrīhi and nañ-tatpuruṣa). (1) an-ākalita 'not conceived, never found' (nañ-tatpuruṣa; the negative na appears as an- before a vowel, a morphological replacement, Pāṇini 6.3.73–74). (2) anākalita-sādṛśya 'whose likeness has never been conceived' (bahuvrīhi), qualifying cibuka 'chin' (karmadhāraya). (3) …cibuka-śrī 'the beauty of that chin' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (4) The participle virājitā 'shining, made splendid' is the head and takes the beauty in the instrumental. Incomparability is not a separate word: it comes from 'whose likeness was never conceived'.

Analysis न आकलितम् अनाकलितम्; अनाकलितम् सादृश्यम् यस्य तत् अनाकलितसादृश्यम्; अनाकलितसादृश्यम् चिबुकम् अनाकलितसादृश्यचिबुकम्; अनाकलितसादृश्यचिबुकस्य श्रीः अनाकलितसादृश्यचिबुकश्रीः; तया विराजिता अनाकलितसादृश्यचिबुकश्रीविराजिता
na ākalitam anākalitam; anākalitam sādṛśyam yasya tat anākalitasādṛśyam; anākalitasādṛśyam cibukam anākalitasādṛśyacibukam; anākalitasādṛśyacibukasya śrīḥ anākalitasādṛśyacibukaśrīḥ; tayā virājitā anākalitasādṛśyacibukaśrīvirājitā

Significance Saundaryalaharī 67 ends its verse on the chin by asking how it can be described, since it has no comparison (aupamya-rahita); here too the poet finds nothing to set beside it.

30 कामेशबद्धमाङ्गल्यसूत्रशोभितकन्धरा kāmeśa-baddha-māṅgalya-sūtra-śobhita-kandharā

She whose neck is adorned with the marriage thread tied by Kāmeśa

Sandhi कामेश = काम + ईश (kāma + īśa) — guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ), inside the lexicalised name Kāmeśa

Compound bahuvrīhi (over inner tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣas and karmadhārayas). (1) kāmeśa-baddha 'tied by Kāmeśa' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa: agent in the instrumental with a past participle). (2) māṅgalya-sūtra 'the auspicious thread', the marriage thread (karmadhāraya), qualified by (1). (3) śobhitā 'adorned' takes that thread in the instrumental (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (4) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose neck is adorned with …'; śobhitā takes its masculine stem inside the bahuvrīhi (puṃvadbhāva), and kandharā 'neck' ends the name.

Analysis कामेशेन बद्धम् कामेशबद्धम्; माङ्गल्यम् सूत्रम् माङ्गल्यसूत्रम्; कामेशबद्धम् माङ्गल्यसूत्रम् कामेशबद्धमाङ्गल्यसूत्रम्; कामेशबद्धमाङ्गल्यसूत्रेण शोभिता कामेशबद्धमाङ्गल्यसूत्रशोभिता; कामेशबद्धमाङ्गल्यसूत्रशोभिता कन्धरा यस्याः सा कामेशबद्धमाङ्गल्यसूत्रशोभितकन्धरा
kāmeśena baddham kāmeśabaddham; māṅgalyam sūtram māṅgalyasūtram; kāmeśabaddham māṅgalyasūtram kāmeśabaddhamāṅgalyasūtram; kāmeśabaddhamāṅgalyasūtreṇa śobhitā kāmeśabaddhamāṅgalyasūtraśobhitā; kāmeśabaddhamāṅgalyasūtraśobhitā kandharā yasyāḥ sā kāmeśabaddhamāṅgalyasūtraśobhitakandharā

Significance The māṅgalyasūtra is the emblem of the wedded wife. Traditionally it marks the eternal union of Kāmeśvara and Kāmeśvarī, Śiva and Śakti, who are never apart.

Śloka 13names 31–32

कनकाङ्गदकेयूरकमनीयभुजान्विता ।
रत्नग्रैवेयचिन्ताकलोलमुक्ताफलान्विता ॥ १३ ॥

kanakāṅgadakeyūrakamanīyabhujānvitā |
ratnagraiveyacintākalolamuktāphalānvitā || 13 ||

Where the names meet

Name 32: divide muktāphala-anvitā; phala belongs to muktāphala 'pearl', and anvitā 'endowed with' governs all three ornaments.

The names

31 कनकाङ्गदकेयूरकमनीयभुजान्विता kanakāṅgada-keyūra-kamanīya-bhujānvitā

She who is endowed with arms made lovely by golden armlets (aṅgada and keyūra)

Sandhi कनकाङ्गद = कनक + अङ्गद (kanaka + aṅgada) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); भुजान्विता = भुज + अन्विता (bhuja + anvitā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); अन्विता = अनु + इता (anu + itā) — yaṇ: u becomes v before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci), at the junction of the prefix anu with ita

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over inner karmadhārayas, a tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa and a dvandva). (1) aṅgada and keyūra, two kinds of upper-arm ornament, form a dvandva. (2) kanaka 'gold' qualifies them with the middle word 'made of' understood (karmadhāraya). Since aṅgada stands next to kanaka, one may also take kanaka with aṅgada alone ('golden aṅgadas and keyūras'); the sense is the same. (3) kamanīya 'lovely' takes the ornaments in the instrumental (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa) and (4) qualifies bhuja 'arm' (karmadhāraya). (5) The participle anvitā 'endowed with' is the head and takes the arms in the instrumental.

Analysis अङ्गदानि च केयूराणि च अङ्गदकेयूराणि; कनकमयानि अङ्गदकेयूराणि कनकाङ्गदकेयूराणि; कनकाङ्गदकेयूरैः कमनीयाः कनकाङ्गदकेयूरकमनीयाः; कनकाङ्गदकेयूरकमनीयाः भुजाः कनकाङ्गदकेयूरकमनीयभुजाः; तैः अन्विता कनकाङ्गदकेयूरकमनीयभुजान्विता
aṅgadāni ca keyūrāṇi ca aṅgadakeyūrāṇi; kanakamayāni aṅgadakeyūrāṇi kanakāṅgadakeyūrāṇi; kanakāṅgadakeyūraiḥ kamanīyāḥ kanakāṅgadakeyūrakamanīyāḥ; kanakāṅgadakeyūrakamanīyāḥ bhujāḥ kanakāṅgadakeyūrakamanīyabhujāḥ; taiḥ anvitā kanakāṅgadakeyūrakamanīyabhujānvitā

Significance Part of the head-to-foot description of Her form; the arms that hold the four emblems (names 8–11) are adorned with gold.

32 रत्नग्रैवेयचिन्ताकलोलमुक्ताफलान्विता ratna-graiveya-cintāka-lola-muktāphalānvitā

She who is adorned with a jewelled necklace, a cintāka and swaying pearls

Sandhi मुक्ताफलान्विता = मुक्ताफल + अन्विता (muktāphala + anvitā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); अन्विता = अनु + इता (anu + itā) — yaṇ: u becomes v before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci), at the junction of the prefix anu with ita

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an itaretara-dvandva of three members, with inner karmadhārayas). (1) ratna-graiveya 'a necklace set with gems' (karmadhāraya with the middle word 'set with' dropped). (2) lola-muktāphala 'swaying pearls' (karmadhāraya). (3) These and cintāka, a neck ornament, are joined as an itaretara-dvandva: 'the jewelled necklace, the cintāka and the swaying pearls'. (4) The participle anvitā 'endowed with, wearing' is the head and takes them in the instrumental. muktāphala 'pearl' is one word (lit. 'pearl-fruit'); its phala belongs to it, not to anvitā.

Analysis रत्नखचितम् ग्रैवेयम् रत्नग्रैवेयम्; लोलानि मुक्ताफलानि लोलमुक्ताफलानि; रत्नग्रैवेयम् च चिन्ताकम् च लोलमुक्ताफलानि च रत्नग्रैवेयचिन्ताकलोलमुक्ताफलानि; तैः अन्विता रत्नग्रैवेयचिन्ताकलोलमुक्ताफलान्विता
ratnakhacitam graiveyam ratnagraiveyam; lolāni muktāphalāni lolamuktāphalāni; ratnagraiveyam ca cintākam ca lolamuktāphalāni ca ratnagraiveyacintākalolamuktāphalāni; taiḥ anvitā ratnagraiveyacintākalolamuktāphalānvitā

Significance Another stage of the description of Her form, at the neck and breast; the ornaments of the Goddess are part of Her worship (bhūṣaṇa), offered to Her in pūjā.

Uncertain The exact form of the cintāka is not certain: it is taken as a gold collar-necklace or as the pendant (locket) of the jewelled necklace. On the second reading the analysis is 'the jewelled necklace with its pendant, and swaying pearls'.

Where the names meet

Name 34 begins nābhi + ālavāla (yaṇ); its metaphor of basin, creeper and fruit continues into name 35.

The names

33 कामेश्वरप्रेमरत्नमणिप्रतिपणस्तनी kāmeśvara-prema-ratna-maṇi-pratipaṇa-stanī

She whose breasts are what She gives in return for the precious gem of Kāmeśvara's love

Sandhi कामेश्वर = काम + ईश्वर (kāma + īśvara) — guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ), inside the lexicalised name Kāmeśvara

Compound bahuvrīhi (over inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas and karmadhārayas). (1) kāmeśvara-prema 'Kāmeśvara's love' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) ratna-maṇi 'a precious gem' (karmadhāraya of two words for jewel), and (1) is identified with it: 'the precious gem that is Kāmeśvara's love' (rūpaka karmadhāraya). (3) …maṇi-pratipaṇa 'the counter-price for that gem', what is given in exchange for it (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (4) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose breasts are the counter-price …'. stana 'breast', a body-part word ending the bahuvrīhi, takes the feminine ī (Pāṇini 4.1.54): -stanī.

Analysis कामेश्वरस्य प्रेम कामेश्वरप्रेम; रत्नम् मणिः रत्नमणिः; कामेश्वरप्रेम एव रत्नमणिः कामेश्वरप्रेमरत्नमणिः; कामेश्वरप्रेमरत्नमणेः प्रतिपणौ कामेश्वरप्रेमरत्नमणिप्रतिपणौ; कामेश्वरप्रेमरत्नमणिप्रतिपणौ स्तनौ यस्याः सा कामेश्वरप्रेमरत्नमणिप्रतिपणस्तनी
kāmeśvarasya prema kāmeśvaraprema; ratnam maṇiḥ ratnamaṇiḥ; kāmeśvaraprema eva ratnamaṇiḥ kāmeśvarapremaratnamaṇiḥ; kāmeśvarapremaratnamaṇeḥ pratipaṇau kāmeśvarapremaratnamaṇipratipaṇau; kāmeśvarapremaratnamaṇipratipaṇau stanau yasyāḥ sā kāmeśvarapremaratnamaṇipratipaṇastanī

Significance Traditionally read as the perfect reciprocity of Śiva and Śakti: He gives His love, and She gives in return the nourishing fullness from which the worlds are sustained.

34 नाभ्यालवालरोमालिलताफलकुचद्वयी nābhyālavāla-romāli-latā-phala-kuca-dvayī

She whose two breasts are the fruits of the creeper of fine hair that rises from the basin of Her navel

Sandhi नाभ्यालवाल = नाभि + आलवाल (nābhi + ālavāla) — yaṇ: i becomes y before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci); रोमालि = रोम + आलि (roma + āli) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over inner rūpaka-karmadhārayas, a saptamī-tatpuruṣa and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). A sustained metaphor. (1) nābhi-ālavāla 'the navel as the water-basin at the foot of a plant' (rūpaka karmadhāraya). (2) roma-āli 'the line of fine hair' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa), itself (3) the creeper, latā (rūpaka). (4) The creeper is rooted in the navel-basin (saptamī-tatpuruṣa). (5) …latā-phala 'its fruit' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (6) kuca-dvayī 'the pair of breasts' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (7) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose pair of breasts is the fruit of the hair-line creeper that grows from the navel-basin'.

Analysis नाभिः एव आलवालम् नाभ्यालवालम्; रोम्णाम् आलिः रोमालिः; रोमालिः एव लता रोमालिलता; नाभ्यालवाले रोमालिलता नाभ्यालवालरोमालिलता; नाभ्यालवालरोमालिलतायाः फलम् नाभ्यालवालरोमालिलताफलम्; कुचयोः द्वयी कुचद्वयी; नाभ्यालवालरोमालिलताफलम् कुचद्वयी यस्याः सा नाभ्यालवालरोमालिलताफलकुचद्वयी
nābhiḥ eva ālavālam nābhyālavālam; romṇām āliḥ romāliḥ; romāliḥ eva latā romālilatā; nābhyālavāle romālilatā nābhyālavālaromālilatā; nābhyālavālaromālilatāyāḥ phalam nābhyālavālaromālilatāphalam; kucayoḥ dvayī kucadvayī; nābhyālavālaromālilatāphalam kucadvayī yasyāḥ sā nābhyālavālaromālilatāphalakucadvayī

Significance A classical figure of Sanskrit poetry, carried through every member: the navel is the basin that waters the plant, the fine line of hair the creeper rising from it, and the breasts its fruit.

Where the names meet

Name 35: divide latā + ādhāratā 'being the support', not latā + dhāratā; the ā of ādhāratā is fused with latā. Name 36: dalan- is the participle dalat, its t nasalised before madhya.

The names

35 लक्ष्यरोमलताधारतासमुन्नेयमध्यमा lakṣya-roma-latādhāratā-samunneya-madhyamā

She whose waist can be known only by inference, from its being the support of the visible creeper of fine hair

Sandhi लताधारता = लता + आधारता (latā + ādhāratā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); the second member is ādhāratā 'being the support', not dhāratā — the fused ā hides the boundary; उन्नेय = उद् + नेय (ud + neya) — nasal assimilation: the d of the prefix ud becomes n before the nasal n (Pāṇini 8.4.45 yaro 'nunāsike 'nunāsiko vā)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa, ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas and a karmadhāraya). (1) roma-latā 'the creeper of fine hair' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, with the creeper metaphor of name 34), qualified by lakṣya 'visible' (karmadhāraya; lakṣyā takes its masculine stem, Pāṇini 6.3.42). (2) …latā-ādhāratā 'the fact of being the support of that creeper' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; ādhāra + the abstract suffix -tā). (3) samunneya 'to be inferred' takes that fact in the instrumental, as the ground of the inference (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (4) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose waist (madhyama) is to be inferred from its being the support of the visible hair-creeper'.

Analysis रोम्णाम् लता रोमलता; लक्ष्या रोमलता लक्ष्यरोमलता; लक्ष्यरोमलतायाः आधारता लक्ष्यरोमलताधारता; लक्ष्यरोमलताधारतया समुन्नेयम् लक्ष्यरोमलताधारतासमुन्नेयम्; लक्ष्यरोमलताधारतासमुन्नेयम् मध्यमम् यस्याः सा लक्ष्यरोमलताधारतासमुन्नेयमध्यमा
romṇām latā romalatā; lakṣyā romalatā lakṣyaromalatā; lakṣyaromalatāyāḥ ādhāratā lakṣyaromalatādhāratā; lakṣyaromalatādhāratayā samunneyam lakṣyaromalatādhāratāsamunneyam; lakṣyaromalatādhāratāsamunneyam madhyamam yasyāḥ sā lakṣyaromalatādhāratāsamunneyamadhyamā

Significance Her waist is so slender that it is not seen; it is inferred because the visible line of hair must rest on something. Traditionally this is compared to the Supreme, which is not perceived directly but known from the world it upholds.

36 स्तनभारदलन्मध्यपट्टबन्धवलित्रया stana-bhāra-dalan-madhya-paṭṭa-bandha-vali-trayā

She whose three folds of skin form a band that binds Her waist, as though it would break under the weight of Her breasts

Sandhi दलन्मध्य = दलत् + मध्य (dalat + madhya) — nasal assimilation: the final t of the participle dalat becomes n before the nasal m (Pāṇini 8.4.45 yaro 'nunāsike 'nunāsiko vā)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over inner tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa, karmadhārayas and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (1) stana-bhāra 'the weight of the breasts' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) The present participle dalat 'splitting, cracking' takes that weight in the instrumental (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa), and (3) qualifies madhya 'waist' (karmadhāraya): 'the waist that seems to crack under the weight'. (4) paṭṭa-bandha 'a binding band' for that waist (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (5) vali-traya 'the three folds' is identified with that band, the word 'in the form of' (rūpa) understood. (6) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose three folds are a binding band for Her waist …'; traya takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis स्तनयोः भारः स्तनभारः; स्तनभारेण दलत् स्तनभारदलत्; स्तनभारदलत् मध्यम् स्तनभारदलन्मध्यम्; पट्टस्य बन्धः पट्टबन्धः; स्तनभारदलन्मध्यस्य पट्टबन्धः स्तनभारदलन्मध्यपट्टबन्धः; वलीनाम् त्रयम् वलित्रयम्; स्तनभारदलन्मध्यपट्टबन्धरूपम् वलित्रयम् यस्याः सा स्तनभारदलन्मध्यपट्टबन्धवलित्रया
stanayoḥ bhāraḥ stanabhāraḥ; stanabhāreṇa dalat stanabhāradalat; stanabhāradalat madhyam stanabhāradalanmadhyam; paṭṭasya bandhaḥ paṭṭabandhaḥ; stanabhāradalanmadhyasya paṭṭabandhaḥ stanabhāradalanmadhyapaṭṭabandhaḥ; valīnām trayam valitrayam; stanabhāradalanmadhyapaṭṭabandharūpam valitrayam yasyāḥ sā stanabhāradalanmadhyapaṭṭabandhavalitrayā

Significance The trivalī, three folds across the midriff, is a classical mark of beauty; the poet imagines them as a band tied by nature round a waist too slender for its burden.

Where the names meet

Name 37: kausumbha is dyed with safflower (kusumbha), not saffron.

The names

37 अरुणारुणकौसुम्भवस्त्रभास्वत्कटीतटी aruṇāruṇa-kausumbha-vastra-bhāsvat-kaṭī-taṭī

She whose hips shine with a safflower-dyed garment as red as the dawn

Sandhi अरुणारुण = अरुण + अरुण (aruṇa + aruṇa) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over inner tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa, karmadhārayas and a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) aruṇa-aruṇa: 'red like Aruṇa, the dawn' (upamāna-karmadhāraya, the standard of comparison compounded with the shared quality). (2) It qualifies kausumbha-vastra 'a safflower-dyed garment' (karmadhāraya). (3) bhāsvat 'shining' takes the garment in the instrumental (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (4) kaṭī-taṭī 'the slope of the hips' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (5) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose hips shine with a safflower-dyed garment red as the dawn'; bhāsvatī takes its masculine stem bhāsvat (puṃvadbhāva).

Analysis अरुणः इव अरुणम् अरुणारुणम्; कौसुम्भम् वस्त्रम् कौसुम्भवस्त्रम्; अरुणारुणम् कौसुम्भवस्त्रम् अरुणारुणकौसुम्भवस्त्रम्; अरुणारुणकौसुम्भवस्त्रेण भास्वती अरुणारुणकौसुम्भवस्त्रभास्वती; कट्याः तटी कटीतटी; अरुणारुणकौसुम्भवस्त्रभास्वती कटीतटी यस्याः सा अरुणारुणकौसुम्भवस्त्रभास्वत्कटीतटी
aruṇaḥ iva aruṇam aruṇāruṇam; kausumbham vastram kausumbhavastram; aruṇāruṇam kausumbhavastram aruṇāruṇakausumbhavastram; aruṇāruṇakausumbhavastreṇa bhāsvatī aruṇāruṇakausumbhavastrabhāsvatī; kaṭyāḥ taṭī kaṭītaṭī; aruṇāruṇakausumbhavastrabhāsvatī kaṭītaṭī yasyāḥ sā aruṇāruṇakausumbhavastrabhāsvatkaṭītaṭī

Significance Red is Her color throughout the hymn; its dhyāna verses picture Her as aruṇā, red, and in red garlands, ornaments and garments (aruṇa-mālya-bhūṣāmbarām). Traditionally the red is read as compassion and the passion (rāga) of creative power.

Uncertain aruṇāruṇa may be read as 'red as the dawn' (upamāna, as analysed) or as the color word doubled for emphasis, 'deep red, red upon red'.

38 रत्नकिङ्किणिकारम्यरशनादामभूषिता ratna-kiṅkiṇikā-ramya-raśanā-dāma-bhūṣitā

She who is adorned with a girdle-chain made lovely by little jewelled bells

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over inner karmadhārayas, a tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa and a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) ratna-kiṅkiṇikā 'little bells made of gems' (karmadhāraya with 'made of' understood). (2) ramya 'lovely' takes them in the instrumental (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (3) raśanā-dāma 'the chain or string of the girdle' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa), qualified by (2) (karmadhāraya). (4) The participle bhūṣitā 'adorned' is the head and takes the girdle-chain in the instrumental.

Analysis रत्नमय्यः किङ्किणिकाः रत्नकिङ्किणिकाः; रत्नकिङ्किणिकाभिः रम्यम् रत्नकिङ्किणिकारम्यम्; रशनायाः दाम रशनादाम; रत्नकिङ्किणिकारम्यम् रशनादाम रत्नकिङ्किणिकारम्यरशनादाम; तेन भूषिता रत्नकिङ्किणिकारम्यरशनादामभूषिता
ratnamayyaḥ kiṅkiṇikāḥ ratnakiṅkiṇikāḥ; ratnakiṅkiṇikābhiḥ ramyam ratnakiṅkiṇikāramyam; raśanāyāḥ dāma raśanādāma; ratnakiṅkiṇikāramyam raśanādāma ratnakiṅkiṇikāramyaraśanādāma; tena bhūṣitā ratnakiṅkiṇikāramyaraśanādāmabhūṣitā

Significance The girdle with small bells (kiṅkiṇī) is a classical ornament of the hips; its sound is part of the poetic picture of Her presence.

कामेशज्ञातसौभाग्यमार्दवोरुद्वयान्विता ।

Where the names meet

Name 39: mārdavoru is mārdava + ūru 'thigh'. Name 40: many editions spell makuṭa, a by-form of mukuṭa 'crown'.

The names

39 कामेशज्ञातसौभाग्यमार्दवोरुद्वयान्विता kāmeśa-jñāta-saubhāgya-mārdavoru-dvayānvitā

She whose two thighs, in their beauty and softness, are known to Kāmeśa alone

Sandhi कामेश = काम + ईश (kāma + īśa) — guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ), inside the lexicalised name Kāmeśa; मार्दवोरु = मार्दव + ऊरु (mārdava + ūru) — guṇa: a + ū → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ); द्वयान्विता = द्वय + अन्विता (dvaya + anvitā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); अन्विता = अनु + इता (anu + itā) — yaṇ: u becomes v before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci), at the junction of the prefix anu with ita

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over inner bahuvrīhi, dvandva, tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa, karmadhāraya and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) saubhāgya-mārdava 'beauty and softness' (dvandva). (2) kāmeśa-jñāta 'known by Kāmeśa' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa) qualifies them. (3) Together they form a bahuvrīhi describing the thighs: 'whose beauty and softness are known to Kāmeśa', qualifying ūru 'thigh' (karmadhāraya). (4) …ūru-dvaya 'the pair of such thighs' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (5) anvitā 'endowed with' is the head and takes the pair in the instrumental. 'Only' is not a word in the name; it is the traditional sense of 'known by Kāmeśa'.

Analysis सौभाग्यम् च मार्दवम् च सौभाग्यमार्दवे; कामेशेन ज्ञाते कामेशज्ञाते; कामेशज्ञाते सौभाग्यमार्दवे ययोः तौ कामेशज्ञातसौभाग्यमार्दवौ; कामेशज्ञातसौभाग्यमार्दवौ ऊरू कामेशज्ञातसौभाग्यमार्दवोरू; तयोः द्वयम् कामेशज्ञातसौभाग्यमार्दवोरुद्वयम्; तेन अन्विता कामेशज्ञातसौभाग्यमार्दवोरुद्वयान्विता
saubhāgyam ca mārdavam ca saubhāgyamārdave; kāmeśena jñāte kāmeśajñāte; kāmeśajñāte saubhāgyamārdave yayoḥ tau kāmeśajñātasaubhāgyamārdavau; kāmeśajñātasaubhāgyamārdavau ūrū kāmeśajñātasaubhāgyamārdavorū; tayoḥ dvayam kāmeśajñātasaubhāgyamārdavorudvayam; tena anvitā kāmeśajñātasaubhāgyamārdavorudvayānvitā

Significance Traditionally read as the intimacy of Śiva and Śakti: what She is in full is known only to Kāmeśvara, who is Her own Self.

40 माणिक्यमुकुटाकारजानुद्वयविराजिता māṇikya-mukuṭākāra-jānu-dvaya-virājitā

She who shines with two knees shaped like crowns of ruby

Sandhi मुकुटाकार = मुकुट + आकार (mukuṭa + ākāra) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya, a bahuvrīhi of resemblance and a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) māṇikya-mukuṭa 'a crown of ruby' (karmadhāraya with 'made of' understood). (2) …mukuṭa-ākāra 'having the shape of such a crown' (bahuvrīhi of resemblance, as in name 25). (3) It qualifies jānu-dvaya 'the pair of knees' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa inside; karmadhāraya). (4) virājitā 'shining' is the head and takes the knees in the instrumental.

Analysis माणिक्यमयः मुकुटः माणिक्यमुकुटः; माणिक्यमुकुटस्य आकारः इव आकारः यस्य तत् माणिक्यमुकुटाकारम्; जान्वोः द्वयम् जानुद्वयम्; माणिक्यमुकुटाकारम् जानुद्वयम् माणिक्यमुकुटाकारजानुद्वयम्; तेन विराजिता माणिक्यमुकुटाकारजानुद्वयविराजिता
māṇikyamayaḥ mukuṭaḥ māṇikyamukuṭaḥ; māṇikyamukuṭasya ākāraḥ iva ākāraḥ yasya tat māṇikyamukuṭākāram; jānvoḥ dvayam jānudvayam; māṇikyamukuṭākāram jānudvayam māṇikyamukuṭākārajānudvayam; tena virājitā māṇikyamukuṭākārajānudvayavirājitā

Significance The rounded, glowing kneecaps are likened to small domed crowns of ruby; the red of the ruby again answers to Her color.

Variants Many printed editions read माणिक्यमकुटाकार (makuṭa). makuṭa is a recognized by-form of mukuṭa 'crown' in the lexicons, so that reading is a variant spelling rather than a misprint; the sense is the same.

Corrected माणिक्यमकुटाकारजानुद्वयविराजिता → माणिक्यमुकुटाकारजानुद्वयविराजिता. Name list read मकुट (makuṭa), the śloka text मुकुट (mukuṭa). Both are recognised spellings of the word for crown; the śloka text's reading is adopted so name and śloka agree.

Where the names meet

Name 41: indragopa is one word, a scarlet insect (not Indra + 'beetle'). The second half holds two names: gūḍhagulphā (42) | kūrmapṛṣṭha… (43).

The names

41 इन्द्रगोपपरिक्षिप्तस्मरतूणाभजङ्घिका indragopa-parikṣipta-smara-tūṇābha-jaṅghikā

She whose calves resemble the quiver of Kāma, studded all around with scarlet indragopas

Sandhi तूणाभ = तूण + आभ (tūṇa + ābha) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner bahuvrīhi of resemblance, a karmadhāraya, a tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa and a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) indragopa-parikṣipta 'set all around with indragopas' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (2) smara-tūṇa 'the quiver of Smara (Kāma)' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa), qualified by (1) (karmadhāraya). (3) …tūṇa-ābha 'having the look of that quiver' (bahuvrīhi of resemblance). (4) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose calves (jaṅghikā) look like Kāma's quiver set around with indragopas'. The tapering, rounded calf is the quiver.

Analysis इन्द्रगोपैः परिक्षिप्तः इन्द्रगोपपरिक्षिप्तः; स्मरस्य तूणः स्मरतूणः; इन्द्रगोपपरिक्षिप्तः स्मरतूणः इन्द्रगोपपरिक्षिप्तस्मरतूणः; इन्द्रगोपपरिक्षिप्तस्मरतूणस्य आभा इव आभा ययोः ते इन्द्रगोपपरिक्षिप्तस्मरतूणाभे; इन्द्रगोपपरिक्षिप्तस्मरतूणाभे जङ्घिके यस्याः सा इन्द्रगोपपरिक्षिप्तस्मरतूणाभजङ्घिका
indragopaiḥ parikṣiptaḥ indragopaparikṣiptaḥ; smarasya tūṇaḥ smaratūṇaḥ; indragopaparikṣiptaḥ smaratūṇaḥ indragopaparikṣiptasmaratūṇaḥ; indragopaparikṣiptasmaratūṇasya ābhā iva ābhā yayoḥ te indragopaparikṣiptasmaratūṇābhe; indragopaparikṣiptasmaratūṇābhe jaṅghike yasyāḥ sā indragopaparikṣiptasmaratūṇābhajaṅghikā

Significance The comparison is to Kāma's quiver, which holds the flower-arrows; in this hymn those arrows are Her own (name 11). The scarlet indragopas, like the ruby knees of name 40, keep the description in Her color, red.

Uncertain Translators take indragopa here either as the scarlet insects themselves, scattered over the quiver, or as red gems of their color set around it; the comparison of the calves to Kāma's quiver is not in doubt.

42 गूढगुल्फा gūḍha-gulphā

She whose ankles are hidden

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. gūḍha 'hidden' qualifies gulpha 'ankle'; the compound describes Her: 'She whose ankles are hidden'. gulpha takes the feminine -ā. The members are simply juxtaposed.

Analysis गूढौ गुल्फौ यस्याः सा गूढगुल्फा
gūḍhau gulphau yasyāḥ sā gūḍhagulphā

Significance Ankles that are full and rounded, with the bone not standing out, are a classical mark of beauty in the description of the body.

43 कूर्मपृष्ठजयिष्णुप्रपदान्विता kūrma-pṛṣṭha-jayiṣṇu-prapadānvitā

She whose insteps surpass the back of a tortoise in their smooth curve

Sandhi प्रपदान्विता = प्रपद + अन्विता (prapada + anvitā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); अन्विता = अनु + इता (anu + itā) — yaṇ: u becomes v before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci), at the junction of the prefix anu with ita

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya, a tatpuruṣa of object and agent-adjective, and a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) kūrma-pṛṣṭha 'the back of a tortoise' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) jayiṣṇu 'surpassing, victorious over' takes it as its object (a tatpuruṣa of object and agent-adjective). (3) It qualifies prapada 'instep, forefoot' (karmadhāraya). (4) The participle anvitā 'endowed with' is the head and takes the insteps in the instrumental.

Analysis कूर्मस्य पृष्ठम् कूर्मपृष्ठम्; कूर्मपृष्ठम् जयिष्णुनी कूर्मपृष्ठजयिष्णुनी; कूर्मपृष्ठजयिष्णुनी प्रपदे कूर्मपृष्ठजयिष्णुप्रपदे; ताभ्याम् अन्विता कूर्मपृष्ठजयिष्णुप्रपदान्विता
kūrmasya pṛṣṭham kūrmapṛṣṭham; kūrmapṛṣṭham jayiṣṇunī kūrmapṛṣṭhajayiṣṇunī; kūrmapṛṣṭhajayiṣṇunī prapade kūrmapṛṣṭhajayiṣṇuprapade; tābhyām anvitā kūrmapṛṣṭhajayiṣṇuprapadānvitā

Significance A high, smoothly arched instep, like a tortoise's shell, is a classical mark of beauty in the description of the feet.

Śloka 19names 44–45

नखदीधितिसञ्छन्ननमज्जनतमोगुणा ।
पदद्वयप्रभाजालपराकृतसरोरुहा ॥ १९ ॥

nakhadīdhitisañchannanamajjanatamoguṇā |
padadvayaprabhājālaparākṛtasaroruhā || 19 ||

44She the radiance of whose toenails overwhelms the darkness (tamoguṇa) of those who bow to Her;

45She whose two feet, by their mass of radiance, put the lotuses to shame.

Where the names meet

tamoguṇa (44) and saroruha (45) both show s → o: tamas + guṇa, saras + ruha.

The names

44 नखदीधितिसञ्छन्ननमज्जनतमोगुणा nakha-dīdhiti-sañchanna-namaj-jana-tamo-guṇā

She the radiance of whose toenails overwhelms the darkness (tamoguṇa) of those who bow to Her

Sandhi सञ्छन्न = सम् + छन्न (sam + channa) — the m of the prefix sam becomes anusvāra and then the palatal nasal ñ before ch (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ; 8.4.58 anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ); written here with ñ, elsewhere as saṃchanna; नमज्जन = नमत् + जन (namat + jana) — the final t of the participle namat is voiced to d (jaśtva, Pāṇini 8.2.39) and assimilated to the following palatal j (ścutva, Pāṇini 8.4.40 stoḥ ścunā ścuḥ); तमोगुण = तमस् + गुण (tamas + guṇa) — the final s becomes ru (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ), which turns to u after a before a voiced consonant (6.1.114 haśi ca); a + u then gives o by guṇa (6.1.87)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over inner tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa, karmadhārayas and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (1) nakha-dīdhiti 'the rays of the (toe)nails' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) sañchanna 'covered over, overwhelmed' takes the rays in the instrumental (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (3) namaj-jana 'people who bow' (karmadhāraya of participle and noun). (4) tamo-guṇa 'the guṇa tamas', darkness, inertia, ignorance (karmadhāraya), and …jana-tamoguṇa 'the tamas of those who bow' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (5) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She by the rays of whose toenails the tamas of those who bow is covered over', i.e. overwhelmed and dispelled by light; guṇa takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis नखानाम् दीधितयः नखदीधितयः; नखदीधितिभिः सञ्छन्नः नखदीधितिसञ्छन्नः; नमन्तः जनाः नमज्जनाः; तमः गुणः तमोगुणः; नमज्जनानाम् तमोगुणः नमज्जनतमोगुणः; नखदीधितिसञ्छन्नः नमज्जनतमोगुणः यस्याः सा नखदीधितिसञ्छन्ननमज्जनतमोगुणा
nakhānām dīdhitayaḥ nakhadīdhitayaḥ; nakhadīdhitibhiḥ sañchannaḥ nakhadīdhitisañchannaḥ; namantaḥ janāḥ namajjanāḥ; tamaḥ guṇaḥ tamoguṇaḥ; namajjanānām tamoguṇaḥ namajjanatamoguṇaḥ; nakhadīdhitisañchannaḥ namajjanatamoguṇaḥ yasyāḥ sā nakhadīdhitisañchannanamajjanatamoguṇā

Significance Those who bow touch Her feet with their heads, and the light of Her toenails falls on them. Traditionally this is the removal of ignorance through surrender at Her feet.

Corrected नखदीधितिसंछन्ननमज्जनतमोगुणा → नखदीधितिसञ्छन्ननमज्जनतमोगुणा. संछन्न → सञ्छन्न: anusvāra written as the homorganic nasal before छ, matching the verse text (both spellings are permitted; one form is used throughout).

45 पदद्वयप्रभाजालपराकृतसरोरुहा pada-dvaya-prabhā-jāla-parākṛta-saroruhā

She whose two feet, by their mass of radiance, put the lotuses to shame

Sandhi सरोरुह = सरस् + रुह (saras + ruha) — the final s becomes ru (Pāṇini 8.2.66), which turns to u after a before the voiced r (6.1.114 haśi ca); a + u gives o by guṇa (6.1.87), inside the lexicalised word saroruha 'lotus'

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (1) pada-dvaya 'the two feet', …dvaya-prabhā 'their radiance', …prabhā-jāla 'the mass (lit. net) of that radiance' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (2) The passive participle parākṛta 'defeated, set aside' takes it in the instrumental (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (3) It qualifies saroruha 'lotus' and the whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She by the radiance of whose two feet the lotuses are put to shame'; saroruha takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis पदयोः द्वयम् पदद्वयम्; पदद्वयस्य प्रभा पदद्वयप्रभा; पदद्वयप्रभायाः जालम् पदद्वयप्रभाजालम्; पदद्वयप्रभाजालेन पराकृतानि पदद्वयप्रभाजालपराकृतानि; पदद्वयप्रभाजालपराकृतानि सरोरुहाणि यस्याः सा पदद्वयप्रभाजालपराकृतसरोरुहा
padayoḥ dvayam padadvayam; padadvayasya prabhā padadvayaprabhā; padadvayaprabhāyāḥ jālam padadvayaprabhājālam; padadvayaprabhājālena parākṛtāni padadvayaprabhājālaparākṛtāni; padadvayaprabhājālaparākṛtāni saroruhāṇi yasyāḥ sā padadvayaprabhājālaparākṛtasaroruhā

Significance The lotus is the usual image for the feet of the deity; here the feet outshine the very flower they are compared to.

Śloka 20names 46–48

शिञ्जानमणिमञ्जीरमण्डितश्रीपदाम्बुजा ।

śiñjānamaṇimañjīramaṇḍitaśrīpadāmbujā |

Where the names meet

With name 46 the head-to-foot description begun at name 13 reaches the feet; 47–48 sum up Her gait and beauty. The second half holds two names: marālīmandagamanā (47) | mahālāvaṇyaśevadhiḥ (48), which keeps the masculine of its head śevadhi.

The names

46 शिञ्जानमणिमञ्जीरमण्डितश्रीपदाम्बुजा śiñjāna-maṇi-mañjīra-maṇḍita-śrī-padāmbujā

She whose auspicious lotus feet are adorned with tinkling jewelled anklets

Sandhi पदाम्बुज = पद + अम्बुज (pada + ambuja) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over inner karmadhārayas, a rūpaka and a tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (1) maṇi-mañjīra 'jewelled anklets' (karmadhāraya with 'made of' understood), qualified by the participle śiñjāna 'tinkling' (karmadhāraya). (2) maṇḍita 'adorned' takes the anklets in the instrumental (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (3) pada-ambuja 'the feet that are lotuses' (rūpaka karmadhāraya), with the honorific śrī 'auspicious, glorious'. (4) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose auspicious lotus-feet are adorned with tinkling jewelled anklets'; ambuja takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis मणिमयाः मञ्जीराः मणिमञ्जीराः; शिञ्जानाः मणिमञ्जीराः शिञ्जानमणिमञ्जीराः; शिञ्जानमणिमञ्जीरैः मण्डिते शिञ्जानमणिमञ्जीरमण्डिते; पदे एव अम्बुजे पदाम्बुजे; श्रीमती पदाम्बुजे श्रीपदाम्बुजे; शिञ्जानमणिमञ्जीरमण्डिते श्रीपदाम्बुजे यस्याः सा शिञ्जानमणिमञ्जीरमण्डितश्रीपदाम्बुजा
maṇimayāḥ mañjīrāḥ maṇimañjīrāḥ; śiñjānāḥ maṇimañjīrāḥ śiñjānamaṇimañjīrāḥ; śiñjānamaṇimañjīraiḥ maṇḍite śiñjānamaṇimañjīramaṇḍite; pade eva ambuje padāmbuje; śrīmatī padāmbuje śrīpadāmbuje; śiñjānamaṇimañjīramaṇḍite śrīpadāmbuje yasyāḥ sā śiñjānamaṇimañjīramaṇḍitaśrīpadāmbujā

Significance With the feet the description of Her form, begun with the hair at name 13, is complete. In Śrīvidyā Her feet (pādukā) are the highest object of worship and the refuge of the devotee.

Variants Some printings spell the participle with dental s: सिञ्जान (siñjāna). √śiñj is the Dhātupāṭha form; siñj is recorded in the lexicons as a by-spelling.

Corrected शिञ्जानमणिमञ्जिरमण्डितश्रीपदाम्बुजा → शिञ्जानमणिमञ्जीरमण्डितश्रीपदाम्बुजा. मञ्जिर → मञ्जीर (mañjīra, anklet: long ī). The verse text printed सिञ्जान; the name list's शिञ्जान is kept and now used in the verse too (√śiji, Dhātupāṭha "śiji avyakte śabde"). Flagged for review.

47 मरालीमन्दगमना marālī-manda-gamanā

She whose gait is as slow and gentle as that of a swan

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner upamāna-karmadhāraya). (1) marālī-manda 'slow like a female swan': the standard of comparison compounded with the shared quality (upamāna-karmadhāraya, as in name 15). (2) It qualifies gamana 'gait', and the whole is a bahuvrīhi describing Her; gamana takes the feminine -ā. The members are simply juxtaposed.

Analysis मराली इव मन्दम् मरालीमन्दम्; मरालीमन्दम् गमनम् यस्याः सा मरालीमन्दगमना
marālī iva mandam marālīmandam; marālīmandam gamanam yasyāḥ sā marālīmandagamanā

Significance The unhurried, gliding gait of the swan is the classical image of graceful, stately movement.

48 महालावण्यशेवधिः mahā-lāvaṇya-śevadhiḥ

She who is the treasure-house of supreme beauty

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (with an inner karmadhāraya). (1) mahā-lāvaṇya 'great beauty' (karmadhāraya; mahat becomes mahā- before a co-referential member, Pāṇini 6.3.46). (2) śevadhi 'treasure, treasury' is the head and the beauty stands to it in the genitive. As a tatpuruṣa it keeps the head's masculine gender (2.4.26), so the name ends -śevadhiḥ, not with a feminine ending, though it names the Goddess.

Analysis महत् लावण्यम् महालावण्यम्; महालावण्यस्य शेवधिः महालावण्यशेवधिः
mahat lāvaṇyam mahālāvaṇyam; mahālāvaṇyasya śevadhiḥ mahālāvaṇyaśevadhiḥ

Significance The name sums up the description of Her form that ends here: all beauty is stored in Her, and every lesser loveliness is drawn from that treasury.

सर्वsarvaall

Where the names meet

सर्वारुणाऽनवद्याङ्गी = सर्वारुणा + अनवद्याङ्गी (sarvāruṇā + anavadyāṅgī) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101); the avagraha ऽ (') marks the absorbed initial a of anavadyāṅgī

Read sarvāruṇā | anavadyāṅgī: the avagraha shows where the second name begins. Names 49–51 close the description of Her form; 52–54 name Her union with Kāmeśvara.

The names

49 सर्वारुणा sarvāruṇā

She who is red in every part

Sandhi सर्वारुणा = सर्व + अरुणा (sarva + aruṇā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound karmadhāraya (sarva 'whole, entire' qualifying aruṇā). sarva in the sense 'whole, in every part' qualifies aruṇā 'red'; aruṇā is the head and the compound describes Her: red throughout. sarvā takes its masculine stem sarva inside the karmadhāraya (puṃvadbhāva, Pāṇini 6.3.42).

Analysis सर्वा अरुणा सर्वारुणा
sarvā aruṇā sarvāruṇā

Significance Her body, garments, garlands and ornaments are all red, as the dhyāna verses picture Her (aruṇāṃ …; aruṇa-mālya-bhūṣāmbarām). In Śrīvidyā this red is read as vimarśa, the self-reflective power of consciousness, and as the color of compassion.

50 अनवद्याङ्गी an-avadyāṅgī

She whose every limb is faultless

Sandhi अवद्याङ्गी = अवद्य + अङ्गी (avadya + aṅgī) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner nañ-tatpuruṣa). (1) an-avadya 'not blameworthy, faultless' (nañ-tatpuruṣa; na appears as an- before a vowel, Pāṇini 6.3.73–74). (2) It qualifies aṅga 'limb', and the whole is a bahuvrīhi describing Her: 'She whose limbs are faultless'. aṅga, a body-part word ending the bahuvrīhi, takes the feminine ī (Pāṇini 4.1.54): -aṅgī.

Analysis न अवद्यम् अनवद्यम्; अनवद्यानि अङ्गानि यस्याः सा अनवद्याङ्गी
na avadyam anavadyam; anavadyāni aṅgāni yasyāḥ sā anavadyāṅgī

Significance No flaw can be found in any part of Her form; traditionally this is read also as freedom from every impurity, since Her body is pure consciousness.

51 सर्वाभरणभूषिता sarvābharaṇa-bhūṣitā

She who is adorned with all ornaments

Sandhi सर्वाभरण = सर्व + आभरण (sarva + ābharaṇa) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (with an inner karmadhāraya). (1) sarva-ābharaṇa 'all ornaments' (karmadhāraya). (2) The participle bhūṣitā 'adorned' is the head and takes the ornaments in the instrumental.

Analysis सर्वाणि आभरणानि सर्वाभरणानि; सर्वाभरणैः भूषिता सर्वाभरणभूषिता
sarvāṇi ābharaṇāni sarvābharaṇāni; sarvābharaṇaiḥ bhūṣitā sarvābharaṇabhūṣitā

Significance The description of Her form closes by gathering every ornament into one; in worship the ornaments (ābharaṇa) are offered to Her as one of the services of pūjā.

52 शिवकामेश्वराङ्कस्था śiva-kāmeśvarāṅka-sthā

She who sits on the lap of Śiva, who is Kāmeśvara

Sandhi कामेश्वर = काम + ईश्वर (kāma + īśvara) — guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ); कामेश्वराङ्क = कामेश्वर + अङ्क (kāmeśvara + aṅka) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and a karmadhāraya). (1) śiva-kāmeśvara 'Śiva who is Kāmeśvara' (karmadhāraya of apposition). (2) …kāmeśvara-aṅka 'His lap' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) -stha 'staying, seated' is √sthā with the suffix -a after a word in the locative (Pāṇini 3.2.4 supi sthaḥ), an upapada-tatpuruṣa; it takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis शिवः कामेश्वरः शिवकामेश्वरः; शिवकामेश्वरस्य अङ्कः शिवकामेश्वराङ्कः; शिवकामेश्वराङ्के तिष्ठति इति शिवकामेश्वराङ्कस्था
śivaḥ kāmeśvaraḥ śivakāmeśvaraḥ; śivakāmeśvarasya aṅkaḥ śivakāmeśvarāṅkaḥ; śivakāmeśvarāṅke tiṣṭhati iti śivakāmeśvarāṅkasthā

Significance Her iconic form is seated on the left lap of Kāmeśvara: Śiva and Śakti as one, never apart. Traditionally the name is read as that inseparability, the stillness of Śiva holding the dynamism of Śakti.

53 शिवा śivā

She who is Śivā, auspiciousness itself, the power of Śiva

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Traditionally there is no difference between Śiva and Śivā: She is Śiva's own nature, and as the auspicious one She bestows auspiciousness and liberation on those who worship Her.

54 स्वाधीनवल्लभा svādhīna-vallabhā

She who keeps Her husband always under Her control

Sandhi स्वाधीन = स्व + अधीन (sva + adhīna) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner saptamī-tatpuruṣa). (1) sva-adhīna 'dependent on oneself, subject to oneself' (saptamī-tatpuruṣa: adhīna 'dependent' governs the locative). Here sva refers to Her. (2) It qualifies vallabha 'beloved, husband', and the whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose beloved is subject to Her'; vallabha takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis स्वस्मिन् अधीनः स्वाधीनः; स्वाधीनः वल्लभः यस्याः सा स्वाधीनवल्लभा
svasmin adhīnaḥ svādhīnaḥ; svādhīnaḥ vallabhaḥ yasyāḥ sā svādhīnavallabhā

Significance In poetics the svādhīnabhartṛkā is the heroine whose husband is under her sway. Saundaryalaharī 1 gives the reason: Śiva joined to Śakti is able to act; without Her He cannot even stir.

Śloka 22names 55–58

सुमेरुमध्यशृङ्गस्था श्रीमन्नगरनायिका ।
चिन्तामणिगृहान्तस्था पञ्चब्रह्मासनस्थिता ॥ २२ ॥

sumerumadhyaśṛṅgasthā śrīmannagaranāyikā |
cintāmaṇigṛhāntasthā pañcabrahmāsanasthitā || 22 ||

The names, separated

55सुमेरु-मध्य-शृङ्ग-स्थाsumeru-madhya-śṛṅga-sthā56श्रीमन्-नगर-नायिकाśrīman-nagara-nāyikā

57चिन्तामणि-गृहान्त-स्थाcintāmaṇi-gṛhānta-sthā58पञ्च-ब्रह्मासन-स्थिताpañca-brahmāsana-sthitā

Translation

55She who sits on the middle peak of Mount Sumeru; 56She who is the sovereign of the glorious city (Śrīpura);

57She who dwells within the palace built of cintāmaṇi, the wish-fulfilling gems; 58She who is seated on the throne formed of the five Brahmas.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish

Where the names meet

Names 55–61 describe Her abode: the central peak of Meru, the city, the cintāmaṇi palace, the throne of the five Brahmas, the lotus and kadamba forests, the ocean of nectar. In 56 śrīman- is śrīmat with t → n before nagara.

The names

55 सुमेरुमध्यशृङ्गस्था sumeru-madhya-śṛṅga-sthā

She who sits on the middle peak of Mount Sumeru

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and a karmadhāraya). (1) madhya-śṛṅga 'the middle peak' (karmadhāraya). (2) sumeru-madhyaśṛṅga 'the middle peak of Sumeru' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) -sthā 'abiding' (√sthā after a word in the locative, Pāṇini 3.2.4) is the head: 'She who abides on the middle peak of Sumeru'. The members are simply juxtaposed.

Analysis मध्यम् शृङ्गम् मध्यशृङ्गम्; सुमेरोः मध्यशृङ्गम् सुमेरुमध्यशृङ्गम्; सुमेरुमध्यशृङ्गे तिष्ठति इति सुमेरुमध्यशृङ्गस्था
madhyam śṛṅgam madhyaśṛṅgam; sumeroḥ madhyaśṛṅgam sumerumadhyaśṛṅgam; sumerumadhyaśṛṅge tiṣṭhati iti sumerumadhyaśṛṅgasthā

Significance Traditionally Meru has three peaks at its corners, the seats of Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva, and a higher middle peak where Her city stands. With this name begins the account of Her abode.

Corrected सुमेरुमध्यश‍ृङ्गस्था → सुमेरुमध्यशृङ्गस्था. Removed a zero-width joiner inside शृ (rendering workaround) that also corrupted the IAST.

56 श्रीमन्नगरनायिका śrīman-nagara-nāyikā

She who is the sovereign of the glorious city (Śrīpura)

Sandhi श्रीमन्नगर = श्रीमत् + नगर (śrīmat + nagara) — nasal assimilation: the final t of śrīmat becomes n before the nasal n (Pāṇini 8.4.45 yaro 'nunāsike 'nunāsiko vā)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (with an inner karmadhāraya). (1) śrīmat-nagara 'the glorious city' (karmadhāraya), i.e. Śrīnagara or Śrīpura, Her city. (2) nāyikā 'mistress, sovereign' is the head and the city stands to it in the genitive.

Analysis श्रीमत् नगरम् श्रीमन्नगरम्; श्रीमन्नगरस्य नायिका श्रीमन्नगरनायिका
śrīmat nagaram śrīmannagaram; śrīmannagarasya nāyikā śrīmannagaranāyikā

Significance Śrīpura, the city on Meru's central peak, is described in the Lalitopākhyāna with its many concentric enclosures; in Śrīvidyā the city is also the Śrīcakra, with Her at its center.

57 चिन्तामणिगृहान्तस्था cintāmaṇi-gṛhānta-sthā

She who dwells within the palace built of cintāmaṇi, the wish-fulfilling gems

Sandhi गृहान्त = गृह + अन्त (gṛha + anta) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and a karmadhāraya). (1) cintāmaṇi-gṛha 'the house made of cintāmaṇi gems' (karmadhāraya with 'made of' understood). (2) …gṛha-anta 'its interior' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) -sthā 'abiding' (√sthā after a word in the locative) is the head.

Analysis चिन्तामणिमयम् गृहम् चिन्तामणिगृहम्; चिन्तामणिगृहस्य अन्तः चिन्तामणिगृहान्तः; चिन्तामणिगृहान्ते तिष्ठति इति चिन्तामणिगृहान्तस्था
cintāmaṇimayam gṛham cintāmaṇigṛham; cintāmaṇigṛhasya antaḥ cintāmaṇigṛhāntaḥ; cintāmaṇigṛhānte tiṣṭhati iti cintāmaṇigṛhāntasthā

Significance The cintāmaṇi palace is the innermost dwelling within Śrīpura. In Śrīvidyā the city and its palace correspond to the Śrīcakra, the palace to its innermost region.

58 पञ्चब्रह्मासनस्थिता pañca-brahmāsana-sthitā

She who is seated on the throne formed of the five Brahmas

Sandhi ब्रह्मासन = ब्रह्म + आसन (brahma + āsana) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound saptamī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya and a dvigu). (1) pañca-brahman 'the five Brahmas', a numeral compound used as a fixed designation (dvigu). (2) …brahma-āsana 'the seat formed of the five Brahmas' (karmadhāraya with 'consisting of' understood). (3) The participle sthitā 'seated' is the head and takes the seat in the locative. pañcan and brahman lose their final n in composition; these are morphological, not sandhi.

Analysis पञ्च ब्रह्माणः पञ्चब्रह्माणः; पञ्चब्रह्मात्मकम् आसनम् पञ्चब्रह्मासनम्; पञ्चब्रह्मासने स्थिता पञ्चब्रह्मासनस्थिता
pañca brahmāṇaḥ pañcabrahmāṇaḥ; pañcabrahmātmakam āsanam pañcabrahmāsanam; pañcabrahmāsane sthitā pañcabrahmāsanasthitā

Significance In Śrīvidyā the throne's four legs are Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra and Īśvara, and Sadāśiva is its seat: the lords of creation, maintenance, dissolution, concealment and grace all serve as Her throne.

Śloka 23names 59–63

महापद्माटवीसंस्था कदम्बवनवासिनी ।
सुधासागरमध्यस्था कामाक्षी कामदायिनी ॥ २३ ॥

mahāpadmāṭavīsaṃsthā kadambavanavāsinī |
sudhāsāgaramadhyasthā kāmākṣī kāmadāyinī || 23 ||

The names, separated

61सुधा-सागर-मध्य-स्थाsudhā-sāgara-madhya-sthā62कामाक्षीkāmākṣī63काम-दायिनीkāma-dāyinī

Translation

59She who resides in the great lotus forest; 60She who resides in the kadamba forest;

61She who resides in the center of the ocean of nectar; 62She whose eyes are lovely, eyes in which love dwells; 63She who grants all wishes.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish
59 महापद्माटवीसंस्था mahā-padmāṭavī-saṃsthā
महत्mahatgreatappears as mahā- (Pāṇini 6.3.46)

कदम्बkadambathe kadamba tree (Neolamarckia cadamba), with fragrant ball-shaped orange flowers
वनvanaforest, grove
वासिनीvāsinīdwelling, she who dwells√vas 'to dwell' + -in, feminine

सुधाsudhānectar, ambrosia
सागरsāgaraocean

स्थाsthāabiding√sthā + -a, feminine

अक्षीakṣīeyeakṣi, as akṣa at the end of the bahuvrīhi, with the feminine ī

कामkāmadesire, wish; also Kāma, the god of love
दायिनीdāyinīgiver, bestower√dā 'to give' + -in, feminine

Where the names meet

The second half holds three names: sudhāsāgaramadhyasthā (61) | kāmākṣī (62) | kāmadāyinī (63).

The names

59 महापद्माटवीसंस्था mahā-padmāṭavī-saṃsthā

She who resides in the great lotus forest

Sandhi पद्माटवी = पद्म + अटवी (padma + aṭavī) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); संस्था = सम् + स्था (sam + sthā) — the m of the prefix sam becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ)

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya and a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) padma-aṭavī 'a forest of lotuses' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) mahā qualifies it, 'the great lotus forest' (karmadhāraya; mahatī → mahā-, Pāṇini 6.3.42 and 6.3.46). It can equally be read as mahāpadma-aṭavī 'the forest of great lotuses'. (3) saṃsthā 'abiding' (sam + √sthā + -a, after a word in the locative) is the head.

Analysis पद्मानाम् अटवी पद्माटवी; महती पद्माटवी महापद्माटवी; महापद्माटव्याम् संतिष्ठते इति महापद्माटवीसंस्था
padmānām aṭavī padmāṭavī; mahatī padmāṭavī mahāpadmāṭavī; mahāpadmāṭavyām saṃtiṣṭhate iti mahāpadmāṭavīsaṃsthā

Significance A great lotus forest is part of the setting of Her city. Traditionally it is also read inwardly, as the lotuses of the yogic body and above all the thousand-petalled lotus at the crown.

Uncertain mahā may qualify the forest ('the great lotus forest') or the lotuses ('the forest of great lotuses'); both readings are current and the sense is the same.

60 कदम्बवनवासिनी kadamba-vana-vāsinī

She who resides in the kadamba forest

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) kadamba-vana 'the forest of kadamba trees' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) vāsin 'dwelling', √vas with the suffix -in after a word in the locative (Pāṇini 3.2.78 supy ajātau ṇinis tācchīlye: one whose nature it is to dwell there), is the head; it takes the feminine ī. The members are simply juxtaposed.

Analysis कदम्बानाम् वनम् कदम्बवनम्; कदम्बवने वसति इति कदम्बवनवासिनी
kadambānām vanam kadambavanam; kadambavane vasati iti kadambavanavāsinī

Significance A grove of kadamba trees surrounds Her palace in Śrīpura. On earth, Madurai, the seat of Mīnākṣī, was anciently a kadamba forest, and the Goddess there is traditionally praised by this name.

61 सुधासागरमध्यस्था sudhā-sāgara-madhya-sthā

She who resides in the center of the ocean of nectar

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (1) sudhā-sāgara 'the ocean of nectar' and …sāgara-madhya 'its middle' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (2) -sthā 'abiding' (√sthā after a word in the locative) is the head. The members are simply juxtaposed.

Analysis सुधायाः सागरः सुधासागरः; सुधासागरस्य मध्यम् सुधासागरमध्यम्; सुधासागरमध्ये तिष्ठति इति सुधासागरमध्यस्था
sudhāyāḥ sāgaraḥ sudhāsāgaraḥ; sudhāsāgarasya madhyam sudhāsāgaramadhyam; sudhāsāgaramadhye tiṣṭhati iti sudhāsāgaramadhyasthā

Significance Traditionally Her city is also placed on an island of gems (maṇidvīpa) in the midst of an ocean of nectar. Inwardly the nectar is read as the amṛta that flows from the thousand-petalled lotus.

62 कामाक्षी kāmākṣī

She whose eyes are lovely, eyes in which love dwells

Sandhi कामाक्षी = काम + अक्षी (kāma + akṣī) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (with the compound-final suffix ṣac). A bahuvrīhi describing Her. akṣi 'eye' at the end of a bahuvrīhi becomes akṣa (the samāsānta suffix ṣac, Pāṇini 5.4.113 bahuvrīhau sakthyakṣṇoḥ svāṅgāt ṣac) and takes the feminine ī: -ākṣī. kāma may be the adjective 'lovely, desirable' ('whose eyes are lovely') or the noun 'love, desire' ('in whose eyes love dwells').

Analysis कामे कमनीये अक्षिणी यस्याः सा कामाक्षी; अथवा कामः अक्ष्णोः यस्याः सा कामाक्षी
kāme kamanīye akṣiṇī yasyāḥ sā kāmākṣī; athavā kāmaḥ akṣṇoḥ yasyāḥ sā kāmākṣī

Significance Kāmākṣī is the Goddess of Kāñcīpuram, traditionally identified with Lalitā. A traditional reading divides kā (Sarasvatī) + mā (Lakṣmī) + akṣī: She whose two eyes are Sarasvatī and Lakṣmī.

Uncertain Several analyses are current: kāma as 'lovely' (the meaning given), as 'love, desire' dwelling in Her eyes, and the traditional kā + mā + akṣī (Sarasvatī and Lakṣmī as Her eyes).

63 कामदायिनी kāma-dāyinī

She who grants all wishes

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. dāyin 'giving', √dā with the agent suffix -in (a y is inserted after the root's ā), takes kāma 'desire, wish' as its object; it is the head and takes the feminine ī. The members are simply juxtaposed.

Analysis कामान् ददाति इति कामदायिनी
kāmān dadāti iti kāmadāyinī

Significance She fulfills the desires of Her devotees, and traditionally the highest of them, the desire for liberation. kāma can also be the god Kāma: She gave back Kāma, burnt by Śiva's eye, a deed named in name 84.

Śloka 24names 64–65

देवर्षिगणसङ्घातस्तूयमानात्मवैभवा ।
भण्डासुरवधोद्युक्तशक्तिसेनासमन्विता ॥ २४ ॥

devarṣigaṇasaṅghātastūyamānātmavaibhavā |
bhaṇḍāsuravadhodyuktaśaktisenāsamanvitā || 24 ||

The names, separated

64देवर्षि-गण-सङ्घात-स्तूयमानात्म-वैभवाdevarṣi-gaṇa-saṅghāta-stūyamānātma-vaibhavā

65भण्डासुर-वधोद्युक्त-शक्ति-सेना-समन्विताbhaṇḍāsura-vadhodyukta-śakti-senā-samanvitā

Translation

64She whose own glory is being praised by the assembled hosts of gods and sages;

65She who is accompanied by an army of śaktis intent on slaying Bhaṇḍāsura.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish
64 देवर्षिगणसङ्घातस्तूयमानात्मवैभवा devarṣi-gaṇa-saṅghāta-stūyamānātma-vaibhavā
देवdevagod

Where the names meet

Here begins the Bhaṇḍāsura episode of the Lalitopākhyāna, which runs to name 84. Name 64: divide stūyamāna + ātma-vaibhava ('Her own glory'), not stūyamānātma.

The names

64 देवर्षिगणसङ्घातस्तूयमानात्मवैभवा devarṣi-gaṇa-saṅghāta-stūyamānātma-vaibhavā

She whose own glory is being praised by the assembled hosts of gods and sages

Sandhi देवर्षि = देव + ऋषि (deva + ṛṣi) — guṇa: a + ṛ → ar (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ); स्तूयमानात्म = स्तूयमान + आत्म (stūyamāna + ātma) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over inner tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa, ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas and a dvandva). (1) deva-ṛṣi 'gods and sages' (dvandva; it can also be read as a karmadhāraya, 'the divine sages'). (2) …ṛṣi-gaṇa 'their hosts' and …gaṇa-saṅghāta 'the assembled multitude of those hosts' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (3) stūyamāna 'being praised', the present passive participle of √stu, takes that multitude as agent in the instrumental (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (4) ātma-vaibhava 'Her own glory' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa), qualified by (3). (5) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose own glory is being praised by …'; vaibhava takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis देवाः च ऋषयः च देवर्षयः; देवर्षीणाम् गणाः देवर्षिगणाः; देवर्षिगणानाम् सङ्घातः देवर्षिगणसङ्घातः; देवर्षिगणसङ्घातेन स्तूयमानम् देवर्षिगणसङ्घातस्तूयमानम्; आत्मनः वैभवम् आत्मवैभवम्; देवर्षिगणसङ्घातस्तूयमानम् आत्मवैभवम् यस्याः सा देवर्षिगणसङ्घातस्तूयमानात्मवैभवा
devāḥ ca ṛṣayaḥ ca devarṣayaḥ; devarṣīṇām gaṇāḥ devarṣigaṇāḥ; devarṣigaṇānām saṅghātaḥ devarṣigaṇasaṅghātaḥ; devarṣigaṇasaṅghātena stūyamānam devarṣigaṇasaṅghātastūyamānam; ātmanaḥ vaibhavam ātmavaibhavam; devarṣigaṇasaṅghātastūyamānam ātmavaibhavam yasyāḥ sā devarṣigaṇasaṅghātastūyamānātmavaibhavā

Significance Here begins the account of the war with Bhaṇḍāsura, told in the Lalitopākhyāna: as She sets out, the gods and sages praise Her.

65 भण्डासुरवधोद्युक्तशक्तिसेनासमन्विता bhaṇḍāsura-vadhodyukta-śakti-senā-samanvitā

She who is accompanied by an army of śaktis intent on slaying Bhaṇḍāsura

Sandhi भण्डासुर = भण्ड + असुर (bhaṇḍa + asura) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); वधोद्युक्त = वध + उद्युक्त (vadha + udyukta) — guṇa: a + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ); अन्विता = अनु + इता (anu + itā) — yaṇ: u becomes v before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci), at the junction of the prefix anu with ita

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over inner karmadhārayas, a saptamī-tatpuruṣa and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (1) bhaṇḍa-asura 'the demon Bhaṇḍa' (karmadhāraya of apposition) and …asura-vadha 'his slaying' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) udyukta 'intent, set upon' takes the slaying in the locative (saptamī-tatpuruṣa). (3) śakti-senā 'the army of śaktis' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa), qualified by (2) (karmadhāraya; udyuktā takes its masculine stem). (4) samanvitā 'accompanied by' is the head and takes the army in the instrumental.

Analysis भण्डः असुरः भण्डासुरः; भण्डासुरस्य वधः भण्डासुरवधः; भण्डासुरवधे उद्युक्ता भण्डासुरवधोद्युक्ता; शक्तीनाम् सेना शक्तिसेना; भण्डासुरवधोद्युक्ता शक्तिसेना भण्डासुरवधोद्युक्तशक्तिसेना; तया समन्विता भण्डासुरवधोद्युक्तशक्तिसेनासमन्विता
bhaṇḍaḥ asuraḥ bhaṇḍāsuraḥ; bhaṇḍāsurasya vadhaḥ bhaṇḍāsuravadhaḥ; bhaṇḍāsuravadhe udyuktā bhaṇḍāsuravadhodyuktā; śaktīnām senā śaktisenā; bhaṇḍāsuravadhodyuktā śaktisenā bhaṇḍāsuravadhodyuktaśaktisenā; tayā samanvitā bhaṇḍāsuravadhodyuktaśaktisenāsamanvitā

Significance In the Lalitopākhyāna Bhaṇḍa arises from the ashes of Kāma, burnt by Śiva's eye. Traditionally he is read as the ignorance that binds the soul, and Her army as the powers that overcome it.

Śloka 25names 66–67

सम्पत्करीसमारूढसिन्धुरव्रजसेविता ।
अश्वारूढाधिष्ठिताश्वकोटिकोटिभिरावृता ॥ २५ ॥

sampatkarīsamārūḍhasindhuravrajasevitā |
aśvārūḍhādhiṣṭhitāśvakoṭikoṭibhirāvṛtā || 25 ||

The names, separated

66सम्पत्करी-समारूढ-सिन्धुर-व्रज-सेविताsampatkarī-samārūḍha-sindhura-vraja-sevitā

67अश्वारूढाधिष्ठिताश्व-कोटि-कोटिभिर्-आवृताaśvārūḍhādhiṣṭhitāśva-koṭi-koṭibhir-āvṛtā

Translation

66She who is attended by a herd of elephants ridden by Sampatkarī;

67She who is surrounded by countless millions of horses commanded by Aśvārūḍhā.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish
66 सम्पत्करीसमारूढसिन्धुरव्रजसेविता sampatkarī-samārūḍha-sindhura-vraja-sevitā

व्रजvrajaherd, troop

67 अश्वारूढाधिष्ठिताश्वकोटिकोटिभिरावृता aśvārūḍhādhiṣṭhitāśva-koṭi-koṭibhir-āvṛtā
अश्वaśvahorse
आरूढाārūḍhāmounted; here the śakti Aśvārūḍhā, 'she who rides a horse'ā + √ruh, past participle, feminine
अधिष्ठितadhiṣṭhitacommanded, presided overadhi + √sthā, past participle
कोटिkoṭia crore, ten million

Where the names meet

Name 67 is one name of two words: …koṭikoṭibhiḥ āvṛtā; the visarga becomes r before ā (koṭibhir āvṛtā).

The names

66 सम्पत्करीसमारूढसिन्धुरव्रजसेविता sampatkarī-samārūḍha-sindhura-vraja-sevitā

She who is attended by a herd of elephants ridden by Sampatkarī

Sandhi सम्पत्करी = सम्पद् + करी (sampad + karī) — cartva: the final d of sampad becomes t before the voiceless k (Pāṇini 8.4.55 khari ca)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, a karmadhāraya and a tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (1) sampatkarī-samārūḍha 'mounted by Sampatkarī' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa: agent with a past participle). (2) It qualifies sindhura 'elephant' (karmadhāraya). (3) …sindhura-vraja 'the herd of those elephants' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (4) The participle sevitā 'attended, served' is the head and takes the herd in the instrumental. Sampatkarī rides at the head of the elephants, and the herd is hers.

Analysis सम्पत्कर्या समारूढाः सम्पत्करीसमारूढाः; सम्पत्करीसमारूढाः सिन्धुराः सम्पत्करीसमारूढसिन्धुराः; सम्पत्करीसमारूढसिन्धुराणाम् व्रजः सम्पत्करीसमारूढसिन्धुरव्रजः; तेन सेविता सम्पत्करीसमारूढसिन्धुरव्रजसेविता
sampatkaryā samārūḍhāḥ sampatkarīsamārūḍhāḥ; sampatkarīsamārūḍhāḥ sindhurāḥ sampatkarīsamārūḍhasindhurāḥ; sampatkarīsamārūḍhasindhurāṇām vrajaḥ sampatkarīsamārūḍhasindhuravrajaḥ; tena sevitā sampatkarīsamārūḍhasindhuravrajasevitā

Significance Sampatkarī leads Her elephant corps in the war with Bhaṇḍa. Traditionally she is said to arise from Her goad (aṅkuśa), as Aśvārūḍhā (name 67) from Her noose (pāśa).

67 अश्वारूढाधिष्ठिताश्वकोटिकोटिभिरावृता aśvārūḍhādhiṣṭhitāśva-koṭi-koṭibhir-āvṛtā

She who is surrounded by countless millions of horses commanded by Aśvārūḍhā

Sandhi अश्वारूढा = अश्व + आरूढा (aśva + ārūḍhā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); आरूढाधिष्ठित = आरूढा + अधिष्ठित (ārūḍhā + adhiṣṭhita) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); अधिष्ठित = अधि + स्थित (adhi + sthita) — after the prefix adhi the s of √sthā becomes ṣ (Pāṇini 8.3.65), and the following t becomes ṭ after ṣ (ṣṭutva, 8.4.41 ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ); अधिष्ठिताश्व = अधिष्ठित + अश्व (adhiṣṭhita + aśva) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); कोटिभिरावृता = कोटिभिः + आवृता (koṭibhiḥ + āvṛtā) — visarga becomes r before a vowel (the s of the ending -bhis becomes ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66, pronounced r before a vowel); this joins two separate words

Compound a phrase of two words: a compound in the instrumental plural (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa over a karmadhāraya, a tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa and a dvitīyā-tatpuruṣa), governed by the participle āvṛtā. (1) aśva-ārūḍhā 'she who has mounted a horse', the name of the śakti Aśvārūḍhā (dvitīyā-tatpuruṣa). (2) adhiṣṭhita 'commanded, presided over' takes her as agent in the instrumental (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa), and (3) qualifies aśva 'horse' (karmadhāraya). (4) koṭi-koṭi 'crores of crores', i.e. countless millions (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa), of those horses. This long compound is declined in the instrumental plural (…koṭibhiḥ) and is a separate word from āvṛtā 'surrounded', which governs it; the visarga becomes r before ā. The name is therefore a two-word phrase, not a single compound.

Analysis अश्वम् आरूढा अश्वारूढा; अश्वारूढया अधिष्ठिताः अश्वारूढाधिष्ठिताः; अश्वारूढाधिष्ठिताः अश्वाः अश्वारूढाधिष्ठिताश्वाः; कोटीनाम् कोटयः कोटिकोटयः; अश्वारूढाधिष्ठिताश्वानाम् कोटिकोटयः अश्वारूढाधिष्ठिताश्वकोटिकोटयः; अश्वारूढाधिष्ठिताश्वकोटिकोटिभिः आवृता
aśvam ārūḍhā aśvārūḍhā; aśvārūḍhayā adhiṣṭhitāḥ aśvārūḍhādhiṣṭhitāḥ; aśvārūḍhādhiṣṭhitāḥ aśvāḥ aśvārūḍhādhiṣṭhitāśvāḥ; koṭīnām koṭayaḥ koṭikoṭayaḥ; aśvārūḍhādhiṣṭhitāśvānām koṭikoṭayaḥ aśvārūḍhādhiṣṭhitāśvakoṭikoṭayaḥ; aśvārūḍhādhiṣṭhitāśvakoṭikoṭibhiḥ āvṛtā

Significance Aśvārūḍhā leads Her cavalry; traditionally she arises from Her noose (pāśa). The horses are often read as the senses, as in the Kaṭha Upaniṣad (indriyāṇi hayān āhuḥ), held in check by the power that rides them.

Where the names meet

Names 68–70 name the three chariots of the war: Cakrarāja (Hers), Geyacakra (Mantriṇī's) and Kiricakra (Daṇḍanāthā's).

The names

68 चक्रराजरथारूढसर्वायुधपरिष्कृता cakra-rāja-rathārūḍha-sarvāyudha-pariṣkṛtā

She who, mounted on the chariot Cakrarāja, is equipped with all weapons

Sandhi रथारूढ = रथ + आरूढ (ratha + ārūḍha) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); सर्वायुध = सर्व + आयुध (sarva + āyudha) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound karmadhāraya of two qualifiers (each a dvitīyā- or tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa over inner karmadhārayas and a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) cakra-rāja 'king of cakras' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; rājan becomes rāja at the end of a tatpuruṣa, Pāṇini 5.4.91), the name of Her chariot, in apposition with ratha (karmadhāraya). (2) ārūḍhā 'mounted on' takes the chariot as object (dvitīyā-tatpuruṣa). (3) sarva-āyudha 'all weapons' (karmadhāraya) in the instrumental with pariṣkṛtā 'equipped, adorned' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (4) The two qualifiers, both describing Her, are joined as a karmadhāraya: 'mounted on Cakrarāja and equipped with all weapons'; the first takes its masculine stem (ārūḍha).

Analysis चक्राणाम् राजा चक्रराजः; चक्रराजः नाम रथः चक्रराजरथः; चक्रराजरथम् आरूढा चक्रराजरथारूढा; सर्वाणि आयुधानि सर्वायुधानि; सर्वायुधैः परिष्कृता सर्वायुधपरिष्कृता; चक्रराजरथारूढा च असौ सर्वायुधपरिष्कृता च चक्रराजरथारूढसर्वायुधपरिष्कृता
cakrāṇām rājā cakrarājaḥ; cakrarājaḥ nāma rathaḥ cakrarājarathaḥ; cakrarājaratham ārūḍhā cakrarājarathārūḍhā; sarvāṇi āyudhāni sarvāyudhāni; sarvāyudhaiḥ pariṣkṛtā sarvāyudhapariṣkṛtā; cakrarājarathārūḍhā ca asau sarvāyudhapariṣkṛtā ca cakrarājarathārūḍhasarvāyudhapariṣkṛtā

Significance Traditionally the chariot Cakrarāja, 'king of cakras', is the Śrīcakra itself, its tiers occupied by the deities of the Śrīcakra's enclosures (āvaraṇa). Names 68–70 name the three chariots of the war.

Uncertain The compound can also be read with ārūḍha qualifying āyudha, 'equipped with all the weapons placed on the Cakrarāja chariot', parallel to names 69–70 where ārūḍha qualifies the following member. The meaning given follows the usual reading.

69 गेयचक्ररथारूढमन्त्रिणीपरिसेविता geya-cakra-rathārūḍha-mantriṇī-parisevitā

She who is attended by Mantriṇī, mounted on the chariot Geyacakra

Sandhi रथारूढ = रथ + आरूढ (ratha + ārūḍha) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over inner karmadhārayas and a dvitīyā-tatpuruṣa). (1) geya-cakra 'the cakra of song', the name of Mantriṇī's chariot, in apposition with ratha (karmadhāraya). (2) ārūḍhā 'mounted on' takes the chariot as object (dvitīyā-tatpuruṣa) and (3) qualifies mantriṇī (karmadhāraya; ārūḍhā takes its masculine stem). (4) The participle parisevitā 'attended, served' is the head and takes Mantriṇī in the instrumental.

Analysis गेयचक्रम् नाम रथः गेयचक्ररथः; गेयचक्ररथम् आरूढा गेयचक्ररथारूढा; गेयचक्ररथारूढा मन्त्रिणी गेयचक्ररथारूढमन्त्रिणी; तया परिसेविता गेयचक्ररथारूढमन्त्रिणीपरिसेविता
geyacakram nāma rathaḥ geyacakrarathaḥ; geyacakraratham ārūḍhā geyacakrarathārūḍhā; geyacakrarathārūḍhā mantriṇī geyacakrarathārūḍhamantriṇī; tayā parisevitā geyacakrarathārūḍhamantriṇīparisevitā

Significance Mantriṇī, also called Śyāmalā, is Her minister and counselor and presides over music and speech; hence her chariot is 'the cakra of song'.

Śloka 27names 70–71

किरिचक्ररथारूढदण्डनाथापुरस्कृता ।
ज्वालामालिनिकाक्षिप्तवह्निप्राकारमध्यगा ॥ २७ ॥

kiricakrarathārūḍhadaṇḍanāthāpuraskṛtā |

Where the names meet

Name 71: Jvālāmālinikā is the goddess Jvālāmālinī (with -kā), one name, followed by ākṣipta 'raised'; do not divide jvālā | mālinikākṣipta.

The names

70 किरिचक्ररथारूढदण्डनाथापुरस्कृता kiri-cakra-rathārūḍha-daṇḍa-nāthā-puraskṛtā

She who is escorted by Daṇḍanāthā, mounted on the chariot Kiricakra

Sandhi रथारूढ = रथ + आरूढ (ratha + ārūḍha) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); पुरस्कृता = पुरस् + कृता (puras + kṛtā) — the s of puras, used as a prefix (gati), stays s before k instead of becoming visarga (Pāṇini 8.3.40 namaspurasor gatyoḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over inner karmadhārayas, a dvitīyā-tatpuruṣa and a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) kiri-cakra 'the boar-cakra', the name of the chariot drawn by boars, in apposition with ratha (karmadhāraya). (2) ārūḍhā takes it as object (dvitīyā-tatpuruṣa) and (3) qualifies daṇḍa-nāthā 'mistress of the rod', the commander (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa inside; karmadhāraya). (4) puraskṛtā 'placed in front, escorted, honored' is the head and takes Daṇḍanāthā in the instrumental: Daṇḍanāthā goes before Her.

Analysis किरिचक्रम् नाम रथः किरिचक्ररथः; किरिचक्ररथम् आरूढा किरिचक्ररथारूढा; दण्डस्य नाथा दण्डनाथा; किरिचक्ररथारूढा दण्डनाथा किरिचक्ररथारूढदण्डनाथा; तया पुरस्कृता किरिचक्ररथारूढदण्डनाथापुरस्कृता
kiricakram nāma rathaḥ kiricakrarathaḥ; kiricakraratham ārūḍhā kiricakrarathārūḍhā; daṇḍasya nāthā daṇḍanāthā; kiricakrarathārūḍhā daṇḍanāthā kiricakrarathārūḍhadaṇḍanāthā; tayā puraskṛtā kiricakrarathārūḍhadaṇḍanāthāpuraskṛtā

Significance Daṇḍanāthā, also called Daṇḍinī, is Vārāhī, the boar-faced commander of Her army, hence her boar chariot. Mantriṇī (name 69) and Daṇḍanāthā are Her two chief ministers, of counsel and of command.

71 ज्वालामालिनिकाक्षिप्तवह्निप्राकारमध्यगा jvālāmālinikākṣipta-vahni-prākāra-madhya-gā

She who stands in the midst of the wall of fire raised by Jvālāmālinī

Sandhi मालिनिकाक्षिप्त = मालिनिका + आक्षिप्त (mālinikā + ākṣipta) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, karmadhārayas and a tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (1) jvālāmālinikā-ākṣipta 'raised by Jvālāmālinikā' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (2) vahni-prākāra 'a wall of fire' (karmadhāraya with 'made of' understood), qualified by (1). (3) …prākāra-madhya 'the inside of that wall' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (4) -gā 'going, being in' (√gam with the suffix -a after the place) is the head (upapada-tatpuruṣa).

Analysis ज्वालामालिनिकया आक्षिप्तः ज्वालामालिनिकाक्षिप्तः; वह्निमयः प्राकारः वह्निप्राकारः; ज्वालामालिनिकाक्षिप्तः वह्निप्राकारः ज्वालामालिनिकाक्षिप्तवह्निप्राकारः; ज्वालामालिनिकाक्षिप्तवह्निप्राकारस्य मध्यम् ज्वालामालिनिकाक्षिप्तवह्निप्राकारमध्यम्; तस्मिन् गच्छति इति ज्वालामालिनिकाक्षिप्तवह्निप्राकारमध्यगा
jvālāmālinikayā ākṣiptaḥ jvālāmālinikākṣiptaḥ; vahnimayaḥ prākāraḥ vahniprākāraḥ; jvālāmālinikākṣiptaḥ vahniprākāraḥ jvālāmālinikākṣiptavahniprākāraḥ; jvālāmālinikākṣiptavahniprākārasya madhyam jvālāmālinikākṣiptavahniprākāramadhyam; tasmin gacchati iti jvālāmālinikākṣiptavahniprākāramadhyagā

Significance In the Lalitopākhyāna, when Bhaṇḍa's forces attack by night, Jvālāmālinī, one of the Nityā goddesses, raises a ring of fire round Her camp. Traditionally this is read as the protection that surrounds those who take refuge in Her.

Where the names meet

Name 73: nityā here names the Nityā goddesses, not 'eternal'.

The names

72 भण्डसैन्यवधोद्युक्तशक्तिविक्रमहर्षिता bhaṇḍa-sainya-vadhodyukta-śakti-vikrama-harṣitā

She who rejoices at the valor of the śaktis intent on destroying the forces of Bhaṇḍa

Sandhi वधोद्युक्त = वध + उद्युक्त (vadha + udyukta) — guṇa: a + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas, a saptamī-tatpuruṣa and a karmadhāraya). (1) bhaṇḍa-sainya 'Bhaṇḍa's army' and …sainya-vadha 'its destruction' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (2) udyukta 'intent upon' takes the destruction in the locative (saptamī-tatpuruṣa) and qualifies śakti (karmadhāraya). (3) …śakti-vikrama 'the valor of those śaktis' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (4) harṣitā 'gladdened' is the head and takes the valor in the instrumental, as its cause.

Analysis भण्डस्य सैन्यम् भण्डसैन्यम्; भण्डसैन्यस्य वधः भण्डसैन्यवधः; भण्डसैन्यवधे उद्युक्ताः भण्डसैन्यवधोद्युक्ताः; भण्डसैन्यवधोद्युक्ताः शक्तयः भण्डसैन्यवधोद्युक्तशक्तयः; भण्डसैन्यवधोद्युक्तशक्तीनाम् विक्रमः भण्डसैन्यवधोद्युक्तशक्तिविक्रमः; तेन हर्षिता भण्डसैन्यवधोद्युक्तशक्तिविक्रमहर्षिता
bhaṇḍasya sainyam bhaṇḍasainyam; bhaṇḍasainyasya vadhaḥ bhaṇḍasainyavadhaḥ; bhaṇḍasainyavadhe udyuktāḥ bhaṇḍasainyavadhodyuktāḥ; bhaṇḍasainyavadhodyuktāḥ śaktayaḥ bhaṇḍasainyavadhodyuktaśaktayaḥ; bhaṇḍasainyavadhodyuktaśaktīnām vikramaḥ bhaṇḍasainyavadhodyuktaśaktivikramaḥ; tena harṣitā bhaṇḍasainyavadhodyuktaśaktivikramaharṣitā

Significance She delights in the courage of Her own powers; traditionally the battle is read as the inner struggle in which the soul's powers, turned toward Her, overcome ignorance and its offspring.

73 नित्यापराक्रमाटोपनिरीक्षणसमुत्सुका nityā-parākramāṭopa-nirīkṣaṇa-samutsukā

She who is eager to watch the full display of the Nityā goddesses' valor

Sandhi पराक्रमाटोप = पराक्रम + आटोप (parākrama + āṭopa) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound saptamī-tatpuruṣa (over inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (1) nityā-parākrama 'the valor of the Nityās', …parākrama-āṭopa 'the swelling display of that valor', and …āṭopa-nirīkṣaṇa 'watching it' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). nityā keeps its feminine ā: it names the goddesses. (2) samutsukā 'eager' is the head and takes the watching in the locative (saptamī-tatpuruṣa).

Analysis नित्यानाम् पराक्रमः नित्यापराक्रमः; नित्यापराक्रमस्य आटोपः नित्यापराक्रमाटोपः; नित्यापराक्रमाटोपस्य निरीक्षणम् नित्यापराक्रमाटोपनिरीक्षणम्; नित्यापराक्रमाटोपनिरीक्षणे समुत्सुका नित्यापराक्रमाटोपनिरीक्षणसमुत्सुका
nityānām parākramaḥ nityāparākramaḥ; nityāparākramasya āṭopaḥ nityāparākramāṭopaḥ; nityāparākramāṭopasya nirīkṣaṇam nityāparākramāṭopanirīkṣaṇam; nityāparākramāṭopanirīkṣaṇe samutsukā nityāparākramāṭopanirīkṣaṇasamutsukā

Significance The Nityās, goddesses of the fifteen lunar days (with Lalitā Herself as the sixteenth), go into battle against Bhaṇḍa's forces, and She watches their prowess. In Śrīvidyā they are worshipped as the phases of the moon and of time itself.

Where the names meet

Name 75 begins mantriṇī + ambā joined by yaṇ (ī → y).

The names

74 भण्डपुत्रवधोद्युक्तबालाविक्रमनन्दिता bhaṇḍa-putra-vadhodyukta-bālā-vikrama-nanditā

She who is delighted by the valor of Bālā, intent on slaying the sons of Bhaṇḍa

Sandhi वधोद्युक्त = वध + उद्युक्त (vadha + udyukta) — guṇa: a + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas, a saptamī-tatpuruṣa and a karmadhāraya). (1) bhaṇḍa-putra 'the sons of Bhaṇḍa' and …putra-vadha 'their slaying' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (2) udyuktā 'intent upon' takes the slaying in the locative (saptamī-tatpuruṣa) and qualifies Bālā (karmadhāraya; udyuktā takes its masculine stem). (3) …bālā-vikrama 'Bālā's valor' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (4) nanditā 'delighted' is the head and takes the valor in the instrumental.

Analysis भण्डस्य पुत्राः भण्डपुत्राः; भण्डपुत्राणाम् वधः भण्डपुत्रवधः; भण्डपुत्रवधे उद्युक्ता भण्डपुत्रवधोद्युक्ता; भण्डपुत्रवधोद्युक्ता बाला भण्डपुत्रवधोद्युक्तबाला; भण्डपुत्रवधोद्युक्तबालायाः विक्रमः भण्डपुत्रवधोद्युक्तबालाविक्रमः; तेन नन्दिता भण्डपुत्रवधोद्युक्तबालाविक्रमनन्दिता
bhaṇḍasya putrāḥ bhaṇḍaputrāḥ; bhaṇḍaputrāṇām vadhaḥ bhaṇḍaputravadhaḥ; bhaṇḍaputravadhe udyuktā bhaṇḍaputravadhodyuktā; bhaṇḍaputravadhodyuktā bālā bhaṇḍaputravadhodyuktabālā; bhaṇḍaputravadhodyuktabālāyāḥ vikramaḥ bhaṇḍaputravadhodyuktabālāvikramaḥ; tena nanditā bhaṇḍaputravadhodyuktabālāvikramananditā

Significance In the Lalitopākhyāna Bālā, the Goddess's young daughter, begs to join the battle and slays the sons of Bhaṇḍa. In Śrīvidyā Bālā Tripurasundarī is worshipped as the girl-form of Lalitā.

75 मन्त्रिण्यम्बाविरचितविषङ्गवधतोषिता mantriṇyambā-viracita-viṣaṅga-vadha-toṣitā

She who is pleased by the slaying of Viṣaṅga accomplished by Mother Mantriṇī

Sandhi मन्त्रिण्यम्बा = मन्त्रिणी + अम्बा (mantriṇī + ambā) — yaṇ: ī becomes y before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over inner karmadhārayas, a tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa and a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) mantriṇī-ambā 'Mother Mantriṇī' (karmadhāraya of apposition; as a proper name Mantriṇī keeps its feminine form). (2) viracita 'accomplished' takes her as agent in the instrumental (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (3) viṣaṅga-vadha 'the slaying of Viṣaṅga' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa), qualified by (2) (karmadhāraya). (4) toṣitā 'pleased' is the head and takes the slaying in the instrumental.

Analysis मन्त्रिणी च असौ अम्बा च मन्त्रिण्यम्बा; मन्त्रिण्यम्बया विरचितः मन्त्रिण्यम्बाविरचितः; विषङ्गस्य वधः विषङ्गवधः; मन्त्रिण्यम्बाविरचितः विषङ्गवधः मन्त्रिण्यम्बाविरचितविषङ्गवधः; तेन तोषिता मन्त्रिण्यम्बाविरचितविषङ्गवधतोषिता
mantriṇī ca asau ambā ca mantriṇyambā; mantriṇyambayā viracitaḥ mantriṇyambāviracitaḥ; viṣaṅgasya vadhaḥ viṣaṅgavadhaḥ; mantriṇyambāviracitaḥ viṣaṅgavadhaḥ mantriṇyambāviracitaviṣaṅgavadhaḥ; tena toṣitā mantriṇyambāviracitaviṣaṅgavadhatoṣitā

Significance Mantriṇī, the counselor of name 69, also takes the field: in this account she slays Viṣaṅga, one of Bhaṇḍa's two brothers.

Where the names meet

Vārāhī (76) is Daṇḍanāthā of name 70. Name 77 introduces Mahāgaṇeśa, who breaks the obstacle-yantra in the next name.

The names

76 विशुक्रप्राणहरणवाराहीवीर्यनन्दिता viśukra-prāṇa-haraṇa-vārāhī-vīrya-nanditā

She who is delighted by the valor of Vārāhī, who took the life of Viśukra

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (1) viśukra-prāṇa 'Viśukra's life-breaths' and …prāṇa-haraṇa 'the taking of them' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (2) vārāhī-vīrya 'Vārāhī's valor' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) (1) and (2) stand in apposition: the valor that was the taking of Viśukra's life (karmadhāraya). (4) nanditā 'delighted' is the head and takes that valor in the instrumental. haraṇa can also be read as an agent noun, 'taking away', qualifying Vārāhī; the sense is the same. The members are simply juxtaposed.

Analysis विशुक्रस्य प्राणाः विशुक्रप्राणाः; विशुक्रप्राणानाम् हरणम् विशुक्रप्राणहरणम्; वाराह्याः वीर्यम् वाराहीवीर्यम्; विशुक्रप्राणहरणम् वाराहीवीर्यम् विशुक्रप्राणहरणवाराहीवीर्यम्; तेन नन्दिता विशुक्रप्राणहरणवाराहीवीर्यनन्दिता
viśukrasya prāṇāḥ viśukraprāṇāḥ; viśukraprāṇānām haraṇam viśukraprāṇaharaṇam; vārāhyāḥ vīryam vārāhīvīryam; viśukraprāṇaharaṇam vārāhīvīryam viśukraprāṇaharaṇavārāhīvīryam; tena nanditā viśukraprāṇaharaṇavārāhīvīryananditā

Significance Vārāhī is Daṇḍanāthā of name 70, the commander of Her army; here she slays Bhaṇḍa's other brother, Viśukra.

77 कामेश्वरमुखालोककल्पितश्रीगणेश्वरा kāmeśvara-mukhāloka-kalpita-śrī-gaṇeśvarā

She who brought forth Śrī Gaṇeśa by a glance at the face of Kāmeśvara

Sandhi कामेश्वर = काम + ईश्वर (kāma + īśvara) — guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ); मुखालोक = मुख + आलोक (mukha + āloka) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); गणेश्वरा = गण + ईश्वरा (gaṇa + īśvarā) — guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over inner tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa, karmadhāraya and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (1) kāmeśvara-mukha 'Kāmeśvara's face' and …mukha-āloka 'the look upon that face' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas; the genitive is that of the object looked at). (2) kalpita 'fashioned, brought forth' takes the look as its means in the instrumental (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (3) gaṇa-īśvara 'lord of the hosts', Gaṇeśa (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa), with the honorific śrī (karmadhāraya). (4) The whole is a bahuvrīhi in the instrumental relation: 'She by whom Śrī Gaṇeśa was brought forth through a look at Kāmeśvara's face'; gaṇeśvara takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis कामेश्वरस्य मुखम् कामेश्वरमुखम्; कामेश्वरमुखस्य आलोकः कामेश्वरमुखालोकः; कामेश्वरमुखालोकेन कल्पितः कामेश्वरमुखालोककल्पितः; गणानाम् ईश्वरः गणेश्वरः; श्रीमान् गणेश्वरः श्रीगणेश्वरः; कामेश्वरमुखालोककल्पितः श्रीगणेश्वरः यया सा कामेश्वरमुखालोककल्पितश्रीगणेश्वरा
kāmeśvarasya mukham kāmeśvaramukham; kāmeśvaramukhasya ālokaḥ kāmeśvaramukhālokaḥ; kāmeśvaramukhālokena kalpitaḥ kāmeśvaramukhālokakalpitaḥ; gaṇānām īśvaraḥ gaṇeśvaraḥ; śrīmān gaṇeśvaraḥ śrīgaṇeśvaraḥ; kāmeśvaramukhālokakalpitaḥ śrīgaṇeśvaraḥ yayā sā kāmeśvaramukhālokakalpitaśrīgaṇeśvarā

Significance In the Lalitopākhyāna Viśukra sets up an obstacle-yantra (jaya-vighna-yantra) that saps Her army's strength; She looks at Kāmeśvara's face, and from that look Mahāgaṇeśa arises to shatter it (the next name).

Where the names meet

Names 78–84 close the war with Bhaṇḍāsura: the obstacle-yantra (78), the counter-missiles (79), the ten avatāras (80), the Pāśupata and Kāmeśvara missiles (81–82), the gods' praise (83) and the revival of Kāma (84). Each half-śloka here is a single name.

The names

78 महागणेशनिर्भिन्नविघ्नयन्त्रप्रहर्षिता mahā-gaṇeśa-nirbhinna-vighna-yantra-praharṣitā

She who was delighted when Mahāgaṇeśa shattered the yantra of obstacles

Sandhi गणेश = गण + ईश (gaṇa + īśa) — guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ), inside the lexicalised compound gaṇeśa; निर्भिन्न = निस् + भिन्न (nis + bhinna) — the final s of the prefix nis becomes r before a vowel or a voiced consonant (s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ; ru turns to visarga only before a voiceless sound or a pause, 8.3.15): nis → nir

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya, a tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa and a karmadhāraya). (1) mahā-gaṇeśa 'the great Gaṇeśa' (karmadhāraya; mahat becomes mahā- before a co-referential member). (2) vighna-yantra 'the yantra of obstacles', a device that causes obstacles (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) mahāgaṇeśa-nirbhinna 'shattered by Mahāgaṇeśa': the agent in the instrumental with a past participle (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (4) That participle qualifies vighnayantra (karmadhāraya): 'the obstacle-yantra shattered by Mahāgaṇeśa'. (5) The head is praharṣitā 'made glad', and the whole event stands to it in the instrumental of cause: 'delighted by (the sight of) it'.

Analysis महान् गणेशः महागणेशः; विघ्नानाम् यन्त्रम् विघ्नयन्त्रम्; महागणेशेन निर्भिन्नम् महागणेशनिर्भिन्नम्; महागणेशनिर्भिन्नम् विघ्नयन्त्रम् महागणेशनिर्भिन्नविघ्नयन्त्रम्; तेन प्रहर्षिता महागणेशनिर्भिन्नविघ्नयन्त्रप्रहर्षिता
mahān gaṇeśaḥ mahāgaṇeśaḥ; vighnānām yantram vighnayantram; mahāgaṇeśena nirbhinnam mahāgaṇeśanirbhinnam; mahāgaṇeśanirbhinnam vighnayantram mahāgaṇeśanirbhinnavighnayantram; tena praharṣitā mahāgaṇeśanirbhinnavighnayantrapraharṣitā

Significance In the Lalitopākhyāna a yantra that spreads obstacles is set up against Her army; from Her glance at Kāmeśvara Mahāgaṇapati arises and smashes it. Inwardly, Her grace removes the obstacles to sādhana, which is why Gaṇeśa is worshipped first.

79 भण्डासुरेन्द्रनिर्मुक्तशस्त्रप्रत्यस्त्रवर्षिणी bhaṇḍāsurendra-nirmukta-śastra-pratyastra-varṣiṇī

She who rained counter-missiles on the weapons released by Bhaṇḍāsura, lord of the demons

Sandhi भण्डासुर = भण्ड + असुर (bhaṇḍa + asura) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); असुरेन्द्र = असुर + इन्द्र (asura + indra) — guṇa: a + i → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ); निर्मुक्त = निस् + मुक्त (nis + mukta) — the final s of the prefix nis becomes r before a vowel or a voiced consonant (s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ; ru turns to visarga only before a voiceless sound or a pause, 8.3.15): nis → nir; प्रत्यस्त्र = प्रति + अस्त्र (prati + astra) — yaṇ: i becomes y before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci)

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over inner karmadhārayas and tṛtīyā- and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (1) asura-indra 'lord of the asuras' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa), in apposition to Bhaṇḍa (karmadhāraya): 'Bhaṇḍa, lord of the asuras'. (2) …-nirmukta 'released by him' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa), qualifying śastra 'weapons' (karmadhāraya). (3) prati-astra 'counter-missile' is itself a prādi compound; here the weapons stand to it in the genitive: 'the counter-missiles to those weapons'. (4) The head varṣiṇī 'raining down' (√vṛṣ + -in, feminine) takes all of this as its object (upapada-tatpuruṣa).

Analysis असुराणाम् इन्द्रः असुरेन्द्रः; भण्डः च असौ असुरेन्द्रः च भण्डासुरेन्द्रः; भण्डासुरेन्द्रेण निर्मुक्तानि भण्डासुरेन्द्रनिर्मुक्तानि; भण्डासुरेन्द्रनिर्मुक्तानि शस्त्राणि भण्डासुरेन्द्रनिर्मुक्तशस्त्राणि; तेषाम् प्रत्यस्त्राणि भण्डासुरेन्द्रनिर्मुक्तशस्त्रप्रत्यस्त्राणि; तानि वर्षति इति भण्डासुरेन्द्रनिर्मुक्तशस्त्रप्रत्यस्त्रवर्षिणी
asurāṇām indraḥ asurendraḥ; bhaṇḍaḥ ca asau asurendraḥ ca bhaṇḍāsurendraḥ; bhaṇḍāsurendreṇa nirmuktāni bhaṇḍāsurendranirmuktāni; bhaṇḍāsurendranirmuktāni śastrāṇi bhaṇḍāsurendranirmuktaśastrāṇi; teṣām pratyastrāṇi bhaṇḍāsurendranirmuktaśastrapratyastrāṇi; tāni varṣati iti bhaṇḍāsurendranirmuktaśastrapratyastravarṣiṇī

Significance In the Purāṇic battle every weapon Bhaṇḍa released was met by a counter-weapon from Her; the next names give examples. Traditionally each of ignorance's assaults is answered by a matching power of knowledge.

Śloka 32names 80–81

कराङ्गुलिनखोत्पन्ननारायणदशाकृतिः ।
