Where the names meet

Name 80 ends in -iḥ, not -ā: its last member ākṛti is a feminine i-stem.

The names

80 कराङ्गुलिनखोत्पन्ननारायणदशाकृतिः karāṅguli-nakhotpanna-nārāyaṇa-daśākṛtiḥ

She from whose fingernails the ten forms of Nārāyaṇa arose

Sandhi कराङ्गुलि = कर + अङ्गुलि (kara + aṅguli) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); उत्पन्न = उद् + पन्न (ud + panna) — cartva: a final d becomes t before a voiceless sound (Pāṇini 8.4.55 khari ca); नखोत्पन्न = नख + उत्पन्न (nakha + utpanna) — guṇa: a + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ); दशाकृति = दश + आकृति (daśa + ākṛti) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas, a pañcamī-tatpuruṣa and a numeral karmadhāraya). (1) kara-aṅguli 'fingers of the hand' and …-nakha 'their nails' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (2) …nakha-utpanna 'sprung from those nails' (pañcamī-tatpuruṣa with the participle utpanna). (3) nārāyaṇa-daśa-ākṛti 'the ten forms of Nārāyaṇa': the numeral daśa qualifies ākṛti, and Nārāyaṇa stands in the genitive. (4) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She from the nails of whose fingers the ten forms of Nārāyaṇa arose'. ākṛti is already a feminine i-stem, so the name ends in -iḥ, not -ā.

Analysis करस्य अङ्गुलयः कराङ्गुलयः; कराङ्गुलीनाम् नखाः कराङ्गुलिनखाः; कराङ्गुलिनखेभ्यः उत्पन्नाः कराङ्गुलिनखोत्पन्नाः; नारायणस्य दश आकृतयः नारायणदशाकृतयः; कराङ्गुलिनखोत्पन्नाः नारायणदशाकृतयः यस्याः सा कराङ्गुलिनखोत्पन्ननारायणदशाकृतिः
karasya aṅgulayaḥ karāṅgulayaḥ; karāṅgulīnām nakhāḥ karāṅgulinakhāḥ; karāṅgulinakhebhyaḥ utpannāḥ karāṅgulinakhotpannāḥ; nārāyaṇasya daśa ākṛtayaḥ nārāyaṇadaśākṛtayaḥ; karāṅgulinakhotpannāḥ nārāyaṇadaśākṛtayaḥ yasyāḥ sā karāṅgulinakhotpannanārāyaṇadaśākṛtiḥ

Significance Traditionally, when Bhaṇḍa loosed a missile that brought forth the great asuras of old, the ten avatāras of Viṣṇu sprang from Her ten fingernails to destroy them: the incarnations are a play of Her power.

81 महापाशुपतास्त्राग्निनिर्दग्धासुरसैनिका mahā-pāśupatāstrāgni-nirdagdhāsura-sainikā

She who burned up the demon soldiers in the fire of the great Pāśupata missile

Sandhi पाशुपतास्त्र = पाशुपत + अस्त्र (pāśupata + astra) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); अस्त्राग्नि = अस्त्र + अग्नि (astra + agni) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); निर्दग्ध = निस् + दग्ध (nis + dagdha) — the final s of the prefix nis becomes r before a vowel or a voiced consonant (s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ; ru turns to visarga only before a voiceless sound or a pause, 8.3.15): nis → nir; दग्धासुर = दग्ध + असुर (dagdha + asura) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over inner karmadhārayas, ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas and a tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (1) mahā-pāśupata-astra 'the great Pāśupata missile' (karmadhārayas; mahat becomes mahā-). (2) …astra-agni 'the fire of that missile' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) …agni-nirdagdha 'burnt up by that fire' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (4) asura-sainika 'the asura soldiers' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (5) The whole is a bahuvrīhi with the instrumental relation: 'She by whom the asura soldiers were burnt up …'; sainika takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis महत् पाशुपतम् महापाशुपतम्; महापाशुपतम् अस्त्रम् महापाशुपतास्त्रम्; महापाशुपतास्त्रस्य अग्निः महापाशुपतास्त्राग्निः; असुराणाम् सैनिकाः असुरसैनिकाः; महापाशुपतास्त्राग्निना निर्दग्धाः असुरसैनिकाः यया सा महापाशुपतास्त्राग्निनिर्दग्धासुरसैनिका
mahat pāśupatam mahāpāśupatam; mahāpāśupatam astram mahāpāśupatāstram; mahāpāśupatāstrasya agniḥ mahāpāśupatāstrāgniḥ; asurāṇām sainikāḥ asurasainikāḥ; mahāpāśupatāstrāgninā nirdagdhāḥ asurasainikāḥ yayā sā mahāpāśupatāstrāgninirdagdhāsurasainikā

Significance In the Purāṇic battle the Mahāpāśupata missile consumes Bhaṇḍa's remaining army; only Bhaṇḍa and his city remain for the next name.

Where the names meet

Name 82: Śūnyaka is the name of Bhaṇḍa's city, and sa-bhaṇḍāsura means 'together with Bhaṇḍāsura'. Name 83: Mahendra is Indra and Upendra is Viṣṇu.

The names

82 कामेश्वरास्त्रनिर्दग्धसभण्डासुरशून्यका kāmeśvarāstra-nirdagdha-sabhaṇḍāsura-śūnyakā

She who with the Kāmeśvara missile burned up Bhaṇḍāsura together with his city Śūnyaka

Sandhi कामेश्वर = काम + ईश्वर (kāma + īśvara) — guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ); कामेश्वरास्त्र = कामेश्वर + अस्त्र (kāmeśvara + astra) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); निर्दग्ध = निस् + दग्ध (nis + dagdha) — the final s of the prefix nis becomes r before a vowel or a voiced consonant (s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ; ru turns to visarga only before a voiceless sound or a pause, 8.3.15): nis → nir; भण्डासुर = भण्ड + असुर (bhaṇḍa + asura) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over inner ṣaṣṭhī- and tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣas, a saha-bahuvrīhi and a karmadhāraya). (1) kāmeśvara-astra 'the missile of Kāmeśvara' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa), and …-nirdagdha 'burnt up by it' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (2) sa-bhaṇḍāsura 'together with Bhaṇḍāsura': a saha-bahuvrīhi in which saha 'with' is shortened to sa- (Pāṇini 2.2.28, 6.3.82). (3) It qualifies Śūnyaka, the name of Bhaṇḍa's city (karmadhāraya). (4) The whole is a bahuvrīhi with the instrumental relation: 'She by whom Śūnyaka, together with Bhaṇḍāsura, was burnt up by the Kāmeśvara missile'; the last member takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis कामेश्वरस्य अस्त्रम् कामेश्वरास्त्रम्; कामेश्वरास्त्रेण निर्दग्धम् कामेश्वरास्त्रनिर्दग्धम्; भण्डासुरेण सह वर्तमानम् सभण्डासुरम्; सभण्डासुरम् शून्यकम् सभण्डासुरशून्यकम्; कामेश्वरास्त्रनिर्दग्धम् सभण्डासुरशून्यकम् यया सा कामेश्वरास्त्रनिर्दग्धसभण्डासुरशून्यका
kāmeśvarasya astram kāmeśvarāstram; kāmeśvarāstreṇa nirdagdham kāmeśvarāstranirdagdham; bhaṇḍāsureṇa saha vartamānam sabhaṇḍāsuram; sabhaṇḍāsuram śūnyakam sabhaṇḍāsuraśūnyakam; kāmeśvarāstranirdagdham sabhaṇḍāsuraśūnyakam yayā sā kāmeśvarāstranirdagdhasabhaṇḍāsuraśūnyakā

Significance The Lalitopākhyāna ends the war with the Kāmeśvara missile, which destroys Bhaṇḍa and Śūnyaka together. The city's name, 'the void', is traditionally read as the emptiness to which ignorance and its works are reduced.

83 ब्रह्मोपेन्द्रमहेन्द्रादिदेवसंस्तुतवैभवा brahmopendra-mahendrādi-deva-saṃstuta-vaibhavā

She whose glory is extolled by Brahmā, Upendra (Viṣṇu), Mahendra (Indra) and the other gods

Sandhi ब्रह्मोपेन्द्र = ब्रह्म + उपेन्द्र (brahma + upendra) — guṇa: a + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ); उपेन्द्र = उप + इन्द्र (upa + indra) — guṇa: a + i → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ), inside the lexicalised compound upendra; महेन्द्र = महा + इन्द्र (mahā + indra) — guṇa: ā + i → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ), inside the lexicalised compound mahendra; महेन्द्रादि = महेन्द्र + आदि (mahendra + ādi) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); संस्तुत = सम् + स्तुत (sam + stuta) — m becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ); before a sibilant it stays anusvāra: sam → saṃ

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an itaretara-dvandva, an inner bahuvrīhi with ādi, a karmadhāraya and a tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (1) brahma-upendra-mahendra 'Brahmā, Upendra and Mahendra' (itaretara-dvandva). (2) …-ādi 'beginning with them' (a bahuvrīhi with ādi), qualifying deva 'the gods' (karmadhāraya): 'the gods headed by Brahmā, Upendra and Mahendra'. (3) …deva-saṃstuta 'extolled by those gods' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa), qualifying vaibhava 'glory'. (4) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose glory is extolled by …'; vaibhava takes the feminine -ā. brahman drops its final n in composition (8.2.7).

Analysis ब्रह्मा च उपेन्द्रः च महेन्द्रः च ब्रह्मोपेन्द्रमहेन्द्राः; ब्रह्मोपेन्द्रमहेन्द्राः आदयः येषाम् ते ब्रह्मोपेन्द्रमहेन्द्रादयः; ब्रह्मोपेन्द्रमहेन्द्रादयः च ते देवाः च ब्रह्मोपेन्द्रमहेन्द्रादिदेवाः; ब्रह्मोपेन्द्रमहेन्द्रादिदेवैः संस्तुतम् वैभवम् यस्याः सा ब्रह्मोपेन्द्रमहेन्द्रादिदेवसंस्तुतवैभवा
brahmā ca upendraḥ ca mahendraḥ ca brahmopendramahendrāḥ; brahmopendramahendrāḥ ādayaḥ yeṣām te brahmopendramahendrādayaḥ; brahmopendramahendrādayaḥ ca te devāḥ ca brahmopendramahendrādidevāḥ; brahmopendramahendrādidevaiḥ saṃstutam vaibhavam yasyāḥ sā brahmopendramahendrādidevasaṃstutavaibhavā

Significance After Bhaṇḍa's fall the gods gather and praise Her. Traditionally even the gods of creation, preservation and rule owe their offices to Her, so their praise is the praise of the source by its powers.

वाग्भवvāgbhavavāgbhava, "source of speech": the first kūṭa of the Pañcadaśīvāc "speech" + bhava "origin"
कूटkūṭakūṭa: a peak; here one of the three syllable-groups of the Pañcadaśī mantra

Where the names meet

Name 84 completes the Bhaṇḍa episode. Name 85 begins the subtle form (sūkṣma-rūpa): the three kūṭas of the Pañcadaśī as Her body (85–89).

The names

84 हरनेत्राग्निसन्दग्धकामसञ्जीवनौषधिः hara-netrāgni-sandagdha-kāma-sañjīvanauṣadhiḥ

She who is the life-restoring herb for Kāma, who had been burned by the fire of Hara's (Śiva's) eye

Sandhi नेत्राग्नि = नेत्र + अग्नि (netra + agni) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); सन्दग्ध = सम् + दग्ध (sam + dagdha) — m becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ), and the anusvāra takes the nasal of the following stop's class (8.4.58 anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ): sam → san; सञ्जीवन = सम् + जीवन (sam + jīvana) — m becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ), and the anusvāra takes the nasal of the following stop's class (8.4.58 anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ): sam → sañ; सञ्जीवनौषधि = सञ्जीवन + ओषधि (sañjīvana + oṣadhi) — vṛddhi: a + o → au (Pāṇini 6.1.88 vṛddhir eci)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over inner ṣaṣṭhī- and tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣas and karmadhārayas). (1) hara-netra-agni 'the fire of Hara's (Śiva's) eye' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (2) …agni-sandagdha 'burnt up by that fire' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa), qualifying kāma (karmadhāraya): 'Kāma, burnt by the fire of Hara's eye'. (3) sañjīvana-oṣadhi 'the reviving herb' (karmadhāraya; sañjīvanī takes its masculine stem before oṣadhi). (4) Kāma stands to it in the genitive (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa), and the whole is identified with Her: She IS the herb. oṣadhi is a feminine i-stem, so the name ends in -iḥ.

Analysis हरस्य नेत्रम् हरनेत्रम्; हरनेत्रस्य अग्निः हरनेत्राग्निः; हरनेत्राग्निना सन्दग्धः हरनेत्राग्निसन्दग्धः; हरनेत्राग्निसन्दग्धः कामः हरनेत्राग्निसन्दग्धकामः; सञ्जीवनी ओषधिः सञ्जीवनौषधिः; हरनेत्राग्निसन्दग्धकामस्य सञ्जीवनौषधिः हरनेत्राग्निसन्दग्धकामसञ्जीवनौषधिः
harasya netram haranetram; haranetrasya agniḥ haranetrāgniḥ; haranetrāgninā sandagdhaḥ haranetrāgnisandagdhaḥ; haranetrāgnisandagdhaḥ kāmaḥ haranetrāgnisandagdhakāmaḥ; sañjīvanī oṣadhiḥ sañjīvanauṣadhiḥ; haranetrāgnisandagdhakāmasya sañjīvanauṣadhiḥ haranetrāgnisandagdhakāmasañjīvanauṣadhiḥ

Significance Kāma, burnt to ashes by Śiva's third eye, is restored to life by Her at the gods' request once Bhaṇḍa, who had risen from those ashes, is destroyed. Traditionally desire purified by Her grace is given back as a power that serves the world.

85 श्रीमद्वाग्भवकूटैकस्वरूपमुखपङ्कजा śrīmad-vāgbhava-kūṭaika-svarūpa-mukha-paṅkajā

She whose lotus face is, in its very nature, the glorious vāgbhava-kūṭa (the first syllable-group of the Pañcadaśī mantra)

Sandhi श्रीमद्वाग्भव = श्रीमत् + वाग्भव (śrīmat + vāgbhava) — jaśtva: a final t becomes d before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.39 jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte); वाग्भव = वाच् + भव (vāc + bhava) — the final c of vāc becomes k at the end of a member (Pāṇini 8.2.30 coḥ kuḥ) and is voiced to g before bh (jaśtva, 8.2.39), inside the lexicalised compound vāgbhava; कूटैक = कूट + एक (kūṭa + eka) — vṛddhi: a + e → ai (Pāṇini 6.1.88 vṛddhir eci)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner bahuvrīhi, a rūpaka-karmadhāraya and karmadhārayas). (1) vāgbhava-kūṭa 'the kūṭa called vāgbhava' (karmadhāraya), qualified by śrīmat 'glorious'. (2) …kūṭa-eka-svarūpa 'having that kūṭa alone as its very nature' (an inner bahuvrīhi; eka 'one, sole'). (3) mukha-paṅkaja 'the lotus that is the face' (rūpaka-karmadhāraya), which that bahuvrīhi qualifies. (4) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose lotus face is, in its very nature, the glorious vāgbhava-kūṭa'; paṅkaja takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis वाग्भवम् कूटम् वाग्भवकूटम्; श्रीमत् वाग्भवकूटम् श्रीमद्वाग्भवकूटम्; श्रीमद्वाग्भवकूटम् एव एकम् स्वरूपम् यस्य तत् श्रीमद्वाग्भवकूटैकस्वरूपम्; मुखम् एव पङ्कजम् मुखपङ्कजम्; श्रीमद्वाग्भवकूटैकस्वरूपम् मुखपङ्कजम् यस्याः सा श्रीमद्वाग्भवकूटैकस्वरूपमुखपङ्कजा
vāgbhavam kūṭam vāgbhavakūṭam; śrīmat vāgbhavakūṭam śrīmadvāgbhavakūṭam; śrīmadvāgbhavakūṭam eva ekam svarūpam yasya tat śrīmadvāgbhavakūṭaikasvarūpam; mukham eva paṅkajam mukhapaṅkajam; śrīmadvāgbhavakūṭaikasvarūpam mukhapaṅkajam yasyāḥ sā śrīmadvāgbhavakūṭaikasvarūpamukhapaṅkajā

Significance Traditionally names 85–89 describe Her subtle form (sūkṣma-rūpa) as the fifteen-syllabled Pañcadaśī: its three kūṭas are Her face, Her body from neck to waist, and the part below the waist. The vāgbhava, 'source of speech', is fittingly the face, the seat of speech.

86कण्ठाधः-कटि-पर्यन्त-मध्य-कूट-स्वरूपिणीkaṇṭhādhaḥ-kaṭi-paryanta-madhya-kūṭa-svarūpiṇī

Where the names meet

Name 86 keeps the visarga of adhaḥ before k (kaṇṭhādhaḥ-kaṭi); in name 87 the same adhas appears as adho- before bh.

The names

86 कण्ठाधःकटिपर्यन्तमध्यकूटस्वरूपिणी kaṇṭhādhaḥ-kaṭi-paryanta-madhya-kūṭa-svarūpiṇī

She whose form from below the throat down to the waist is the middle kūṭa (the kāmarāja-kūṭa) of the Pañcadaśī

Sandhi कण्ठाधः = कण्ठ + अधः (kaṇṭha + adhaḥ) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); अधःकटि = अधस् + कटि (adhas + kaṭi) — visarga sandhi: the final s of adhas becomes ru (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ) and then visarga before the voiceless k (8.3.15 kharavasānayor visarjanīyaḥ); पर्यन्त = परि + अन्त (pari + anta) — yaṇ: i becomes y before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci), inside the lexicalised compound paryanta

Compound saptamī-tatpuruṣa in sense (the body-region in the locative), over an inner bahuvrīhi, a karmadhāraya and the possessive -in. (1) kaṇṭha-adhas 'below the throat' (the indeclinable adhas with the throat as its point of reference). (2) kaṭi-paryanta 'having the waist as its limit' (bahuvrīhi), together with (1) naming the region of the body 'from below the throat down to the waist'. (3) madhya-kūṭa 'the middle kūṭa' (karmadhāraya). (4) svarūpiṇī 'having as Her own form' (svarūpa + the possessive -in, feminine -iṇī) is the head; madhyakūṭa is what She has as Her form, and the region is where: 'She who, from below the throat to the waist, has the middle kūṭa as Her form'.

Analysis कण्ठात् अधः कण्ठाधः; कटिः पर्यन्तः यस्य तत् कटिपर्यन्तम्; कण्ठाधः कटिपर्यन्तम् (अङ्गम्) कण्ठाधःकटिपर्यन्तम्; मध्यम् कूटम् मध्यकूटम्; मध्यकूटम् स्वरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति मध्यकूटस्वरूपिणी; कण्ठाधःकटिपर्यन्ते मध्यकूटस्वरूपिणी कण्ठाधःकटिपर्यन्तमध्यकूटस्वरूपिणी
kaṇṭhāt adhaḥ kaṇṭhādhaḥ; kaṭiḥ paryantaḥ yasya tat kaṭiparyantam; kaṇṭhādhaḥ kaṭiparyantam (aṅgam) kaṇṭhādhaḥkaṭiparyantam; madhyam kūṭam madhyakūṭam; madhyakūṭam svarūpam asyāḥ asti iti madhyakūṭasvarūpiṇī; kaṇṭhādhaḥkaṭiparyante madhyakūṭasvarūpiṇī kaṇṭhādhaḥkaṭiparyantamadhyakūṭasvarūpiṇī

Significance The middle kūṭa of the Pañcadaśī, called kāmarāja, is traditionally Her body from the throat to the waist, the second of the three parts of Her subtle form.

Uncertain The first part, kaṇṭhādhaḥ-kaṭiparyanta, can be analysed adverbially or as a bahuvrīhi qualifying an understood 'part of the body'; the relation to the head is therefore stated in sense (locative) rather than as one fixed samāsa type.

87 शक्तिकूटैकतापन्नकट्यधोभागधारिणी śakti-kūṭaikatāpanna-kaṭyadho-bhāga-dhāriṇī

She whose form below the waist has become one with the śakti-kūṭa (the last four syllables of the Pañcadaśī mantra)

Sandhi कूटैकता = कूट + एकता (kūṭa + ekatā) — vṛddhi: a + e → ai (Pāṇini 6.1.88 vṛddhir eci); एकतापन्न = एकता + आपन्न (ekatā + āpanna) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); कट्यधः = कटि + अधः (kaṭi + adhaḥ) — yaṇ: i becomes y before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci); अधोभाग = अधस् + भाग (adhas + bhāga) — visarga sandhi: final s becomes ru (Pāṇini 8.2.66), which after a and before a voiced consonant becomes u (6.1.114 haśi ca); a + u then gives o (6.1.87)

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over inner karmadhārayas, a tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa and a dvitīyā-tatpuruṣa). (1) śakti-kūṭa 'the kūṭa called śakti' (karmadhāraya); …-ekatā 'oneness with it' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (2) …ekatā-āpanna 'having attained that oneness': an accusative with āpanna (dvitīyā-tatpuruṣa, Pāṇini 2.1.24, which names āpanna). (3) kaṭi-adhas-bhāga 'the part below the waist', qualified by (2) (karmadhāraya). (4) The head dhāriṇī 'bearing' (√dhṛ + -in, feminine) takes it as object (upapada-tatpuruṣa): 'She who bears a lower body that has become one with the śakti-kūṭa'.

Analysis शक्तिः इति कूटम् शक्तिकूटम्; शक्तिकूटेन एकता शक्तिकूटैकता; शक्तिकूटैकताम् आपन्नः शक्तिकूटैकतापन्नः; कटेः अधः कट्यधः; कट्यधः भागः कट्यधोभागः; शक्तिकूटैकतापन्नः कट्यधोभागः शक्तिकूटैकतापन्नकट्यधोभागः; तम् धारयति इति शक्तिकूटैकतापन्नकट्यधोभागधारिणी
śaktiḥ iti kūṭam śaktikūṭam; śaktikūṭena ekatā śaktikūṭaikatā; śaktikūṭaikatām āpannaḥ śaktikūṭaikatāpannaḥ; kaṭeḥ adhaḥ kaṭyadhaḥ; kaṭyadhaḥ bhāgaḥ kaṭyadhobhāgaḥ; śaktikūṭaikatāpannaḥ kaṭyadhobhāgaḥ śaktikūṭaikatāpannakaṭyadhobhāgaḥ; tam dhārayati iti śaktikūṭaikatāpannakaṭyadhobhāgadhāriṇī

Significance The śakti-kūṭa, the last four syllables of the Pañcadaśī, completes Her subtle form as the part below the waist. Traditionally the three kūṭas are also read as Her three powers and as the three sections of the Śrīcakra.

कुलामृतैकरसिका कुलसङ्केतपालिनी ॥ ३६ ॥

mūlamantrātmikā mūlakūṭatrayakalevarā |
kulāmṛtaikarasikā kulasaṅketapālinī || 36 ||

Where the names meet

Four names in this śloka. From name 90 the hymn turns to kula and the ascent of kuṇḍalinī (to name 111).

The names

88 मूलमन्त्रात्मिका mūla-mantrātmikā

She whose very self is the root mantra (the fifteen-syllabled Pañcadaśī)

Sandhi मन्त्रात्मिका = मन्त्र + आत्मिका (mantra + ātmikā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) mūla-mantra 'the root mantra' (karmadhāraya: mūla qualifies mantra), i.e. the Pañcadaśī. (2) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose self (ātman) is the root mantra'. ātman takes the suffix -ka at the end of the bahuvrīhi (ātmaka), and its feminine is ātmikā.

Analysis मूलम् मन्त्रः मूलमन्त्रः; मूलमन्त्रः आत्मा यस्याः सा मूलमन्त्रात्मिका
mūlam mantraḥ mūlamantraḥ; mūlamantraḥ ātmā yasyāḥ sā mūlamantrātmikā

Significance The mūla-mantra of Śrīvidyā is the Pañcadaśī; the deity and Her mantra are not two, so to repeat the mantra is to meet Her directly.

89 मूलकूटत्रयकलेवरा mūla-kūṭa-traya-kalevarā

She whose (subtle) body is the three kūṭas of the root mantra

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (over inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (1) mūla-kūṭa 'the kūṭas of the root (mantra)' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; mūla is short for mūlamantra, name 88). (2) …kūṭa-traya 'the triad of those kūṭas' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose body is the triad of kūṭas of the root mantra'; kalevara takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis मूलस्य कूटानि मूलकूटानि; मूलकूटानाम् त्रयम् मूलकूटत्रयम्; मूलकूटत्रयम् कलेवरम् यस्याः सा मूलकूटत्रयकलेवरा
mūlasya kūṭāni mūlakūṭāni; mūlakūṭānām trayam mūlakūṭatrayam; mūlakūṭatrayam kalevaram yasyāḥ sā mūlakūṭatrayakalevarā

Significance This name sums up names 85–87: the three kūṭas together are Her subtle body.

90 कुलामृतैकरसिका kulāmṛtaika-rasikā

She who delights solely in the nectar of kula

Sandhi कुलामृत = कुल + अमृत (kula + amṛta) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); अमृतैक = अमृत + एक (amṛta + eka) — vṛddhi: a + e → ai (Pāṇini 6.1.88 vṛddhir eci)

Compound saptamī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and an inner bahuvrīhi). (1) kula-amṛta 'the nectar of kula' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) eka-rasikā 'having a single relish, devoted to one delight': eka-rasa 'one taste' with the possessive suffix -ika, feminine -ikā. (3) The nectar stands to it in the locative (saptamī-tatpuruṣa): 'She whose one delight is in the nectar of kula'.

Analysis कुलस्य अमृतम् कुलामृतम्; एकः रसः यस्याः सा एकरसिका; कुलामृते एकरसिका कुलामृतैकरसिका
kulasya amṛtam kulāmṛtam; ekaḥ rasaḥ yasyāḥ sā ekarasikā; kulāmṛte ekarasikā kulāmṛtaikarasikā

Significance Traditionally the kula-nectar is the stream that flows when kuṇḍalinī, rising along the kula path, reaches the sahasrāra; it is also read as the bliss in which knower, knowing and known become one.

Uncertain eka can be taken with kulāmṛta ('the kula-nectar alone') or with rasikā (eka-rasikā 'having one delight'); the sense is the same.

91 कुलसङ्केतपालिनी kula-saṅketa-pālinī

She who guards the secret conventions of the kula path

Sandhi सङ्केत = सम् + केत (sam + keta) — m becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ), and the anusvāra takes the nasal of the following stop's class (8.4.58 anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ): sam → saṅ, inside the lexicalised word saṅketa

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) kula-saṅketa 'the secret conventions of the kula' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) The head pālinī 'protecting' (√pāl + -in, feminine) takes them as object (upapada-tatpuruṣa).

Analysis कुलस्य सङ्केताः कुलसङ्केताः; कुलसङ्केतान् पालयति इति कुलसङ्केतपालिनी
kulasya saṅketāḥ kulasaṅketāḥ; kulasaṅketān pālayati iti kulasaṅketapālinī

Significance Traditionally the kula teachings (mantras, signs and practices) are kept from the unprepared, and She herself guards them.

Śloka 37names 92–98

कुलाङ्गना कुलान्तस्था कौलिनी कुलयोगिनी ।
अकुला समयान्तस्था समयाचारतत्परा ॥ ३७ ॥

kulāṅganā kulāntasthā kaulinī kulayoginī |
akulā samayāntasthā samayācāratatparā || 37 ||

The names, separated

92कुलाङ्गनाkulāṅganā93कुलान्त-स्थाkulānta-sthā94कौलिनीkaulinī95कुल-योगिनीkula-yoginī

96अकुलाakulā97समयान्त-स्थाsamayānta-sthā98समयाचार-तत्पराsamayācāra-tatparā

Translation

92She who is well-born (a lady of noble family); 93She who abides within the kula; 94She who belongs to the Kaula tradition; 95She who is the yoginī (presiding deity) of the kula;

96She who has no family (She who is beyond kula); 97She who abides within samaya; 98She who is devoted to the Samaya mode of worship.

Word by word

आचारācārapractice, mode of worship

Where the names meet

Kula and its opposite are paired: Kaulinī (94) and Akulā (96, beginning with the negative a-); the Kaula and Samaya paths (93, 97–98). In 93 and 97, -āntasthā is best divided antar + sthā ('abiding within').

The names

92 कुलाङ्गना kulāṅganā

She who is well-born (a lady of noble family)

Sandhi कुलाङ्गना = कुल + अङ्गना (kula + aṅganā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. aṅganā 'woman, lady' is the head and kula 'noble family' stands to it in the genitive: 'the lady of a noble house', i.e. a well-born lady. Read with the surrounding names, kula is also the Kaula path, and She is its lady.

Analysis कुलस्य अङ्गना कुलाङ्गना
kulasya aṅganā kulāṅganā

Significance Traditionally, as a lady of a noble house is not seen in public, the Śrīvidyā is kept hidden and is not displayed to all.

93 कुलान्तस्था kulānta-sthā

She who abides within the kula

Sandhi कुलान्तः = कुल + अन्तः (kula + antaḥ) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); अन्तस्था = अन्तर् + स्था (antar + sthā) — the final r of antar becomes visarga before a voiceless sound (Pāṇini 8.3.15), and a visarga before a sibilant followed by a voiceless consonant may be dropped (a vārttika on 8.3.36): antaḥ-sthā → antasthā

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (with kula dependent on the indeclinable antar). sthā 'standing, abiding' (√sthā with the suffix ka, used only at the end of a compound) is the head; antar 'within' says where, and kula stands to antar in the genitive: 'She who abides within the kula'.

Analysis कुलस्य अन्तः तिष्ठति इति कुलान्तस्था
kulasya antaḥ tiṣṭhati iti kulāntasthā

Significance Traditionally She dwells within the kula both as the inner meaning of the Kaula teaching and as the presence within the suṣumnā through which kuṇḍalinī rises.

Uncertain The division kula-anta-sthā 'abiding at the end (or the inner part) of kula' is also possible; the reading antar + sthā is followed here.

94 कौलिनी kaulinī

She who belongs to the Kaula tradition

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Traditionally kula is Śakti and akula is Śiva, and kaula is their union; She who belongs to it is that union itself.

95 कुलयोगिनी kula-yoginī

She who is the yoginī (presiding deity) of the kula

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. yoginī is the head and kula stands to it in the genitive: 'the yoginī of the kula', i.e. the one who presides over it and is joined (yoga) with it.

Analysis कुलस्य योगिनी कुलयोगिनी
kulasya yoginī kulayoginī

Significance Traditionally the kula is read as the group of cakras along the suṣumnā, over which She presides as yoginī.

96 अकुला akulā

She who has no family (She who is beyond kula)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound nañ-bahuvrīhi. The negative a- (from nañ) with kula: 'She who has no kula', i.e. no family or lineage and nothing that bounds Her as a group. The name describes Her, so kula takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis न विद्यते कुलम् यस्याः सा अकुला
na vidyate kulam yasyāḥ sā akulā

Significance Traditionally akula is the sahasrāra beyond the kula path of the suṣumnā, and also Śiva; She who is Kaulinī (94) is equally beyond all kula.

97 समयान्तस्था samayānta-sthā

She who abides within samaya

Sandhi समयान्तः = समय + अन्तः (samaya + antaḥ) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); अन्तस्था = अन्तर् + स्था (antar + sthā) — the final r of antar becomes visarga before a voiceless sound (Pāṇini 8.3.15), and a visarga before a sibilant followed by a voiceless consonant may be dropped (a vārttika on 8.3.36): antaḥ-sthā → antasthā

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (with samaya dependent on the indeclinable antar). As in name 93: sthā 'abiding' is the head, antar 'within' says where, and samaya stands to antar in the genitive: 'She who abides within samaya'.

Analysis समयस्य अन्तः तिष्ठति इति समयान्तस्था
samayasya antaḥ tiṣṭhati iti samayāntasthā

Significance Traditionally samaya is the inward worship of the Goddess in the cakras of one's own body, and also the equality (sāmya) of Śiva and Śakti; She abides within both.

Uncertain As with name 93, the division samaya-anta-sthā ('abiding at the end of samaya') is also possible.

98 समयाचारतत्परा samayācāra-tatparā

She who is devoted to the Samaya mode of worship

Sandhi समयाचार = समय + आचार (samaya + ācāra) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound saptamī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya; tatparā is itself a bahuvrīhi). (1) samaya-ācāra 'the Samaya mode of worship' (karmadhāraya). (2) tat-parā 'devoted, intent', literally 'having that as the highest' (a lexicalised bahuvrīhi). (3) The Samaya practice stands to tatparā in the locative (saptamī-tatpuruṣa): 'intent upon the Samaya practice'.

Analysis समयः आचारः समयाचारः; तत् परम् यस्याः सा तत्परा; समयाचारे तत्परा समयाचारतत्परा
samayaḥ ācāraḥ samayācāraḥ; tat param yasyāḥ sā tatparā; samayācāre tatparā samayācāratatparā

Significance Traditionally Samayācāra is the inward worship of the Goddess in the cakras, beginning at the mūlādhāra, which the next names describe; external ritual is not its means.

Śloka 38names 99–102

मूलाधारैकनिलया ब्रह्मग्रन्थिविभेदिनी ।
मणिपूरान्तरुदिता विष्णुग्रन्थिविभेदिनी ॥ ३८ ॥

mūlādhāraikanilayā brahmagranthivibhedinī |
maṇipūrāntaruditā viṣṇugranthivibhedinī || 38 ||

101She who rises within the maṇipūra cakra; 102She who pierces the knot of Viṣṇu.

Where the names meet

Names 99–104 trace kuṇḍalinī's ascent in order: mūlādhāra, the knot of Brahmā, maṇipūra, the knot of Viṣṇu, ājñā, the knot of Rudra. Name 101 is maṇipūra-antar-uditā; maṇipūra is one cakra name.

The names

99 मूलाधारैकनिलया mūlādhāraika-nilayā

She whose principal abode is the mūlādhāra

Sandhi मूलाधार = मूल + आधार (mūla + ādhāra) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ), inside the lexicalised compound mūlādhāra; आधारैक = आधार + एक (ādhāra + eka) — vṛddhi: a + e → ai (Pāṇini 6.1.88 vṛddhir eci)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) mūla-ādhāra 'the root support', the lowest cakra (karmadhāraya). (2) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose one (principal) abode is the mūlādhāra'; eka qualifies nilaya and nilaya takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis मूलम् आधारः मूलाधारः; मूलाधारः एव एकः निलयः यस्याः सा मूलाधारैकनिलया
mūlam ādhāraḥ mūlādhāraḥ; mūlādhāraḥ eva ekaḥ nilayaḥ yasyāḥ sā mūlādhāraikanilayā

Significance As kuṇḍalinī She lies coiled in the mūlādhāra; the following names trace Her ascent through the three knots (granthis) to the sahasrāra.

100 ब्रह्मग्रन्थिविभेदिनी brahma-granthi-vibhedinī

She who pierces the knot of Brahmā

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) brahma-granthi 'the knot of Brahmā' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) The head vibhedinī 'piercing, breaking through' (vi + √bhid + -in, feminine) takes it as object (upapada-tatpuruṣa).

Analysis ब्रह्मणः ग्रन्थिः ब्रह्मग्रन्थिः; ब्रह्मग्रन्थिम् विभिनत्ति इति ब्रह्मग्रन्थिविभेदिनी
brahmaṇaḥ granthiḥ brahmagranthiḥ; brahmagranthim vibhinatti iti brahmagranthivibhedinī

Significance The brahmagranthi is the first of the three knots that bar kuṇḍalinī's path; rising from the mūlādhāra She pierces it before appearing in the maṇipūra (101).

101 मणिपूरान्तरुदिता maṇipūrāntar-uditā

She who rises within the maṇipūra cakra

Sandhi पूरान्तर् = पूर + अन्तर् (pūra + antar) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound tatpuruṣa (maṇipūra dependent on the indeclinable antar, which qualifies the participle). uditā 'risen, appeared' is the head; antar 'within' qualifies it, and maṇipūra stands to antar in the genitive: 'risen within the maṇipūra'. The r of antar simply runs into the vowel of uditā.

Analysis मणिपूरस्य अन्तः उदिता मणिपूरान्तरुदिता
maṇipūrasya antaḥ uditā maṇipūrāntaruditā

Significance Having pierced the brahmagranthi, kuṇḍalinī becomes manifest in the maṇipūra at the navel, before the knot of Viṣṇu (102).

102 विष्णुग्रन्थिविभेदिनी viṣṇu-granthi-vibhedinī

She who pierces the knot of Viṣṇu

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). As in name 100: viṣṇu-granthi 'the knot of Viṣṇu' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa) is the object of vibhedinī 'piercing' (upapada-tatpuruṣa).

Analysis विष्णोः ग्रन्थिः विष्णुग्रन्थिः; विष्णुग्रन्थिम् विभिनत्ति इति विष्णुग्रन्थिविभेदिनी
viṣṇoḥ granthiḥ viṣṇugranthiḥ; viṣṇugranthim vibhinatti iti viṣṇugranthivibhedinī

Significance The viṣṇugranthi, above the maṇipūra, is the second of the three knots on kuṇḍalinī's path.

Śloka 39names 103–106

आज्ञाचक्रान्तरालस्था रुद्रग्रन्थिविभेदिनी ।
सहस्राराम्बुजारूढा सुधासाराभिवर्षिणी ॥ ३९ ॥

ājñācakrāntarālasthā rudragranthivibhedinī |
sahasrārāmbujārūḍhā sudhāsārābhivarṣiṇī || 39 ||

105सहस्राराम्बुजारूढाsahasrārāmbujārūḍhā106सुधासाराभिवर्षिणीsudhāsārābhivarṣiṇī

Where the names meet

Name 106: sudhāsāra is best divided sudhā + āsāra 'downpour of nectar'.

The names

103 आज्ञाचक्रान्तरालस्था ājñā-cakrāntarāla-sthā

She who abides within the ājñā cakra

Sandhi चक्रान्तराल = चक्र + अन्तराल (cakra + antarāla) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) ājñā-cakra 'the cakra called ājñā' (karmadhāraya of name). (2) …cakra-antarāla 'the interior of that cakra' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) sthā 'abiding' is the head, with the interior in the locative (upapada-tatpuruṣa).

Analysis आज्ञा इति चक्रम् आज्ञाचक्रम्; आज्ञाचक्रस्य अन्तरालम् आज्ञाचक्रान्तरालम्; आज्ञाचक्रान्तराले तिष्ठति इति आज्ञाचक्रान्तरालस्था
ājñā iti cakram ājñācakram; ājñācakrasya antarālam ājñācakrāntarālam; ājñācakrāntarāle tiṣṭhati iti ājñācakrāntarālasthā

Significance The ājñā cakra between the eyebrows is the seat of the guru's command; there kuṇḍalinī meets the last knot, of Rudra (104).

104 रुद्रग्रन्थिविभेदिनी rudra-granthi-vibhedinī

She who pierces the knot of Rudra

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). As in names 100 and 102: rudra-granthi 'the knot of Rudra' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa) is the object of vibhedinī 'piercing' (upapada-tatpuruṣa).

Analysis रुद्रस्य ग्रन्थिः रुद्रग्रन्थिः; रुद्रग्रन्थिम् विभिनत्ति इति रुद्रग्रन्थिविभेदिनी
rudrasya granthiḥ rudragranthiḥ; rudragranthim vibhinatti iti rudragranthivibhedinī

Significance The rudragranthi at the ājñā is the last of the three knots; once it is pierced, the way to the sahasrāra (105) is open.

105 सहस्राराम्बुजारूढा sahasrārāmbujārūḍhā

She who ascends to the thousand-petaled lotus

Sandhi सहस्रार = सहस्र + अर (sahasra + ara) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ), inside the lexicalised compound sahasrāra; सहस्राराम्बुज = सहस्रार + अम्बुज (sahasrāra + ambuja) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); अम्बुजारूढा = अम्बुज + आरूढा (ambuja + ārūḍhā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound dvitīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner bahuvrīhi and karmadhāraya). (1) sahasra-ara 'thousand-spoked, thousand-petalled' (bahuvrīhi). (2) It qualifies ambuja 'lotus' (karmadhāraya). (3) The head ārūḍhā 'having mounted' takes the lotus as its object in the accusative (dvitīyā-tatpuruṣa).

Analysis सहस्रम् अराः यस्य तत् सहस्रारम्; सहस्रारम् अम्बुजम् सहस्राराम्बुजम्; सहस्राराम्बुजम् आरूढा सहस्राराम्बुजारूढा
sahasram arāḥ yasya tat sahasrāram; sahasrāram ambujam sahasrārāmbujam; sahasrārāmbujam ārūḍhā sahasrārāmbujārūḍhā

Significance The sahasrāra at the crown is Śiva's abode; kuṇḍalinī's ascent ends there in their union.

106 सुधासाराभिवर्षिणी sudhāsārābhivarṣiṇī

She who pours down streams of nectar

Sandhi सुधासार = सुधा + आसार (sudhā + āsāra) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); the second member is āsāra 'downpour', its ā absorbed into sudhā's; आसाराभि = आसार + अभि (āsāra + abhi) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) sudhā-āsāra 'a downpour of nectar' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) The head abhivarṣiṇī 'raining down upon' (abhi + √vṛṣ + -in, feminine) takes it as object (upapada-tatpuruṣa).

Analysis सुधायाः आसारः सुधासारः; सुधासारम् अभिवर्षति इति सुधासाराभिवर्षिणी
sudhāyāḥ āsāraḥ sudhāsāraḥ; sudhāsāram abhivarṣati iti sudhāsārābhivarṣiṇī

Significance Traditionally, when kuṇḍalinī unites with Śiva in the sahasrāra, nectar flows down from the moon there and drenches the whole subtle body.

Uncertain sudhā-sāra 'the essence of nectar' is also a possible division; 'downpour' suits abhivarṣiṇī 'raining down' and is followed here.

Śloka 40names 107–111

तडिल्लतासमरुचिः षट्चक्रोपरिसंस्थिता ।
महासक्तिः कुण्डलिनी बिसतन्तुतनीयसी ॥ ४० ॥

taḍillatāsamaruciḥ ṣaṭcakroparisaṃsthitā |
mahāsaktiḥ kuṇḍalinī bisatantutanīyasī || 40 ||

The names, separated

107तडिल्लता-सम-रुचिःtaḍillatā-sama-ruciḥ108षट्-चक्रोपरि-संस्थिताṣaṭ-cakropari-saṃsthitā

109महासक्तिःmahāsaktiḥ110कुण्डलिनीkuṇḍalinī111बिस-तन्तु-तनीयसीbisa-tantu-tanīyasī

Translation

107She whose radiance equals a streak of lightning; 108She who abides above the six cakras;

109She who is devoted to the festival (of the union of Śiva and Śakti); 110She who is coiled (the kuṇḍalinī); 111She who is more slender than the fiber of a lotus stalk.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish
107 तडिल्लतासमरुचिः taḍillatā-sama-ruciḥ
तडित्taḍitlightning
लताlatācreeper; with taḍit, a streak of lightning
समsamaequal, like
रुचिःruciḥradiance, lusterfeminine i-stem; nominative
108 षट्चक्रोपरिसंस्थिता ṣaṭ-cakropari-saṃsthitā
षष्ṣaṣsixappears as ṣaṭ-
चक्रcakracakra
उपरिupariaboveindeclinable
संस्थिताsaṃsthitāestablished, abidingsam + √sthā, past participle, feminine
109 महासक्तिः mahāsaktiḥ
महmahafestival, celebration
आसक्तिःāsaktiḥattachment, devotionā + √sañj "to cling", feminine i-stem; nominative
110 कुण्डलिनी kuṇḍalinī
कुण्डलिनीkuṇḍalinīcoiled; She who has coilskuṇḍala "coil, ring" + the possessive -in, feminine -inī
111 बिसतन्तुतनीयसी bisa-tantu-tanīyasī
बिसbisalotus stalk
तन्तुtantuthread, fiber
तनीयसीtanīyasīmore slender, finercomparative of tanu "thin" with -īyas (the final u drops), feminine -īyasī

Where the names meet

Name 109 is read महासक्तिः with dental s (maha 'festival' + āsakti 'attachment'); many printed editions have महाशक्तिः 'the great power'. Name 107 is also found as taṭillatā.

The names

107 तडिल्लतासमरुचिः taḍillatā-sama-ruciḥ

She whose radiance equals a streak of lightning

Sandhi तडिल्लता = तडित् + लता (taḍit + latā) — t becomes l before l (Pāṇini 8.4.60 tor li), inside the compound taḍillatā

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner rūpaka-karmadhāraya and a tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (1) taḍit-latā 'the lightning-creeper', a streak of lightning (rūpaka-karmadhāraya: the lightning is the creeper). (2) …latā-sama 'equal to it' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa with sama). (3) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose radiance equals a streak of lightning'. ruci is a feminine i-stem, so the name ends in -iḥ; samā takes its masculine stem sama- inside the compound.

Analysis तडित् एव लता तडिल्लता; तडिल्लतया समा तडिल्लतासमा; तडिल्लतासमा रुचिः यस्याः सा तडिल्लतासमरुचिः
taḍit eva latā taḍillatā; taḍillatayā samā taḍillatāsamā; taḍillatāsamā ruciḥ yasyāḥ sā taḍillatāsamaruciḥ

Significance Traditionally kuṇḍalinī rising through the suṣumnā is seen as a thin streak of lightning: brilliant, swift and subtle.

Variants Some copies read तटिल्लता (taṭillatā); taḍit and taṭit both mean lightning (see corrections.json, variants).

108 षट्चक्रोपरिसंस्थिता ṣaṭ-cakropari-saṃsthitā

She who abides above the six cakras

Sandhi षट्चक्र = षष् + चक्र (ṣaṣ + cakra) — the final ṣ of ṣaṣ becomes ḍ at the end of a member (jaśtva, Pāṇini 8.2.39) and then ṭ before the voiceless c (cartva, 8.4.55 khari ca); चक्रोपरि = चक्र + उपरि (cakra + upari) — guṇa: a + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ); संस्थिता = सम् + स्थिता (sam + sthitā) — m becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ); before a sibilant it stays anusvāra: sam → saṃ

Compound saptamī-tatpuruṣa in sense (over a dvigu and the indeclinable upari). (1) ṣaṭ-cakra 'the six cakras' (a numeral compound, dvigu, before a further member). (2) …cakra-upari 'above the six cakras' (the indeclinable upari with the cakras in the genitive). (3) The head saṃsthitā 'established, abiding' is qualified by that place.

Analysis षट् चक्राणि षट्चक्राणि; षट्चक्राणाम् उपरि षट्चक्रोपरि; षट्चक्रोपरि संस्थिता षट्चक्रोपरिसंस्थिता
ṣaṭ cakrāṇi ṣaṭcakrāṇi; ṣaṭcakrāṇām upari ṣaṭcakropari; ṣaṭcakropari saṃsthitā ṣaṭcakroparisaṃsthitā

Significance The six cakras are mūlādhāra, svādhiṣṭhāna, maṇipūra, anāhata, viśuddhi and ājñā; She abides above them in the sahasrāra.

109 महासक्तिः mahāsaktiḥ

She who is devoted to the festival (of the union of Śiva and Śakti)

Sandhi महासक्ति = मह + आसक्ति (maha + āsakti) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); the second member is āsakti 'attachment', its ā absorbed into maha

Compound vyadhikaraṇa-bahuvrīhi (members in different cases). maha 'festival' and āsakti 'attachment' are in different cases (the festival in the locative), as in cakrapāṇi 'whose discus is in his hand': 'She whose attachment is to the festival'. āsakti is a feminine i-stem, so the name ends in -iḥ.

Analysis महे आसक्तिः यस्याः सा महासक्तिः
mahe āsaktiḥ yasyāḥ sā mahāsaktiḥ

Significance Traditionally the 'festival' (maha) is the union of Śiva and Śakti in the sahasrāra, to which kuṇḍalinī is drawn; read with a dental s, the name does not mean 'great power'.

Uncertain The division mahā + sakti 'great attachment' is also possible; maha 'festival' + āsakti 'attachment' is followed here because it explains the festive union of the traditional gloss.

Variants Many printed editions read महाशक्तिः (mahāśaktiḥ, 'the great power'); this edition follows the reading with dental s, महासक्तिः.

110 कुण्डलिनी kuṇḍalinī

She who is coiled (the kuṇḍalinī)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Kuṇḍalinī lies coiled, traditionally three and a half times, in the mūlādhāra; Her rising through the cakras is the subject of names 99–111.

111 बिसतन्तुतनीयसी bisa-tantu-tanīyasī

She who is more slender than the fiber of a lotus stalk

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound pañcamī-tatpuruṣa (ablative of comparison, over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) bisa-tantu 'the fiber of a lotus stalk' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) The head tanīyasī 'more slender' is a comparative, and the thing compared stands in the ablative: 'more slender than a lotus fiber'.

Analysis बिसस्य तन्तुः बिसतन्तुः; बिसतन्तोः तनीयसी बिसतन्तुतनीयसी
bisasya tantuḥ bisatantuḥ; bisatantoḥ tanīyasī bisatantutanīyasī

Significance Kuṇḍalinī in the suṣumnā is traditionally pictured as finer than a lotus fiber, so subtle that only inner sight perceives Her.

Śloka 41names 112–117

भवानी भावनागम्या भवारण्यकुठारिका ।
भद्रप्रिया भद्रमूर्तिर् भक्तसौभाग्यदायिनी ॥ ४१ ॥

bhavānī bhāvanāgamyā bhavāraṇyakuṭhārikā |
bhadrapriyā bhadramūrtir bhaktasaubhāgyadāyinī || 41 ||

The names, separated ° form as a name on its own; in the recitation above it joins its neighbour

112भवानीbhavānī113भावना-गम्याbhāvanā-gamyā114भवारण्य-कुठारिकाbhavāraṇya-kuṭhārikā

115भद्र-प्रियाbhadra-priyā116भद्र-मूर्तिः°bhadra-mūrtiḥ117भक्त-सौभाग्य-दायिनीbhakta-saubhāgya-dāyinī

Translation

112She who is the consort of Bhava (Śiva); 113She who is attained through contemplation (bhāvanā); 114She who is the axe that clears the forest of worldly existence (saṃsāra);

115She who is fond of all that is auspicious; 116She who is the embodiment of auspiciousness or benevolence; 117She who bestows good fortune (saubhāgya) on Her devotees.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish
112 भवानी bhavānī
भवानीbhavānīthe consort of Bhava (Śiva)bhava + the feminine suffix -ī with the augment ān (Pāṇini 4.1.49 indravaruṇabhavaśarvarudra…)
113 भावनागम्या bhāvanā-gamyā
भावनाbhāvanācontemplation, meditative realizationfrom the causative of √bhū "to become": "causing to become"
गम्याgamyāto be reached, attainable√gam "to go" + the gerundive suffix -ya, feminine
114 भवारण्यकुठारिका bhavāraṇya-kuṭhārikā
भवbhavabecoming, worldly existence (saṃsāra)
अरण्यaraṇyaforest, wilderness
कुठारिकाkuṭhārikāaxekuṭhāra "axe" + -ka, feminine -ikā
115 भद्रप्रिया bhadra-priyā
भद्रbhadraauspicious, good, blessed
प्रियाpriyādear, beloved; fond ofpriya, with the feminine -ā
116 भद्रमूर्तिः bhadra-mūrtiḥ
भद्रbhadraauspicious, gracious, benevolent
मूर्तिःmūrtiḥform, embodimentfeminine i-stem; nominative
117 भक्तसौभाग्यदायिनी bhakta-saubhāgya-dāyinī
भक्तbhaktadevotee
सौभाग्यsaubhāgyagood fortune, blessedness; the auspicious state of a married womanfrom subhaga "fortunate", with vṛddhi
दायिनीdāyinīgiving, bestowing√dā "to give" + -in, with y inserted before the suffix (Pāṇini 7.3.33 āto yuk ciṇkṛtoḥ); feminine

Where the names meet

भद्रमूर्तिर्भक्त = भद्रमूर्तिः + भक्त… (bhadramūrtiḥ + bhakta…) — visarga sandhi: final s becomes ru (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ), which after i stays r before a voiced sound (it becomes visarga only before a voiceless sound or a pause, 8.3.15)

Name 113 can be divided bhāvanā-gamyā 'attainable through contemplation' or bhāvanā-agamyā 'unattainable by imagining'; the letters are the same. Names 112–125 turn to Her as Śiva's consort and to devotion.

The names

112 भवानी bhavānī

She who is the consort of Bhava (Śiva)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Bhava, 'existence', is Śiva as the one from whom all becoming arises; as Bhavānī She is the power that gives that existence life.

113 भावनागम्या bhāvanā-gamyā

She who is attained through contemplation (bhāvanā)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa. gamyā 'to be reached, attainable' (√gam + the gerundive -ya, feminine) is the head, and bhāvanā 'contemplation' stands to it in the instrumental: 'attainable through contemplation'. The text can also be divided bhāvanā + agamyā, with the a of agamyā absorbed into the long ā (savarṇa-dīrgha): 'unattainable by mere imagining'.

Analysis भावनया गम्या भावनागम्या
bhāvanayā gamyā bhāvanāgamyā

Significance In Śrīvidyā bhāvanā is the inner contemplation in which the worshipper realizes body and mind as the Śrīcakra and the Goddess, as taught in the Bhāvanopaniṣad; She is reached through it.

Uncertain Both divisions are traditional: bhāvanā-gamyā 'attainable through contemplation' and bhāvanā-agamyā 'unattainable through (mere) imagination'. The Devanagari is the same either way.

114 भवारण्यकुठारिका bhavāraṇya-kuṭhārikā

She who is the axe that clears the forest of worldly existence (saṃsāra)

Sandhi भवारण्य = भव + अरण्य (bhava + araṇya) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner rūpaka-karmadhāraya). (1) bhava-araṇya 'the forest that is worldly existence' (rūpaka-karmadhāraya: existence is identified with a forest). (2) The head kuṭhārikā 'axe' takes that forest in the genitive: 'the axe of (for) the forest of existence'. The name identifies Her with the axe.

Analysis भवः एव अरण्यम् भवारण्यम्; भवारण्यस्य कुठारिका भवारण्यकुठारिका
bhavaḥ eva araṇyam bhavāraṇyam; bhavāraṇyasya kuṭhārikā bhavāraṇyakuṭhārikā

Significance Saṃsāra is a pathless forest of births and deaths; She cuts it down at the root, which is ignorance.

115 भद्रप्रिया bhadra-priyā

She who is fond of all that is auspicious

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. 'She to whom what is auspicious (bhadra) is dear (priya)': priya is the predicate of the bahuvrīhi and takes the feminine -ā. A ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa 'dear to the auspicious ones (the good)' is also possible.

Analysis भद्रम् प्रियम् यस्याः सा भद्रप्रिया
bhadram priyam yasyāḥ sā bhadrapriyā

Significance Traditionally what is auspicious is dear to Her, and She grants it to those who seek Her, so the name also implies that She gives what is good.

116 भद्रमूर्तिः bhadra-mūrtiḥ

She who is the embodiment of auspiciousness or benevolence

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. 'She whose form (mūrti) is auspicious (bhadra)'. bhadrā takes its masculine stem bhadra- inside the compound, and mūrti is a feminine i-stem, so the name ends in -iḥ. It can also be taken as a karmadhāraya, 'auspiciousness in embodied form'.

Analysis भद्रा मूर्तिः यस्याः सा भद्रमूर्तिः
bhadrā mūrtiḥ yasyāḥ sā bhadramūrtiḥ

Significance Her very form is auspicious, so to see or meditate on Her is itself a blessing.

117 भक्तसौभाग्यदायिनी bhakta-saubhāgya-dāyinī

She who bestows good fortune (saubhāgya) on Her devotees

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) bhakta-saubhāgya 'the good fortune of devotees' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) The head dāyinī 'giving' takes it as object (upapada-tatpuruṣa).

Analysis भक्तानाम् सौभाग्यम् भक्तसौभाग्यम्; भक्तसौभाग्यम् ददाति इति भक्तसौभाग्यदायिनी
bhaktānām saubhāgyam bhaktasaubhāgyam; bhaktasaubhāgyam dadāti iti bhaktasaubhāgyadāyinī

Significance Saubhāgya, 'blessedness', is the characteristic gift of Lalitā; Bhāskararāya's commentary is itself named Saubhāgyabhāskara.

Śloka 42names 118–125

भक्तिप्रिया भक्तिगम्या भक्तिवश्या भयापहा ।
शाम्भवी शारदाराध्या शर्वाणी शर्मदायिनी ॥ ४२ ॥

bhaktipriyā bhaktigamyā bhaktivaśyā bhayāpahā |
śāmbhavī śāradārādhyā śarvāṇī śarmadāyinī || 42 ||

The names, separated

122She who is the consort of Śambhu (Śiva); 123She who is worshipped by Śāradā (Sarasvatī, the goddess of speech); 124She who is the consort of Śarva (Śiva); 125She who confers happiness.

Where the names meet

Bhavānī (112), Śāmbhavī (122), Śarvāṇī (124) and Śāṅkarī (126) are each formed from a name of Śiva: Bhava, Śambhu, Śarva, Śaṅkara.

The names

118 भक्तिप्रिया bhakti-priyā

She who is fond of (and pleased by) devotion

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. 'She to whom devotion (bhakti) is dear (priya)'; priya takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis भक्तिः प्रिया यस्याः सा भक्तिप्रिया
bhaktiḥ priyā yasyāḥ sā bhaktipriyā

Significance Names 118–120 form a group: devotion pleases Her, devotion reaches Her, and devotion wins Her.

119 भक्तिगम्या bhakti-gamyā

She who is attained through devotion

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa. gamyā 'attainable' is the head and bhakti stands to it in the instrumental: 'attainable through devotion'.

Analysis भक्त्या गम्या भक्तिगम्या
bhaktyā gamyā bhaktigamyā

Significance Traditionally devotion is the surest way to Her, as the Bhagavad Gītā says of the Lord: He is reached by undivided devotion.

120 भक्तिवश्या bhakti-vaśyā

She who is won over by devotion

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa. vaśyā 'to be brought under control, won over' is the head and bhakti stands to it in the instrumental: 'won over by devotion'.

Analysis भक्त्या वश्या भक्तिवश्या
bhaktyā vaśyā bhaktivaśyā

Significance The Mother who rules all worlds lets Herself be ruled by Her devotees' love.

121 भयापहा bhayāpahā

She who dispels fear

Sandhi भयापहा = भय + अपहा (bhaya + apahā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. apahā 'removing, driving away' (apa + √han 'strike', as an agent at the end of a compound) is the head, and bhaya 'fear' is its object.

Analysis भयम् अपहन्ति इति भयापहा
bhayam apahanti iti bhayāpahā

Significance Above all She dispels the fear of saṃsāra, the root of every other fear.

122 शाम्भवी śāmbhavī

She who is the consort of Śambhu (Śiva)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Śāmbhavī is also the name of an initiation (śāmbhavī dīkṣā) and a yogic gaze (śāmbhavī mudrā); traditionally She is all three.

123 शारदाराध्या śāradārādhyā

She who is worshipped by Śāradā (Sarasvatī, the goddess of speech)

Sandhi शारदाराध्या = शारदा + आराध्या (śāradā + ārādhyā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa. ārādhyā 'to be worshipped' (ā + √rādh + the gerundive -ya, feminine) is the head, and Śāradā, the agent of the worship, stands in the instrumental: 'worshipped by Śāradā'.

Analysis शारदया आराध्या शारदाराध्या
śāradayā ārādhyā śāradārādhyā

Significance Even Sarasvatī, the goddess of speech and learning, worships Her; so do all who seek knowledge.

124 शर्वाणी śarvāṇī

She who is the consort of Śarva (Śiva)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Śarva is Śiva as the archer who destroys; Śarvāṇī is His inseparable power.

125 शर्मदायिनी śarma-dāyinī

She who confers happiness

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. dāyinī 'giving' is the head, and śarman 'happiness, shelter' is its object.

Analysis शर्म ददाति इति शर्मदायिनी
śarma dadāti iti śarmadāyinī

Significance Śarman is happiness that is also shelter: She gives the peace of being protected.

Śloka 43names 126–133

शाङ्करी श्रीकरी साध्वी शरच्चन्द्रनिभानना ।
शातोदरी शान्तिमती निराधारा निरञ्जना ॥ ४३ ॥

śāṅkarī śrīkarī sādhvī śaraccandranibhānanā |
śātodarī śāntimatī nirādhārā nirañjanā || 43 ||

The names, separated

126शाङ्करीśāṅkarī127श्री-करीśrī-karī128साध्वीsādhvī129शरच्चन्द्र-निभाननाśaraccandra-nibhānanā

130शातोदरीśātodarī131शान्ति-मतीśānti-matī132निर्-आधाराnir-ādhārā133निर्-अञ्जनाnir-añjanā

Translation

126She who is the consort of Śaṅkara (Śiva); 127She who brings about prosperity (śrī); 128She who is chaste; 129She whose face is like the autumn moon;

130She who is slender-waisted; 131She who is peaceful; 132She who is without support (resting on nothing); 133She who is without stain.

Where the names meet

Name 128 sādhvī is one name here; at 711–712 Bhāskararāya divides the same word into sādhu + ī. With nirādhārā (132) begins the long series of names of the attributeless Brahman, mostly built on nis 'without' (to 187).

The names

126 शाङ्करी śāṅkarī

She who is the consort of Śaṅkara (Śiva)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Śaṅkara means 'the maker of welfare' (śam karoti), so as His consort She too brings about happiness, which is the sense the previous meaning gave.

127 श्रीकरी śrī-karī

She who brings about prosperity (śrī)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. karī 'making, bringing about' (√kṛ + the agent suffix -a, feminine -ī) is the head, and śrī 'prosperity' is its object.

Analysis श्रियम् करोति इति श्रीकरी
śriyam karoti iti śrīkarī

Significance Śrī is every kind of wealth, outer and inner; She is its source, and Śrī (Lakṣmī) herself is Her form.

128 साध्वी sādhvī

She who is chaste

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance She is wholly faithful to Śiva and never separate from Him. Here sādhvī is one name; at names 711–712 Bhāskararāya divides the same word into sādhu and ī.

129 शरच्चन्द्रनिभानना śaraccandra-nibhānanā

She whose face is like the autumn moon

Sandhi शरच्चन्द्र = शरद् + चन्द्र (śarad + candra) — d becomes t before a voiceless sound (cartva, Pāṇini 8.4.55 khari ca), then c beside the palatal c (ścutva, 8.4.40 stoḥ ścunā ścuḥ); निभानना = निभ + आनना (nibha + ānanā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and a tatpuruṣa with nibha). (1) śarat-candra 'the autumn moon' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) …candra-nibha 'resembling that moon' (nibha 'like' at the end of a compound). (3) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose face (ānana) is like the autumn moon'; ānana takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis शरदः चन्द्रः शरच्चन्द्रः; शरच्चन्द्रेण निभम् शरच्चन्द्रनिभम्; शरच्चन्द्रनिभम् आननम् यस्याः सा शरच्चन्द्रनिभानना
śaradaḥ candraḥ śaraccandraḥ; śaraccandreṇa nibham śaraccandranibham; śaraccandranibham ānanam yasyāḥ sā śaraccandranibhānanā

Significance The autumn moon, shining in a sky cleared by the rains, is the poets' image of a calm, radiant face.

130 शातोदरी śātodarī

She who is slender-waisted

Sandhi शातोदरी = शात + उदरी (śāta + udarī) — guṇa: a + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi. 'She whose waist (udara) is slender (śāta)'. A bahuvrīhi ending in udara may take the feminine -ī (Pāṇini 4.1.55), hence śātodarī rather than śātodarā.

Analysis शातम् उदरम् यस्याः सा शातोदरी
śātam udaram yasyāḥ sā śātodarī

Significance A slender waist is a classical mark of beauty; it recalls the description of Her form in the earlier names.

131 शान्तिमती śānti-matī

She who is peaceful

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Her peace is not the absence of activity but the stillness from which all activity arises.

132 निराधारा nir-ādhārā

She who is without support (resting on nothing)

Sandhi निराधारा = निस् + आधारा (nis + ādhārā) — the final s of the prefix nis becomes r before a vowel or a voiced consonant (s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ; ru turns to visarga only before a voiceless sound or a pause, 8.3.15): nis → nir

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom support has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without support'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending.

Analysis निर्गतः आधारः यस्याः सा निराधारा
nirgataḥ ādhāraḥ yasyāḥ sā nirādhārā

Significance She is the support (ādhāra) of everything and herself rests on nothing. With name 132 begins the long series of names of the attributeless (nirguṇa) Brahman, most built with nis 'without'.

133 निरञ्जना nir-añjanā

She who is without stain

Sandhi निरञ्जना = निस् + अञ्जना (nis + añjanā) — the final s of the prefix nis becomes r before a vowel or a voiced consonant (s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ; ru turns to visarga only before a voiceless sound or a pause, 8.3.15): nis → nir

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom añjana (stain) has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without añjana (stain)'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending.

Analysis निर्गतम् अञ्जनम् यस्याः सा निरञ्जना
nirgatam añjanam yasyāḥ sā nirañjanā

Significance Añjana is the black collyrium of the eyes, and traditionally stands for the darkening stain of ignorance (avidyā), which never touches Her.

Śloka 44names 134–143

निर्लेपा निर्मला नित्या निराकारा निराकुला ।
निर्गुणा निष्कला शान्ता निष्कामा निरुपप्लवा ॥ ४४ ॥

nirlepā nirmalā nityā nirākārā nirākulā |
nirguṇā niṣkalā śāntā niṣkāmā nirupaplavā || 44 ||

The names, separated

134निर्-लेपाnir-lepā135निर्-मलाnir-malā136नित्याnityā137निर्-आकाराnir-ākārā138निर्-आकुलाnir-ākulā

134She who is untainted (by the effects of action); 135She who is free from all impurities; 136She who is eternal; 137She who is without form; 138She who is without agitation;

139She who is without qualities, beyond the three guṇas (sattva, rajas and tamas); 140She who is without parts; 141She who is tranquil; 142She who is without desire; 143She who is free from all affliction and disturbance.

Where the names meet

The prefix nis takes its shape from the next sound: nir before vowels and voiced sounds (nirlepā), niṣ before k and p (niṣkalā); the meaning never changes. Name 137 is nirākārā with long ā (corrected).

The names

134 निर्लेपा nir-lepā

She who is untainted (by the effects of action)

Sandhi निर्लेपा = निस् + लेपा (nis + lepā) — the final s of the prefix nis becomes r before a vowel or a voiced consonant (s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ; ru turns to visarga only before a voiceless sound or a pause, 8.3.15): nis → nir

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom lepa (taint) has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without lepa (taint)'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending.

Analysis निर्गतः लेपः यस्याः सा निर्लेपा
nirgataḥ lepaḥ yasyāḥ sā nirlepā

Significance Lepa is the residue that action leaves on the doer; She acts through all beings yet nothing clings to Her.

135 निर्मला nir-malā

She who is free from all impurities

Sandhi निर्मला = निस् + मला (nis + malā) — the final s of the prefix nis becomes r before a vowel or a voiced consonant (s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ; ru turns to visarga only before a voiceless sound or a pause, 8.3.15): nis → nir

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom mala (impurity) has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without mala (impurity)'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending.

Analysis निर्गतः मलः यस्याः सा निर्मला
nirgataḥ malaḥ yasyāḥ sā nirmalā

Significance In the Śaiva and Śākta traditions the three impurities (malas) — the sense of limitation (āṇava), the veil of māyā (māyīya) and the residue of action (kārma) — bind the soul; She is free of all three.

136 नित्या nityā

She who is eternal

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance She is also the Nityās, the goddesses of the fifteen lunar days (Kāmeśvarī to Citrā), with Lalitā herself as the sixteenth, Mahānityā.

137 निराकारा nir-ākārā

She who is without form

Sandhi निराकारा = निस् + आकारा (nis + ākārā) — the final s of the prefix nis becomes r before a vowel or a voiced consonant (s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ; ru turns to visarga only before a voiceless sound or a pause, 8.3.15): nis → nir

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom ākāra (form) has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without ākāra (form)'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending.

Analysis निर्गतः आकारः यस्याः सा निराकारा
nirgataḥ ākāraḥ yasyāḥ sā nirākārā

Significance Beyond the forms She takes for Her devotees, She is in essence formless consciousness; the name balances the long description of Her form.

Corrected निराकरा → निराकारा. निराकरा → निराकारा (nir-ākārā, formless): ākāra "form" has a long ā; the verse text reads निराकारा.

138 निराकुला nir-ākulā

She who is without agitation

Sandhi निराकुला = निस् + आकुला (nis + ākulā) — the final s of the prefix nis becomes r before a vowel or a voiced consonant (s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ; ru turns to visarga only before a voiceless sound or a pause, 8.3.15): nis → nir

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom ākula (agitation) has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without ākula (agitation)'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending.

Analysis निर्गतम् आकुलम् यस्याः सा निराकुला
nirgatam ākulam yasyāḥ sā nirākulā

Significance No disturbance reaches Her, and those who take refuge in Her share that steadiness.

139 निर्गुणा nir-guṇā

She who is without qualities, beyond the three guṇas (sattva, rajas and tamas)

Sandhi निर्गुणा = निस् + गुणा (nis + guṇā) — the final s of the prefix nis becomes r before a vowel or a voiced consonant (s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ; ru turns to visarga only before a voiceless sound or a pause, 8.3.15): nis → nir

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom the guṇas has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without the guṇas'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending.

Analysis निर्गताः गुणाः यस्याः सा निर्गुणा
nirgatāḥ guṇāḥ yasyāḥ sā nirguṇā

Significance The guṇas are the strands of prakṛti; as Brahman without attributes She is beyond them, though as Māyā She wields them.

140 निष्कला niṣ-kalā

She who is without parts

Sandhi निष्कला = निस् + कला (nis + kalā) — the final s of nis becomes visarga before a voiceless sound (8.2.66, 8.3.15), and after i that visarga becomes ṣ before k or p (Pāṇini 8.3.41 idudupadhasya cāpratyayasya): nis → niṣ

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom parts (kalā) has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without parts (kalā)'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending.

Analysis निर्गताः कलाः यस्याः सा निष्कला
nirgatāḥ kalāḥ yasyāḥ sā niṣkalā

Significance What has parts can come apart; She is partless, undivided and indestructible.

141 शान्ता śāntā

She who is tranquil

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Her tranquility is that of Brahman, in which all movement has come to rest.

142 निष्कामा niṣ-kāmā

She who is without desire

Sandhi निष्कामा = निस् + कामा (nis + kāmā) — the final s of nis becomes visarga before a voiceless sound (8.2.66, 8.3.15), and after i that visarga becomes ṣ before k or p (Pāṇini 8.3.41 idudupadhasya cāpratyayasya): nis → niṣ

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom desire has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without desire'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending.

Analysis निर्गतः कामः यस्याः सा निष्कामा
nirgataḥ kāmaḥ yasyāḥ sā niṣkāmā

Significance Being complete, She lacks nothing to desire; Her creative will is play (līlā), not want.

143 निरुपप्लवा nir-upaplavā

She who is free from all affliction and disturbance

Sandhi निरुपप्लवा = निस् + उपप्लवा (nis + upaplavā) — the final s of the prefix nis becomes r before a vowel or a voiced consonant (s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ; ru turns to visarga only before a voiceless sound or a pause, 8.3.15): nis → nir

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom upaplava (affliction) has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without upaplava (affliction)'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending.

Analysis निर्गतः उपप्लवः यस्याः सा निरुपप्लवा
nirgataḥ upaplavaḥ yasyāḥ sā nirupaplavā

Significance Upaplava is any calamity that befalls a thing, even an eclipse of the moon; nothing can overtake Her, and so She is also called indestructible.

Śloka 45names 144–151

नित्यमुक्ता निर्विकारा निष्प्रपञ्चा निराश्रया ।
नित्यशुद्धा नित्यबुद्धा निरवद्या निरन्तरा ॥ ४५ ॥

nityamuktā nirvikārā niṣprapañcā nirāśrayā |
nityaśuddhā nityabuddhā niravadyā nirantarā || 45 ||

The names, separated

144नित्य-मुक्ताnitya-muktā145निर्-विकाराnir-vikārā146निष्-प्रपञ्चाniṣ-prapañcā147निर्-आश्रयाnir-āśrayā

148नित्य-शुद्धाnitya-śuddhā149नित्य-बुद्धाnitya-buddhā150निर्-अवद्याnir-avadyā151निर्-अन्तराnir-antarā

Where the names meet

Names 144, 148 and 149 (with nitya 'ever') recall the Vedāntic 'ever pure, awake and free'.

The names

144 नित्यमुक्ता nitya-muktā

She who is ever free from worldly bonds

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya (nitya used adverbially). muktā 'freed' (√muc, past participle, feminine) is the head, and nitya 'ever' qualifies it adverbially: 'ever free'.

Analysis नित्यम् मुक्ता नित्यमुक्ता
nityam muktā nityamuktā

Significance She was never bound and so is never freed: Her freedom is not an achievement but Her nature.

145 निर्विकारा nir-vikārā

She who is unchanging

Sandhi निर्विकारा = निस् + विकारा (nis + vikārā) — the final s of the prefix nis becomes r before a vowel or a voiced consonant (s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ; ru turns to visarga only before a voiceless sound or a pause, 8.3.15): nis → nir

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom change (vikāra) has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without change (vikāra)'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending.

Analysis निर्गतः विकारः यस्याः सा निर्विकारा
nirgataḥ vikāraḥ yasyāḥ sā nirvikārā

Significance All change belongs to the world She projects; She, its ground, is without modification.

146 निष्प्रपञ्चा niṣ-prapañcā

She who is beyond the phenomenal world

Sandhi निष्प्रपञ्चा = निस् + प्रपञ्चा (nis + prapañcā) — the final s of nis becomes visarga before a voiceless sound (8.2.66, 8.3.15), and after i that visarga becomes ṣ before k or p (Pāṇini 8.3.41 idudupadhasya cāpratyayasya): nis → niṣ

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom the manifold world (prapañca) has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without the manifold world (prapañca)'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending.

Analysis निर्गतः प्रपञ्चः यस्याः सा निष्प्रपञ्चा
nirgataḥ prapañcaḥ yasyāḥ sā niṣprapañcā

Significance Prapañca is the expansion of the one into the many; in Her own nature She is untouched by it, as the Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad describes the fourth state as the stilling of prapañca (prapañcopaśama).

147 निराश्रया nir-āśrayā

She who does not depend on anything

Sandhi निराश्रया = निस् + आश्रया (nis + āśrayā) — the final s of the prefix nis becomes r before a vowel or a voiced consonant (s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ; ru turns to visarga only before a voiceless sound or a pause, 8.3.15): nis → nir

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom āśraya (support) has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without āśraya (support)'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending.

Analysis निर्गतः आश्रयः यस्याः सा निराश्रया
nirgataḥ āśrayaḥ yasyāḥ sā nirāśrayā

Significance Everything depends on Her, and She depends on nothing.

148 नित्यशुद्धा nitya-śuddhā

She who is eternally pure

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya (nitya used adverbially). śuddhā 'pure' (√śudh, past participle, feminine) is the head, and nitya 'ever' qualifies it: 'ever pure'.

Analysis नित्यम् शुद्धा नित्यशुद्धा
nityam śuddhā nityaśuddhā

Significance Names 148–149 echo the Vedāntic description of the Self as nitya-śuddha-buddha-mukta, 'ever pure, awake and free' (with 144).

149 नित्यबुद्धा nitya-buddhā

She who is ever awake (eternally enlightened)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya (nitya used adverbially). buddhā 'awake, knowing' (√budh, past participle, feminine) is the head, and nitya 'ever' qualifies it: 'ever awake'.

Analysis नित्यम् बुद्धा नित्यबुद्धा
nityam buddhā nityabuddhā

Significance She is consciousness itself, never clouded by sleep or ignorance.

150 निरवद्या nir-avadyā

She who is blameless (and so praiseworthy)

Sandhi निरवद्या = निस् + अवद्या (nis + avadyā) — the final s of the prefix nis becomes r before a vowel or a voiced consonant (s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ; ru turns to visarga only before a voiceless sound or a pause, 8.3.15): nis → nir

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom avadya (blame) has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without avadya (blame)'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending.

Analysis निर्गतम् अवद्यम् यस्याः सा निरवद्या
nirgatam avadyam yasyāḥ sā niravadyā

Significance Avadya, literally 'not to be spoken of', is what deserves blame; nothing in Her deserves it.

151 निरन्तरा nir-antarā

She who is without any gap or interval (all-pervading)

Sandhi निरन्तरा = निस् + अन्तरा (nis + antarā) — the final s of the prefix nis becomes r before a vowel or a voiced consonant (s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ; ru turns to visarga only before a voiceless sound or a pause, 8.3.15): nis → nir

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom antara (gap, interval) has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without antara (gap, interval)'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending.

Analysis निर्गतम् अन्तरम् यस्याः सा निरन्तरा
nirgatam antaram yasyāḥ sā nirantarā

Significance Nothing separates Her from anything, in space, in time or in substance; She pervades all without interruption.

niṣkāraṇā niṣkalaṅkā nirupādhir nirīśvarā |

Where the names meet

निरुपाधिर्निरीश्वरा = निरुपाधिः + निरीश्वरा (nirupādhiḥ + nirīśvarā) — visarga sandhi: final s becomes ru (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ), which after i stays r before a voiced sound (it becomes visarga only before a voiceless sound or a pause, 8.3.15)

Name 156 is nī-rāgā (nis + rāga), not nīr + āgā. From here the names come in pairs, 'without X' and 'destroyer of X' (156–181); name 159 is mada-nāśinī, not madana + aśinī.

The names

152 निष्कारणा niṣ-kāraṇā

She who is without cause

Sandhi निष्कारणा = निस् + कारणा (nis + kāraṇā) — the final s of nis becomes visarga before a voiceless sound (8.2.66, 8.3.15), and after i that visarga becomes ṣ before k or p (Pāṇini 8.3.41 idudupadhasya cāpratyayasya): nis → niṣ

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom a cause has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without a cause'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending.

Analysis निर्गतम् कारणम् यस्याः सा निष्कारणा
nirgatam kāraṇam yasyāḥ sā niṣkāraṇā

Significance She is the cause of everything and has no cause herself.

153 निष्कलङ्का niṣ-kalaṅkā

She who is faultless

Sandhi निष्कलङ्का = निस् + कलङ्का (nis + kalaṅkā) — the final s of nis becomes visarga before a voiceless sound (8.2.66, 8.3.15), and after i that visarga becomes ṣ before k or p (Pāṇini 8.3.41 idudupadhasya cāpratyayasya): nis → niṣ

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom kalaṅka (stain) has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without kalaṅka (stain)'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending.

Analysis निर्गतः कलङ्कः यस्याः सा निष्कलङ्का
nirgataḥ kalaṅkaḥ yasyāḥ sā niṣkalaṅkā

Significance Unlike the moon, whose spot is its kalaṅka (cf. name 16), She is without any blemish.

154 निरुपाधिः nir-upādhiḥ

She who is free from all limiting adjuncts (upādhi)

Sandhi निरुपाधिः = निस् + उपाधिः (nis + upādhiḥ) — the final s of the prefix nis becomes r before a vowel or a voiced consonant (s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ; ru turns to visarga only before a voiceless sound or a pause, 8.3.15): nis → nir; उपाधि = उप + आधि (upa + ādhi) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ), inside the lexicalised word upādhi

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom upādhi (limiting adjunct) has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without upādhi (limiting adjunct)'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending. upādhi is a masculine i-stem; in the bahuvrīhi it keeps its i, so the feminine nominative is nirupādhiḥ, not -ā.

Analysis निर्गतः उपाधिः यस्याः सा निरुपाधिः
nirgataḥ upādhiḥ yasyāḥ sā nirupādhiḥ

Significance In Vedānta the upādhis — body, mind and the rest — make the one consciousness appear limited, as a jar seems to enclose space; She is free of them.

155 निरीश्वरा nir-īśvarā

She who has no superior or protector

Sandhi निरीश्वरा = निस् + ईश्वरा (nis + īśvarā) — the final s of the prefix nis becomes r before a vowel or a voiced consonant (s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ; ru turns to visarga only before a voiceless sound or a pause, 8.3.15): nis → nir

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom a lord (īśvara) has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without a lord (īśvara)'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending.

Analysis निर्गतः ईश्वरः यस्याः सा निरीश्वरा
nirgataḥ īśvaraḥ yasyāḥ sā nirīśvarā

Significance She is the supreme ruler; there is no lord over Her.

156 नीरागा nī-rāgā

She who is free from passion

Sandhi नीरागा = निस् + रागा (nis + rāgā) — the final s of nis becomes r (8.2.66); an r before r is dropped (Pāṇini 8.3.14 ro ri) and the vowel before it is lengthened (6.3.111 ḍhralope pūrvasya dīrgho 'ṇaḥ): nis + r → nī r

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom rāga (passion) has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without rāga (passion)'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending.

Analysis निर्गतः रागः यस्याः सा नीरागा
nirgataḥ rāgaḥ yasyāḥ sā nīrāgā

Significance Rāga, 'coloring', is the passion that colors the mind; from here the names come in pairs: She is free of a fault and destroys it in others (156–181).

157 रागमथनी rāga-mathanī

She who destroys desires (passions)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. mathanī 'crushing, churning up' (√math + the agent suffix -ana, feminine -ī) is the head and rāga 'passion' its object.

Analysis रागम् मथ्नाति इति रागमथनी
rāgam mathnāti iti rāgamathanī

Significance Free of passion herself (156), She crushes it in Her devotees.

158 निर्मदा nir-madā

She who is without pride

Sandhi निर्मदा = निस् + मदा (nis + madā) — the final s of the prefix nis becomes r before a vowel or a voiced consonant (s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ; ru turns to visarga only before a voiceless sound or a pause, 8.3.15): nis → nir

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom mada (pride) has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without mada (pride)'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending.

Analysis निर्गतः मदः यस्याः सा निर्मदा
nirgataḥ madaḥ yasyāḥ sā nirmadā

Significance Mada is the intoxication of pride; She, who has everything, has none.

159 मदनाशिनी mada-nāśinī

She who destroys pride

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. nāśinī 'destroying' (causative of √naś + -in, feminine) is the head and mada 'pride' its object. The division is mada-nāśinī; it is not madana 'Kāma' + aśinī.

Analysis मदम् नाशयति इति मदनाशिनी
madam nāśayati iti madanāśinī

Significance Free of pride (158), She destroys it in others.

Śloka 47names 160–167

निर्ममा ममताहन्त्री निष्पापा पापनाशिनी ॥ ४७ ॥

niścintā nirahaṅkārā nirmohā mohanāśinī |
nirmamā mamatāhantrī niṣpāpā pāpanāśinī || 47 ||
