Where the names meet

niścintā (160): the s of nis becomes ś before c.

The names

160 निश्चिन्ता niś-cintā

She who is free from anxiety

Sandhi निश्चिन्ता = निस् + चिन्ता (nis + cintā) — the final s of nis, by way of visarga, is restored as s before a voiceless stop (Pāṇini 8.3.34 visarjanīyasya saḥ) and becomes ś beside the palatal c (8.4.40 stoḥ ścunā ścuḥ): nis → niś

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom cintā (anxiety) has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without cintā (anxiety)'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending.

Analysis निर्गता चिन्ता यस्याः सा निश्चिन्ता
nirgatā cintā yasyāḥ sā niścintā

Significance Nothing is lacking or threatened in Her, so there is nothing to worry over.

161 निरहङ्कारा nir-ahaṅkārā

She who is without ego (ahaṅkāra, the sense of 'I')

Sandhi निरहङ्कारा = निस् + अहङ्कारा (nis + ahaṅkārā) — the final s of the prefix nis becomes r before a vowel or a voiced consonant (s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ; ru turns to visarga only before a voiceless sound or a pause, 8.3.15): nis → nir; अहङ्कार = अहम् + कार (aham + kāra) — m becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ), and the anusvāra takes the nasal of the following stop's class (8.4.58 anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ): aham → ahaṅ, inside the lexicalised compound ahaṅkāra

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom ahaṅkāra (ego) has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without ahaṅkāra (ego)'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending.

Analysis निर्गतः अहङ्कारः यस्याः सा निरहङ्कारा
nirgataḥ ahaṅkāraḥ yasyāḥ sā nirahaṅkārā

Significance Ahaṅkāra is the 'I-maker' that identifies with body and mind; She, the true Self, has no such false identification.

162 निर्मोहा nir-mohā

She who is free from delusion

Sandhi निर्मोहा = निस् + मोहा (nis + mohā) — the final s of the prefix nis becomes r before a vowel or a voiced consonant (s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ; ru turns to visarga only before a voiceless sound or a pause, 8.3.15): nis → nir

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom moha (delusion) has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without moha (delusion)'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending.

Analysis निर्गतः मोहः यस्याः सा निर्मोहा
nirgataḥ mohaḥ yasyāḥ sā nirmohā

Significance Moha mistakes the unreal for the real; She is pure knowledge.

163 मोहनाशिनी moha-nāśinī

She who destroys delusion

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. nāśinī 'destroying' is the head and moha 'delusion' its object.

Analysis मोहम् नाशयति इति मोहनाशिनी
moham nāśayati iti mohanāśinī

Significance Free of delusion (162), She destroys it in Her devotees.

164 निर्ममा nir-mamā

She who is free from the sense of 'mine'

Sandhi निर्ममा = निस् + ममा (nis + mamā) — the final s of the prefix nis becomes r before a vowel or a voiced consonant (s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ; ru turns to visarga only before a voiceless sound or a pause, 8.3.15): nis → nir

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom (the sense of) mine has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without the sense of mine'. Here mama, the genitive 'my, mine', is treated as a noun, 'the sense of mine'; as the name describes Her, it takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis निर्गतम् मम यस्याः सा निर्ममा
nirgatam mama yasyāḥ sā nirmamā

Significance Mamatā, 'mine-ness', is the possessive twin of ahaṅkāra (161); She owns all and claims nothing.

165 ममताहन्त्री mamatā-hantrī

She who destroys the sense of ownership

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. hantrī 'slayer' (√han + the agent suffix -tṛ, feminine -trī) is the head and mamatā 'the sense of mine' stands to it in the genitive. Classical grammar is wary of compounding a genitive with an agent noun in -tṛ (the sūtra tṛjakābhyāṃ kartari), but such compounds are common in the hymns.

Analysis ममतायाः हन्त्री ममताहन्त्री
mamatāyāḥ hantrī mamatāhantrī

Significance Free of 'mine' herself (164), She destroys possessiveness in Her devotees.

166 निष्पापा niṣ-pāpā

She who is without sin

Sandhi निष्पापा = निस् + पापा (nis + pāpā) — the final s of nis becomes visarga before a voiceless sound (8.2.66, 8.3.15), and after i that visarga becomes ṣ before k or p (Pāṇini 8.3.41 idudupadhasya cāpratyayasya): nis → niṣ

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom pāpa (sin) has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without pāpa (sin)'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending.

Analysis निर्गतम् पापम् यस्याः सा निष्पापा
nirgatam pāpam yasyāḥ sā niṣpāpā

Significance No act and no fruit of action clings to Her.

167 पापनाशिनी pāpa-nāśinī

She who destroys sin

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. nāśinī 'destroying' is the head and pāpa 'sin' its object.

Analysis पापम् नाशयति इति पापनाशिनी
pāpam nāśayati iti pāpanāśinī

Significance Free of sin (166), She destroys the sins of those who take refuge in Her.

nirgataḥ krodhaḥ yasyāḥ sā niṣkrodhā

169 क्रोधशमनी krodha-śamanī

170 निर्लोभा nir-lobhā

She who is without greed

171 लोभनाशिनी lobha-nāśinī

She who destroys greed

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. nāśinī 'destroying' is the head and lobha 'greed' its object.

Analysis लोभम् नाशयति इति लोभनाशिनी
lobham nāśayati iti lobhanāśinī

172 निःसंशया niḥ-saṃśayā

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom saṃśaya (doubt) has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without saṃśaya (doubt)'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending.

nirgataḥ saṃśayaḥ yasyāḥ sā niḥsaṃśayā

Significance She is certain knowledge itself, in which no doubt can arise.

173 संशयघ्नी saṃśaya-ghnī

She who kills all doubts

Sandhi संशय = सम् + शय (sam + śaya) — m becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ); before a sibilant it stays anusvāra: sam → saṃ, inside the lexicalised word saṃśaya

saṃśayam hanti iti saṃśayaghnī

Significance Free of doubt (172), She dispels the doubts of Her devotees, the last obstacle to knowledge.

174 निर्भवा nir-bhavā

She who is without origin

Sandhi निर्भवा = निस् + भवा (nis + bhavā) — the final s of the prefix nis becomes r before a vowel or a voiced consonant (s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ; ru turns to visarga only before a voiceless sound or a pause, 8.3.15): nis → nir

The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom bhava (birth, becoming) has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without bhava (birth, becoming)'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending.

nirgataḥ bhavaḥ yasyāḥ sā nirbhavā

Significance She was never born and never enters the round of becoming.

175 भवनाशिनी bhava-nāśinī

She who destroys bhava, the round of worldly existence (saṃsāra)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. nāśinī 'destroying' is the head and bhava 'worldly existence' its object.

bhavam nāśayati iti bhavanāśinī

Significance Without origin herself (174), She ends the cycle of births for Her devotees.

The names

176 निर्विकल्पा nir-vikalpā

She who is free from mental constructs (vikalpa)

Sandhi निर्विकल्पा = निस् + विकल्पा (nis + vikalpā) — the final s of the prefix nis becomes r before a vowel or a voiced consonant (s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ; ru turns to visarga only before a voiceless sound or a pause, 8.3.15): nis → nir

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom vikalpa (mental construction) has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without vikalpa (mental construction)'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending.

Analysis निर्गतः विकल्पः यस्याः सा निर्विकल्पा
nirgataḥ vikalpaḥ yasyāḥ sā nirvikalpā

Significance Vikalpa is the mind's division of experience into this and that; She is the undivided awareness before such division (nirvikalpa).

177 निराबाधा nir-ābādhā

She who is not disturbed by anything

Sandhi निराबाधा = निस् + आबाधा (nis + ābādhā) — the final s of the prefix nis becomes r before a vowel or a voiced consonant (s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ; ru turns to visarga only before a voiceless sound or a pause, 8.3.15): nis → nir

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom ābādhā (affliction) has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without ābādhā (affliction)'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending.

Analysis निर्गता आबाधा यस्याः सा निराबाधा
nirgatā ābādhā yasyāḥ sā nirābādhā

Significance No affliction or obstruction can reach Her.

178 निर्भेदा nir-bhedā

She who is beyond all sense of difference

Sandhi निर्भेदा = निस् + भेदा (nis + bhedā) — the final s of the prefix nis becomes r before a vowel or a voiced consonant (s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ; ru turns to visarga only before a voiceless sound or a pause, 8.3.15): nis → nir

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom bheda (difference) has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without bheda (difference)'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending.

Analysis निर्गतः भेदः यस्याः सा निर्भेदा
nirgataḥ bhedaḥ yasyāḥ sā nirbhedā

Significance She is non-dual: no difference within Her, from others of Her kind, or from anything else.

179 भेदनाशिनी bheda-nāśinī

She who destroys the sense of difference

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. nāśinī 'destroying' is the head and bheda 'difference' its object.

Analysis भेदम् नाशयति इति भेदनाशिनी
bhedam nāśayati iti bhedanāśinī

Significance Free of difference (178), She removes from Her devotees the sense of separation born of past impressions (vāsanās).

180 निर्नाशा nir-nāśā

She who is imperishable

Sandhi निर्नाशा = निस् + नाशा (nis + nāśā) — the final s of the prefix nis becomes r before a vowel or a voiced consonant (s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ; ru turns to visarga only before a voiceless sound or a pause, 8.3.15): nis → nir

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom nāśa (destruction) has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without nāśa (destruction)'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending.

Analysis निर्गतः नाशः यस्याः सा निर्नाशा
nirgataḥ nāśaḥ yasyāḥ sā nirnāśā

Significance What is never born (174) never perishes.

181 मृत्युमथनी mṛtyu-mathanī

She who destroys death

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. mathanī 'crushing, destroying' is the head and mṛtyu 'death' its object.

Analysis मृत्युम् मथ्नाति इति मृत्युमथनी
mṛtyum mathnāti iti mṛtyumathanī

Significance Imperishable herself (180), She frees Her devotees from death by granting knowledge of the deathless Self.

182 निष्क्रिया niṣ-kriyā

She who remains without action

Sandhi निष्क्रिया = निस् + क्रिया (nis + kriyā) — the final s of nis becomes visarga before a voiceless sound (8.2.66, 8.3.15), and after i that visarga becomes ṣ before k or p (Pāṇini 8.3.41 idudupadhasya cāpratyayasya): nis → niṣ

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom kriyā (action) has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without kriyā (action)'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending.

Analysis निर्गता क्रिया यस्याः सा निष्क्रिया
nirgatā kriyā yasyāḥ sā niṣkriyā

Significance All activity is Her power at work, yet She herself, as the witness, does not act.

183 निष्परिग्रहा niṣ-parigrahā

She who does not acquire or accept anything

Sandhi निष्परिग्रहा = निस् + परिग्रहा (nis + parigrahā) — the final s of nis becomes visarga before a voiceless sound (8.2.66, 8.3.15), and after i that visarga becomes ṣ before k or p (Pāṇini 8.3.41 idudupadhasya cāpratyayasya): nis → niṣ

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom parigraha (taking, possession) has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without parigraha (taking, possession)'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending.

Analysis निर्गतः परिग्रहः यस्याः सा निष्परिग्रहा
nirgataḥ parigrahaḥ yasyāḥ sā niṣparigrahā

Significance Possessing everything already, She has nothing to acquire or receive.

Where the names meet

nistulā (184) shows nis unchanged before t. Names 188–190 play on dur- 'hard': durlabhā, durgamā, durgā.

The names

184 निस्तुला nis-tulā

She who is incomparable, unequalled

Sandhi निस्तुला = निस् + तुला (nis + tulā) — the final s of nis, by way of visarga, is restored as s before the voiceless dental t (Pāṇini 8.3.34 visarjanīyasya saḥ), so the prefix shows no visible change

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom tulā (comparison) has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without tulā (comparison)'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending.

Analysis निर्गता तुला यस्याः सा निस्तुला
nirgatā tulā yasyāḥ sā nistulā

Significance There is nothing beside Her to weigh against Her.

185 नीलचिकुरा nīla-cikurā

She whose hair is dark (blue-black)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. 'She whose tresses (cikura) are dark (nīla)'; cikura takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis नीलाः चिकुराः यस्याः सा नीलचिकुरा
nīlāḥ cikurāḥ yasyāḥ sā nīlacikurā

Significance Amid the names of the formless, a single image of Her form; dark, abundant tresses are a classical mark of beauty (cf. name 13).

186 निरपाया nir-apāyā

She who is beyond loss or decay

Sandhi निरपाया = निस् + अपाया (nis + apāyā) — the final s of the prefix nis becomes r before a vowel or a voiced consonant (s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ; ru turns to visarga only before a voiceless sound or a pause, 8.3.15): nis → nir; अपाय = अप + आय (apa + āya) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ), inside the lexicalised word apāya

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom apāya (loss, harm) has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without apāya (loss, harm)'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending.

Analysis निर्गतः अपायः यस्याः सा निरपाया
nirgataḥ apāyaḥ yasyāḥ sā nirapāyā

Significance Apāya is any falling away or harm; nothing in Her can wane.

187 निरत्यया nir-atyayā

She who cannot be transgressed

Sandhi निरत्यया = निस् + अत्यया (nis + atyayā) — the final s of the prefix nis becomes r before a vowel or a voiced consonant (s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ; ru turns to visarga only before a voiceless sound or a pause, 8.3.15): nis → nir; अत्यय = अति + अय (ati + aya) — yaṇ: i becomes y before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci), inside the lexicalised word atyaya

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi-bahuvrīhi with the prefix nis). The prefix nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone out', whose participle is dropped in the compound (prādi-bahuvrīhi): 'She from whom atyaya (transgression, passing away) has gone out', i.e. 'She who is without atyaya (transgression, passing away)'. The name describes Her, so the last member takes the feminine ending.

Analysis निर्गतः अत्ययः यस्याः सा निरत्यया
nirgataḥ atyayaḥ yasyāḥ sā niratyayā

Significance No one can go beyond Her or set aside Her law; atyaya also means passing away, so the name also says She does not pass away.

188 दुर्लभा dur-labhā

She who is won only with much difficulty

Sandhi दुर्लभा = दुस् + लभा (dus + labhā) — the final s of the prefix dus becomes r before a voiced consonant (s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ; ru turns to visarga only before a voiceless sound or a pause, 8.3.15): dus → dur

Compound upapada compound (dus with √labh and the suffix khal). dus 'with difficulty' combined with √labh 'to obtain' and the suffix khal (-a), which forms such 'hard/easy to …' words (Pāṇini 3.3.126 īṣaddussuṣu kṛcchrākṛcchrārtheṣu khal): 'hard to obtain'. The feminine -ā describes Her.

Analysis दुःखेन लभ्यते इति दुर्लभा
duḥkhena labhyate iti durlabhā

Significance Names 188–190 play on dur- 'hard': She is hard to win, hard to approach, and is Durgā; yet She is easily won by devotion (120).

189 दुर्गमा dur-gamā

She who is approachable only with extreme effort

Sandhi दुर्गमा = दुस् + गमा (dus + gamā) — the final s of the prefix dus becomes r before a voiced consonant (s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ; ru turns to visarga only before a voiceless sound or a pause, 8.3.15): dus → dur

Compound upapada compound (dus with √gam and the suffix khal). As in name 188: dus 'with difficulty' with √gam 'to go' and the suffix khal (-a): 'hard to approach'.

Analysis दुःखेन गम्यते इति दुर्गमा
duḥkhena gamyate iti durgamā

Significance The way to Her is steep for one who relies only on effort; Her grace makes it open.

190 दुर्गा durgā

She who is the Goddess Durgā

Sandhi दुर्गा = दुस् + गा (dus + gā) — the final s of the prefix dus becomes r before a voiced consonant (s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ; ru turns to visarga only before a voiceless sound or a pause, 8.3.15): dus → dur, inside the word durgā

Compound not a compound

Significance In the Devī Māhātmya the Goddess foretells that She will be called Durgā for slaying the asura Durgama; traditionally She is also the fortress that protects Her devotees.

191 दुःखहन्त्री duḥkha-hantrī

She who is the destroyer of sorrow

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. hantrī 'slayer' (√han + -tṛ, feminine) is the head and duḥkha 'sorrow' stands to it in the genitive (see name 165 on compounds with -tṛ).

Analysis दुःखस्य हन्त्री दुःखहन्त्री
duḥkhasya hantrī duḥkhahantrī

Significance She destroys sorrow at its root, which is ignorance, and so gives happiness (192).

192 सुखप्रदा sukha-pradā

She who is the giver of happiness

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. pradā 'giving' (pra + √dā with the suffix ka, feminine) is the head and sukha 'happiness' its object.

Analysis सुखम् प्रददाति इति सुखप्रदा
sukham pradadāti iti sukhapradā

Significance Having removed sorrow (191), She gives happiness, in this world and as the bliss of liberation.

वर्जिताvarjitādevoid of, without√vṛj, causative past participle, feminine

Where the names meet

Name 194: durācāra is the prefix dus (dur) + ācāra 'conduct'. Name 198 echoes the Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad (6.8): none is equal to Her, none greater.

The names

193 दुष्टदूरा duṣṭa-dūrā

She who is far from the wicked

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound pañcamī-tatpuruṣa. dūrā 'far, remote' is the head; duṣṭa 'the wicked' stands to it in the ablative: 'far from the wicked'. The genitive (duṣṭānām dūrā, ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa) gives the same sense, since words for 'far' take either case. The two members are simply juxtaposed.

Analysis दुष्टेभ्यः दूरा दुष्टदूरा
duṣṭebhyaḥ dūrā duṣṭadūrā

Significance Traditionally: those who harm others cannot reach Her by worship alone, because their own malice keeps them away; the distance is theirs, not Hers.

194 दुराचारशमनी durācāra-śamanī

She who quells evil conduct

Sandhi दुराचार = दुस् + आचार (dus + ācāra) — visarga sandhi: the final s of the prefix dus (dur) becomes r before a vowel (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ, the r then kept before a vowel)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (with an inner prādi-tatpuruṣa). Inner layer: dur-ācāra 'evil conduct', a prādi compound in which the prefix dus 'bad, ill' qualifies ācāra 'conduct'. Outer layer: śamanī 'she who quells' is the head and takes the inner compound in the genitive: 'the quencher of evil conduct'. Durācāra may also denote the evil-doers themselves; the sense is the same.

Analysis दुष्टः आचारः दुराचारः; दुराचारस्य शमनी दुराचारशमनी
duṣṭaḥ ācāraḥ durācāraḥ; durācārasya śamanī durācāraśamanī

Significance Traditionally She both checks the wrongdoing of the world and, for the devotee, calms the inner tendencies that lead to wrong action.

195 दोषवर्जिता doṣa-varjitā

She who is free from all faults

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa. The past participle varjitā 'free from, devoid of' is the head and the faults stand to it in the instrumental: 'devoid of faults'. The members are juxtaposed without sound change.

Analysis दोषैः वर्जिता दोषवर्जिता
doṣaiḥ varjitā doṣavarjitā

Significance Traditionally the faults are those of embodied existence — attachment, aversion, delusion and the like — which cannot touch Her, as the sky is untouched by the clouds that pass through it.

196 सर्वज्ञा sarva-jñā

She who is omniscient

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. -jña 'knowing' is a verbal noun from √jñā formed with the suffix ka (Pāṇini 3.2.3 āto 'nupasarge kaḥ), which only occurs with a preceding word (upapada); sarva 'all' is its object. The feminine is -jñā. No sound change at the junction.

Analysis सर्वम् जानाति इति सर्वज्ञा
sarvam jānāti iti sarvajñā

Significance Her knowledge is not acquired piece by piece; She knows all because all is Her own self-awareness. Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad 1.1.9 calls the Absolute 'yaḥ sarvajñaḥ sarvavit'.

197 सान्द्रकरुणा sāndra-karuṇā

She who shows intense compassion

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. sāndra 'dense, thick, abundant' qualifies karuṇā 'compassion', and the whole describes Her: 'She whose compassion is dense'. A karmadhāraya reading ('She who is dense compassion itself') is also possible. The members are juxtaposed.

Analysis सान्द्रा करुणा यस्याः सा सान्द्रकरुणा
sāndrā karuṇā yasyāḥ sā sāndrakaruṇā

Significance Traditionally Her compassion is 'dense' because it is unmixed: it does not wait to be earned.

198 समानाधिकवर्जिता samānādhika-varjitā

She who has neither equal nor superior

Sandhi समानाधिक = समान + अधिक (samāna + adhika) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (with an inner itaretara-dvandva). Inner layer: samāna 'equal' and adhika 'greater, superior' are joined as a dvandva, 'an equal and a superior'. Outer layer: the participle varjitā 'devoid of' is the head and takes the pair in the instrumental: 'devoid of an equal or a superior'.

Analysis समानः च अधिकः च समानाधिकौ; समानाधिकाभ्याम् वर्जिता समानाधिकवर्जिता
samānaḥ ca adhikaḥ ca samānādhikau; samānādhikābhyām varjitā samānādhikavarjitā

Significance The name echoes the Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad (6.8): 'na tat-samaś cābhyadhikaś ca dṛśyate' — none is seen equal to It, nor greater.

Śloka 52names 199–204

सर्वशक्तिमयी सर्वमङ्गला सद्गतिप्रदा ।
सर्वेश्वरी सर्वमयी सर्वमन्त्रस्वरूपिणी ॥ ५२ ॥

sarvaśaktimayī sarvamaṅgalā sadgatipradā |
sarveśvarī sarvamayī sarvamantrasvarūpiṇī || 52 ||

The names, separated

199सर्व-शक्ति-मयीsarva-śakti-mayī200सर्व-मङ्गलाsarva-maṅgalā201सद्-गति-प्रदाsad-gati-pradā

202सर्वेश्वरीsarveśvarī203सर्व-मयीsarva-mayī204सर्व-मन्त्र-स्वरूपिणीsarva-mantra-svarūpiṇī

Translation

199She who consists of all powers; 200She who is the source of all that is auspicious; 201She who bestows the true goal;

202She who is the sovereign of all; 203She who is everything; 204She who is the essence of all the mantras.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish
199 सर्वशक्तिमयी sarva-śakti-mayī
सर्वsarvaall
शक्तिśaktipower, energy; also a goddess as a power
मयीmayīconsisting of, made ofthe taddhita suffix -maya, feminine -mayī
200 सर्वमङ्गला sarva-maṅgalā
सर्वsarvaall
मङ्गलाmaṅgalāauspicious; auspiciousnessmaṅgala, with the feminine -ā
201 सद्गतिप्रदा sad-gati-pradā
सत्sattrue, real, goodpresent participle of √as 'to be'; appears as sad- by jaśtva
गतिgatiway, path; goal, final destination√gam 'to go'
प्रदाpradāgiving, bestowingpra + √dā 'to give', feminine
202 सर्वेश्वरी sarveśvarī
सर्वsarvaall, everyone and everything
ईश्वरीīśvarīsovereign, ruling ladyfeminine of īśvara, from √īś 'to rule'

सर्वsarvaall, everything
मयीmayīconsisting of, made ofthe taddhita suffix -maya (mayaṭ), feminine -mayī
204 सर्वमन्त्रस्वरूपिणी sarva-mantra-svarūpiṇī
सर्वsarvaall
मन्त्रmantramantra, sacred formula√man 'to think' + -tra: 'instrument of thought'
स्वरूपिणीsvarūpiṇīwhose own form is, having the nature ofsva 'own' + rūpa 'form', with the possessive suffix -in, feminine

Where the names meet

Names 199–206 form a run of sarva- ('all') names: She is all powers, all auspiciousness, all mantras, yantras and Tantras.

The names

199 सर्वशक्तिमयी sarva-śakti-mayī

She who consists of all powers

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya, followed by the taddhita suffix -maya (mayaṭ). Inner layer: sarva-śakti 'all powers' (karmadhāraya, sarva qualifying śakti). To this the suffix -maya 'consisting of, made of' (mayaṭ, Pāṇini 5.4.21 in the sense of 'consisting abundantly of') is added, feminine -mayī: 'consisting of all powers'. The second step is a derivation, not a further compound; its gloss sarvaśaktisvarūpā shows the sense.

Analysis सर्वाः शक्तयः सर्वशक्तयः; सर्वशक्तिस्वरूपा सर्वशक्तिमयी
sarvāḥ śaktayaḥ sarvaśaktayaḥ; sarvaśaktisvarūpā sarvaśaktimayī

Significance In Śrīvidyā every power — of will, knowledge and action, and every deity of the Śrīcakra's enclosures — is a portion of Her; She does not merely possess the powers, She is made of them.

200 सर्वमङ्गला sarva-maṅgalā

She who is the source of all that is auspicious

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. 'She to whom all auspicious things belong', i.e. from whom they come; maṅgala takes the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi. A karmadhāraya reading (sarvā cāsau maṅgalā ca, 'She who is wholly auspicious') is also current. The members are juxtaposed.

Analysis सर्वाणि मङ्गलानि यस्याः सा सर्वमङ्गला
sarvāṇi maṅgalāni yasyāḥ sā sarvamaṅgalā

Significance The Devī Māhātmya salutes Her as 'sarvamaṅgala-māṅgalye', the auspiciousness of all that is auspicious.

201 सद्गतिप्रदा sad-gati-pradā

She who bestows the true goal

Sandhi सद्गति = सत् + गति (sat + gati) — jaśtva: a final t becomes d before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.39 jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte)

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (with an inner karmadhāraya). Inner layer: sat 'true, good' qualifies gati 'way, goal, destination' (karmadhāraya; the feminine satī takes the masculine stem sat, puṃvadbhāva). Outer layer: -pradā 'giving' (pra + √dā with the suffix -a) is the head and governs the inner compound as its object.

Analysis सती गतिः सद्गतिः; सद्गतिम् प्रददाति इति सद्गतिप्रदा
satī gatiḥ sadgatiḥ; sadgatim pradadāti iti sadgatipradā

Significance Sadgati is both the good path and its end, liberation; traditionally She grants each seeker the right way and, at last, the highest state.

202 सर्वेश्वरी sarveśvarī

She who is the sovereign of all

Sandhi सर्वेश्वरी = सर्व + ईश्वरी (sarva + īśvarī) — guṇa: a/ā + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. īśvarī 'sovereign, ruling lady' is the head and sarva 'all' stands to it in the genitive: 'the sovereign of all'.

Analysis सर्वेषाम् ईश्वरी सर्वेश्वरी
sarveṣām īśvarī sarveśvarī

Significance Her rule extends over all that moves and does not move; nothing lies outside Her governance.

203 सर्वमयी sarva-mayī

She who is everything

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Traditionally: since She consists of all, there is nothing outside Her to pervade; the world is not a container She fills but Her own form.

204 सर्वमन्त्रस्वरूपिणी sarva-mantra-svarūpiṇī

She who is the essence of all the mantras

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (with an inner karmadhāraya), followed by the possessive suffix -in. (1) sarva-mantra 'all mantras' (karmadhāraya). (2) sarvamantra-svarūpa 'the essential form of all mantras' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; svarūpa is the head). (3) The possessive suffix -in (feminine -inī) makes the whole an adjective: 'She who has the essential form of all mantras', i.e. who is their very nature. Juxtaposition throughout.

Analysis सर्वे मन्त्राः सर्वमन्त्राः; सर्वमन्त्राणाम् स्वरूपम् सर्वमन्त्रस्वरूपम्; तत् अस्याः अस्ति इति सर्वमन्त्रस्वरूपिणी
sarve mantrāḥ sarvamantrāḥ; sarvamantrāṇām svarūpam sarvamantrasvarūpam; tat asyāḥ asti iti sarvamantrasvarūpiṇī

Significance In Śrīvidyā every mantra is a sound-form of the Goddess, and Her own fifteen-syllabled vidyā is held to contain them all.

Śloka 53names 205–211

सर्वयन्त्रात्मिका सर्वतन्त्ररूपा मनोन्मनी ।
माहेश्वरी महादेवी महालक्ष्मीर् मृडप्रिया ॥ ५३ ॥

sarvayantrātmikā sarvatantrarūpā manonmanī |
māheśvarī mahādevī mahālakṣmīr mṛḍapriyā || 53 ||

The names, separated ° form as a name on its own; in the recitation above it joins its neighbour

205सर्व-यन्त्रात्मिकाsarva-yantrātmikā206सर्व-तन्त्र-रूपाsarva-tantra-rūpā207मनोन्मनीmanonmanī

208माहेश्वरीmāheśvarī209महा-देवीmahā-devī210महा-लक्ष्मीः°mahā-lakṣmīḥ211मृड-प्रियाmṛḍa-priyā

Translation

205She whose very nature is all the yantras; 206She whose form is all the Tantras; 207She who is Manonmanī, the state in which the mind transcends itself;

208She who is the consort of Maheśvara; 209She who is the great Goddess; 210She who is the great goddess Lakṣmī; 211She who is the beloved of Mṛḍa (Śiva).

Word by word

SanskritEnglish
205 सर्वयन्त्रात्मिका sarva-yantrātmikā
सर्वsarvaall
यन्त्रyantrayantra, sacred diagram (lit. 'instrument of restraint')√yam 'to hold' + -tra
आत्मिकाātmikāhaving as its self or natureātman + the suffix -ka, feminine -ikā
206 सर्वतन्त्ररूपा sarva-tantra-rūpā
सर्वsarvaall
तन्त्रtantraTantra, a body of scripture and practice (lit. 'loom, framework')√tan 'to extend'
रूपाrūpāformrūpa, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi
207 मनोन्मनी manonmanī
मनस्manasmindappears as mano- in the name
उत्utup, beyond (prefix)appears as un- before m
मनीmanīmindmanas, shortened, with feminine -ī in the bahuvrīhi unmanī
208 माहेश्वरी māheśvarī
माहेश्वरीmāheśvarībelonging to Maheśvara; the consort and power of Maheśvara (Śiva)taddhita (suffix -a with vṛddhi, feminine -ī) from maheśvara = mahā 'great' + īśvara 'lord'
209 महादेवी mahā-devī
महत्mahatgreatappears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)
देवीdevīgoddessfeminine of deva, from √div 'to shine, to play'
210 महालक्ष्मीः mahā-lakṣmīḥ
महत्mahatgreatappears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)
लक्ष्मीःlakṣmīḥLakṣmī, goddess of fortune and prosperity; fortune, splendornominative singular with -ḥ
211 मृडप्रिया mṛḍa-priyā
मृडmṛḍaMṛḍa, 'the gracious one', a name of Śiva√mṛḍ 'to be gracious, to delight'
प्रियाpriyābeloved, dear

Where the names meet

महालक्ष्मीर्मृड = महालक्ष्मीः + मृड… (mahālakṣmīḥ + mṛḍa…) — visarga becomes r before a voiced sound

Name 210 ends in -ḥ (mahālakṣmīḥ): lakṣmī keeps the nominative s, which surfaces as r before mṛḍa-. Name 208 begins the long run of mahā- names that continues to name 237.

The names

205 सर्वयन्त्रात्मिका sarva-yantrātmikā

She whose very nature is all the yantras

Sandhi यन्त्रात्मिका = यन्त्र + आत्मिका (yantra + ātmikā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (with an inner karmadhāraya). Inner layer: sarva-yantra 'all yantras' (karmadhāraya). Outer layer: a bahuvrīhi with ātman 'self, nature' as final member, which takes the suffix -ka; the feminine is -ātmikā (a → i before the suffix, Pāṇini 7.3.44): 'She whose very self is all yantras', i.e. who is their nature.

Analysis सर्वाणि यन्त्राणि सर्वयन्त्राणि; सर्वयन्त्राणि आत्मा यस्याः सा सर्वयन्त्रात्मिका
sarvāṇi yantrāṇi sarvayantrāṇi; sarvayantrāṇi ātmā yasyāḥ sā sarvayantrātmikā

Significance Every yantra is a diagram of Her presence, and the Śrīcakra, king of yantras, contains them all.

206 सर्वतन्त्ररूपा sarva-tantra-rūpā

She whose form is all the Tantras

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (with an inner karmadhāraya). Inner layer: sarva-tantra 'all the Tantras' (karmadhāraya). Outer layer: a bahuvrīhi, 'She whose form is all the Tantras'; rūpa takes the feminine -ā. Juxtaposition throughout.

Analysis सर्वाणि तन्त्राणि सर्वतन्त्राणि; सर्वतन्त्राणि रूपम् यस्याः सा सर्वतन्त्ररूपा
sarvāṇi tantrāṇi sarvatantrāṇi; sarvatantrāṇi rūpam yasyāḥ sā sarvatantrarūpā

Significance Names 204–206 together: She is the sound (mantra), the diagram (yantra) and the method (tantra) of Her own worship.

207 मनोन्मनी manonmanī

She who is Manonmanī, the state in which the mind transcends itself

Sandhi उन्मनी = उत् + मनी (ut + manī) — a stop becomes the nasal of its class before a nasal: t → n (Pāṇini 8.4.45 yaro 'nunāsike 'nunāsiko vā), inside unmanī; मनोन्मनी = मनस् + उन्मनी (manas + unmanī) — manas appears without its final s and its a coalesces with the u of unmanī by guṇa: a + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ). Regular sandhi of manaḥ + unmanī would leave a hiatus (mana unmanī); the fused form is that of the lexicalised technical term

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (traditional analysis), with an inner prādi-bahuvrīhi. Inner layer: un-manī 'she whose mind has risen beyond', a bahuvrīhi with the prefix ut 'up, beyond' (manas is shortened and takes the feminine -ī): the state in which the mind is transcended. Outer layer: manas-unmanī 'the transcending of the mind', with manas in the genitive. The name is a technical term of Śaiva and Śākta yoga and is not built by ordinary sandhi.

Analysis उद्गतम् मनः यस्याः सा उन्मनी; मनसः उन्मनी मनोन्मनी
udgatam manaḥ yasyāḥ sā unmanī; manasaḥ unmanī manonmanī

Significance In Śaiva and Śākta yoga unmanī is the last stage of the subtle ascent of sound beyond the mind, where thought falls silent; Manonmanī is also the name of the highest of Śiva's nine powers in the Śaiva Āgamas.

Uncertain The junction mano + unmanī is not regular sandhi and the analysis of this technical term varies (some read manas + unmanī as a karmadhāraya, 'the mind that has become unmanī'); the meaning follows the common yogic sense.

208 माहेश्वरी māheśvarī

She who is the consort of Maheśvara

Sandhi माहेश्वरी = महा + ईश्वर (mahā + īśvara) — guṇa: a/ā + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ), inside the base maheśvara 'great lord'; the derivative then strengthens its first vowel (ma → mā, vṛddhi), a morphological change, not sandhi

Compound not a compound

Significance As the power (śakti) of the Great Lord She is inseparable from Him; Māheśvarī is also one of the seven Mothers (mātṛkās), the śakti of Maheśvara.

209 महादेवी mahā-devī

She who is the great Goddess

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya. mahat 'great' qualifies devī 'goddess', the head; the feminine mahatī takes the masculine stem (puṃvadbhāva) and mahat becomes mahā- (Pāṇini 6.3.46). The name can also be read as the feminine of mahādeva, 'the consort of Mahādeva'. No sound change.

Analysis महती देवी महादेवी
mahatī devī mahādevī

Significance Traditionally mahā is read as 'immeasurable': Her body cannot be measured, since it is the universe itself. She is also the consort of Mahādeva.

210 महालक्ष्मीः mahā-lakṣmīḥ

She who is the great goddess Lakṣmī

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya. mahat 'great' (as mahā-) qualifies lakṣmī, the head. Lakṣmī belongs to the small group of ī-stems that keep the nominative -s (-ḥ), unlike the derived feminines in -ī; hence mahālakṣmīḥ, which the verse shows as mahālakṣmīr before mṛḍa-.

Analysis महती लक्ष्मीः महालक्ष्मीः
mahatī lakṣmīḥ mahālakṣmīḥ

Significance In the Devī Māhātmya Mahālakṣmī is the form of the Goddess who destroys Mahiṣa; here She is Lakṣmī not as one goddess among others but as the source of all fortune and splendor.

Corrected महालक्ष्मी → महालक्ष्मीः. महालक्ष्मी → महालक्ष्मीः: lakṣmī keeps the nominative -ḥ (not a ṅīp stem); the verse shows it as महालक्ष्मीर्मृडप्रिया.

211 मृडप्रिया mṛḍa-priyā

She who is the beloved of Mṛḍa (Śiva)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. priyā 'beloved' is the head and Mṛḍa stands to it in the genitive: 'the beloved of Mṛḍa'. A bahuvrīhi reading (mṛḍaḥ priyaḥ yasyāḥ sā, 'She to whom Mṛḍa is dear') is also possible. Juxtaposition.

Analysis मृडस्य प्रिया मृडप्रिया
mṛḍasya priyā mṛḍapriyā

Significance Mṛḍa names Śiva as gracious and kindly; She is dear to Him in His aspect of grace.

Śloka 54names 212–218

महारूपा महापूज्या महापातकनाशिनी ।
महामाया महासत्त्वा महाशक्तिर् महारतिः ॥ ५४ ॥

mahārūpā mahāpūjyā mahāpātakanāśinī |
mahāmāyā mahāsattvā mahāśaktir mahāratiḥ || 54 ||

The names, separated ° form as a name on its own; in the recitation above it joins its neighbour

212महा-रूपाmahā-rūpā213महा-पूज्याmahā-pūjyā214महा-पातक-नाशिनीmahā-pātaka-nāśinī

215महा-मायाmahā-māyā216महा-सत्त्वाmahā-sattvā217महा-शक्तिः°mahā-śaktiḥ218महा-रतिःmahā-ratiḥ

Translation

212She who has a great form; 213She who is the greatest object of worship; 214She who destroys even the greatest of sins;

215She who is the great illusion; 216She who possesses great sattva; 217She who is the great Power; 218She who is boundless delight.

महत्mahatgreatappears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)

महत्mahatgreatappears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)

Where the names meet

महाशक्तिर्महारतिः = महाशक्तिः + महारतिः (mahāśaktiḥ + mahāratiḥ) — visarga becomes r before a voiced sound

The names

212 महारूपा mahā-rūpā

She who has a great form

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. 'She whose form is great'; mahat appears as mahā- (Pāṇini 6.3.46) and rūpa takes the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi. No sound change.

Analysis महत् रूपम् यस्याः सा महारूपा
mahat rūpam yasyāḥ sā mahārūpā

Significance Traditionally Her form is great because it surpasses everything that has form, including the Purāṇic universe-form.

213 महापूज्या mahā-pūjyā

She who is the greatest object of worship

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya. The gerundive pūjyā 'to be worshipped' is the head; mahā- 'greatly, supremely' qualifies it. No sound change.

Analysis महती पूज्या महापूज्या
mahatī pūjyā mahāpūjyā

Significance Traditionally even the gods who are themselves worshipped — Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva — worship Her.

214 महापातकनाशिनी mahā-pātaka-nāśinī

She who destroys even the greatest of sins

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (with an inner karmadhāraya). Inner layer: mahā-pātaka 'great sins' (karmadhāraya). Outer layer: nāśinī 'destroyer' (from the causative of √naś with the agent suffix -in) is the head and takes the sins in the genitive.

Analysis महान्ति पातकानि महापातकानि; महापातकानाम् नाशिनी महापातकनाशिनी
mahānti pātakāni mahāpātakāni; mahāpātakānām nāśinī mahāpātakanāśinī

Significance The mahāpātakas are the gravest sins of the Dharmaśāstra (such as killing a brāhmaṇa and theft of gold); traditionally even these are destroyed by remembrance of Her.

215 महामाया mahā-māyā

She who is the great illusion

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya. mahā- (from mahat) qualifies māyā, the head. No sound change.

Analysis महती माया महामाया
mahatī māyā mahāmāyā

Significance The Devī Māhātmya says that Mahāmāyā draws even the minds of the wise into delusion; the same power, when pleased, grants release.

216 महासत्त्वा mahā-sattvā

She who possesses great sattva

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. 'She whose sattva is great'; sattva takes the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi. No sound change.

Analysis महत् सत्त्वम् यस्याः सा महासत्त्वा
mahat sattvam yasyāḥ sā mahāsattvā

Significance Sattva here covers both pure being and the strength or courage that flows from it; traditionally She is supreme in both.

217 महाशक्तिः mahā-śaktiḥ

She who is the great Power

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya. mahā- qualifies śakti 'power', the head: 'the great Power'. Because śakti is itself feminine, a bahuvrīhi ('She whose power is great') would give the same form. No sound change.

Analysis महती शक्तिः महाशक्तिः
mahatī śaktiḥ mahāśaktiḥ

Significance She is not one power among many but the Power from which every other power is drawn.

218 महारतिः mahā-ratiḥ

She who is boundless delight

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya. mahā- qualifies rati 'delight, love', the head. No sound change.

Analysis महती रतिः महारतिः
mahatī ratiḥ mahāratiḥ

Significance Traditionally Her delight is the unending joy of the Self, of which every lesser pleasure is a faint reflection.

Śloka 55names 219–225

महाभोगा महैश्वर्या महावीर्या महाबला ।
महाबुद्धिर् महासिद्धिर् महायोगेश्वरेश्वरी ॥ ५५ ॥

mahābhogā mahaiśvaryā mahāvīryā mahābalā |
mahābuddhir mahāsiddhir mahāyogeśvareśvarī || 55 ||

The names, separated ° form as a name on its own; in the recitation above it joins its neighbour

219महा-भोगाmahā-bhogā220महैश्वर्याmahaiśvaryā221महा-वीर्याmahā-vīryā222महा-बलाmahā-balā

223महा-बुद्धिः°mahā-buddhiḥ224महा-सिद्धिः°mahā-siddhiḥ225महा-योगेश्वरेश्वरीmahā-yogeśvareśvarī

Translation

219She who has immense wealth; 220She who has supreme sovereignty; 221She who is supreme in valor; 222She who is supreme in might;

223She who is supreme in intelligence; 224She who is endowed with the highest attainments; 225She who is the sovereign of the great lords of yoga.

भोगाbhogāenjoyment, experience; wealth, possessions√bhuj 'to enjoy', with the feminine -ā

महत्mahatgreatappears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)
ऐश्वर्याaiśvaryāsovereignty, lordship, divine powerabstract noun from īśvara, with the feminine -ā

महत्mahatgreatappears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)
वीर्याvīryāvalor, heroism; potencyvīrya (from vīra 'hero'), with the feminine -ā

महत्mahatgreatappears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)
बलाbalāstrength, mightbala, with the feminine -ā
223 महाबुद्धिः mahā-buddhiḥ
महत्mahatgreatappears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)
बुद्धिःbuddhiḥintelligence, intellect, understanding√budh 'to awaken, know', nominative singular
224 महासिद्धिः mahā-siddhiḥ
महत्mahatgreatappears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)
सिद्धिःsiddhiḥattainment, accomplishment, perfection; supernatural power√sidh 'to succeed', nominative singular
225 महायोगेश्वरेश्वरी mahā-yogeśvareśvarī
महत्mahatgreatappears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)
योगyogayoga, union, discipline
ईश्वरīśvaralord, master√īś 'to rule'
ईश्वरीīśvarīsovereign, ruling ladyfeminine of īśvara

Where the names meet

महाबुद्धिर्महासिद्धिः = महाबुद्धिः + महासिद्धिः (mahābuddhiḥ + mahāsiddhiḥ) — visarga becomes r before a voiced sound

महासिद्धिर्महायोगे = महासिद्धिः + महायोगे… (mahāsiddhiḥ + mahāyoge…) — visarga becomes r before a voiced sound

Name 220 is mahā + aiśvaryā fused by vṛddhi (mahaiśvaryā); name 225 is one name, the sovereign of the great lords of yoga.

The names

219 महाभोगा mahā-bhogā

She who has immense wealth

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. 'She whose enjoyment (or wealth) is great'; bhoga takes the feminine -ā. No sound change.

Analysis महान् भोगः यस्याः सा महाभोगा
mahān bhogaḥ yasyāḥ sā mahābhogā

Significance Bhoga is both enjoyment and the riches enjoyed; traditionally the whole universe is the object of Her enjoyment.

220 महैश्वर्या mahaiśvaryā

She who has supreme sovereignty

Sandhi महैश्वर्या = महा + ऐश्वर्या (mahā + aiśvaryā) — vṛddhi: ā + ai → ai (Pāṇini 6.1.88 vṛddhir eci)

Compound bahuvrīhi. 'She whose sovereignty is great'; aiśvarya takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis महत् ऐश्वर्यम् यस्याः सा महैश्वर्या
mahat aiśvaryam yasyāḥ sā mahaiśvaryā

Significance Aiśvarya is the lordship of the Lord; traditionally Hers is the sovereignty that even the gods' powers derive from.

221 महावीर्या mahā-vīryā

She who is supreme in valor

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. 'She whose valor is great'; vīrya takes the feminine -ā. No sound change.

Analysis महत् वीर्यम् यस्याः सा महावीर्या
mahat vīryam yasyāḥ sā mahāvīryā

Significance Her valor is shown in the Purāṇic battles against Bhaṇḍa and the other demons; inwardly it is the strength that overcomes ignorance.

222 महाबला mahā-balā

She who is supreme in might

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. 'She whose strength is great'; bala takes the feminine -ā. No sound change.

Analysis महत् बलम् यस्याः सा महाबला
mahat balam yasyāḥ sā mahābalā

Significance Traditionally Her might is that on which every other strength depends, as the Kena Upaniṣad shows the gods' powers failing without Brahman.

223 महाबुद्धिः mahā-buddhiḥ

She who is supreme in intelligence

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. 'She whose intelligence is great'. Because buddhi is feminine, the bahuvrīhi keeps the form buddhiḥ. No sound change.

Analysis महती बुद्धिः यस्याः सा महाबुद्धिः
mahatī buddhiḥ yasyāḥ sā mahābuddhiḥ

Significance Traditionally She is the intelligence that illumines every intellect; Mahat or Buddhi is also the first evolute of nature, which She governs.

224 महासिद्धिः mahā-siddhiḥ

She who is endowed with the highest attainments

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. 'She whose attainments are great'; siddhi, being feminine, keeps its form. A karmadhāraya ('She who is the great attainment') is equally possible. No sound change.

Analysis महत्यः सिद्धयः यस्याः सा महासिद्धिः
mahatyaḥ siddhayaḥ yasyāḥ sā mahāsiddhiḥ

Significance The siddhis are the powers of the yogin, beginning with aṇimā; the greatest attainment is liberation, which She herself is.

225 महायोगेश्वरेश्वरी mahā-yogeśvareśvarī

She who is the sovereign of the great lords of yoga

Sandhi योगेश्वर = योग + ईश्वर (yoga + īśvara) — guṇa: a/ā + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ); योगेश्वरेश्वरी = योगेश्वर + ईश्वरी (yogeśvara + īśvarī) — guṇa: a/ā + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) yoga-īśvara 'lord of yoga', i.e. a master yogin (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) mahā-yogeśvara 'the great lords of yoga' (karmadhāraya). (3) īśvarī 'sovereign' is the head of the whole and takes the great yogins in the genitive: 'the sovereign of the great lords of yoga'.

Analysis योगस्य ईश्वरः योगेश्वरः; महान्तः योगेश्वराः महायोगेश्वराः; महायोगेश्वराणाम् ईश्वरी महायोगेश्वरेश्वरी
yogasya īśvaraḥ yogeśvaraḥ; mahāntaḥ yogeśvarāḥ mahāyogeśvarāḥ; mahāyogeśvarāṇām īśvarī mahāyogeśvareśvarī

Significance Traditionally even the greatest yogins, Śiva foremost among them, are under Her rule and worship Her.

Śloka 56names 226–231

महातन्त्रा महामन्त्रा महायन्त्रा महासना ।
महायागक्रमाराध्या महाभैरवपूजिता ॥ ५६ ॥

mahātantrā mahāmantrā mahāyantrā mahāsanā |
mahāyāgakramārādhyā mahābhairavapūjitā || 56 ||

The names, separated

226महा-तन्त्राmahā-tantrā227महा-मन्त्राmahā-mantrā228महा-यन्त्राmahā-yantrā229महासनाmahāsanā

230महा-याग-क्रमाराध्याmahā-yāga-kramārādhyā231महा-भैरव-पूजिताmahā-bhairava-pūjitā

Translation

226She who is the great Tantra; 227She who is the greatest mantra; 228She who is in the form of the great yantras; 229She whose seat is great;

230She who is to be worshipped through the ordered rite of the great sacrifice; 231She who is worshipped even by Mahābhairava (Śiva).

Word by word

SanskritEnglish
226 महातन्त्रा mahā-tantrā
महत्mahatgreatappears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)
तन्त्राtantrāTantra, scripture and system of practicetantra, with the feminine -ā
227 महामन्त्रा mahā-mantrā
महत्mahatgreatappears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)
मन्त्राmantrāmantra, sacred formulamantra, with the feminine -ā
228 महायन्त्रा mahā-yantrā
महत्mahatgreatappears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)
यन्त्राyantrāyantra, sacred diagramyantra, with the feminine -ā
229 महासना mahāsanā
महत्mahatgreatappears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)
आसनाāsanāseat, throneāsana (√ās 'to sit'), with the feminine -ā
230 महायागक्रमाराध्या mahā-yāga-kramārādhyā
महत्mahatgreatappears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)
यागyāgasacrifice, worship√yaj 'to sacrifice'
क्रमkramaorder, sequence, prescribed method√kram 'to step'
आराध्याārādhyāto be worshipped, to be propitiatedā + √rādh + the gerundive -ya, feminine
231 महाभैरवपूजिता mahā-bhairava-pūjitā
महत्mahatgreatappears as mahā- in a karmadhāraya or bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 6.3.46)
भैरवbhairavaBhairava, the awe-inspiring form of Śivafrom bhīru 'fearful'; traditionally 'the one who bears, sustains and removes (the world)'
पूजिताpūjitāworshipped√pūj, past participle, feminine

Where the names meet

Name 229 is mahā + āsanā (mahāsanā, 'whose seat is great'), not mahā-sanā.

The names

226 महातन्त्रा mahā-tantrā

She who is the great Tantra

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. Formally a bahuvrīhi, 'She whose Tantra is great', with the feminine -ā; in sense it identifies Her with the great Tantra, as names 227 and 228 do with mantra and yantra. No sound change.

Analysis महत् तन्त्रम् यस्याः सा महातन्त्रा
mahat tantram yasyāḥ sā mahātantrā

Significance Traditionally the great Tantras (the Kulārṇava, Jñānārṇava and others) are counted as Her body; She is both what they teach and the teaching itself.

227 महामन्त्रा mahā-mantrā

She who is the greatest mantra

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. Formally 'She whose mantra is great', with the feminine -ā; in sense She is the great mantra itself. No sound change.

Analysis महान् मन्त्रः यस्याः सा महामन्त्रा
mahān mantraḥ yasyāḥ sā mahāmantrā

Significance In Śrīvidyā the great mantra is Her fifteen-syllabled (pañcadaśī) vidyā, which is held to be Her sound-body.

228 महायन्त्रा mahā-yantrā

She who is in the form of the great yantras

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. Formally 'She whose yantra is great', with the feminine -ā; in sense She is the great yantra itself. No sound change.

Analysis महत् यन्त्रम् यस्याः सा महायन्त्रा
mahat yantram yasyāḥ sā mahāyantrā

Significance The great yantra is the Śrīcakra, which in Śrīvidyā is not a symbol of Her but Her very form.

229 महासना mahāsanā

She whose seat is great

Sandhi महासना = महा + आसना (mahā + āsanā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi. 'She whose seat is great'; āsana takes the feminine -ā. Mahā and āsanā fuse by savarṇa-dīrgha, so the name cannot be cut as mahā-sanā.

Analysis महत् आसनम् यस्याः सा महासना
mahat āsanam yasyāḥ sā mahāsanā

Significance Traditionally Her great seat is the whole hierarchy of the tattvas, or the couch formed by the five Brahmās (name 249).

230 महायागक्रमाराध्या mahā-yāga-kramārādhyā

She who is to be worshipped through the ordered rite of the great sacrifice

Sandhi क्रमाराध्या = क्रम + आराध्या (krama + ārādhyā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and karmadhāraya). (1) mahā-yāga 'the great sacrifice' (karmadhāraya). (2) mahāyāga-krama 'the ordered sequence of the great sacrifice' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) The gerundive ārādhyā 'to be worshipped' is the head and takes the sequence in the instrumental: 'to be worshipped by the sequence of the great sacrifice'.

Analysis महान् यागः महायागः; महायागस्य क्रमः महायागक्रमः; महायागक्रमेण आराध्या महायागक्रमाराध्या
mahān yāgaḥ mahāyāgaḥ; mahāyāgasya kramaḥ mahāyāgakramaḥ; mahāyāgakrameṇa ārādhyā mahāyāgakramārādhyā

Significance In Śrīvidyā the mahāyāga is the complete worship of the Śrīcakra, enclosure by enclosure in its prescribed order; inwardly it is the offering of all experience into the fire of consciousness.

231 महाभैरवपूजिता mahā-bhairava-pūjitā

She who is worshipped even by Mahābhairava (Śiva)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (with an inner karmadhāraya). Inner layer: mahā-bhairava 'the great Bhairava' (karmadhāraya). Outer layer: the past participle pūjitā 'worshipped' is the head and takes the agent in the instrumental: 'worshipped by Mahābhairava'.

Analysis महान् भैरवः महाभैरवः; महाभैरवेण पूजिता महाभैरवपूजिता
mahān bhairavaḥ mahābhairavaḥ; mahābhairaveṇa pūjitā mahābhairavapūjitā

Significance Traditionally Śiva as Mahābhairava, the Lord of dissolution, Himself worships Her.

Śloka 57names 232–234

Where the names meet

Name 232 fills the whole first half: Maheśvara's great dance at the end of the great aeon, and She its witness.

The names

232 महेश्वरमहाकल्पमहाताण्डवसाक्षिणी maheśvara-mahā-kalpa-mahā-tāṇḍava-sākṣiṇī

She who is the witness of the great dance of Maheśvara (Śiva) at the end of the great cycle of creation

Sandhi महेश्वर = महा + ईश्वर (mahā + īśvara) — guṇa: a/ā + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ), inside maheśvara 'great lord'

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over inner karmadhāraya, saptamī-tatpuruṣa and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa layers). (1) Three karmadhārayas: maheśvara 'the great Lord', mahā-kalpa 'the great aeon' (whose end is the great dissolution) and mahā-tāṇḍava 'the great dance'. (2) They combine as 'the great dance of Maheśvara at the great aeon('s end)', the Lord in the genitive and the aeon in the locative. (3) sākṣiṇī 'witness' is the head of the whole and takes the dance in the genitive: 'the witness of that dance'.

Analysis महान् ईश्वरः महेश्वरः; महान् कल्पः महाकल्पः; महत् ताण्डवम् महाताण्डवम्; महेश्वरस्य महाकल्पे महाताण्डवम् महेश्वरमहाकल्पमहाताण्डवम्; तस्य साक्षिणी महेश्वरमहाकल्पमहाताण्डवसाक्षिणी
mahān īśvaraḥ maheśvaraḥ; mahān kalpaḥ mahākalpaḥ; mahat tāṇḍavam mahātāṇḍavam; maheśvarasya mahākalpe mahātāṇḍavam maheśvaramahākalpamahātāṇḍavam; tasya sākṣiṇī maheśvaramahākalpamahātāṇḍavasākṣiṇī

Significance When all else is dissolved at the end of the great aeon, Śiva dances and She alone remains to watch; traditionally this shows that She outlasts dissolution itself.

233 महाकामेशमहिषी mahā-kāmeśa-mahiṣī

She who is the great queen of Mahākāmeśvara (Śiva)

Sandhi कामेश = काम + ईश (kāma + īśa) — guṇa: a/ā + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) kāma-īśa 'the Lord of desire', Kāmeśvara (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) mahā-kāmeśa 'the great Kāmeśa' (karmadhāraya). (3) mahiṣī 'chief queen' is the head and takes Him in the genitive.

Analysis कामस्य ईशः कामेशः; महान् कामेशः महाकामेशः; महाकामेशस्य महिषी महाकामेशमहिषी
kāmasya īśaḥ kāmeśaḥ; mahān kāmeśaḥ mahākāmeśaḥ; mahākāmeśasya mahiṣī mahākāmeśamahiṣī

Significance Kāmeśvara is Śiva as Lord of desire, on whose lap She is seated (name 52, śiva-kāmeśvarāṅkasthā).

234 महात्रिपुरसुन्दरी mahā-tripura-sundarī

She who is the great Tripurasundarī, the beautiful one of the three cities

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya (over an inner saptamī-tatpuruṣa and dvigu). (1) tri-pura 'the three cities' (a dvigu of the collective type). (2) tripura-sundarī 'the beautiful one in the three cities', i.e. the most beautiful in all three worlds (saptamī-tatpuruṣa; a genitive reading is also given). (3) mahā- qualifies the whole: 'the great Tripurasundarī'.

Analysis त्रयाणाम् पुराणाम् समाहारः त्रिपुरम्; त्रिपुरे सुन्दरी त्रिपुरसुन्दरी; महती त्रिपुरसुन्दरी महात्रिपुरसुन्दरी
trayāṇām purāṇām samāhāraḥ tripuram; tripure sundarī tripurasundarī; mahatī tripurasundarī mahātripurasundarī

Significance Traditionally tripura is read through every triad — the three worlds, three bodies, three states, three guṇas, three syllable-groups of Her mantra — and She is the beauty that shines through all of them.

Where the names meet

Names 235–237 spell 'sixty-four' with the visarga kept (catuḥṣaṣṭi, Pāṇini 8.3.36 vā śari); catuṣṣaṣṭi is the equally correct assimilated spelling.

The names

235 चतुःषष्ट्युपचाराढ्या catuḥ-ṣaṣṭy-upacārāḍhyā

She who is honored with the sixty-four services of worship

Sandhi चतुःषष्टि = चतुर् + षष्टि (catur + ṣaṣṭi) — visarga: the final r of catur becomes visarga before a sibilant (Pāṇini 8.3.15 kharavasānayor visarjanīyaḥ), and the visarga may stay before ṣ (8.3.36 vā śari); the text keeps it rather than assimilating to catuṣṣaṣṭi; षष्ट्युपचार = षष्टि + उपचार (ṣaṣṭi + upacāra) — yaṇ: i becomes y before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci); उपचाराढ्या = उपचार + आढ्या (upacāra + āḍhyā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya of numeral and noun). (1) catuḥ-ṣaṣṭi 'sixty-four', i.e. 'sixty increased by four' (a karmadhāraya in which the middle word 'increased' is understood). (2) The numeral qualifies upacāra 'service of worship' (a dvigu-type karmadhāraya). (3) āḍhyā 'rich in, endowed with' is the head and takes the services in the instrumental: 'rich in the sixty-four services of worship'.

Analysis चतुरधिका षष्टिः चतुःषष्टिः; चतुःषष्टिः उपचाराः चतुःषष्ट्युपचाराः; चतुःषष्ट्युपचारैः आढ्या चतुःषष्ट्युपचाराढ्या
caturadhikā ṣaṣṭiḥ catuḥṣaṣṭiḥ; catuḥṣaṣṭiḥ upacārāḥ catuḥṣaṣṭyupacārāḥ; catuḥṣaṣṭyupacāraiḥ āḍhyā catuḥṣaṣṭyupacārāḍhyā

Significance In Śrīvidyā the fullest worship offers sixty-four upacāras, the services fit for a sovereign queen; inwardly they are the offering of every faculty to Her.

Corrected चतुष्षष्ट्युपचाराढ्या → चतुःषष्ट्युपचाराढ्या. चतुष्षष्टि → चतुःषष्टि: visarga before ṣ may be kept or assimilated (Pāṇini 8.3.36 vā śari); the verse text keeps it, so the names follow.

236 चतुःषष्टिकलामयी catuḥ-ṣaṣṭi-kalā-mayī

She who embodies the sixty-four fine arts

Sandhi चतुःषष्टि = चतुर् + षष्टि (catur + ṣaṣṭi) — visarga: the final r of catur becomes visarga before a sibilant (Pāṇini 8.3.15 kharavasānayor visarjanīyaḥ), and the visarga may stay before ṣ (8.3.36 vā śari); the text keeps it rather than assimilating to catuṣṣaṣṭi

Compound karmadhāraya of numeral and noun (over an inner karmadhāraya), followed by the taddhita suffix -maya. (1) catuḥ-ṣaṣṭi 'sixty-four'. (2) catuḥṣaṣṭi-kalā 'the sixty-four arts' (numeral + noun). (3) The suffix -maya 'consisting of', feminine -mayī: 'consisting of the sixty-four arts'.

Analysis चतुरधिका षष्टिः चतुःषष्टिः; चतुःषष्टिः कलाः चतुःषष्टिकलाः; चतुःषष्टिकलास्वरूपा चतुःषष्टिकलामयी
caturadhikā ṣaṣṭiḥ catuḥṣaṣṭiḥ; catuḥṣaṣṭiḥ kalāḥ catuḥṣaṣṭikalāḥ; catuḥṣaṣṭikalāsvarūpā catuḥṣaṣṭikalāmayī

Significance The sixty-four arts range from music and painting to the crafts of daily life; traditionally the number also recalls the sixty-four Tantras which, the Saundaryalaharī (31) says, Śiva taught before Her own.

Corrected चतुष्षष्टिकलामयी → चतुःषष्टिकलामयी. As 235.

237 महाचतुःषष्टिकोटियोगिनीगणसेविता mahā-catuḥ-ṣaṣṭi-koṭi-yoginī-gaṇa-sevitā

She who is served by the great hosts of sixty-four crore yoginīs

Sandhi चतुःषष्टि = चतुर् + षष्टि (catur + ṣaṣṭi) — visarga: the final r of catur becomes visarga before a sibilant (Pāṇini 8.3.15 kharavasānayor visarjanīyaḥ), and the visarga may stay before ṣ (8.3.36 vā śari); the text keeps it rather than assimilating to catuṣṣaṣṭi

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over inner karmadhāraya and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa layers). (1) catuḥṣaṣṭi-koṭi 'sixty-four crores' (numeral + noun). (2) mahā- 'great' and the number qualify yoginī, the yoginīs (karmadhāraya). (3) …yoginī-gaṇa 'the hosts of those yoginīs' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (4) The past participle sevitā 'served, attended' is the head and takes the hosts in the instrumental.

Analysis चतुःषष्टिः कोटयः चतुःषष्टिकोटयः; महत्यः चतुःषष्टिकोटयः योगिन्यः महाचतुःषष्टिकोटियोगिन्यः; महाचतुःषष्टिकोटियोगिनीनाम् गणाः महाचतुःषष्टिकोटियोगिनीगणाः; तैः सेविता महाचतुःषष्टिकोटियोगिनीगणसेविता
catuḥṣaṣṭiḥ koṭayaḥ catuḥṣaṣṭikoṭayaḥ; mahatyaḥ catuḥṣaṣṭikoṭayaḥ yoginyaḥ mahācatuḥṣaṣṭikoṭiyoginyaḥ; mahācatuḥṣaṣṭikoṭiyoginīnām gaṇāḥ mahācatuḥṣaṣṭikoṭiyoginīgaṇāḥ; taiḥ sevitā mahācatuḥṣaṣṭikoṭiyoginīgaṇasevitā

Significance Traditionally the yoginīs are attendant powers grouped under the Mothers (mātṛkās) of the Śrīcakra's enclosures; their countless number shows the reach of Her retinue.

Uncertain Whether mahā- qualifies the number, the yoginīs or their hosts is not decided by the grammar; the sense hardly changes.

Corrected महाचतुष्षष्टिकोटियोगिनीगणसेविता → महाचतुःषष्टिकोटियोगिनीगणसेविता. As 235.

Where the names meet

Names 238–239 are two of the traditional twelve forms of the Śrīvidyā mantra, named after their worshippers (Manu, the Moon); names 239–243 gather round the moon.

The names

238 मनुविद्या manu-vidyā

She who is the Manuvidyā, the form of Her mantra worshipped by Manu

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. vidyā 'mantra-knowledge' is the head and Manu stands to it in the genitive: 'the vidyā of Manu', the form of the mantra that Manu worshipped. Juxtaposition.

Analysis मनोः विद्या मनुविद्या
manoḥ vidyā manuvidyā

Significance Traditionally twelve great devotees — among them Manu, Candra, Kubera, Lopāmudrā, Agastya and Kāma — each worshipped Her through a form of the Śrīvidyā mantra; names 238 and 239 name two of them.

239 चन्द्रविद्या candra-vidyā

She who is the Candravidyā, the form of Her mantra worshipped by the Moon

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. 'The vidyā of Candra (the Moon)', the form of Her mantra worshipped by the Moon. Juxtaposition.

Analysis चन्द्रस्य विद्या चन्द्रविद्या
candrasya vidyā candravidyā

Significance Another of the twelve traditional forms of the Śrīvidyā mantra, named after the devotee who worshipped Her through it.

240 चन्द्रमण्डलमध्यगा candra-maṇḍala-madhyagā

She who resides in the center of the moon's disc

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (1) candra-maṇḍala 'the disc of the moon' and (2) …maṇḍala-madhya 'its center' are ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas. (3) -gā 'going, being in' (from √gam) is the head and takes the center as its place: 'She who abides in the center of the moon's disc'.

Analysis चन्द्रस्य मण्डलम् चन्द्रमण्डलम्; चन्द्रमण्डलस्य मध्यम् चन्द्रमण्डलमध्यम्; चन्द्रमण्डलमध्ये गच्छति तिष्ठति इति चन्द्रमण्डलमध्यगा
candrasya maṇḍalam candramaṇḍalam; candramaṇḍalasya madhyam candramaṇḍalamadhyam; candramaṇḍalamadhye gacchati tiṣṭhati iti candramaṇḍalamadhyagā

Significance Traditionally the lunar disc is also inward: the cool, nectar-dropping moon in the thousand-petalled lotus at the crown of the head, where She is meditated upon.

241 चारुरूपा cāru-rūpā

She whose form is beautiful

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. 'She whose form is beautiful'; rūpa takes the feminine -ā. Juxtaposition.

Analysis चारु रूपम् यस्याः सा चारुरूपा
cāru rūpam yasyāḥ sā cārurūpā

Significance Traditionally Her beauty, unlike the moon's of the previous names, neither waxes nor wanes.

242 चारुहासा cāru-hāsā

She who has a beautiful smile

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. 'She whose smile is beautiful'; hāsa takes the feminine -ā. Juxtaposition.

Analysis चारुः हासः यस्याः सा चारुहासा
cāruḥ hāsaḥ yasyāḥ sā cāruhāsā

Significance Traditionally Her smile is the visible sign of Her grace, and the devotee's sorrow dissolves before it.

243 चारुचन्द्रकलाधरा cāru-candra-kalā-dharā

She who wears a lovely crescent moon

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) candra-kalā 'a digit of the moon', the crescent (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) cāru 'lovely' qualifies it (karmadhāraya; the feminine cārvī takes the masculine stem cāru). (3) -dharā 'bearing, wearing' (√dhṛ + -a) is the head and governs the crescent as its object.

Analysis चन्द्रस्य कला चन्द्रकला; चार्वी चन्द्रकला चारुचन्द्रकला; चारुचन्द्रकलाम् धरति इति चारुचन्द्रकलाधरा
candrasya kalā candrakalā; cārvī candrakalā cārucandrakalā; cārucandrakalām dharati iti cārucandrakalādharā

Significance Traditionally the crescent on Her crown is the eternal digit that never waxes or wanes.

Where the names meet

Name 248: padmarāga 'lotus-hued' is the ruby; rāga here means color, not passion.

The names

244 चराचरजगन्नाथा carācara-jagan-nāthā

She who is the ruler of the animate and inanimate worlds

Sandhi चराचर = चर + अचर (cara + acara) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); जगन्नाथा = जगत् + नाथा (jagat + nāthā) — a stop becomes the nasal of its class before a nasal: t → n (Pāṇini 8.4.45 yaro 'nunāsike 'nunāsiko vā)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya and samāhāra-dvandva). (1) cara-acara 'the moving and the unmoving' (dvandva; carācara is also explained as a reduplicated adjective from √car). (2) It qualifies jagat 'world' (karmadhāraya). (3) nāthā 'mistress, ruler', the feminine of nātha, is the head and takes the world in the genitive.

Analysis चरम् च अचरम् च चराचरम्; चराचरम् जगत् चराचरजगत्; चराचरजगतः नाथा चराचरजगन्नाथा
caram ca acaram ca carācaram; carācaram jagat carācarajagat; carācarajagataḥ nāthā carācarajagannāthā

Significance Nātha is a protector as well as a ruler; traditionally She guards every being, moving or still, as Her own.

245 चक्रराजनिकेतना cakra-rāja-niketanā

She whose abode is the king of cakras, the Śrīcakra

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (with an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). Inner layer: cakra-rāja 'the king of cakras' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; rājan becomes rāja at the end of a tatpuruṣa, Pāṇini 5.4.91 rājāhaḥsakhibhyaṣ ṭac). Outer layer: a bahuvrīhi, 'She whose abode is the king of cakras'; niketana takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis चक्राणाम् राजा चक्रराजः; चक्रराजः निकेतनम् यस्याः सा चक्रराजनिकेतना
cakrāṇām rājā cakrarājaḥ; cakrarājaḥ niketanam yasyāḥ sā cakrarājaniketanā

Significance The Śrīcakra is called the king of cakras; She dwells in it as in Her own palace, and in Śrīvidyā it is identical with Her body and with the body of the worshipper.

246 पार्वती pārvatī

She who is the daughter of the Mountain (Himavat)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance As Pārvatī, daughter of Himavat, the supreme Goddess enters the Purāṇic story as the consort whom Śiva wins and who wins Śiva by austerity.

247 पद्मनयना padma-nayanā

She whose eyes are like lotuses

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (with an inner upamāna relation). 'She whose eyes are like lotuses': padma is the standard of comparison for nayana, and the whole is a bahuvrīhi; nayana takes the feminine -ā. Juxtaposition.

Analysis पद्मे इव नयने यस्याः सा पद्मनयना
padme iva nayane yasyāḥ sā padmanayanā

Significance Lotus eyes are long, soft and wide open; traditionally they are also eyes that look on all with compassion.

248 पद्मरागसमप्रभा padma-rāga-sama-prabhā

She whose radiance equals that of the ruby

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner bahuvrīhi and tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (1) padma-rāga 'lotus-hued', the ruby (a bahuvrīhi that has become a noun). (2) padmarāga-samā 'equal to the ruby' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa: words of equality govern the instrumental). (3) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose radiance is equal to that of the ruby'; sama takes the masculine stem before prabhā (puṃvadbhāva).

Analysis पद्मस्य इव रागः यस्य सः पद्मरागः; पद्मरागेण समा पद्मरागसमा; पद्मरागसमा प्रभा यस्याः सा पद्मरागसमप्रभा
padmasya iva rāgaḥ yasya saḥ padmarāgaḥ; padmarāgeṇa samā padmarāgasamā; padmarāgasamā prabhā yasyāḥ sā padmarāgasamaprabhā

Significance The ruby-red continues the crimson of Her form (names 6 and 12); in Śrīvidyā the red is the color of compassion and of vimarśa, Her self-awareness.

Śloka 61names 249–253

pañcapretāsanāsīnā pañcabrahmasvarūpiṇī |

Translation

251She who is consciousness itself; 252She who is supreme bliss; 253She whose form is a solid mass of pure consciousness.

SanskritEnglish
249 पञ्चप्रेतासनासीना pañca-pretāsanāsīnā

आसीनाāsīnāseated, sitting√ās, middle participle, feminine
250 पञ्चब्रह्मस्वरूपिणी pañca-brahma-svarūpiṇī
पञ्चन्pañcanfiveappears as pañca- (final n dropped, Pāṇini 8.2.7)
ब्रह्मन्brahmanhere: one of the five Brahmās, the deities of the five cosmic actsappears as brahma- (final n dropped)
स्वरूपिणीsvarūpiṇīwhose own form is, having the nature ofsva 'own' + rūpa 'form' + the possessive suffix -in, feminine

विज्ञानvijñānaconsciousness, knowingvi + √jñā 'to know'
घनghanadense, compact, a solid mass
रूपिणीrūpiṇīhaving the form ofrūpa + the possessive suffix -in, feminine

Where the names meet

Names 249–250 pair the five Brahmās (Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Īśvara, Sadāśiva): lifeless as Her seat, alive as Her form. Names 251–253 then name Her as consciousness and bliss.

The names

249 पञ्चप्रेतासनासीना pañca-pretāsanāsīnā

She who sits on the seat formed by the five corpses

Sandhi प्रेतासन = प्रेत + आसन (preta + āsana) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); आसनासीना = आसन + आसीना (āsana + āsīnā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound saptamī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya of identification and a numeral compound). (1) pañca-preta 'the five pretas' (numeral compound). (2) pañcapreta-āsana 'the seat that is the five pretas', a karmadhāraya of identification: the five are themselves the seat. (3) The participle āsīnā 'seated' is the head and takes the seat in the locative: 'seated on the seat of the five pretas'.

Analysis पञ्च प्रेताः पञ्चप्रेताः; पञ्चप्रेताः एव आसनम् पञ्चप्रेतासनम्; पञ्चप्रेतासने आसीना पञ्चप्रेतासनासीना
pañca pretāḥ pañcapretāḥ; pañcapretāḥ eva āsanam pañcapretāsanam; pañcapretāsane āsīnā pañcapretāsanāsīnā

Significance In Śrīvidyā the five pretas are Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra and Īśvara as the four legs of Her couch and Sadāśiva as its plank: without Her power even these gods are lifeless, and only as Her seat do they act.

250 पञ्चब्रह्मस्वरूपिणी pañca-brahma-svarūpiṇī

She whose own form is the five Brahmās

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (with an inner numeral compound), followed by the possessive suffix -in. (1) pañca-brahma 'the five Brahmās' (numeral compound; brahman drops its final n, 8.2.7). (2) …brahma-svarūpa 'the own form of the five Brahmās' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) The possessive suffix -in, feminine -inī: 'She who has the own form of the five Brahmās', i.e. who is their very nature. Juxtaposition throughout.

Analysis पञ्च ब्रह्माणः पञ्चब्रह्माणः; पञ्चब्रह्मणाम् स्वरूपम् पञ्चब्रह्मस्वरूपम्; तत् अस्याः अस्ति इति पञ्चब्रह्मस्वरूपिणी
pañca brahmāṇaḥ pañcabrahmāṇaḥ; pañcabrahmaṇām svarūpam pañcabrahmasvarūpam; tat asyāḥ asti iti pañcabrahmasvarūpiṇī

Significance The same five gods who are Her lifeless seat in name 249 are, as active powers, nothing but Her own form: they act only as She acts through them.

Corrected पञ्चब्रह्मस्वरुपिणी → पञ्चब्रह्मस्वरूपिणी. स्वरुपिणी → स्वरूपिणी (svarūpa: long ū).

251 चिन्मयी cin-mayī

She who is consciousness itself

Sandhi चिन्मयी = चित् + मयी (cit + mayī) — a stop becomes the nasal of its class before a nasal: t → n (Pāṇini 8.4.45 yaro 'nunāsike 'nunāsiko vā)

Compound not a compound

Significance She does not have consciousness as a quality; She consists of it, as Vedānta says of Brahman.

252 परमानन्दा paramānandā

She who is supreme bliss

Sandhi परमानन्दा = परम + आनन्दा (parama + ānandā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (with an inner karmadhāraya). Inner layer: parama 'supreme' qualifies ānanda 'bliss' (karmadhāraya). Applied to Her it takes the feminine -ā, as a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose very nature is supreme bliss'.

Analysis परमः आनन्दः परमानन्दः; परमानन्दः स्वरूपम् यस्याः सा परमानन्दा
paramaḥ ānandaḥ paramānandaḥ; paramānandaḥ svarūpam yasyāḥ sā paramānandā

Significance The Taittirīya Upaniṣad (3.6) teaches that Brahman is bliss, from which all beings arise; She is that bliss.

253 विज्ञानघनरूपिणी vijñāna-ghana-rūpiṇī

She whose form is a solid mass of pure consciousness

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya (over an inner tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa), followed by the possessive suffix -in. (1) vijñāna-ghana 'dense with consciousness alone', a solid mass of consciousness (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (2) It qualifies rūpa 'form' (karmadhāraya). (3) The possessive suffix -in, feminine -inī: 'She who has a form that is a mass of consciousness'.

Analysis विज्ञानेन घनः विज्ञानघनः; विज्ञानघनम् रूपम् विज्ञानघनरूपम्; तत् अस्याः अस्ति इति विज्ञानघनरूपिणी
vijñānena ghanaḥ vijñānaghanaḥ; vijñānaghanam rūpam vijñānaghanarūpam; tat asyāḥ asti iti vijñānaghanarūpiṇī

Significance The Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad (2.4.12) calls the Self 'vijñānaghana eva', nothing but a mass of consciousness, like a lump of salt that is salty through and through.

Śloka 62names 254–259

ध्यानध्यातृध्येयरूपा धर्माधर्मविवर्जिता ।
विश्वरूपा जागरिणी स्वपन्ती तैजसात्मिका ॥ ६२ ॥

dhyānadhyātṛdhyeyarūpā dharmādharmavivarjitā |
viśvarūpā jāgariṇī svapantī taijasātmikā || 62 ||

The names, separated

254ध्यान-ध्यातृ-ध्येय-रूपाdhyāna-dhyātṛ-dhyeya-rūpā255धर्माधर्म-विवर्जिताdharmādharma-vivarjitā

254She whose form is meditation, the meditator and the object of meditation; 255She who is devoid of (who transcends) both virtue and vice;

Word by word

SanskritEnglish

ध्यानdhyānameditation√dhyai + -ana

Where the names meet

Names 256–263 follow the states of the self in the Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad: waking (Viśva), dream (Taijasa), deep sleep (Prājña), the Fourth (turya) and beyond all states.

The names

254 ध्यानध्यातृध्येयरूपा dhyāna-dhyātṛ-dhyeya-rūpā

She whose form is meditation, the meditator and the object of meditation

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (with an inner itaretara-dvandva). Inner layer: a dvandva of three derivatives of √dhyai 'to meditate' — dhyāna 'meditation', dhyātṛ 'meditator', dhyeya 'what is to be meditated upon'. Outer layer: a bahuvrīhi, 'She whose form is these three'; rūpa takes the feminine -ā. Juxtaposition throughout.

Analysis ध्यानम् च ध्याता च ध्येयम् च ध्यानध्यातृध्येयानि; ध्यानध्यातृध्येयानि रूपम् यस्याः सा ध्यानध्यातृध्येयरूपा
dhyānam ca dhyātā ca dhyeyam ca dhyānadhyātṛdhyeyāni; dhyānadhyātṛdhyeyāni rūpam yasyāḥ sā dhyānadhyātṛdhyeyarūpā

Significance The triad of knower, knowing and known (tripuṭī) is all Her; when it is seen as one, meditation reaches its end.

255 धर्माधर्मविवर्जिता dharmādharma-vivarjitā

She who is devoid of (who transcends) both virtue and vice

Sandhi धर्माधर्म = धर्म + अधर्म (dharma + adharma) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (with an inner itaretara-dvandva). Inner layer: dharma 'merit, virtue' and adharma 'demerit' form a dvandva. Outer layer: the participle vivarjitā 'wholly free from' is the head and takes the pair in the instrumental.

Analysis धर्मः च अधर्मः च धर्माधर्मौ; धर्माधर्माभ्याम् विवर्जिता धर्माधर्मविवर्जिता
dharmaḥ ca adharmaḥ ca dharmādharmau; dharmādharmābhyām vivarjitā dharmādharmavivarjitā

Significance Merit and demerit bind only one who acts as a separate agent; the Kaṭha Upaniṣad speaks of That which is other than dharma and other than adharma.

256 विश्वरूपा viśva-rūpā

She who has the whole universe as Her form

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. 'She whose form is the universe'; rūpa takes the feminine -ā. Juxtaposition. In this sequence the name can also be read 'She who has the form of Viśva', the self of the waking state.

Analysis विश्वम् रूपम् यस्याः सा विश्वरूपा
viśvam rūpam yasyāḥ sā viśvarūpā

Significance Names 256–263 follow the states of the self in the Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad; here She is the universe, and also Viśva, the self as experiencer of the waking world.

Corrected विश्वरुपा → विश्वरूपा. विश्वरुपा → विश्वरूपा (rūpa: long ū).

257 जागरिणी jāgariṇī

She who is in the waking state, or She who assumes the form of the jīva who is in the waking state

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Traditionally She is both the waking state itself and the individual (jīva) who experiences it.

258 स्वपन्ती svapantī

She who is in the dream state, or She who assumes the form of the jīva in the dream state

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance As dreamer She creates and enjoys a world of Her own making, a picture of how the whole universe is Her projection.

Uncertain By Pāṇini (7.1.80–81) the feminine participle of the class-2 root svap (svapiti) would be svapatī; svapantī follows the thematic inflection (svapati) found in epic usage. The text reads svapantī and the metre is the same either way.

259 तैजसात्मिका taijasātmikā

She whose self is Taijasa, the dreaming self

Sandhi तैजसात्मिका = तैजस + आत्मिका (taijasa + ātmikā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi. 'She whose self is Taijasa'; ātman takes the suffix -ka and the feminine -ikā (a → i, Pāṇini 7.3.44).

Analysis तैजसः आत्मा यस्याः सा तैजसात्मिका
taijasaḥ ātmā yasyāḥ sā taijasātmikā

Significance The Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad names the dreaming self Taijasa, 'the luminous', because in dream it is lit by its own light; it is identified with the subtle body.

Śloka 63names 260–267

सुप्ता प्राज्ञात्मिका तुर्या सर्वावस्थाविवर्जिता ।
सृष्टिकर्त्री ब्रह्मरूपा गोप्त्री गोविन्दरूपिणी ॥ ६३ ॥

suptā prājñātmikā turyā sarvāvasthāvivarjitā |
sṛṣṭikartrī brahmarūpā goptrī govindarūpiṇī || 63 ||

The names, separated

260सुप्ताsuptā261प्राज्ञात्मिकाprājñātmikā262तुर्याturyā263सर्वावस्था-विवर्जिताsarvāvasthā-vivarjitā

264सृष्टि-कर्त्रीsṛṣṭi-kartrī265ब्रह्म-रूपाbrahma-rūpā266गोप्त्रीgoptrī267गोविन्द-रूपिणीgovinda-rūpiṇī

264She who is the creator; 265She who has the form of Brahmā, the creator; 266She who protects; 267She who has assumed the form of Govinda (Viṣṇu) for the preservation of the universe.
