Where the names meet

Names 264–274 set out the five cosmic acts with their deities: creation (Brahmā), protection (Govinda), dissolution (Rudra), concealment (Īśvara) and grace (Sadāśiva).

The names

260 सुप्ता suptā

She who is in the deep-sleep state or assumes the form of the jīva experiencing deep sleep

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance In deep sleep all distinctions rest in Her, as the world rests in Her at dissolution.

261 प्राज्ञात्मिका prājñātmikā

She whose self is Prājña, the self in deep sleep

Sandhi प्राज्ञात्मिका = प्राज्ञ + आत्मिका (prājña + ātmikā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi. 'She whose self is Prājña'; ātman takes -ka and the feminine -ikā, as in name 259.

Analysis प्राज्ञः आत्मा यस्याः सा प्राज्ञात्मिका
prājñaḥ ātmā yasyāḥ sā prājñātmikā

Significance The Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad calls the self in deep sleep Prājña, a mass of knowing made of bliss; it is identified with the causal body.

262 तुर्या turyā

She who is the Fourth (turya), the state beyond waking, dream and deep sleep

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance The Māṇḍūkya Upaniṣad calls the Self beyond the three states 'the fourth': not a further state but the witness present in all three.

263 सर्वावस्थाविवर्जिता sarvāvasthā-vivarjitā

She who transcends all states

Sandhi सर्वावस्था = सर्व + अवस्था (sarva + avasthā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (with an inner karmadhāraya). Inner layer: sarva-avasthā 'all states' (karmadhāraya). Outer layer: vivarjitā 'wholly free from' is the head and takes the states in the instrumental.

Analysis सर्वाः अवस्थाः सर्वावस्थाः; सर्वावस्थाभिः विवर्जिता सर्वावस्थाविवर्जिता
sarvāḥ avasthāḥ sarvāvasthāḥ; sarvāvasthābhiḥ vivarjitā sarvāvasthāvivarjitā

Significance Traditionally this is the state beyond even the fourth (turyātīta): She is not touched by any state, the fourth included.

264 सृष्टिकर्त्री sṛṣṭi-kartrī

She who is the creator

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. kartrī 'maker', the feminine of the agent noun kartṛ, is the head and sṛṣṭi 'creation' stands to it in the genitive: 'the maker of creation'. Juxtaposition.

Analysis सृष्टेः कर्त्री सृष्टिकर्त्री
sṛṣṭeḥ kartrī sṛṣṭikartrī

Significance Names 264–274 set out the five cosmic acts — creation, protection, dissolution, concealment and grace — each with its presiding deity; here She creates, as Brahmā (name 265).

Uncertain Pāṇini 2.2.15 restricts compounding a genitive with an agent noun in -tṛ; compounds like sṛṣṭi-kartṛ are nevertheless standard in usage and are usually explained as a general genitive (śeṣa-ṣaṣṭhī).

265 ब्रह्मरूपा brahma-rūpā

She who has the form of Brahmā, the creator

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. 'She whose form is Brahmā'; brahman drops its final n in composition and rūpa takes the feminine -ā. Juxtaposition.

Analysis ब्रह्मा रूपम् यस्याः सा ब्रह्मरूपा
brahmā rūpam yasyāḥ sā brahmarūpā

Significance In the sequence of cosmic acts She creates as Brahmā; read with the neuter brahman, the name also says She is the Absolute itself.

266 गोप्त्री goptrī

She who protects

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance The second of the cosmic acts, protection or maintenance (sthiti), which She performs as Govinda (name 267).

267 गोविन्दरूपिणी govinda-rūpiṇī

She who has assumed the form of Govinda (Viṣṇu) for the preservation of the universe

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, followed by the possessive suffix -in. govinda-rūpa 'the form of Govinda' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa), with the possessive suffix -in, feminine -inī: 'She who has the form of Govinda'. Juxtaposition.

Analysis गोविन्दस्य रूपम् गोविन्दरूपम्; तत् अस्याः अस्ति इति गोविन्दरूपिणी
govindasya rūpam govindarūpam; tat asyāḥ asti iti govindarūpiṇī

Significance As Viṣṇu She sustains the worlds; the gods of the five acts are Her forms, not powers beside Her.

Śloka 64names 268–274

संहारिणी रुद्ररूपा तिरोधानकरीश्वरी ।
सदाशिवा ऽनुग्रहदा पञ्चकृत्यपरायणा ॥ ६४ ॥

saṃhāriṇī rudrarūpā tirodhānakarīśvarī |
sadāśivā 'nugrahadā pañcakṛtyaparāyaṇā || 64 ||

The names, separated ° form as a name on its own; in the recitation above it joins its neighbour

268संहारिणीsaṃhāriṇī269रुद्र-रूपाrudra-rūpā270तिरोधान-करी°tirodhāna-karī271ईश्वरी°īśvarī

272सदा-शिवाsadā-śivā273अनुग्रह-दा°anugraha-dā274पञ्च-कृत्य-परायणाpañca-kṛtya-parāyaṇā

Translation

268She who is the destroyer of the universe; 269She who has assumed the form of Rudra (Śiva) for the dissolution of the universe; 270She who brings about concealment (tirodhāna); 271She who is the Sovereign, Īśvarī;

272She who is Sadāśiva, the ever-auspicious; 273She who confers blessing; 274She who is devoted to the five functions (creation, preservation, dissolution, concealment and grace).

Word by word

SanskritEnglish
268 संहारिणी saṃhāriṇī
सम्samtogether, completely (prefix)appears as saṃ- before h
हारिणीhāriṇīshe who takes away, withdraws√hṛ 'to take' + the agent suffix -in, feminine -inī
269 रुद्ररूपा rudra-rūpā
रुद्रrudraRudra, Śiva as the lord of dissolution
रूपाrūpāformrūpa, with the feminine -ā
270 तिरोधानकरी tirodhāna-karī
तिरस्tirasout of sight, hidden (indeclinable)appears as tiro- before dh
धानdhānaplacing, putting√dhā 'to put'
करीkarīshe who makes, causes√kṛ + -a, feminine -ī
271 ईश्वरी īśvarī
ईश्वरीīśvarīsovereign, ruling ladyfeminine of īśvara, from √īś 'to rule'
272 सदाशिवा sadā-śivā
सदाsadāalways, ever (indeclinable)
शिवाśivāauspicious, benign; the consort of Śivafeminine of śiva
273 अनुग्रहदा anugraha-dā
अनुग्रहanugrahagrace, favor, blessing (lit. 'taking hold of after')anu + √grah 'to seize'
दाdāgiving, bestowing√dā 'to give', feminine
274 पञ्चकृत्यपरायणा pañca-kṛtya-parāyaṇā
पञ्चन्pañcanfiveappears as pañca- (final n dropped, Pāṇini 8.2.7)
कृत्यkṛtyaact, function√kṛ + the gerundive suffix -ya: 'what is to be done'
परायणाparāyaṇāwholly devoted to, intent onpara 'highest' + ayana 'goal, resort', feminine

Where the names meet

तिरोधानकरीश्वरी = तिरोधानकरी + ईश्वरी (tirodhānakarī + īśvarī) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ī + ī → ī (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

सदाशिवाऽनुग्रहदा = सदाशिवा + अनुग्रहदा (sadāśivā + anugrahadā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā; the avagraha (ऽ) marks the a absorbed at the start of the next name

Bhāskararāya's division reads tirodhānakarīśvarī as two names, tirodhānakarī (270) and īśvarī (271): the long ī belongs to both. Likewise sadāśivā'nugrahadā is sadāśivā (272) + anugrahadā (273), the avagraha showing the elided a.

The names

268 संहारिणी saṃhāriṇī

She who is the destroyer of the universe

Sandhi संहारिणी = सम् + हारिणी (sam + hāriṇī) — the final m of the prefix sam becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ)

Compound not a compound

Significance Saṃhāra is a 'drawing together': at dissolution She withdraws the worlds into Herself as a tortoise draws in its limbs.

269 रुद्ररूपा rudra-rūpā

She who has assumed the form of Rudra (Śiva) for the dissolution of the universe

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. 'She whose form is Rudra'; rūpa takes the feminine -ā. Juxtaposition.

Analysis रुद्रः रूपम् यस्याः सा रुद्ररूपा
rudraḥ rūpam yasyāḥ sā rudrarūpā

Significance Dissolution, the third cosmic act, She performs as Rudra.

270 तिरोधानकरी tirodhāna-karī

She who brings about concealment (tirodhāna)

Sandhi तिरोधान = तिरस् + धान (tiras + dhāna) — the s of tiras becomes u before a voiced consonant and combines with the preceding a as o (Pāṇini 6.1.114 haśi ca; 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. -karī 'making, causing' (√kṛ with the suffix -a, feminine -ī) is the head and takes tirodhāna 'concealment' as its object. Tirodhāna itself is tiras 'out of sight' + dhāna 'placing', i.e. hiding from view.

Analysis तिरोधानम् करोति इति तिरोधानकरी
tirodhānam karoti iti tirodhānakarī

Significance Concealment, the fourth cosmic act, is the veiling by which She hides Her own nature so that the play of the world can go on; it is performed as Īśvara (name 271).

271 ईश्वरी īśvarī

She who is the Sovereign, Īśvarī

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance In the sequence of the five acts She is the power of Īśvara, the deity of concealment; read on its own, the name makes Her ruler of all.

272 सदाशिवा sadā-śivā

She who is Sadāśiva, the ever-auspicious

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya (supsupā). The indeclinable sadā 'always' qualifies śivā 'auspicious, benign', the head: 'ever auspicious'. As a name it is the feminine of Sadāśiva, the deity of the fifth act. Juxtaposition.

Analysis सदा शिवा सदाशिवा
sadā śivā sadāśivā

Significance Sadāśiva is the deity of grace (anugraha), the fifth act, named in the next name.

273 अनुग्रहदा anugraha-dā

She who confers blessing

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. -dā 'giving' (√dā with the suffix -a, feminine -ā) is the head and takes anugraha 'grace' as its object.

Analysis अनुग्रहम् ददाति इति अनुग्रहदा
anugraham dadāti iti anugrahadā

Significance Grace (anugraha) is the fifth cosmic act, which ends concealment and reveals the Self; it is the act by which She frees.

274 पञ्चकृत्यपरायणा pañca-kṛtya-parāyaṇā

She who is devoted to the five functions (creation, preservation, dissolution, concealment and grace)

Sandhi परायणा = पर + अयना (para + ayanā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); the n of ayana then becomes ṇ after the r of para (retroflexion)

Compound saptamī-tatpuruṣa (with an inner numeral compound). (1) pañca-kṛtya 'the five acts' (numeral compound). (2) parāyaṇā 'wholly given to, intent on' — itself para 'highest' + ayana 'goal', 'having as highest goal' — is the head and takes the acts in the locative.

Analysis पञ्च कृत्यानि पञ्चकृत्यानि; पञ्चकृत्येषु परायणा पञ्चकृत्यपरायणा
pañca kṛtyāni pañcakṛtyāni; pañcakṛtyeṣu parāyaṇā pañcakṛtyaparāyaṇā

Significance Names 264–273 have named the five acts with their deities; this name gathers them, for She alone performs them all.

Śloka 65names 275–280

भानुमण्डलमध्यस्था भैरवी भगमालिनी ।
पद्मासना भगवती पद्मनाभसहोदरी ॥ ६५ ॥

bhānumaṇḍalamadhyasthā bhairavī bhagamālinī |
padmāsanā bhagavatī padmanābhasahodarī || 65 ||

The names, separated

275भानु-मण्डल-मध्य-स्थाbhānu-maṇḍala-madhya-sthā276भैरवीbhairavī277भग-मालिनीbhaga-mālinī

278पद्मासनाpadmāsanā279भगवतीbhagavatī280पद्म-नाभ-सहोदरीpadma-nābha-sahodarī

Translation

275She who abides at the center of the sun's disc; 276She who is the wife of Bhairava (Śiva); 277She who wears a garland made of the six excellences (of auspiciousness, supremacy, fame, valor, detachment and knowledge);

278She who is seated in the lotus flower; 279She who is the Blessed One, possessed of all six excellences; 280She who is the sister of Padmanābha (Viṣṇu).

Where the names meet

Name 277 Bhagamālinī is also the second of the fifteen Nityā goddesses; names 277 and 279 both turn on bhaga, the six divine excellences.

The names

275 भानुमण्डलमध्यस्था bhānu-maṇḍala-madhya-sthā

She who abides at the center of the sun's disc

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (1) bhānu-maṇḍala 'the disc of the sun' and (2) …maṇḍala-madhya 'its center' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (3) -sthā 'standing, abiding' (√sthā + -a, Pāṇini 3.2.4 supi sthaḥ) is the head and takes the center as its place.

Analysis भानोः मण्डलम् भानुमण्डलम्; भानुमण्डलस्य मध्यम् भानुमण्डलमध्यम्; भानुमण्डलमध्ये तिष्ठति इति भानुमण्डलमध्यस्था
bhānoḥ maṇḍalam bhānumaṇḍalam; bhānumaṇḍalasya madhyam bhānumaṇḍalamadhyam; bhānumaṇḍalamadhye tiṣṭhati iti bhānumaṇḍalamadhyasthā

Significance Traditionally She is meditated upon in the sun's orb at the twilight worship (sandhyā), as the light within the light; compare name 240, the moon's disc.

276 भैरवी bhairavī

She who is the wife of Bhairava (Śiva)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Bhairavī is also the Goddess in Her own awe-inspiring form, worshipped as Tripurabhairavī among the great Wisdom Goddesses.

277 भगमालिनी bhaga-mālinī

She who wears a garland made of the six excellences (of auspiciousness, supremacy, fame, valor, detachment and knowledge)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, followed by the possessive suffix -in. bhaga-mālā 'a garland of excellences' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa), with the possessive suffix -in, feminine -inī: 'She who has (wears) a garland of excellences'. Juxtaposition.

Analysis भगानाम् माला भगमाला; सा अस्याः अस्ति इति भगमालिनी
bhagānām mālā bhagamālā; sā asyāḥ asti iti bhagamālinī

Significance The Viṣṇu Purāṇa defines bhaga as the six excellences — sovereignty, valor, fame, prosperity, knowledge and dispassion. Bhagamālinī is also the second of the fifteen Nityā goddesses of the Śrīcakra.

278 पद्मासना padmāsanā

She who is seated in the lotus flower

Sandhi पद्मासना = पद्म + आसना (padma + āsanā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi. 'She whose seat is a lotus'; āsana takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis पद्मम् आसनम् यस्याः सा पद्मासना
padmam āsanam yasyāḥ sā padmāsanā

Significance Traditionally the lotus is also inward: She is seated in the lotuses (cakras) of the body, and in the thousand-petalled lotus above them.

279 भगवती bhagavatī

She who is the Blessed One, possessed of all six excellences

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance The Viṣṇu Purāṇa calls Bhagavān the one who has the six excellences, and the one who knows the arising and dissolution of beings, their coming and going, knowledge and ignorance; She is Bhagavatī in that full sense.

280 पद्मनाभसहोदरी padma-nābha-sahodarī

She who is the sister of Padmanābha (Viṣṇu)

Sandhi सहोदरी = सह + उदरी (saha + udarī) — guṇa: a + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner bahuvrīhi). Inner layer: padma-nābha 'He in whose navel is a lotus', Viṣṇu (bahuvrīhi; nābhi 'navel' takes the form nābha at the end of the compound). Outer layer: sahodarī 'sister' (lit. 'of the same womb') is the head and takes Him in the genitive.

Analysis पद्मम् नाभौ यस्य सः पद्मनाभः; पद्मनाभस्य सहोदरी पद्मनाभसहोदरी
padmam nābhau yasya saḥ padmanābhaḥ; padmanābhasya sahodarī padmanābhasahodarī

Significance Traditionally Pārvatī is Viṣṇu's sister; in Śrīvidyā the two are one power, appearing as Viṣṇu in male form and as the Goddess in female form.

Śloka 66names 281–284

उन्मेषनिमिषोत्पन्नविपन्नभुवनावली ।
सहस्रशीर्षवदना सहस्राक्षी सहस्रपात् ॥ ६६ ॥

sahasraśīrṣavadanā sahasrākṣī sahasrapāt || 66 ||

282She who has a thousand heads and faces; 283She who has a thousand eyes; 284She who has a thousand feet.

Where the names meet

Name 281 fills the whole first half; names 282–284 echo the Puruṣa-sūkta ('sahasraśīrṣā puruṣaḥ sahasrākṣaḥ sahasrapāt').

The names

281 उन्मेषनिमिषोत्पन्नविपन्नभुवनावली unmeṣa-nimiṣotpanna-vipanna-bhuvanāvalī

She at the opening and closing of whose eyes whole rows of worlds arise and perish

Sandhi उन्मेष = उत् + मेष (ut + meṣa) — a stop becomes the nasal of its class before a nasal: t → n (Pāṇini 8.4.45 yaro 'nunāsike 'nunāsiko vā); निमिषोत्पन्न = निमिष + उत्पन्न (nimiṣa + utpanna) — guṇa: a + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ); भुवनावली = भुवन + आवली (bhuvana + āvalī) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner itaretara-dvandva, a karmadhāraya of two participles and a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) unmeṣa-nimiṣa 'the opening and the closing (of the eyes)' (dvandva). (2) utpanna-vipanna 'arisen and perished', two participles joined as a karmadhāraya, taken in order with the dvandva: arising with the opening, perishing with the closing. (3) bhuvana-āvalī 'the row of worlds' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (4) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She by whose opening and closing of the eyes rows of worlds arise and perish'.

Analysis उन्मेषः च निमिषः च उन्मेषनिमिषौ; उत्पन्ना च विपन्ना च उत्पन्नविपन्ना; भुवनानाम् आवली भुवनावली; उन्मेषनिमिषाभ्याम् उत्पन्नविपन्ना भुवनावली यस्याः सा उन्मेषनिमिषोत्पन्नविपन्नभुवनावली
unmeṣaḥ ca nimiṣaḥ ca unmeṣanimiṣau; utpannā ca vipannā ca utpannavipannā; bhuvanānām āvalī bhuvanāvalī; unmeṣanimiṣābhyām utpannavipannā bhuvanāvalī yasyāḥ sā unmeṣanimiṣotpannavipannabhuvanāvalī

Significance Creation and dissolution cost Her no more than a blink. In Kashmir Śaivism unmeṣa and nimeṣa are also the unfolding and infolding of consciousness, by which the world appears and withdraws.

Uncertain A bahuvrīhi ending in an ī-stem like āvalī would by Pāṇini 5.4.153 normally take the suffix -ka (…āvalīkā); the name keeps -āvalī, which is common in such poetic compounds.

282 सहस्रशीर्षवदना sahasra-śīrṣa-vadanā

She who has a thousand heads and faces

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (with an inner itaretara-dvandva). Inner layer: śīrṣa-vadana 'heads and faces' (dvandva). Outer layer: a bahuvrīhi with the numeral sahasra 'a thousand': 'She who has a thousand heads and faces'; vadana takes the feminine -ā. Juxtaposition.

Analysis शीर्षाणि च वदनानि च शीर्षवदनानि; सहस्रम् शीर्षवदनानि यस्याः सा सहस्रशीर्षवदना
śīrṣāṇi ca vadanāni ca śīrṣavadanāni; sahasram śīrṣavadanāni yasyāḥ sā sahasraśīrṣavadanā

Significance Names 282–284 echo the Puruṣa-sūkta of the Ṛgveda — 'sahasraśīrṣā puruṣaḥ sahasrākṣaḥ sahasrapāt' — and give the cosmic Person's form to Her; 'thousand' means countless.

283 सहस्राक्षी sahasrākṣī

She who has a thousand eyes

Sandhi सहस्राक्षी = सहस्र + अक्षी (sahasra + akṣī) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi. 'She who has a thousand eyes'. In a bahuvrīhi akṣi 'eye' takes the suffix -a (ṣac, Pāṇini 5.4.113), giving -akṣa, and the feminine is -ākṣī (4.1.41).

Analysis सहस्रम् अक्षीणि यस्याः सा सहस्राक्षी
sahasram akṣīṇi yasyāḥ sā sahasrākṣī

Significance Her eyes are everywhere: nothing happens unseen by Her.

284 सहस्रपात् sahasra-pāt

She who has a thousand feet

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. 'She who has a thousand feet'. After a numeral, pāda loses its final a in a bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 5.4.140) and becomes pād, whose nominative is pāt; the bahuvrīhi may keep this form in the feminine (4.1.8 pādo 'nyatarasyām).

Analysis सहस्रम् पादाः यस्याः सा सहस्रपात्
sahasram pādāḥ yasyāḥ sā sahasrapāt

Significance With the Puruṣa-sūkta's thousand feet She stands in every place at once.

Śloka 67names 285–288

निजाज्ञारूपनिगमा पुण्यापुण्यफलप्रदा ॥ ६७ ॥

ābrahmakīṭajananī varṇāśramavidhāyinī |

The names, separated

285आब्रह्म-कीट-जननीābrahma-kīṭa-jananī286वर्णाश्रम-विधायिनीvarṇāśrama-vidhāyinī

Where the names meet

Name 285: ābrahma-kīṭa is 'from Brahmā down to the worm', the indeclinable ā + brahma, not a word ābrahma.

The names

285 आब्रह्मकीटजननी ābrahma-kīṭa-jananī

She who is the mother of everything from Brahmā to the lowliest insect

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (with an inner avyayībhāva). Inner layer: ā-brahma-kīṭa 'from Brahmā down to the worm', an avyayībhāva with the indeclinable ā 'up to, including' (Pāṇini 2.1.13 āṅ maryādābhividhyoḥ), naming every being between the two limits. Outer layer: jananī 'mother' is the head, with all those beings in the genitive. brahman drops its final n in composition.

Analysis ब्रह्मणः आरभ्य कीटपर्यन्तम् आब्रह्मकीटम्; आब्रह्मकीटम् सर्वेषाम् जननी आब्रह्मकीटजननी
brahmaṇaḥ ārabhya kīṭaparyantam ābrahmakīṭam; ābrahmakīṭam sarveṣām jananī ābrahmakīṭajananī

Significance No being is too high or too low to be Her child: the creator himself and the smallest insect have the same Mother.

286 वर्णाश्रमविधायिनी varṇāśrama-vidhāyinī

She who ordains the order of the classes and the stages of life

Sandhi वर्णाश्रम = वर्ण + आश्रम (varṇa + āśrama) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (with an inner itaretara-dvandva). Inner layer: varṇa-āśrama 'the classes and the stages of life' (dvandva). Outer layer: vidhāyinī 'she who ordains' (vi + √dhā with the agent suffix -in, y inserted after the ā, feminine -inī) is the head and takes them in the genitive.

Analysis वर्णाः च आश्रमाः च वर्णाश्रमाः; वर्णाश्रमाणाम् विधायिनी वर्णाश्रमविधायिनी
varṇāḥ ca āśramāḥ ca varṇāśramāḥ; varṇāśramāṇām vidhāyinī varṇāśramavidhāyinī

Significance Traditionally the order of duties belongs to Her because the Vedas that teach it are Her command (name 287).

Corrected वर्णाश्रमविधायिनि → वर्णाश्रमविधायिनी. विधायिनि → विधायिनी: the nominative feminine ends in long ī (-inī).

287 निजाज्ञारूपनिगमा nijājñā-rūpa-nigamā

She whose own commands are the Vedas

Sandhi निजाज्ञा = निजा + आज्ञा (nijā + ājñā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner bahuvrīhi and karmadhāraya). (1) nija-ājñā 'Her own command' (karmadhāraya). (2) nijājñā-rūpa 'having Her own command as their form', a bahuvrīhi qualifying nigama. (3) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose Vedas have the form of Her own command'; nigama takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis निजा आज्ञा निजाज्ञा; निजाज्ञा रूपम् येषाम् ते निजाज्ञारूपाः; निजाज्ञारूपाः निगमाः यस्याः सा निजाज्ञारूपनिगमा
nijā ājñā nijājñā; nijājñā rūpam yeṣām te nijājñārūpāḥ; nijājñārūpāḥ nigamāḥ yasyāḥ sā nijājñārūpanigamā

Significance Traditionally the Vedas are Her command, which no one may transgress; dharma is what She has spoken.

288 पुण्यापुण्यफलप्रदा puṇyāpuṇya-phala-pradā

She who dispenses the fruits of both good and evil actions

Sandhi पुण्यापुण्य = पुण्य + अपुण्य (puṇya + apuṇya) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and itaretara-dvandva). (1) puṇya-apuṇya 'merit and demerit' (dvandva). (2) …puṇya-phala 'their fruit' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) -pradā 'giving' is the head and governs the fruit as its object.

Analysis पुण्यम् च अपुण्यम् च पुण्यापुण्ये; पुण्यापुण्ययोः फलम् पुण्यापुण्यफलम्; पुण्यापुण्यफलम् प्रददाति इति पुण्यापुण्यफलप्रदा
puṇyam ca apuṇyam ca puṇyāpuṇye; puṇyāpuṇyayoḥ phalam puṇyāpuṇyaphalam; puṇyāpuṇyaphalam pradadāti iti puṇyāpuṇyaphalapradā

Significance Actions do not reward themselves; traditionally it is She, as the Lord who governs karma, who brings each deed to its fruit.

Śloka 68names 289–290

श्रुतिसीमन्तसिन्दूरीकृतपादाब्जधूलिका ।

śrutisīmantasindūrīkṛtapādābjadhūlikā |
sakalāgamasandohaśuktisampuṭamauktikā || 68 ||

289श्रुति-सीमन्त-सिन्दूरी-कृत-पादाब्ज-धूलिकाśruti-sīmanta-sindūrī-kṛta-pādābja-dhūlikā

290She who is the pearl within the oyster-shell formed by all the scriptures together.

Where the names meet

Each half is a single name (289, 290): the Vedas bowing to Her feet, and the scriptures as the shell that holds Her as a pearl.

The names

289 श्रुतिसीमन्तसिन्दूरीकृतपादाब्जधूलिका śruti-sīmanta-sindūrī-kṛta-pādābja-dhūlikā

She the dust of whose lotus feet becomes the vermilion in the hair-parting of the Vedas

Sandhi सीमन्त = सीमन् + अन्त (sīman + anta) — irregular fusion: in the sense 'hair-parting' sīman (its n dropped) + anta gives sīmanta, the second vowel replacing the first (pararūpa; the śakandhu group of words); पादाब्ज = पाद + अब्ज (pāda + abja) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, saptamī-tatpuruṣa and gati-compound layers). (1) śruti-sīmanta 'the hair-partings of the Vedas', the Vedas pictured as women (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) pāda-abja 'lotus feet' (feet like lotuses) and …abja-dhūlikā 'the dust of those feet' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) sindūrī-kṛta 'made into vermilion', a cvi formation: sindūra + kṛta with a → ī, meaning 'turned into what it was not' (Pāṇini 7.4.32). (4) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She the dust of whose lotus feet is made the vermilion in the hair-partings of the Vedas'.

Analysis श्रुतीनाम् सीमन्ताः श्रुतिसीमन्ताः; पादौ अब्जे इव पादाब्जे; पादाब्जयोः धूलिका पादाब्जधूलिका; असिन्दूरम् सिन्दूरम् कृता सिन्दूरीकृता; श्रुतिसीमन्तेषु सिन्दूरीकृता पादाब्जधूलिका यस्याः सा श्रुतिसीमन्तसिन्दूरीकृतपादाब्जधूलिका
śrutīnām sīmantāḥ śrutisīmantāḥ; pādau abje iva pādābje; pādābjayoḥ dhūlikā pādābjadhūlikā; asindūram sindūram kṛtā sindūrīkṛtā; śrutisīmanteṣu sindūrīkṛtā pādābjadhūlikā yasyāḥ sā śrutisīmantasindūrīkṛtapādābjadhūlikā

Significance The Vedas, pictured as married women, bow their heads at Her feet so that the dust of Her feet marks their partings like the vermilion of the auspicious wife: the Upaniṣads, the crown of the Veda, rest at Her feet.

290 सकलागमसन्दोहशुक्तिसम्पुटमौक्तिका sakalāgama-sandoha-śukti-sampuṭa-mauktikā

She who is the pearl within the oyster-shell formed by all the scriptures together

Sandhi सकलागम = सकल + आगम (sakala + āgama) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); सन्दोह = सम् + दोह (sam + doha) — m becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23) and the anusvāra takes the nasal of the following stop's class, n before d (8.4.58 anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over inner karmadhāraya, ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and rūpaka layers), applied to Her with the feminine -ā. (1) sakala-āgama 'all the scriptures' (karmadhāraya) and …āgama-sandoha 'their whole mass' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) śukti-sampuṭa 'the closed pair of oyster-valves' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) The mass of scripture IS that oyster-shell (a karmadhāraya of identification, rūpaka). (4) mauktika 'pearl' is the head, with the shell in the genitive: She is the pearl within; it takes the feminine -ā as applied to Her.

Analysis सकलाः आगमाः सकलागमाः; सकलागमानाम् सन्दोहः सकलागमसन्दोहः; शुक्तेः सम्पुटम् शुक्तिसम्पुटम्; सकलागमसन्दोहः एव शुक्तिसम्पुटम् सकलागमसन्दोहशुक्तिसम्पुटम्; तस्य मौक्तिकम् इव सकलागमसन्दोहशुक्तिसम्पुटमौक्तिका
sakalāḥ āgamāḥ sakalāgamāḥ; sakalāgamānām sandohaḥ sakalāgamasandohaḥ; śukteḥ sampuṭam śuktisampuṭam; sakalāgamasandohaḥ eva śuktisampuṭam sakalāgamasandohaśuktisampuṭam; tasya mauktikam iva sakalāgamasandohaśuktisampuṭamauktikā

Significance The scriptures enclose and guard Her as the shell guards the pearl: their whole worth lies in what they hold, and what they hold is She.

Śloka 69names 291–297

पुरुषार्थप्रदा पूर्णा भोगिनी भुवनेश्वरी ।
अम्बिका ऽनादिनिधना हरिब्रह्मेन्द्रसेविता ॥ ६९ ॥

puruṣārthapradā pūrṇā bhoginī bhuvaneśvarī |
ambikā 'nādinidhanā haribrahmendrasevitā || 69 ||

The names, separated ° form as a name on its own; in the recitation above it joins its neighbour

291पुरुषार्थ-प्रदाpuruṣārtha-pradā292पूर्णाpūrṇā293भोगिनीbhoginī294भुवनेश्वरीbhuvaneśvarī

295अम्बिकाambikā296अनादि-निधना°anādi-nidhanā297हरि-ब्रह्मेन्द्र-सेविताhari-brahmendra-sevitā

Translation

291She who grants the (four-fold) objects of human life; 292She who is full and complete; 293She who is the enjoyer; 294She who is the ruler of the universe;

295She who is the Mother, Ambikā; 296She who has neither beginning nor end; 297She who is attended by Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Indra.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish

भोगिनीbhoginīenjoyer, she who enjoysbhoga 'enjoyment' + the possessive suffix -in, feminine -inī

भुवनbhuvanaworld√bhū 'to be, become'

अanot (negative particle)appears as an- before a vowel
आदिādibeginning

ब्रह्मन्brahmanBrahmā, the creatorappears as brahma- (final n dropped)
इन्द्रindraIndra, king of the gods

Where the names meet

अम्बिकाऽनादिनिधना = अम्बिका + अनादिनिधना (ambikā + anādinidhanā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā; the avagraha (ऽ) marks the a absorbed at the start of the next name

Divide ambikā (295) | anādinidhanā (296): the avagraha marks the initial a of anādi, which carries the negation.

The names

291 पुरुषार्थप्रदा puruṣārtha-pradā

She who grants the (four-fold) objects of human life

Sandhi पुरुषार्थ = पुरुष + अर्थ (puruṣa + artha) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (with an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). Inner layer: puruṣa-artha 'the aims of a person' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). Outer layer: -pradā 'giving' is the head and governs them as its object.

Analysis पुरुषस्य अर्थाः पुरुषार्थाः; पुरुषार्थान् प्रददाति इति पुरुषार्थप्रदा
puruṣasya arthāḥ puruṣārthāḥ; puruṣārthān pradadāti iti puruṣārthapradā

Significance The four aims are dharma (right living), artha (wealth), kāma (fulfilled desire) and mokṣa (liberation); She grants each in its place, and the last above all.

292 पूर्णा pūrṇā

She who is full and complete

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance The Upaniṣadic invocation 'pūrṇam adaḥ pūrṇam idam' describes Her: whole, and whole even when the whole is taken from Her. Traditionally She neither grows nor decays, unlike the moon.

293 भोगिनी bhoginī

She who is the enjoyer

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Traditionally all experience is finally Hers: She is the one who enjoys in every enjoyer.

294 भुवनेश्वरी bhuvaneśvarī

She who is the ruler of the universe

Sandhi भुवनेश्वरी = भुवन + ईश्वरी (bhuvana + īśvarī) — guṇa: a/ā + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. īśvarī 'sovereign' is the head and bhuvana 'world' stands to it in the genitive: 'the sovereign of the worlds'.

Analysis भुवनानाम् ईश्वरी भुवनेश्वरी
bhuvanānām īśvarī bhuvaneśvarī

Significance Bhuvaneśvarī is also the Goddess whose seed-syllable is hrīṃ (name 301), worshipped among the great Wisdom Goddesses.

295 अम्बिका ambikā

She who is the Mother, Ambikā

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Ambikā is the Mother of all the worlds; traditionally the name is also read as the union of Her three powers of will, knowledge and action.

296 अनादिनिधना anādi-nidhanā

She who has neither beginning nor end

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound nañ-bahuvrīhi (over an inner itaretara-dvandva). Inner layer: ādi 'beginning' and nidhana 'end' (dvandva). Outer layer: a bahuvrīhi with the negative particle (nañ, appearing as an- before a vowel): 'She for whom beginning and end do not exist'. nidhana takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis आदिः च निधनम् च आदिनिधने; न विद्येते आदिनिधने यस्याः सा अनादिनिधना
ādiḥ ca nidhanam ca ādinidhane; na vidyete ādinidhane yasyāḥ sā anādinidhanā

Significance What has a beginning has an end; She has neither, because time itself arises in Her.

297 हरिब्रह्मेन्द्रसेविता hari-brahmendra-sevitā

She who is attended by Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Indra

Sandhi ब्रह्मेन्द्र = ब्रह्म + इन्द्र (brahma + indra) — guṇa: a + i → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (with an inner itaretara-dvandva). Inner layer: hari-brahma-indra 'Hari, Brahmā and Indra' (dvandva; brahman drops its final n). Outer layer: the past participle sevitā 'served, attended' is the head and takes the gods in the instrumental.

Analysis हरिः च ब्रह्मा च इन्द्रः च हरिब्रह्मेन्द्राः; हरिब्रह्मेन्द्रैः सेविता हरिब्रह्मेन्द्रसेविता
hariḥ ca brahmā ca indraḥ ca haribrahmendrāḥ; haribrahmendraiḥ sevitā haribrahmendrasevitā

Significance The highest gods are Her attendants; their powers are Her gifts.

Śloka 70names 298–304

नारायणी नादरूपा नामरूपविवर्जिता ।
ह्रीङ्कारी ह्रीमती हृद्या हेयोपादेयवर्जिता ॥ ७० ॥

nārāyaṇī nādarūpā nāmarūpavivarjitā |
hrīṅkārī hrīmatī hṛdyā heyopādeyavarjitā || 70 ||

The names, separated

298नारायणीnārāyaṇī299नाद-रूपाnāda-rūpā300नाम-रूप-विवर्जिताnāma-rūpa-vivarjitā

301ह्रीङ्-कारीhrīṅ-kārī302ह्री-मतीhrī-matī303हृद्याhṛdyā304हेयोपादेय-वर्जिताheyopādeya-varjitā

Translation

298She who is the feminine counterpart of Nārāyaṇa; 299She who is in the form of sound; 300She who has no name or form;

301She who is the syllable hrīṃ; 302She who is endowed with modesty; 303She who abides in the heart and delights it; 304She who has nothing to reject or accept.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish
298 नारायणी nārāyaṇī
नारायणीnārāyaṇīthe feminine power of Nārāyaṇafeminine of nārāyaṇa = nāra 'the waters' (or 'beings') + ayana 'resting-place'

नादnādanāda, sound; in Tantra the subtle, unstruck sound from which speech unfolds√nad 'to sound'
रूपाrūpāformrūpa, with the feminine -ā
300 नामरूपविवर्जिता nāma-rūpa-vivarjitā
नामन्nāmannameappears as nāma- (final n dropped)
रूपrūpaform
विवर्जिताvivarjitāwholly free fromvi + √vṛj, causative past participle, feminine

ह्रीम्hrīmhrīṃ, the seed-syllable (bīja) of the Goddess
कारीkārīthe syllable (as in oṅkāra), feminine-kāra, the suffix that names a sound, with the feminine -ī

हेयheyato be abandoned, rejected√hā 'to leave' + the gerundive -ya
उपादेयupādeyato be taken up, acceptedupa + ā + √dā 'to take' + the gerundive -ya
वर्जिताvarjitāfree from, devoid of√vṛj, causative past participle, feminine

Where the names meet

Names 301–302 open with hrī: hrīṅkārī is the seed-syllable hrīṃ, and hrīmatī can be read with it as well as 'modest'.

The names

298 नारायणी nārāyaṇī

She who is the feminine counterpart of Nārāyaṇa

Sandhi नारायण = नार + अयन (nāra + ayana) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ), inside nārāyaṇa; the n of ayana then becomes ṇ after r (retroflexion)

Compound not a compound

Significance The Devī Māhātmya hymns Her with the refrain 'nārāyaṇi namo 'stu te'; as Nārāyaṇī She is Viṣṇu's own power (compare name 280).

299 नादरूपा nāda-rūpā

She who is in the form of sound

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. 'She whose form is nāda'; rūpa takes the feminine -ā. Juxtaposition.

Analysis नादः रूपम् यस्याः सा नादरूपा
nādaḥ rūpam yasyāḥ sā nādarūpā

Significance In Śrīvidyā nāda is the subtle resonance that rises after the bindu in the utterance of a seed-syllable such as hrīṃ, and from which all speech and all things unfold.

300 नामरूपविवर्जिता nāma-rūpa-vivarjitā

She who has no name or form

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (with an inner itaretara-dvandva). Inner layer: nāma-rūpa 'name and form' (dvandva; nāman drops its final n). Outer layer: vivarjitā 'wholly free from' is the head and takes them in the instrumental.

Analysis नाम च रूपम् च नामरूपे; नामरूपाभ्याम् विवर्जिता नामरूपविवर्जिता
nāma ca rūpam ca nāmarūpe; nāmarūpābhyām vivarjitā nāmarūpavivarjitā

Significance In the Chāndogya Upaniṣad (6.3) Being enters the world to unfold name and form; She is that Being, Herself untouched by name and form — even as She bears a thousand names.

301 ह्रीङ्कारी hrīṅ-kārī

She who is the syllable hrīṃ

Sandhi ह्रीङ्कारी = ह्रीम् + कारी (hrīm + kārī) — m becomes the nasal of the following stop's class, ṅ before k (via anusvāra, Pāṇini 8.3.23 and 8.4.58)

Compound not a compound

Significance Hrīṃ, the māyā-bīja or Bhuvaneśvarī-bīja, closes each of the three sections of Her fifteen-syllabled mantra; the name can also be read 'She who makes the syllable hrīṃ'.

302 ह्रीमती hrī-matī

She who is endowed with modesty

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Traditionally modesty here is the reserve of the noble; the name can also be read 'She who possesses the syllable hrīṃ', continuing name 301.

303 हृद्या hṛdyā

She who abides in the heart and delights it

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance She is found in the heart of the devotee, and is what the heart finds dearest.

Uncertain Two derivations are current: 'dear to the heart' (4.4.95) and 'being in the heart'; the meaning gives both.

304 हेयोपादेयवर्जिता heyopādeya-varjitā

She who has nothing to reject or accept

Sandhi हेयोपादेय = हेय + उपादेय (heya + upādeya) — guṇa: a + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ); उपादेय = उप + आदेय (upa + ādeya) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a/ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ), inside the prefixed word upādeya

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (with an inner itaretara-dvandva). Inner layer: heya 'what is to be given up' and upādeya 'what is to be taken up' (dvandva of two gerundives). Outer layer: varjitā 'free from' is the head and takes the pair in the instrumental: for Her there is nothing to reject and nothing to accept.

Analysis हेयम् च उपादेयम् च हेयोपादेये; हेयोपादेयाभ्याम् वर्जिता हेयोपादेयवर्जिता
heyam ca upādeyam ca heyopādeye; heyopādeyābhyām varjitā heyopādeyavarjitā

Significance Since all is Her own self, nothing can be shunned or sought; the seeker's discipline of rejecting and accepting ends in Her.

Śloka 71names 305–312

राजराजार्चिता राज्ञी रम्या राजीवलोचना ।
रञ्जनी रमणी रस्या रणत्किङ्किणिमेखला ॥ ७१ ॥

rājarājārcitā rājñī ramyā rājīvalocanā |
rañjanī ramaṇī rasyā raṇatkiṅkiṇimekhalā || 71 ||

The names, separated

305राज-राजार्चिताrāja-rājārcitā306राज्ञीrājñī307रम्याramyā308राजीव-लोचनाrājīva-locanā

Word by word

SanskritEnglish

राजन्rājankingfirst member; its n drops in composition (rāja-)
राजन्rājankinghead of the inner compound; with the samāsānta ṭac it becomes rāja, giving rājarāja 'king of kings'

राजीवrājīvalotususually the blue or the red lotus

रस्याrasyāto be relished; full of flavor and delightfrom rasa 'taste, essence, delight' (or √ras) with the suffix -ya, feminine

Where the names meet

Names 305–320 (to the end of śloka 72) all begin with ra/rā; the next ślokas group names by initial sound in the same way: k in 73–74 (except 325 jagatīkandā), v in 74–75 and 77, kṣ in 76, t in 79. Name 305 divides rāja-rāja + arcitā ('worshipped by the king of kings').

The names

305 राजराजार्चिता rāja-rājārcitā

She who is worshipped by the King of kings

Sandhi राजार्चिता = राज + अर्चिता (rāja + arcitā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (with an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). Inner layer: rājñām rājā 'the king of kings' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). The first rājan loses its n in composition (Pāṇini 8.2.7 nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya); the second, as the final of a tatpuruṣa, takes the samāsānta suffix ṭac (5.4.91 rājāhaḥsakhibhyaṣ ṭac), so the stem is rājarāja. Outer layer: the participle arcitā 'worshipped' is the head, and the king of kings stands to it in the instrumental as the agent.

Analysis राज्ञाम् राजा राजराजः; राजराजेन अर्चिता राजराजार्चिता
rājñām rājā rājarājaḥ; rājarājena arcitā rājarājārcitā

Significance Rājarāja 'king of kings' is a standard name of Kubera, lord of wealth (so the Amarakośa), and Kubera is counted traditionally among the great worshippers of Śrīvidyā. The name also implies that every sovereign's power is received from Her.

306 राज्ञी rājñī

She who is the Queen

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Traditionally read with the previous name: She is the consort of the King of kings, Śiva as Kāmeśvara, and the ruling queen in Her own right.

307 रम्या ramyā

She who is lovely and delightful

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Traditionally, all that delights the mind delights because of Her; She is the one whose beauty draws the devotee.

308 राजीवलोचना rājīva-locanā

She whose eyes are like lotuses

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi of comparison. The two members stand in a comparison: rājīva 'lotus' is the standard of comparison (upamāna) and locana 'eye' what is compared. The whole describes Her as a bahuvrīhi, 'She whose eyes are (like) lotuses'; locana takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis राजीवे इव लोचने यस्याः सा राजीवलोचना
rājīve iva locane yasyāḥ sā rājīvalocanā

Significance The lotus-eye is the classical image of beauty and tenderness; traditionally Her glance is said to bless as a lotus opens to the sun.

309 रञ्जनी rañjanī

She who delights the mind

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance The root rañj means both 'to color' and 'to delight'. Traditionally it is said that Her crimson radiance tints even the white Śiva, and that She colors the mind with joy.

Uncertain The root allows two senses, 'one who colors (reddens)' and 'one who delights'; the meaning gives the second, the significance the first.

310 रमणी ramaṇī

She who gives joy

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Ramaṇī is also an ordinary word for a beautiful woman; traditionally She is the one who delights in Her play of creation and makes Her devotees rejoice.

311 रस्या rasyā

She who is to be relished, the essence of all delight

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance The Taittirīya Upaniṣad says of the Real, raso vai saḥ, 'It is rasa itself; having gained rasa one becomes blissful'. She is that essence, the delight that is tasted in every delight.

312 रणत्किङ्किणिमेखला raṇat-kiṅkiṇi-mekhalā

She who wears a girdle of tinkling bells

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (over a karmadhāraya with a dropped middle member and an inner karmadhāraya). (1) raṇat-kiṅkiṇi 'tinkling bells': the present participle raṇat qualifies kiṅkiṇi (karmadhāraya). (2) …kiṅkiṇi-mekhalā 'a girdle set with tinkling bells': a karmadhāraya whose middle word 'yukta, furnished with' is understood (madhyamapadalopin). (3) The whole is a bahuvrīhi describing Her: 'She whose girdle has tinkling bells'.

Analysis रणन्त्यः किङ्किण्यः रणत्किङ्किण्यः; रणत्किङ्किणीभिः युक्ता मेखला रणत्किङ्किणिमेखला; रणत्किङ्किणिमेखला यस्याः सा रणत्किङ्किणिमेखला
raṇantyaḥ kiṅkiṇyaḥ raṇatkiṅkiṇyaḥ; raṇatkiṅkiṇībhiḥ yuktā mekhalā raṇatkiṅkiṇimekhalā; raṇatkiṅkiṇimekhalā yasyāḥ sā raṇatkiṅkiṇimekhalā

Significance Traditionally the soft sound of the bells announces Her presence; the girdle belongs to the description of Her form.

Śloka 72names 313–320

रमा राकेन्दुवदना रतिरूपा रतिप्रिया ।
रक्षाकरी राक्षसघ्नी रामा रमणलम्पटा ॥ ७२ ॥

ramā rākenduvadanā ratirūpā ratipriyā |
rakṣākarī rākṣasaghnī rāmā ramaṇalampaṭā || 72 ||

The names, separated

313रमाramā314राकेन्दु-वदनाrākendu-vadanā315रति-रूपाrati-rūpā316रति-प्रियाrati-priyā

317रक्षा-करीrakṣā-karī318राक्षस-घ्नीrākṣasa-ghnī319रामाrāmā320रमण-लम्पटाramaṇa-lampaṭā

Where the names meet

Name 313 ramā is a name of Lakṣmī; 319 rāmā (long first ā) is a different word, 'delightful woman'.

The names

313 रमा ramā

She who is Ramā (Lakṣmī)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Ramā, 'she who delights', is a standard name of Lakṣmī, goddess of fortune; here Lalitā is Lakṣmī Herself.

Uncertain The earlier rendering added Sarasvatī; that rests on a commentarial derivation I could not confirm, so it is left out.

314 राकेन्दुवदना rākendu-vadanā

She whose face is like the full moon

Sandhi राकेन्दु = राका + इन्दु (rākā + indu) — guṇa: ā + i → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi of comparison (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) rākā-indu 'the moon of the full-moon night', i.e. the full moon (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) The whole is a bahuvrīhi of comparison: 'She whose face (vadana) is like the full moon'; vadana takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis राकायाः इन्दुः राकेन्दुः; राकेन्दुः इव वदनम् यस्याः सा राकेन्दुवदना
rākāyāḥ induḥ rākenduḥ; rākenduḥ iva vadanam yasyāḥ sā rākenduvadanā

Significance The full moon is whole, cool and radiant without glare: so is Her face. Traditionally, the moon lacking nothing points to Her as the fullness that never wanes.

315 रतिरूपा rati-rūpā

She who is in the form of Rati, the wife of Kāma

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. rati 'Rati, delight' and rūpa 'form' are co-referential, and the compound describes Her: 'She whose form is Rati'. It may equally be taken as a karmadhāraya in apposition ('She who is Rati in form'); the sense is the same.

Analysis रतिः रूपम् यस्याः सा रतिरूपा
ratiḥ rūpam yasyāḥ sā ratirūpā

Significance Rati is the delight of love personified, the consort of Kāma; traditionally every delight is a form of Hers.

316 रतिप्रिया rati-priyā

She who is fond of Rati

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi; alternatively ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. As a bahuvrīhi, Rati (or delight) is dear to Her: 'She to whom Rati is dear', i.e. who is fond of Rati. As a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, priyā 'beloved' is the head and Rati stands in the genitive: 'She who is dear to Rati'. The members are simply juxtaposed.

Analysis रतिः प्रिया यस्याः सा रतिप्रिया; अथवा रतेः प्रिया रतिप्रिया
ratiḥ priyā yasyāḥ sā ratipriyā; athavā rateḥ priyā ratipriyā

Significance Traditionally Rati, being dear to Her, attends on Her; read inwardly, She delights in the joy of Her devotees.

Uncertain Bahuvrīhi ('to whom Rati is dear') and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa ('dear to Rati') are both possible; rati may also be the common noun 'delight'.

317 रक्षाकरी rakṣā-karī

She who is the protector

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. The second member karī is an agent form of √kṛ 'to make' that exists only with a preceding object word (upapada): 'she who makes protection'. The suffix ṭa (Pāṇini 3.2.20) makes the feminine end in -ī.

Analysis रक्षाम् करोति इति रक्षाकरी
rakṣām karoti iti rakṣākarī

Significance She protects the worlds She has made; traditionally, the protection is above all from fear and from bondage.

318 राक्षसघ्नी rākṣasa-ghnī

She who slays the demons

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. ghnī is an agent form of √han 'to strike, slay', used only after its object (upapada): 'she who slays the rākṣasas'. With the suffix (ṭak) the root is reduced to ghn- and the feminine ends in -ī.

Analysis राक्षसान् हन्ति इति राक्षसघ्नी
rākṣasān hanti iti rākṣasaghnī

Significance Traditionally, outwardly the demons of the Purāṇic wars, inwardly the dark tendencies (lust, anger, greed) that oppose the devotee.

319 रामा rāmā

She who gives delight

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Rāmā is also a common word for a woman; traditionally every woman is seen as Her form, as the Devī Māhātmya says in its hymn to Nārāyaṇī (striyaḥ samastāḥ sakalā jagatsu).

320 रमणलम्पटा ramaṇa-lampaṭā

She who is passionately devoted to Her beloved, Lord Śiva

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound saptamī-tatpuruṣa. lampaṭā 'eagerly devoted, passionately attached' is the head; the object of the attachment, ramaṇa 'the beloved', stands to it in the locative ('devoted to'). The members are simply juxtaposed.

Analysis रमणे लम्पटा रमणलम्पटा
ramaṇe lampaṭā ramaṇalampaṭā

Significance Traditionally the beloved is Kāmeśvara; Her devotion to Him is the model of the devotee's own longing.

Uncertain ramaṇa can be the beloved (Śiva) or the act of love-play itself ('eager for love-play'); the meaning follows the first.

Śloka 73names 321–326

काम्या कामकलारूपा कदम्बकुसुमप्रिया ।
कल्याणी जगतीकन्दा करुणारससागरा ॥ ७३ ॥

kāmyā kāmakalārūpā kadambakusumapriyā |
kalyāṇī jagatīkandā karuṇārasasāgarā || 73 ||

Where the names meet

Name 322 kāmakalā is a technical term of Śrīvidyā, the subtle triangular form of the Goddess, not 'the art of love'.

The names

321 काम्या kāmyā

She who is to be desired

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Traditionally She is the one goal worth desiring, sought above all by those who seek liberation; every other desire is a distant reflection of the longing for Her.

322 कामकलारूपा kāma-kalā-rūpā

She who is in the form of Kāmakalā

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) kāma-kalā 'the kalā (subtle digit, power) of Kāma' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose form is the kāmakalā'. kāmakalā can also be analysed as a dvandva, Kāma and Kalā, i.e. Kāmeśvara and Kāmeśvarī together.

Analysis कामस्य कला कामकला; कामकला रूपम् यस्याः सा कामकलारूपा
kāmasya kalā kāmakalā; kāmakalā rūpam yasyāḥ sā kāmakalārūpā

Significance In Śrīvidyā the kāmakalā is the most subtle form of the Goddess: the triangle of three bindus (sun, moon and fire) with the half-digit below, the union of Śiva and Śakti from which the Śrīcakra and the mantra unfold. Puṇyānanda's Kāmakalāvilāsa is devoted to it.

Uncertain kāmakalā is analysed both as 'the digit of Kāma' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa) and as 'Kāma and Kalā' (dvandva).

323 कदम्बकुसुमप्रिया kadamba-kusuma-priyā

She who is fond of kadamba flowers

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) kadamba-kusuma 'the flowers of the kadamba tree' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) The whole is a bahuvrīhi with priya 'dear' as its predicate: 'She to whom kadamba flowers are dear'; priya takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis कदम्बस्य कुसुमानि कदम्बकुसुमानि; कदम्बकुसुमानि प्रियाणि यस्याः सा कदम्बकुसुमप्रिया
kadambasya kusumāni kadambakusumāni; kadambakusumāni priyāṇi yasyāḥ sā kadambakusumapriyā

Significance Her abode in Maṇidvīpa lies within a kadamba forest (name 60, kadambavanavāsinī), and kadamba blossoms adorn Her ears (name 21).

324 कल्याणी kalyāṇī

She who is auspicious

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance She is auspiciousness itself, and so the giver of all that is good; traditionally kalyāṇī also means 'beautiful'.

325 जगतीकन्दा jagatī-kandā

She who is the root of the whole world

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (the final member made feminine to agree with Her). kanda 'bulbous root' is the head and jagatī 'the world' stands to it in the genitive: 'the root of the world'. Because the name is in apposition to the Goddess, kanda takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis जगत्याः कन्दः जगतीकन्दः; सा जगतीकन्दा
jagatyāḥ kandaḥ jagatīkandaḥ; sā jagatīkandā

Significance As a plant springs from its bulb and is sustained by it, the world sprouts from Her and is nourished by Her.

326 करुणारससागरा karuṇā-rasa-sāgarā

She who is an ocean of the nectar of compassion

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya), the final member made feminine. (1) karuṇā-rasa 'the rasa that is compassion' (karmadhāraya of identification): compassion is both a liquid essence and the aesthetic sentiment (rasa) of pathos. (2) …rasa-sāgara 'the ocean of that essence' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) In apposition to Her, sāgara takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis करुणा एव रसः करुणारसः; करुणारसस्य सागरः करुणारससागरः; सा करुणारससागरा
karuṇā eva rasaḥ karuṇārasaḥ; karuṇārasasya sāgaraḥ karuṇārasasāgaraḥ; sā karuṇārasasāgarā

Significance The ocean is limitless and never exhausted however much is drawn from it; so is Her compassion.

Where the names meet

Name 333 is one compound, vāruṇī-mada-vihvalā (spelled ह्व, vihvalā); the printed source had split it and misspelled it.

The names

327 कलावती kalāvatī

She who possesses all the arts

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance The kalās are the sixty-four arts (compare name 236, catuḥṣaṣṭikalāmayī) and also the sixteen digits of the moon; She possesses them all, and they are Hers to bestow.

328 कलालापा kalālāpā

She who speaks musically and sweetly

Sandhi कलालाप = कल + आलाप (kala + ālāpa) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi. kala 'soft, sweet, melodious' qualifies ālāpa 'speech, discourse', and the whole describes Her: 'She whose speech is sweet and soft'. ālāpa takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis कलः आलापः यस्याः सा कलालापा
kalaḥ ālāpaḥ yasyāḥ sā kalālāpā

Significance Name 27 says the sweetness of Her speech puts to shame the vīṇā (kacchapī) of Sarasvatī; traditionally Her speech is gentle even when it commands.

Uncertain The fused ā allows kalā 'art' + ālāpa as well: 'She whose talk is of the arts'. The usual reading takes kala 'sweet'.

329 कान्ता kāntā

She who is beautiful

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Kāntā is literally 'the desired one': She is beautiful and the beloved of Kāmeśvara; traditionally Her beauty is the radiance (kānti) of consciousness.

330 कादम्बरीप्रिया kādambarī-priyā

She who is fond of kādambarī, the kadamba-flower wine

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. kādambarī is the subject and priyā 'dear' its predicate within the compound, and the whole describes Her: 'She to whom kādambarī is dear'.

Analysis कादम्बरी प्रिया यस्याः सा कादम्बरीप्रिया
kādambarī priyā yasyāḥ sā kādambarīpriyā

Significance In Śrīvidyā ritual, offerings of wine have an inner sense: the nectar of bliss that flows when kuṇḍalinī reaches the crown.

331 वरदा vara-dā

She who grants boons

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. dā is an agent form of √dā 'to give' used only after its object (Pāṇini 3.2.3 āto 'nupasarge kaḥ: suffix ka after roots in ā): 'she who gives boons'. It takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis वरम् ददाति इति वरदा
varam dadāti iti varadā

Significance The boon-granting gesture (varada-mudrā) is one of the classical hand-poses of the Goddess; traditionally She grants even more than is asked.

332 वामनयना vāma-nayanā

She who has beautiful eyes

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. vāma 'beautiful' qualifies nayana 'eye', and the whole describes Her: 'She whose eyes are beautiful'; nayana takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis वामे नयने यस्याः सा वामनयना
vāme nayane yasyāḥ sā vāmanayanā

Significance vāma also means 'left': traditionally a hint that She is the left half of Śiva.

Uncertain vāma means both 'beautiful' and 'left'; the meaning takes the first.

333 वारुणीमदविह्वला vāruṇī-mada-vihvalā

She who is overcome by the intoxication of vāruṇī

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) vāruṇī-mada 'the intoxication of vāruṇī' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) The adjective vihvalā 'overcome, reeling' is the head, and the intoxication stands to it in the instrumental as the cause.

Analysis वारुण्याः मदः वारुणीमदः; वारुणीमदेन विह्वला वारुणीमदविह्वला
vāruṇyāḥ madaḥ vāruṇīmadaḥ; vāruṇīmadena vihvalā vāruṇīmadavihvalā

Significance Traditionally read inwardly: the rapture of the bliss of the Self, which leaves one heedless of the world.

Corrected वारुणी मदविव्हला → वारुणीमदविह्वला. "वारुणी मदविव्हला" → वारुणीमदविह्वला: one compound name, not two words; विव्हला is a misspelling of vihvalā (ह्व).

Śloka 75names 334–340

विश्वाधिका वेदवेद्या विन्ध्याचलनिवासिनी ।
विधात्री वेदजननी विष्णुमाया विलासिनी ॥ ७५ ॥

viśvādhikā vedavedyā vindhyācalanivāsinī |
vidhātrī vedajananī viṣṇumāyā vilāsinī || 75 ||

The names, separated

334विश्वाधिकाviśvādhikā335वेद-वेद्याveda-vedyā336विन्ध्याचल-निवासिनीvindhyācala-nivāsinī

337She who creates and sustains this universe; 338She who is the mother of the Vedas; 339She who is the illusory power (māyā) of Viṣṇu; 340She who is playful.

The names

334 विश्वाधिका viśvādhikā

She who transcends the universe

Sandhi विश्वाधिका = विश्व + अधिका (viśva + adhikā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound pañcamī-tatpuruṣa. adhikā 'exceeding, greater' is the head and viśva 'the universe' stands to it in the ablative of comparison: 'greater than the universe'.

Analysis विश्वस्मात् अधिका विश्वाधिका
viśvasmāt adhikā viśvādhikā

Significance As the Puruṣasūkta says of the Person, all beings are one quarter of Him and three quarters are immortal beyond; She pervades the universe and exceeds it.

335 वेदवेद्या veda-vedyā

She who is to be known through the Vedas

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa. vedyā 'to be known' (gerundive of √vid) is the head, and veda stands to it in the instrumental as the means: 'to be known through the Vedas'.

Analysis वेदैः वेद्या वेदवेद्या
vedaiḥ vedyā vedavedyā

Significance As Kṛṣṇa says in the Bhagavad Gītā (15.15), 'I alone am to be known by all the Vedas' (vedaiś ca sarvair aham eva vedyaḥ); the whole of the Veda points to Her.

336 विन्ध्याचलनिवासिनी vindhyācala-nivāsinī

She who resides in the Vindhya mountains

Sandhi विन्ध्याचल = विन्ध्य + अचल (vindhya + acala) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) vindhya-acala 'the Vindhya mountain' (karmadhāraya of apposition: the mountain that is Vindhya). (2) nivāsin 'dwelling' is an agent noun from ni + √vas with the suffix ṇini (Pāṇini 3.2.78 supy ajātau ṇinis tācchīlye), compounded with its place in the locative sense: 'she who dwells on the Vindhya mountain'; feminine -inī.

Analysis विन्ध्यः एव अचलः विन्ध्याचलः; विन्ध्याचले निवसति इति विन्ध्याचलनिवासिनी
vindhyaḥ eva acalaḥ vindhyācalaḥ; vindhyācale nivasati iti vindhyācalanivāsinī

Significance In the Devī Māhātmya (ch. 11) the Goddess foretells that She will be born of Yaśodā and dwell on the Vindhya mountain (vindhyācalanivāsinī); She is worshipped there as Vindhyavāsinī.

337 विधात्री vidhātrī

She who creates and sustains this universe

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance vidhātṛ is a name of Brahmā as creator and ordainer; dhātrī also means a nurse or mother. She both ordains the world and nourishes it.

338 वेदजननी veda-jananī

She who is the mother of the Vedas

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. jananī 'mother, she who gives birth' is the head and the Vedas stand to it in the genitive: 'the mother of the Vedas'.

Analysis वेदानाम् जननी वेदजननी
vedānām jananī vedajananī

Significance The Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad says the Ṛg, Yajur and Sāma Vedas are the breath of the Great Being; traditionally the Vedas issue from Her as Her breath.

339 विष्णुमाया viṣṇu-māyā

She who is the illusory power (māyā) of Viṣṇu

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. māyā is the head and Viṣṇu stands to it in the genitive: 'the māyā of Viṣṇu'. The members are simply juxtaposed.

Analysis विष्णोः माया विष्णुमाया
viṣṇoḥ māyā viṣṇumāyā

Significance The Devī Māhātmya (ch. 5) hails the Goddess 'who in all beings is called Viṣṇumāyā' (yā devī sarvabhūteṣu viṣṇumāyeti śabditā): the power by which even the all-pervading Lord appears in forms.

340 विलासिनी vilāsinī

She who is playful

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Traditionally the universe is Her play (vilāsa, līlā); the play is the projecting power by which the One appears as the many.

Śloka 76names 341–345

क्षेत्रस्वरूपा क्षेत्रेशी क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञपालिनी ।
क्षयवृद्धिविनिर्मुक्ता क्षेत्रपालसमर्चिता ॥ ७६ ॥

kṣetrasvarūpā kṣetreśī kṣetrakṣetrajñapālinī |
kṣayavṛddhivinirmuktā kṣetrapālasamarcitā || 76 ||

The names, separated

341क्षेत्र-स्वरूपाkṣetra-svarūpā342क्षेत्रेशीkṣetreśī343क्षेत्र-क्षेत्रज्ञ-पालिनीkṣetra-kṣetrajña-pālinī

344क्षय-वृद्धि-विनिर्मुक्ताkṣaya-vṛddhi-vinirmuktā345क्षेत्र-पाल-समर्चिताkṣetra-pāla-samarcitā

Translation

341She whose very form is the field (kṣetra), the body and all matter; 342She who is the Sovereign of the field (kṣetra); 343She who protects both the field and the knower of the field;

344She who is free from growth and decay; 345She who is worshipped by Kṣetrapāla, guardian of the sacred field.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish
341 क्षेत्रस्वरूपा kṣetra-svarūpā
क्षेत्रkṣetrafield; in the Gītā's sense, the body and all of matter
स्वरूपाsvarūpāown form, essential naturesva + rūpa, with the feminine -ā
342 क्षेत्रेशी kṣetreśī
क्षेत्रkṣetrafield; body, matter, sacred precinct
ईशीīśīruler, sovereign ladyfeminine of īśa 'lord', from √īś 'to rule'
343 क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञपालिनी kṣetra-kṣetrajña-pālinī
क्षेत्रkṣetrathe field: body, matter
क्षेत्रज्ञkṣetrajñathe knower of the field: the conscious selfkṣetra + jña 'knowing' (√jñā)
पालिनीpālinīprotector, guardian√pāl 'to protect' + -in, feminine

क्षयkṣayadecay, waning, loss

विनिर्मुक्ताvinirmuktācompletely freedvi + nis + √muc 'to release', past participle, feminine

क्षेत्रkṣetrafield, sacred precinct
पालpālaguardian√pāl 'to protect'
समर्चिताsamarcitāduly worshippedsam + √arc 'to honor', past participle, feminine

Where the names meet

Names 341–345 all begin with kṣ and take up the Bhagavad Gītā's teaching of the field (kṣetra) and the knower of the field (kṣetrajña).

The names

341 क्षेत्रस्वरूपा kṣetra-svarūpā

She whose very form is the field (kṣetra), the body and all matter

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. kṣetra 'the field' and svarūpa 'own form, nature' are co-referential, and the whole describes Her: 'She whose own form is the field'. svarūpa itself is sva 'own' + rūpa 'form'.

Analysis क्षेत्रम् स्वरूपम् यस्याः सा क्षेत्रस्वरूपा
kṣetram svarūpam yasyāḥ sā kṣetrasvarūpā

Significance The Bhagavad Gītā (ch. 13) calls the body, and all of prakṛti, the field (kṣetra), and the one who knows it the knower of the field (kṣetrajña). Names 341–345 develop that teaching.

342 क्षेत्रेशी kṣetreśī

She who is the Sovereign of the field (kṣetra)

Sandhi क्षेत्रेशी = क्षेत्र + ईशी (kṣetra + īśī) — guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; alternatively the feminine of a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa by association (puṃyoga). Read directly, īśī 'ruler' is the head and kṣetra stands to it in the genitive: 'the sovereign of the field'. Read the other way, kṣetreśa 'Lord of the field' is Śiva, and kṣetreśī is his consort, the feminine formed by association with the husband (Pāṇini 4.1.48 puṃyogād ākhyāyām).

Analysis क्षेत्रस्य ईशी क्षेत्रेशी; अथवा क्षेत्रस्य ईशः क्षेत्रेशः तस्य पत्नी क्षेत्रेशी
kṣetrasya īśī kṣetreśī; athavā kṣetrasya īśaḥ kṣetreśaḥ tasya patnī kṣetreśī

Significance She rules over every body and the whole field of matter, as the inner controller; traditionally She is also the consort of Śiva, the Lord of the field.

Uncertain The name may mean 'ruler of the field' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa) or 'wife of Kṣetreśa, Śiva' (puṃyoga feminine); both are current.

343 क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञपालिनी kṣetra-kṣetrajña-pālinī

She who protects both the field and the knower of the field

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner itaretara-dvandva and an upapada-tatpuruṣa). (1) kṣetra-jña 'the knower of the field' (upapada-tatpuruṣa; jña from √jñā with the suffix ka, Pāṇini 3.2.3). (2) kṣetra-kṣetrajña 'the field and the knower of the field' (itaretara-dvandva). (3) pālinī 'protector' is the head and the pair stands to it in the genitive.

Analysis क्षेत्रम् जानाति इति क्षेत्रज्ञः; क्षेत्रम् च क्षेत्रज्ञः च क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञौ; क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञयोः पालिनी क्षेत्रक्षेत्रज्ञपालिनी
kṣetram jānāti iti kṣetrajñaḥ; kṣetram ca kṣetrajñaḥ ca kṣetrakṣetrajñau; kṣetrakṣetrajñayoḥ pālinī kṣetrakṣetrajñapālinī

Significance The field is the body and the world; its knower is the conscious self. She guards both: matter and spirit, body and soul.

344 क्षयवृद्धिविनिर्मुक्ता kṣaya-vṛddhi-vinirmuktā

She who is free from growth and decay

Sandhi निर्मुक्ता = निस् + मुक्ता (nis + muktā) — the s of the prefix nis becomes r (through ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ) before a voiced sound

Compound pañcamī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner itaretara-dvandva). (1) kṣaya-vṛddhi 'decay and growth' (itaretara-dvandva). (2) The participle vinirmuktā 'wholly freed' is the head and the pair stands to it in the ablative: 'freed from decay and growth'.

Analysis क्षयः च वृद्धिः च क्षयवृद्धी; क्षयवृद्धिभ्याम् विनिर्मुक्ता क्षयवृद्धिविनिर्मुक्ता
kṣayaḥ ca vṛddhiḥ ca kṣayavṛddhī; kṣayavṛddhibhyām vinirmuktā kṣayavṛddhivinirmuktā

Significance The moon waxes and wanes; traditionally She is the sixteenth digit of the moon, which neither grows nor wanes, and the Self that is untouched by birth and death.

345 क्षेत्रपालसमर्चिता kṣetra-pāla-samarcitā

She who is worshipped by Kṣetrapāla, guardian of the sacred field

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner upapada-tatpuruṣa). (1) kṣetra-pāla 'guardian of the field' (upapada-tatpuruṣa; pāla from √pāl 'to protect' with the suffix aṇ). (2) The participle samarcitā 'well worshipped' is the head and Kṣetrapāla stands to it in the instrumental as the agent.

Analysis क्षेत्रम् पालयति इति क्षेत्रपालः; क्षेत्रपालेन समर्चिता क्षेत्रपालसमर्चिता
kṣetram pālayati iti kṣetrapālaḥ; kṣetrapālena samarcitā kṣetrapālasamarcitā

Significance Kṣetrapāla is the guardian deity of a temple precinct, a form of Bhairava (Śiva). Traditionally a Purāṇic story is told here: after Kālī slew the demon Dāruka, Śiva took the form of an infant to draw off Her fury, and that child is Kṣetrapāla.

Uncertain The story of the infant Kṣetrapāla is traditionally told on this name; I could not confirm its Purāṇic source, so it is not attributed.

Śloka 77names 346–352

विजया विमला वन्द्या वन्दारुजनवत्सला ।
वाग्वादिनी वामकेशी वह्निमण्डलवासिनी ॥ ७७ ॥

vijayā vimalā vandyā vandārujanavatsalā |
vāgvādinī vāmakeśī vahnimaṇḍalavāsinī || 77 ||

346विजयाvijayā347विमलाvimalā348वन्द्याvandyā349वन्दारु-जन-वत्सलाvandāru-jana-vatsalā

Where the names meet

Name 350 vāgvādinī: the stem is vāc 'speech'; its c appears as g before v.

The names

346 विजया vijayā

She who is ever-victorious

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance The prefix vi- intensifies: Her victory is complete and unique. Vijayā is also a name of Durgā and one of the Nityā goddesses of the lunar fortnight.

347 विमला vimalā

She who is without a trace of impurity

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound prādi-bahuvrīhi. The prefix vi- stands for vigata 'gone away', and the compound describes Her: 'She from whom impurity has gone'; mala takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis विगतम् मलम् यस्याः सा विमला
vigatam malam yasyāḥ sā vimalā

Significance In Śaiva and Śākta thought the soul is bound by three impurities (āṇava, māyīya and kārma mala); She is untouched by any of them, and frees those who worship Her.

348 वन्द्या vandyā

She who is adorable, worthy of worship

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance She is to be saluted by all, the gods included; traditionally the salutation itself is a form of Her worship.

349 वन्दारुजनवत्सला vandāru-jana-vatsalā

She who is full of motherly love for those who worship Her

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound saptamī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) vandāru-jana 'people given to worship' (karmadhāraya). (2) vatsalā 'tenderly loving' is the head and the worshippers stand to it in the locative: 'loving towards those who bow to Her'.

Analysis वन्दारवः जनाः वन्दारुजनाः; वन्दारुजनेषु वत्सला वन्दारुजनवत्सला
vandāravaḥ janāḥ vandārujanāḥ; vandārujaneṣu vatsalā vandārujanavatsalā

Significance vatsala is the love of a cow for her calf: She runs to the devotee who bows to Her as a mother to her child.

350 वाग्वादिनी vāg-vādinī

She who gives voice to all speech

Sandhi वाग्वादिनी = वाच् + वादिनी (vāc + vādinī) — the final c of vāc becomes a velar at the end of a member (Pāṇini 8.2.30 coḥ kuḥ), voiced to g before v by jaśtva (8.2.39): vāg-

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. vādinī is an agent noun from √vad 'to speak' with the suffix ṇini, compounded with its object vāc 'speech': 'she who utters speech'. Feminine -inī.

Analysis वाचम् वदति इति वाग्वादिनी
vācam vadati iti vāgvādinī

Significance The Kena Upaniṣad speaks of 'that which is not uttered by speech, by which speech is uttered' (yad vācānabhyuditaṃ yena vāg abhyudyate). Vāgvādinī is also the name invoked in the mantra of Sarasvatī (vada vada vāgvādini).

351 वामकेशी vāma-keśī

She who has beautiful hair

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. vāma 'beautiful' qualifies keśa 'hair', and the whole describes Her: 'She whose hair is beautiful'. Because keśa is a part of the body, the feminine may end in -ī (Pāṇini 4.1.54 svāṅgāc copasarjanād asaṃyogopadhāt).

Analysis वामाः केशाः यस्याः सा वामकेशी
vāmāḥ keśāḥ yasyāḥ sā vāmakeśī

Significance Traditionally also read as the consort of Vāmakeśa (Śiva); the Vāmakeśvara Tantra is one of the root texts of Śrīvidyā (compare name 945, vāmakeśvarī).

Uncertain Read as a bahuvrīhi ('beautiful-haired') or as the consort of Vāmakeśa, Śiva; the meaning takes the first.

352 वह्निमण्डलवासिनी vahni-maṇḍala-vāsinī

She who resides in the disc of fire

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) vahni-maṇḍala 'the disc (region) of fire' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) vāsinī 'dwelling', an agent noun from √vas with the suffix ṇini, is compounded with its place in the locative sense: 'she who dwells in the region of fire'.

Analysis वह्नेः मण्डलम् वह्निमण्डलम्; वह्निमण्डले वसति इति वह्निमण्डलवासिनी
vahneḥ maṇḍalam vahnimaṇḍalam; vahnimaṇḍale vasati iti vahnimaṇḍalavāsinī

Significance Traditionally the body holds three regions, of fire, sun and moon; the region of fire is placed at the base of the spine, where kuṇḍalinī sleeps.

Śloka 78names 353–356

भक्तिमत्कल्पलतिका पशुपाशविमोचिनी ।
संहृताशेषपाषण्डा सदाचारप्रवर्तिका ॥ ७८ ॥

bhaktimatkalpalatikā paśupāśavimocinī |
saṃhṛtāśeṣapāṣaṇḍā sadācārapravartikā || 78 ||

The names, separated

353भक्तिमत्-कल्प-लतिकाbhaktimat-kalpa-latikā354पशु-पाश-विमोचिनीpaśu-pāśa-vimocinī

355संहृताशेष-पाषण्डाsaṃhṛtāśeṣa-pāṣaṇḍā356सद्-आचार-प्रवर्तिकाsad-ācāra-pravartikā

Translation

353She who is the wish-granting creeper for Her devotees; 354She who frees bound souls (paśu) from their bonds (pāśa);

355She by whom all heretics have been destroyed; 356She who establishes and promotes right conduct.

Where the names meet

Name 355 divides saṃhṛta + aśeṣa + pāṣaṇḍā; the long ā joins saṃhṛta and aśeṣa.

The names

353 भक्तिमत्कल्पलतिका bhaktimat-kalpa-latikā

She who is the wish-granting creeper for Her devotees

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) kalpa-latikā 'the wish-fulfilling creeper': kalpa, as in kalpa-vṛkṣa 'the tree that grants whatever is wished', qualifies latikā (karmadhāraya). (2) The creeper is the head and bhaktimat 'those who have devotion' stands to it in the genitive: 'the wish-granting creeper of the devotees'. The t of bhaktimat stands unchanged before k.

Analysis कल्पा लतिका कल्पलतिका; भक्तिमताम् कल्पलतिका भक्तिमत्कल्पलतिका
kalpā latikā kalpalatikā; bhaktimatām kalpalatikā bhaktimatkalpalatikā

Significance The kalpa creeper of Indra's heaven yields whatever is wished; She gives Her devotees all they seek, and in the end Herself.

354 पशुपाशविमोचिनी paśu-pāśa-vimocinī

She who frees bound souls (paśu) from their bonds (pāśa)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) paśu-pāśa 'the bonds of the bound souls' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) vimocinī 'releaser', an agent noun from the causative of vi + √muc with the suffix ṇini, is compounded with its object: 'she who loosens those bonds'.

Analysis पशूनाम् पाशाः पशुपाशाः; पशुपाशान् विमोचयति इति पशुपाशविमोचिनी
paśūnām pāśāḥ paśupāśāḥ; paśupāśān vimocayati iti paśupāśavimocinī

Significance In Śaiva and Śākta thought the soul bound by impurity is a paśu, its fetters are pāśa, and the Lord is Paśupati; She cuts those fetters.

355 संहृताशेषपाषण्डा saṃhṛtāśeṣa-pāṣaṇḍā

She by whom all heretics have been destroyed

Sandhi संहृत = सम् + हृत (sam + hṛta) — m becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ); before h it remains anusvāra; संहृताशेष = संहृत + अशेष (saṃhṛta + aśeṣa) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya and a nañ-bahuvrīhi). (1) a-śeṣa 'with nothing left over, all' (nañ-bahuvrīhi). (2) aśeṣa-pāṣaṇḍa 'all the heretics' (karmadhāraya). (3) The participle saṃhṛta 'destroyed' is placed first, as is usual for a participle in a bahuvrīhi, and the whole describes Her: 'She by whom all heretics have been destroyed'.

Analysis न शेषः येषाम् ते अशेषाः; अशेषाः पाषण्डाः अशेषपाषण्डाः; संहृताः अशेषपाषण्डाः यया सा संहृताशेषपाषण्डा
na śeṣaḥ yeṣām te aśeṣāḥ; aśeṣāḥ pāṣaṇḍāḥ aśeṣapāṣaṇḍāḥ; saṃhṛtāḥ aśeṣapāṣaṇḍāḥ yayā sā saṃhṛtāśeṣapāṣaṇḍā

Significance Traditionally pāṣaṇḍas are those who abandon dharma and mislead others; inwardly, She destroys hypocrisy and false views in the devotee.

356 सदाचारप्रवर्तिका sad-ācāra-pravartikā

She who establishes and promotes right conduct

Sandhi सदाचार = सत् + आचार (sat + ācāra) — jaśtva: a final t becomes d before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.39 jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) sat-ācāra 'good conduct' (karmadhāraya; sat 'good, true'). (2) pravartikā 'one who sets in motion' is the head and good conduct stands to it in the genitive (as the object of the agent noun).

Analysis सन् आचारः सदाचारः; सदाचारस्य प्रवर्तिका सदाचारप्रवर्तिका
san ācāraḥ sadācāraḥ; sadācārasya pravartikā sadācārapravartikā

Significance Traditionally She upholds the dharma taught in the Veda and the conduct of the good, and inspires others to follow it.

Śloka 79names 357–361

तापत्रयाग्निसन्तप्तसमाह्लादनचन्द्रिका ।
तरुणी तापसाराध्या तनुमध्या तमोऽपहा ॥ ७९ ॥

tāpatrayāgnisantaptasamāhlādanacandrikā |
taruṇī tāpasārādhyā tanumadhyā tamo'pahā || 79 ||

The names, separated

357ताप-त्रयाग्नि-सन्तप्त-समाह्लादन-चन्द्रिकाtāpa-trayāgni-santapta-samāhlādana-candrikā

358तरुणीtaruṇī359तापसाराध्याtāpasārādhyā360तनु-मध्याtanu-madhyā361तमोऽपहाtamo'pahā

Translation

357She who is the moonlight that gives joy to those burned by the triple fire of misery;

358She who is ever young; 359She who is worshipped by ascetics; 360She who is slender-waisted; 361She who dispels darkness, the ignorance of tamas.

तापtāpaburning; affliction, suffering

Where the names meet

Name 357 fills the whole first half. In 361 tamo'pahā the avagraha (ऽ) marks the a of apahā absorbed into the o of tamo.

The names

357 तापत्रयाग्निसन्तप्तसमाह्लादनचन्द्रिका tāpa-trayāgni-santapta-samāhlādana-candrikā

She who is the moonlight that gives joy to those burned by the triple fire of misery

Sandhi त्रयाग्नि = त्रय + अग्नि (traya + agni) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); सन्तप्त = सम् + तप्त (sam + tapta) — m becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ), which takes the place of articulation of the following stop (8.4.58–59 anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ): written n before a dental

Compound karmadhāraya (over inner ṣaṣṭhī-, tṛtīyā- and karmadhāraya compounds). (1) tāpa-traya 'the triad of afflictions' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) …traya-agni 'the fire that is that triad' (karmadhāraya of identification). (3) …agni-santapta 'scorched by that fire' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa): those who suffer. (4) samāhlādana 'gladdening' (agent noun in -ana) takes them as its object (genitive relation) and qualifies candrikā 'moonlight' (karmadhāraya): 'the moonlight that gladdens those scorched …'. In composition the feminine agent noun stands in its stem form.

Analysis तापानाम् त्रयम् तापत्रयम्; तापत्रयम् एव अग्निः तापत्रयाग्निः; तापत्रयाग्निना सन्तप्ताः तापत्रयाग्निसन्तप्ताः; तापत्रयाग्निसन्तप्तानाम् समाह्लादनी चन्द्रिका तापत्रयाग्निसन्तप्तसमाह्लादनचन्द्रिका
tāpānām trayam tāpatrayam; tāpatrayam eva agniḥ tāpatrayāgniḥ; tāpatrayāgninā santaptāḥ tāpatrayāgnisantaptāḥ; tāpatrayāgnisantaptānām samāhlādanī candrikā tāpatrayāgnisantaptasamāhlādanacandrikā

Significance The three afflictions are those arising from oneself (ādhyātmika), from other beings (ādhibhautika) and from the powers of nature (ādhidaivika). As moonlight cools after the heat of day, She brings relief.

358 तरुणी taruṇī

She who is ever young

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance She is beyond time and so never ages; traditionally She is pictured always in the bloom of youth, with the freshness of a girl of sixteen (ṣoḍaśī).

359 तापसाराध्या tāpasārādhyā

She who is worshipped by ascetics

Sandhi तापसाराध्या = तापस + आराध्या (tāpasa + ārādhyā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa. ārādhyā 'to be worshipped' (gerundive) is the head and the ascetics stand to it in the instrumental as the agents.

Analysis तापसैः आराध्या तापसाराध्या
tāpasaiḥ ārādhyā tāpasārādhyā

Significance Those who practise austerity seek Her; traditionally, tapas undertaken without Her is said to bear no fruit.

360 तनुमध्या tanu-madhyā

She who is slender-waisted

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. tanu 'slender' qualifies madhya 'middle, waist', and the whole describes Her: 'She whose waist is slender'; madhya takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis तनु मध्यम् यस्याः सा तनुमध्या
tanu madhyam yasyāḥ sā tanumadhyā

Significance The slender waist belongs to the classical picture of beauty; traditionally it also suggests the subtle, scarcely visible link between the manifest and the unmanifest.

361 तमोऽपहा tamo'pahā

She who dispels darkness, the ignorance of tamas

Sandhi तमोऽपहा = तमस् + अपहा (tamas + apahā) — s becomes ru (Pāṇini 8.2.66), ru becomes u after a and before a (6.1.113 ato ror aplutād aplute), a + u → o by guṇa (6.1.87), and the following a merges into the o (6.1.109 eṅaḥ padāntād ati), marked by the avagraha ऽ

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. apahā is an agent form of apa + √han 'to strike away' (suffix ḍa, with the root reduced to -ha) used after its object: 'she who strikes away darkness'. Feminine -ā.

Analysis तमः अपहन्ति इति तमोऽपहा
tamaḥ apahanti iti tamo'pahā

Significance The prayer 'lead me from darkness to light' (tamaso mā jyotir gamaya, Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad) is answered by Her.

Śloka 80names 362–365

चितिस् तत्पदलक्ष्यार्था चिदेकरसरूपिणी ।
स्वात्मानन्दलवीभूतब्रह्माद्यानन्दसन्ततिः ॥ ८० ॥

citis tatpadalakṣyārthā cidekarasarūpiṇī |
svātmānandalavībhūtabrahmādyānandasantatiḥ || 80 ||

The names, separated ° form as a name on its own; in the recitation above it joins its neighbour

365She for whom the whole range of bliss of Brahmā and the other gods is but a particle of the bliss of Her own Self.
