Where the names meet

चितिस्तत्पद = चितिः + तत्पद… (citiḥ + tatpada…) — visarga becomes s before t (Pāṇini 8.3.34 visarjanīyasya saḥ)

citiḥ (362) is a name on its own; the s of citis- is its visarga before tat-. Names 362–365 open a run of Vedāntic names; 365 fills the whole second half.

The names

362 चितिः citiḥ

She who is Consciousness itself

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance The first sūtra of Kṣemarāja's Pratyabhijñāhṛdaya reads citiḥ svatantrā viśvasiddhihetuḥ, 'Consciousness, free, is the cause of the accomplishment of the universe'. With this name begins a run of names on Her as pure consciousness.

Corrected चित् (चितिः) → चितिः. "चित् (चितिः)" → चितिः: the verse reads चितिस्तत्पदलक्ष्यार्था, so the name is citiḥ; the bracketed alternative was an editorial note left in the name.

363 तत्पदलक्ष्यार्था tat-pada-lakṣyārthā

She who is the implied meaning (lakṣyārtha) of the word 'tat' (That)

Sandhi लक्ष्यार्था = लक्ष्य + अर्था (lakṣya + arthā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over inner karmadhārayas), the final member made feminine. (1) tat-pada 'the word tat' (karmadhāraya of apposition: the word that is 'tat'). (2) lakṣya-artha 'the indicated (implied) meaning' (karmadhāraya). (3) The implied meaning is the head and the word stands to it in the genitive. In apposition to Her the final member takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis तत् इति पदम् तत्पदम्; लक्ष्यः अर्थः लक्ष्यार्थः; तत्पदस्य लक्ष्यार्थः तत्पदलक्ष्यार्थः; सा तत्पदलक्ष्यार्था
tat iti padam tatpadam; lakṣyaḥ arthaḥ lakṣyārthaḥ; tatpadasya lakṣyārthaḥ tatpadalakṣyārthaḥ; sā tatpadalakṣyārthā

Significance In the great saying tat tvam asi ('You are That', Chāndogya Upaniṣad 6.8.7), Vedānta takes 'tat' not in its literal sense (the omniscient Lord with attributes) but in its implied sense, pure consciousness free of qualities; She is that implied meaning. Names 425–427 return to the same saying.

364 चिदेकरसरूपिणी cid-eka-rasa-rūpiṇī

She whose nature is consciousness alone, one undivided essence

Sandhi चिदेक = चित् + एक (cit + eka) — jaśtva: a final t becomes d before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.39 jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte)

Compound karmadhāraya (over an inner karmadhāraya) with the possessive suffix -in. (1) eka-rasa 'a single, uniform essence' (karmadhāraya). (2) cit-ekarasa 'the uniform essence that is consciousness' (karmadhāraya of identification). (3) It is compounded with rūpa 'form', and the possessive suffix -in makes rūpiṇī 'having as form': 'She whose form is consciousness alone, one undivided essence'.

Analysis एकः रसः एकरसः; चित् एव एकरसः चिदेकरसः; चिदेकरसः रूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति चिदेकरसरूपिणी
ekaḥ rasaḥ ekarasaḥ; cit eva ekarasaḥ cidekarasaḥ; cidekarasaḥ rūpam asyāḥ asti iti cidekarasarūpiṇī

Significance Ekarasa is 'of one taste throughout': as the Bṛhadāraṇyaka's lump of salt is salty through and through, She is consciousness through and through, with nothing else mixed in.

365 स्वात्मानन्दलवीभूतब्रह्माद्यानन्दसन्ततिः svātmānanda-lavī-bhūta-brahmādyānanda-santatiḥ

She for whom the whole range of bliss of Brahmā and the other gods is but a particle of the bliss of Her own Self

Sandhi स्वात्म = स्व + आत्म (sva + ātma) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); आत्मानन्द = आत्म + आनन्द (ātma + ānanda) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); ब्रह्मादि = ब्रह्म + आदि (brahma + ādi) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); आद्यानन्द = आदि + आनन्द (ādi + ānanda) — yaṇ: i becomes y before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci); सन्तति = सम् + तति (sam + tati) — m becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ), which takes the place of articulation of the following stop (8.4.58–59 anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ): written n before a dental

Compound bahuvrīhi (over a gati-compound with cvi, ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas and an inner bahuvrīhi). (1) sva-ātman 'Her own Self' and svātma-ānanda 'the bliss of Her own Self' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas; ātman loses its n in composition). (2) lavībhūta 'become a mere particle': lava 'particle' takes the suffix cvi, which turns its a into ī (Pāṇini 7.4.32 asya cvau) and expresses 'becoming what it was not', and it is compounded with bhūta as a gati (1.4.61 ūryādicviḍācaś ca); the bliss of Her Self stands to it in the genitive ('a particle of …'). (3) brahma-ādi 'Brahmā and the others' (bahuvrīhi), brahmādi-ānanda 'their bliss', and …ānanda-santati 'the whole succession of those blisses' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (4) The whole is a bahuvrīhi describing Her: 'She for whom the whole range of the bliss of Brahmā and the other gods has become a mere particle of the bliss of Her own Self'. santati is feminine, so the name ends in -iḥ.

Analysis स्वस्य आत्मा स्वात्मा; स्वात्मनः आनन्दः स्वात्मानन्दः; अलवः लवः भूता लवीभूता; स्वात्मानन्दस्य लवीभूता स्वात्मानन्दलवीभूता; ब्रह्मा आदिः येषाम् ते ब्रह्मादयः; ब्रह्मादीनाम् आनन्दः ब्रह्माद्यानन्दः; ब्रह्माद्यानन्दानाम् सन्ततिः ब्रह्माद्यानन्दसन्ततिः; स्वात्मानन्दलवीभूता ब्रह्माद्यानन्दसन्ततिः यस्याः सा स्वात्मानन्दलवीभूतब्रह्माद्यानन्दसन्ततिः
svasya ātmā svātmā; svātmanaḥ ānandaḥ svātmānandaḥ; alavaḥ lavaḥ bhūtā lavībhūtā; svātmānandasya lavībhūtā svātmānandalavībhūtā; brahmā ādiḥ yeṣām te brahmādayaḥ; brahmādīnām ānandaḥ brahmādyānandaḥ; brahmādyānandānām santatiḥ brahmādyānandasantatiḥ; svātmānandalavībhūtā brahmādyānandasantatiḥ yasyāḥ sā svātmānandalavībhūtabrahmādyānandasantatiḥ

Significance The Taittirīya Upaniṣad measures bliss in steps, each a hundredfold the one before, up to the bliss of Brahmā, and all of it is a fraction of the bliss of Brahman; the Bṛhadāraṇyaka says other beings live on a particle of that bliss. Her own bliss is that whole.

Śloka 81names 366–372

परा प्रत्यक्चितीरूपा पश्यन्ती परदेवता ।
मध्यमा वैखरीरूपा भक्तमानसहंसिका ॥ ८१ ॥

parā pratyakcitīrūpā paśyantī paradevatā |
madhyamā vaikharīrūpā bhaktamānasahaṃsikā || 81 ||

The names, separated

366पराparā367प्रत्यक्-चिती-रूपाpratyak-citī-rūpā368पश्यन्तीpaśyantī369पर-देवताpara-devatā

370मध्यमाmadhyamā371वैखरी-रूपाvaikharī-rūpā372भक्त-मानस-हंसिकाbhakta-mānasa-haṃsikā

Translation

366She who is Parā, the Supreme, the highest level of speech; 367She whose form is inward-turned consciousness; 368She who is Paśyantī, the second level of speech; 369She who is the supreme Deity;

370She who is Madhyamā, the middle level of speech; 371She who is in the form of Vaikharī, audible speech; 372She who is the swan in the minds of Her devotees.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish

पराparāsupreme, highest, beyondpara, feminine
367 प्रत्यक्चितीरूपा pratyak-citī-rūpā
प्रत्यञ्च्pratyañcturned inward, turned backprati + √añc; weak stem pratyac, which ends a member as pratyak
चितीcitīconsciousnessciti with the long ī of this name
रूपाrūpāformrūpa, with the feminine -ā
368 पश्यन्ती paśyantī
पश्यन्तीpaśyantīseeing√dṛś 'to see' (present stem paśya-), present participle, feminine
369 परदेवता para-devatā
परparasupreme, higheststem of parā, by puṃvadbhāva
देवताdevatādeity, divinity

मध्यमाmadhyamāmiddle, intermediatemadhyama 'middlemost', feminine

वैखरीvaikharīvaikharī, audible articulate speech
रूपाrūpāformrūpa, with the feminine -ā
372 भक्तमानसहंसिका bhakta-mānasa-haṃsikā
भक्तbhaktadevotee
मानसmānasamind; Lake Mānasamanas + the suffix -a
हंसिकाhaṃsikāfemale swanhaṃsī with the suffix -ka; the ī is shortened before it

Where the names meet

The four levels of speech run through this śloka: parā (366), paśyantī (368), madhyamā (370) and vaikharī (371), interleaved with 367 and 369. Name 367 pratyak-citī: the k is the c of pratyac before c-.

The names

366 परा parā

She who is Parā, the Supreme, the highest level of speech

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Names 366, 368, 370 and 371 give the four levels of speech: parā (transcendent, undifferentiated), paśyantī ('seeing'), madhyamā ('middle', inner speech) and vaikharī (audible). As Parā She is speech before any distinction of word and meaning, one with consciousness.

367 प्रत्यक्चितीरूपा pratyak-citī-rūpā

She whose form is inward-turned consciousness

Sandhi प्रत्यक्चिती = प्रत्यच् + चिती (pratyac + citī) — the final c of pratyac becomes k at the end of a member (Pāṇini 8.2.30 coḥ kuḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) pratyak-citi 'inward-turned consciousness' (karmadhāraya; the feminine pratīcī returns to the stem pratyac by puṃvadbhāva, Pāṇini 6.3.42). (2) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose form is inward consciousness'. The name has citī with a long ī, a lengthened form of citi.

Analysis प्रतीची चितिः प्रत्यक्चितिः; प्रत्यक्चितिः रूपम् यस्याः सा प्रत्यक्चितीरूपा
pratīcī citiḥ pratyakcitiḥ; pratyakcitiḥ rūpam yasyāḥ sā pratyakcitīrūpā

Significance In Vedānta pratyak-cit or pratyag-ātman is the Self known inwardly as the witness; the Kaṭha Upaniṣad says 'a wise one, seeking immortality, turned his eyes inward and saw the inner Self' (pratyagātmānam aikṣat).

Uncertain The long ī of citī is not the regular form of citi; it is analysed here as a lengthening of citi (some take it as metrical).

368 पश्यन्ती paśyantī

She who is Paśyantī, the second level of speech

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Paśyantī, 'the seeing', is speech in which word and meaning are still one, beheld as a whole before they unfold in sequence; it rises from parā.

Uncertain The bodily seat of each level of speech is placed differently in different texts (paśyantī at the svādhiṣṭhāna in some, at the navel in others); the sequence parā–paśyantī–madhyamā–vaikharī itself is undisputed.

369 परदेवता para-devatā

She who is the supreme Deity

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya. The adjective parā 'supreme' qualifies devatā 'deity' and, in a karmadhāraya, takes its masculine stem para- (puṃvadbhāva, Pāṇini 6.3.42).

Analysis परा देवता परदेवता
parā devatā paradevatā

Significance She is the deity beyond all deities, Parāśakti, from whom the gods receive their power.

370 मध्यमा madhyamā

She who is Madhyamā, the middle level of speech

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Madhyamā is inner speech, where words are formed in sequence in the mind but not yet spoken; traditionally it is placed at the heart.

Uncertain The bodily seat of each level of speech is placed differently in different texts (paśyantī at the svādhiṣṭhāna in some, at the navel in others); the sequence parā–paśyantī–madhyamā–vaikharī itself is undisputed.

371 वैखरीरूपा vaikharī-rūpā

She who is in the form of Vaikharī, audible speech

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. vaikharī and rūpa are co-referential and the whole describes Her: 'She whose form is vaikharī'.

Analysis वैखरी रूपम् यस्याः सा वैखरीरूपा
vaikharī rūpam yasyāḥ sā vaikharīrūpā

Significance Vaikharī is speech articulated through throat and mouth and heard by the ear: the fourth and outermost level. Every spoken word is thus Her form.

372 भक्तमानसहंसिका bhakta-mānasa-haṃsikā

She who is the swan in the minds of Her devotees

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound saptamī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) bhakta-mānasa 'the mind of the devotees' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) haṃsikā 'swan' is the head and the mind stands to it in the locative: 'the swan in the devotees' minds'. mānasa also means Lake Mānasa, home of the swans, so the compound carries a double image.

Analysis भक्तानाम् मानसम् भक्तमानसम्; भक्तमानसे हंसिका भक्तमानसहंसिका
bhaktānām mānasam bhaktamānasam; bhaktamānase haṃsikā bhaktamānasahaṃsikā

Significance As swans live on Lake Mānasa, She lives in the devotee's mind (mānasa); the swan, said to separate milk from water, is also the emblem of discrimination and of the paramahaṃsa. Compare name 816, munimānasahaṃsikā.

Śloka 82names 373–378

कामेश्वरप्राणनाडी कृतज्ञा कामपूजिता ।
शृङ्गाररससम्पूर्णा जया जालन्धरस्थिता ॥ ८२ ॥

kāmeśvaraprāṇanāḍī kṛtajñā kāmapūjitā |
śṛṅgārarasasampūrṇā jayā jālandharasthitā || 82 ||

The names, separated

373कामेश्वर-प्राण-नाडीkāmeśvara-prāṇa-nāḍī374कृत-ज्ञाkṛta-jñā375काम-पूजिताkāma-pūjitā

376शृङ्गार-रस-सम्पूर्णाśṛṅgāra-rasa-sampūrṇā377जयाjayā378जालन्धर-स्थिताjālandhara-sthitā

Translation

373She who is the very life-channel of Kāmeśvara, Her consort; 374She who knows all that is done, and is grateful for it; 375She who is worshipped by Kāma;

376She who is filled with śṛṅgāra, the rasa of love; 377She who is victorious; 378She who abides in the Jālandhara pīṭha.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish
373 कामेश्वरप्राणनाडी kāmeśvara-prāṇa-nāḍī
कामkāmadesire; Kāma
ईश्वरīśvaralord
प्राणprāṇalife-breath, life
नाडीnāḍīchannel, vessel, artery
374 कृतज्ञा kṛta-jñā
कृतkṛtawhat has been done, a deed; a service done√kṛ, past participle
ज्ञाjñāknowing√jñā 'to know' with the suffix ka, feminine
375 कामपूजिता kāma-pūjitā
कामkāmaKāma (Manmatha), the god of love
पूजिताpūjitāworshipped√pūj, past participle, feminine
376 शृङ्गाररससम्पूर्णा śṛṅgāra-rasa-sampūrṇā
शृङ्गारśṛṅgāraśṛṅgāra, the erotic or romantic sentiment, love
रसrasarasa, aesthetic sentiment; essence
सम्पूर्णाsampūrṇācompletely fullsam + √pṝ 'to fill', past participle, feminine

जयाjayāvictorious; victory√ji 'to conquer' (jaya), feminine
378 जालन्धरस्थिता jālandhara-sthitā
जालन्धरjālandharaJālandhara, one of the four principal pīṭhas (seats of the Goddess)
स्थिताsthitāabiding, situated√sthā, past participle, feminine

Where the names meet

Names 375–379 are traditionally read as recalling the four pīṭhas: Kāma(giri) in 375, Pūrṇa(giri) in 376 sampūrṇā, then Jālandhara (378) and Oḍyāṇa (379); the bindu (380) lies beyond them.

The names

373 कामेश्वरप्राणनाडी kāmeśvara-prāṇa-nāḍī

She who is the very life-channel of Kāmeśvara, Her consort

Sandhi कामेश्वर = काम + ईश्वर (kāma + īśvara) — guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (1) kāma-īśvara 'the Lord of desire', Śiva as Kāmeśvara (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) prāṇa-nāḍī 'the channel of the life-breath', the vital artery (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) The life-channel is the head and Kāmeśvara stands to it in the genitive.

Analysis कामस्य ईश्वरः कामेश्वरः; प्राणस्य नाडी प्राणनाडी; कामेश्वरस्य प्राणनाडी कामेश्वरप्राणनाडी
kāmasya īśvaraḥ kāmeśvaraḥ; prāṇasya nāḍī prāṇanāḍī; kāmeśvarasya prāṇanāḍī kāmeśvaraprāṇanāḍī

Significance Without Her, Śiva cannot even stir (Saundaryalaharī 1). The Saundaryalaharī (28) also says that the gods who drank nectar perish at the dissolution while Śiva, who drank poison, lives, because of the power of Her earrings: She is His life.

374 कृतज्ञा kṛta-jñā

She who knows all that is done, and is grateful for it

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. jñā is an agent form of √jñā 'to know' (suffix ka, Pāṇini 3.2.3 āto 'nupasarge kaḥ), used only after its object: 'she who knows what has been done'. Feminine -ā.

Analysis कृतम् जानाति इति कृतज्ञा
kṛtam jānāti iti kṛtajñā

Significance Traditionally She is the inner witness who knows every act as it occurs; in ordinary usage kṛtajña means 'grateful', and She remembers and rewards the least service done to Her.

Uncertain kṛtajñā means both 'knowing what is done' and 'grateful'; both are given.

375 कामपूजिता kāma-pūjitā

She who is worshipped by Kāma

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa. pūjitā 'worshipped' is the head and Kāma stands to it in the instrumental as the agent.

Analysis कामेन पूजिता कामपूजिता
kāmena pūjitā kāmapūjitā

Significance Kāma is counted traditionally among the great worshippers of Śrīvidyā, and the kādi form of the fifteen-syllabled mantra is associated with him. Traditionally the name also alludes to Kāmagiri (Kāmarūpa), first of the four pīṭhas that names 375–379 recall.

Uncertain The allusion to the Kāmagiri pīṭha (reading 'worshipped at Kāma[giri]') is traditional but not in the grammar of the name.

376 शृङ्गाररससम्पूर्णा śṛṅgāra-rasa-sampūrṇā

She who is filled with śṛṅgāra, the rasa of love

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) śṛṅgāra-rasa 'the rasa that is śṛṅgāra', the sentiment of love (karmadhāraya of apposition). (2) The participle sampūrṇā 'completely filled' is the head and the rasa stands to it in the instrumental.

Analysis शृङ्गारः एव रसः शृङ्गाररसः; शृङ्गाररसेन सम्पूर्णा शृङ्गाररससम्पूर्णा
śṛṅgāraḥ eva rasaḥ śṛṅgārarasaḥ; śṛṅgārarasena sampūrṇā śṛṅgārarasasampūrṇā

Significance Śṛṅgāra is the first and chief of the rasas of poetics; She is its fullness, the love between Śiva and Śakti. Traditionally the word sampūrṇā also alludes to Pūrṇagiri, the second of the four pīṭhas.

Corrected श‍ृङ्गाररससम्पूर्णा → शृङ्गाररससम्पूर्णा. Removed a zero-width joiner inside शृ; the IAST had become "śa‍ṛṅgāra".

377 जया jayā

She who is victorious

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Jayā is also a name of Durgā; She is victory itself, and victory in any field is Hers.

378 जालन्धरस्थिता jālandhara-sthitā

She who abides in the Jālandhara pīṭha

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound saptamī-tatpuruṣa. The participle sthitā 'abiding' is the head and Jālandhara stands to it in the locative of place.

Analysis जालन्धरे स्थिता जालन्धरस्थिता
jālandhare sthitā jālandharasthitā

Significance Jālandhara is the third of the four pīṭhas (Kāmagiri, Pūrṇagiri, Jālandhara, Oḍyāṇa); in the body it is traditionally placed at the throat (viśuddhi).

Śloka 83names 379–382

ओड्याणपीठनिलया बिन्दुमण्डलवासिनी ।
रहोयागक्रमाराध्या रहस्तर्पणतर्पिता ॥ ८३ ॥

oḍyāṇapīṭhanilayā bindumaṇḍalavāsinī |
rahoyāgakramārādhyā rahastarpaṇatarpitā || 83 ||

The names, separated

379ओड्याण-पीठ-निलयाoḍyāṇa-pīṭha-nilayā380बिन्दु-मण्डल-वासिनीbindu-maṇḍala-vāsinī

381रहो-याग-क्रमाराध्याraho-yāga-kramārādhyā382रहस्-तर्पण-तर्पिताrahas-tarpaṇa-tarpitā

Translation

379She whose abode is the Oḍyāṇa pīṭha; 380She who resides in the bindu at the center of the Śrīcakra;

381She who is to be worshipped by the method of secret, inner worship; 382She who is gratified by secret offerings of libation.

Where the names meet

381 raho-yāga: raho is rahas before a voiced sound; 382 keeps the s (rahas-tarpaṇa) before t.

The names

379 ओड्याणपीठनिलया oḍyāṇa-pīṭha-nilayā

She whose abode is the Oḍyāṇa pīṭha

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) oḍyāṇa-pīṭha 'the seat that is Oḍyāṇa' (karmadhāraya of apposition). (2) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose abode (nilaya) is the Oḍyāṇa seat'; nilaya takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis ओड्याणम् एव पीठम् ओड्याणपीठम्; ओड्याणपीठम् निलयः यस्याः सा ओड्याणपीठनिलया
oḍyāṇam eva pīṭham oḍyāṇapīṭham; oḍyāṇapīṭham nilayaḥ yasyāḥ sā oḍyāṇapīṭhanilayā

Significance Oḍyāṇa is the fourth of the four pīṭhas; in the body it is traditionally placed between the eyebrows (ājñā). Beyond the four lies the bindu, the next name.

380 बिन्दुमण्डलवासिनी bindu-maṇḍala-vāsinī

She who resides in the bindu at the center of the Śrīcakra

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) bindu-maṇḍala 'the circle that is the bindu' (karmadhāraya of apposition). (2) vāsinī 'dwelling', an agent noun from √vas with ṇini, is compounded with its place in the locative sense.

Analysis बिन्दुः एव मण्डलम् बिन्दुमण्डलम्; बिन्दुमण्डले वसति इति बिन्दुमण्डलवासिनी
binduḥ eva maṇḍalam bindumaṇḍalam; bindumaṇḍale vasati iti bindumaṇḍalavāsinī

Significance The bindu is the innermost enclosure of the Śrīcakra, the sarvānandamaya cakra, where She is one with Kāmeśvara; in the body it corresponds to the crown, beyond the four pīṭhas.

381 रहोयागक्रमाराध्या raho-yāga-kramārādhyā

She who is to be worshipped by the method of secret, inner worship

Sandhi रहोयाग = रहस् + याग (rahas + yāga) — final -as before a voiced consonant: s becomes ru (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ), ru becomes u after a (6.1.114 haśi ca), and a + u → o by guṇa (6.1.87): -o; क्रमाराध्या = क्रम + आराध्या (krama + ārādhyā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over inner ṣaṣṭhī- and saptamī-tatpuruṣas). (1) rahas-yāga 'worship in secret' (saptamī-tatpuruṣa). (2) …yāga-krama 'the ordered method of that worship' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) ārādhyā 'to be worshipped' is the head and the method stands to it in the instrumental: 'to be worshipped by the method of secret worship'.

Analysis रहसि यागः रहोयागः; रहोयागस्य क्रमः रहोयागक्रमः; रहोयागक्रमेण आराध्या रहोयागक्रमाराध्या
rahasi yāgaḥ rahoyāgaḥ; rahoyāgasya kramaḥ rahoyāgakramaḥ; rahoyāgakrameṇa ārādhyā rahoyāgakramārādhyā

Significance Traditionally rahoyāga is antar-yāga, the inner worship in which the offerings are mental and kuṇḍalinī is led through the cakras to unite with Śiva; it is guarded and taught only from teacher to disciple.

382 रहस्तर्पणतर्पिता rahas-tarpaṇa-tarpitā

She who is gratified by secret offerings of libation

Sandhi रहस्तर्पण = रहस् + तर्पण (rahas + tarpaṇa) — s becomes ru (Pāṇini 8.2.66) and visarga before a voiceless sound (8.3.15 kharavasānayor visarjanīyaḥ), which becomes s before t (8.3.34 visarjanīyasya saḥ): the s reappears

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner saptamī-tatpuruṣa). (1) rahas-tarpaṇa 'a secret oblation' (saptamī-tatpuruṣa). (2) The participle tarpitā 'gratified' is the head and the oblation stands to it in the instrumental as the means. The same root √tṛp 'to satisfy' gives both members.

Analysis रहसि तर्पणम् रहस्तर्पणम्; रहस्तर्पणेन तर्पिता रहस्तर्पणतर्पिता
rahasi tarpaṇam rahastarpaṇam; rahastarpaṇena tarpitā rahastarpaṇatarpitā

Significance Traditionally the secret tarpaṇa is inward: the nectar released when kuṇḍalinī reaches the crown floods and satisfies the deities of the body, or the senses' objects are offered into the fire of consciousness.

Śloka 84names 383–387

सद्यःप्रसादिनी विश्वसाक्षिणी साक्षिवर्जिता ।
षडङ्गदेवतायुक्ता षाड्गुण्यपरिपूरिता ॥ ८४ ॥

sadyaḥprasādinī viśvasākṣiṇī sākṣivarjitā |
ṣaḍaṅgadevatāyuktā ṣāḍguṇyaparipūritā || 84 ||

The names, separated

383सद्यः-प्रसादिनीsadyaḥ-prasādinī384विश्व-साक्षिणीviśva-sākṣiṇī385साक्षि-वर्जिताsākṣi-varjitā

383She who bestows Her grace immediately; 384She who is witness to the whole universe; 385She who has no other witness;

386She who is accompanied by the deities of the six aṅgas (heart, head, crest, armor, eyes and weapon); 387She who is completely filled with the six excellences (bhaga).

Where the names meet

383 keeps the visarga inside the name: sadyaḥ-prasādinī.

The names

383 सद्यःप्रसादिनी sadyaḥ-prasādinī

She who bestows Her grace immediately

Sandhi सद्यःप्रसादिनी = सद्यस् + प्रसादिनी (sadyas + prasādinī) — s becomes ru (Pāṇini 8.2.66) and then visarga before the voiceless p (8.3.15 kharavasānayor visarjanīyaḥ)

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (with the adverb sadyas). prasādinī is an agent noun from pra + √sad 'to be pleased, gracious' with the suffix ṇini (Pāṇini 3.2.78), which here marks a habit; the indeclinable sadyas 'at once' is compounded with it: 'she who is gracious at once'.

Analysis सद्यः प्रसीदति इति सद्यःप्रसादिनी
sadyaḥ prasīdati iti sadyaḥprasādinī

Significance Traditionally She is quickly pleased by sincere devotion, without long austerities; Her grace is not delayed.

384 विश्वसाक्षिणी viśva-sākṣiṇī

She who is witness to the whole universe

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. sākṣiṇī 'witness' is the head and the universe stands to it in the genitive.

Analysis विश्वस्य साक्षिणी विश्वसाक्षिणी
viśvasya sākṣiṇī viśvasākṣiṇī

Significance As pure consciousness She sees all without being touched by what She sees, as the Upaniṣads describe the Self as the witness (sākṣin).

385 साक्षिवर्जिता sākṣi-varjitā

She who has no other witness

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa. The participle varjitā 'devoid of' is the head and sākṣin 'witness' stands to it in the instrumental (sākṣin loses its n in composition).

Analysis साक्षिभिः वर्जिता साक्षिवर्जिता
sākṣibhiḥ varjitā sākṣivarjitā

Significance She is the witness of all, and nothing stands outside Her to witness Her; consciousness is known by itself alone.

386 षडङ्गदेवतायुक्ता ṣaḍ-aṅga-devatā-yuktā

She who is accompanied by the deities of the six aṅgas (heart, head, crest, armor, eyes and weapon)

Sandhi षडङ्ग = षष् + अङ्ग (ṣaṣ + aṅga) — the final ṣ of ṣaṣ 'six' becomes ḍ at the end of a member (jaśtva, Pāṇini 8.2.39)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and a dvigu). (1) ṣaṭ-aṅga 'the six limbs' (a numeral compound, dvigu). (2) …aṅga-devatā 'the deities of the six limbs' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) The participle yuktā 'accompanied' is the head and the deities stand to it in the instrumental.

Analysis षट् अङ्गानि षडङ्गानि; षडङ्गानाम् देवताः षडङ्गदेवताः; षडङ्गदेवताभिः युक्ता षडङ्गदेवतायुक्ता
ṣaṭ aṅgāni ṣaḍaṅgāni; ṣaḍaṅgānām devatāḥ ṣaḍaṅgadevatāḥ; ṣaḍaṅgadevatābhiḥ yuktā ṣaḍaṅgadevatāyuktā

Significance In ritual the six limbs of the mantra are placed on the body (aṅga-nyāsa) as heart, head, crest of hair, armor, eyes and weapon. Traditionally the name is also read of Śiva's six attributes: omniscience, contentment, beginningless knowledge, independence, unfailing power and infinite power.

387 षाड्गुण्यपरिपूरिता ṣāḍguṇya-paripūritā

She who is completely filled with the six excellences (bhaga)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa. The participle paripūritā 'completely filled' is the head and ṣāḍguṇya 'the six excellences' stands to it in the instrumental. ṣāḍguṇya is a single derived word (from ṣaḍ-guṇa 'six qualities' with a collective suffix and vṛddhi), so no junction inside it is analysed here.

Analysis षाड्गुण्येन परिपूरिता षाड्गुण्यपरिपूरिता
ṣāḍguṇyena paripūritā ṣāḍguṇyaparipūritā

Significance The Viṣṇu Purāṇa names the six that make up bhaga, divine excellence: complete sovereignty, dharma, glory, fortune, knowledge and dispassion; some lists have valor (vīrya) in place of dharma.

Śloka 85names 388–392

नित्यक्लिन्ना निरुपमा निर्वाणसुखदायिनी ।
नित्याषोडशिकारूपा श्रीकण्ठार्धशरीरिणी ॥ ८५ ॥

nityaklinnā nirupamā nirvāṇasukhadāyinī |
nityāṣoḍaśikārūpā śrīkaṇṭhārdhaśarīriṇī || 85 ||

The names, separated

388नित्य-क्लिन्नाnitya-klinnā389निर्-उपमाnir-upamā390निर्वाण-सुख-दायिनीnirvāṇa-sukha-dāyinī

391नित्या-षोडशिका-रूपाnityā-ṣoḍaśikā-rūpā392श्रीकण्ठार्ध-शरीरिणीśrīkaṇṭhārdha-śarīriṇī

Translation

388She who is ever moist with compassion; 389She who is incomparable; 390She who confers the bliss of liberation;

391She who has the form of the sixteen Nityā goddesses; 392She who possesses half of the body of Śrīkaṇṭha (Śiva), as Ardhanārīśvara.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish

Where the names meet

Nityaklinnā (388), Śivadūtī (405) and Vijayā (346) are also names of individual Nityā goddesses; 391 names the sixteen together. 390 is one compound (nirvāṇa-sukha-dāyinī), though it was printed as two words.

The names

388 नित्यक्लिन्ना nitya-klinnā

She who is ever moist with compassion

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya (supsupā, with an adverbial first member). The adverb nityam 'always' qualifies the participle klinnā 'moist': 'ever-moist'. The members are simply juxtaposed.

Analysis नित्यम् क्लिन्ना नित्यक्लिन्ना
nityam klinnā nityaklinnā

Significance The moistness is the melting of Her heart in compassion. Nityaklinnā is also the third of the Nityā goddesses of the lunar fortnight (see name 391).

389 निरुपमा nir-upamā

She who is incomparable

Sandhi निरुपमा = निस् + उपमा (nis + upamā) — the s of the prefix nis becomes r (through ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ) before a voiced sound

Compound prādi-bahuvrīhi. nis stands for nirgata 'gone out', and the compound describes Her: 'She from whom all comparison has gone', i.e. who has no equal.

Analysis निर्गता उपमा यस्याः सा निरुपमा
nirgatā upamā yasyāḥ sā nirupamā

Significance Nothing can be compared with Her, since there is nothing other than Her; as the Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad says, 'there is no likeness of Him' (na tasya pratimā asti).

390 निर्वाणसुखदायिनी nirvāṇa-sukha-dāyinī

She who confers the bliss of liberation

Sandhi निर्वाण = निस् + वाण (nis + vāṇa) — the s of the prefix nis becomes r (through ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ) before a voiced sound; the r then turns the n of vāna into ṇ (ṇatva)

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) nirvāṇa-sukha 'the bliss that is liberation' (karmadhāraya of identification; a genitive reading 'the bliss of liberation' gives the same sense). (2) dāyinī 'giver', an agent noun from √dā with ṇini (the root takes y before -in), is compounded with its object.

Analysis निर्वाणम् एव सुखम् निर्वाणसुखम्; निर्वाणसुखम् ददाति इति निर्वाणसुखदायिनी
nirvāṇam eva sukham nirvāṇasukham; nirvāṇasukham dadāti iti nirvāṇasukhadāyinī

Significance Nirvāṇa is the 'blowing out' of bondage; its bliss is not a pleasure that ends but the Self's own nature, which She reveals.

Corrected निर्वाण सुखदायिनी → निर्वाणसुखदायिनी. "निर्वाण सुखदायिनी" → निर्वाणसुखदायिनी: one compound name; the space split it into what reads as two words.

391 नित्याषोडशिकारूपा nityā-ṣoḍaśikā-rūpā

She who has the form of the sixteen Nityā goddesses

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) nityā-ṣoḍaśikā 'the group of sixteen Nityās' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). The first member keeps its feminine -ā (nityā, not nitya-) as the name of the goddesses. (2) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose form is the sixteen Nityās'.

Analysis नित्यानाम् षोडशिका नित्याषोडशिका; नित्याषोडशिका रूपम् यस्याः सा नित्याषोडशिकारूपा
nityānām ṣoḍaśikā nityāṣoḍaśikā; nityāṣoḍaśikā rūpam yasyāḥ sā nityāṣoḍaśikārūpā

Significance The Nityās are the deities of the lunar days: Kāmeśvarī, Bhagamālinī, Nityaklinnā, Bheruṇḍā, Vahnivāsinī, Mahāvajreśvarī, Śivadūtī, Tvaritā, Kulasundarī, Nityā, Nīlapatākā, Vijayā, Sarvamaṅgalā, Jvālāmālinī and Citrā, with Lalitā Herself as the sixteenth, Mahānityā. Their worship is set out in the Nityāṣoḍaśikārṇava.

Corrected नित्या-षोडशिकारूपा → नित्याषोडशिकारूपा. A hyphen had been typed into the Devanagari (नित्या-षोडशिका); Devanagari compounds are written solid.

392 श्रीकण्ठार्धशरीरिणी śrīkaṇṭhārdha-śarīriṇī

She who possesses half of the body of Śrīkaṇṭha (Śiva), as Ardhanārīśvara

Sandhi श्रीकण्ठार्ध = श्रीकण्ठ + अर्ध (śrīkaṇṭha + ardha) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound karmadhāraya with the possessive suffix -in (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and a bahuvrīhi). (1) śrī-kaṇṭha 'he in whose throat is beauty' (bahuvrīhi), a name of Śiva, whose throat is marked by the poison He held there. (2) śrīkaṇṭha-ardha 'half of Śrīkaṇṭha' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) This is compounded with śarīra 'body', and the possessive suffix -in makes śarīriṇī: 'She who has half of Śiva as Her body'.

Analysis श्रीः कण्ठे यस्य सः श्रीकण्ठः; श्रीकण्ठस्य अर्धम् श्रीकण्ठार्धम्; श्रीकण्ठार्धम् शरीरम् अस्याः अस्ति इति श्रीकण्ठार्धशरीरिणी
śrīḥ kaṇṭhe yasya saḥ śrīkaṇṭhaḥ; śrīkaṇṭhasya ardham śrīkaṇṭhārdham; śrīkaṇṭhārdham śarīram asyāḥ asti iti śrīkaṇṭhārdhaśarīriṇī

Significance She is the left half of Śiva in the form Ardhanārīśvara, half woman and half man: Śiva and Śakti are inseparable.

Uncertain For an exact half Pāṇini's rule (2.2.2 ardhaṃ napuṃsakam) puts ardha first; here, as often in later usage, it follows in a genitive compound.

Where the names meet

मूलप्रकृतिरव्यक्ता = मूलप्रकृतिः + अव्यक्ता (mūlaprakṛtiḥ + avyaktā) — visarga after i becomes r before a vowel (the r of ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66)

mūlaprakṛtiḥ (397) and avyaktā (398) are separate names; the r of -prakṛtir is the visarga before a-.

The names

393 प्रभावती prabhāvatī

She who is effulgent

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Traditionally Her radiance is the light of the deities who surround Her in the Śrīcakra, rays of Her own splendor.

394 प्रभारूपा prabhā-rūpā

She who is effulgence

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. prabhā 'radiance' and rūpa 'form' are co-referential, and the compound describes Her: 'She whose form is radiance'.

Analysis प्रभा रूपम् यस्याः सा प्रभारूपा
prabhā rūpam yasyāḥ sā prabhārūpā

Significance She does not merely possess light (previous name); She is light, the light of consciousness by which all else is seen.

395 प्रसिद्धा prasiddhā

She who is celebrated

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Traditionally She is known to everyone, since She is the 'I' that each being knows as itself, even when Her true nature is not recognized.

396 परमेश्वरी parameśvarī

She who is the supreme sovereign

Sandhi परमेश्वरी = परम + ईश्वरी (parama + īśvarī) — guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound karmadhāraya. The adjective paramā 'supreme' qualifies īśvarī 'sovereign' and takes its masculine stem parama- in the karmadhāraya (puṃvadbhāva, Pāṇini 6.3.42).

Analysis परमा ईश्वरी परमेश्वरी
paramā īśvarī parameśvarī

Significance She rules over all rulers, including the gods who govern creation, preservation and dissolution.

397 मूलप्रकृतिः mūla-prakṛtiḥ

She who is the root Nature (mūlaprakṛti), the first cause of the universe

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya. mūla 'root' stands in apposition to prakṛti 'nature', the head: 'the Nature that is the root'. prakṛti is feminine, so the name ends in -iḥ.

Analysis मूलम् प्रकृतिः मूलप्रकृतिः
mūlam prakṛtiḥ mūlaprakṛtiḥ

Significance Mūlaprakṛti is the Sāṅkhya term for primal matter, itself uncaused (the Sāṅkhyakārikā: mūlaprakṛtir avikṛtiḥ); in Śrīvidyā this root of all evolution is Her own power.

398 अव्यक्ता avyaktā

She who is unmanifested

Sandhi व्यक्ता = वि + अक्ता (vi + aktā) — yaṇ: i becomes y before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci), at the junction of the prefix vi with akta (√añj)

Compound nañ-tatpuruṣa. The negative na, reduced to a- (Pāṇini 6.3.73 nalopo nañaḥ), is compounded with the participle vyaktā 'manifest': 'not manifest'.

Analysis न व्यक्ता अव्यक्ता
na vyaktā avyaktā

Significance Avyakta is the unmanifest state of prakṛti, beyond the great principle (mahat), as the Kaṭha Upaniṣad says: mahataḥ param avyaktam.

399 व्यक्ताव्यक्तस्वरूपिणी vyaktāvyakta-svarūpiṇī

She who is in the manifested and unmanifested forms

Sandhi व्यक्ताव्यक्त = व्यक्त + अव्यक्त (vyakta + avyakta) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound karmadhāraya with the possessive suffix -in (over an inner itaretara-dvandva). (1) vyakta-avyakta 'the manifest and the unmanifest' (itaretara-dvandva). (2) This is compounded with svarūpa 'own nature', and the possessive suffix -in makes svarūpiṇī 'having as Her own nature'.

Analysis व्यक्तम् च अव्यक्तम् च व्यक्ताव्यक्ते; व्यक्ताव्यक्ते स्वरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति व्यक्ताव्यक्तस्वरूपिणी
vyaktam ca avyaktam ca vyaktāvyakte; vyaktāvyakte svarūpam asyāḥ asti iti vyaktāvyaktasvarūpiṇī

Significance Both the evolved world and its unevolved cause are Her; She is not only the root (397–398) but also all that grows from it.

Corrected व्यक्ताव्यक्तस्वरूपीणि → व्यक्ताव्यक्तस्वरूपिणी. स्वरूपीणि → स्वरूपिणी (-iṇī: short i, long final ī).

Where the names meet

The half-line in text.json reads विद्याविद्या-स्वरूपिणी, with a hyphen typed into the Devanagari and without the avagraha that the name (402) has; see the text concern on 402. Name 403 fills the whole second half.

The names

400 व्यापिनी vyāpinī

She who is all-pervading

Sandhi व्यापिनी = वि + आपिनी (vi + āpinī) — yaṇ: i becomes y before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci), at the junction of the prefix vi with āpinī

Compound not a compound

Significance There is no place where She is not; as space pervades all pots, She pervades all beings.

401 विविधाकारा vividhākārā

She who has a multitude of forms

Sandhi विविधाकारा = विविध + आकारा (vividha + ākārā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi. vividha 'various' qualifies ākāra 'form', and the whole describes Her: 'She whose forms are manifold'; ākāra takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis विविधाः आकाराः यस्याः सा विविधाकारा
vividhāḥ ākārāḥ yasyāḥ sā vividhākārā

Significance Every form in the universe is one of Her forms; traditionally, in worship She takes whatever form the devotee holds dear.

402 विद्याऽविद्यास्वरूपिणी vidyā'vidyā-svarūpiṇī

She who is the form of both knowledge and ignorance

Sandhi विद्याऽविद्या = विद्या + अविद्या (vidyā + avidyā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); the avagraha ऽ marks the absorbed a

Compound karmadhāraya with the possessive suffix -in (over an inner itaretara-dvandva). (1) vidyā-avidyā 'knowledge and ignorance' (itaretara-dvandva). (2) This is compounded with svarūpa 'own nature', and the possessive suffix -in makes svarūpiṇī.

Analysis विद्या च अविद्या च विद्याविद्ये; विद्याविद्ये स्वरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति विद्याऽविद्यास्वरूपिणी
vidyā ca avidyā ca vidyāvidye; vidyāvidye svarūpam asyāḥ asti iti vidyā'vidyāsvarūpiṇī

Significance The Devī Māhātmya (ch. 1) calls Her the supreme knowledge that is the cause of liberation and also the cause of the bondage of saṃsāra; the Īśa Upaniṣad teaches that one crosses death by avidyā and gains immortality by vidyā.

403 महाकामेशनयनकुमुदाह्लादकौमुदी mahā-kāmeśa-nayana-kumudāhlāda-kaumudī

She who is the moonlight that gladdens the water-lilies that are Mahākāmeśa's eyes

Sandhi कामेश = काम + ईश (kāma + īśa) — guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ); कुमुदाह्लाद = कुमुद + आह्लाद (kumuda + āhlāda) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound karmadhāraya with a dropped middle member (over inner karmadhārayas and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (1) kāma-īśa 'the Lord of desire' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa), and mahā-kāmeśa 'the great Kāmeśa' (karmadhāraya; mahat becomes mahā-). (2) …kāmeśa-nayana 'the eyes of Mahākāmeśa' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) …nayana-kumuda 'the eyes, which are night-lilies' (karmadhāraya of identification, rūpaka). (4) …kumuda-āhlāda 'the gladdening of those lilies' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (5) …āhlāda-kaumudī 'the moonlight that causes that gladdening' (karmadhāraya with the middle word kāriṇī 'causing' understood). kaumudī is feminine already.

Analysis कामस्य ईशः कामेशः; महान् कामेशः महाकामेशः; महाकामेशस्य नयने महाकामेशनयने; महाकामेशनयने एव कुमुदे महाकामेशनयनकुमुदे; महाकामेशनयनकुमुदयोः आह्लादः महाकामेशनयनकुमुदाह्लादः; महाकामेशनयनकुमुदाह्लादकारिणी कौमुदी महाकामेशनयनकुमुदाह्लादकौमुदी
kāmasya īśaḥ kāmeśaḥ; mahān kāmeśaḥ mahākāmeśaḥ; mahākāmeśasya nayane mahākāmeśanayane; mahākāmeśanayane eva kumude mahākāmeśanayanakumude; mahākāmeśanayanakumudayoḥ āhlādaḥ mahākāmeśanayanakumudāhlādaḥ; mahākāmeśanayanakumudāhlādakāriṇī kaumudī mahākāmeśanayanakumudāhlādakaumudī

Significance The kumuda opens only at moonrise: Śiva's eyes open in joy only at the sight of Her. Traditionally the image also says that without Her, Śiva does not act.

शिवśivaŚiva

Where the names meet

Name 404 fills the first half. Names 405–410 (into śloka 89) all begin with śiva-; 408 śivaṅkarī is śivam + karī.

The names

404 भक्तहार्दतमोभेदभानुमद्भानुसन्ततिः bhakta-hārda-tamo-bheda-bhānumad-bhānu-santatiḥ

She who is the stream of sunrays that dispels the darkness in the hearts of Her devotees

Sandhi तमोभेद = तमस् + भेद (tamas + bheda) — final -as before a voiced consonant: s becomes ru (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ), ru becomes u after a (6.1.114 haśi ca), and a + u → o by guṇa (6.1.87): -o; भानुमद्भानु = भानुमत् + भानु (bhānumat + bhānu) — jaśtva: a final t becomes d before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.39 jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte); सन्तति = सम् + तति (sam + tati) — m becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ), which takes the place of articulation of the following stop (8.4.58–59 anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ): written n before a dental

Compound karmadhāraya with a dropped middle member (over inner karmadhārayas and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas). (1) hārda-tamas 'the darkness of the heart' (karmadhāraya; hārda 'belonging to the heart'), and bhakta-hārdatamas 'the heart-darkness of the devotees' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) …tamo-bheda 'the piercing of that darkness' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) bhānumad-bhānu 'the rays of the sun' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; bhānumat 'possessing rays' is the sun) and …bhānu-santati 'a stream of those rays'. (4) The two halves join as a karmadhāraya with 'causing' understood: 'the stream of sunrays that pierces the darkness in the devotees' hearts'. santati is feminine, so the name ends in -iḥ.

Analysis हार्दम् तमः हार्दतमः; भक्तानाम् हार्दतमः भक्तहार्दतमः; भक्तहार्दतमसः भेदः भक्तहार्दतमोभेदः; भानुमतः भानवः भानुमद्भानवः; भानुमद्भानूनाम् सन्ततिः भानुमद्भानुसन्ततिः; भक्तहार्दतमोभेदकारिणी भानुमद्भानुसन्ततिः भक्तहार्दतमोभेदभानुमद्भानुसन्ततिः
hārdam tamaḥ hārdatamaḥ; bhaktānām hārdatamaḥ bhaktahārdatamaḥ; bhaktahārdatamasaḥ bhedaḥ bhaktahārdatamobhedaḥ; bhānumataḥ bhānavaḥ bhānumadbhānavaḥ; bhānumadbhānūnām santatiḥ bhānumadbhānusantatiḥ; bhaktahārdatamobhedakāriṇī bhānumadbhānusantatiḥ bhaktahārdatamobhedabhānumadbhānusantatiḥ

Significance A single ray does not end the night; a continuous stream of sunlight does. So Her grace, flowing without break, removes the ignorance in the devotee's heart.

405 शिवदूती śiva-dūtī

She for whom Śiva is the messenger

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi; alternatively ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. As a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose messenger is Śiva'; the final takes the feminine -ī. As a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, dūtī 'female messenger' is the head: 'Śiva's messenger'.

Analysis शिवः दूतः यस्याः सा शिवदूती; अथवा शिवस्य दूती शिवदूती
śivaḥ dūtaḥ yasyāḥ sā śivadūtī; athavā śivasya dūtī śivadūtī

Significance In the Devī Māhātmya (ch. 8) the Śakti that emerges from the Goddess sends Śiva Himself as Her envoy to the demons Śumbha and Niśumbha, and so is known as Śivadūtī. Śivadūtī is also the seventh of the Nityā goddesses.

Uncertain The bahuvrīhi ('whose messenger is Śiva', as in the Devī Māhātmya story) and the ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa ('messenger of Śiva') are both current.

406 शिवाराध्या śivārādhyā

She who is worshipped by Śiva

Sandhi शिवाराध्या = शिव + आराध्या (śiva + ārādhyā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa. ārādhyā 'to be worshipped' (gerundive) is the head and Śiva stands to it in the instrumental as the agent.

Analysis शिवेन आराध्या शिवाराध्या
śivena ārādhyā śivārādhyā

Significance Even Śiva worships Her: the power by which He is what He is.

407 शिवमूर्तिः śiva-mūrtiḥ

She whose form is Śiva Himself

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi; alternatively karmadhāraya. As a bahuvrīhi, Śiva and mūrti 'form' are co-referential: 'She whose form is Śiva'. As a karmadhāraya, śivā 'auspicious' qualifies mūrti: 'the auspicious form'. mūrti is feminine, so the name ends in -iḥ.

Analysis शिवः मूर्तिः यस्याः सा शिवमूर्तिः; अथवा शिवा मूर्तिः शिवमूर्तिः
śivaḥ mūrtiḥ yasyāḥ sā śivamūrtiḥ; athavā śivā mūrtiḥ śivamūrtiḥ

Significance Śiva and Śakti are one; Her form is His. Read the other way, Her form is auspiciousness itself.

Uncertain 'whose form is Śiva' (bahuvrīhi) and 'auspicious form' (karmadhāraya) are both possible.

408 शिवङ्करी śivaṅ-karī

She who brings about auspiciousness

Sandhi शिवङ्करी = शिवम् + करी (śivam + karī) — m becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ), and the anusvāra becomes ṅ before k (8.4.58 anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ)

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. karī is an agent form of √kṛ 'to make', compounded with its object śiva 'auspiciousness, welfare': 'she who brings about welfare'. The m before kara is the augment mum, as in bhayaṅkara, kṣemaṅkara (Pāṇini 6.3.67 arurdviṣadajantasya mum); it may also be taken as the accusative ending kept. Either way the surface is śivaṅ-.

Analysis शिवम् करोति इति शिवङ्करी
śivam karoti iti śivaṅkarī

Significance Traditionally also: She makes Her devotees into Śiva, bringing them to identity with Him.

Śloka 89names 409–415

शिवप्रिया शिवपरा शिष्टेष्टा शिष्टपूजिता ।
अप्रमेया स्वप्रकाशा मनोवाचामगोचरा ॥ ८९ ॥

śivapriyā śivaparā śiṣṭeṣṭā śiṣṭapūjitā |
aprameyā svaprakāśā manovācāmagocarā || 89 ||

The names, separated

409शिव-प्रियाśiva-priyā410शिव-पराśiva-parā411शिष्टेष्टाśiṣṭeṣṭā412शिष्ट-पूजिताśiṣṭa-pūjitā

413अ-प्रमेयाa-prameyā414स्व-प्रकाशाsva-prakāśā415मनो-वाचाम्-अगोचराmano-vācām-agocarā

Translation

409She who is beloved of Śiva; 410She who is solely devoted to Śiva; 411She who is dear to the righteous; 412She who is worshipped by the righteous;

413She who is immeasurable, beyond every means of knowledge; 414She who is self-luminous; 415She who is beyond the range of mind and speech.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish

शिवśivaŚiva
प्रियाpriyābeloved, dear
410 शिवपरा śiva-parā
शिवśivaŚiva

411 शिष्टेष्टा śiṣṭeṣṭā
शिष्टśiṣṭathe disciplined, the cultured; those who follow the Veda√śās 'to instruct', past participle
इष्टाiṣṭādear, desired; worshipped√iṣ 'to desire' or √yaj 'to worship', past participle, feminine
412 शिष्टपूजिता śiṣṭa-pūjitā
शिष्टśiṣṭathe disciplined, the cultured√śās, past participle
पूजिताpūjitāworshipped√pūj, past participle, feminine
413 अप्रमेया a-prameyā
अanotthe negative nañ
प्रमेयाprameyāmeasurable, knowable by a pramāṇapra + √mā 'to measure', gerundive, feminine
414 स्वप्रकाशा sva-prakāśā
स्वsvaown, self
प्रकाशाprakāśālight, shining, manifestationprakāśa (pra + √kāś 'to shine'), with the feminine -ā
415 मनोवाचामगोचरा mano-vācām-agocarā
मनस्manasmind
वाचाम्vācāmof words, of speechgenitive plural of vāc

Where the names meet

Name 415 divides mano-vācām + agocarā ('beyond the range of minds and words'), not vācāma + gocarā.

The names

409 शिवप्रिया śiva-priyā

She who is beloved of Śiva

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; alternatively bahuvrīhi. As a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, priyā 'beloved' is the head: 'the beloved of Śiva'. As a bahuvrīhi: 'She to whom Śiva is dear'. Both are true of Her.

Analysis शिवस्य प्रिया शिवप्रिया; अथवा शिवः प्रियः यस्याः सा शिवप्रिया
śivasya priyā śivapriyā; athavā śivaḥ priyaḥ yasyāḥ sā śivapriyā

Significance She is dear to Śiva and Śiva is dear to Her; the love of the divine couple is the model of the devotee's love.

410 शिवपरा śiva-parā

She who is solely devoted to Śiva

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi; alternatively pañcamī-tatpuruṣa. As a bahuvrīhi, para 'highest, devoted to' is predicated of Śiva: 'She for whom Śiva is the highest', i.e. wholly devoted to Him. As a pañcamī-tatpuruṣa: 'She who is beyond Śiva'.

Analysis शिवः परः यस्याः सा शिवपरा; अथवा शिवात् परा शिवपरा
śivaḥ paraḥ yasyāḥ sā śivaparā; athavā śivāt parā śivaparā

Significance She has no aim but Śiva; read the other way, She is beyond even Śiva, as the supreme power.

Uncertain 'devoted to Śiva' (bahuvrīhi) and 'beyond Śiva' (pañcamī-tatpuruṣa) are both current; the meaning follows the first.

411 शिष्टेष्टा śiṣṭeṣṭā

She who is dear to the righteous

Sandhi शिष्टेष्टा = शिष्ट + इष्टा (śiṣṭa + iṣṭā) — guṇa: a + i → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; alternatively tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa. iṣṭā is the head. From √iṣ 'to desire' it means 'dear, desired', and the righteous stand to it in the genitive: 'dear to the righteous'. From √yaj 'to worship' it means 'worshipped', and they stand to it in the instrumental: 'worshipped by the righteous'.

Analysis शिष्टानाम् इष्टा शिष्टेष्टा; अथवा शिष्टैः इष्टा शिष्टेष्टा
śiṣṭānām iṣṭā śiṣṭeṣṭā; athavā śiṣṭaiḥ iṣṭā śiṣṭeṣṭā

Significance She is the chosen deity (iṣṭa-devatā) of the disciplined, who worship Her; traditionally She in turn loves those who live by dharma.

Uncertain iṣṭā may be from √iṣ ('dear to the righteous') or √yaj ('worshipped by the righteous'); a bahuvrīhi 'to whom the righteous are dear' is also given by some.

412 शिष्टपूजिता śiṣṭa-pūjitā

She who is worshipped by the righteous

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa. pūjitā 'worshipped' is the head and the śiṣṭas stand to it in the instrumental as the agents.

Analysis शिष्टैः पूजिता शिष्टपूजिता
śiṣṭaiḥ pūjitā śiṣṭapūjitā

Significance The śiṣṭas, those trained in the Veda and its discipline, are traditionally the standard of right practice; their worship of Her is itself authority for Her worship.

413 अप्रमेया a-prameyā

She who is immeasurable, beyond every means of knowledge

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound nañ-tatpuruṣa. The negative na, reduced to a- (Pāṇini 6.3.73 nalopo nañaḥ), is compounded with the gerundive prameyā 'to be measured, known by a means of knowledge'.

Analysis न प्रमेया अप्रमेया
na prameyā aprameyā

Significance No means of valid knowledge (pramāṇa), perception, inference or any other, can make Her its object, since She is the consciousness by which they all work.

414 स्वप्रकाशा sva-prakāśā

She who is self-luminous

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. sva 'own' qualifies prakāśa 'light', and the whole describes Her: 'She whose light is Her own'. A tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa reading ('shining by Herself', svena prakāśā) gives the same sense.

Analysis स्वः प्रकाशः यस्याः सा स्वप्रकाशा
svaḥ prakāśaḥ yasyāḥ sā svaprakāśā

Significance 'Everything shines after Him as He shines; by His light all this is lit' (tam eva bhāntam anubhāti sarvam, Kaṭha and Muṇḍaka Upaniṣads). She needs no other light to be known.

415 मनोवाचामगोचरा mano-vācām-agocarā

She who is beyond the range of mind and speech

Sandhi मनोवाचाम् = मनस् + वाचाम् (manas + vācām) — final -as before a voiced consonant: s becomes ru (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ), ru becomes u after a (6.1.114 haśi ca), and a + u → o by guṇa (6.1.87): -o

Compound a genitive dvandva governed by a nañ-tatpuruṣa, written as one name. (1) mano-vāc 'minds and words' (itaretara-dvandva), here in the genitive plural, manovācām. (2) a-gocarā 'not within the range' (nañ-tatpuruṣa; gocara 'range of the senses', used adjectivally and made feminine). (3) The genitive depends on agocarā: 'not within the range of minds and words'. The genitive ending is kept, so this is either a compound that retains its case ending (aluk) or two words read together as one name; the m of vācām simply stands before the a of agocarā.

Analysis मनांसि च वाचः च मनोवाचः; न गोचरा अगोचरा; मनोवाचाम् अगोचरा मनोवाचामगोचरा
manāṃsi ca vācaḥ ca manovācaḥ; na gocarā agocarā; manovācām agocarā manovācāmagocarā

Significance The Taittirīya Upaniṣad says of the bliss of Brahman: 'from which words turn back, together with the mind, not having reached it' (yato vāco nivartante aprāpya manasā saha).

Uncertain Whether manovācām agocarā is one compound with the genitive retained or two words read as a single name is not settled; the meaning is the same.

Śloka 90names 416–423

चिच्छक्तिश् चेतनारूपा जडशक्तिर् जडात्मिका ।
गायत्री व्याहृतिः सन्ध्या द्विजवृन्दनिषेविता ॥ ९० ॥

cicchaktiś cetanārūpā jaḍaśaktir jaḍātmikā |
gāyatrī vyāhṛtiḥ sandhyā dvijavṛndaniṣevitā || 90 ||

The names, separated ° form as a name on its own; in the recitation above it joins its neighbour

416चिच्-छक्तिः°cic-chaktiḥ417चेतना-रूपाcetanā-rūpā418जड-शक्तिः°jaḍa-śaktiḥ419जडात्मिकाjaḍātmikā

420गायत्रीgāyatrī421व्याहृतिःvyāhṛtiḥ422सन्ध्याsandhyā423द्विज-वृन्द-निषेविताdvija-vṛnda-niṣevitā

Translation

416She who is the power of consciousness; 417She whose form is awareness (cetanā); 418She who is the power that becomes the insentient world; 419She who is in the form of the inanimate world;

420She who is the Gāyatrī mantra; 421She who is the Vyāhṛti, the sacred utterance; 422She who is in the form of twilight; 423She who is worshipped by hosts of the twice-born.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish

चेतनाcetanāsentience, awareness, consciousness√cit 'to perceive'

जडjaḍainsentient, inert

Where the names meet

चिच्छक्तिश् चेतना = चिच्छक्तिः + चेतना… (cicchaktiḥ + cetanā…) — visarga becomes s before a voiceless stop (Pāṇini 8.3.34 visarjanīyasya saḥ), and that s becomes ś before the palatal c (8.4.40 stoḥ ścunā ścuḥ)

जडशक्तिर्जडात्मिका = जडशक्तिः + जडात्मिका (jaḍaśaktiḥ + jaḍātmikā) — visarga after i becomes r before a voiced sound (the r of ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66)

Names 416–419 pair the sentient and insentient powers; 420–423 recall the twilight worship (Gāyatrī, vyāhṛti, sandhyā, the twice-born). The visarga of vyāhṛtiḥ stands unchanged before s- (optional, Pāṇini 8.3.36 vā śari).

The names

416 चिच्छक्तिः cic-chaktiḥ

She who is the power of consciousness

Sandhi चिच्छक्ति = चित् + शक्ति (cit + śakti) — t becomes c before ś (Pāṇini 8.4.40 stoḥ ścunā ścuḥ), and ś after it becomes ch (8.4.63 śaś cho 'ṭi, optional): cit + śakti → cicchakti

Compound karmadhāraya; alternatively ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. As a karmadhāraya: 'the power that is consciousness'. As a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa: 'the power of consciousness'. śakti is feminine, so the name ends in -iḥ.

Analysis चित् एव शक्तिः चिच्छक्तिः; अथवा चितः शक्तिः चिच्छक्तिः
cit eva śaktiḥ cicchaktiḥ; athavā citaḥ śaktiḥ cicchaktiḥ

Significance Names 416–419 pair Her sentient and insentient powers: consciousness (416–417) and the inert world (418–419); both are one Śakti.

417 चेतनारूपा cetanā-rūpā

She whose form is awareness (cetanā)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. cetanā 'sentience' and rūpa 'form' are co-referential, and the compound describes Her: 'She whose form is sentience'.

Analysis चेतना रूपम् यस्याः सा चेतनारूपा
cetanā rūpam yasyāḥ sā cetanārūpā

Significance The Devī Māhātmya (ch. 5) salutes the Goddess 'who in all beings is called awareness' (yā devī sarvabhūteṣu cetanety abhidhīyate): the sentience by which each being knows.

418 जडशक्तिः jaḍa-śaktiḥ

She who is the power that becomes the insentient world

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya; alternatively ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. As a karmadhāraya: 'the insentient power' (jaḍā takes the stem jaḍa- by puṃvadbhāva). As a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa: 'the power of (that which is) insentient', i.e. the power that becomes matter.

Analysis जडा शक्तिः जडशक्तिः; अथवा जडस्य शक्तिः जडशक्तिः
jaḍā śaktiḥ jaḍaśaktiḥ; athavā jaḍasya śaktiḥ jaḍaśaktiḥ

Significance Traditionally this is māyā, Her power as the material cause, which transforms itself into the inert universe; it complements cicchakti (416).

419 जडात्मिका jaḍātmikā

She who is in the form of the inanimate world

Sandhi जडात्मिका = जड + आत्मिका (jaḍa + ātmikā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi. jaḍa 'insentient' and ātman 'self, nature' are co-referential, and the whole describes Her: 'She whose nature is the insentient'. The bahuvrīhi takes the suffix kap (ātman → ātmaka), and the feminine is -ikā (Pāṇini 7.3.44).

Analysis जडः आत्मा यस्याः सा जडात्मिका
jaḍaḥ ātmā yasyāḥ sā jaḍātmikā

Significance The inert world too is Her, as the sentient beings are; nothing is outside Her.

420 गायत्री gāyatrī

She who is the Gāyatrī mantra

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance The Gāyatrī (tat savitur vareṇyam, Ṛgveda 3.62.10) is the mother of the Vedas; the traditional derivation explains the name as that which protects the one who sings it (gāyantaṃ trāyate). Names 420–423 recall the twilight worship (sandhyā-vandana) of the twice-born.

421 व्याहृतिः vyāhṛtiḥ

She who is the Vyāhṛti, the sacred utterance

Sandhi व्याहृति = वि + आहृति (vi + āhṛti) — yaṇ: i becomes y before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci), at the junction of the prefix vi with āhṛti

Compound not a compound

Significance The vyāhṛtis bhūḥ, bhuvaḥ, svaḥ are uttered before the Gāyatrī; they name the three worlds. Traditionally She is also all utterance, the power of speech.

422 सन्ध्या sandhyā

She who is in the form of twilight

Sandhi सन्ध्या = सम् + ध्या (sam + dhyā) — m becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ), which takes the place of articulation of the following stop (8.4.58–59 anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ): written n before a dental

Compound not a compound

Significance Sandhyā is the junction of night and day and the worship performed at those junctions; She is both the hour and the rite.

Uncertain The word is derived from sam + √dhyai ('meditation') or from sandhi 'junction' (sam + √dhā); both are traditional.

423 द्विजवृन्दनिषेविता dvija-vṛnda-niṣevitā

She who is worshipped by hosts of the twice-born

Sandhi निषेविता = नि + सेविता (ni + sevitā) — ṣatva: the s of √sev becomes ṣ after the prefix ni

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and an upapada-tatpuruṣa). (1) dvi-ja 'twice-born' (upapada-tatpuruṣa; ja from √jan 'to be born'). (2) dvija-vṛnda 'the host of the twice-born' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) The participle niṣevitā 'served, worshipped' is the head and the host stands to it in the instrumental.

Analysis द्विः जातः द्विजः; द्विजानाम् वृन्दम् द्विजवृन्दम्; द्विजवृन्देन निषेविता द्विजवृन्दनिषेविता
dviḥ jātaḥ dvijaḥ; dvijānām vṛndam dvijavṛndam; dvijavṛndena niṣevitā dvijavṛndaniṣevitā

Significance The twice-born worship Her daily through the Gāyatrī at the twilights; the second birth is initiation into the Veda.

निःसीममहिमा नित्ययौवना मदशालिनी ॥ ९१ ॥

tattvāsanā tat tvam ayī pañcakośāntarasthitā |

Where the names meet

तत्त्वमयी = तत् + त्वम् + अयी (tat + tvam + ayī) — no sound change: three names written together (tvam keeps its m before the vowel of ayī). This is Bhāskararāya's division; read as one word, tattvamayī is name 907

Names 425–427 (tat · tvam · ayī) divide the letters tattvamayī into three names and recall the teaching tat tvam asi, 'That thou art'; the single word tattvamayī comes later as name 907. Names 431–433 (into śloka 92) describe Her mada, the rapture of Her bliss.

The names

424 तत्त्वासना tattvāsanā

She whose seat is the tattvas, the principles of reality

Sandhi तत्त्वासना = तत्त्व + आसना (tattva + āsanā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi. The members are tattva 'principle of reality' and āsana 'seat'; the whole is a bahuvrīhi describing Her: 'She whose seat is the tattvas'. The neuter āsana takes the feminine -ā because the compound qualifies the Goddess.

Analysis तत्त्वानि आसनम् यस्याः सा तत्त्वासना
tattvāni āsanam yasyāḥ sā tattvāsanā

Significance In Śrīvidyā the tattvas, from earth up to Śiva, are the throne on which She is enthroned and worshipped; She rests on all of manifest reality and is not contained by it.

Uncertain A second analysis takes āsana as an agent noun from √ās 'to sit': tattveṣu āste 'She who abides in the tattvas'. The bahuvrīhi ('whose seat is the tattvas') is the more natural reading of the compound.

425 तत् tat

She who is 'That', the supreme reality (brahman)

Sandhi तत्त्वमयी = तत् + त्वम् + अयी (tat + tvam + ayī) — No sound changes here. tat and tvam are simply juxtaposed (t + tv), and the final m of tvam stays m before the vowel of ayī (it becomes anusvāra only before a consonant, Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ). The same letters read as one word give tattvamayī 'consisting of the tattvas', which is name 907; here Bhāskararāya divides them into three names, tat (425), tvam (426) and ayī (427), as the 1,000-name count requires.

Compound not a compound

Significance In the Upaniṣadic teaching tat tvam asi, 'That thou art' (Chāndogya Upaniṣad 6.8.7), tat denotes brahman; the Bhagavad Gītā (17.23) names brahman as oṃ tat sat. With 426 and 427 this name sets the teaching of identity within the hymn.

426 त्वम् tvam

She who is 'Thou', the self addressed in the teaching 'That thou art'

Sandhi त्वमयी = त्वम् + अयी (tvam + ayī) — No sound change: the final m of tvam stays m before a vowel (it would become anusvāra only before a consonant, Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ), so tvam and ayī are written together as tvamayī. On the division of tattvamayī into tat, tvam and ayī see name 425.

Compound not a compound

Significance In tat tvam asi the word tvam denotes the individual self (jīva); its identity with tat (425) is the teaching of Advaita. Name 908, tattvamarthasvarūpiṇī, takes up the same pair: She is the meaning of tat and tvam.

Corrected त्वं → त्वम्. त्वं → त्वम्: a word standing alone ends in m, not anusvāra. (425 tat, 426 tvam, 427 ayī is Bhāskararāya's division of tattvamayī and is kept.)

427 अयी ayī

She who is called upon with the loving cry 'ayī', 'O Mother!'

Sandhi त्वमयी = त्वम् + अयी (tvam + ayī) — No sound change: the m of tvam stays m before the vowel a of ayī (Pāṇini 8.3.23 makes m anusvāra only before a consonant). Bhāskararāya's division of tattvamayī into tat, tvam and ayī: see name 425.

Compound not a compound

Significance Traditionally ayī is the call of a devotee to the Mother, completing the triad tat, tvam, ayī; some read the three names together as echoing tat tvam asi, 'That thou art'.

Uncertain The sense of ayī is not settled. The common interjection of address is ayi with a short i; the long ī here is read either as that particle lengthened or as a feminine form, and the commentarial derivation could not be confirmed here. The rendering follows the usual reading as a call of address.

428 पञ्चकोशान्तरस्थिता pañca-kośāntara-sthitā

She who abides within the five sheaths

Sandhi कोशान्तर = कोश + अन्तर (kośa + antara) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound saptamī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and a dvigu). (1) pañca-kośa 'the five sheaths': a numeral compound, which counts as a dvigu because another member follows (Pāṇini 2.1.51 taddhitārthottarapadasamāhāre ca). (2) …kośa-antara 'the interior of the five sheaths' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; antara is a noun, 'inside'). (3) The participle sthitā 'abiding' is the head of the whole and takes that interior in the locative. The n of pañcan drops at the end of a compound member; that is morphology, not sandhi.

Analysis पञ्च कोशाः पञ्चकोशाः; पञ्चकोशानाम् अन्तरम् पञ्चकोशान्तरम्; पञ्चकोशान्तरे स्थिता पञ्चकोशान्तरस्थिता
pañca kośāḥ pañcakośāḥ; pañcakośānām antaram pañcakośāntaram; pañcakośāntare sthitā pañcakośāntarasthitā

Significance The five sheaths of the Taittirīya Upaniṣad — of food, breath, mind, understanding and bliss — enclose the Self; She is that innermost Self, hidden within all five.

429 निःसीममहिमा niḥsīma-mahimā

She whose glory is limitless

Sandhi निःसीम = निस् + सीम (nis + sīma) — the s of nis becomes visarga before the sibilant (s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66; ru → visarga before a voiceless sound, 8.3.15), and the visarga is kept instead of becoming s (optional, 8.3.36 vā śari): niḥsīma, also written nissīma

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya and a prādi-compound). (1) niḥ-sīma 'gone beyond limit, boundless': the prefix nis with the sense of nirgata 'gone out of' compounds with sīman 'boundary' (a prādi-compound; sīman loses its final n). (2) niḥsīma qualifies mahiman 'greatness'. (3) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose greatness is boundless'. The an-stem mahiman keeps its form, and its nominative mahimā serves as the feminine.

Analysis निर्गतः सीम्नः निःसीमः; निःसीमः महिमा यस्याः सा निःसीममहिमा
nirgataḥ sīmnaḥ niḥsīmaḥ; niḥsīmaḥ mahimā yasyāḥ sā niḥsīmamahimā

Significance Her greatness has no boundary in space, time or form; the Upaniṣads speak of brahman as resting in its own greatness.

430 नित्ययौवना nitya-yauvanā

She who is ever youthful

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. nitya 'everlasting' qualifies yauvana 'youth'; the whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose youth is everlasting'. The neuter yauvana takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis नित्यम् यौवनम् यस्याः सा नित्ययौवना
nityam yauvanam yasyāḥ sā nityayauvanā

Significance Untouched by time, She never ages; compare 470, vayo'vasthāvivarjitā, free from the stages of age.

431 मदशालिनी mada-śālinī

She who is resplendent with rapture (mada)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa. śālinī 'resplendent, abounding' is the head; mada 'exhilaration, rapture' stands to it in the instrumental: 'resplendent with rapture'.

Analysis मदेन शालिनी मदशालिनी
madena śālinī madaśālinī

Significance Names 431–433 describe the mada of the Goddess. Traditionally this is the overflowing joy of Her own bliss (ānanda), not ordinary intoxication; in Kaula ritual it is linked with the offering of wine, understood inwardly.

चन्दनद्रवदिग्धाङ्गी चाम्पेयकुसुमप्रिया ॥ ९२ ॥

Where the names meet

Name 433 ends in the ū-stem bhū, so it ends -bhūḥ, as name 23 does.

The names

432 मदघूर्णितरक्ताक्षी mada-ghūrṇita-raktākṣī

She whose eyes are red and rolling with rapture

Sandhi रक्ताक्षी = रक्त + अक्षी (rakta + akṣī) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa and a karmadhāraya). (1) mada-ghūrṇita 'rolling with rapture' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (2) It and rakta 'red' qualify akṣi 'eye'. (3) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose eyes are red and rolling with rapture'. At the end of a bahuvrīhi akṣi takes the suffix ṣac (Pāṇini 5.4.113 bahuvrīhau sakthyakṣṇoḥ svāṅgāt ṣac), giving akṣa, and its feminine is akṣī.

Analysis मदेन घूर्णिते मदघूर्णिते; मदघूर्णिते रक्ते अक्षिणी यस्याः सा मदघूर्णितरक्ताक्षी
madena ghūrṇite madaghūrṇite; madaghūrṇite rakte akṣiṇī yasyāḥ sā madaghūrṇitaraktākṣī

Significance The reddened, rolling eyes are the classical marks of mada; traditionally they show Her absorption in Her own bliss, turned inward.

433 मदपाटलगण्डभूः mada-pāṭala-gaṇḍa-bhūḥ

She whose cheeks are rosy with rapture

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa and a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) mada-pāṭala 'rosy with rapture' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (2) gaṇḍa-bhū 'the expanse of the cheeks' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) (1) qualifies (2), and the whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose cheeks are rosy with rapture'. The feminine pāṭalā takes the masculine stem in the bahuvrīhi (puṃvadbhāva); bhū is not shortened, so the name ends -bhūḥ, as in name 23.

Analysis मदेन पाटला मदपाटला; गण्डयोः भूः गण्डभूः; मदपाटला गण्डभूः यस्याः सा मदपाटलगण्डभूः
madena pāṭalā madapāṭalā; gaṇḍayoḥ bhūḥ gaṇḍabhūḥ; madapāṭalā gaṇḍabhūḥ yasyāḥ sā madapāṭalagaṇḍabhūḥ

Significance The flush of the cheeks completes the picture of 431–432: the outward signs of Her inner bliss.

434 चन्दनद्रवदिग्धाङ्गी candana-drava-digdhāṅgī

She whose limbs are anointed with sandalwood paste

Sandhi दिग्धाङ्गी = दिग्ध + अङ्गी (digdha + aṅgī) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa and a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) candana-drava 'liquid sandalwood, sandal paste' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) …drava-digdha 'anointed with it' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa with the past participle). (3) It qualifies aṅga 'limb', and the whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose limbs are anointed with sandal paste'. A body-part word at the end of a bahuvrīhi may take the feminine -ī (Pāṇini 4.1.54, extended to aṅga by a vārttika): -aṅgī.

Analysis चन्दनस्य द्रवः चन्दनद्रवः; चन्दनद्रवेण दिग्धानि चन्दनद्रवदिग्धानि; चन्दनद्रवदिग्धानि अङ्गानि यस्याः सा चन्दनद्रवदिग्धाङ्गी
candanasya dravaḥ candanadravaḥ; candanadraveṇa digdhāni candanadravadigdhāni; candanadravadigdhāni aṅgāni yasyāḥ sā candanadravadigdhāṅgī

Significance Sandal paste is a cooling unguent and one of the offerings (upacāra) of Her worship; it also links with 458, Her dwelling on the Malaya mountain, home of the sandalwood tree.

435 चाम्पेयकुसुमप्रिया cāmpeya-kusuma-priyā

She who loves campaka flowers

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) cāmpeya-kusuma 'campaka flowers' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) The whole is a bahuvrīhi with priya 'dear' as the final member: 'She to whom campaka flowers are dear'.

Analysis चाम्पेयस्य कुसुमानि चाम्पेयकुसुमानि; चाम्पेयकुसुमानि प्रियाणि यस्याः सा चाम्पेयकुसुमप्रिया
cāmpeyasya kusumāni cāmpeyakusumāni; cāmpeyakusumāni priyāṇi yasyāḥ sā cāmpeyakusumapriyā

Significance The fragrant golden campaka is among the flowers offered to Her; name 13 already crowns Her hair with campaka.

Where the names meet

Names 436–441 alliterate on ku-/ko-/kau-. kurukullā (438) is the name of a goddess, not a compound; 439–441 concern kula and the Kaula path.

The names

436 कुशला kuśalā

She who is skillful

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Traditionally She is expert in every act — the creation, maintenance and withdrawal of the worlds — and in guiding devotees to their good (kuśala, welfare).

437 कोमलाकारा komalākārā

She whose form is tender and graceful

Sandhi कोमलाकारा = कोमल + आकारा (komala + ākārā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi. komala 'tender, soft' qualifies ākāra 'form, figure'; the whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose form is tender'.

Analysis कोमलः आकारः यस्याः सा कोमलाकारा
komalaḥ ākāraḥ yasyāḥ sā komalākārā

Significance The terrible and the gentle are both Her forms; here She is gentle, delicate and lovely.

438 कुरुकुल्ला kurukullā

She who is the goddess Kurukullā

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Kurukullā, a red goddess of enchantment who, like Lalitā, bears a bow and arrows of flowers, is worshipped in the Tantras (Buddhist as well as Hindu). In Śrīvidyā she belongs to the Goddess's own circle and is traditionally given a place within Her city.

Uncertain The derivation of the name is obscure, and the place Kurukullā holds in Śrīnagara is described differently in the sources; the old note that she resides in the kuruvinda ruby could not be confirmed.

439 कुलेश्वरी kuleśvarī

She who is the sovereign of kula (the triad of knower, knowing and known)

Sandhi कुलेश्वरी = कुल + ईश्वरी (kula + īśvarī) — guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. īśvarī 'sovereign' is the head; kula stands to it in the genitive: 'the sovereign of kula'.

Analysis कुलस्य ईश्वरी कुलेश्वरी
kulasya īśvarī kuleśvarī

Significance In Śrīvidyā kula is read as the triad of knower (mātṛ), knowing (māna) and known (meya), and also as the Kaula path and the kuṇḍalinī's course; She rules over all of these. Compare names 90–95 (kulāmṛtaikarasikā … kulayoginī).

440 कुलकुण्डालया kula-kuṇḍālayā

She who dwells in the kulakuṇḍa, the hollow at the center of the mūlādhāra

Sandhi कुण्डालया = कुण्ड + आलया (kuṇḍa + ālayā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) kula-kuṇḍa 'the hollow of kula' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa): here kula is the mūlādhāra, and the kuṇḍa the small cavity at its center. (2) The whole is a bahuvrīhi with ālaya 'dwelling' as the final member: 'She whose dwelling is the kulakuṇḍa'.

Analysis कुलस्य कुण्डम् कुलकुण्डम्; कुलकुण्डम् आलयः यस्याः सा कुलकुण्डालया
kulasya kuṇḍam kulakuṇḍam; kulakuṇḍam ālayaḥ yasyāḥ sā kulakuṇḍālayā

Significance As kuṇḍalinī (name 110) She lies coiled in the kulakuṇḍa at the base of the spine, the starting point of Her ascent through the cakras.

441 कौलमार्गतत्परसेविता kaula-mārga-tatpara-sevitā

She who is worshipped by those devoted to the Kaula path

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner saptamī-tatpuruṣa and a karmadhāraya). (1) kaula-mārga 'the Kaula path' (karmadhāraya). (2) …mārga-tatpara 'those devoted to that path' (saptamī-tatpuruṣa). (3) The participle sevitā 'worshipped' is the head of the whole and takes the devotees in the instrumental: 'worshipped by those devoted to the Kaula path'.

Analysis कौलः मार्गः कौलमार्गः; कौलमार्गे तत्पराः कौलमार्गतत्पराः; कौलमार्गतत्परैः सेविता कौलमार्गतत्परसेविता
kaulaḥ mārgaḥ kaulamārgaḥ; kaulamārge tatparāḥ kaulamārgatatparāḥ; kaulamārgatatparaiḥ sevitā kaulamārgatatparasevitā

Significance In Śrīvidyā the Kaula path centers on kula — the kuṇḍalinī and the union of Śakti with Śiva — and is understood above all as inner worship. Name 98 names Her as devoted to samayācāra; both paths are Hers.

Śloka 94names 442–451

कुमारगणनाथाम्बा तुष्टिः पुष्टिर् मतिर् धृतिः ।
शान्तिः स्वस्तिमती कान्तिर् नन्दिनी विघ्ननाशिनी ॥ ९४ ॥

kumāragaṇanāthāmbā tuṣṭiḥ puṣṭir matir dhṛtiḥ |
śāntiḥ svastimatī kāntir nandinī vighnanāśinī || 94 ||

The names, separated ° form as a name on its own; in the recitation above it joins its neighbour

442कुमार-गणनाथाम्बाkumāra-gaṇanāthāmbā443तुष्टिःtuṣṭiḥ444पुष्टिः°puṣṭiḥ445मतिः°matiḥ446धृतिःdhṛtiḥ

442She who is the mother of Kumāra (Skanda) and Gaṇanātha (Gaṇeśa); 443She who is contentment itself; 444She who is the power of nourishment; 445She who manifests as intelligence; 446She who is fortitude;

447She who is tranquility itself; 448She who is endowed with well-being (svasti); 449She who is effulgence; 450She who gives delight; 451She who destroys obstacles.

Where the names meet

पुष्टिर्मतिर्धृतिः = पुष्टिः + मतिः + धृतिः (puṣṭiḥ + matiḥ + dhṛtiḥ) — visarga after i becomes r before a voiced sound (final s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66; ru is kept as r, since the change to u applies only after a)

कान्तिर्नन्दिनी = कान्तिः + नन्दिनी (kāntiḥ + nandinī) — visarga after i becomes r before a voiced sound (final s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66; ru is kept as r, since the change to u applies only after a)

Name 442 is one name: Kumāra and Gaṇanātha form a dvandva, and She is the mother of both. Names 443–449 are abstract nouns — She is contentment, nourishment, understanding, fortitude, peace, well-being and radiance themselves.

The names

442 कुमारगणनाथाम्बा kumāra-gaṇanāthāmbā

She who is the mother of Kumāra (Skanda) and Gaṇanātha (Gaṇeśa)

Sandhi गणनाथाम्बा = गणनाथ + अम्बा (gaṇanātha + ambā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner itaretara-dvandva and a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) gaṇa-nātha 'lord of the gaṇas', i.e. Gaṇeśa (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) kumāra-gaṇanātha 'Kumāra and Gaṇanātha' (itaretara-dvandva). (3) ambā 'mother' is the head, and the pair stands to it in the genitive: 'the mother of both'.

Analysis गणानाम् नाथः गणनाथः; कुमारः च गणनाथः च कुमारगणनाथौ; कुमारगणनाथयोः अम्बा कुमारगणनाथाम्बा
gaṇānām nāthaḥ gaṇanāthaḥ; kumāraḥ ca gaṇanāthaḥ ca kumāragaṇanāthau; kumāragaṇanāthayoḥ ambā kumāragaṇanāthāmbā

Significance Skanda and Gaṇeśa are the sons of Śiva and the Goddess; Kumāra leads the army of the gods and Gaṇeśa removes obstacles. Compare name 77, where Gaṇeśa is born from Kāmeśvara's glance at Her face.

443 तुष्टिः tuṣṭiḥ

She who is contentment itself

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Names 443–449 name Her as qualities of mind. As the Devīmāhātmya sings, the Goddess dwells in all beings in the form of contentment (tuṣṭirūpeṇa saṃsthitā).

444 पुष्टिः puṣṭiḥ

She who is the power of nourishment

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance She nourishes all beings, body and spirit; traditionally the growth of every living thing is Her work.

445 मतिः matiḥ

She who manifests as intelligence

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance She is the understanding by which beings know and discern.

446 धृतिः dhṛtiḥ

She who is fortitude

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance She is the steadiness that holds the mind to its purpose.

447 शान्तिः śāntiḥ

She who is tranquility itself

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance She is peace; the Devīmāhātmya praises the Goddess who abides in all beings as peace (śāntirūpeṇa). Compare 131, śāntimatī.

448 स्वस्तिमती svasti-matī

She who is endowed with well-being (svasti)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Traditionally svasti — 'it is well' — is also read as imperishable, true being, which is why the name was once rendered 'the ultimate truth'.

Uncertain The reading of svasti as 'imperishable being' is traditional; the exact source in the commentaries could not be confirmed here.

449 कान्तिः kāntiḥ

She who is effulgence

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Her radiance is the light by which all things shine; the Devīmāhātmya praises the Goddess as abiding in all beings as loveliness (kāntirūpeṇa). Compare 465, kāntimatī.

450 नन्दिनी nandinī

She who gives delight

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance She gladdens Her devotees; traditionally the name also recalls Nandinī, the wish-fulfilling cow.

451 विघ्ननाशिनी vighna-nāśinī

She who destroys obstacles

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. nāśinī 'destroying' is an agent noun from the causative of √naś with the suffix -in (ṇini, of habitual action, Pāṇini 3.2.78 supy ajātau ṇinis tācchīlye); it governs vighna 'obstacle' as its object.

Analysis विघ्नान् नाशयति इति विघ्ननाशिनी
vighnān nāśayati iti vighnanāśinī

Significance She removes every obstacle on the path, outer and inner; the same power appears in Her son Gaṇeśa (442).

Śloka 95names 452–458

तेजोवती त्रिनयना लोलाक्षीकामरूपिणी ।
मालिनी हंसिनी माता मलयाचलवासिनी ॥ ९५ ॥

tejovatī trinayanā lolākṣīkāmarūpiṇī |
mālinī haṃsinī mātā malayācalavāsinī || 95 ||

The names, separated

452She who is effulgent; 453She who has three eyes; 454She who takes the form of love (kāma) in women, the restless-eyed;

455She who wears garlands; 456She who is one with the haṃsas, the yogins of the highest attainment; 457She who is the Mother; 458She who dwells on the Malaya mountain.

Word by word
