Where the names meet

Name 454 lolākṣīkāmarūpiṇī is one name in the 1,000-name count; do not cut off kāmarūpiṇī, which is name 796.

The names

452 तेजोवती tejovatī

She who is effulgent

Sandhi तेजोवती = तेजस् + वती (tejas + vatī) — the s of tejas, treated as a word-end before the suffix, becomes ru (Pāṇini 8.2.66), which after a and before a voiced consonant becomes u (6.1.114 haśi ca); a + u then gives o (6.1.87), as in tejomaya

Compound not a compound

Significance She is full of tejas, the radiant power that shines in sun, moon and fire and is the light of consciousness itself.

Uncertain The usual Pāṇinian derivation keeps the s of tejas before a possessive suffix (Pāṇini 1.4.19 tasau matvarthe), giving tejasvatī; tejovatī, with the s treated as a word-end, is the attested form of the name.

453 त्रिनयना tri-nayanā

She who has three eyes

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. The numeral tri 'three' qualifies nayana 'eye'; the whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She who has three eyes'.

Analysis त्रीणि नयनानि यस्याः सा त्रिनयना
trīṇi nayanāni yasyāḥ sā trinayanā

Significance Traditionally Her three eyes are the sun, the moon and fire, which light the three worlds; compare 477, trilocanā.

454 लोलाक्षीकामरूपिणी lolākṣī-kāma-rūpiṇī

She who takes the form of love (kāma) in women, the restless-eyed

Sandhi लोलाक्षी = लोल + अक्षी (lola + akṣī) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner bahuvrīhi), with the possessive suffix -in. (1) lola-akṣī 'one with restless eyes', a woman (bahuvrīhi; akṣi with the suffix ṣac, Pāṇini 5.4.113, and the feminine -ī). (2) lolākṣī-kāma 'the desire of women' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; the first member keeps its feminine form). (3) To lolākṣīkāma + rūpa 'form' is added the possessive suffix -in (Pāṇini 5.2.115 ata iniṭhanau): 'having the desire of women as Her form'. This is one name; the separate name kāmarūpiṇī is 796.

Analysis लोले अक्षिणी यस्याः सा लोलाक्षी; लोलाक्षीणाम् कामः लोलाक्षीकामः; लोलाक्षीकामः रूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति लोलाक्षीकामरूपिणी
lole akṣiṇī yasyāḥ sā lolākṣī; lolākṣīṇām kāmaḥ lolākṣīkāmaḥ; lolākṣīkāmaḥ rūpam asyāḥ asti iti lolākṣīkāmarūpiṇī

Significance Traditionally She is present as the love and longing in all women; even this desire, through which life continues, is Her form.

Uncertain lolākṣī can also be taken as an epithet of the Goddess herself ('the restless-eyed one, whose form is Kāma'); the rendering follows the reading of lolākṣī as 'women'.

Corrected लोलाक्षी → लोलाक्षीकामरूपिणी. The name was cut to लोलाक्षी with "separate name कामरूपिणी" in its meaning. In the 1,000-name count (Bhāskararāya) 454 is the single name lolākṣīkāmarūpiṇī; there is no separate kāmarūpiṇī here (that is name 796). The verse reads लोलाक्षीकामरूपिणी.

455 मालिनी mālinī

She who wears garlands

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Traditionally also the garland of the letters of the alphabet: in Trika Śaivism Mālinī is the name of the fifty letters arranged in their mixed order.

456 हंसिनी haṃsinī

She who is one with the haṃsas, the yogins of the highest attainment

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Haṃsa, the swan that is said to separate milk from water, is the image of the discerning ascetic (paramahaṃsa) and of the self; traditionally it is also the haṃsa mantra repeated unspoken in every breath. Compare 372, bhaktamānasahaṃsikā.

Uncertain The possessive suffix allows several senses — 'having the haṃsas (great yogins) as Her own', 'having the haṃsa (swan or breath-mantra)' — and the tradition gives more than one.

457 माता mātā

She who is the Mother

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance She is the Mother of the universe (compare name 1, śrīmātā). Mātṛ can also mean 'the one who measures, the knower', the first member of the kula triad named in 439.

458 मलयाचलवासिनी malayācala-vāsinī

She who dwells on the Malaya mountain

Sandhi मलयाचल = मलय + अचल (malaya + acala) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) malaya-acala 'the mountain Malaya' (karmadhāraya of name and kind). (2) vāsinī 'dwelling' is an agent noun from √vas with the suffix -in (Pāṇini 3.2.78), and takes the mountain in the locative: 'She who dwells on the Malaya mountain'.

Analysis मलयः अचलः मलयाचलः; मलयाचले वसति इति मलयाचलवासिनी
malayaḥ acalaḥ malayācalaḥ; malayācale vasati iti malayācalavāsinī

Significance The Malaya range is the home of the sandalwood tree (compare 434) and of the cool southern breeze; traditionally it is one of Her abodes on earth.

कालकण्ठी कान्तिमती क्षोभिणी सूक्ष्मरूपिणी ॥ ९६ ॥

sumukhī nalinī subhrūḥ śobhanā suranāyikā |

464 कालकण्ठी kāla-kaṇṭhī
कालkāladark, black
कण्ठीkaṇṭhīthroatkaṇṭha with the feminine -ī
465 कान्तिमती kānti-matī
कान्तिkāntiradiance, loveliness
मतीmatīpossessingthe possessive suffix -mat (matup), feminine -ī
466 क्षोभिणी kṣobhiṇī
क्षोभिणीkṣobhiṇīshe who stirs, agitatescausative of √kṣubh 'to be agitated' + -in, feminine -ī; n becomes ṇ after ṣ (Pāṇini 8.4.2)
467 सूक्ष्मरूपिणी sūkṣma-rūpiṇī
सूक्ष्मsūkṣmasubtle, fine
रूपिणीrūpiṇīhaving the form ofrūpa + the possessive suffix -in, feminine -ī

Where the names meet

Names 459–462 praise Her beauty; 464 (kālakaṇṭhī) and 469 (vāmadevī, śloka 97) name Her as Śiva's consort under two of his names.

The names

459 सुमुखी su-mukhī

She who has a beautiful face

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi). The prefix su 'well, beautiful' qualifies mukha 'face'; the whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose face is beautiful'. A body-part word at the end of a bahuvrīhi takes the feminine -ī (Pāṇini 4.1.54 svāṅgāc copasarjanād asaṃyogopadhāt): sumukhī.

Analysis शोभनम् मुखम् यस्याः सा सुमुखी
śobhanam mukham yasyāḥ sā sumukhī

Significance Her face is gracious and benign toward Her devotees; the name also suggests Her favor (sumukha, 'well-disposed').

460 नलिनी nalinī

She who is lotus-like, tender and lovely as the lotus

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Traditionally Her hands, feet, eyes and face are all lotus-like, soft and beautiful; the lotus is also the image of purity rising untouched from the water.

Uncertain nalinī also means a lotus pond, and is the name of one of the streams of the Gaṅgā; which sense is primary is a matter of interpretation.

461 सुभ्रूः su-bhrūḥ

She who has beautiful eyebrows

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (prādi). su 'beautiful' qualifies bhrū 'eyebrow'; the whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose eyebrows are beautiful'. bhrū is a feminine ū-stem and keeps its form, so the nominative is subhrūḥ.

Analysis शोभने भ्रुवौ यस्याः सा सुभ्रूः
śobhane bhruvau yasyāḥ sā subhrūḥ

Significance Her brows are praised by the poets: Saundaryalaharī 47 likens them to the bow of Kāma.

462 शोभना śobhanā

She who is radiant and beautiful

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Her beauty is also auspiciousness: śobhana means both 'lovely' and 'auspicious'.

463 सुरनायिका sura-nāyikā

She who is the leader of the gods

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. nāyikā 'leader' is the head; sura 'god' stands to it in the genitive: 'leader of the gods'.

Analysis सुराणाम् नायिका सुरनायिका
surāṇām nāyikā suranāyikā

Significance It was the gods who invoked Her from the fire (name 4), and She leads them against Bhaṇḍa.

464 कालकण्ठी kāla-kaṇṭhī

She who is the consort of Kālakaṇṭha (Śiva, the dark-throated)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (kālakaṇṭha, a name of Śiva), with the feminine of relationship. (1) kāla-kaṇṭha 'he whose throat is dark' (bahuvrīhi), Śiva, whose throat was darkened by the poison he swallowed. (2) The feminine -ī names the wife of the one so called (Pāṇini 4.1.48 puṃyogād ākhyāyām): 'the consort of Kālakaṇṭha'.

Analysis कालः कण्ठः यस्य सः कालकण्ठः; कालकण्ठस्य पत्नी कालकण्ठी
kālaḥ kaṇṭhaḥ yasya saḥ kālakaṇṭhaḥ; kālakaṇṭhasya patnī kālakaṇṭhī

Significance Śiva held the cosmic poison in his throat, which turned dark; Saundaryalaharī 28 attributes his survival to the power of Her earrings (compare name 22).

Uncertain The name can also be read directly as a bahuvrīhi of Her own ('She whose throat is dark'), or with kālakaṇṭha in the sense 'whose throat is sweet-voiced'; the reading as Śiva's consort is the usual one.

465 कान्तिमती kānti-matī

She who is radiant

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Possessed of kānti, the loveliness that is Her very self (449).

466 क्षोभिणी kṣobhiṇī

She who stirs the stillness into creation

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Traditionally kṣobha is the first stirring by which the quiescent becomes creative: She agitates the balance of the guṇas, and so the worlds begin. In the Śrīcakra worship the first of the ten mudrā-śaktis is Sarvasaṃkṣobhiṇī.

Uncertain What She stirs is not named; the creative agitation of prakṛti is the usual reading, and agitation of the mind of Śiva or of devotees is also given.

467 सूक्ष्मरूपिणी sūkṣma-rūpiṇī

She whose form is subtle, beyond the reach of the senses

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya, with the possessive suffix -in. (1) sūkṣma-rūpa 'subtle form' (karmadhāraya). (2) The possessive suffix -in (Pāṇini 5.2.115) makes 'having a subtle form'.

Analysis सूक्ष्मम् रूपम् सूक्ष्मरूपम्; सूक्ष्मरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति सूक्ष्मरूपिणी
sūkṣmam rūpam sūkṣmarūpam; sūkṣmarūpam asyāḥ asti iti sūkṣmarūpiṇī

Significance In Śrīvidyā Her forms are counted as gross (the embodied image), subtle (the mantra) and supreme; this name points to the subtle.

Śloka 97names 468–474

वज्रेश्वरी वामदेवी वयोऽवस्थाविवर्जिता ।
सिद्धेश्वरी सिद्धविद्या सिद्धमाता यशस्विनी ॥ ९७ ॥

vajreśvarī vāmadevī vayo'vasthāvivarjitā |
siddheśvarī siddhavidyā siddhamātā yaśasvinī || 97 ||

The names, separated

468वज्रेश्वरीvajreśvarī469वाम-देवीvāma-devī470वयोऽवस्था-विवर्जिताvayo'vasthā-vivarjitā

471सिद्धेश्वरीsiddheśvarī472सिद्ध-विद्याsiddha-vidyā473सिद्ध-माताsiddha-mātā474यशस्विनीyaśasvinī

Translation

468She who is Vajreśvarī, the sixth of the Nityā goddesses; 469She who is the consort of Vāmadeva (Śiva); 470She who is free from the changes of age;

471She who is the sovereign of the siddhas, the perfected adepts; 472She who is the Siddhavidyā, the accomplished mantra (the fifteen-syllable mantra); 473She who is the mother of the siddhas; 474She who is renowned, possessed of glory.

SanskritEnglish

Where the names meet

Name 470: the avagraha in vayo'vasthā marks the a of avasthā absorbed after o (vayas + avasthā). Names 471–473 form a group on siddha.

The names

468 वज्रेश्वरी vajreśvarī

She who is Vajreśvarī, the sixth of the Nityā goddesses

Sandhi वज्रेश्वरी = वज्र + ईश्वरी (vajra + īśvarī) — guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. īśvarī 'sovereign' is the head; vajra 'thunderbolt, diamond' stands to it in the genitive: 'sovereign of the vajra'.

Analysis वज्रस्य ईश्वरी वज्रेश्वरी
vajrasya īśvarī vajreśvarī

Significance (Mahā)vajreśvarī is the sixth of the fifteen Nityās who preside over the lunar days, and one of the three goddesses at the corners of the central triangle of the Śrīcakra, with Kāmeśvarī and Bhagamālinī.

469 वामदेवी vāma-devī

She who is the consort of Vāmadeva (Śiva)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya (vāmadeva, a name of Śiva), with the feminine of relationship. (1) vāma-deva 'the lovely god' (karmadhāraya), a name of Śiva. (2) The feminine -ī names his consort (Pāṇini 4.1.48 puṃyogād ākhyāyām). Read instead as vāmā devī 'the lovely goddess' (karmadhāraya with puṃvadbhāva) the sense is close.

Analysis वामः देवः वामदेवः; वामदेवस्य पत्नी वामदेवी
vāmaḥ devaḥ vāmadevaḥ; vāmadevasya patnī vāmadevī

Significance Vāmadeva is one of the five faces of Śiva, with Sadyojāta, Aghora, Tatpuruṣa and Īśāna; vāma also evokes the 'left-hand' path of the Tantras.

Uncertain Two analyses are current: the consort of Vāmadeva, followed here, and 'the lovely goddess' (vāmā devī).

470 वयोऽवस्थाविवर्जिता vayo'vasthā-vivarjitā

She who is free from the changes of age

Sandhi वयोऽवस्था = वयस् + अवस्था (vayas + avasthā) — the s of vayas becomes ru (Pāṇini 8.2.66), which after a and before a becomes u (6.1.113 ato ror aplutād aplute); a + u → o (6.1.87); the o then absorbs the initial a of avasthā (pūrvarūpa, 6.1.109 eṅaḥ padāntād ati), marked by the avagraha ऽ

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) vayo-avasthā 'the stages of age' — childhood, youth, old age (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) The participle vivarjitā 'free from' is the head and takes the stages in the instrumental (an ablative vigraha, vayo'vasthābhyaḥ vivarjitā, gives the same sense).

Analysis वयसः अवस्थाः वयोऽवस्थाः; वयोऽवस्थाभिः विवर्जिता वयोऽवस्थाविवर्जिता
vayasaḥ avasthāḥ vayo'vasthāḥ; vayo'vasthābhiḥ vivarjitā vayo'vasthāvivarjitā

Significance Birth, growth, change, decline and death touch the body, not Her; compare 430, nityayauvanā.

471 सिद्धेश्वरी siddheśvarī

She who is the sovereign of the siddhas, the perfected adepts

Sandhi सिद्धेश्वरी = सिद्ध + ईश्वरी (siddha + īśvarī) — guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. īśvarī 'sovereign' is the head; siddha 'perfected one, adept' stands to it in the genitive: 'sovereign of the siddhas'.

Analysis सिद्धानाम् ईश्वरी सिद्धेश्वरी
siddhānām īśvarī siddheśvarī

Significance The siddhas are those who have reached perfection; She rules over them, as their goal and the giver of their powers.

Corrected सिद्धेश्वरि → सिद्धेश्वरी. सिद्धेश्वरि → सिद्धेश्वरी (nominative -ī; the short form is the vocative).

472 सिद्धविद्या siddha-vidyā

She who is the Siddhavidyā, the accomplished mantra (the fifteen-syllable mantra)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya. siddha 'accomplished, perfected' qualifies vidyā 'mantra, knowledge'; the feminine siddhā takes the masculine stem in the karmadhāraya (puṃvadbhāva, Pāṇini 6.3.42).

Analysis सिद्धा विद्या सिद्धविद्या
siddhā vidyā siddhavidyā

Significance Traditionally Siddhavidyā names the fifteen-syllable Śrīvidyā mantra (pañcadaśī), called 'accomplished' because it is held to need none of the preliminary tests by which other mantras are judged suitable for a practitioner.

Uncertain The reason the pañcadaśī is called siddha is given traditionally as above; the exact commentarial source could not be confirmed here.

473 सिद्धमाता siddha-mātā

She who is the mother of the siddhas

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. mātā 'mother' is the head; siddha 'perfected one' stands to it in the genitive: 'mother of the siddhas'.

Analysis सिद्धानाम् माता सिद्धमाता
siddhānām mātā siddhamātā

Significance She cares for the perfected ones as a mother for her children; names 471–473 form a group on siddha.

474 यशस्विनी yaśasvinī

She who is renowned, possessed of glory

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Her glory is sung in all the worlds; She also grants renown to Her devotees.

Śloka 98names 475–479

विशुद्धिचक्रनिलया ऽऽरक्तवर्णा त्रिलोचना ।
खट्वाङ्गादिप्रहरणा वदनैकसमन्विता ॥ ९८ ॥

viśuddhicakranilayā ''raktavarṇā trilocanā |
khaṭvāṅgādipraharaṇā vadanaikasamanvitā || 98 ||

The names, separated ° form as a name on its own; in the recitation above it joins its neighbour

475विशुद्धि-चक्र-निलयाviśuddhi-cakra-nilayā476आरक्त-वर्णा°ārakta-varṇā477त्रि-लोचनाtri-locanā

478खट्वाङ्गादि-प्रहरणाkhaṭvāṅgādi-praharaṇā479वदनैक-समन्विताvadanaika-samanvitā

Translation

475She who resides in the viśuddhi cakra; 476She who is of slightly red (rosy) complexion; 477She who has three eyes;

478She whose weapons are the khaṭvāṅga (skull-topped staff) and others; 479She who has a single face.

Where the names meet

निलयाऽऽरक्तवर्णा = …निलया + आरक्तवर्णा (…nilayā + āraktavarṇā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); the double avagraha ऽऽ marks the long ā of ārakta that has merged

The section of the seven yoginīs begins: Ḍākinī in the viśuddhi (475–484), Rākiṇī in the anāhata (485–494), Lākinī in the maṇipūra (495–503), Kākinī in the svādhiṣṭhāna (504–513), Sākinī in the mūlādhāra (514–520), Hākinī in the ājñā (521–527) and Yākinī in the sahasrāra (528–534). Name 476 is āraktavarṇā, not raktavarṇā (that is 499).

The names

475 विशुद्धिचक्रनिलया viśuddhi-cakra-nilayā

She who resides in the viśuddhi cakra

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) viśuddhi-cakra 'the cakra called viśuddhi' (karmadhāraya of name and kind). (2) The whole is a bahuvrīhi with nilaya 'abode' as the final member: 'She whose abode is the viśuddhi cakra'.

Analysis विशुद्धिः इति चक्रम् विशुद्धिचक्रम्; विशुद्धिचक्रम् निलयः यस्याः सा विशुद्धिचक्रनिलया
viśuddhiḥ iti cakram viśuddhicakram; viśuddhicakram nilayaḥ yasyāḥ sā viśuddhicakranilayā

Significance Here begins the section of the seven yoginīs (475–534): in each cakra She takes the form of a yoginī with her own color, faces, weapons, bodily tissue, food and attendant śaktis. In the sixteen-petaled viśuddhi at the throat She is Ḍākinī (475–484).

476 आरक्तवर्णा ārakta-varṇā

She who is of slightly red (rosy) complexion

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner prādi-compound). (1) ā-rakta 'slightly red, rosy': the prefix ā in the sense 'a little' with the participle rakta 'red'. (2) It qualifies varṇa 'color, complexion', and the whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose complexion is rosy'.

Analysis ईषत् रक्तः आरक्तः; आरक्तः वर्णः यस्याः सा आरक्तवर्णा
īṣat raktaḥ āraktaḥ; āraktaḥ varṇaḥ yasyāḥ sā āraktavarṇā

Significance The complexion of Ḍākinī, the yoginī of the viśuddhi cakra.

Uncertain ā- can also intensify ('deep red'); the rendering 'rosy, reddish' is the usual one.

477 त्रिलोचना tri-locanā

She who has three eyes

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. The numeral tri 'three' qualifies locana 'eye'; the whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She who has three eyes'.

Analysis त्रीणि लोचनानि यस्याः सा त्रिलोचना
trīṇi locanāni yasyāḥ sā trilocanā

Significance Here the three eyes are those of Ḍākinī; compare 453, trinayanā, of the Goddess Herself.

478 खट्वाङ्गादिप्रहरणा khaṭvāṅgādi-praharaṇā

She whose weapons are the khaṭvāṅga (skull-topped staff) and others

Sandhi खट्वाङ्ग = खट्वा + अङ्ग (khaṭvā + aṅga) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ), inside the lexicalised compound khaṭvāṅga; खट्वाङ्गादि = खट्वाङ्ग + आदि (khaṭvāṅga + ādi) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner bahuvrīhi). (1) khaṭvāṅga-ādi 'those of which the khaṭvāṅga is the first' (bahuvrīhi with ādi). (2) It qualifies praharaṇa 'weapon', and the whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose weapons are the khaṭvāṅga and the rest'.

Analysis खट्वाङ्गम् आदिः येषाम् तानि खट्वाङ्गादीनि; खट्वाङ्गादीनि प्रहरणानि यस्याः सा खट्वाङ्गादिप्रहरणा
khaṭvāṅgam ādiḥ yeṣām tāni khaṭvāṅgādīni; khaṭvāṅgādīni praharaṇāni yasyāḥ sā khaṭvāṅgādipraharaṇā

Significance The weapons of Ḍākinī; the khaṭvāṅga is the emblem of the ascetic who has passed beyond fear of death.

479 वदनैकसमन्विता vadanaika-samanvitā

She who has a single face

Sandhi वदनैक = वदन + एक (vadana + eka) — vṛddhi: a + e → ai (Pāṇini 6.1.88 vṛddhir eci); अन्विता = अनु + इता (anu + itā) — yaṇ: u before an unlike vowel becomes v (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci), inside the prefixed participle anvita

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya with the numeral placed second). (1) vadana-eka 'one face', with the numeral placed after the noun, as in vadana-dvaya (487) and vadana-traya (496). (2) The participle samanvitā 'endowed with' is the head and takes it in the instrumental: 'endowed with a single face'.

Analysis एकम् वदनम् वदनैकम्; वदनैकेन समन्विता वदनैकसमन्विता
ekam vadanam vadanaikam; vadanaikena samanvitā vadanaikasamanvitā

Significance Ḍākinī has one face; the yoginīs that follow have two, three, four, five and six, and Yākinī faces every direction (532, sarvatomukhī).

Uncertain The order face-one is unusual. It is read here as a karmadhāraya with the numeral placed second (compare 487 and 496, where dvaya and traya are nouns, 'a pair', 'a triad'); the sense is not in doubt.

Śloka 99names 480–484

पायसान्नप्रिया त्वक्स्था पशुलोकभयङ्करी ।
अमृतादिमहाशक्तिसंवृता डाकिनीश्वरी ॥ ९९ ॥

pāyasānnapriyā tvaksthā paśulokabhayaṅkarī |
amṛtādimahāśaktisaṃvṛtā ḍākinīśvarī || 99 ||

The names, separated

Where the names meet

Name 482: bhayaṅkarī carries the augment m (bhaya-m-karī), written ṅ before k. Name 484 closes the Ḍākinī group.

The names

480 पायसान्नप्रिया pāyasānna-priyā

She who loves rice cooked in milk (pāyasa)

Sandhi पायसान्न = पायस + अन्न (pāyasa + anna) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) pāyasa-anna 'food that is pāyasa', rice cooked in milk (karmadhāraya). (2) The whole is a bahuvrīhi with priya 'dear': 'She to whom milk-rice is dear'.

Analysis पायसम् अन्नम् पायसान्नम्; पायसान्नम् प्रियम् यस्याः सा पायसान्नप्रिया
pāyasam annam pāyasānnam; pāyasānnam priyam yasyāḥ sā pāyasānnapriyā

Significance Each yoginī has her favorite offering: milk-rice for Ḍākinī; then rice with ghee, with jaggery, with curd, with green gram, with turmeric, and all foods for Yākinī.

481 त्वक्स्था tvak-sthā

She who abides in the skin

Sandhi त्वक्स्था = त्वच् + स्था (tvac + sthā) — the final c of tvac becomes k at the end of a member (kutva, Pāṇini 8.2.30 coḥ kuḥ)

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. sthā 'abiding' is formed from √sthā with the suffix ka after a word in the locative (Pāṇini 3.2.4 supi sthaḥ); the skin is where She abides.

Analysis त्वचि तिष्ठति इति त्वक्स्था
tvaci tiṣṭhati iti tvaksthā

Significance Each yoginī presides over one of the seven bodily tissues (dhātu): skin for Ḍākinī, then blood, flesh, fat, bone, marrow and semen.

482 पशुलोकभयङ्करी paśu-loka-bhayaṅkarī

She who strikes fear into the world of paśus, the bound souls

Sandhi भयङ्करी = भयम् + करी (bhayam + karī) — with the suffix khac (Pāṇini 3.2.43 meghartibhayeṣu kṛñaḥ) bhaya takes the augment m (6.3.67); m becomes anusvāra before a consonant (8.3.23) and then ṅ, homorganic with k (8.4.58 anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ)

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) paśu-loka 'the world of paśus', the bound souls (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) bhayaṅkarī 'causing fear' is an agent noun from √kṛ with its object bhaya 'fear'; the bound world is the one made to fear.

Analysis पशूनाम् लोकः पशुलोकः; पशुलोकस्य भयम् करोति इति पशुलोकभयङ्करी
paśūnām lokaḥ paśulokaḥ; paśulokasya bhayam karoti iti paśulokabhayaṅkarī

Significance In Śaiva doctrine the paśu is the soul bound by the fetters (pāśa) of ignorance; to those who live only for the world the fierce yoginī is terrifying.

483 अमृतादिमहाशक्तिसंवृता amṛtādi-mahā-śakti-saṃvṛtā

She who is surrounded by Amṛtā and the other great śaktis

Sandhi अमृतादि = अमृता + आदि (amṛtā + ādi) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); संवृता = सम् + वृता (sam + vṛtā) — the final m of the prefix sam becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya and a bahuvrīhi). (1) amṛtā-ādi 'those of whom Amṛtā is the first' (bahuvrīhi with ādi). (2) mahā-śakti 'great powers' (karmadhāraya; mahatī → mahā-, Pāṇini 6.3.46). (3) (1) qualifies (2) (karmadhāraya). (4) The participle saṃvṛtā 'surrounded' is the head of the whole and takes the śaktis in the instrumental.

Analysis अमृता आदिः यासाम् ताः अमृतादयः; महत्यः शक्तयः महाशक्तयः; अमृतादयः महाशक्तयः अमृतादिमहाशक्तयः; अमृतादिमहाशक्तिभिः संवृता अमृतादिमहाशक्तिसंवृता
amṛtā ādiḥ yāsām tāḥ amṛtādayaḥ; mahatyaḥ śaktayaḥ mahāśaktayaḥ; amṛtādayaḥ mahāśaktayaḥ amṛtādimahāśaktayaḥ; amṛtādimahāśaktibhiḥ saṃvṛtā amṛtādimahāśaktisaṃvṛtā

Significance Traditionally the sixteen śaktis of the viśuddhi, beginning with Amṛtā, stand on its sixteen petals, one for each of the sixteen vowels.

484 डाकिनीश्वरी ḍākinīśvarī

She who is Ḍākinī, the sovereign goddess

Sandhi डाकिनीश्वरी = डाकिनी + ईश्वरी (ḍākinī + īśvarī) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ī + ī → ī (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound karmadhāraya. The two members are in apposition: She is Ḍākinī and She is the sovereign goddess. A genitive reading, ḍākinīnām īśvarī 'sovereign of the ḍākinīs' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa), is also possible.

Analysis डाकिनी च असौ ईश्वरी च डाकिनीश्वरी
ḍākinī ca asau īśvarī ca ḍākinīśvarī

Significance This name closes the description of Ḍākinī (475–484), whose attributes — throat cakra, rosy color, three eyes, khaṭvāṅga, one face, milk-rice, skin, sixteen śaktis — the preceding names list.

Uncertain Karmadhāraya ('She who is Ḍākinī, the sovereign') and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa ('sovereign of the ḍākinīs') are both possible; the parallel names 494, 503, 520 and 534 (…ambāsvarūpiṇī) favor the first.

Śloka 100names 485–490

अनाहताब्जनिलया श्यामाभा वदनद्वया ।
दंष्ट्रोज्ज्वला ऽक्षमालादिधरा रुधिरसंस्थिता ॥ १०० ॥

anāhatābjanilayā śyāmābhā vadanadvayā |
daṃṣṭrojjvalā 'kṣamālādidharā rudhirasaṃsthitā || 100 ||

The names, separated ° form as a name on its own; in the recitation above it joins its neighbour

485She who resides in the anāhata lotus in the heart; 486She whose luster is dark (śyāma); 487She who has two faces;

488She who gleams with Her tusks; 489She who holds the rosary (akṣamālā) and other emblems; 490She who abides in the blood.

दंष्ट्राdaṃṣṭrātusk, fang

Where the names meet

दंष्ट्रोज्ज्वलाऽक्षमालादिधरा = दंष्ट्रोज्ज्वला + अक्षमालादिधरा (daṃṣṭrojjvalā + akṣamālādidharā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); the avagraha ऽ marks the a of akṣa that has merged

Names 485–490 describe Rākiṇī of the heart lotus (her group ends at 494). Name 489 begins akṣa- 'bead' (akṣamālā, rosary); the avagraha shows its a.

The names

485 अनाहताब्जनिलया anāhatābja-nilayā

She who resides in the anāhata lotus in the heart

Sandhi अनाहताब्ज = अनाहत + अब्ज (anāhata + abja) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); अब्ज = अप् + ज (ap + ja) — jaśtva: a final p becomes b before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.39 jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte), inside the lexicalised compound abja

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya and a nañ-tatpuruṣa). (1) an-āhata 'unstruck' (nañ-tatpuruṣa; the negative na becomes a and takes n before a vowel, Pāṇini 6.3.73–74, a morphological change, not sandhi). (2) anāhata-abja 'the lotus called anāhata' (karmadhāraya). (3) The whole is a bahuvrīhi with nilaya 'abode': 'She whose abode is the anāhata lotus'.

Analysis न आहतम् अनाहतम्; अनाहतम् अब्जम् अनाहताब्जम्; अनाहताब्जम् निलयः यस्याः सा अनाहताब्जनिलया
na āhatam anāhatam; anāhatam abjam anāhatābjam; anāhatābjam nilayaḥ yasyāḥ sā anāhatābjanilayā

Significance The anāhata, the twelve-petaled heart lotus, is named after the 'unstruck' sound heard there in meditation; here She is the yoginī Rākiṇī (485–494).

486 श्यामाभा śyāmābhā

She whose luster is dark (śyāma)

Sandhi श्यामाभा = श्याम + आभा (śyāma + ābhā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi. śyāma 'dark' qualifies the feminine noun ābhā 'luster'; the whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose luster is dark'. The first member takes the masculine stem śyāma (puṃvadbhāva).

Analysis श्यामा आभा यस्याः सा श्यामाभा
śyāmā ābhā yasyāḥ sā śyāmābhā

Significance The dark complexion of Rākiṇī, the yoginī of the heart lotus.

487 वदनद्वया vadana-dvayā

She who has two faces

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) vadana-dvaya 'a pair of faces' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; dvaya is a noun, 'a pair'). (2) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She who has a pair of faces'.

Analysis वदनयोः द्वयम् वदनद्वयम्; वदनद्वयम् यस्याः सा वदनद्वया
vadanayoḥ dvayam vadanadvayam; vadanadvayam yasyāḥ sā vadanadvayā

Significance Rākiṇī has two faces, one more than Ḍākinī (479).

488 दंष्ट्रोज्ज्वला daṃṣṭrojjvalā

She who gleams with Her tusks

Sandhi दंष्ट्रोज्ज्वला = दंष्ट्रा + उज्ज्वला (daṃṣṭrā + ujjvalā) — guṇa: ā + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ); उज्ज्वला = उद् + ज्वला (ud + jvalā) — the prefix ud assimilates to the following palatal: d becomes j before j (ścutva, Pāṇini 8.4.40 stoḥ ścunā ścuḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa. ujjvalā 'blazing, gleaming' is the head and takes daṃṣṭrā 'tusk, fang' in the instrumental: 'gleaming with tusks'.

Analysis दंष्ट्राभिः उज्ज्वला दंष्ट्रोज्ज्वला
daṃṣṭrābhiḥ ujjvalā daṃṣṭrojjvalā

Significance The tusks mark Rākiṇī as a fierce form, terrible to what is opposed to the devotee.

489 अक्षमालादिधरा akṣamālādi-dharā

She who holds the rosary (akṣamālā) and other emblems

Sandhi अक्षमालादि = अक्षमाला + आदि (akṣamālā + ādi) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner bahuvrīhi and a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) akṣa-mālā 'a garland of beads', a rosary (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) …mālā-ādi 'the rosary and the rest' (bahuvrīhi with ādi). (3) dharā 'holding' (√dhṛ + the agent suffix a) governs them as its object.

Analysis अक्षाणाम् माला अक्षमाला; अक्षमाला आदिः येषाम् तानि अक्षमालादीनि; अक्षमालादीनि धरति इति अक्षमालादिधरा
akṣāṇām mālā akṣamālā; akṣamālā ādiḥ yeṣām tāni akṣamālādīni; akṣamālādīni dharati iti akṣamālādidharā

Significance The emblems of Rākiṇī. Traditionally the akṣamālā is also the garland of letters from a to kṣa, the whole alphabet.

490 रुधिरसंस्थिता rudhira-saṃsthitā

She who abides in the blood

Sandhi संस्थिता = सम् + स्थिता (sam + sthitā) — the final m of the prefix sam becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ)

Compound saptamī-tatpuruṣa. The participle saṃsthitā 'abiding' is the head and takes rudhira 'blood' in the locative: 'abiding in the blood'.

Analysis रुधिरे संस्थिता रुधिरसंस्थिता
rudhire saṃsthitā rudhirasaṃsthitā

Significance Blood is the bodily tissue (dhātu) of Rākiṇī, as skin is of Ḍākinī (481).

Where the names meet

Names 491–494 complete Rākiṇī of the anāhata: her twelve attendant śaktis, her food and her name.

The names

491 कालरात्र्यादिशक्त्यौघवृता kālarātryādi-śaktyaugha-vṛtā

She who is surrounded by the host of śaktis beginning with Kālarātri

Sandhi कालरात्र्यादि = कालरात्रि + आदि (kālarātri + ādi) — yaṇ: i before an unlike vowel becomes y (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci); शक्त्यौघ = शक्ति + औघ (śakti + augha) — yaṇ: i before an unlike vowel becomes y (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, a karmadhāraya and a bahuvrīhi). (1) kālarātri-ādi 'those of whom Kālarātri is the first' (bahuvrīhi with ādi). (2) It qualifies śakti (karmadhāraya). (3) …śakti-augha 'the host of those śaktis' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (4) The participle vṛtā 'surrounded' is the head of the whole and takes the host in the instrumental.

Analysis कालरात्रिः आदिः यासाम् ताः कालरात्र्यादयः; कालरात्र्यादयः शक्तयः कालरात्र्यादिशक्तयः; कालरात्र्यादिशक्तीनाम् औघः कालरात्र्यादिशक्त्यौघः; कालरात्र्यादिशक्त्यौघेन वृता कालरात्र्यादिशक्त्यौघवृता
kālarātriḥ ādiḥ yāsām tāḥ kālarātryādayaḥ; kālarātryādayaḥ śaktayaḥ kālarātryādiśaktayaḥ; kālarātryādiśaktīnām aughaḥ kālarātryādiśaktyaughaḥ; kālarātryādiśaktyaughena vṛtā kālarātryādiśaktyaughavṛtā

Significance Traditionally the twelve śaktis of the anāhata, beginning with Kālarātri, stand on its twelve petals, one for each letter from ka to ṭha.

Uncertain śaktyaugha requires the member augha, a by-form of ogha 'flood, host' (śakti + ogha would give śaktyogha); the sense is not affected.

492 स्निग्धौदनप्रिया snigdhaudana-priyā

She who loves rice made rich with ghee

Sandhi स्निग्धौदन = स्निग्ध + ओदन (snigdha + odana) — vṛddhi: a + o → au (Pāṇini 6.1.88 vṛddhir eci)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) snigdha-odana 'rice made rich (with ghee)' (karmadhāraya). (2) The whole is a bahuvrīhi with priya 'dear': 'She to whom rich ghee-rice is dear'.

Analysis स्निग्धः ओदनः स्निग्धौदनः; स्निग्धौदनः प्रियः यस्याः सा स्निग्धौदनप्रिया
snigdhaḥ odanaḥ snigdhaudanaḥ; snigdhaudanaḥ priyaḥ yasyāḥ sā snigdhaudanapriyā

Significance The favorite offering of Rākiṇī, the yoginī of the heart lotus.

493 महावीरेन्द्रवरदा mahā-vīrendra-varadā

She who grants boons to the foremost of great heroes

Sandhi वीरेन्द्र = वीर + इन्द्र (vīra + indra) — guṇa: a + i → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner upapada-tatpuruṣa, ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and karmadhāraya). (1) mahā-vīra 'great heroes' (karmadhāraya; mahat → mahā-, Pāṇini 6.3.46). (2) …vīra-indra 'the chiefs among them' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; indra 'lord, chief' at the end of a compound). (3) vara-dā 'boon-giver' (upapada-tatpuruṣa, √dā + ka, Pāṇini 3.2.3). (4) The heroes stand to the boon-giver in the genitive, here in the sense 'to'.

Analysis महान्तः वीराः महावीराः; महावीराणाम् इन्द्राः महावीरेन्द्राः; वरम् ददाति इति वरदा; महावीरेन्द्राणाम् वरदा महावीरेन्द्रवरदा
mahāntaḥ vīrāḥ mahāvīrāḥ; mahāvīrāṇām indrāḥ mahāvīrendrāḥ; varam dadāti iti varadā; mahāvīrendrāṇām varadā mahāvīrendravaradā

Significance Traditionally the vīras are also the heroic practitioners of the Tantras, who worship without fear; She grants their aims.

494 राकिण्यम्बास्वरूपिणी rākiṇyambā-svarūpiṇī

She who has the form of Mother Rākiṇī

Sandhi राकिण्यम्बा = राकिणी + अम्बा (rākiṇī + ambā) — yaṇ: ī before an unlike vowel becomes y (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci)

Compound karmadhāraya, with the possessive suffix -in (svarūpa itself a karmadhāraya). (1) rākiṇī-ambā 'Mother Rākiṇī' (karmadhāraya of apposition). (2) sva-rūpa 'own form, true nature' (karmadhāraya). (3) The possessive suffix -in (Pāṇini 5.2.115) is added to the whole: 'She whose own form is Mother Rākiṇī'.

Analysis राकिणी च असौ अम्बा च राकिण्यम्बा; स्वम् रूपम् स्वरूपम्; राकिण्यम्बा स्वरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति राकिण्यम्बास्वरूपिणी
rākiṇī ca asau ambā ca rākiṇyambā; svam rūpam svarūpam; rākiṇyambā svarūpam asyāḥ asti iti rākiṇyambāsvarūpiṇī

Significance This name closes the Rākiṇī group (485–494). She is dark (486), two-faced (487), with gleaming tusks (488), dwelling in the blood (490) and fond of ghee-rice (492).

Śloka 102names 495–498

मणिपूराब्जनिलया वदनत्रयसंयुता ।
वज्रादिकायुधोपेता डामर्यादिभिरावृता ॥ १०२ ॥

maṇipūrābjanilayā vadanatrayasaṃyutā |
vajrādikāyudhopetā ḍāmaryādibhirāvṛtā || 102 ||

The names, separated

495मणिपूराब्ज-निलयाmaṇipūrābja-nilayā496वदन-त्रय-संयुताvadana-traya-saṃyutā

497वज्रादिकायुधोपेताvajrādikāyudhopetā498डामर्यादिभिर्-आवृताḍāmaryādibhir-āvṛtā

Translation

495She who resides in the maṇipūra lotus; 496She who has three faces;

497She who is armed with the vajra (thunderbolt) and other weapons; 498She who is surrounded by Ḍāmarī and the other śaktis.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish
495 मणिपूराब्जनिलया maṇipūrābja-nilayā
मणिपूरmaṇipūramaṇipūra, the navel cakra (lit. 'city of jewels' or 'full of jewels')
अब्जabjalotus (lit. 'water-born')ap 'water' + ja 'born'
निलयाnilayāabodenilaya, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi
496 वदनत्रयसंयुता vadana-traya-saṃyutā
वदनvadanaface
त्रयtrayatriad, group of three
संयुताsaṃyutājoined with, possessed ofsam + √yu 'to join', past participle, feminine
497 वज्रादिकायुधोपेता vajrādikāyudhopetā
वज्रvajrathunderbolt
आदिकādikabeginning with; 'and the rest'ādi + the suffix ka
आयुधāyudhaweapon
उपेताupetāfurnished with, possessed ofupa + √i 'to go', past participle, feminine
498 डामर्यादिभिरावृता ḍāmaryādibhir-āvṛtā
डामरीḍāmarīḌāmarī, name of a śakti
आदिभिःādibhiḥby those beginning withādi, instrumental plural
आवृताāvṛtāsurroundedā + √vṛ 'to cover', past participle, feminine

Where the names meet

Lākinī of the maṇipūra (495–503). Name 498 is a phrase, not a compound: ḍāmaryādibhiḥ 'by Ḍāmarī and the rest' keeps its instrumental ending and is joined to āvṛtā by sandhi (-bhir āvṛtā).

The names

495 मणिपूराब्जनिलया maṇipūrābja-nilayā

She who resides in the maṇipūra lotus

Sandhi मणिपूराब्ज = मणिपूर + अब्ज (maṇipūra + abja) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); अब्ज = अप् + ज (ap + ja) — jaśtva: a final p becomes b before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.39 jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte), inside the lexicalised compound abja

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) maṇipūra-abja 'the lotus called maṇipūra' (karmadhāraya of name and kind). (2) The whole is a bahuvrīhi with nilaya 'abode': 'She whose abode is the maṇipūra lotus'.

Analysis मणिपूरम् अब्जम् मणिपूराब्जम्; मणिपूराब्जम् निलयः यस्याः सा मणिपूराब्जनिलया
maṇipūram abjam maṇipūrābjam; maṇipūrābjam nilayaḥ yasyāḥ sā maṇipūrābjanilayā

Significance The ten-petaled lotus at the navel; here She is the yoginī Lākinī (495–503).

496 वदनत्रयसंयुता vadana-traya-saṃyutā

She who has three faces

Sandhi संयुता = सम् + युता (sam + yutā) — the final m of the prefix sam becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) vadana-traya 'a triad of faces' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; traya is a noun, 'a group of three'). (2) The participle saṃyutā 'joined with' is the head and takes it in the instrumental.

Analysis वदनानाम् त्रयम् वदनत्रयम्; वदनत्रयेण संयुता वदनत्रयसंयुता
vadanānām trayam vadanatrayam; vadanatrayeṇa saṃyutā vadanatrayasaṃyutā

Significance Lākinī has three faces: one more than Rākiṇī (487).

497 वज्रादिकायुधोपेता vajrādikāyudhopetā

She who is armed with the vajra (thunderbolt) and other weapons

Sandhi वज्रादिक = वज्र + आदिक (vajra + ādika) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); आदिकायुध = आदिक + आयुध (ādika + āyudha) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); आयुधोपेता = आयुध + उपेता (āyudha + upetā) — guṇa: a + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ); उपेता = उप + इता (upa + itā) — guṇa: a + i → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ), inside the prefixed participle upeta

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya and a bahuvrīhi). (1) vajra-ādika 'beginning with the vajra' (bahuvrīhi; ādi takes the optional compound-final suffix ka). (2) It qualifies āyudha 'weapon' (karmadhāraya). (3) The participle upetā 'furnished with' is the head and takes the weapons in the instrumental.

Analysis वज्रम् आदिः येषाम् तानि वज्रादिकानि; वज्रादिकानि आयुधानि वज्रादिकायुधानि; वज्रादिकायुधैः उपेता वज्रादिकायुधोपेता
vajram ādiḥ yeṣām tāni vajrādikāni; vajrādikāni āyudhāni vajrādikāyudhāni; vajrādikāyudhaiḥ upetā vajrādikāyudhopetā

Significance The weapons of Lākinī, the yoginī of the navel lotus.

498 डामर्यादिभिरावृता ḍāmaryādibhir-āvṛtā

She who is surrounded by Ḍāmarī and the other śaktis

Sandhi डामर्यादि = डामरी + आदि (ḍāmarī + ādi) — yaṇ: ī before an unlike vowel becomes y (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci); डामर्यादिभिरावृता = डामर्यादिभिः + आवृता (ḍāmaryādibhiḥ + āvṛtā) — visarga after i becomes r before a vowel (final s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66, kept as r): the instrumental ending -bhiḥ joins the next word

Compound a two-word phrase, not one compound: the bahuvrīhi ḍāmaryādi in the instrumental, governed by the participle āvṛtā. (1) ḍāmarī-ādi 'those of whom Ḍāmarī is the first' (bahuvrīhi with ādi). (2) This stands as a separate word in the instrumental plural, ḍāmaryādibhiḥ 'by Ḍāmarī and the rest', and the participle āvṛtā 'surrounded' governs it. The case ending is not dropped, so the name is a phrase joined by sandhi, not a compound.

Analysis डामरी आदिः यासाम् ताः डामर्यादयः; डामर्यादिभिः आवृता
ḍāmarī ādiḥ yāsām tāḥ ḍāmaryādayaḥ; ḍāmaryādibhiḥ āvṛtā

Significance Traditionally the ten śaktis of the maṇipūra, beginning with Ḍāmarī, stand on its ten petals, one for each letter from ḍa to pha.

Śloka 103names 499–503

रक्तवर्णा मांसनिष्ठा गुडान्नप्रीतमानसा ।
समस्तभक्तसुखदा लाकिन्यम्बास्वरूपिणी ॥ १०३ ॥

raktavarṇā māṃsaniṣṭhā guḍānnaprītamānasā |
samastabhaktasukhadā lākinyambāsvarūpiṇī || 103 ||

The names, separated

499रक्त-वर्णाrakta-varṇā500मांस-निष्ठाmāṃsa-niṣṭhā501गुडान्न-प्रीत-मानसाguḍānna-prīta-mānasā

502समस्त-भक्त-सुख-दाsamasta-bhakta-sukha-dā503लाकिन्यम्बा-स्वरूपिणीlākinyambā-svarūpiṇī

Translation

499She who is red in complexion; 500She who abides in the flesh; 501She whose heart delights in rice cooked with jaggery;

502She who confers happiness on all Her devotees; 503She who has the form of Mother Lākinī.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish
499 रक्तवर्णा rakta-varṇā
रक्तraktared√rañj 'to be colored', past participle
वर्णाvarṇācolor, complexionvarṇa, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi
500 मांसनिष्ठा māṃsa-niṣṭhā
मांसmāṃsaflesh
निष्ठाniṣṭhāabiding, established inni + √sthā 'to stand' + ka, feminine -ā
501 गुडान्नप्रीतमानसा guḍānna-prīta-mānasā
गुडguḍajaggery, raw cane sugar
अन्नannafood, cooked rice
प्रीतprītapleased, delighted√prī 'to please', past participle
मानसाmānasāmind, heartmānasa, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi
502 समस्तभक्तसुखदा samasta-bhakta-sukha-dā
समस्तsamastaall, entiresam + asta, lit. 'thrown together'
भक्तbhaktadevotee
सुखsukhahappiness
दाdāgiving√dā 'to give' + ka, feminine -ā
503 लाकिन्यम्बास्वरूपिणी lākinyambā-svarūpiṇī
लाकिनीlākinīLākinī, the yoginī of the maṇipūra
अम्बाambāmother
स्वरूपिणीsvarūpiṇīhaving as Her own formsva 'own' + rūpa 'form' + the possessive suffix -in, feminine -ī; n becomes ṇ after r (Pāṇini 8.4.2)

Where the names meet

Name 499 raktavarṇā (Lākinī) is not 476 āraktavarṇā (Ḍākinī).

The names

499 रक्तवर्णा rakta-varṇā

She who is red in complexion

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. rakta 'red' qualifies varṇa 'complexion'; the whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose complexion is red'.

Analysis रक्तः वर्णः यस्याः सा रक्तवर्णा
raktaḥ varṇaḥ yasyāḥ sā raktavarṇā

Significance The color of Lākinī; compare 476, āraktavarṇā, of Ḍākinī.

500 मांसनिष्ठा māṃsa-niṣṭhā

She who abides in the flesh

Sandhi निष्ठा = नि + स्था (ni + sthā) — after the i of the prefix ni the s of √sthā becomes ṣ (Pāṇini 8.3.65), and th then becomes ṭh beside ṣ (ṣṭutva, 8.4.41 ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ)

Compound saptamī-tatpuruṣa. niṣṭhā 'abiding, fixed in' (ni + √sthā + ka) is the head and takes māṃsa 'flesh' in the locative: 'abiding in the flesh'.

Analysis मांसे निष्ठा मांसनिष्ठा
māṃse niṣṭhā māṃsaniṣṭhā

Significance Flesh is the bodily tissue (dhātu) of Lākinī, as skin is of Ḍākinī and blood of Rākiṇī.

501 गुडान्नप्रीतमानसा guḍānna-prīta-mānasā

She whose heart delights in rice cooked with jaggery

Sandhi गुडान्न = गुड + अन्न (guḍa + anna) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa and a karmadhāraya). (1) guḍa-anna 'rice with jaggery' (karmadhāraya with the middle word yukta 'joined with' dropped). (2) …anna-prīta 'pleased by it' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (3) It qualifies mānasa 'mind, heart', and the whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose heart is pleased by jaggery-rice'.

Analysis गुडयुक्तम् अन्नम् गुडान्नम्; गुडान्नेन प्रीतम् गुडान्नप्रीतम्; गुडान्नप्रीतम् मानसम् यस्याः सा गुडान्नप्रीतमानसा
guḍayuktam annam guḍānnam; guḍānnena prītam guḍānnaprītam; guḍānnaprītam mānasam yasyāḥ sā guḍānnaprītamānasā

Significance The favorite offering of Lākinī.

502 समस्तभक्तसुखदा samasta-bhakta-sukha-dā

She who confers happiness on all Her devotees

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner upapada-tatpuruṣa and a karmadhāraya). (1) samasta-bhakta 'all devotees' (karmadhāraya). (2) sukha-dā 'giver of happiness' (upapada-tatpuruṣa, √dā + ka). (3) The devotees stand to the giver in the genitive, in the sense 'to'.

Analysis समस्ताः भक्ताः समस्तभक्ताः; सुखम् ददाति इति सुखदा; समस्तभक्तानाम् सुखदा समस्तभक्तसुखदा
samastāḥ bhaktāḥ samastabhaktāḥ; sukham dadāti iti sukhadā; samastabhaktānām sukhadā samastabhaktasukhadā

Significance Though Lākinī is fierce, to every devotee She gives happiness.

503 लाकिन्यम्बास्वरूपिणी lākinyambā-svarūpiṇī

She who has the form of Mother Lākinī

Sandhi लाकिन्यम्बा = लाकिनी + अम्बा (lākinī + ambā) — yaṇ: ī before an unlike vowel becomes y (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci)

Compound karmadhāraya, with the possessive suffix -in (svarūpa itself a karmadhāraya). (1) lākinī-ambā 'Mother Lākinī' (karmadhāraya of apposition). (2) sva-rūpa 'own form, true nature' (karmadhāraya). (3) The possessive suffix -in (Pāṇini 5.2.115) is added to the whole: 'She whose own form is Mother Lākinī'.

Analysis लाकिनी च असौ अम्बा च लाकिन्यम्बा; स्वम् रूपम् स्वरूपम्; लाकिन्यम्बा स्वरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति लाकिन्यम्बास्वरूपिणी
lākinī ca asau ambā ca lākinyambā; svam rūpam svarūpam; lākinyambā svarūpam asyāḥ asti iti lākinyambāsvarūpiṇī

Significance This name closes the Lākinī group (495–503). She is three-faced (496), red (499), abiding in the flesh (500) and fond of jaggery-rice (501).

Śloka 104names 504–508

स्वाधिष्ठानाम्बुजगता चतुर्वक्त्रमनोहरा ।
शूलाद्यायुधसम्पन्ना पीतवर्णा ऽतिगर्विता ॥ १०४ ॥

svādhiṣṭhānāmbujagatā caturvaktramanoharā |
śūlādyāyudhasampannā pītavarṇā 'tigarvitā || 104 ||

The names, separated ° form as a name on its own; in the recitation above it joins its neighbour

504स्वाधिष्ठानाम्बुज-गताsvādhiṣṭhānāmbuja-gatā505चतुर्-वक्त्र-मनोहराcatur-vaktra-manoharā

506शूलाद्यायुध-सम्पन्नाśūlādyāyudha-sampannā507पीत-वर्णाpīta-varṇā508अति-गर्विता°ati-garvitā

Translation

504She who abides in the svādhiṣṭhāna lotus; 505She who is captivating with Her four faces;

506She who is endowed with the trident and other weapons; 507She who is yellow in color; 508She who is very proud.

Where the names meet

पीतवर्णाऽतिगर्विता = पीतवर्णा + अतिगर्विता (pītavarṇā + atigarvitā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); the avagraha ऽ marks the a that has merged

Kākinī of the svādhiṣṭhāna (504–513). The avagraha marks the a of ati: name 508 is atigarvitā.

The names

504 स्वाधिष्ठानाम्बुजगता svādhiṣṭhānāmbuja-gatā

She who abides in the svādhiṣṭhāna lotus

Sandhi स्वाधिष्ठान = स्व + अधिष्ठान (sva + adhiṣṭhāna) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ), inside the name svādhiṣṭhāna; अधिष्ठान = अधि + स्थान (adhi + sthāna) — after the i of the prefix ni the s of √sthā becomes ṣ (Pāṇini 8.3.65), and th then becomes ṭh beside ṣ (ṣṭutva, 8.4.41 ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ); स्वाधिष्ठानाम्बुज = स्वाधिष्ठान + अम्बुज (svādhiṣṭhāna + ambuja) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound dvitīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) svādhiṣṭhāna-ambuja 'the lotus called svādhiṣṭhāna' (karmadhāraya of name and kind). (2) The participle gatā 'gone to, abiding in' is the head and takes the lotus in the accusative (Pāṇini 2.1.24 dvitīyā śritātītapatitagatātyastaprāptāpannaiḥ).

Analysis स्वाधिष्ठानम् अम्बुजम् स्वाधिष्ठानाम्बुजम्; स्वाधिष्ठानाम्बुजम् गता स्वाधिष्ठानाम्बुजगता
svādhiṣṭhānam ambujam svādhiṣṭhānāmbujam; svādhiṣṭhānāmbujam gatā svādhiṣṭhānāmbujagatā

Significance The six-petaled lotus above the mūlādhāra, 'Her own seat'; here She is the yoginī Kākinī (504–513).

505 चतुर्वक्त्रमनोहरा catur-vaktra-manoharā

She who is captivating with Her four faces

Sandhi मनोहरा = मनस् + हरा (manas + harā) — visarga sandhi: final s becomes ru (Pāṇini 8.2.66), which after a and before a voiced consonant becomes u (6.1.114 haśi ca); a + u then gives o (6.1.87) — inside the lexicalised compound manohara

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner dvigu). (1) catur-vaktra 'four faces': a numeral compound, a dvigu because another member follows (Pāṇini 2.1.51). (2) manoharā 'captivating' is the head and takes the faces in the instrumental: 'captivating with four faces'.

Analysis चत्वारि वक्त्राणि चतुर्वक्त्रम्; चतुर्वक्त्रेण मनोहरा चतुर्वक्त्रमनोहरा
catvāri vaktrāṇi caturvaktram; caturvaktreṇa manoharā caturvaktramanoharā

Significance Kākinī has four faces, one more than Lākinī (496).

506 शूलाद्यायुधसम्पन्ना śūlādyāyudha-sampannā

She who is endowed with the trident and other weapons

Sandhi शूलादि = शूल + आदि (śūla + ādi) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); आद्यायुध = आदि + आयुध (ādi + āyudha) — yaṇ: i before an unlike vowel becomes y (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya and a bahuvrīhi). (1) śūla-ādi 'beginning with the trident' (bahuvrīhi with ādi). (2) It qualifies āyudha 'weapon' (karmadhāraya). (3) The participle sampannā 'endowed' is the head and takes the weapons in the instrumental.

Analysis शूलम् आदिः येषाम् तानि शूलादीनि; शूलादीनि आयुधानि शूलाद्यायुधानि; शूलाद्यायुधैः सम्पन्ना शूलाद्यायुधसम्पन्ना
śūlam ādiḥ yeṣām tāni śūlādīni; śūlādīni āyudhāni śūlādyāyudhāni; śūlādyāyudhaiḥ sampannā śūlādyāyudhasampannā

Significance The emblems of Kākinī; traditionally the trident, the noose, a skull-cup and the gesture of fearlessness (abhaya).

507 पीतवर्णा pīta-varṇā

She who is yellow in color

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. pīta 'yellow' qualifies varṇa 'complexion'; the whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose complexion is yellow'.

Analysis पीतः वर्णः यस्याः सा पीतवर्णा
pītaḥ varṇaḥ yasyāḥ sā pītavarṇā

Significance The color of Kākinī.

508 अतिगर्विता ati-garvitā

She who is very proud

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound prādi-tatpuruṣa. The prefix ati 'exceedingly' qualifies garvitā 'proud' (Pāṇini 2.2.18 kugatiprādayaḥ).

Analysis अतिशयेन गर्विता अतिगर्विता
atiśayena garvitā atigarvitā

Significance Traditionally the pride of Kākinī is the majesty of one who has no equal, or pride in Her own beauty.

Śloka 105names 509–513

मेदोनिष्ठा मधुप्रीता बन्धिन्यादिसमन्विता ।
दध्यन्नासक्तहृदया काकिनीरूपधारिणी ॥ १०५ ॥

medoniṣṭhā madhuprītā bandhinyādisamanvitā |
dadhyannāsaktahṛdayā kākinīrūpadhāriṇī || 105 ||

The names, separated

509मेदो-निष्ठाmedo-niṣṭhā510मधु-प्रीताmadhu-prītā511बन्धिन्यादि-समन्विताbandhinyādi-samanvitā

512दध्यन्नासक्त-हृदयाdadhyannāsakta-hṛdayā513काकिनी-रूप-धारिणीkākinī-rūpa-dhāriṇī

Translation

509She who abides in the fat; 510She who is pleased with honey; 511She who is accompanied by Bandhinī and the other śaktis;

512She whose heart is fond of curd-rice; 513She who bears the form of Kākinī.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish
509 मेदोनिष्ठा medo-niṣṭhā
मेदस्medasfat, the fatty tissue
निष्ठाniṣṭhāabiding, established inni + √sthā 'to stand' + ka, feminine -ā
510 मधुप्रीता madhu-prītā
मधुmadhuhoney
प्रीताprītāpleased, delighted√prī 'to please', past participle, feminine
511 बन्धिन्यादिसमन्विता bandhinyādi-samanvitā
बन्धिनीbandhinīBandhinī, name of a śakti (lit. 'she who binds')
आदिādibeginning; 'and the rest'
समन्विताsamanvitāaccompanied bysam + anu + √i, past participle, feminine
512 दध्यन्नासक्तहृदया dadhyannāsakta-hṛdayā
दधिdadhicurd
अन्नannafood, cooked rice
आसक्तāsaktaattached to, fond ofā + √sañj 'to cling', past participle
हृदयाhṛdayāhearthṛdaya, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi
513 काकिनीरूपधारिणी kākinī-rūpa-dhāriṇī
काकिनीkākinīKākinī, the yoginī of the svādhiṣṭhāna
रूपrūpaform
धारिणीdhāriṇībearing, assuming√dhṛ, causative, + -in, feminine -ī; n becomes ṇ after r (Pāṇini 8.4.2)

Where the names meet

Name 509: medo- is medas 'fat' in its sandhi form (s → o before the voiced n).

The names

509 मेदोनिष्ठा medo-niṣṭhā

She who abides in the fat

Sandhi मेदोनिष्ठा = मेदस् + निष्ठा (medas + niṣṭhā) — visarga sandhi: final s becomes ru (Pāṇini 8.2.66), which after a and before a voiced consonant becomes u (6.1.114 haśi ca); a + u then gives o (6.1.87); निष्ठा = नि + स्था (ni + sthā) — after the i of the prefix ni the s of √sthā becomes ṣ (Pāṇini 8.3.65), and th then becomes ṭh beside ṣ (ṣṭutva, 8.4.41 ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ)

Compound saptamī-tatpuruṣa. niṣṭhā 'abiding in' is the head and takes medas 'fat' in the locative.

Analysis मेदसि निष्ठा मेदोनिष्ठा
medasi niṣṭhā medoniṣṭhā

Significance Fat is the bodily tissue (dhātu) of Kākinī.

510 मधुप्रीता madhu-prītā

She who is pleased with honey

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa. The participle prītā 'pleased' is the head and takes madhu 'honey' in the instrumental: 'pleased with honey'.

Analysis मधुना प्रीता मधुप्रीता
madhunā prītā madhuprītā

Significance Honey is among the offerings dear to Kākinī.

511 बन्धिन्यादिसमन्विता bandhinyādi-samanvitā

She who is accompanied by Bandhinī and the other śaktis

Sandhi बन्धिन्यादि = बन्धिनी + आदि (bandhinī + ādi) — yaṇ: ī before an unlike vowel becomes y (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci); अन्विता = अनु + इता (anu + itā) — yaṇ: u before an unlike vowel becomes v (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci), inside the prefixed participle anvita

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner bahuvrīhi). (1) bandhinī-ādi 'those of whom Bandhinī is the first' (bahuvrīhi with ādi). (2) The participle samanvitā 'accompanied by' is the head and takes them in the instrumental.

Analysis बन्धिनी आदिः यासाम् ताः बन्धिन्यादयः; बन्धिन्यादिभिः समन्विता बन्धिन्यादिसमन्विता
bandhinī ādiḥ yāsām tāḥ bandhinyādayaḥ; bandhinyādibhiḥ samanvitā bandhinyādisamanvitā

Significance Traditionally the six śaktis of the svādhiṣṭhāna, beginning with Bandhinī, stand on its six petals, one for each letter from ba to la.

512 दध्यन्नासक्तहृदया dadhyannāsakta-hṛdayā

She whose heart is fond of curd-rice

Sandhi दध्यन्न = दधि + अन्न (dadhi + anna) — yaṇ: i before an unlike vowel becomes y (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci); अन्नासक्त = अन्न + आसक्त (anna + āsakta) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner saptamī-tatpuruṣa and a karmadhāraya). (1) dadhi-anna 'rice with curd' (karmadhāraya with the middle word yukta dropped). (2) …anna-āsakta 'attached to it' (saptamī-tatpuruṣa). (3) It qualifies hṛdaya 'heart', and the whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose heart is attached to curd-rice'.

Analysis दधियुक्तम् अन्नम् दध्यन्नम्; दध्यन्ने आसक्तम् दध्यन्नासक्तम्; दध्यन्नासक्तम् हृदयम् यस्याः सा दध्यन्नासक्तहृदया
dadhiyuktam annam dadhyannam; dadhyanne āsaktam dadhyannāsaktam; dadhyannāsaktam hṛdayam yasyāḥ sā dadhyannāsaktahṛdayā

Significance The favorite offering of Kākinī.

513 काकिनीरूपधारिणी kākinī-rūpa-dhāriṇī

She who bears the form of Kākinī

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) kākinī-rūpa 'the form of Kākinī' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) dhāriṇī 'bearing' is an agent noun from the causative of √dhṛ with the suffix -in (Pāṇini 3.2.78) and takes the form as its object.

Analysis काकिन्याः रूपम् काकिनीरूपम्; काकिनीरूपम् धारयति इति काकिनीरूपधारिणी
kākinyāḥ rūpam kākinīrūpam; kākinīrūpam dhārayati iti kākinīrūpadhāriṇī

Significance This name closes the Kākinī group (504–513): four-faced (505), yellow (507), abiding in the fat (509), fond of honey and curd-rice (510, 512).

Śloka 106names 514–518

मूलाधाराम्बुजारूढा पञ्चवक्त्रा ऽस्थिसंस्थिता ।
अङ्कुशादिप्रहरणा वरदादिनिषेविता ॥ १०६ ॥

mūlādhārāmbujārūḍhā pañcavaktrā 'sthisaṃsthitā |
aṅkuśādipraharaṇā varadādiniṣevitā || 106 ||

The names, separated ° form as a name on its own; in the recitation above it joins its neighbour

514मूलाधाराम्बुजारूढाmūlādhārāmbujārūḍhā515पञ्च-वक्त्राpañca-vaktrā516अस्थि-संस्थिता°asthi-saṃsthitā

517अङ्कुशादि-प्रहरणाaṅkuśādi-praharaṇā518वरदादि-निषेविताvaradādi-niṣevitā

Translation

514She who is seated on the mūlādhāra lotus; 515She who has five faces; 516She who resides in the bones;

517She who holds the goad and other weapons; 518She who is attended by Varadā and the other śaktis.

515 पञ्चवक्त्रा pañca-vaktrā
पञ्चन्pañcanfiveappears as pañca- in the compound

Where the names meet

पञ्चवक्त्राऽस्थिसंस्थिता = पञ्चवक्त्रा + अस्थिसंस्थिता (pañcavaktrā + asthisaṃsthitā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); the avagraha ऽ marks the a that has merged

Sākinī of the mūlādhāra (514–520). The avagraha marks the a of asthi 'bone': name 516 is asthisaṃsthitā.

The names

514 मूलाधाराम्बुजारूढा mūlādhārāmbujārūḍhā

She who is seated on the mūlādhāra lotus

Sandhi मूलाधार = मूल + आधार (mūla + ādhāra) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ), inside the name mūlādhāra; मूलाधाराम्बुज = मूलाधार + अम्बुज (mūlādhāra + ambuja) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); अम्बुजारूढा = अम्बुज + आरूढा (ambuja + ārūḍhā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound dvitīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) mūla-ādhāra 'the root-support' (karmadhāraya), the name of the lowest cakra. (2) mūlādhāra-ambuja 'the mūlādhāra lotus' (karmadhāraya of name and kind). (3) The participle ārūḍhā 'mounted on, seated on' is the head and takes the lotus in the accusative.

Analysis मूलम् आधारः मूलाधारः; मूलाधारम् अम्बुजम् मूलाधाराम्बुजम्; मूलाधाराम्बुजम् आरूढा मूलाधाराम्बुजारूढा
mūlam ādhāraḥ mūlādhāraḥ; mūlādhāram ambujam mūlādhārāmbujam; mūlādhārāmbujam ārūḍhā mūlādhārāmbujārūḍhā

Significance The four-petaled root lotus at the base of the spine; here She is the yoginī Sākinī (514–520). Compare 105, sahasrārāmbujārūḍhā, at the crown.

515 पञ्चवक्त्रा pañca-vaktrā

She who has five faces

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. The numeral pañca 'five' qualifies vaktra 'face'; the whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She who has five faces'.

Analysis पञ्च वक्त्राणि यस्याः सा पञ्चवक्त्रा
pañca vaktrāṇi yasyāḥ sā pañcavaktrā

Significance Sākinī has five faces, one more than Kākinī (505).

516 अस्थिसंस्थिता asthi-saṃsthitā

She who resides in the bones

Sandhi संस्थिता = सम् + स्थिता (sam + sthitā) — the final m of the prefix sam becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ)

Compound saptamī-tatpuruṣa. The participle saṃsthitā 'abiding' is the head and takes asthi 'bone' in the locative.

Analysis अस्थिषु संस्थिता अस्थिसंस्थिता
asthiṣu saṃsthitā asthisaṃsthitā

Significance Bone is the bodily tissue (dhātu) of Sākinī.

517 अङ्कुशादिप्रहरणा aṅkuśādi-praharaṇā

She who holds the goad and other weapons

Sandhi अङ्कुशादि = अङ्कुश + आदि (aṅkuśa + ādi) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner bahuvrīhi). (1) aṅkuśa-ādi 'beginning with the goad' (bahuvrīhi with ādi). (2) It qualifies praharaṇa 'weapon', and the whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose weapons are the goad and the rest'.

Analysis अङ्कुशः आदिः येषाम् तानि अङ्कुशादीनि; अङ्कुशादीनि प्रहरणानि यस्याः सा अङ्कुशादिप्रहरणा
aṅkuśaḥ ādiḥ yeṣām tāni aṅkuśādīni; aṅkuśādīni praharaṇāni yasyāḥ sā aṅkuśādipraharaṇā

Significance The weapons of Sākinī; the goad recalls the aṅkuśa that the Goddess Herself holds (name 10).

518 वरदादिनिषेविता varadādi-niṣevitā

She who is attended by Varadā and the other śaktis

Sandhi वरदादि = वरदा + आदि (varadā + ādi) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); निषेविता = नि + सेविता (ni + sevitā) — after the i of the prefix ni the s of √sev becomes ṣ (retroflexion, Pāṇini 8.3.70)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner bahuvrīhi). (1) varadā-ādi 'those of whom Varadā is the first' (bahuvrīhi with ādi). (2) The participle niṣevitā 'attended, served' is the head and takes them in the instrumental.

Analysis वरदा आदिः यासाम् ताः वरदादयः; वरदादिभिः निषेविता वरदादिनिषेविता
varadā ādiḥ yāsām tāḥ varadādayaḥ; varadādibhiḥ niṣevitā varadādiniṣevitā

Significance Traditionally the four śaktis of the mūlādhāra, beginning with Varadā, stand on its four petals, one for each of the letters va, śa, ṣa and sa.

Śloka 107names 519–523

मुद्गौदनासक्तचित्ता साकिन्यम्बास्वरूपिणी ।
आज्ञाचक्राब्जनिलया शुक्लवर्णा षडानना ॥ १०७ ॥

mudgaudanāsaktacittā sākinyambāsvarūpiṇī |
ājñācakrābjanilayā śuklavarṇā ṣaḍānanā || 107 ||

The names, separated

519मुद्गौदनासक्त-चित्ताmudgaudanāsakta-cittā520साकिन्यम्बा-स्वरूपिणीsākinyambā-svarūpiṇī

521आज्ञा-चक्राब्ज-निलयाājñā-cakrābja-nilayā522शुक्ल-वर्णाśukla-varṇā523षड्-आननाṣaḍ-ānanā

Translation

519She whose mind delights in rice cooked with green gram (mudga); 520She who has the form of Mother Sākinī;

521She who resides in the lotus of the ājñā cakra; 522She who is white in color; 523She who has six faces.

SanskritEnglish

ओदनodanaboiled rice

साकिनीsākinīSākinī, the yoginī of the mūlādhāra
अम्बाambāmother
स्वरूपिणीsvarūpiṇīhaving as Her own formsva 'own' + rūpa 'form' + the possessive suffix -in, feminine -ī; n becomes ṇ after r (Pāṇini 8.4.2)
521 आज्ञाचक्राब्जनिलया ājñā-cakrābja-nilayā

चक्रcakrawheel; a center of the subtle body

षष्ṣaṣsix
आननाānanāfaceānana, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

Where the names meet

Name 520 closes Sākinī; Hākinī of the ājñā begins at 521 (521–527).

The names

519 मुद्गौदनासक्तचित्ता mudgaudanāsakta-cittā

She whose mind delights in rice cooked with green gram (mudga)

Sandhi मुद्गौदन = मुद्ग + ओदन (mudga + odana) — vṛddhi: a + o → au (Pāṇini 6.1.88 vṛddhir eci); ओदनासक्त = ओदन + आसक्त (odana + āsakta) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner saptamī-tatpuruṣa and a karmadhāraya). (1) mudga-odana 'rice cooked with green gram' (karmadhāraya with the middle word yukta dropped). (2) …odana-āsakta 'attached to it' (saptamī-tatpuruṣa). (3) It qualifies citta 'mind', and the whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose mind is attached to green-gram rice'.

Analysis मुद्गयुक्तः ओदनः मुद्गौदनः; मुद्गौदने आसक्तम् मुद्गौदनासक्तम्; मुद्गौदनासक्तम् चित्तम् यस्याः सा मुद्गौदनासक्तचित्ता
mudgayuktaḥ odanaḥ mudgaudanaḥ; mudgaudane āsaktam mudgaudanāsaktam; mudgaudanāsaktam cittam yasyāḥ sā mudgaudanāsaktacittā

Significance The favorite offering of Sākinī.

520 साकिन्यम्बास्वरूपिणी sākinyambā-svarūpiṇī

She who has the form of Mother Sākinī

Sandhi साकिन्यम्बा = साकिनी + अम्बा (sākinī + ambā) — yaṇ: ī before an unlike vowel becomes y (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci)

Compound karmadhāraya, with the possessive suffix -in (svarūpa itself a karmadhāraya). (1) sākinī-ambā 'Mother Sākinī' (karmadhāraya of apposition). (2) sva-rūpa 'own form, true nature' (karmadhāraya). (3) The possessive suffix -in (Pāṇini 5.2.115) is added to the whole: 'She whose own form is Mother Sākinī'.

Analysis साकिनी च असौ अम्बा च साकिन्यम्बा; स्वम् रूपम् स्वरूपम्; साकिन्यम्बा स्वरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति साकिन्यम्बास्वरूपिणी
sākinī ca asau ambā ca sākinyambā; svam rūpam svarūpam; sākinyambā svarūpam asyāḥ asti iti sākinyambāsvarūpiṇī

Significance This name closes the Sākinī group (514–520). She is five-faced (515), abiding in the bones (516) and fond of green-gram rice (519).

521 आज्ञाचक्राब्जनिलया ājñā-cakrābja-nilayā

She who resides in the lotus of the ājñā cakra

Sandhi चक्राब्ज = चक्र + अब्ज (cakra + abja) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); अब्ज = अप् + ज (ap + ja) — jaśtva: a final p becomes b before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.39 jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte), inside the lexicalised compound abja

Compound bahuvrīhi (over inner karmadhārayas). (1) ājñā-cakra 'the cakra called ājñā' (karmadhāraya of name and kind). (2) …cakra-abja 'the lotus that is that cakra' (karmadhāraya). (3) The whole is a bahuvrīhi with nilaya 'abode'.

Analysis आज्ञा इति चक्रम् आज्ञाचक्रम्; आज्ञाचक्रम् अब्जम् आज्ञाचक्राब्जम्; आज्ञाचक्राब्जम् निलयः यस्याः सा आज्ञाचक्राब्जनिलया
ājñā iti cakram ājñācakram; ājñācakram abjam ājñācakrābjam; ājñācakrābjam nilayaḥ yasyāḥ sā ājñācakrābjanilayā

Significance The two-petaled lotus between the eyebrows; here She is the yoginī Hākinī (521–527).

522 शुक्लवर्णा śukla-varṇā

She who is white in color

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. śukla 'white' qualifies varṇa 'complexion'; the whole is a bahuvrīhi.

Analysis शुक्लः वर्णः यस्याः सा शुक्लवर्णा
śuklaḥ varṇaḥ yasyāḥ sā śuklavarṇā

Significance The color of Hākinī.

523 षडानना ṣaḍ-ānanā

She who has six faces

Sandhi षडानना = षष् + आनना (ṣaṣ + ānanā) — jaśtva: the final ṣ of ṣaṣ becomes ḍ before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.39 jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte)

Compound bahuvrīhi. The numeral ṣaṣ 'six' qualifies ānana 'face'; the whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She who has six faces'.

Analysis षट् आननानि यस्याः सा षडानना
ṣaṭ ānanāni yasyāḥ sā ṣaḍānanā

Significance Hākinī has six faces, one more than Sākinī (515).

Śloka 108names 524–527

मज्जासंस्था हंसवतीमुख्यशक्तिसमन्विता ।
हरिद्रान्नैकरसिका हाकिनीरूपधारिणी ॥ १०८ ॥

majjāsaṃsthā haṃsavatīmukhyaśaktisamanvitā |
haridrānnaikarasikā hākinīrūpadhāriṇī || 108 ||

The names, separated

524मज्जा-संस्थाmajjā-saṃsthā525हंसवती-मुख्य-शक्ति-समन्विताhaṃsavatī-mukhya-śakti-samanvitā

526हरिद्रान्नैक-रसिकाharidrānnaika-rasikā527हाकिनी-रूप-धारिणीhākinī-rūpa-dhāriṇī

Translation

524She who abides in the marrow; 525She who is accompanied by the śaktis headed by Haṃsavatī;

526She whose special delight is rice cooked with turmeric; 527She who bears the form of Hākinī.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish
524 मज्जासंस्था majjā-saṃsthā
मज्जाmajjāmarrow
संस्थाsaṃsthāabiding, established insam + √sthā + ka, feminine -ā
525 हंसवतीमुख्यशक्तिसमन्विता haṃsavatī-mukhya-śakti-samanvitā
हंसवतीhaṃsavatīHaṃsavatī, name of a śaktihaṃsa + the possessive suffix -vat, feminine -ī
मुख्यmukhyachief, foremost
शक्तिśaktipower; a goddess of the retinue
समन्विताsamanvitāaccompanied bysam + anu + √i, past participle, feminine
526 हरिद्रान्नैकरसिका haridrānnaika-rasikā
हरिद्राharidrāturmeric
अन्नannafood, cooked rice
एकekaone; alone, solely
रसिकाrasikāone who relishes, delighting inrasa 'taste' + -ika, feminine
527 हाकिनीरूपधारिणी hākinī-rūpa-dhāriṇī
हाकिनीhākinīHākinī, the yoginī of the ājñā cakra
रूपrūpaform
धारिणीdhāriṇībearing, assuming√dhṛ, causative, + -in, feminine -ī; n becomes ṇ after r (Pāṇini 8.4.2)

Where the names meet

Name 526 is haridrānna + ekarasikā ('delighting solely in turmeric-rice'); compare 90, kulāmṛtaikarasikā.

The names

524 मज्जासंस्था majjā-saṃsthā

She who abides in the marrow

Sandhi संस्था = सम् + स्था (sam + sthā) — the final m of the prefix sam becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ)

Compound saptamī-tatpuruṣa. saṃsthā 'abiding' (sam + √sthā + ka, Pāṇini 3.2.4) is the head and takes majjā 'marrow' in the locative.

Analysis मज्जायाम् संस्था मज्जासंस्था
majjāyām saṃsthā majjāsaṃsthā

Significance Marrow is the bodily tissue (dhātu) of Hākinī.

525 हंसवतीमुख्यशक्तिसमन्विता haṃsavatī-mukhya-śakti-samanvitā

She who is accompanied by the śaktis headed by Haṃsavatī

Sandhi अन्विता = अनु + इता (anu + itā) — yaṇ: u before an unlike vowel becomes v (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci), inside the prefixed participle anvita

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya and a bahuvrīhi). (1) haṃsavatī-mukhya 'those of whom Haṃsavatī is the chief' (bahuvrīhi with mukhya). (2) It qualifies śakti (karmadhāraya). (3) The participle samanvitā 'accompanied by' is the head and takes the śaktis in the instrumental.

Analysis हंसवती मुख्या यासाम् ताः हंसवतीमुख्याः; हंसवतीमुख्याः शक्तयः हंसवतीमुख्यशक्तयः; हंसवतीमुख्यशक्तिभिः समन्विता हंसवतीमुख्यशक्तिसमन्विता
haṃsavatī mukhyā yāsām tāḥ haṃsavatīmukhyāḥ; haṃsavatīmukhyāḥ śaktayaḥ haṃsavatīmukhyaśaktayaḥ; haṃsavatīmukhyaśaktibhiḥ samanvitā haṃsavatīmukhyaśaktisamanvitā

Significance Traditionally the two śaktis of the ājñā, Haṃsavatī and Kṣamāvatī, stand on its two petals, for the letters ha and kṣa.

526 हरिद्रान्नैकरसिका haridrānnaika-rasikā

She whose special delight is rice cooked with turmeric

Sandhi हरिद्रान्न = हरिद्रा + अन्न (haridrā + anna) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); अन्नैक = अन्न + एक (anna + eka) — vṛddhi: a + e → ai (Pāṇini 6.1.88 vṛddhir eci)

Compound saptamī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) haridrā-anna 'rice with turmeric' (karmadhāraya with the middle word yukta dropped). (2) eka-rasikā 'delighting solely' (eka used adverbially, 'alone, only'). (3) The rice stands to it in the locative: 'delighting solely in turmeric-rice'. Compare name 90, kulāmṛtaikarasikā.

Analysis हरिद्रायुक्तम् अन्नम् हरिद्रान्नम्; एकम् रसिका एकरसिका; हरिद्रान्ने एकरसिका हरिद्रान्नैकरसिका
haridrāyuktam annam haridrānnam; ekam rasikā ekarasikā; haridrānne ekarasikā haridrānnaikarasikā

Significance The favorite offering of Hākinī.

Uncertain eka-rasikā may also be read as 'having a single taste, absorbed in one relish'; the sense is the same.

527 हाकिनीरूपधारिणी hākinī-rūpa-dhāriṇī

She who bears the form of Hākinī

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) hākinī-rūpa 'the form of Hākinī' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) dhāriṇī 'bearing' (causative of √dhṛ + -in) takes the form as its object.

Analysis हाकिन्याः रूपम् हाकिनीरूपम्; हाकिनीरूपम् धारयति इति हाकिनीरूपधारिणी
hākinyāḥ rūpam hākinīrūpam; hākinīrūpam dhārayati iti hākinīrūpadhāriṇī

Significance This name closes the Hākinī group (521–527): white (522), six-faced (523), abiding in the marrow (524), fond of turmeric-rice (526).

Śloka 109names 528–532

सहस्रदलपद्मस्था सर्ववर्णोपशोभिता ।
सर्वायुधधरा शुक्लसंस्थिता सर्वतोमुखी ॥ १०९ ॥

sahasradalapadmasthā sarvavarṇopaśobhitā |
sarvāyudhadharā śuklasaṃsthitā sarvatomukhī || 109 ||

The names, separated

528सहस्र-दल-पद्म-स्थाsahasra-dala-padma-sthā529सर्व-वर्णोपशोभिताsarva-varṇopaśobhitā

530सर्वायुध-धराsarvāyudha-dharā531शुक्ल-संस्थिताśukla-saṃsthitā532सर्वतो-मुखीsarvato-mukhī

Translation

528She who resides in the thousand-petaled lotus; 529She who is resplendent with all colors;

530She who holds all weapons; 531She who resides in the semen, the vital essence; 532She who has faces turned in all directions.

SanskritEnglish
528 सहस्रदलपद्मस्था sahasra-dala-padma-sthā
सहस्रsahasrathousand
दलdalapetal
पद्मpadmalotus
स्थाsthāabiding√sthā 'to stand' + ka, feminine -ā
529 सर्ववर्णोपशोभिता sarva-varṇopaśobhitā
सर्वsarvaall
वर्णvarṇacolor; also letter (of the alphabet)
उपशोभिताupaśobhitāadorned, made resplendentupa + √śubh, causative, past participle, feminine
530 सर्वायुधधरा sarvāyudha-dharā
सर्वsarvaall
आयुधāyudhaweapon

Where the names meet

Yākinī of the sahasrāra (528–534), who gathers the attributes of all the others: all colors, all weapons, faces in every direction.

The names

528 सहस्रदलपद्मस्था sahasra-dala-padma-sthā

She who resides in the thousand-petaled lotus

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya and a bahuvrīhi). (1) sahasra-dala 'thousand-petaled' (bahuvrīhi). (2) It qualifies padma 'lotus' (karmadhāraya). (3) sthā 'abiding' (√sthā + ka after a word in the locative, Pāṇini 3.2.4 supi sthaḥ) takes the lotus as its place.

Analysis सहस्रम् दलानि यस्य तत् सहस्रदलम्; सहस्रदलम् पद्मम् सहस्रदलपद्मम्; सहस्रदलपद्मे तिष्ठति इति सहस्रदलपद्मस्था
sahasram dalāni yasya tat sahasradalam; sahasradalam padmam sahasradalapadmam; sahasradalapadme tiṣṭhati iti sahasradalapadmasthā

Significance The sahasrāra at the crown of the head, where She is the yoginī Yākinī (528–534); compare 105, sahasrārāmbujārūḍhā.

529 सर्ववर्णोपशोभिता sarva-varṇopaśobhitā

She who is resplendent with all colors

Sandhi वर्णोपशोभिता = वर्ण + उपशोभिता (varṇa + upaśobhitā) — guṇa: a + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) sarva-varṇa 'all colors' (karmadhāraya). (2) The participle upaśobhitā 'adorned, made beautiful' is the head and takes the colors in the instrumental.

Analysis सर्वे वर्णाः सर्ववर्णाः; सर्ववर्णैः उपशोभिता सर्ववर्णोपशोभिता
sarve varṇāḥ sarvavarṇāḥ; sarvavarṇaiḥ upaśobhitā sarvavarṇopaśobhitā

Significance Yākinī shines with every color. Since varṇa also means 'letter', it is traditionally read too as 'adorned with all the letters', which are said to cover the petals of the thousand-petaled lotus.

530 सर्वायुधधरा sarvāyudha-dharā

She who holds all weapons

Sandhi सर्वायुध = सर्व + आयुध (sarva + āyudha) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) sarva-āyudha 'all weapons' (karmadhāraya). (2) dharā 'holding' (√dhṛ + the agent suffix a) takes them as its object.

Analysis सर्वाणि आयुधानि सर्वायुधानि; सर्वायुधानि धरति इति सर्वायुधधरा
sarvāṇi āyudhāni sarvāyudhāni; sarvāyudhāni dharati iti sarvāyudhadharā

Significance Yākinī bears the weapons of all the other yoginīs: every power is hers.

531 शुक्लसंस्थिता śukla-saṃsthitā

She who resides in the semen, the vital essence

Sandhi संस्थिता = सम् + स्थिता (sam + sthitā) — the final m of the prefix sam becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ)

Compound saptamī-tatpuruṣa. The participle saṃsthitā 'abiding' is the head and takes śukla 'semen, vital essence' in the locative.

Analysis शुक्ले संस्थिता शुक्लसंस्थिता
śukle saṃsthitā śuklasaṃsthitā

Significance Śukla is the seventh and last of the bodily tissues (dhātu), the essence of all the others; it belongs to Yākinī.

532 सर्वतोमुखी sarvato-mukhī

She who has faces turned in all directions

Sandhi सर्वतोमुखी = सर्वतस् + मुखी (sarvatas + mukhī) — visarga sandhi: final s becomes ru (Pāṇini 8.2.66), which after a and before a voiced consonant becomes u (6.1.114 haśi ca); a + u then gives o (6.1.87)

Compound bahuvrīhi. The adverb sarvatas 'on all sides' qualifies mukha 'face'; the whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose faces are on all sides'. mukha takes the feminine -ī (Pāṇini 4.1.54).

Analysis सर्वतः मुखानि यस्याः सा सर्वतोमुखी
sarvataḥ mukhāni yasyāḥ sā sarvatomukhī

Significance Yākinī faces every direction; so the Bhagavad Gītā describes the Supreme as having eyes, heads and faces everywhere (sarvato'kṣiśiromukham).

Śloka 110names 533–541

सर्वौदनप्रीतचित्ता याकिन्यम्बास्वरूपिणी ।
स्वाहा स्वधा ऽमतिर् मेधा श्रुतिः स्मृतिर् अनुत्तमा ॥ ११० ॥

sarvaudanaprītacittā yākinyambāsvarūpiṇī |
svāhā svadhā 'matir medhā śrutiḥ smṛtir anuttamā || 110 ||

The names, separated ° form as a name on its own; in the recitation above it joins its neighbour

533सर्वौदन-प्रीत-चित्ताsarvaudana-prīta-cittā534याकिन्यम्बा-स्वरूपिणीyākinyambā-svarūpiṇī

535स्वाहाsvāhā536स्वधाsvadhā537अ-मतिः°a-matiḥ538मेधाmedhā539श्रुतिःśrutiḥ540स्मृतिः°smṛtiḥ541अन्-उत्तमाan-uttamā

Translation

533She whose mind is pleased by all kinds of rice offerings; 534She who has the form of Mother Yākinī;

535She who is Svāhā, the call with which offerings are made to the gods in the fire; 536She who is Svadhā, the call with which offerings are made to the ancestors; 537She who is in the form of ignorance or nescience; 538She who is in the form of wisdom (medhā); 539She who is in the form of the Vedas; 540She who is smṛti, the remembered tradition that rests on the Vedas; 541She who is the best; She who is not excelled by anyone.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish
533 सर्वौदनप्रीतचित्ता sarvaudana-prīta-cittā
सर्वsarvaall
ओदनodanaboiled rice, a rice dish
प्रीतprītapleased√prī 'to please', past participle
चित्ताcittāmindcitta, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi
534 याकिन्यम्बास्वरूपिणी yākinyambā-svarūpiṇī
याकिनीyākinīYākinī, the yoginī of the sahasrāra
अम्बाambāmother
स्वरूपिणीsvarūpiṇīhaving as Her own formsva 'own' + rūpa 'form' + the possessive suffix -in, feminine -ī; n becomes ṇ after r (Pāṇini 8.4.2)
535 स्वाहा svāhā
स्वाहाsvāhāsvāhā, the call with which an oblation is offered to the godsindeclinable
536 स्वधा svadhā
स्वधाsvadhāsvadhā, the call with which offerings are made to the ancestorsindeclinable

अanot, non-the negative na in compound
मतिःmatiḥunderstanding, knowledge√man + -ti

मेधाmedhāintelligence, wisdom; the power of retaining knowledge

श्रुतिःśrutiḥwhat is heard: the Veda√śru 'to hear' + -ti (ktin, Pāṇini 3.3.94)
