स्मृतिःsmṛtiḥmemory; the remembered tradition√smṛ 'to remember' + -ti (ktin, Pāṇini 3.3.94)
541 अनुत्तमा an-uttamā
अन्annot, there is nothe negative na before a vowel
उत्तमाuttamāhighest, bestud + the superlative suffix -tama; uttama with the feminine -ā

Where the names meet

स्वधाऽमतिर्मेधा = स्वधा + अमतिः + मेधा (svadhā + amatiḥ + medhā) — ā + a → ā (savarṇa-dīrgha, Pāṇini 6.1.101), marked by the avagraha; then the visarga of amatiḥ becomes r before the voiced m (final s → ru, 8.2.66, kept as r after i)

स्मृतिरनुत्तमा = स्मृतिः + अनुत्तमा (smṛtiḥ + anuttamā) — visarga after i becomes r before a voiced sound or a vowel (final s → ru, Pāṇini 8.2.66; ru is kept as r, since the change to u applies only after a)

The yoginī section ends with 534. Name 537 is amatiḥ 'ignorance' (svadhā + amatiḥ; the avagraha shows the a), not matiḥ, which is name 445; 537 and 538 (medhā) pair ignorance and wisdom. 535–536 are the sacrificial calls svāhā and svadhā.

The names

533 सर्वौदनप्रीतचित्ता sarvaudana-prīta-cittā

She whose mind is pleased by all kinds of rice offerings

Sandhi सर्वौदन = सर्व + ओदन (sarva + odana) — vṛddhi: a + o → au (Pāṇini 6.1.88 vṛddhir eci)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa and a karmadhāraya). (1) sarva-odana 'all kinds of rice' (karmadhāraya). (2) …odana-prīta 'pleased by them' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (3) It qualifies citta 'mind', and the whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose mind is pleased by all kinds of rice'.

Analysis सर्वे ओदनाः सर्वौदनाः; सर्वौदनैः प्रीतम् सर्वौदनप्रीतम्; सर्वौदनप्रीतम् चित्तम् यस्याः सा सर्वौदनप्रीतचित्ता
sarve odanāḥ sarvaudanāḥ; sarvaudanaiḥ prītam sarvaudanaprītam; sarvaudanaprītam cittam yasyāḥ sā sarvaudanaprītacittā

Significance Yākinī accepts every offering, as all the yoginīs are gathered in her.

534 याकिन्यम्बास्वरूपिणी yākinyambā-svarūpiṇī

She who has the form of Mother Yākinī

Sandhi याकिन्यम्बा = याकिनी + अम्बा (yākinī + ambā) — yaṇ: ī before an unlike vowel becomes y (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci)

Compound karmadhāraya, with the possessive suffix -in (svarūpa itself a karmadhāraya). (1) yākinī-ambā 'Mother Yākinī' (karmadhāraya of apposition). (2) sva-rūpa 'own form, true nature' (karmadhāraya). (3) The possessive suffix -in (Pāṇini 5.2.115) is added to the whole: 'She whose own form is Mother Yākinī'.

Analysis याकिनी च असौ अम्बा च याकिन्यम्बा; स्वम् रूपम् स्वरूपम्; याकिन्यम्बा स्वरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति याकिन्यम्बास्वरूपिणी
yākinī ca asau ambā ca yākinyambā; svam rūpam svarūpam; yākinyambā svarūpam asyāḥ asti iti yākinyambāsvarūpiṇī

Significance This name closes the Yākinī group (528–534). With her the section of the seven yoginīs (475–534) ends.

535 स्वाहा svāhā

She who is Svāhā, the call with which offerings are made to the gods in the fire

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Svāhā is personified as the consort of Agni, through whom the gods receive the oblations; She is the power that makes the offering reach them.

536 स्वधा svadhā

She who is Svadhā, the call with which offerings are made to the ancestors

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Svadhā is the counterpart of svāhā: with it offerings are made to the pitṛs, the ancestors; personified, she too is a form of the Goddess.

537 अमतिः a-matiḥ

She who is in the form of ignorance or nescience

Sandhi स्वधाऽमतिः = स्वधा + अमतिः (svadhā + amatiḥ) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101), between this name and 536; the avagraha ऽ marks the merged a. Bhāskararāya reads svadhā + amatiḥ here, not svadhā + matiḥ (matiḥ is already name 445).

Compound nañ-tatpuruṣa. The negative na, reduced to a before a consonant (Pāṇini 6.3.73 nalopo nañaḥ), compounds with mati 'understanding': 'non-understanding', ignorance.

Analysis न मतिः अमतिः
na matiḥ amatiḥ

Significance Ignorance too is Her power: the Devīmāhātmya calls Her both the supreme knowledge that is the cause of liberation and the cause of bondage in saṃsāra. The next name, medhā, gives the other side.

538 मेधा medhā

She who is in the form of wisdom (medhā)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Medhā is the intelligence that grasps and retains knowledge, especially of the sacred texts; with 537 She is both ignorance and wisdom.

539 श्रुतिः śrutiḥ

She who is in the form of the Vedas

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Śruti, 'what was heard' by the seers, is the Veda; She is its very substance.

540 स्मृतिः smṛtiḥ

She who is smṛti, the remembered tradition that rests on the Vedas

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Smṛti, the dharma texts and Purāṇas that draw out the meaning of the Veda, follows śruti (539); smṛti is also memory, and the Devīmāhātmya praises the Goddess who abides in all beings as memory (smṛtirūpeṇa).

541 अनुत्तमा an-uttamā

She who is the best; She who is not excelled by anyone

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (nañ-bahuvrīhi). The negative na with uttama 'higher, best' makes a bahuvrīhi: 'She than whom there is none higher'. Before a vowel na becomes an- (Pāṇini 6.3.73–74, a morphological change, not sandhi).

Analysis न विद्यते उत्तमः यस्याः सा अनुत्तमा
na vidyate uttamaḥ yasyāḥ sā anuttamā

Significance None surpasses Her; She is the highest.

Śloka 111names 542–547

पुण्यकीर्तिः पुण्यलभ्या पुण्यश्रवणकीर्तना ।
पुलोमजार्चिता बन्धमोचनी बन्धुरालका ॥ १११ ॥

puṇyakīrtiḥ puṇyalabhyā puṇyaśravaṇakīrtanā |
pulomajārcitā bandhamocanī bandhurālakā || 111 ||

The names, separated

542पुण्य-कीर्तिःpuṇya-kīrtiḥ543पुण्य-लभ्याpuṇya-labhyā544पुण्य-श्रवण-कीर्तनाpuṇya-śravaṇa-kīrtanā

545पुलोमजार्चिताpulomajārcitā546बन्ध-मोचनीbandha-mocanī547बन्धुरालकाbandhurālakā

Translation

542She whose fame is holy; 543She who is attained through merit; 544She whom it is meritorious to hear of and to praise;

545She who is worshipped by Pulomajā (Śacī, the wife of Indra); 546She who releases from bondage; 547She whose locks of hair are wavy.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish
542 पुण्यकीर्तिः puṇya-kīrtiḥ
पुण्यpuṇyaholy, meritorious, purifying
कीर्तिःkīrtiḥfame, renown, praisefeminine i-stem kīrti, nominative singular
543 पुण्यलभ्या puṇya-labhyā
पुण्यpuṇyamerit, the fruit of good deeds
लभ्याlabhyāto be attained, attainable√labh 'to obtain' with the gerundive suffix -ya (yat), feminine
544 पुण्यश्रवणकीर्तना puṇya-śravaṇa-kīrtanā
पुण्यpuṇyameritorious, merit-giving
श्रवणśravaṇahearing, listening√śru 'to hear'
कीर्तनाkīrtanāsinging, praising, glorifyingkīrtana (√kīrt 'to celebrate'), with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi
545 पुलोमजार्चिता pulomajārcitā
पुलोमजाpulomajāPulomajā, 'daughter of Puloman': Śacī (Indrāṇī), wife of Indrapuloman (a Dānava chief) + -ja 'born' (√jan)
अर्चिताarcitāworshipped, honored√arc 'to worship', past participle, feminine
546 बन्धमोचनी bandha-mocanī
बन्धbandhabondage, binding, fetter√bandh 'to bind'
मोचनीmocanīshe who releases, sets freecausative of √muc 'to free', agent noun in -ana, feminine -ī
547 बन्धुरालका bandhurālakā
बन्धुरbandhurawavy, curving; also lovely
अलकाalakālocks of hair, curls (especially on the forehead)alaka, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

Where the names meet

Name 545: divide pulomajā + arcitā (Śacī + 'worshipped'). Name 547 reads bandhurālakā here; the old name list had barbarālakā (see the name's variants).

The names

542 पुण्यकीर्तिः puṇya-kīrtiḥ

She whose fame is holy

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya). Inner layer: puṇyā kīrtiḥ 'holy fame' (karmadhāraya: the adjective puṇya qualifies kīrti). Outer layer: a bahuvrīhi, 'She whose fame is holy'. The feminine adjective puṇyā returns to its masculine stem puṇya- in the compound (puṃvadbhāva); kīrti, already feminine, is unchanged. The members meet without sound change.

Analysis पुण्या कीर्तिः यस्याः सा पुण्यकीर्तिः
puṇyā kīrtiḥ yasyāḥ sā puṇyakīrtiḥ

Significance Her renown itself purifies: traditionally, to speak of Her glory is already an act of merit, which the next two names develop.

543 पुण्यलभ्या puṇya-labhyā

She who is attained through merit

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa. puṇya 'merit' stands in the instrumental to the gerundive labhyā 'to be attained': 'attainable by (means of) merit'. labhyā is the head.

Analysis पुण्येन लभ्या पुण्यलभ्या
puṇyena labhyā puṇyalabhyā

Significance Traditionally, devotion to Her and initiation into Her worship are said to come only as the ripened fruit of merit gathered over many lives.

544 पुण्यश्रवणकीर्तना puṇya-śravaṇa-kīrtanā

She whom it is meritorious to hear of and to praise

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner itaretara-dvandva and karmadhāraya). (1) śravaṇa 'hearing' and kīrtana 'singing, praising' form a dvandva, 'hearing and praising'. (2) puṇya qualifies the pair: 'meritorious hearing and praising' (karmadhāraya). (3) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She, the hearing (of whom) and the praising (of whom) are meritorious'; the neuter kīrtana takes the feminine -ā. She is the object of the hearing and singing, not their agent.

Analysis श्रवणम् च कीर्तनम् च श्रवणकीर्तने; पुण्ये श्रवणकीर्तने यस्याः सा पुण्यश्रवणकीर्तना
śravaṇam ca kīrtanam ca śravaṇakīrtane; puṇye śravaṇakīrtane yasyāḥ sā puṇyaśravaṇakīrtanā

Significance Śravaṇa and kīrtana head the traditional list of the forms of devotion; simply listening to Her names and singing them is said to yield merit.

545 पुलोमजार्चिता pulomajārcitā

She who is worshipped by Pulomajā (Śacī, the wife of Indra)

Sandhi पुलोमजार्चिता = पुलोमजा + अर्चिता (pulomajā + arcitā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (with an inner upapada-tatpuruṣa). (1) pulomajā 'she who was born of Puloman', i.e. Śacī: the stem puloman (final n dropped in composition) with -ja 'born' from √jan (upapada-tatpuruṣa, feminine -ā). (2) Pulomajā stands in the instrumental to the participle arcitā 'worshipped', which is the head: 'worshipped by Śacī'.

Analysis पुलोम्नः जाता पुलोमजा; पुलोमजया अर्चिता पुलोमजार्चिता
pulomnaḥ jātā pulomajā; pulomajayā arcitā pulomajārcitā

Significance Even Śacī, queen of the gods, worships Her; traditionally her worship is said to keep Indra's sovereignty secure.

Uncertain That Śacī's worship secures Indra's rule is a traditional reading; no single source for it was confirmed here.

546 बन्धमोचनी bandha-mocanī

She who releases from bondage

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. mocanī is an agent noun, 'one who releases'; bandha 'bondage' is its object, expressed in the genitive that goes with an agent noun (kṛd-yoga ṣaṣṭhī). mocanī is the head: 'the releaser from bondage'.

Analysis बन्धस्य मोचनी बन्धमोचनी
bandhasya mocanī bandhamocanī

Significance The bondage is outward (prison, debt, trouble) and inward: the bonds of karma and ignorance that tie the self to saṃsāra, from which She alone frees.

547 बन्धुरालका bandhurālakā

She whose locks of hair are wavy

Sandhi बन्धुरालका = बन्धुर + अलका (bandhura + alakā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya). Inner layer: bandhura 'wavy' qualifies alaka 'lock of hair, curl' (karmadhāraya). Outer layer: a bahuvrīhi, 'She whose locks are wavy'; alaka takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis बन्धुराः अलकाः बन्धुरालकाः; बन्धुराः अलकाः यस्याः सा बन्धुरालका
bandhurāḥ alakāḥ bandhurālakāḥ; bandhurāḥ alakāḥ yasyāḥ sā bandhurālakā

Significance A return to the description of Her beauty: the gently curling locks framing Her face.

Uncertain The reading itself: this edition follows the verse text (bandhurālakā) where the old name list read barbarālakā; which of the two Bhāskararāya's text adopts could not be confirmed here. The sense is the same either way.

Variants The source's name list reads बर्बरालका barbarālakā (barbara 'curly'); the verse text, followed here, reads बन्धुरालका. Both readings are current in printed editions.

Corrected बर्बरालका → बन्धुरालका. Name list read बर्बरालका, verse text बन्धुरालका. The verse reading is adopted (bandhura, wavy; barbara, curly — the sense is the same); barbarālakā is recorded as a variant. Flagged for review.

Śloka 112names 548–552

विमर्शरूपिणी विद्या वियदादिजगत्प्रसूः ।
सर्वव्याधिप्रशमनी सर्वमृत्युनिवारिणी ॥ ११२ ॥

vimarśarūpiṇī vidyā viyadādijagatprasūḥ |
sarvavyādhipraśamanī sarvamṛtyunivāriṇī || 112 ||

548She whose form is vimarśa, the reflective awareness of consciousness; 549She who is in the form of knowledge; 550She who is the mother of the world, which begins with ether;

551She who allays all diseases; 552She who wards off every kind of death.

आदिādibeginning with, and the rest
जगत्jagatthe world, all that movespresent participle of √gam, used as a noun
प्रसूःprasūḥmother, she who brings forthpra + √sū 'to give birth', root noun; ū-stem, nominative -ūḥ
551 सर्वव्याधिप्रशमनी sarva-vyādhi-praśamanī
सर्वsarvaall, every
व्याधिvyādhidisease, sicknessvi + ā + √dhā
प्रशमनीpraśamanīshe who allays, quiets, curespra + causative of √śam 'to be calm', agent noun in -ana, feminine -ī
552 सर्वमृत्युनिवारिणी sarva-mṛtyu-nivāriṇī
सर्वsarvaall, every
मृत्युmṛtyudeath
निवारिणीnivāriṇīshe who wards off, preventsni + causative of √vṛ 'to cover, restrain', agent suffix -in, feminine -ī; n becomes ṇ after r (ṇatva)

Where the names meet

Name 550 is one compound, viyad-ādi-jagat-prasūḥ, though it was once printed as two words; the d is the voiced t of viyat 'ether'.

The names

548 विमर्शरूपिणी vimarśa-rūpiṇī

She whose form is vimarśa, the reflective awareness of consciousness

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya (identification) with the possessive suffix -in. vimarśa-rūpa 'the form that is vimarśa' is a karmadhāraya of identification. The possessive suffix -in (Pāṇini 5.2.115 ata iniṭhanau) and the feminine -ī make rūpiṇī 'having the form of': 'She whose form is vimarśa'.

Analysis विमर्शः एव रूपम् विमर्शरूपम्; विमर्शरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति विमर्शरूपिणी
vimarśaḥ eva rūpam vimarśarūpam; vimarśarūpam asyāḥ asti iti vimarśarūpiṇī

Significance In Śrīvidyā and Kashmir Śaivism, Śiva is prakāśa, the light of consciousness, and Śakti is vimarśa, its power to know itself; without vimarśa the light would be inert. The Goddess is that self-knowing power.

549 विद्या vidyā

She who is in the form of knowledge

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance She is the liberating knowledge that dispels ignorance (avidyā); in Śrīvidyā, vidyā also means the mantra, so She is the mantra as well as the knowledge it gives.

550 वियदादिजगत्प्रसूः viyad-ādi-jagat-prasūḥ

She who is the mother of the world, which begins with ether

Sandhi वियदादि = वियत् + आदि (viyat + ādi) — jaśtva: a final t becomes d at the end of a member, here before a vowel (Pāṇini 8.2.39 jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner bahuvrīhi and karmadhāraya). (1) viyad-ādi 'that which begins with ether (space)': a bahuvrīhi in -ādi, 'having viyat as its first'. (2) It qualifies jagat 'the world' (karmadhāraya): 'the world beginning with ether', i.e. the whole order of the elements from space down to earth. (3) prasū 'mother, she who brings forth' is the head; the world stands to it in the genitive. At jagat-prasū the t stays unvoiced before p.

Analysis वियत् आदिः यस्य तत् वियदादि; वियदादि जगत् वियदादिजगत्; वियदादिजगतः प्रसूः वियदादिजगत्प्रसूः
viyat ādiḥ yasya tat viyadādi; viyadādi jagat viyadādijagat; viyadādijagataḥ prasūḥ viyadādijagatprasūḥ

Significance The world unfolds from Her as the five elements, ether first, as in the Taittirīya Upaniṣad (2.1): from the Self, space; from space, air; and so on down to earth.

Corrected वियदादि जगत्प्रसूः → वियदादिजगत्प्रसूः. "वियदादि जगत्प्रसूः" → one compound name, written solid.

551 सर्वव्याधिप्रशमनी sarva-vyādhi-praśamanī

She who allays all diseases

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (with an inner karmadhāraya). (1) sarva-vyādhi 'all diseases' (karmadhāraya: sarva qualifies vyādhi). (2) praśamanī 'she who allays' is an agent noun and the head; the diseases are its object in the genitive.

Analysis सर्वे व्याधयः सर्वव्याधयः; सर्वव्याधीनाम् प्रशमनी सर्वव्याधिप्रशमनी
sarve vyādhayaḥ sarvavyādhayaḥ; sarvavyādhīnām praśamanī sarvavyādhipraśamanī

Significance Traditionally both the illnesses of the body and the root disease of saṃsāra (bhava-roga) are meant; recitation of this name is customary for healing.

552 सर्वमृत्युनिवारिणी sarva-mṛtyu-nivāriṇī

She who wards off every kind of death

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (with an inner karmadhāraya). (1) sarva-mṛtyu 'every death', i.e. death in all its forms (karmadhāraya). (2) nivāriṇī 'she who wards off' is the head and takes the deaths as its object in the genitive.

Analysis सर्वे मृत्यवः सर्वमृत्यवः; सर्वमृत्यूनाम् निवारिणी सर्वमृत्युनिवारिणी
sarve mṛtyavaḥ sarvamṛtyavaḥ; sarvamṛtyūnām nivāriṇī sarvamṛtyunivāriṇī

Significance Traditionally untimely death (apamṛtyu) is meant, and beyond it the endless round of dying and being born, which ends in knowledge of Her.

Śloka 113names 553–558

अग्रगण्या ऽचिन्त्यरूपा कलिकल्मषनाशिनी ।
कात्यायनी कालहन्त्री कमलाक्षनिषेविता ॥ ११३ ॥

agragaṇyā 'cintyarūpā kalikalmaṣanāśinī |
kātyāyanī kālahantrī kamalākṣaniṣevitā || 113 ||

The names, separated ° form as a name on its own; in the recitation above it joins its neighbour

553अग्र-गण्याagra-gaṇyā554अचिन्त्य-रूपा°acintya-rūpā555कलि-कल्मष-नाशिनीkali-kalmaṣa-nāśinī

556कात्यायनीkātyāyanī557काल-हन्त्रीkāla-hantrī558कमलाक्ष-निषेविताkamalākṣa-niṣevitā

Translation

553She who is to be counted the foremost; 554She whose form is beyond the reach of thought; 555She who destroys the sins of the Kali age;

556She who is Kātyāyanī, daughter of the sage Kātyāyana of Kata's line; 557She who is the destroyer of time (death); 558She who is served and worshipped by lotus-eyed Viṣṇu.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish
553 अग्रगण्या agra-gaṇyā
अग्रagrafront, first place, top
गण्याgaṇyāto be counted, reckoned√gaṇ 'to count', gerundive in -ya, feminine
554 अचिन्त्यरूपा acintya-rūpā
अanot (the negative prefix)
चिन्त्यcintyato be thought of, conceivable√cint 'to think', gerundive
रूपाrūpāform, naturerūpa, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi
555 कलिकल्मषनाशिनी kali-kalmaṣa-nāśinī
कलिkalithe Kali age, the last and darkest of the four ages; also strife
कल्मषkalmaṣasin, impurity, stain
नाशिनीnāśinīshe who destroyscausative of √naś 'to perish', agent suffix -in, feminine -ī
556 कात्यायनी kātyāyanī
कात्यायनीkātyāyanīKātyāyanī, 'the daughter of Kātyāyana'patronymic chain: Kata (a sage) → Kātya 'descendant of Kata' → Kātyāyana 'descendant of Kātya' → Kātyāyanī, the female of that line
557 कालहन्त्री kāla-hantrī
कालkālatime; also death, Yama, who comes with time
हन्त्रीhantrīshe who slays, destroyerhantṛ (√han 'to strike, slay' + agent suffix -tṛ), feminine -ī
558 कमलाक्षनिषेविता kamalākṣa-niṣevitā
कमलkamalalotus
अक्षakṣaeyeakṣi 'eye' as a compound-final -akṣa
निषेविताniṣevitāserved, worshipped, resorted toni + √sev 'to serve, attend', past participle, feminine

Where the names meet

अग्रगण्याऽचिन्त्य = अग्रगण्या + अचिन्त्य… (agragaṇyā + acintya…) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101); the avagraha (ऽ) marks the absorbed initial a of acintya

Divide agragaṇyā + acintyarūpā: the avagraha shows that the next name begins with the negative a- ('inconceivable'), not cintya ('conceivable').

The names

553 अग्रगण्या agra-gaṇyā

She who is to be counted the foremost

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound saptamī-tatpuruṣa. agra 'the front, the first place' stands in the locative to the gerundive gaṇyā 'to be counted': 'to be counted in the first place', foremost. gaṇyā is the head.

Analysis अग्रे गण्या अग्रगण्या
agre gaṇyā agragaṇyā

Significance Whenever beings are reckoned up, She is counted first: She precedes the gods themselves.

554 अचिन्त्यरूपा acintya-rūpā

She whose form is beyond the reach of thought

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner nañ-tatpuruṣa). (1) a-cintya 'not to be thought, inconceivable': a nañ-tatpuruṣa, the negative na appearing as a- before a consonant (a morphological replacement, Pāṇini 6.3.73 nalopo nañaḥ, not sound-sandhi). (2) A bahuvrīhi: 'She whose form is inconceivable'; rūpa takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis न चिन्त्यम् अचिन्त्यम्; अचिन्त्यम् रूपम् यस्याः सा अचिन्त्यरूपा
na cintyam acintyam; acintyam rūpam yasyāḥ sā acintyarūpā

Significance Her true form cannot be made an object of the mind, which itself arises in Her; the Kena Upaniṣad says of Brahman that it is not what the mind thinks but that by which the mind thinks.

555 कलिकल्मषनाशिनी kali-kalmaṣa-nāśinī

She who destroys the sins of the Kali age

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (with an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) kali-kalmaṣa 'the impurities of the Kali age' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) nāśinī 'she who destroys' is the head and takes them as object in the genitive.

Analysis कलेः कल्मषाणि कलिकल्मषाणि; कलिकल्मषाणाम् नाशिनी कलिकल्मषनाशिनी
kaleḥ kalmaṣāṇi kalikalmaṣāṇi; kalikalmaṣāṇām nāśinī kalikalmaṣanāśinī

Significance The faults peculiar to the Kali age (impurity, forgetfulness of dharma, strife) are cleansed by the remembrance of Her names, traditionally the chief means for this age.

556 कात्यायनी kātyāyanī

She who is Kātyāyanī, daughter of the sage Kātyāyana of Kata's line

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance In the Purāṇas the Goddess born from the united radiance of the gods to slay Mahiṣa was first worshipped by, or born in the hermitage of, the sage Kātyāyana, and so is called Kātyāyanī; She is the Durgā of the Devī-Māhātmya.

Uncertain Purāṇic accounts differ on whether She was born in Kātyāyana's hermitage or first worshipped by him; the derivation from Kata is standard grammar.

557 कालहन्त्री kāla-hantrī

She who is the destroyer of time (death)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. hantrī 'slayer' is an agent noun (hantṛ, feminine -ī) and the head; kāla is its object in the genitive.

Analysis कालस्य हन्त्री कालहन्त्री
kālasya hantrī kālahantrī

Significance For Her devotee She ends death; at the great dissolution She withdraws time itself, which devours all else.

558 कमलाक्षनिषेविता kamalākṣa-niṣevitā

She who is served and worshipped by lotus-eyed Viṣṇu

Sandhi कमलाक्ष = कमल + अक्ष (kamala + akṣa) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (with an inner bahuvrīhi). (1) kamalākṣa 'he whose eyes are like lotuses', Viṣṇu: a bahuvrīhi in which akṣi 'eye' becomes akṣa (the compound-final suffix ṣac, Pāṇini 5.4.113 bahuvrīhau sakthyakṣṇoḥ svāṅgāt ṣac). (2) He stands in the instrumental to the participle niṣevitā 'served, resorted to', which is the head.

Analysis कमले इव अक्षिणी यस्य सः कमलाक्षः; कमलाक्षेण निषेविता कमलाक्षनिषेविता
kamale iva akṣiṇī yasya saḥ kamalākṣaḥ; kamalākṣeṇa niṣevitā kamalākṣaniṣevitā

Significance Viṣṇu Himself attends on Her; traditionally He is counted among Her worshippers, and the power by which He preserves the world is Hers.

Śloka 114names 559–565

ताम्बूलपूरितमुखी दाडिमीकुसुमप्रभा ।
मृगाक्षी मोहिनी मुख्या मृडानी मित्ररूपिणी ॥ ११४ ॥

tāmbūlapūritamukhī dāḍimīkusumaprabhā |
mṛgākṣī mohinī mukhyā mṛḍānī mitrarūpiṇī || 114 ||

The names, separated

559ताम्बूल-पूरित-मुखीtāmbūla-pūrita-mukhī560दाडिमी-कुसुम-प्रभाdāḍimī-kusuma-prabhā

561मृगाक्षीmṛgākṣī562मोहिनीmohinī563मुख्याmukhyā564मृडानीmṛḍānī565मित्र-रूपिणीmitra-rūpiṇī

Translation

559She whose mouth is filled with betel; 560She who shines like a pomegranate flower;

561She whose eyes are long and beautiful like those of a doe; 562She who is enchanting; 563She who is the first; 564She who is the wife of Mṛḍa (Śiva); 565She who has the form of a friend (to all beings).

SanskritEnglish

ताम्बूलtāmbūlabetel (the rolled betel leaf with areca and spices)

Where the names meet

Names 559–561 return briefly to Her physical beauty (betel-filled mouth, pomegranate-red complexion, doe's eyes) amid names of Her power.

The names

559 ताम्बूलपूरितमुखी tāmbūla-pūrita-mukhī

She whose mouth is filled with betel

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (1) tāmbūla-pūrita 'filled with betel' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa: tāmbūla is the instrument of the participle pūrita). (2) A bahuvrīhi with mukha 'mouth': 'She whose mouth is filled with betel'. A bahuvrīhi ending in a body-part word takes the feminine -ī (Pāṇini 4.1.54 svāṅgāc copasarjanād asaṃyogopadhāt), hence mukhī.

Analysis ताम्बूलेन पूरितम् ताम्बूलपूरितम्; ताम्बूलपूरितम् मुखम् यस्याः सा ताम्बूलपूरितमुखी
tāmbūlena pūritam tāmbūlapūritam; tāmbūlapūritam mukham yasyāḥ sā tāmbūlapūritamukhī

Significance The red betel deepens the crimson of Her lips (name 24), and its camphor fragrance is the theme of name 26; in Her worship tāmbūla is offered among the closing courtly attentions.

560 दाडिमीकुसुमप्रभा dāḍimī-kusuma-prabhā

She who shines like a pomegranate flower

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi of resemblance (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) dāḍimī-kusuma 'the pomegranate flower' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) A bahuvrīhi of resemblance: 'She whose radiance is (like) the radiance of the pomegranate flower'. prabhā is already feminine.

Analysis दाडिम्याः कुसुमम् दाडिमीकुसुमम्; दाडिमीकुसुमस्य प्रभा इव प्रभा यस्याः सा दाडिमीकुसुमप्रभा
dāḍimyāḥ kusumam dāḍimīkusumam; dāḍimīkusumasya prabhā iva prabhā yasyāḥ sā dāḍimīkusumaprabhā

Significance The pomegranate blossom is a deep scarlet: Her complexion is the rosy red (aruṇa) of the meditation verses, the color of compassion.

561 मृगाक्षी mṛgākṣī

She whose eyes are long and beautiful like those of a doe

Sandhi मृगाक्षी = मृग + अक्षी (mṛga + akṣī) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (of comparison). A bahuvrīhi of comparison: 'She whose eyes are like a deer's'. akṣi 'eye' becomes -akṣa at the end of the bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 5.4.113) and then takes the feminine -ī: mṛgākṣī.

Analysis मृगस्य अक्षिणी इव अक्षिणी यस्याः सा मृगाक्षी
mṛgasya akṣiṇī iva akṣiṇī yasyāḥ sā mṛgākṣī

Significance The doe's eye is the classical image of eyes that are large, long and gently restless.

562 मोहिनी mohinī

She who is enchanting

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance She enchants all by Her beauty and, as Mahāmāyā, casts the spell by which the world forgets itself. Traditionally the Mohinī form Viṣṇu took at the churning of the ocean is regarded as Hers.

563 मुख्या mukhyā

She who is the first

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance She stands at the head of all: the first of the gods and the source from which they come.

564 मृडानी mṛḍānī

She who is the wife of Mṛḍa (Śiva)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Mṛḍa means 'the gracious one', from √mṛḍ 'to be kind': as His consort She is the grace by which Śiva blesses.

565 मित्ररूपिणी mitra-rūpiṇī

She who has the form of a friend (to all beings)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya (identification) with the possessive suffix -in. mitra-rūpa 'the form of a friend' (karmadhāraya of identification), with the possessive -in and feminine -ī: 'She who has the form of a friend'. mitra (neuter) is 'friend'; the masculine Mitra is the sun-god, one of the Ādityas, and the name allows that reading too.

Analysis मित्रम् एव रूपम् मित्ररूपम्; मित्ररूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति मित्ररूपिणी
mitram eva rūpam mitrarūpam; mitrarūpam asyāḥ asti iti mitrarūpiṇī

Significance She is the friend of the whole world, wishing good to all without being asked; traditionally the name is also read as Her being the sun (Mitra), one of the twelve Ādityas.

Śloka 115names 566–571

नित्यतृप्ता भक्तनिधिर् नियन्त्री निखिलेश्वरी ।
मैत्र्यादिवासनालभ्या महाप्रलयसाक्षिणी ॥ ११५ ॥

nityatṛptā bhaktanidhir niyantrī nikhileśvarī |
maitryādivāsanālabhyā mahāpralayasākṣiṇī || 115 ||

The names, separated ° form as a name on its own; in the recitation above it joins its neighbour

566नित्य-तृप्ताnitya-tṛptā567भक्त-निधिः°bhakta-nidhiḥ568नियन्त्रीniyantrī569निखिलेश्वरीnikhileśvarī

570मैत्र्यादि-वासना-लभ्याmaitryādi-vāsanā-labhyā571महा-प्रलय-साक्षिणीmahā-pralaya-sākṣiṇī

Translation

566She who is eternally contented; 567She who is the treasure of the devotees; 568She who controls and governs all beings; 569She who is the ruler of all;

570She who is attained through friendliness and the other good dispositions; 571She who is witness to the great dissolution.

Where the names meet

भक्तनिधिर्नियन्त्री = भक्तनिधिः + नियन्त्री (bhaktanidhiḥ + niyantrī) — visarga becomes r before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ)

Name 570 refers to the four attitudes of Yoga Sūtra 1.33 (friendliness, compassion, gladness, equanimity).

The names

566 नित्यतृप्ता nitya-tṛptā

She who is eternally contented

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya (nitya used adverbially). nitya 'always' qualifies the participle tṛptā 'contented', which is the head: 'ever contented'.

Analysis नित्यम् तृप्ता नित्यतृप्ता
nityam tṛptā nityatṛptā

Significance Lacking nothing, She needs nothing; She accepts offerings for the devotee's sake, not Her own.

567 भक्तनिधिः bhakta-nidhiḥ

She who is the treasure of the devotees

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. nidhi 'treasure' is the head and the devotees stand to it in the genitive: 'the treasure of the devotees'. nidhi is masculine and keeps its form in a name of the Goddess (in apposition).

Analysis भक्तानाम् निधिः भक्तनिधिः
bhaktānām nidhiḥ bhaktanidhiḥ

Significance To Her devotees She is the inexhaustible store from which every good, worldly and spiritual, is drawn.

568 नियन्त्री niyantrī

She who controls and governs all beings

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance As the inner controller (antaryāmin) She directs every being from within and keeps it on its course.

569 निखिलेश्वरी nikhileśvarī

She who is the ruler of all

Sandhi निखिलेश्वरी = निखिल + ईश्वरी (nikhila + īśvarī) — guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. īśvarī 'sovereign' is the head and nikhila 'all, the whole' stands to it in the genitive: 'the ruler of all'.

Analysis निखिलस्य ईश्वरी निखिलेश्वरी
nikhilasya īśvarī nikhileśvarī

Significance Nothing lies outside Her rule: She is sovereign over the whole, without remainder.

570 मैत्र्यादिवासनालभ्या maitryādi-vāsanā-labhyā

She who is attained through friendliness and the other good dispositions

Sandhi मैत्र्यादि = मैत्री + आदि (maitrī + ādi) — yaṇ: ī becomes y before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner bahuvrīhi and karmadhāraya). (1) maitry-ādi 'those beginning with friendliness' (bahuvrīhi in -ādi). (2) These qualify vāsanā 'dispositions, cultivated attitudes' (karmadhāraya). (3) The gerundive labhyā 'attainable' is the head; the dispositions are its instrument: 'attainable through friendliness and the other dispositions'.

Analysis मैत्री आदिः यासाम् ताः मैत्र्यादयः; मैत्र्यादयः वासनाः मैत्र्यादिवासनाः; मैत्र्यादिवासनाभिः लभ्या मैत्र्यादिवासनालभ्या
maitrī ādiḥ yāsām tāḥ maitryādayaḥ; maitryādayaḥ vāsanāḥ maitryādivāsanāḥ; maitryādivāsanābhiḥ labhyā maitryādivāsanālabhyā

Significance The four are those of Yoga Sūtra 1.33: friendliness toward the happy, compassion toward the suffering, gladness toward the virtuous and equanimity toward the wicked, by which the mind becomes clear; a mind so cleared finds Her.

571 महाप्रलयसाक्षिणी mahā-pralaya-sākṣiṇī

She who is witness to the great dissolution

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (with an inner karmadhāraya). (1) mahā-pralaya 'the great dissolution' (karmadhāraya; mahat becomes mahā- before a co-referential member, Pāṇini 6.3.46). (2) sākṣiṇī 'witness' is the head and takes the dissolution in the genitive.

Analysis महान् प्रलयः महाप्रलयः; महाप्रलयस्य साक्षिणी महाप्रलयसाक्षिणी
mahān pralayaḥ mahāpralayaḥ; mahāpralayasya sākṣiṇī mahāpralayasākṣiṇī

Significance When all the worlds and even the gods are dissolved, She alone remains, watching; compare name 232, where She witnesses Śiva's great dance at the end of the aeon.

Śloka 116names 572–577

परा शक्तिः परा निष्ठा प्रज्ञानघनरूपिणी ।
माध्वीपानालसा मत्ता मातृकावर्णरूपिणी ॥ ११६ ॥

parā śaktiḥ parā niṣṭhā prajñānaghanarūpiṇī |
mādhvīpānālasā mattā mātṛkāvarṇarūpiṇī || 116 ||

The names, separated

572परा-शक्तिःparā-śaktiḥ573परा-निष्ठाparā-niṣṭhā574प्रज्ञान-घन-रूपिणीprajñāna-ghana-rūpiṇī

575माध्वी-पानालसाmādhvī-pānālasā576मत्ताmattā577मातृका-वर्ण-रूपिणीmātṛkā-varṇa-rūpiṇī

Translation

572She who is the supreme Power (Parā Śakti); 573She who is the supreme end, the supreme abidance; 574She whose form is a solid mass of pure consciousness;

575She who is languid from drinking honey-wine; 576She who is intoxicated; 577She who is in the form of the letters of the alphabet.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish
572 पराशक्तिः parā-śaktiḥ
पराparāsupreme, highest, beyond allfeminine of para, agreeing with śaktiḥ. Not a compound but a phrase of two words: the adjective parā agrees with the noun, and the pair is counted as one name. Had they been compounded as a karmadhāraya, the feminine parā would normally return to the masculine stem (puṃvadbhāva, Pāṇini 6.3.42): para-. The verse text accordingly prints them as two words.
शक्तिःśaktiḥpower, energy√śak 'to be able'; feminine i-stem, nominative singular
573 परानिष्ठा parā-niṣṭhā
पराparāsupreme, highestfeminine of para, agreeing with niṣṭhā; as in name 572 the two words stand in agreement and are not compounded (a karmadhāraya would normally give para-).
निष्ठाniṣṭhāculmination, final goal; firm ground, steadfast abidingni + √sthā 'to stand'

पानpānadrinking√pā 'to drink'
अलसाalasālanguid, indolent, slowa- 'not' + lasa 'lively', feminine

मातृकाmātṛkāmātṛkā, the 'little mothers': the letters of the Sanskrit alphabet as the matrix of all speech and mantra
वर्णvarṇaletter, sound; also color

Where the names meet

Names 572 and 573 are each written as two words, parā śaktiḥ and parā niṣṭhā: adjective and noun in agreement, each pair counted as one name. Name 575: divide pāna + alasā ('languid from drinking').

The names

572 पराशक्तिः parā-śaktiḥ

She who is the supreme Power (Parā Śakti)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance The one power inseparable from Śiva, from which the powers of will, knowledge and action (name 658) and every lesser power proceed.

Uncertain Phrase or compound: the retained feminine parā and the verse's spacing point to two words in agreement (no samāsa); in later usage Parāśakti is also treated as a fixed compound title.

573 परानिष्ठा parā-niṣṭhā

She who is the supreme end, the supreme abidance

Sandhi निष्ठा = नि + स्था (ni + sthā) — after a prefix ending in i, the s of sthā becomes ṣ (Pāṇini 8.3.65), and th then becomes ṭh by retroflex assimilation (8.4.41 ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ), inside the word niṣṭhā

Compound not a compound

Significance She is the culmination in which every path comes to rest: the Gītā (3.3) speaks of two kinds of niṣṭhā, of knowledge and of action, and both end in Her.

Uncertain Phrase or compound, as with name 572: the feminine parā is kept, so the name is read as two words in agreement.

574 प्रज्ञानघनरूपिणी prajñāna-ghana-rūpiṇī

She whose form is a solid mass of pure consciousness

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya (identification) with the possessive suffix -in (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) prajñāna-ghana 'a solid mass of consciousness' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, like saindhava-ghana 'a lump of salt'). (2) It is identified with rūpa 'form' (karmadhāraya). (3) The possessive -in and feminine -ī: 'She whose form is a solid mass of consciousness'.

Analysis प्रज्ञानस्य घनः प्रज्ञानघनः; प्रज्ञानघनः एव रूपम् प्रज्ञानघनरूपम्; प्रज्ञानघनरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति प्रज्ञानघनरूपिणी
prajñānasya ghanaḥ prajñānaghanaḥ; prajñānaghanaḥ eva rūpam prajñānaghanarūpam; prajñānaghanarūpam asyāḥ asti iti prajñānaghanarūpiṇī

Significance The phrase is Upaniṣadic: the Bṛhadāraṇyaka (4.5.13) says that as a lump of salt is salt throughout, so the Self is prajñānaghana, consciousness through and through, with no inside or outside; the Māṇḍūkya (5) uses the same word.

Corrected प्रज्ञानघनरुपिणी → प्रज्ञानघनरूपिणी. रुपिणी → रूपिणी.

575 माध्वीपानालसा mādhvī-pānālasā

She who is languid from drinking honey-wine

Sandhi पानालसा = पान + अलसा (pāna + alasā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (with an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) mādhvī-pāna 'the drinking of honey-wine' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) alasā 'languid' is the head and the drinking is its cause, in the instrumental: 'languid from drinking honey-wine'.

Analysis माध्व्याः पानम् माध्वीपानम्; माध्वीपानेन अलसा माध्वीपानालसा
mādhvyāḥ pānam mādhvīpānam; mādhvīpānena alasā mādhvīpānālasā

Significance Traditionally read inwardly: the wine is the bliss of the Self, and Her languor is the absence of all striving, since for Her nothing remains to be gained.

576 मत्ता mattā

She who is intoxicated

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Traditionally, the intoxication is the bliss of Her own Self, which needs nothing outside it.

577 मातृकावर्णरूपिणी mātṛkā-varṇa-rūpiṇī

She who is in the form of the letters of the alphabet

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya (identification) with the possessive suffix -in (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) mātṛkā-varṇa 'the letters that are the mātṛkā' (karmadhāraya; a genitive reading, 'the letters of the mātṛkā', comes to the same). (2) Identified with rūpa 'form'. (3) The possessive -in and feminine -ī: 'She whose form is the letters of the mātṛkā'.

Analysis मातृकाः एव वर्णाः मातृकावर्णाः; मातृकावर्णाः एव रूपम् मातृकावर्णरूपम्; मातृकावर्णरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति मातृकावर्णरूपिणी
mātṛkāḥ eva varṇāḥ mātṛkāvarṇāḥ; mātṛkāvarṇāḥ eva rūpam mātṛkāvarṇarūpam; mātṛkāvarṇarūpam asyāḥ asti iti mātṛkāvarṇarūpiṇī

Significance The mātṛkā are the fifty letters from a to kṣa; in mātṛkā-nyāsa they are placed on the worshipper's body as on Hers, since every mantra and every word is made of them.

Śloka 117names 578–582

महनीया दयामूर्तिर् महासाम्राज्यशालिनी ॥ ११७ ॥

mahākailāsanilayā mṛṇālamṛdudorlatā |
mahanīyā dayāmūrtir mahāsāmrājyaśālinī || 117 ||

Where the names meet

दयामूर्तिर्महासाम्राज्य = दयामूर्तिः + महासाम्राज्य… (dayāmūrtiḥ + mahāsāmrājya…) — visarga becomes r before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ)

Name 579: dorlatā is dos 'arm' + latā 'creeper'; the r is the s of dos before l.

The names

578 महाकैलासनिलया mahā-kailāsa-nilayā

She who dwells in the great Kailāsa

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) mahā-kailāsa 'the great Kailāsa' (karmadhāraya; mahat becomes mahā-, Pāṇini 6.3.46). (2) A bahuvrīhi with nilaya 'dwelling': 'She whose dwelling is the great Kailāsa'; nilaya takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis महान् कैलासः महाकैलासः; महाकैलासः निलयः यस्याः सा महाकैलासनिलया
mahān kailāsaḥ mahākailāsaḥ; mahākailāsaḥ nilayaḥ yasyāḥ sā mahākailāsanilayā

Significance Mahākailāsa is traditionally the supreme abode of Śiva and Śakti, beyond the earthly mountain; inwardly it is placed at the crown of the head.

579 मृणालमृदुदोर्लता mṛṇāla-mṛdu-dorlatā

She whose creeper-like arms are as soft as lotus stalks

Sandhi दोर्लता = दोस् + लता (dos + latā) — final s becomes r (ru) before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ); the r stays before l

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an upamita-karmadhāraya and an upamāna-karmadhāraya). (1) dor-latā 'an arm (slender) as a creeper': the thing compared comes first and the standard second (upamita-karmadhāraya, Pāṇini 2.1.56). (2) mṛṇāla-mṛdu 'soft as a lotus stalk': standard of comparison + shared quality (upamāna-karmadhāraya, Pāṇini 2.1.55). (3) A bahuvrīhi: 'She whose creeper-like arms are soft as lotus stalks'. The feminine mṛdvī appears as the stem mṛdu (puṃvadbhāva); latā is already feminine. The singular stands for the class: She has four arms (name 7).

Analysis दोः लता इव दोर्लता; मृणालम् इव मृदु मृणालमृदु; मृणालमृद्वी दोर्लता यस्याः सा मृणालमृदुदोर्लता
doḥ latā iva dorlatā; mṛṇālam iva mṛdu mṛṇālamṛdu; mṛṇālamṛdvī dorlatā yasyāḥ sā mṛṇālamṛdudorlatā

Significance Her four arms are slender and graceful like creepers and tender like the lotus stalk, a stock image of classical poetry.

580 महनीया mahanīyā

She who is worthy of adoration

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Being greatest, She alone is wholly worthy of worship; traditionally all honor offered anywhere is said to reach Her in the end.

581 दयामूर्तिः dayā-mūrtiḥ

She who is the personification of compassion

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (alternatively bahuvrīhi). As a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, mūrti 'embodiment' is the head: 'the embodiment of compassion'. As a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose form is compassion'. mūrti is feminine, so the form is the same either way.

Analysis दयायाः मूर्तिः दयामूर्तिः; अथवा दया मूर्तिः यस्याः सा दयामूर्तिः
dayāyāḥ mūrtiḥ dayāmūrtiḥ; athavā dayā mūrtiḥ yasyāḥ sā dayāmūrtiḥ

Significance She took form at all only out of compassion, appearing from the fire for the gods' sake (names 4–5); compassion is Her very body.

582 महासाम्राज्यशालिनी mahā-sāmrājya-śālinī

She who possesses the great empire, sovereign over all

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (with an inner karmadhāraya). (1) mahā-sāmrājya 'great sovereignty, the great empire' (karmadhāraya; mahat → mahā-, Pāṇini 6.3.46). (2) śālinī 'possessed of, resplendent with' is the head and takes the empire in the instrumental.

Analysis महत् साम्राज्यम् महासाम्राज्यम्; महासाम्राज्येन शालिनी महासाम्राज्यशालिनी
mahat sāmrājyam mahāsāmrājyam; mahāsāmrājyena śālinī mahāsāmrājyaśālinī

Significance Her empire is the whole of creation: the worlds, their gods and their guardians are within Her rule.

Śloka 118names 583–589

आत्मविद्या महाविद्या श्रीविद्या कामसेविता ।
श्रीषोडशाक्षरीविद्या त्रिकूटा कामकोटिका ॥ ११८ ॥

ātmavidyā mahāvidyā śrīvidyā kāmasevitā |
śrīṣoḍaśākṣarīvidyā trikūṭā kāmakoṭikā || 118 ||

The names, separated

583आत्म-विद्याātma-vidyā584महा-विद्याmahā-vidyā585श्री-विद्याśrī-vidyā586काम-सेविताkāma-sevitā

587श्री-षोडशाक्षरी-विद्याśrī-ṣoḍaśākṣarī-vidyā588त्रि-कूटाtri-kūṭā589काम-कोटिकाkāma-koṭikā

Where the names meet

Names 583–589 are names of the mantra: the Vidyās, the sixteen-syllable Ṣoḍaśī, the three kūṭas of the Pañcadaśī.

The names

583 आत्मविद्या ātma-vidyā

She who is the knowledge of the Self

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. vidyā 'knowledge' is the head and ātman 'the Self' stands to it in the genitive: 'knowledge of the Self'. ātman drops its final n in composition.

Analysis आत्मनः विद्या आत्मविद्या
ātmanaḥ vidyā ātmavidyā

Significance She is the knowledge of the Self taught in the Upaniṣads, which the Gītā (10.32) calls the foremost of all knowledges.

584 महाविद्या mahā-vidyā

She who is the great knowledge

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya. mahatī 'great' qualifies vidyā; the feminine adjective takes the masculine stem (puṃvadbhāva, Pāṇini 6.3.42) and mahat becomes mahā- (6.3.46), as in name 2.

Analysis महती विद्या महाविद्या
mahatī vidyā mahāvidyā

Significance In the Tantras mahāvidyā is the great mantra-knowledge, and the name is given to the ten Wisdom Goddesses (daśa mahāvidyā), all regarded as Her forms.

585 श्रीविद्या śrī-vidyā

She who is Śrīvidyā, the auspicious knowledge (the Pañcadaśī mantra)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya (alternatively ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). As a karmadhāraya, śrī qualifies vidyā: 'the auspicious knowledge'. As a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa: 'the knowledge (mantra) of Śrī', the Goddess. vidyā is the head either way.

Analysis श्रीः विद्या श्रीविद्या; अथवा श्रियः विद्या श्रीविद्या
śrīḥ vidyā śrīvidyā; athavā śriyaḥ vidyā śrīvidyā

Significance Śrīvidyā names both Her fifteen-syllable mantra, the Pañcadaśī, and the whole tradition of Her worship; the mantra is Her subtle body (names 85–89).

586 कामसेविता kāma-sevitā

She who is worshipped by Kāmadeva

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa. Kāma stands in the instrumental to the participle sevitā 'worshipped', which is the head: 'worshipped by Kāma'.

Analysis कामेन सेविता कामसेविता
kāmena sevitā kāmasevitā

Significance Kāma, revived by Her after Śiva's eye burned him (name 84), is traditionally counted among the twelve great worshippers of Śrīvidyā, and the kādi form of the Pañcadaśī is called the Kāmarāja-vidyā after him. Compare name 375, kāmapūjitā.

587 श्रीषोडशाक्षरीविद्या śrī-ṣoḍaśākṣarī-vidyā

She who is the auspicious sixteen-syllable Vidyā (the Ṣoḍaśī mantra)

Sandhi षोडशाक्षरी = षोडश + अक्षरी (ṣoḍaśa + akṣarī) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound karmadhāraya (over an inner samāhāra-dvigu). (1) ṣoḍaśākṣarī 'the group of sixteen syllables': a collective numeral compound (samāhāra-dvigu); a dvigu ending in -a takes the feminine -ī (Pāṇini 4.1.21 dvigoḥ). (2) It stands in apposition to vidyā 'mantra' (karmadhāraya): 'the sixteen-syllable mantra'. Being a collective noun, not an adjective, it keeps its -ī. (3) śrī qualifies the whole as in names 1–3.

Analysis षोडशानाम् अक्षराणाम् समाहारः षोडशाक्षरी; षोडशाक्षरी विद्या षोडशाक्षरीविद्या; श्रीः षोडशाक्षरीविद्या श्रीषोडशाक्षरीविद्या
ṣoḍaśānām akṣarāṇām samāhāraḥ ṣoḍaśākṣarī; ṣoḍaśākṣarī vidyā ṣoḍaśākṣarīvidyā; śrīḥ ṣoḍaśākṣarīvidyā śrīṣoḍaśākṣarīvidyā

Significance Traditionally the Ṣoḍaśī is the Pañcadaśī completed by a sixteenth seed-syllable (śrīṃ), the highest form of Her mantra, imparted only at the final initiation.

Uncertain The composition of the Ṣoḍaśī (which syllable completes the Pañcadaśī, and where it is placed) differs between lineages; the significance gives the commonest account.

588 त्रिकूटा tri-kūṭā

She who has three sections (the three kūṭas of the Pañcadaśī mantra)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. A bahuvrīhi with a numeral first member: 'She who has three kūṭas'. kūṭa takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis त्रयः कूटाः यस्याः सा त्रिकूटा
trayaḥ kūṭāḥ yasyāḥ sā trikūṭā

Significance The Pañcadaśī falls into three kūṭas, vāgbhava, kāmarāja and śakti, which are Her face, Her middle body and the body below the waist (names 85–87); traditionally every triad (the three worlds, guṇas, states, deities) is read in them.

589 कामकोटिका kāma-koṭikā

She of whom Kāma (Kāmeśvara, Śiva) is but a part

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (with the suffix -ka). A bahuvrīhi, 'She of whom Kāma is a koṭi (a portion)', with the optional bahuvrīhi suffix -ka (kap, Pāṇini 5.4.154 śeṣād vibhāṣā) and the feminine -ā. Kāma here is Kāmeśvara, Śiva as Her lover.

Analysis कामः कोटिः यस्याः सा कामकोटिका
kāmaḥ koṭiḥ yasyāḥ sā kāmakoṭikā

Significance Even Kāmeśvara, Her consort, is a portion of Her: Śiva and Śakti are one, and the whole is Hers.

Uncertain koṭi has several senses (portion, extremity, ten million), and the name is also read as 'She who dwells at Kāmakoṭi', the pīṭha at Kāñcī. The meaning follows the reading of Kāma as a part of Her.

शिरःस्थिता चन्द्रनिभा भालस्थेन्द्रधनुःप्रभा ॥ ११९ ॥

kaṭākṣakiṅkarībhūtakamalākoṭisevitā |
śiraḥsthitā candranibhā bhālasthendradhanuḥprabhā || 119 ||

590She who is attended by millions of Lakṣmīs who have become handmaids of Her side-glance;

Where the names meet

भालस्थेन्द्र = भालस्था + इन्द्र… (bhālasthā + indra…) — guṇa: ā + i → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Divide bhālasthā + indradhanuḥprabhā. Names 591–597 (into śloka 120) place Her at four points for meditation: in the head like the moon, at the brow like the rainbow, in the heart like the sun, in the triangle as a lamp.

The names

590 कटाक्षकिङ्करीभूतकमलाकोटिसेविता kaṭākṣa-kiṅkarī-bhūta-kamalā-koṭi-sevitā

She who is attended by millions of Lakṣmīs who have become handmaids of Her side-glance

Sandhi कटाक्ष = कट + अक्ष (kaṭa + akṣa) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ), inside the lexicalised compound kaṭākṣa 'side-glance'

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner cvi-compound, ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣas and a karmadhāraya). (1) kiṅkarī-bhūta 'become handmaids' (those who were not handmaids have become so): the cvi construction with √bhū (Pāṇini 5.4.50), whose -ī also replaces a final a (7.4.32 asya cvau), so the surface is the same whether one starts from kiṅkara or the feminine kiṅkarī. (2) kaṭākṣa-kiṅkarībhūta 'become handmaids of (Her) side-glance' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) kamalā-koṭi 'millions of Lakṣmīs' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa), qualified by (2) (karmadhāraya). (4) The participle sevitā 'served' is the head of the whole and takes them in the instrumental.

Analysis अकिङ्कर्यः किङ्कर्यः भूताः किङ्करीभूताः; कटाक्षस्य किङ्करीभूताः कटाक्षकिङ्करीभूताः; कमलानाम् कोटयः कमलाकोटयः; कटाक्षकिङ्करीभूताः कमलाकोटयः कटाक्षकिङ्करीभूतकमलाकोटयः; ताभिः सेविता कटाक्षकिङ्करीभूतकमलाकोटिसेविता
akiṅkaryaḥ kiṅkaryaḥ bhūtāḥ kiṅkarībhūtāḥ; kaṭākṣasya kiṅkarībhūtāḥ kaṭākṣakiṅkarībhūtāḥ; kamalānām koṭayaḥ kamalākoṭayaḥ; kaṭākṣakiṅkarībhūtāḥ kamalākoṭayaḥ kaṭākṣakiṅkarībhūtakamalākoṭayaḥ; tābhiḥ sevitā kaṭākṣakiṅkarībhūtakamalākoṭisevitā

Significance A single glance from Her brings forth fortune upon fortune: countless Lakṣmīs wait on that glance as servants. Traditionally, a mere glance of Her grace makes the devotee prosperous.

Uncertain kaṭākṣa may be taken in the genitive ('handmaids of Her glance') or the instrumental ('made handmaids by Her glance'); the image is the same.

Corrected कटाक्षकिङ्करीभुतकमलाकोटिसेविता → कटाक्षकिङ्करीभूतकमलाकोटिसेविता. भुत → भूत (bhūta: long ū); the IAST was already right.

591 शिरःस्थिता śiraḥ-sthitā

She who resides in the head

Sandhi शिरःस्थिता = शिरस् + स्थिता (śiras + sthitā) — final s becomes visarga (Pāṇini 8.2.66 with 8.3.15), and the visarga stays before a sibilant followed by a hard consonant (8.3.35 śarpare visarjanīyaḥ)

Compound saptamī-tatpuruṣa. The participle sthitā 'abiding' is the head and śiras 'head' stands to it in the locative: 'abiding in the head'.

Analysis शिरसि स्थिता शिरःस्थिता
śirasi sthitā śiraḥsthitā

Significance Names 591–597 place Her at four points of the body for meditation; here, at the crown of the head, She is meditated on as shining like the moon (name 592).

592 चन्द्रनिभा candra-nibhā

She who is resplendent like the moon

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi of resemblance. nibhā 'luster, appearance' (at the end of a compound, 'resembling'): 'She whose luster is like the moon's'. Read with nibha as an adjective, 'like the moon', the sense is the same.

Analysis चन्द्रस्य निभा इव निभा यस्याः सा चन्द्रनिभा
candrasya nibhā iva nibhā yasyāḥ sā candranibhā

Significance Meditated on in the head (name 591), She is cool and white like the full moon, the nectar-giving light at the crown.

593 भालस्था bhāla-sthā

She who resides in the forehead (between the eyebrows)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. -stha 'standing, abiding' is formed from √sthā with the suffix ka when a noun precedes (Pāṇini 3.2.4 supi sthaḥ), and takes the feminine -ā; bhāla 'forehead' is its locative complement: 'She who abides in the forehead'.

Analysis भाले तिष्ठति इति भालस्था
bhāle tiṣṭhati iti bhālasthā

Significance At the brow, the place of the ājñā center, She is meditated on as shining with the colors of the rainbow (name 594).

594 इन्द्रधनुःप्रभा indra-dhanuḥ-prabhā

She who is resplendent like the rainbow

Sandhi धनुःप्रभा = धनुस् + प्रभा (dhanus + prabhā) — final s becomes visarga before a hard consonant (Pāṇini 8.2.66 with 8.3.15 kharavasānayor visarjanīyaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi of resemblance (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) indra-dhanus 'Indra's bow', the rainbow (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) A bahuvrīhi of resemblance: 'She whose radiance is like the radiance of the rainbow'.

Analysis इन्द्रस्य धनुः इन्द्रधनुः; इन्द्रधनुषः प्रभा इव प्रभा यस्याः सा इन्द्रधनुःप्रभा
indrasya dhanuḥ indradhanuḥ; indradhanuṣaḥ prabhā iva prabhā yasyāḥ sā indradhanuḥprabhā

Significance The rainbow holds every color at once: so, at the brow (name 593), She is seen in many hues.

Where the names meet

Names 598 and 600 recall the Dakṣa episode: Satī, Dakṣa's daughter, and the destruction of his sacrifice.

The names

595 हृदयस्था hṛdaya-sthā

She who resides in the heart

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. As in name 593: -stha from √sthā with ka (Pāṇini 3.2.4), feminine -ā, with hṛdaya 'heart' as its locative complement.

Analysis हृदये तिष्ठति इति हृदयस्था
hṛdaye tiṣṭhati iti hṛdayasthā

Significance In the heart, the seat of the Self, She is meditated on as shining like the sun (name 596).

596 रविप्रख्या ravi-prakhyā

She who shines like the sun

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi of resemblance. prakhyā 'brightness, appearance' (at the end of a compound, 'like'): 'She whose brightness is like the sun's'.

Analysis रवेः प्रख्या इव प्रख्या यस्याः सा रविप्रख्या
raveḥ prakhyā iva prakhyā yasyāḥ sā raviprakhyā

Significance In the heart (name 595) She is the inner sun that lights all experience.

597 त्रिकोणान्तरदीपिका tri-koṇāntara-dīpikā

She who shines as a light within the triangle

Sandhi कोणान्तर = कोण + अन्तर (koṇa + antara) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound saptamī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and bahuvrīhi). (1) tri-koṇa 'that which has three angles', the triangle (bahuvrīhi). (2) trikoṇa-antara 'the inside of the triangle' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) dīpikā 'lamp' is the head and the interior is its place, in the locative: 'the lamp within the triangle'.

Analysis त्रयः कोणाः यस्य तत् त्रिकोणम्; त्रिकोणस्य अन्तरम् त्रिकोणान्तरम्; त्रिकोणान्तरे दीपिका त्रिकोणान्तरदीपिका
trayaḥ koṇāḥ yasya tat trikoṇam; trikoṇasya antaram trikoṇāntaram; trikoṇāntare dīpikā trikoṇāntaradīpikā

Significance The triangle is traditionally both the one in the mūlādhāra where kuṇḍalinī rests and the innermost triangle of the Śrīcakra around the bindu; there She burns as a steady flame.

598 दाक्षायणी dākṣāyaṇī

She who is Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa Prajāpati

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance As Satī She was born to Dakṣa and gave up that body when he insulted Śiva at his sacrifice (name 600), to be born again as Pārvatī.

599 दैत्यहन्त्री daitya-hantrī

She who is the killer of demons

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. hantrī 'slayer' (agent noun) is the head and the daityas are its object in the genitive.

Analysis दैत्यानाम् हन्त्री दैत्यहन्त्री
daityānām hantrī daityahantrī

Significance As Durgā and Caṇḍikā, and as Lalitā against Bhaṇḍa, She destroys the powers hostile to the gods; inwardly, the demonic tendencies of the mind.

600 दक्षयज्ञविनाशिनी dakṣa-yajña-vināśinī

She who is the destroyer of Dakṣa's sacrifice

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (with an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) dakṣa-yajña 'Dakṣa's sacrifice' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) vināśinī 'destroyer' is the head and takes the sacrifice in the genitive.

Analysis दक्षस्य यज्ञः दक्षयज्ञः; दक्षयज्ञस्य विनाशिनी दक्षयज्ञविनाशिनी
dakṣasya yajñaḥ dakṣayajñaḥ; dakṣayajñasya vināśinī dakṣayajñavināśinī

Significance After Satī gave up her body at Dakṣa's sacrifice, Śiva's wrath, in the form of Vīrabhadra with Bhadrakālī, laid it waste; traditionally the episode warns against ritual performed without devotion to the Lord.

Śloka 121names 601–606

दरान्दोलितदीर्घाक्षी दरहासोज्ज्वलन्मुखी ।
गुरुमूर्तिर् गुणनिधिर् गोमाता गुहजन्मभूः ॥ १२१ ॥

darāndolitadīrghākṣī darahāsojjvalanmukhī |
gurumūrtir guṇanidhir gomātā guhajanmabhūḥ || 121 ||

The names, separated ° form as a name on its own; in the recitation above it joins its neighbour

601दरान्दोलित-दीर्घाक्षीdarāndolita-dīrghākṣī602दर-हासोज्ज्वलन्-मुखीdara-hāsojjvalan-mukhī

603गुरु-मूर्तिः°guru-mūrtiḥ604गुण-निधिः°guṇa-nidhiḥ605गो-माताgo-mātā606गुह-जन्म-भूःguha-janma-bhūḥ

Translation

601She whose long eyes are gently tremulous; 602She whose face shines with a gentle smile;

603She who has assumed the form of the guru; 604She who is the treasure house of all good qualities; 605She who is the mother of cows (as Surabhi, the wish-granting cow); 606She who is the source from which Guha (Skanda) was born.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish

Where the names meet

गुरुमूर्तिर्गुण = गुरुमूर्तिः + गुण… (gurumūrtiḥ + guṇa…) — visarga becomes r before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ)

गुणनिधिर्गोमाता = गुणनिधिः + गोमाता (guṇanidhiḥ + gomātā) — visarga becomes r before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ)

Names 601–602 return to Her eyes and smile, both qualified by dara 'gently'. Name 606 ends in the ū-stem bhū, so its nominative is -bhūḥ.

The names

601 दरान्दोलितदीर्घाक्षी darāndolita-dīrghākṣī

She whose long eyes are gently tremulous

Sandhi दरान्दोलित = दर + आन्दोलित (dara + āndolita) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); दीर्घाक्षी = दीर्घ + अक्षी (dīrgha + akṣī) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya with an adverbial first member). (1) dara-āndolita 'slightly moving': the indeclinable dara 'a little, gently' qualifies the participle āndolita 'swung, set in motion'. (2) A bahuvrīhi: 'She whose long eyes are gently moving'. akṣi 'eye' becomes -akṣa at the end of the bahuvrīhi (Pāṇini 5.4.113) and takes the feminine -ī.

Analysis दर आन्दोलिते दरान्दोलिते; दरान्दोलिते दीर्घे अक्षिणी यस्याः सा दरान्दोलितदीर्घाक्षी
dara āndolite darāndolite; darāndolite dīrghe akṣiṇī yasyāḥ sā darāndolitadīrghākṣī

Significance Her long eyes move only slightly as they rest on the devotees; traditionally every movement of Her eyes is an act of grace.

602 दरहासोज्ज्वलन्मुखी dara-hāsojjvalan-mukhī

She whose face shines with a gentle smile

Sandhi हासोज्ज्वल = हास + उज्ज्वल (hāsa + ujjvala) — guṇa: a + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ); उज्ज्वल = उद् + ज्वल (ud + jvala) — ścutva: d becomes j before j (Pāṇini 8.4.40 stoḥ ścunā ścuḥ), at the prefix junction ud + jval; उज्ज्वलन्मुखी = उज्ज्वलत् + मुखी (ujjvalat + mukhī) — a stop becomes the nasal of its class before a nasal: t → n before m (Pāṇini 8.4.45 yaro 'nunāsike 'nunāsiko vā)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya and tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (1) dara-hāsa 'a slight smile' (dara 'gently' qualifies hāsa). (2) darahāsa-ujjvalat 'shining with that smile' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa with the participle ujjvalat). (3) A bahuvrīhi with mukha 'face': 'She whose face shines with a gentle smile'; the body-part word takes the feminine -ī (Pāṇini 4.1.54).

Analysis दर हासः दरहासः; दरहासेन उज्ज्वलत् दरहासोज्ज्वलत्; दरहासोज्ज्वलत् मुखम् यस्याः सा दरहासोज्ज्वलन्मुखी
dara hāsaḥ darahāsaḥ; darahāsena ujjvalat darahāsojjvalat; darahāsojjvalat mukham yasyāḥ sā darahāsojjvalanmukhī

Significance The gentle smile (darahāsa) is the mark of Her grace and ease; the same smile appears in name 28 (mandasmita).

603 गुरुमूर्तिः guru-mūrtiḥ

She who has assumed the form of the guru

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (alternatively karmadhāraya). As a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose form is the guru', i.e. who takes the form of the teacher. As a karmadhāraya, guru is the adjective 'weighty, venerable, awesome' (feminine gurvī, reduced to guru- by puṃvadbhāva): 'the awe-inspiring form'. mūrti is feminine, so the name has the same form either way.

Analysis गुरुः मूर्तिः यस्याः सा गुरुमूर्तिः; अथवा गुर्वी मूर्तिः गुरुमूर्तिः
guruḥ mūrtiḥ yasyāḥ sā gurumūrtiḥ; athavā gurvī mūrtiḥ gurumūrtiḥ

Significance In Śrīvidyā the guru is not different from the Goddess and Śiva; it is She who teaches through the guru and who is received through him.

Uncertain Two compound analyses: bahuvrīhi ('whose form is the guru') and karmadhāraya ('the weighty, awesome form'). The meaning follows the first.

604 गुणनिधिः guṇa-nidhiḥ

She who is the treasure house of all good qualities

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. nidhi 'treasure, store' is the head and the qualities stand to it in the genitive. nidhi is masculine and keeps its form in a name of the Goddess, as in name 567.

Analysis गुणानाम् निधिः गुणनिधिः
guṇānām nidhiḥ guṇanidhiḥ

Significance Every excellence is stored in Her; traditionally the three guṇas from which the world is woven are also held in Her as their source.

605 गोमाता go-mātā

She who is the mother of cows (as Surabhi, the wish-granting cow)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. mātā 'mother' is the head and go 'cow' stands to it in the genitive: 'the mother of cows'.

Analysis गवाम् माता गोमाता
gavām mātā gomātā

Significance As Surabhi, the mother of all cattle and the wish-granting cow, She gives every desire; since go also means earth, speech, rays and the senses, She is mother of all of these.

606 गुहजन्मभूः guha-janma-bhūḥ

She who is the source from which Guha (Skanda) was born

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (with an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) guha-janman 'the birth of Guha' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; janman drops its final n in composition). (2) bhū 'ground, place of origin' is the head: 'the ground of Guha's birth'. bhū is a feminine ū-stem, so the nominative is bhūḥ.

Analysis गुहस्य जन्म गुहजन्म; गुहजन्मनः भूः गुहजन्मभूः
guhasya janma guhajanma; guhajanmanaḥ bhūḥ guhajanmabhūḥ

Significance She is the mother of Skanda, the commander of the gods' army; traditionally Guha, 'the hidden one', is also read as the Self hidden in the cave of the heart, which is born of Her.

Śloka 122names 607–610

देवेशी दण्डनीतिस्था दहराकाशरूपिणी ।
प्रतिपन्मुख्यराकान्ततिथिमण्डलपूजिता ॥ १२२ ॥

deveśī daṇḍanītisthā daharākāśarūpiṇī |
pratipanmukhyarākāntatithimaṇḍalapūjitā || 122 ||

The names, separated

607देवेशीdeveśī608दण्ड-नीति-स्थाdaṇḍa-nīti-sthā609दहराकाश-रूपिणीdaharākāśa-rūpiṇī

610प्रतिपन्-मुख्य-राकान्त-तिथि-मण्डल-पूजिताpratipan-mukhya-rākānta-tithi-maṇḍala-pūjitā

Translation

607She who is the ruler of the gods; 608She who abides in daṇḍanīti, the science of just rule; 609She whose form is the subtle space (daharākāśa) within the heart;

610She who is worshipped by the circle of lunar days, from the first day to the full moon.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish

देवdevagod

608 दण्डनीतिस्था daṇḍa-nīti-sthā
दण्डdaṇḍathe rod of authority; punishment
नीतिnīticonduct, policy, guidance√nī 'to lead'
स्थाsthāabiding in, upholding√sthā + ka (-stha), feminine -ā
609 दहराकाशरूपिणी daharākāśa-rūpiṇī
दहरdaharasmall, subtle

Where the names meet

Name 609 refers to the dahara-vidyā of the Chāndogya Upaniṣad (8.1.1); name 610 fills the whole second half and names the lunar days from pratipad to the full moon.

The names

607 देवेशी deveśī

She who is the ruler of the gods

Sandhi देवेशी = देव + ईशी (deva + īśī) — guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. īśī 'ruler, mistress' (feminine of īśa) is the head and the gods stand to it in the genitive.

Analysis देवानाम् ईशी देवेशी
devānām īśī deveśī

Significance The gods hold their offices under Her; ruling them, She also protects them.

608 दण्डनीतिस्था daṇḍa-nīti-sthā

She who abides in daṇḍanīti, the science of just rule

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (with an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) daṇḍa-nīti 'the conduct of the rod', the science of government and just punishment (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) -sthā 'abiding in' from √sthā with ka (Pāṇini 3.2.4 supi sthaḥ), feminine -ā: 'She who abides in daṇḍanīti'.

Analysis दण्डस्य नीतिः दण्डनीतिः; दण्डनीतौ तिष्ठति इति दण्डनीतिस्था
daṇḍasya nītiḥ daṇḍanītiḥ; daṇḍanītau tiṣṭhati iti daṇḍanītisthā

Significance Daṇḍanīti is counted with philosophy, the Vedas and economics among the four branches of knowledge (Arthaśāstra 1.2); She upholds the order of the world through just restraint, without error.

609 दहराकाशरूपिणी daharākāśa-rūpiṇī

She whose form is the subtle space (daharākāśa) within the heart

Sandhi दहराकाश = दहर + आकाश (dahara + ākāśa) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound karmadhāraya (identification) with the possessive suffix -in (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) dahara-ākāśa 'the small space' (karmadhāraya: dahara 'small, subtle' qualifies ākāśa). (2) It is identified with rūpa 'form'. (3) The possessive -in and feminine -ī: 'She whose form is the small space (within the heart)'.

Analysis दहरः आकाशः दहराकाशः; दहराकाशः एव रूपम् दहराकाशरूपम्; दहराकाशरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति दहराकाशरूपिणी
daharaḥ ākāśaḥ daharākāśaḥ; daharākāśaḥ eva rūpam daharākāśarūpam; daharākāśarūpam asyāḥ asti iti daharākāśarūpiṇī

Significance The Chāndogya Upaniṣad (8.1.1) teaches meditation on the small space within the lotus of the heart, and the Brahma Sūtra (1.3.14) shows that this 'small' is Brahman itself: She is that inner space.

610 प्रतिपन्मुख्यराकान्ततिथिमण्डलपूजिता pratipan-mukhya-rākānta-tithi-maṇḍala-pūjitā

She who is worshipped by the circle of lunar days, from the first day to the full moon

Sandhi प्रतिपन्मुख्य = प्रतिपद् + मुख्य (pratipad + mukhya) — a stop becomes the nasal of its class before a nasal: d → n before m (Pāṇini 8.4.45 yaro 'nunāsike 'nunāsiko vā); राकान्त = राका + अन्त (rākā + anta) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over inner bahuvrīhis, a karmadhāraya and a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) pratipan-mukhya 'having the first lunar day (pratipad) at their head' and (2) rākā-anta 'having the full-moon day (rākā) as their end' are bahuvrīhis. (3) Both qualify tithi 'lunar days' (karmadhāraya): 'the lunar days from the first to the full moon'. (4) tithi-maṇḍala 'the circle of those days' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (5) The participle pūjitā 'worshipped' is the head and takes the circle in the instrumental: 'worshipped by the circle of lunar days'.

Analysis प्रतिपत् मुख्या यासाम् ताः प्रतिपन्मुख्याः; राका अन्तः यासाम् ताः राकान्ताः; प्रतिपन्मुख्याः राकान्ताः तिथयः प्रतिपन्मुख्यराकान्ततिथयः; तासाम् मण्डलम् प्रतिपन्मुख्यराकान्ततिथिमण्डलम्; तेन पूजिता प्रतिपन्मुख्यराकान्ततिथिमण्डलपूजिता
pratipat mukhyā yāsām tāḥ pratipanmukhyāḥ; rākā antaḥ yāsām tāḥ rākāntāḥ; pratipanmukhyāḥ rākāntāḥ tithayaḥ pratipanmukhyarākāntatithayaḥ; tāsām maṇḍalam pratipanmukhyarākāntatithimaṇḍalam; tena pūjitā pratipanmukhyarākāntatithimaṇḍalapūjitā

Significance The fifteen days of the bright fortnight are presided over by the fifteen Nityā goddesses, Her own forms (name 391); traditionally the days themselves worship Her, and She is worshipped on each in turn.

Uncertain tithimaṇḍala may be taken as the agent (instrumental, 'by the circle of days', i.e. their deities) or as the time (locative, 'on each of the days'); both readings are current.

Śloka 123names 611–614

कलात्मिका कलानाथा काव्यालापविनोदिनी ।
सचामररमावाणीसव्यदक्षिणसेविता ॥ १२३ ॥

kalātmikā kalānāthā kāvyālāpavinodinī |
sacāmararamāvāṇīsavyadakṣiṇasevitā || 123 ||

The names, separated

611कलात्मिकाkalātmikā612कला-नाथाkalā-nāthā613काव्यालाप-विनोदिनीkāvyālāpa-vinodinī

Translation

611She whose very self is the kalās; 612She who is the mistress of all the kalās; 613She who delights in hearing poetry;

614She who is attended by Lakṣmī on the left and Sarasvatī on the right, each bearing a chowrie.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish

कलाkalākalā: a digit (of the moon, sun or fire); a part; an art

आलापālāparecitation, discourse, conversationā + √lap 'to speak'
विनोदिनीvinodinīshe who delights, amuses herselfvi + causative of √nud, agent suffix -in, feminine -ī

सsawithsaha 'with', reduced to sa- in a bahuvrīhi
चामरcāmarachowrie, the yak-tail fly-whisk, a royal insignia

वाणीvāṇīVāṇī, Sarasvatī, goddess of speech

दक्षिणdakṣiṇaright

Where the names meet

Name 614 fills the second half; its two pairs correspond in order: Ramā (Lakṣmī) on the left, Vāṇī (Sarasvatī) on the right.

The names

611 कलात्मिका kalātmikā

She whose very self is the kalās

Sandhi कलात्मिका = कला + आत्मिका (kalā + ātmikā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (with the suffix -ka). A bahuvrīhi, 'She whose self (ātman) is the kalās', with the bahuvrīhi suffix -ka (kap): ātman + ka gives ātmaka, and in the feminine the a before -kā becomes i (Pāṇini 7.3.44): -ātmikā.

Analysis कलाः आत्मा यस्याः सा कलात्मिका
kalāḥ ātmā yasyāḥ sā kalātmikā

Significance Traditionally the kalās are the sixteen digits of the moon, the twelve of the sun and the ten of fire, and also the sixty-four arts; all of them are Her parts.

612 कलानाथा kalā-nāthā

She who is the mistress of all the kalās

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. nāthā 'mistress' (nātha 'lord' with the feminine -ā) is the head and the kalās stand to it in the genitive: 'the mistress of the kalās'.

Analysis कलानाम् नाथा कलानाथा
kalānām nāthā kalānāthā

Significance She rules every digit and art; since kalānātha, 'lord of the digits', is also a name of the moon, the name is traditionally read as Her being the moon as well.

Uncertain Read as a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa ('mistress of the kalās'); the sense 'She who is the moon' (kalānātha) is also current.

613 काव्यालापविनोदिनी kāvyālāpa-vinodinī

She who delights in hearing poetry

Sandhi काव्यालाप = काव्य + आलाप (kāvya + ālāpa) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (with an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) kāvya-ālāpa 'the recitation of poetry' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) vinodinī 'she who delights' is the head and the recitation is the means of Her delight, in the instrumental.

Analysis काव्यानाम् आलापः काव्यालापः; काव्यालापेन विनोदिनी काव्यालापविनोदिनी
kāvyānām ālāpaḥ kāvyālāpaḥ; kāvyālāpena vinodinī kāvyālāpavinodinī

Significance Poetry offered in Her praise pleases Her; traditionally the hymns of devoted poets are counted among Her chief delights.

614 सचामररमावाणीसव्यदक्षिणसेविता sacāmara-ramā-vāṇī-savya-dakṣiṇa-sevitā

She who is attended by Lakṣmī on the left and Sarasvatī on the right, each bearing a chowrie

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over a saha-bahuvrīhi, two itaretara-dvandvas, a karmadhāraya and a saptamī-tatpuruṣa). (1) sa-cāmara 'with chowries': a bahuvrīhi with saha 'with', which becomes sa- (Pāṇini 6.3.82). (2) ramā-vāṇī 'Ramā and Vāṇī', i.e. Lakṣmī and Sarasvatī (dvandva), qualified by (1). (3) savya-dakṣiṇa 'left and right' (dvandva), the places where (4) sevitā 'served' takes effect (saptamī-tatpuruṣa). (5) The goddesses are the agents, in the instrumental: 'served on the left and right by Ramā and Vāṇī bearing chowries'. The pairs correspond in order: Ramā on the left, Vāṇī on the right.

Analysis चामराभ्याम् सह सचामरे; रमा च वाणी च रमावाण्यौ; सचामरे रमावाण्यौ सचामररमावाण्यौ; सव्यम् च दक्षिणम् च सव्यदक्षिणे; सव्यदक्षिणयोः सेविता सव्यदक्षिणसेविता; सचामररमावाणीभ्याम् सव्यदक्षिणसेविता सचामररमावाणीसव्यदक्षिणसेविता
cāmarābhyām saha sacāmare; ramā ca vāṇī ca ramāvāṇyau; sacāmare ramāvāṇyau sacāmararamāvāṇyau; savyam ca dakṣiṇam ca savyadakṣiṇe; savyadakṣiṇayoḥ sevitā savyadakṣiṇasevitā; sacāmararamāvāṇībhyām savyadakṣiṇasevitā sacāmararamāvāṇīsavyadakṣiṇasevitā

Significance Prosperity and learning wait on Her as attendants, fanning Her with the royal fly-whisks; both goddesses serve the one Queen.

Śloka 124names 615–621

आदिशक्तिर् अमेया ऽऽत्मा परमा पावनाकृतिः ।
अनेककोटिब्रह्माण्डजननी दिव्यविग्रहा ॥ १२४ ॥

ādiśaktir ameyā ''tmā paramā pāvanākṛtiḥ |
anekakoṭibrahmāṇḍajananī divyavigrahā || 124 ||

The names, separated ° form as a name on its own; in the recitation above it joins its neighbour

615आदि-शक्तिः°ādi-śaktiḥ616अमेयाameyā617आत्मा°ātmā618परमाparamā619पावनाकृतिःpāvanākṛtiḥ

620अनेक-कोटि-ब्रह्माण्ड-जननीaneka-koṭi-brahmāṇḍa-jananī621दिव्य-विग्रहाdivya-vigrahā

Translation

615She who is the primordial Power, the first cause of the universe; 616She who is not measurable by any means; 617She who is the self in all; 618She who is the supreme; 619She whose form is purifying;

620She who is the mother of countless millions of universes; 621She who has a divine body.

शक्तिःśaktiḥpower, energyfeminine i-stem, nominative singular

अanot
मेयाmeyāmeasurable, to be measured√mā 'to measure', gerundive in -ya, feminine
617 आत्मा ātmā
आत्माātmāthe Selfnominative singular of the masculine ātman, kept as a name of the Goddess

परमाparamāsupreme, highestsuperlative of para, feminine

पावनpāvanapurifying, holycausative of √pū 'to purify'
आकृतिःākṛtiḥform, figureā + √kṛ; feminine i-stem, nominative singular
620 अनेककोटिब्रह्माण्डजननी aneka-koṭi-brahmāṇḍa-jananī
अनेकanekamany, countlessan- 'not' + eka 'one'
कोटिkoṭiten million (a crore)
ब्रह्माण्डbrahmāṇḍauniverse (lit. 'Brahmā's egg', the cosmic egg)
जननीjananīmother, she who gives birth√jan 'to be born', causative sense, -ana + feminine -ī

दिव्यdivyadivine, heavenly

Where the names meet

आदिशक्तिरमेया = आदिशक्तिः + अमेया (ādiśaktiḥ + ameyā) — visarga becomes r before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ)

अमेयाऽऽत्मा = अमेया + आत्मा (ameyā + ātmā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101); the double avagraha (ऽऽ) marks the absorbed long ā of ātmā

The first quarter holds three names: ādiśaktiḥ / ameyā / ātmā. Do not read 'rameyā': the r is the visarga of śaktiḥ before a vowel.

The names

615 आदिशक्तिः ādi-śaktiḥ

She who is the primordial Power, the first cause of the universe

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya. ādi 'first, beginning' qualifies śakti 'power', which is the head: 'the first power'.

Analysis आदिः च असौ शक्तिः च आदिशक्तिः
ādiḥ ca asau śaktiḥ ca ādiśaktiḥ

Significance Before all other powers She is; from Her as Parā Śakti (name 572) everything that exists comes forth.

616 अमेया ameyā

She who is not measurable by any means

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound nañ-tatpuruṣa. The negative na (appearing as a- before a consonant) is compounded with the gerundive meyā 'to be measured': 'not to be measured'.

Analysis न मेया अमेया
na meyā ameyā

Significance No means of knowledge (pramāṇa), neither perception nor inference nor any other, can measure Her; compare name 413, aprameyā.

617 आत्मा ātmā

She who is the self in all

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance She is the Self of every being, the one consciousness in all; the masculine word ātmā is kept as Her name.

618 परमा paramā

She who is the supreme

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Nothing stands above Her; She is the highest, beyond whom there is nothing.

619 पावनाकृतिः pāvanākṛtiḥ

She whose form is purifying

Sandhi पावनाकृतिः = पावन + आकृतिः (pāvana + ākṛtiḥ) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi. pāvana 'purifying' qualifies ākṛti 'form'; the feminine pāvanī takes the stem pāvana- (puṃvadbhāva). The whole is a bahuvrīhi, 'She whose form is purifying'; ākṛti is already feminine.

Analysis पावनी आकृतिः यस्याः सा पावनाकृतिः
pāvanī ākṛtiḥ yasyāḥ sā pāvanākṛtiḥ

Significance To see or meditate on Her form purifies; traditionally Her form is holy because it makes holy.

620 अनेककोटिब्रह्माण्डजननी aneka-koṭi-brahmāṇḍa-jananī

She who is the mother of countless millions of universes

Sandhi ब्रह्माण्ड = ब्रह्म + अण्ड (brahma + aṇḍa) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ), inside the lexicalised compound brahmāṇḍa (brahman drops its final n first, 8.2.7)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner nañ-tatpuruṣa and karmadhārayas). (1) an-eka 'not one, many': nañ-tatpuruṣa, the negative appearing as an- before a vowel (Pāṇini 6.3.74, a morphological replacement). (2) aneka-koṭi 'many crores' (karmadhāraya). (3) That number stands in apposition to brahmāṇḍa 'world-eggs, universes' (karmadhāraya). (4) jananī 'mother' is the head and takes the universes in the genitive.

Analysis न एकाः अनेकाः; अनेकाः कोटयः अनेककोटयः; अनेककोटयः ब्रह्माण्डानि अनेककोटिब्रह्माण्डानि; अनेककोटिब्रह्माण्डानाम् जननी अनेककोटिब्रह्माण्डजननी
na ekāḥ anekāḥ; anekāḥ koṭayaḥ anekakoṭayaḥ; anekakoṭayaḥ brahmāṇḍāni anekakoṭibrahmāṇḍāni; anekakoṭibrahmāṇḍānām jananī anekakoṭibrahmāṇḍajananī

Significance Our universe is one of innumerable world-eggs, each with its own Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva; all of them are born of Her.

621 दिव्यविग्रहा divya-vigrahā

She who has a divine body

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. divya 'divine' qualifies vigraha 'body, form'; the whole is a bahuvrīhi, 'She whose body is divine', and vigraha takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis दिव्यः विग्रहः यस्याः सा दिव्यविग्रहा
divyaḥ vigrahaḥ yasyāḥ sā divyavigrahā

Significance Her body is not made of the elements but of pure consciousness and bliss, taken for the sake of the devotees.

Śloka 125names 622–629

क्लीङ्कारी केवला गुह्या कैवल्यपददायिनी ।
त्रिपुरा त्रिजगद्वन्द्या त्रिमूर्तिस् त्रिदशेश्वरी ॥ १२५ ॥

klīṅkārī kevalā guhyā kaivalyapadadāyinī |
tripurā trijagadvandyā trimūrtis tridaśeśvarī || 125 ||

The names, separated ° form as a name on its own; in the recitation above it joins its neighbour

622क्लीङ्कारीklīṅkārī623केवलाkevalā624गुह्याguhyā625कैवल्य-पद-दायिनीkaivalya-pada-dāyinī

626त्रिपुराtripurā627त्रि-जगद्-वन्द्याtri-jagad-vandyā628त्रि-मूर्तिः°tri-mūrtiḥ629त्रि-दशेश्वरीtri-daśeśvarī

Translation

622She who is the source of the syllable klīṃ; 623She who is absolute, alone and unconditioned; 624She who is secret, to be known in secret; 625She who bestows the state of kaivalya, final liberation;

626She who is Tripurā, the Goddess of the three cities, prior to the three gods; 627She who is adored by the inhabitants of all three worlds; 628She who has three forms (as Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva); 629She who is the ruler of the gods.

केवलाkevalāalone, absolute, unmixed, entirekevala, feminine

कैवल्यkaivalyakaivalya, absolute aloneness: final liberationfrom kevala 'alone'
पदpadastate, station, abode

त्रिtrithree

त्रिtrithree

वन्द्याvandyāto be saluted, worthy of praise√vand 'to salute', gerundive, feminine

त्रिtrithree
मूर्तिःmūrtiḥform, embodimentfeminine i-stem, nominative singular
