त्रिदशtridaśathe godslit. 'the thirty' (three times ten), a round number for the thirty-three gods; traditionally also explained as those always in the third state of life (youth)
ईश्वरीīśvarīsovereign, ruling lady

Where the names meet

त्रिमूर्तिस्त्रिदशेश्वरी = त्रिमूर्तिः + त्रिदशेश्वरी (trimūrtiḥ + tridaśeśvarī) — visarga becomes s before t (Pāṇini 8.3.34 visarjanīyasya saḥ)

Names 626–630 form a run on 'three' (Tripurā, the three worlds, three forms, the thirty gods, three syllables).

The names

622 क्लीङ्कारी klīṅkārī

She who is the source of the syllable klīṃ

Sandhi क्लीङ्कारी = क्लीम् + कारी (klīm + kārī) — m becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ), which takes the nasal of the following stop's class: ṅ before k (8.4.58 anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ)

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. kārī 'maker' is from √kṛ with the suffix aṇ after an object (Pāṇini 3.2.1 karmaṇy aṇ) and the feminine -ī; the seed-syllable klīm is its object: 'She who makes (is the source of) klīṃ'. Alternatively klīṅkāra 'the syllable klīṃ' (kāra names a sound, as in oṅkāra) with the feminine -ī: 'She who is the syllable klīṃ'.

Analysis क्लीम् करोति इति क्लीङ्कारी
klīm karoti iti klīṅkārī

Significance klīṃ is the kāmabīja, the seed-syllable of desire and attraction; with aiṃ and sauḥ it forms the three-syllable Bālā mantra (compare name 630).

Uncertain Two analyses: 'maker of klīṃ' (upapada-tatpuruṣa) and 'She who is the syllable klīṃ' (klīṅkāra + feminine -ī); traditionally She is both its source and its form.

623 केवला kevalā

She who is absolute, alone and unconditioned

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance She is complete in Herself, independent of anything else and without qualities; kaivalya, the liberation of name 625, is the state of this 'aloneness'.

624 गुह्या guhyā

She who is secret, to be known in secret

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Her worship and Her mantra are to be kept hidden, revealed only by the guru; traditionally the name is also read from guhā 'cave', as She who dwells in the cave of the heart.

Uncertain Derived from √guh 'to hide' (gerundive) or from guhā 'cave' ('dwelling in the cave of the heart'); both are traditional.

625 कैवल्यपददायिनी kaivalya-pada-dāyinī

She who bestows the state of kaivalya, final liberation

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (with an inner karmadhāraya). (1) kaivalya-pada 'the state that is kaivalya' (karmadhāraya of identification). (2) dāyinī 'she who gives' is the head and takes that state in the genitive.

Analysis कैवल्यम् एव पदम् कैवल्यपदम्; कैवल्यपदस्य दायिनी कैवल्यपददायिनी
kaivalyam eva padam kaivalyapadam; kaivalyapadasya dāyinī kaivalyapadadāyinī

Significance Kaivalya is the Self standing alone, free of all that is not the Self; She grants it, being Herself kevalā (name 623).

626 त्रिपुरा tripurā

She who is Tripurā, the Goddess of the three cities, prior to the three gods

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (traditionally also read as tri + purā). Grammatically a bahuvrīhi, 'She who has three cities (abodes)'; pura takes the feminine -ā. The traditional derivation reads the indeclinable purā 'before': 'She who was before the three (gods)'. Both are given by commentators.

Analysis त्रीणि पुराणि यस्याः सा त्रिपुरा; अथवा त्रिभ्यः पुरा त्रिपुरा
trīṇi purāṇi yasyāḥ sā tripurā; athavā tribhyaḥ purā tripurā

Significance Every triad is in Her: the three worlds, the three bodies, the three states of waking, dream and sleep, the three powers and the three gods; Śrīvidyā names Her Tripurasundarī, the beauty of the three cities.

Uncertain Two derivations: tri + pura 'three cities' (bahuvrīhi) and tri + purā 'before the three' (the traditional reading). The meaning gives both.

627 त्रिजगद्वन्द्या tri-jagad-vandyā

She who is adored by the inhabitants of all three worlds

Sandhi जगद्वन्द्या = जगत् + वन्द्या (jagat + vandyā) — jaśtva: a final t becomes d before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.39 jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (with an inner samāhāra-dvigu). (1) tri-jagat 'the three worlds' taken together (samāhāra-dvigu). (2) The gerundive vandyā 'to be saluted, praised' is the head and the three worlds are its agent, in the instrumental.

Analysis त्रयाणाम् जगताम् समाहारः त्रिजगत्; त्रिजगता वन्द्या त्रिजगद्वन्द्या
trayāṇām jagatām samāhāraḥ trijagat; trijagatā vandyā trijagadvandyā

Significance Heaven, earth and the underworld all bow to Her.

628 त्रिमूर्तिः tri-mūrtiḥ

She who has three forms (as Brahmā, Viṣṇu and Śiva)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. A bahuvrīhi with a numeral first member: 'She who has three forms'. The feminine numeral tisraḥ appears as the stem tri- in the compound; mūrti is already feminine.

Analysis तिस्रः मूर्तयः यस्याः सा त्रिमूर्तिः
tisraḥ mūrtayaḥ yasyāḥ sā trimūrtiḥ

Significance Creating, sustaining and dissolving, She takes the three forms of the gods (or of their powers Brāhmī, Vaiṣṇavī and Raudrī), being Herself the One behind them.

629 त्रिदशेश्वरी tri-daśeśvarī

She who is the ruler of the gods

Sandhi त्रिदशेश्वरी = त्रिदश + ईश्वरी (tridaśa + īśvarī) — guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. īśvarī 'sovereign' is the head and tridaśa 'the gods' stands to it in the genitive: 'the sovereign of the gods'. tridaśa is a fixed word for the gods.

Analysis त्रिदशानाम् ईश्वरी त्रिदशेश्वरी
tridaśānām īśvarī tridaśeśvarī

Significance Indra and all the gods hold their sovereignty from Her, as name 607 also says.

Śloka 126names 630–636

त्र्यक्षरी दिव्यगन्धाढ्या सिन्दूरतिलकाञ्चिता ।
उमा शैलेन्द्रतनया गौरी गन्धर्वसेविता ॥ १२६ ॥

tryakṣarī divyagandhāḍhyā sindūratilakāñcitā |
umā śailendratanayā gaurī gandharvasevitā || 126 ||

The names, separated

630त्र्य्-अक्षरीtry-akṣarī631दिव्य-गन्धाढ्याdivya-gandhāḍhyā632सिन्दूर-तिलकाञ्चिताsindūra-tilakāñcitā

633उमाumā634शैलेन्द्र-तनयाśailendra-tanayā635गौरीgaurī636गन्धर्व-सेविताgandharva-sevitā

Translation

630She who is the three-syllabled (mantra); 631She who is richly endowed with divine fragrance; 632She who is adorned with a tilaka of vermilion;

633She who is Umā (Pārvatī); 634She who is the daughter of Himavat, the king of the mountains; 635She who has a fair complexion; 636She who is served by the Gandharvas (such as Viśvāvasu).

Where the names meet

Names 633–635 name Her as Pārvatī: Umā, daughter of the mountain king, Gaurī.

The names

630 त्र्यक्षरी try-akṣarī

She who is the three-syllabled (mantra)

Sandhi त्र्यक्षरी = त्रि + अक्षरी (tri + akṣarī) — yaṇ: i becomes y before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci)

Compound samāhāra-dvigu. A collective numeral compound, 'the group of three syllables'; a dvigu ending in -a takes the feminine -ī (Pāṇini 4.1.21 dvigoḥ). She is identified with that three-syllable whole.

Analysis त्रयाणाम् अक्षराणाम् समाहारः त्र्यक्षरी
trayāṇām akṣarāṇām samāhāraḥ tryakṣarī

Significance Traditionally the three syllables are read as a, u and m of Oṃ, as the three seed-syllables of the Bālā mantra (aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ, compare name 622), or as the three kūṭas of the Pañcadaśī (name 588).

Uncertain Which three syllables are meant is explained in more than one way (Oṃ, the Bālā mantra, the three kūṭas).

Corrected त्र्यक्षरि → त्र्यक्षरी. त्र्यक्षरि → त्र्यक्षरी (nominative -ī).

631 दिव्यगन्धाढ्या divya-gandhāḍhyā

She who is richly endowed with divine fragrance

Sandhi गन्धाढ्या = गन्ध + आढ्या (gandha + āḍhyā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (with an inner karmadhāraya). (1) divya-gandha 'divine fragrance' (karmadhāraya). (2) āḍhyā 'rich, abounding' is the head and takes the fragrance in the instrumental: 'rich in divine fragrance'.

Analysis दिव्यः गन्धः दिव्यगन्धः; दिव्यगन्धेन आढ्या दिव्यगन्धाढ्या
divyaḥ gandhaḥ divyagandhaḥ; divyagandhena āḍhyā divyagandhāḍhyā

Significance Her body is naturally fragrant; traditionally the scent of the flowers and unguents offered to Her comes from Her, not to Her (compare name 13).

632 सिन्दूरतिलकाञ्चिता sindūra-tilakāñcitā

She who is adorned with a tilaka of vermilion

Sandhi तिलकाञ्चिता = तिलक + अञ्चिता (tilaka + añcitā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (with an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) sindūra-tilaka 'a tilaka of vermilion' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa of material). (2) The participle añcitā 'adorned' is the head and takes the tilaka in the instrumental.

Analysis सिन्दूरस्य तिलकम् सिन्दूरतिलकम्; सिन्दूरतिलकेन अञ्चिता सिन्दूरतिलकाञ्चिता
sindūrasya tilakam sindūratilakam; sindūratilakena añcitā sindūratilakāñcitā

Significance The vermilion mark is the sign of the auspicious married woman: it marks Her eternal union with Kāmeśvara.

633 उमा umā

She who is Umā (Pārvatī)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Kālidāsa (Kumārasambhava 1.26) derives the name from her mother's cry u mā, 'O, do not!', forbidding her austerities; in the Kena Upaniṣad Umā Haimavatī appears to Indra and teaches him Brahman.

634 शैलेन्द्रतनया śailendra-tanayā

She who is the daughter of Himavat, the king of the mountains

Sandhi शैलेन्द्र = शैल + इन्द्र (śaila + indra) — guṇa: a + i → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (with an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) śaila-indra 'the lord of mountains', Himavat (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; indra at the end of a compound means 'chief, king'). (2) tanayā 'daughter' is the head.

Analysis शैलानाम् इन्द्रः शैलेन्द्रः; शैलेन्द्रस्य तनया शैलेन्द्रतनया
śailānām indraḥ śailendraḥ; śailendrasya tanayā śailendratanayā

Significance Born again as Pārvatī after giving up Her body as Satī (name 598), She won Śiva by Her austerities.

635 गौरी gaurī

She who has a fair complexion

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance In a Purāṇic story Pārvatī, teased for Her dark skin, performed austerities and became golden-fair, Gaurī; Gaurī is also the name given to the girl worshipped as the Goddess.

636 गन्धर्वसेविता gandharva-sevitā

She who is served by the Gandharvas (such as Viśvāvasu)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa. The participle sevitā 'served' is the head; the Gandharvas are its agent, in the instrumental.

Analysis गन्धर्वैः सेविता गन्धर्वसेविता
gandharvaiḥ sevitā gandharvasevitā

Significance The celestial musicians serve Her with song; Viśvāvasu, their chief, is traditionally named among them.

Śloka 127names 637–644

विश्वगर्भा स्वर्णगर्भा ऽवरदा वागधीश्वरी ।
ध्यानगम्या ऽपरिच्छेद्या ज्ञानदा ज्ञानविग्रहा ॥ १२७ ॥

viśvagarbhā svarṇagarbhā 'varadā vāgadhīśvarī |
dhyānagamyā 'paricchedyā jñānadā jñānavigrahā || 127 ||

The names, separated ° form as a name on its own; in the recitation above it joins its neighbour

637विश्व-गर्भाviśva-garbhā638स्वर्ण-गर्भाsvarṇa-garbhā639अवरदा°avaradā640वाग्-अधीश्वरीvāg-adhīśvarī

641ध्यान-गम्याdhyāna-gamyā642अपरिच्छेद्या°aparicchedyā643ज्ञान-दाjñāna-dā644ज्ञान-विग्रहाjñāna-vigrahā

Translation

637She who contains the whole universe in Her womb; 638She whose womb is golden, the source of the world (as Hiraṇyagarbha); 639She who destroys the base (the demons); 640She who presides over speech;

641She who is to be attained through meditation; 642She who cannot be delimited; 643She who bestows knowledge; 644She whose very body is knowledge.

गर्भाgarbhāwomb; what is held withingarbha, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

Where the names meet

स्वर्णगर्भाऽवरदा = स्वर्णगर्भा + अवरदा (svarṇagarbhā + avaradā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101); the avagraha (ऽ) marks the absorbed initial a of the next name

ध्यानगम्याऽपरिच्छेद्या = ध्यानगम्या + अपरिच्छेद्या (dhyānagamyā + aparicchedyā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101); the avagraha (ऽ) marks the absorbed initial a of the next name

Both avagrahas mark a name beginning with a-: name 639 is avaradā (not varadā), name 642 is aparicchedyā. Name 640: vāg is the c of vāc voiced before adhīśvarī.

The names

637 विश्वगर्भा viśva-garbhā

She who contains the whole universe in Her womb

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. A bahuvrīhi, 'She in whose womb is the universe'; garbha takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis विश्वम् गर्भे यस्याः सा विश्वगर्भा
viśvam garbhe yasyāḥ sā viśvagarbhā

Significance The universe is held within Her before it is born and after it is withdrawn.

638 स्वर्णगर्भा svarṇa-garbhā

She whose womb is golden, the source of the world (as Hiraṇyagarbha)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. A bahuvrīhi, 'She whose womb holds gold' (or 'whose womb is golden'); garbha takes the feminine -ā. The name echoes Hiraṇyagarbha, 'the golden embryo', the first-born source of the world.

Analysis स्वर्णम् गर्भे यस्याः सा स्वर्णगर्भा
svarṇam garbhe yasyāḥ sā svarṇagarbhā

Significance Hiraṇyagarbha, the golden embryo of Ṛgveda 10.121, is the first manifest form from which the world unfolds; She is that golden source.

Uncertain The old meaning gave an interpretation ('the cause of the universe'); the literal bahuvrīhi and its echo of Hiraṇyagarbha are given here. Bhāskararāya's own gloss of this name was not confirmed.

639 अवरदा avaradā

She who destroys the base (the demons)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. -da 'cutting down' is from √do 'to cut' with the suffix ka (Pāṇini 3.2.3 āto 'nupasarge kaḥ) and the feminine -ā; avara 'the low, the base' is its object: 'She who cuts down the base (the demons)'.

Analysis अवरान् द्यति इति अवरदा
avarān dyati iti avaradā

Significance She cuts down whatever is low and opposed to the good, outward demons and the base tendencies of the mind.

Uncertain The derivation from √do 'to cut' is the traditional one; -dā could also be read from √dā 'to give' ('She who gives even to the lowly'). The name is avaradā, not varadā: the avagraha in the verse marks the elided a.

640 वागधीश्वरी vāg-adhīśvarī

She who presides over speech

Sandhi वागधी = वाच् + अधी (vāc + adhī) — c becomes k at the end of a member (Pāṇini 8.2.30 coḥ kuḥ), then voiced to g before a vowel (jaśtva, 8.2.39); अधीश्वरी = अधि + ईश्वरी (adhi + īśvarī) — savarṇa-dīrgha: i + ī → ī (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. adhīśvarī 'presiding sovereign' is the head and vāc 'speech' stands to it in the genitive: 'the presiding sovereign of speech'.

Analysis वाचः अधीश्वरी वागधीश्वरी
vācaḥ adhīśvarī vāgadhīśvarī

Significance All speech, from the Veda to ordinary words, arises from Her (compare name 577); She is Sarasvatī and more than Sarasvatī.

641 ध्यानगम्या dhyāna-gamyā

She who is to be attained through meditation

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa. The gerundive gamyā 'to be reached' is the head; dhyāna 'meditation' is the means, in the instrumental.

Analysis ध्यानेन गम्या ध्यानगम्या
dhyānena gamyā dhyānagamyā

Significance She is reached not by argument but by steady meditation; the next names say why She cannot be reached otherwise.

642 अपरिच्छेद्या aparicchedyā

She who cannot be delimited

Sandhi परिच्छेद्या = परि + छेद्या (pari + chedyā) — after a short vowel, ch takes the augment t (Pāṇini 6.1.73 che ca), which becomes c before ch (8.4.40 stoḥ ścunā ścuḥ), at the prefix junction pari + chedya

Compound nañ-tatpuruṣa. The negative na (a- before a consonant) is compounded with the gerundive paricchedyā 'to be delimited': 'not to be delimited'.

Analysis न परिच्छेद्या अपरिच्छेद्या
na paricchedyā aparicchedyā

Significance She is not bounded by space, time or any object; compare name 701, deśakālāparicchinnā.

643 ज्ञानदा jñāna-dā

She who bestows knowledge

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. -da 'giving' is from √dā with the suffix ka (Pāṇini 3.2.3 āto 'nupasarge kaḥ), feminine -ā, with jñāna as its object.

Analysis ज्ञानम् ददाति इति ज्ञानदा
jñānam dadāti iti jñānadā

Significance Traditionally the knowledge meant is knowledge of the Self, which frees.

644 ज्ञानविग्रहा jñāna-vigrahā

She whose very body is knowledge

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. A bahuvrīhi, 'She whose body is knowledge'; vigraha takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis ज्ञानम् विग्रहः यस्याः सा ज्ञानविग्रहा
jñānam vigrahaḥ yasyāḥ sā jñānavigrahā

Significance Her form is not made of matter: it is knowledge itself taking shape.

सर्ववेदान्तसंवेद्या सत्यानन्दस्वरूपिणी ।
लोपामुद्रार्चिता लीलाकॢप्तब्रह्माण्डमण्डला ॥ १२८ ॥

sarvavedāntasaṃvedyā satyānandasvarūpiṇī |

लीलाlīlāplay, sport, effortless pastime
कॢप्तkḷptafashioned, arranged, made√kḷp 'to be fit, arrange', past participle; spelled with vocalic ḷ
ब्रह्माण्डbrahmāṇḍauniverse (lit. 'Brahmā's egg')
मण्डलाmaṇḍalācircle, spheremaṇḍala, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

Where the names meet

Name 648 is spelled with vocalic ḷ: कॢप्त (kḷpta), as in name 21.

The names

645 सर्ववेदान्तसंवेद्या sarva-vedānta-saṃvedyā

She who is to be known through all the Upaniṣads

Sandhi वेदान्त = वेद + अन्त (veda + anta) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ), inside the lexicalised compound vedānta; संवेद्या = सम् + वेद्या (sam + vedyā) — m becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ), at the prefix junction sam + vedya

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (with an inner karmadhāraya). (1) sarva-vedānta 'all the Upaniṣads' (karmadhāraya). (2) The gerundive saṃvedyā 'to be known fully' is the head and takes them as its means, in the instrumental.

Analysis सर्वे वेदान्ताः सर्ववेदान्ताः; सर्ववेदान्तैः संवेद्या सर्ववेदान्तसंवेद्या
sarve vedāntāḥ sarvavedāntāḥ; sarvavedāntaiḥ saṃvedyā sarvavedāntasaṃvedyā

Significance All the Upaniṣads converge on one meaning (Brahma Sūtra 1.1.4, tat tu samanvayāt), and that meaning is She.

646 सत्यानन्दस्वरूपिणी satyānanda-svarūpiṇī

She whose very nature is truth (being) and bliss

Sandhi सत्यानन्द = सत्य + आनन्द (satya + ānanda) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound karmadhāraya with the possessive suffix -in (over an inner dvandva). (1) satya-ānanda 'truth (being) and bliss' (dvandva; a karmadhāraya 'true bliss' is also possible). (2) sva-rūpa 'own form, essential nature'. (3) The two are identified (karmadhāraya), and the possessive -in with feminine -ī gives 'She whose essential nature is truth and bliss'.

Analysis सत्यम् च आनन्दः च सत्यानन्दौ; स्वम् रूपम् स्वरूपम्; सत्यानन्दौ स्वरूपम् सत्यानन्दस्वरूपम्; सत्यानन्दस्वरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति सत्यानन्दस्वरूपिणी
satyam ca ānandaḥ ca satyānandau; svam rūpam svarūpam; satyānandau svarūpam satyānandasvarūpam; satyānandasvarūpam asyāḥ asti iti satyānandasvarūpiṇī

Significance Sat and ānanda, with cit, are the classic description of Brahman (compare name 700, saccidānandarūpiṇī); She is that being and bliss itself.

647 लोपामुद्रार्चिता lopāmudrārcitā

She who is worshipped by Lopāmudrā (wife of the sage Agastya)

Sandhi लोपामुद्रार्चिता = लोपामुद्रा + अर्चिता (lopāmudrā + arcitā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa. The participle arcitā 'worshipped' is the head and Lopāmudrā is its agent, in the instrumental.

Analysis लोपामुद्रया अर्चिता लोपामुद्रार्चिता
lopāmudrayā arcitā lopāmudrārcitā

Significance Lopāmudrā is counted among the great worshippers of Śrīvidyā, and the hādi form of the Pañcadaśī is named after her; her husband Agastya is the hearer to whom Hayagrīva teaches these thousand names.

648 लीलाकॢप्तब्रह्माण्डमण्डला līlā-kḷpta-brahmāṇḍa-maṇḍalā

She who has fashioned the whole sphere of the universe in play

Sandhi ब्रह्माण्ड = ब्रह्म + अण्ड (brahma + aṇḍa) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ), inside the lexicalised compound brahmāṇḍa (brahman drops its final n first, 8.2.7)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) līlā-kḷpta 'fashioned in play' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa: līlā is the manner, in the instrumental). (2) brahmāṇḍa-maṇḍala 'the round of the world-eggs', the whole universe (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa), qualified by (1). (3) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She by whom the sphere of the universe is fashioned in play'; maṇḍala takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis लीलया कॢप्तम् लीलाकॢप्तम्; ब्रह्माण्डानाम् मण्डलम् ब्रह्माण्डमण्डलम्; लीलाकॢप्तम् ब्रह्माण्डमण्डलम् यस्याः सा लीलाकॢप्तब्रह्माण्डमण्डला
līlayā kḷptam līlākḷptam; brahmāṇḍānām maṇḍalam brahmāṇḍamaṇḍalam; līlākḷptam brahmāṇḍamaṇḍalam yasyāḥ sā līlākḷptabrahmāṇḍamaṇḍalā

Significance Creation costs Her no effort and serves no need: it is līlā, play (compare Brahma Sūtra 2.1.33, lokavat tu līlākaivalyam).

Śloka 129names 649–657

अदृश्या दृश्यरहिता विज्ञात्री वेद्यवर्जिता ।
योगिनी योगदा योग्या योगानन्दा युगन्धरा ॥ १२९ ॥

adṛśyā dṛśyarahitā vijñātrī vedyavarjitā |
yoginī yogadā yogyā yogānandā yugandharā || 129 ||

The names, separated

649अदृश्याadṛśyā650दृश्य-रहिताdṛśya-rahitā651विज्ञात्रीvijñātrī652वेद्य-वर्जिताvedya-varjitā

Where the names meet

Names 649–652 pair off: unseen and without anything seen, the knower and without anything to know. Names 653–657 play on yoga (yoginī, yogadā, yogyā, yogānandā) and close with yugandharā.

The names

649 अदृश्या adṛśyā

She who is invisible, beyond the reach of the senses

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound nañ-tatpuruṣa. The negative na (a- before a consonant) is compounded with the gerundive dṛśyā 'to be seen': 'not to be seen'.

Analysis न दृश्या अदृश्या
na dṛśyā adṛśyā

Significance The Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad (1.1.6) calls the Imperishable 'that which cannot be seen, cannot be grasped'; She is not an object of the senses.

650 दृश्यरहिता dṛśya-rahitā

She who is free of anything seen, with nothing outside Her to see

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa. The participle rahitā 'free from, without' is the head and dṛśya 'the seen' stands to it in the instrumental: 'free from what is seen'.

Analysis दृश्येन रहिता दृश्यरहिता
dṛśyena rahitā dṛśyarahitā

Significance Since nothing exists apart from Her, there is no object standing over against Her; She is the seer without a seen.

651 विज्ञात्री vijñātrī

She who is the knower

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance The Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad (2.4.14) asks: 'By what should one know the knower?' She is that knower, never the known.

652 वेद्यवर्जिता vedya-varjitā

She who has nothing to be known apart from Herself

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa. The participle varjitā 'devoid of' is the head and vedya 'the knowable' stands to it in the instrumental: 'free from anything to be known'.

Analysis वेद्येन वर्जिता वेद्यवर्जिता
vedyena varjitā vedyavarjitā

Significance With name 651: She is the knower with no object outside Her, since all that could be known is Herself.

653 योगिनी yoginī

She who possesses the power of yoga, ever united with Paraśiva

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance She is ever in union (yoga) with Śiva; the yoginīs who attend Her in the Śrīcakra and in the bodily centers are Her own powers.

654 योगदा yoga-dā

She who bestows the power of yoga

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. -da 'giving' from √dā with ka (Pāṇini 3.2.3), feminine -ā, with yoga as its object.

Analysis योगम् ददाति इति योगदा
yogam dadāti iti yogadā

Significance Success in yoga, and the union that is its goal, come by Her grace.

655 योग्या yogyā

She who is fit to be reached through yoga

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance She is the proper object of every kind of yoga; traditionally also, She is fit, worthy in every respect.

Uncertain yogya means both 'fit, worthy' and 'to be attained by yoga'; the meaning follows the second, the significance mentions the first.

656 योगानन्दा yogānandā

She who enjoys the bliss of yoga, and is that bliss

Sandhi योगानन्दा = योग + आनन्दा (yoga + ānandā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) yoga-ānanda 'the bliss of yoga' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) A bahuvrīhi, 'She whose bliss is the bliss of yoga'; ānanda takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis योगस्य आनन्दः योगानन्दः; योगानन्दः यस्याः सा योगानन्दा
yogasya ānandaḥ yogānandaḥ; yogānandaḥ yasyāḥ sā yogānandā

Significance The bliss that the yogin finds in union is Hers; She both enjoys it and is it.

657 युगन्धरा yugan-dharā

She who is the bearer of the yugas

Sandhi युगन्धरा = युगम् + धरा (yugam + dharā) — the augment m becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23) and then the dental nasal n before dh (8.4.58 anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ)

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. dharā 'bearing' is from causative √dhṛ with the suffix khac; before a member so formed, a stem ending in a vowel takes the augment m (Pāṇini 6.3.67 arurdviṣadajantasya mum): yuga-m-dhara, written yugan-dharā. The feminine is -ā.

Analysis युगम् धारयति इति युगन्धरा
yugam dhārayati iti yugandharā

Significance She upholds the ages of the world in their succession, as a yoke holds the team together.

Śloka 130names 658–661

इच्छाशक्तिज्ञानशक्तिक्रियाशक्तिस्वरूपिणी ।
सर्वाधारा सुप्रतिष्ठा सदसद्रूपधारिणी ॥ १३० ॥

icchāśaktijñānaśaktikriyāśaktisvarūpiṇī |
sarvādhārā supratiṣṭhā sadasadrūpadhāriṇī || 130 ||

The names, separated

658इच्छा-शक्ति-ज्ञान-शक्ति-क्रिया-शक्ति-स्वरूपिणीicchā-śakti-jñāna-śakti-kriyā-śakti-svarūpiṇī

659सर्वाधाराsarvādhārā660सु-प्रतिष्ठाsu-pratiṣṭhā661सद्-असद्-रूप-धारिणीsad-asad-rūpa-dhāriṇī

Translation

658She who is in the form of the powers of will, knowledge and action;

659She who is the support of all; 660She who is firmly established; 661She who assumes the forms of both being and non-being.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish
658 इच्छाशक्तिज्ञानशक्तिक्रियाशक्तिस्वरूपिणी icchā-śakti-jñāna-śakti-kriyā-śakti-svarūpiṇī
इच्छाicchāwill, desire
शक्तिśaktipower

शक्तिśaktipower
क्रियाkriyāaction
शक्तिśaktipower

659 सर्वाधारा sarvādhārā
सर्वsarvaall, everything
आधाराādhārāsupport, foundation, containerādhāra (ā + √dhṛ 'to hold'), with the feminine -ā
660 सुप्रतिष्ठा su-pratiṣṭhā
सुsuwell, firmly, excellently
प्रतिष्ठाpratiṣṭhāstanding, foundation, supportprati + √sthā 'to stand'

सत्satbeing, the existent, the manifest
असत्asatnon-being, the non-existent, the unmanifest
रूपrūpaform
धारिणीdhāriṇīshe who bears, holds, assumescausative of √dhṛ 'to hold', agent suffix -in, feminine -ī

Where the names meet

Name 658 fills the whole first half: the three powers of will, knowledge and action.

The names

658 इच्छाशक्तिज्ञानशक्तिक्रियाशक्तिस्वरूपिणी icchā-śakti-jñāna-śakti-kriyā-śakti-svarūpiṇī

She who is in the form of the powers of will, knowledge and action

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya with the possessive suffix -in (over an inner itaretara-dvandva of three karmadhārayas). (1) Three karmadhārayas of identification: icchā-śakti 'the power that is will', jñāna-śakti 'the power that is knowledge', kriyā-śakti 'the power that is action'. (2) The three form a dvandva. (3) They are identified with sva-rūpa 'own nature', and the possessive -in with feminine -ī gives 'She whose own nature is the powers of will, knowledge and action'. The members meet without sound change.

Analysis इच्छा एव शक्तिः इच्छाशक्तिः; ज्ञानम् एव शक्तिः ज्ञानशक्तिः; क्रिया एव शक्तिः क्रियाशक्तिः; इच्छाशक्तिः च ज्ञानशक्तिः च क्रियाशक्तिः च इच्छाशक्तिज्ञानशक्तिक्रियाशक्तयः; इच्छाशक्तिज्ञानशक्तिक्रियाशक्तयः स्वरूपम् इच्छाशक्तिज्ञानशक्तिक्रियाशक्तिस्वरूपम्; तत् अस्याः अस्ति इति इच्छाशक्तिज्ञानशक्तिक्रियाशक्तिस्वरूपिणी
icchā eva śaktiḥ icchāśaktiḥ; jñānam eva śaktiḥ jñānaśaktiḥ; kriyā eva śaktiḥ kriyāśaktiḥ; icchāśaktiḥ ca jñānaśaktiḥ ca kriyāśaktiḥ ca icchāśaktijñānaśaktikriyāśaktayaḥ; icchāśaktijñānaśaktikriyāśaktayaḥ svarūpam icchāśaktijñānaśaktikriyāśaktisvarūpam; tat asyāḥ asti iti icchāśaktijñānaśaktikriyāśaktisvarūpiṇī

Significance Will, knowledge and action are the three powers of the one consciousness, by which every act of creation proceeds: first the will, then the knowing of what is willed, then the doing. Traditionally they are placed at the three corners of the central triangle of the Śrīcakra.

659 सर्वाधारा sarvādhārā

She who is the support of all

Sandhi सर्वाधारा = सर्व + आधारा (sarva + ādhārā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. ādhārā 'support' is the head and sarva 'all' stands to it in the genitive: 'the support of all'. ādhāra takes the feminine -ā because it describes Her.

Analysis सर्वस्य आधारा सर्वाधारा
sarvasya ādhārā sarvādhārā

Significance Everything rests in Her as the pot rests on the ground, while She rests on nothing else.

660 सुप्रतिष्ठा su-pratiṣṭhā

She who is firmly established

Sandhi प्रतिष्ठा = प्रति + स्था (prati + sthā) — after a prefix ending in i, the s of sthā becomes ṣ (Pāṇini 8.3.65), and th then becomes ṭh by retroflex assimilation (8.4.41 ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (alternatively prādi-tatpuruṣa). As a bahuvrīhi, su 'well, firmly' qualifies pratiṣṭhā 'standing, foundation': 'She whose standing is firm'. As a prādi-tatpuruṣa: 'the excellent foundation' (of the world). pratiṣṭhā is already feminine.

Analysis सुष्ठु प्रतिष्ठा यस्याः सा सुप्रतिष्ठा; अथवा शोभना प्रतिष्ठा सुप्रतिष्ठा
suṣṭhu pratiṣṭhā yasyāḥ sā supratiṣṭhā; athavā śobhanā pratiṣṭhā supratiṣṭhā

Significance She stands on Herself and on nothing else, and is the firm ground on which all else stands (name 659).

Corrected सुप्रतीष्ठा → सुप्रतिष्ठा. सुप्रतीष्ठा → सुप्रतिष्ठा (prati-ṣṭhā: short i).

661 सदसद्रूपधारिणी sad-asad-rūpa-dhāriṇī

She who assumes the forms of both being and non-being

Sandhi सदसद् = सत् + असत् (sat + asat) — jaśtva: the final t of sat becomes d at the end of a member, here before a vowel (Pāṇini 8.2.39 jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte); the t of asat is voiced in the next junction; सदसद्रूप = सदसत् + रूप (sadasat + rūpa) — jaśtva: a final t becomes d before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.39 jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner dvandva and karmadhāraya). (1) sad-asat 'being and non-being' (dvandva). (2) They are identified with rūpa 'form' (karmadhāraya): 'the forms that are being and non-being'. (3) dhāriṇī 'she who bears, assumes' is an agent noun and the head, with the forms as its object in the genitive.

Analysis सत् च असत् च सदसती; सदसती एव रूपे सदसद्रूपे; सदसद्रूपयोः धारिणी सदसद्रूपधारिणी
sat ca asat ca sadasatī; sadasatī eva rūpe sadasadrūpe; sadasadrūpayoḥ dhāriṇī sadasadrūpadhāriṇī

Significance In the Gītā (9.19) the Lord says 'I am being and non-being'; She holds both the manifest and the unmanifest, the real and the apparent.

Śloka 131names 662–668

अष्टमूर्तिर् अजाजैत्री लोकयात्राविधायिनी ।
एकाकिनी भूमरूपा निर्द्वैता द्वैतवर्जिता ॥ १३१ ॥

aṣṭamūrtir ajājaitrī lokayātrāvidhāyinī |
ekākinī bhūmarūpā nirdvaitā dvaitavarjitā || 131 ||

The names, separated ° form as a name on its own; in the recitation above it joins its neighbour

Where the names meet

अष्टमूर्तिरजाजैत्री = अष्टमूर्तिः + अजाजैत्री (aṣṭamūrtiḥ + ajājaitrī) — visarga becomes r before a vowel or voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ)

The r in -mūrtir- is the visarga of aṣṭamūrtiḥ (662); name 663 begins ajā-, not rajā-.

The names

662 अष्टमूर्तिः aṣṭa-mūrtiḥ

She who has eight forms

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. aṣṭan 'eight' qualifies mūrti 'form, embodiment', and the whole points outside itself to the Goddess: 'She who has eight forms'. The numeral's final n is dropped at the end of a compound member (aṣṭan → aṣṭa-), a morphological change, not sandhi; mūrti keeps its i-stem and the nominative is aṣṭamūrtiḥ.

Analysis अष्टौ मूर्तयः यस्याः सा अष्टमूर्तिः
aṣṭau mūrtayaḥ yasyāḥ sā aṣṭamūrtiḥ

Significance Traditionally the eight forms (aṣṭamūrti) of Śiva — earth, water, fire, air, space, sun, moon and the sacrificer — which She, as His power, also is. The eightfold nature (prakṛti) of Bhagavad Gītā 7.4 is another octad read here.

663 अजाजैत्री ajā-jaitrī

She who conquers Ajā, the unborn Māyā of ignorance

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (objective genitive). jaitrī 'victorious, conqueror' is the head; ajā 'the unborn (she)' stands to it as the one conquered: 'the conqueror of Ajā'. Ajā is the feminine of aja 'unborn' and, after Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad 4.5 (ajām ekāṃ lohitaśuklakṛṣṇām, 'the one unborn [she] of red, white and black'), names beginningless Māyā or ignorance. The two members meet with no sound change.

Analysis अजायाः जैत्री अजाजैत्री
ajāyāḥ jaitrī ajājaitrī

Significance Traditionally Ajā is avidyā, without beginning but not without end: She who is Knowledge overcomes it in the devotee.

Variants The site's earlier text read अजाजेत्री (ajājetrī, feminine of jetṛ 'conqueror'), with the same sense; the verse reads jaitrī (see the correction log).

Corrected अजाजेत्री → अजाजैत्री. अजाजेत्री → अजाजैत्री (jaitrī, victorious: vṛddhi ai); the verse reads अजाजैत्री.

664 लोकयात्राविधायिनी loka-yātrā-vidhāyinī

She who directs the course of the worlds

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (with an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) loka-yātrā 'the course, the going-on of the world' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, yātrā the head). (2) vidhāyinī 'one who arranges, ordains' is an agent noun in -in from vi + √dhā, with the y inserted after a root in ā; it governs lokayātrā as its object (upapada-tatpuruṣa): 'She who ordains the course of the world'.

Analysis लोकस्य यात्रा लोकयात्रा; लोकयात्राम् विदधाति इति लोकयात्राविधायिनी
lokasya yātrā lokayātrā; lokayātrām vidadhāti iti lokayātrāvidhāyinī

Significance Traditionally the ongoing life of the worlds — creation, sustenance and the working-out of each being's karma — runs by Her ordinance.

Corrected लोकयात्रविधायिनी → लोकयात्राविधायिनी. लोकयात्र → लोकयात्रा (yātrā: long final ā); the verse reads लोकयात्राविधायिनी.

665 एकाकिनी ekākinī

She who is the lone One

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Before creation there is nothing beside Her; the Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad (1.4.3) says the Self, being alone (ekākī), did not delight and wished for a second. She is the One without a second (ekam evādvitīyam, Chāndogya Upaniṣad 6.2.1).

666 भूमरूपा bhūma-rūpā

She whose form is the Bhūman, the boundless Plenitude

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. rūpa 'form, nature' is qualified by bhūman 'plenitude' in apposition, and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She whose form is the Plenitude'. bhūman is an n-stem; its n is dropped at the end of a compound member (bhūma-), a morphological change, not sandhi.

Analysis भूमा रूपम् यस्याः सा भूमरूपा
bhūmā rūpam yasyāḥ sā bhūmarūpā

Significance The Chāndogya Upaniṣad (7.23–24) teaches that 'the Plenitude (bhūmā) alone is happiness': where one sees nothing else, hears nothing else, knows nothing else, that is the Bhūman. Taking bhūman as 'manyness', the name also means that She is the sum of all that exists.

Uncertain bhūman can mean 'the Infinite' (Chāndogya 7.23–24) or 'manyness, the aggregate'; both are current for this name.

667 निर्द्वैता nir-dvaitā

She who is without duality

Sandhi निर्द्वैता = निस् + द्वैता (nis + dvaitā) — the final s of nis becomes r before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ)

Compound prādi-bahuvrīhi. nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone away', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She from whom duality has gone', i.e. in whom there is no duality. dvaita takes the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi.

Analysis निर्गतम् द्वैतम् यस्याः सा निर्द्वैता
nirgatam dvaitam yasyāḥ sā nirdvaitā

Significance Traditionally: nothing exists beside Her to make a second, so duality has no place in Her nature.

668 द्वैतवर्जिता dvaita-varjitā

She who is beyond duality

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa. The participle varjitā 'devoid, left out' is the head; dvaita 'duality' stands to it in the instrumental: 'devoid of duality'. The members meet with no sound change.

Analysis द्वैतेन वर्जिता द्वैतवर्जिता
dvaitena varjitā dvaitavarjitā

Significance With name 667 it states non-duality twice: no second exists in Her, and She remains untouched by the dualities of the world She manifests.

Where the names meet

Names 673–676 play on one root (√bṛh, whence brahman): bṛhatī, brāhmaṇī, brāhmī, brahmānandā.

The names

669 अन्नदा anna-dā

She who is the giver of food to all living things

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. -da 'giving' from √dā (suffix ka after a root in ā preceded by its object, Pāṇini 3.2.3 āto 'nupasarge kaḥ), feminine -dā; anna is its object: 'giver of food'.

Analysis अन्नम् ददाति इति अन्नदा
annam dadāti iti annadā

Significance Traditionally She is Annapūrṇā, the nourisher of all; the Taittirīya Upaniṣad (3.2) teaches 'food is Brahman', the first step of Bhṛgu's inquiry.

670 वसुदा vasu-dā

She who is the giver of wealth

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. As in name 669: -dā 'giving' from √dā is the head and vasu 'wealth' its object.

Analysis वसु ददाति इति वसुदा
vasu dadāti iti vasudā

Significance Traditionally wealth of every kind — material prosperity and the inner riches of virtue and knowledge — flows from Her.

671 वृद्धा vṛddhā

She who is ancient

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance She is older than all that exists, the first before creation; the Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad (4.3) addresses the One as the old man who totters with a staff, as well as the youth and the maiden.

672 ब्रह्मात्मैक्यस्वरूपिणी brahmātmaikya-svarūpiṇī

She whose very nature is the oneness of Brahman and the Self (Ātman)

Sandhi ब्रह्मात्म = ब्रह्म + आत्म (brahma + ātma) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); आत्मैक्य = आत्म + ऐक्य (ātma + aikya) — vṛddhi: a + ai → ai (Pāṇini 6.1.88 vṛddhir eci)

Compound karmadhāraya with the possessive suffix -in (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and dvandva). (1) brahman and ātman, the absolute and the Self, are joined as a dvandva (both stems lose their final n, a morphological change). (2) aikya 'oneness' takes them in the genitive: 'the oneness of Brahman and the Self' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) That oneness is identified with svarūpa 'own nature' (karmadhāraya). (4) The possessive suffix -in (Pāṇini 5.2.115 ata iniṭhanau) makes 'she who has this as her own nature'.

Analysis ब्रह्म च आत्मा च ब्रह्मात्मानौ; ब्रह्मात्मनोः ऐक्यम् ब्रह्मात्मैक्यम्; ब्रह्मात्मैक्यम् एव स्वरूपम् ब्रह्मात्मैक्यस्वरूपम्; तत् अस्याः अस्ति इति ब्रह्मात्मैक्यस्वरूपिणी
brahma ca ātmā ca brahmātmānau; brahmātmanoḥ aikyam brahmātmaikyam; brahmātmaikyam eva svarūpam brahmātmaikyasvarūpam; tat asyāḥ asti iti brahmātmaikyasvarūpiṇī

Significance The central teaching of the Upaniṣads (tat tvam asi, ahaṃ brahmāsmi): the Self and Brahman are not two. She is that identity itself, not a union of two things.

673 बृहती bṛhatī

She who is immense

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance She is Brahman, the word itself coming from the same root √bṛh 'to grow great'. Bṛhatī is also the name of a Vedic metre.

674 ब्राह्मणी brāhmaṇī

She who is Brāhmaṇī, belonging to Brahman

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Traditionally the brāhmaṇa is the type of sattva, the quality of clarity and calm, and so the name is read as 'She in whom sattva predominates'. Brāhmaṇī is also a name of the Śakti of Brahmā.

Uncertain Several readings are current: 'of the nature of Brahman', 'predominantly sāttvic' (the brāhmaṇa as sattva), and the Śakti of Brahmā; the source of the sāttvic gloss could not be confirmed.

675 ब्राह्मी brāhmī

She who is Brāhmī, the power of speech

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Brāhmī is a classical name of speech and of Sarasvatī; She is also the Śakti of Brahmā, first of the Mothers (Mātṛkās).

676 ब्रह्मानन्दा brahmānandā

She whose being is the bliss of Brahman

Sandhi ब्रह्मानन्दा = ब्रह्म + आनन्दा (brahma + ānandā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) brahma-ānanda 'the bliss of Brahman' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; brahman loses its n). (2) As a bahuvrīhi with the feminine -ā: 'She whose (very being) is the bliss of Brahman'. A karmadhāraya reading, 'She who is the bliss that is Brahman', gives the same sense.

Analysis ब्रह्मणः आनन्दः ब्रह्मानन्दः; ब्रह्मानन्दः यस्याः सा ब्रह्मानन्दा
brahmaṇaḥ ānandaḥ brahmānandaḥ; brahmānandaḥ yasyāḥ sā brahmānandā

Significance The Taittirīya Upaniṣad (2.4, 2.9) speaks of 'the bliss of Brahman' (ānandaṃ brahmaṇo vidvān), knowing which one fears nothing; She is that bliss.

677 बलिप्रिया bali-priyā

She who is fond of offerings (bali)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. priya 'dear' and bali 'offering' are joined as a bahuvrīhi with priya placed second (as in guḍapriya 'fond of molasses'): 'She to whom offerings are dear'. If bali is taken from balin 'the strong' (n dropped in the compound), the vigraha is balinaḥ priyāḥ yasyāḥ sā, 'She to whom the strong are dear'.

Analysis बलिः प्रियः यस्याः सा बलिप्रिया
baliḥ priyaḥ yasyāḥ sā balipriyā

Significance Traditionally the true offering is the self — the devotee's ego offered into Her; worship (pūjā) closes with bali to Her attendant powers.

Uncertain bali may also be read from balin 'the strong': 'She who loves the strong' (those strong in devotion and self-mastery).

Where the names meet

The second half holds three names, not five: 681, 682 and 683 śobhanā sulabhā gatiḥ, which Bhāskararāya counts as one name (śobhanā alone would repeat name 462).

The names

678 भाषारूपा bhāṣā-rūpā

She who is in the form of language

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. rūpa 'form' is identified with bhāṣā 'speech, language', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She whose form is language'.

Analysis भाषा रूपम् यस्याः सा भाषारूपा
bhāṣā rūpam yasyāḥ sā bhāṣārūpā

Significance Every language, sacred or common, is a form of Her as Vāk (speech); all words are Her body, as the alphabet (mātṛkā) is in Śrīvidyā.

679 बृहत्सेना bṛhat-senā

She who has a vast army

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. bṛhat 'vast' qualifies senā 'army', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She whose army is vast'. The feminine bṛhatī takes its masculine stem bṛhat before another member of a bahuvrīhi (puṃvadbhāva). t and s meet with no change.

Analysis बृहती सेना यस्याः सा बृहत्सेना
bṛhatī senā yasyāḥ sā bṛhatsenā

Significance In the Lalitopākhyāna Her hosts of śaktis, led by Mantriṇī and Daṇḍanāthā, march against Bhaṇḍāsura; inwardly they are Her countless powers.

680 भावाभावविवर्जिता bhāvābhāva-vivarjitā

She who is beyond being and non-being

Sandhi भावाभाव = भाव + अभाव (bhāva + abhāva) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner dvandva and nañ-tatpuruṣa). (1) a-bhāva 'non-being' (nañ-tatpuruṣa). (2) bhāva-abhāva 'being and non-being' (itaretara-dvandva). (3) The participle vivarjitā 'wholly devoid' is the head and takes the pair in the instrumental: 'devoid of being and non-being'.

Analysis न भावः अभावः; भावः च अभावः च भावाभावौ; भावाभावाभ्याम् विवर्जिता भावाभावविवर्जिता
na bhāvaḥ abhāvaḥ; bhāvaḥ ca abhāvaḥ ca bhāvābhāvau; bhāvābhāvābhyām vivarjitā bhāvābhāvavivarjitā

Significance She cannot be called existent or non-existent in the ordinary sense: 'then there was neither non-being nor being' (Ṛgveda 10.129.1); 'it is called neither being nor non-being' (Bhagavad Gītā 13.12).

681 सुखाराध्या sukhārādhyā

She who is easily worshipped

Sandhi सुखाराध्या = सुख + आराध्या (sukha + ārādhyā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa. The gerundive ārādhyā 'to be worshipped' is the head; sukha 'ease' stands to it in the instrumental of manner: 'to be worshipped with ease'. A reading with sukha as 'joy' — 'to be worshipped joyfully' — is also possible.

Analysis सुखेन आराध्या सुखाराध्या
sukhena ārādhyā sukhārādhyā

Significance Traditionally Her worship needs no harsh austerity: devotion, Her name and simple offerings please Her, and the worship is itself a joy.

682 शुभकरी śubha-karī

She who brings about what is auspicious

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. -kara 'making, doing' from √kṛ (suffix ṭa, which takes the feminine -ī: karī) is the head; śubha 'good, auspicious' is its object: 'maker of the auspicious'.

Analysis शुभम् करोति इति शुभकरी
śubham karoti iti śubhakarī

Significance She works good for Her devotees — prosperity here and liberation hereafter.

683 शोभनासुलभागतिः śobhanā-sulabhā-gatiḥ

She who is the auspicious goal, easily reached

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Bhāskararāya counts the three words śobhanā sulabhā gatiḥ as one name, since śobhanā alone would repeat name 462. She is the goal (gati) of all, and for those who love Her that goal is near.

Uncertain Not a compound: the adjectives keep their feminine -ā, which they would lose inside a karmadhāraya (śobhana-sulabha-gati); the name is three nominatives in apposition, counted as one name. gati can be 'goal' or 'path'.

Where the names meet

Names 684–692 are a run of royal names (rāja-, rājya-, sāmrājya-).

The names

684 राजराजेश्वरी rāja-rājeśvarī

She who is the sovereign of the kings of kings

Sandhi राजराजेश्वरी = राजराज + ईश्वरी (rājarāja + īśvarī) — guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) rāja-rāja 'king of kings' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa); rājan as the last member of a tatpuruṣa ends in -a (samāsānta ṭac, Pāṇini 5.4.91 rājāhaḥsakhibhyaṣ ṭac), and as first member loses its n. (2) īśvarī 'sovereign' is the head: 'sovereign of the kings of kings'. Rājarāja is also a title of Kubera, giving 'the sovereign of Kubera'.

Analysis राज्ञाम् राजा राजराजः; राजराजानाम् ईश्वरी राजराजेश्वरी
rājñām rājā rājarājaḥ; rājarājānām īśvarī rājarājeśvarī

Significance Rājarājeśvarī is one of the principal names of the Śrīvidyā Goddess: She rules over every ruler, the guardians of the world and the lord of wealth alike.

Uncertain rājarāja may be 'kings of kings' (emperors) or Kubera, the king of the yakṣas; both readings are current.

685 राज्यदायिनी rājya-dāyinī

She who gives dominion

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. dāyinī 'giving' is an agent noun in -in from √dā (with y inserted after a root in ā), feminine; it governs rājya 'kingdom, dominion' as its object.

Analysis राज्यम् ददाति इति राज्यदायिनी
rājyam dadāti iti rājyadāyinī

Significance She grants outward rule, and inwardly the sovereignty of the Self (svārājya), mastery over one's own mind and senses.

686 राज्यवल्लभा rājya-vallabhā

She to whom sovereignty is dear

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. vallabha 'dear, beloved' and rājya 'kingdom, sovereignty' are joined as a bahuvrīhi: 'She to whom sovereignty is dear'. Read as a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (rājyasya vallabhā) it means 'the beloved of the kingdom'.

Analysis राज्यम् वल्लभम् यस्याः सा राज्यवल्लभा
rājyam vallabham yasyāḥ sā rājyavallabhā

Significance With names 684–685 it shows Her as the sovereign who delights in rule, cherishes the realm, and gives dominion to Her devotees.

Uncertain vallabha also means 'lord, overseer' in some lexicons, which would support 'protector of kingdoms'; the bahuvrīhi 'to whom sovereignty is dear' and the tatpuruṣa 'beloved of the realm' are the plain readings.

687 राजत्कृपा rājat-kṛpā

She whose compassion shines forth

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. The participle rājat 'shining' qualifies kṛpā 'compassion', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She whose compassion shines'. The feminine rājantī takes its masculine stem rājat inside the bahuvrīhi (puṃvadbhāva); t and k meet with no change.

Analysis राजन्ती कृपा यस्याः सा राजत्कृपा
rājantī kṛpā yasyāḥ sā rājatkṛpā

Significance Her grace is not hidden: it shines, like a ruler's splendor, on all who turn to Her. The participle also echoes rājan 'king', continuing the royal names around it.

688 राजपीठनिवेशितनिजाश्रिता rāja-pīṭha-niveśita-nijāśritā

She who seats on royal thrones those who take refuge in Her

Sandhi निजाश्रिता = निज + आश्रिता (nija + āśritā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over inner ṣaṣṭhī-, saptamī-tatpuruṣa and karmadhāraya). (1) rāja-pīṭha 'royal seat, throne' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; rājan loses its n). (2) rājapīṭha-niveśita 'placed on the throne' (saptamī-tatpuruṣa with the causative participle). (3) nija-āśrita 'Her own dependents, those who take refuge in Her' (karmadhāraya). (4) The whole is a bahuvrīhi with the instrumental yayā: 'She by whom Her own dependents are seated on royal thrones'. The participle stands first, as is usual in a bahuvrīhi.

Analysis राज्ञः पीठम् राजपीठम्; राजपीठे निवेशिताः राजपीठनिवेशिताः; निजाः आश्रिताः निजाश्रिताः; राजपीठनिवेशिताः निजाश्रिताः यया सा राजपीठनिवेशितनिजाश्रिता
rājñaḥ pīṭham rājapīṭham; rājapīṭhe niveśitāḥ rājapīṭhaniveśitāḥ; nijāḥ āśritāḥ nijāśritāḥ; rājapīṭhaniveśitāḥ nijāśritāḥ yayā sā rājapīṭhaniveśitanijāśritā

Significance She raises Her devotees to sovereignty — worldly, and inwardly to the throne of the Self.

Where the names meet

rājyalakṣmīḥ (689) keeps its visarga before kośanāthā: lakṣmī is not a derived feminine in -ī and takes -ḥ in the nominative (compare 210).

The names

689 राज्यलक्ष्मीः rājya-lakṣmīḥ

She who is the Fortune (Lakṣmī) of the kingdom

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. lakṣmī 'fortune, prosperity, the goddess Lakṣmī' is the head and rājya 'kingdom' stands to it in the genitive: 'the fortune of the kingdom'. lakṣmī keeps the nominative -ḥ (it is not a derived feminine in -ī; compare name 210).

Analysis राज्यस्य लक्ष्मीः राज्यलक्ष्मीः
rājyasya lakṣmīḥ rājyalakṣmīḥ

Significance Rājyalakṣmī is the goddess of a realm's prosperity and royal splendor; where She dwells, the kingdom flourishes.

Corrected राज्यलक्ष्मी → राज्यलक्ष्मीः. As 210: nominative lakṣmīḥ; the verse reads राज्यलक्ष्मीः कोशनाथा.

690 कोशनाथा kośa-nāthā

She who is the mistress of the treasury

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. nāthā 'mistress, protector' is the head; kośa 'treasury' (or 'sheath') stands to it in the genitive.

Analysis कोशस्य नाथा कोशनाथा
kośasya nāthā kośanāthā

Significance As queen She owns the treasury of the realm. Kośa also means 'sheath', so the name is read inwardly as 'Lord of the five sheaths (kośas)' that cover the Self.

691 चतुरङ्गबलेश्वरी caturaṅga-baleśvarī

She who is sovereign of the fourfold army

Sandhi बलेश्वरी = बल + ईश्वरी (bala + īśvarī) — guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya and bahuvrīhi). (1) catur-aṅga 'having four limbs' (bahuvrīhi): the army's four arms — elephants, chariots, cavalry and infantry. (2) caturaṅga-bala 'the fourfold army' (karmadhāraya). (3) īśvarī 'sovereign' is the head: 'sovereign of the fourfold army'. catur's final r simply joins aṅga.

Analysis चत्वारि अङ्गानि यस्य तत् चतुरङ्गम्; चतुरङ्गम् बलम् चतुरङ्गबलम्; चतुरङ्गबलस्य ईश्वरी चतुरङ्गबलेश्वरी
catvāri aṅgāni yasya tat caturaṅgam; caturaṅgam balam caturaṅgabalam; caturaṅgabalasya īśvarī caturaṅgabaleśvarī

Significance The classical Indian army had four arms; in the Lalitopākhyāna Her own hosts — elephant, horse and chariot corps and foot-soldiers — fight under Her command.

692 साम्राज्यदायिनी sāmrājya-dāyinī

She who is the bestower of imperial dominion

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. As in name 685: dāyinī 'giving' (agent noun in -in from √dā) is the head and sāmrājya 'empire' its object.

Analysis साम्राज्यम् ददाति इति साम्राज्यदायिनी
sāmrājyam dadāti iti sāmrājyadāyinī

Significance Beyond a kingdom (685) She grants empire; traditionally the highest empire is liberation, sovereignty over all.

693 सत्यसन्धा satya-sandhā

She who is true to Her word

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. satya 'true' qualifies sandhā 'promise, compact', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She whose promise is true'. The feminine satyā takes its masculine stem satya inside the bahuvrīhi (puṃvadbhāva).

Analysis सत्या सन्धा यस्याः सा सत्यसन्धा
satyā sandhā yasyāḥ sā satyasandhā

Significance Her promise of protection to those who take refuge in Her never fails.

694 सागरमेखला sāgara-mekhalā

She who is girdled by the oceans

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. mekhalā 'girdle' is identified with sāgara 'the ocean(s)', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She whose girdle is the ocean'.

Analysis सागराः मेखला यस्याः सा सागरमेखला
sāgarāḥ mekhalā yasyāḥ sā sāgaramekhalā

Significance 'Ocean-girdled' is a classical epithet of the Earth; She is the Earth, with the encircling seas as Her waistband.

695 दीक्षिता dīkṣitā

She who is consecrated (dīkṣitā)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Traditionally read both ways: She is the consecrated sacrificer of the cosmic rite, and She is the one in whom initiation (dīkṣā) resides and who gives it to the devotee, removing bondage.

Uncertain The participle is passive ('consecrated'), but the name is commonly explained as 'She who initiates', taking dīkṣitā as 'possessed of dīkṣā'; both are current.

696 दैत्यशमनी daitya-śamanī

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (with an agent noun). śamanī 'one who quells' is an agent noun in -ana from the causative of √śam 'to be calm', feminine; daitya 'demon' stands to it as the object, in the genitive.

Analysis दैत्यानाम् शमनी दैत्यशमनी
daityānām śamanī daityaśamanī

Significance Outwardly She destroys the demon hosts of the Purāṇas; inwardly She quells the demonic tendencies in the heart.

697 सर्वलोकवशङ्करी sarva-loka-vaśaṅkarī

She who keeps all the worlds under Her control

Sandhi वशङ्करी = वशम् + करी (vaśam + karī) — the m (an augment inserted after the object, as in priyaṅkara) becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ) and then the nasal of the following k's class, ṅ (8.4.58 anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ)

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) sarva-loka 'all the worlds' (karmadhāraya). (2) vaśaṅ-karī 'one who brings under control' (vaśa 'control' + kara from √kṛ, with the augment m after vaśa and the feminine -ī). (3) The worlds are the object of that action: 'She who brings all the worlds under Her sway'.

Analysis सर्वे लोकाः सर्वलोकाः; सर्वलोकान् वशम् करोति इति सर्वलोकवशङ्करी
sarve lokāḥ sarvalokāḥ; sarvalokān vaśam karoti iti sarvalokavaśaṅkarī

Significance All beings move by Her will; in worship She is invoked to draw all to Her (vaśīkaraṇa), and the true subjugation is of one's own mind.

698 सर्वार्थदात्री sarvārtha-dātrī

She who grants all desires

Sandhi सर्वार्थ = सर्व + अर्थ (sarva + artha) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) sarva-artha 'all aims, all things sought' (karmadhāraya). (2) dātrī 'giver' (agent noun in -tṛ from √dā, feminine) is the head and takes them as its object in the genitive.

Analysis सर्वे अर्थाः सर्वार्थाः; सर्वार्थानाम् दात्री सर्वार्थदात्री
sarve arthāḥ sarvārthāḥ; sarvārthānām dātrī sarvārthadātrī

Significance Artha is all that is sought; traditionally the name covers all four aims of life — dharma, artha, kāma and mokṣa.

699 सावित्री sāvitrī

She who is Sāvitrī, the impelling power of the Sun that brings the worlds forth

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Sāvitrī is the Ṛgvedic verse to Savitṛ (the Gāyatrī) and its goddess; from the root √sū 'to bring forth' the name is read as the creative power that impels the universe.

700 सच्चिदानन्दरूपिणी sac-cid-ānanda-rūpiṇī

She who is of the nature of existence, consciousness and bliss

Sandhi सच्चित् = सत् + चित् (sat + cit) — ścutva: t becomes c before c (Pāṇini 8.4.40 stoḥ ścunā ścuḥ); चिदानन्द = चित् + आनन्द (cit + ānanda) — jaśtva: a final t becomes d before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.39 jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte)

Compound karmadhāraya with the possessive suffix -in (Pāṇini 5.2.115 ata iniṭhanau) (over an inner samāhāra-dvandva). (1) sat-cit-ānanda 'being, consciousness and bliss' taken together as one whole (samāhāra-dvandva). (2) That whole is identified with rūpa 'form, nature' (karmadhāraya). (3) The possessive suffix -in makes 'She whose form is being-consciousness-bliss'.

Analysis सत् च चित् च आनन्दः च सच्चिदानन्दम्; सच्चिदानन्दम् एव रूपम् सच्चिदानन्दरूपम्; तत् अस्याः अस्ति इति सच्चिदानन्दरूपिणी
sat ca cit ca ānandaḥ ca saccidānandam; saccidānandam eva rūpam saccidānandarūpam; tat asyāḥ asti iti saccidānandarūpiṇī

Significance Saccidānanda is the Vedāntic description of Brahman — not three qualities but one reality seen three ways — and She is that reality.

Śloka 137names 701–707

देशकालापरिच्छिन्ना सर्वगा सर्वमोहिनी ।
सरस्वती शास्त्रमयी गुहाम्बा गुह्यरूपिणी ॥ १३७ ॥

deśakālāparicchinnā sarvagā sarvamohinī |
sarasvatī śāstramayī guhāmbā guhyarūpiṇī || 137 ||

The names, separated

701देश-कालापरिच्छिन्नाdeśa-kālāparicchinnā702सर्व-गाsarva-gā703सर्व-मोहिनीsarva-mohinī

704सरस्वतीsarasvatī705शास्त्र-मयीśāstra-mayī706गुहाम्बाguhāmbā707गुह्य-रूपिणीguhya-rūpiṇī

Translation

701She who is not limited by space and time; 702She who is all-pervading, present everywhere; 703She who deludes all;

704She who is Sarasvatī, the goddess of knowledge and speech; 705She who consists of the scriptures; 706She who is the mother of Guha (Skanda); 707She who has a secret form.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish

देशdeśaplace, space
कालkālatime
अपरिच्छिन्नाaparicchinnāunlimited, not boundeda- 'not' + pari + √chid 'to cut', past participle, feminine
702 सर्वगा sarva-gā
सर्वsarvaall, everything

सरस्वतीsarasvatīSarasvatī, goddess of learning and speech; 'she who has pools (of water)'saras 'pool, lake' + the possessive suffix -vat, feminine -ī
705 शास्त्रमयी śāstra-mayī
शास्त्रमयीśāstramayīconsisting of the scriptures, made of śāstraśāstra 'teaching, scripture' + the suffix -maya 'consisting of', feminine -ī

Where the names meet

In deśakālāparicchinnā (701) the negative a- of aparicchinnā is hidden in the long ā of kālā-: the name says 'not limited' by space and time.

The names

701 देशकालापरिच्छिन्ना deśa-kālāparicchinnā

She who is not limited by space and time

Sandhi कालापरिच्छिन्ना = काल + अपरिच्छिन्ना (kāla + aparicchinnā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); परिच्छिन्ना = परि + छिन्ना (pari + chinnā) — a short vowel before ch takes the augment t (Pāṇini 6.1.73 che ca), which becomes c by ścutva (8.4.40): pari + chinnā → paricchinnā

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner dvandva and nañ-tatpuruṣa). (1) deśa-kāla 'space and time' (itaretara-dvandva). (2) a-paricchinnā 'not limited, not cut off' (nañ-tatpuruṣa on the participle of pari + √chid). (3) The pair stands in the instrumental of agent: 'not limited by space and time'.

Analysis देशः च कालः च देशकालौ; न परिच्छिन्ना अपरिच्छिन्ना; देशकालाभ्याम् अपरिच्छिन्ना देशकालापरिच्छिन्ना
deśaḥ ca kālaḥ ca deśakālau; na paricchinnā aparicchinnā; deśakālābhyām aparicchinnā deśakālāparicchinnā

Significance Whatever is in space and time is bounded; She, the ground of space and time, is bounded by neither — present everywhere and at every moment.

702 सर्वगा sarva-gā

She who is all-pervading, present everywhere

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. -ga 'going' from √gam (suffix ḍa after sarva and similar words, Pāṇini 3.2.48 antātyantādhvadūrapārasarvānanteṣu ḍaḥ), feminine -gā; sarva is its object: 'going to all, reaching everything'.

Analysis सर्वम् गच्छति इति सर्वगा
sarvam gacchati iti sarvagā

Significance She pervades every world and every being, moving and unmoving, as the one consciousness in all.

703 सर्वमोहिनी sarva-mohinī

She who deludes all

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. mohinī 'deluding, enchanting' is an agent noun in -in from the causative of √muh 'to be bewildered', feminine; it governs sarva 'all' as its object.

Analysis सर्वान् मोहयति इति सर्वमोहिनी
sarvān mohayati iti sarvamohinī

Significance By Her Māyā even the wise are bewildered; the same power that binds is withdrawn by Her grace.

704 सरस्वती sarasvatī

She who is Sarasvatī, the goddess of knowledge and speech

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Sarasvatī is the river-goddess of the Ṛgveda who became the goddess of speech and learning; She is that flowing knowledge.

705 शास्त्रमयी śāstra-mayī

She who consists of the scriptures

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance The scriptures are Her form; traditionally the sciences and sacred texts are described as Her limbs.

706 गुहाम्बा guhāmbā

She who is the mother of Guha (Skanda)

Sandhi गुहाम्बा = गुह + अम्बा (guha + ambā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); the same surface results from guhā + ambā (ā + a → ā), which gives the second reading

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (alternatively saptamī-tatpuruṣa). ambā 'mother' is the head. With guha 'Skanda' in the genitive: 'the mother of Guha'. With guhā 'cave' in the locative: 'the mother in the cave (of the heart)'. The fused long ā hides whether the first member is guha or guhā.

Analysis गुहस्य अम्बा गुहाम्बा; अथवा गुहायाम् अम्बा गुहाम्बा
guhasya ambā guhāmbā; athavā guhāyām ambā guhāmbā

Significance As Pārvatī She is the mother of Skanda; read as guhā, She is the Mother hidden in the cave of the heart, where the Upaniṣads place the Self.

Uncertain The fused ā allows guha 'Skanda' or guhā 'cave'; both readings are traditional.

707 गुह्यरूपिणी guhya-rūpiṇī

She who has a secret form

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya with the possessive suffix -in (Pāṇini 5.2.115 ata iniṭhanau). (1) guhya 'secret' qualifies rūpa 'form' (karmadhāraya). (2) The possessive suffix -in makes 'She who has a secret form'.

Analysis गुह्यम् रूपम् गुह्यरूपम्; तत् अस्याः अस्ति इति गुह्यरूपिणी
guhyam rūpam guhyarūpam; tat asyāḥ asti iti guhyarūpiṇī

Significance Her true form is hidden from the senses and revealed only in the teacher's instruction and within; Her mantra and its inner sense are kept secret in Śrīvidyā.

Śloka 138names 708–713

सर्वोपाधिविनिर्मुक्ता सदाशिवपतिव्रता ।
सम्प्रदायेश्वरी साध्वी गुरुमण्डलरूपिणी ॥ १३८ ॥

sarvopādhivinirmuktā sadāśivapativratā |
sampradāyeśvarī sādhvī gurumaṇḍalarūpiṇī || 138 ||

The names, separated ° form as a name on its own; in the recitation above it joins its neighbour

708सर्वोपाधि-विनिर्मुक्ताsarvopādhi-vinirmuktā709सदाशिव-पतिव्रताsadāśiva-pativratā

710सम्प्रदायेश्वरीsampradāyeśvarī711साधु°sādhu712ई°ī713गुरु-मण्डल-रूपिणीguru-maṇḍala-rūpiṇī

Translation

708She who is free of all limiting adjuncts (upādhi); 709She who is the devoted wife of Sadāśiva;

710She who is the sovereign of the sacred traditions; 711She who is sādhu, the good and upright; 712She who is the syllable ī (kāmakalā); 713She whose form is the circle (lineage) of the gurus.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish
708 सर्वोपाधिविनिर्मुक्ता sarvopādhi-vinirmuktā
सर्वsarvaall
उपाधिupādhilimiting adjunct, a condition that seems to limit the limitless
विनिर्मुक्ताvinirmuktāwholly released, entirely freevi + nis + √muc 'to release', past participle, feminine
709 सदाशिवपतिव्रता sadāśiva-pativratā
सदाsadāalways, ever
शिवśivaauspicious; Śiva
पतिpatihusband, lord
व्रताvratāvow, devotionvrata 'vow', with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi
710 सम्प्रदायेश्वरी sampradāyeśvarī
सम्प्रदायsampradāyatradition handed down from teacher to disciplesam + pra + √dā 'to give': what is fully handed over
ईश्वरीīśvarīsovereign, ruling ladyfeminine of īśvara
711 साधु sādhu
साधुsādhugood, upright, right, excellent√sādh 'to accomplish' + the Uṇādi suffix -u; used here as a name of the Goddess
712 ई ī
ईīthe long vowel ī; in Śrīvidyā the syllable of kāmakalā
713 गुरुमण्डलरूपिणी guru-maṇḍala-rūpiṇī
गुरुguruteacher, preceptor
मण्डलmaṇḍalacircle, assembly, lineage
रूपिणीrūpiṇīhaving the formrūpa + -in, feminine

Where the names meet

साध्वी = साधु + ई (sādhu + ī) — yaṇ: u becomes v before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci)

साध्वी is two names in Bhāskararāya's division: 711 sādhu and 712 ī, since sādhvī is already name 128.

The names

708 सर्वोपाधिविनिर्मुक्ता sarvopādhi-vinirmuktā

She who is free of all limiting adjuncts (upādhi)

Sandhi सर्वोपाधि = सर्व + उपाधि (sarva + upādhi) — guṇa: a + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ); निर्मुक्ता = निस् + मुक्ता (nis + muktā) — the final s of nis becomes r before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ)

Compound pañcamī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) sarva-upādhi 'all limiting adjuncts' (karmadhāraya). (2) The participle vinirmuktā 'wholly released' is the head and takes them in the ablative: 'released from all limiting adjuncts'.

Analysis सर्वे उपाधयः सर्वोपाधयः; सर्वोपाधिभ्यः विनिर्मुक्ता सर्वोपाधिविनिर्मुक्ता
sarve upādhayaḥ sarvopādhayaḥ; sarvopādhibhyaḥ vinirmuktā sarvopādhivinirmuktā

Significance In Vedānta body, mind and name are upādhis that seem to limit pure consciousness; She, as that consciousness, is untouched by all of them.

709 सदाशिवपतिव्रता sadāśiva-pativratā

She who is the devoted wife of Sadāśiva

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner bahuvrīhi and karmadhāraya). (1) sadā-śiva 'ever auspicious', the name of the fifth Brahma. (2) pati-vratā 'she whose vow is her husband', the faithful wife (bahuvrīhi). (3) Sadāśiva stands to her in the genitive: 'the faithful wife of Sadāśiva'.

Analysis सदा शिवः सदाशिवः; पतिः व्रतम् यस्याः सा पतिव्रता; सदाशिवस्य पतिव्रता सदाशिवपतिव्रता
sadā śivaḥ sadāśivaḥ; patiḥ vratam yasyāḥ sā pativratā; sadāśivasya pativratā sadāśivapativratā

Significance In Śrīvidyā Sadāśiva is the highest of the five Brahmas, the Lord who grants grace; She is inseparable from Him as His faithful consort and power.

710 सम्प्रदायेश्वरी sampradāyeśvarī

She who is the sovereign of the sacred traditions

Sandhi सम्प्रदायेश्वरी = सम्प्रदाय + ईश्वरी (sampradāya + īśvarī) — guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. īśvarī 'sovereign' is the head; sampradāya 'tradition handed down' stands to it in the genitive.

Analysis सम्प्रदायस्य ईश्वरी सम्प्रदायेश्वरी
sampradāyasya īśvarī sampradāyeśvarī

Significance Sampradāya is teaching passed from teacher to disciple without a break; She presides over it and is its source, so knowledge received in the lineage is received from Her.

711 साधु sādhu

She who is sādhu, the good and upright

Sandhi साध्वी = साधु + ई (sādhu + ī) — yaṇ: u becomes v before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci). The surface sādhvī is read by Bhāskararāya as two names, 711 sādhu and 712 ī, because sādhvī as one word would repeat name 128; the junction between them is this sandhi.

Compound not a compound

Significance Bhāskararāya divides the surface sādhvī into two names so that name 128 (sādhvī) is not repeated: 711 sādhu 'the good' and 712 ī. She is goodness itself, straight and even toward all.

Uncertain Bhāskararāya's own gloss of sādhu could not be checked against a printed Saubhāgyabhāskara; 'equanimity' (the earlier meaning) may reflect it.

Variants Lists that do not follow Bhāskararāya read sādhvī here as one name, repeating name 128.

712 ई ī

She who is the syllable ī (kāmakalā)

Sandhi साध्वी = साधु + ई (sādhu + ī) — yaṇ: u becomes v before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci). The surface sādhvī is read by Bhāskararāya as two names, 711 sādhu and 712 ī, because sādhvī as one word would repeat name 128; the junction between them is this sandhi.

Compound not a compound

Significance In Śrīvidyā the long vowel ī is the letter of kāmakalā, the union of Śiva and Śakti that is the seed of creation (compare name 322, kāmakalārūpā); it stands in Her Pañcadaśī mantra.

Uncertain The kāmakalā reading is the Śrīvidyā one; single-syllable lexicons also give ī as a name of Lakṣmī. Bhāskararāya's exact gloss could not be checked against a printed text.

Variants Lists that do not follow Bhāskararāya read sādhvī (711–712) as one name, repeating name 128, and reach 1,000 by dividing elsewhere.

713 गुरुमण्डलरूपिणी guru-maṇḍala-rūpiṇī

She whose form is the circle (lineage) of the gurus

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya with the possessive suffix -in (Pāṇini 5.2.115 ata iniṭhanau) (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) guru-maṇḍala 'the circle of gurus' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) That circle is identified with rūpa 'form' (karmadhāraya). (3) The possessive -in: 'She whose form is the circle of gurus'.

Analysis गुरूणाम् मण्डलम् गुरुमण्डलम्; गुरुमण्डलम् एव रूपम् गुरुमण्डलरूपम्; तत् अस्याः अस्ति इति गुरुमण्डलरूपिणी
gurūṇām maṇḍalam gurumaṇḍalam; gurumaṇḍalam eva rūpam gurumaṇḍalarūpam; tat asyāḥ asti iti gurumaṇḍalarūpiṇī

Significance In Śrīvidyā worship the lineage of teachers — the divine, the perfected and the human streams (divyaugha, siddhaugha, mānavaugha) — is worshipped as Her own form.

Corrected गुरूमण्डलरूपिणी → गुरुमण्डलरूपिणी. गुरूमण्डल → गुरुमण्डल (guru: short u).

Śloka 139names 714–722

कुलोत्तीर्णा भगाराध्या माया मधुमती मही ।
गणाम्बा गुह्यकाराध्या कोमलाङ्गी गुरुप्रिया ॥ १३९ ॥

kulottīrṇā bhagārādhyā māyā madhumatī mahī |
gaṇāmbā guhyakārādhyā komalāṅgī gurupriyā || 139 ||

The names, separated

714कुलोत्तीर्णाkulottīrṇā715भगाराध्याbhagārādhyā716मायाmāyā717मधुमतीmadhumatī718महीmahī

719गणाम्बाgaṇāmbā720गुह्यकाराध्याguhyakārādhyā721कोमलाङ्गीkomalāṅgī722गुरु-प्रियाguru-priyā
