714She who transcends the kula (the senses); 715She who is worshipped in the sun's disc; 716She who is Māyā, the power of illusion; 717She who is full of sweetness; 718She who is the Earth;

719She who is the mother of the Gaṇas, Śiva's attendants; 720She who is worshipped by the Guhyakas; 721She whose limbs are soft and tender; 722She who is beloved of the gurus.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish
714 कुलोत्तीर्णा kulottīrṇā
कुलkulakula: the group (of the senses); family; the Kaula path; the region of the lower cakras
उत्तीर्णाuttīrṇāhaving crossed over, gone beyondud + √tṝ 'to cross', past participle, feminine
715 भगाराध्या bhagārādhyā
भगbhagathe orb of the sun; also the downward triangle (trikoṇa); excellence, fortune
आराध्याārādhyāto be worshippedā + √rādh, gerundive, feminine
716 माया māyā
मायाmāyāMāyā, the power that veils reality and projects the world; illusion
717 मधुमती madhumatī
मधुमतीmadhumatīfull of honey, sweetmadhu 'honey, sweetness' + the possessive suffix -mat, feminine -ī
718 मही mahī
महीmahīthe Earth; 'the great one'feminine of mah 'great'
719 गणाम्बा gaṇāmbā
गणgaṇatroop; the Gaṇas, Śiva's attendants
अम्बाambāmother
720 गुह्यकाराध्या guhyakārādhyā
गुह्यकguhyakaGuhyaka, a class of semi-divine beings attending Kuberafrom guhya 'hidden'
आराध्याārādhyāto be worshippedā + √rādh, gerundive, feminine
721 कोमलाङ्गी komalāṅgī
कोमलkomalasoft, tender, delicate
अङ्गीaṅgīlimb, bodyaṅga, with the feminine -ī of the bahuvrīhi
722 गुरुप्रिया guru-priyā
गुरुguruteacher, preceptor; Śiva as the supreme Guru
प्रियाpriyābeloved, dear

Where the names meet

bhagārādhyā (715) and guhyakārādhyā (720) both end in ārādhyā 'to be worshipped', its ā fused with the preceding a.

The names

714 कुलोत्तीर्णा kulottīrṇā

She who transcends the kula (the senses)

Sandhi कुलोत्तीर्णा = कुल + उत्तीर्णा (kula + uttīrṇā) — guṇa: a + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ); उत्तीर्णा = उद् + तीर्णा (ud + tīrṇā) — the d of ud becomes voiceless t before t (cartva, Pāṇini 8.4.55 khari ca)

Compound dvitīyā-tatpuruṣa. The participle uttīrṇā 'having crossed over' is the head; kula stands to it as the thing crossed, in the accusative: 'She who has crossed beyond the kula'.

Analysis कुलम् उत्तीर्णा कुलोत्तीर्णा
kulam uttīrṇā kulottīrṇā

Significance Kula is a word of many senses in Śrīvidyā; taken as the group of the senses, She is beyond their reach. Taken as the Kaula path, She is also beyond every particular path of worship.

Uncertain kula has several traditional senses here — the senses, the Kaula path, the family of the knower–knowing–known; the reading as 'the senses' follows the earlier meaning.

715 भगाराध्या bhagārādhyā

She who is worshipped in the sun's disc

Sandhi भगाराध्या = भग + आराध्या (bhaga + ārādhyā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound saptamī-tatpuruṣa. The gerundive ārādhyā 'to be worshipped' is the head; bhaga stands to it in the locative, as the place of worship: 'to be worshipped in the bhaga'.

Analysis भगे आराध्या भगाराध्या
bhage ārādhyā bhagārādhyā

Significance Bhaga is also a name of the Sun (one of the Ādityas), and She is meditated on within the solar orb; in Śrīcakra worship bhaga is also the central triangle, Her seat.

Uncertain bhaga can be taken as the sun's disc or as the trikoṇa of Śrīcakra; the meaning follows the first.

716 माया māyā

She who is Māyā, the power of illusion

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance 'Know Prakṛti to be Māyā, and the great Lord the wielder of Māyā' (Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad 4.10). Her Māyā veils and projects the world, and by Her grace it is removed.

717 मधुमती madhumatī

She who is full of sweetness

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Her nature is sweet as honey to the devotee; madhumatī is also the name of an advanced stage of yoga in the commentary on the Yoga Sūtras, and is traditionally read here too.

718 मही mahī

She who is the Earth

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance She is the great Earth that bears and nourishes all beings, as in name 694.

719 गणाम्बा gaṇāmbā

She who is the mother of the Gaṇas, Śiva's attendants

Sandhi गणाम्बा = गण + अम्बा (gaṇa + ambā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. ambā 'mother' is the head; gaṇa 'the troops (of Śiva)' stands to it in the genitive.

Analysis गणानाम् अम्बा गणाम्बा
gaṇānām ambā gaṇāmbā

Significance As Pārvatī She is mother to Śiva's hosts and to Gaṇeśa, their lord.

720 गुह्यकाराध्या guhyakārādhyā

She who is worshipped by the Guhyakas

Sandhi गुह्यकाराध्या = गुह्यक + आराध्या (guhyaka + ārādhyā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa. The gerundive ārādhyā is the head; the Guhyakas stand to it in the instrumental of agent: 'to be worshipped by the Guhyakas'.

Analysis गुह्यकैः आराध्या गुह्यकाराध्या
guhyakaiḥ ārādhyā guhyakārādhyā

Significance The Guhyakas, 'hidden ones', are the attendants of Kubera, guardians of hidden treasure; even such beings worship Her.

721 कोमलाङ्गी komalāṅgī

She whose limbs are soft and tender

Sandhi कोमलाङ्गी = कोमल + अङ्गी (komala + aṅgī) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi. komala 'soft, tender' qualifies aṅga 'limb', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She whose limbs are soft'. A bahuvrīhi ending in a word for a body part forms its feminine in -ī.

Analysis कोमलानि अङ्गानि यस्याः सा कोमलाङ्गी
komalāni aṅgāni yasyāḥ sā komalāṅgī

Significance Her form is gentle and graceful — the gentleness of the Mother toward Her children.

722 गुरुप्रिया guru-priyā

She who is beloved of the gurus

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (alternatively bahuvrīhi). As a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, priyā 'beloved' is the head: 'the beloved of the gurus' (or of the supreme Guru, Śiva). As a bahuvrīhi: 'She to whom the gurus are dear'.

Analysis गुरूणाम् प्रिया गुरुप्रिया; अथवा गुरवः प्रियाः यस्याः सा गुरुप्रिया
gurūṇām priyā gurupriyā; athavā guravaḥ priyāḥ yasyāḥ sā gurupriyā

Significance She is dear to the teachers of the lineage, and the gurus are dear to Her; read with guru as Śiva, She is the beloved of the supreme Teacher.

Śloka 140names 723–727

स्वतन्त्रा सर्वतन्त्रेशी दक्षिणामूर्तिरूपिणी ।
सनकादिसमाराध्या शिवज्ञानप्रदायिनी ॥ १४० ॥

svatantrā sarvatantreśī dakṣiṇāmūrtirūpiṇī |
sanakādisamārādhyā śivajñānapradāyinī || 140 ||

The names, separated

723स्वतन्त्राsvatantrā724सर्व-तन्त्रेशीsarva-tantreśī725दक्षिणामूर्ति-रूपिणीdakṣiṇāmūrti-rūpiṇī

726सनकादि-समाराध्याsanakādi-samārādhyā727शिव-ज्ञान-प्रदायिनीśiva-jñāna-pradāyinī

Translation

723She who is independent, subject to none; 724She who is the goddess of all Tantras; 725She who is in the form of Dakṣiṇāmūrti;

726She who is worshipped by Sanaka and the other sages; 727She who bestows the knowledge of Śiva.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish
723 स्वतन्त्रा svatantrā
स्वsvaown, self
तन्त्राtantrārule, authority, governing principletantra, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi
724 सर्वतन्त्रेशी sarva-tantreśī
सर्वsarvaall
तन्त्रtantraTantra, a body of scripture and ritual teaching
ईशीīśīsovereign, mistressfeminine of īśa, from √īś 'to rule'
725 दक्षिणामूर्तिरूपिणी dakṣiṇāmūrti-rūpiṇī
दक्षिणाdakṣiṇāsouthward, facing south; also 'gracious, skilled'
मूर्तिmūrtiform, embodiment
रूपिणीrūpiṇīhaving the formrūpa + -in, feminine
726 सनकादिसमाराध्या sanakādi-samārādhyā
सनकsanakaSanaka, eldest of the four mind-born sons of Brahmā
आदिādibeginning; 'and the others' at the end of a compound
समाराध्याsamārādhyāto be fully worshippedsam + ā + √rādh, gerundive, feminine
727 शिवज्ञानप्रदायिनी śiva-jñāna-pradāyinī
शिवśivaŚiva; auspicious
ज्ञानjñānaknowledge
प्रदायिनीpradāyinībestowing, grantingpra + √dā 'to give' + -in, feminine

Where the names meet

Names 725–726 belong together: Dakṣiṇāmūrti and His disciples, Sanaka and the other sages.

The names

723 स्वतन्त्रा svatantrā

She who is independent, subject to none

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. sva 'own' qualifies tantra 'rule, governing principle', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She whose rule is Her own', i.e. dependent on none.

Analysis स्वम् तन्त्रम् यस्याः सा स्वतन्त्रा
svam tantram yasyāḥ sā svatantrā

Significance Absolute freedom (svātantrya) is the nature of supreme Consciousness: She depends on nothing, and everything depends on Her.

724 सर्वतन्त्रेशी sarva-tantreśī

She who is the goddess of all Tantras

Sandhi तन्त्रेशी = तन्त्र + ईशी (tantra + īśī) — guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) sarva-tantra 'all the Tantras' (karmadhāraya). (2) īśī 'sovereign, mistress' is the head and takes them in the genitive.

Analysis सर्वाणि तन्त्राणि सर्वतन्त्राणि; सर्वतन्त्राणाम् ईशी सर्वतन्त्रेशी
sarvāṇi tantrāṇi sarvatantrāṇi; sarvatantrāṇām īśī sarvatantreśī

Significance All the Tantras teach of Her and are Her word; She is their ruler and their goal.

725 दक्षिणामूर्तिरूपिणी dakṣiṇāmūrti-rūpiṇī

She who is in the form of Dakṣiṇāmūrti

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya with the possessive suffix -in (Pāṇini 5.2.115 ata iniṭhanau). (1) Dakṣiṇāmūrti, the name of Śiva as teacher, is identified with rūpa 'form' (karmadhāraya). (2) The possessive -in: 'She who has the form of Dakṣiṇāmūrti'. Within the proper name, dakṣiṇā is 'southward' (the form faces south), and mūrti 'form'.

Analysis दक्षिणामूर्तिः एव रूपम् दक्षिणामूर्तिरूपम्; तत् अस्याः अस्ति इति दक्षिणामूर्तिरूपिणी
dakṣiṇāmūrtiḥ eva rūpam dakṣiṇāmūrtirūpam; tat asyāḥ asti iti dakṣiṇāmūrtirūpiṇī

Significance Dakṣiṇāmūrti is Śiva as the silent teacher, facing south beneath the banyan tree, who dispels the doubts of the sages by silence; She, inseparable from Śiva, is that teacher.

Uncertain The sense of dakṣiṇā in the proper name is explained variously ('facing south', 'gracious', 'skilled'); 'facing south' is the usual one.

726 सनकादिसमाराध्या sanakādi-samārādhyā

She who is worshipped by Sanaka and the other sages

Sandhi सनकादि = सनक + आदि (sanaka + ādi) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner bahuvrīhi). (1) sanaka-ādi 'those of whom Sanaka is the first' (bahuvrīhi): Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanātana and Sanatkumāra. (2) The gerundive samārādhyā 'to be fully worshipped' is the head and takes them in the instrumental of agent.

Analysis सनकः आदिः येषाम् ते सनकादयः; सनकादिभिः समाराध्या सनकादिसमाराध्या
sanakaḥ ādiḥ yeṣām te sanakādayaḥ; sanakādibhiḥ samārādhyā sanakādisamārādhyā

Significance Sanaka and his brothers, the ever-youthful sages, are the disciples of Dakṣiṇāmūrti (name 725); they too worship Her.

727 शिवज्ञानप्रदायिनी śiva-jñāna-pradāyinī

She who bestows the knowledge of Śiva

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) śiva-jñāna 'knowledge of Śiva' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; also read as a karmadhāraya, 'the auspicious knowledge'). (2) pradāyinī 'bestowing' (agent noun in -in from pra + √dā) is the head and governs that knowledge as its object.

Analysis शिवस्य ज्ञानम् शिवज्ञानम्; शिवज्ञानम् प्रददाति इति शिवज्ञानप्रदायिनी
śivasya jñānam śivajñānam; śivajñānam pradadāti iti śivajñānapradāyinī

Significance Traditionally Śiva is known only through His Śakti, the doorway to Him; She grants the knowledge in which the knower becomes Śiva.

Śloka 141names 728–734

चित्कला ऽऽनन्दकलिका प्रेमरूपा प्रियङ्करी ।
नामपारायणप्रीता नन्दिविद्या नटेश्वरी ॥ १४१ ॥

citkalā ''nandakalikā premarūpā priyaṅkarī |
nāmapārāyaṇaprītā nandividyā naṭeśvarī || 141 ||

The names, separated ° form as a name on its own; in the recitation above it joins its neighbour

728चित्-कलाcit-kalā729आनन्द-कलिका°ānanda-kalikā730प्रेम-रूपाprema-rūpā731प्रियङ्करीpriyaṅkarī

732नाम-पारायण-प्रीताnāma-pārāyaṇa-prītā733नन्दि-विद्याnandi-vidyā734नटेश्वरीnaṭeśvarī

Translation

728She who is the digit (kalā) of consciousness; 729She who is the bud of bliss; 730She whose form is love; 731She who grants what is dear to Her devotees;

732She who is pleased by the recitation of Her names; 733She who is the Vidyā (mantra) of Nandi; 734She who is the consort of Naṭeśvara (Śiva, Lord of the dance).

Word by word

SanskritEnglish
728 चित्कला cit-kalā
चित्citconsciousness
कलाkalādigit (of the moon), a small part; subtle power
729 आनन्दकलिका ānanda-kalikā
आनन्दānandabliss
कलिकाkalikābud; also a small digit
730 प्रेमरूपा prema-rūpā
प्रेमन्premanlove, affectionappears as prema- in the compound
रूपाrūpāhaving the formrūpa, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi
731 प्रियङ्करी priyaṅkarī
प्रियpriyawhat is dear, pleasing
करीkarīmaking, doing√kṛ 'to do, make', feminine -ī
732 नामपारायणप्रीता nāma-pārāyaṇa-prītā
नामन्nāmannameappears as nāma- in the compound
पारायणpārāyaṇarecitation from beginning to endpāra 'the far shore' + ayana 'going': going through to the end
प्रीताprītāpleased, delighted√prī 'to please', past participle, feminine
733 नन्दिविद्या nandi-vidyā
नन्दिन्nandinNandi (Nandikeśvara), Śiva's attendant and devoteeappears as nandi- in the compound
विद्याvidyāknowledge; in Śrīvidyā, a mantra of the Goddess
734 नटेश्वरी naṭeśvarī
नटnaṭadancer, actor
ईश्वरीīśvarīsovereign; the consort of Īśvarafeminine of īśvara

Where the names meet

चित्कलाऽऽनन्दकलिका = चित्कला + आनन्दकलिका (citkalā + ānandakalikā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); the double avagraha (ऽऽ) marks the long ā of ānanda absorbed in the fusion

Read citkalā | ānandakalikā (728–729): the double avagraha shows where the second name begins.

The names

728 चित्कला cit-kalā

She who is the digit (kalā) of consciousness

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (alternatively karmadhāraya). kalā 'digit, part, subtle power' is the head. As a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa: 'a digit of consciousness'; as a karmadhāraya: 'the subtle power that is consciousness'. t and k meet with no change.

Analysis चितः कला चित्कला; अथवा चित् एव कला चित्कला
citaḥ kalā citkalā; athavā cit eva kalā citkalā

Significance Traditionally the name is read as consciousness present in each being as a ray or digit of the infinite, as the moon's digits are parts of the one moon.

Uncertain ṣaṣṭhī ('a digit of consciousness') and karmadhāraya ('consciousness as subtle power') readings are both possible.

729 आनन्दकलिका ānanda-kalikā

She who is the bud of bliss

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. kalikā 'bud' is the head; ānanda 'bliss' stands to it in the genitive: 'the bud of bliss'.

Analysis आनन्दस्य कलिका आनन्दकलिका
ānandasya kalikā ānandakalikā

Significance As a bud holds the whole flower unopened, She holds bliss that blossoms in the devotee's heart.

730 प्रेमरूपा prema-rūpā

She whose form is love

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. rūpa 'form' is identified with preman 'love', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She whose form is love'. preman loses its n in the compound (prema-), a morphological change.

Analysis प्रेम रूपम् यस्याः सा प्रेमरूपा
prema rūpam yasyāḥ sā premarūpā

Significance Love is not something She has but what She is; pure devotion (prema) toward Her is Her own form reflected in the devotee.

731 प्रियङ्करी priyaṅkarī

She who grants what is dear to Her devotees

Sandhi प्रियङ्करी = प्रियम् + करी (priyam + karī) — the m (an augment, as in vaśaṅkara, name 697) becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ) and then ṅ, the nasal of k's class (8.4.58 anusvārasya yayi parasavarṇaḥ)

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. -kara 'making, doing' from √kṛ (suffix khac, which brings the augment m after the first member) is the head, with the feminine -ī; priya 'what is dear' is its object.

Analysis प्रियम् करोति इति प्रियङ्करी
priyam karoti iti priyaṅkarī

Significance She does what is dear to those who love Her — granting their wishes and, above all, the dearest thing, Herself.

732 नामपारायणप्रीता nāma-pārāyaṇa-prītā

She who is pleased by the recitation of Her names

Sandhi पारायण = पार + अयन (pāra + ayana) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ), inside the lexicalised compound pārāyaṇa; the n of ayana becomes retroflex ṇ after the r of pāra (ṇatva)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) nāma-pārāyaṇa 'the full recitation of the names' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; nāman loses its n). (2) The participle prītā 'pleased' is the head and takes that recitation in the instrumental of cause.

Analysis नाम्नाम् पारायणम् नामपारायणम्; नामपारायणेन प्रीता नामपारायणप्रीता
nāmnām pārāyaṇam nāmapārāyaṇam; nāmapārāyaṇena prītā nāmapārāyaṇaprītā

Significance Recitation of this Thousand Names is itself such a pārāyaṇa; the hymn's closing section (phalaśruti) praises its daily recitation.

733 नन्दिविद्या nandi-vidyā

She who is the Vidyā (mantra) of Nandi

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. vidyā 'mantra, sacred knowledge' is the head; Nandin (Nandi) stands to it in the genitive: 'the vidyā of Nandi'. nandin loses its n in the compound.

Analysis नन्दिनः विद्या नन्दिविद्या
nandinaḥ vidyā nandividyā

Significance Traditionally the Śrīvidyā mantra has forms associated with its great worshippers; Nandividyā is the form handed down through Nandikeśvara, and She is that mantra.

Uncertain Which form of the mantra is meant by Nandividyā, and its place among the worshippers' vidyās, could not be confirmed against a printed commentary.

734 नटेश्वरी naṭeśvarī

She who is the consort of Naṭeśvara (Śiva, Lord of the dance)

Sandhi नटेश्वरी = नट + ईश्वरी (naṭa + īśvarī) — guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, with the feminine of relationship. (1) naṭa-īśvara 'the lord of dancers', Śiva as Naṭarāja (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) The feminine -ī denotes His wife (Pāṇini 4.1.48 puṃyogād ākhyāyām): 'the consort of the Lord of dancers'. Read directly as naṭānām īśvarī, it is 'the queen of dancers'.

Analysis नटानाम् ईश्वरः नटेश्वरः; नटेश्वरस्य पत्नी नटेश्वरी
naṭānām īśvaraḥ naṭeśvaraḥ; naṭeśvarasya patnī naṭeśvarī

Significance As Śiva dances the cosmic dance, She is His partner and witness; Her dance is the lāsya of name 738.

लास्यप्रिया लयकरी लज्जा रम्भादिवन्दिता ॥ १४२ ॥

Where the names meet

Names 738–740 alliterate on l (lāsyapriyā, layakarī, lajjā).

The names

735 मिथ्याजगदधिष्ठाना mithyā-jagad-adhiṣṭhānā

She who is the basis of the illusory universe

Sandhi जगदधि = जगत् + अधि (jagat + adhi) — jaśtva: a final t becomes d before a vowel (Pāṇini 8.2.39 jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte); अधिष्ठाना = अधि + स्थाना (adhi + sthānā) — the s of sthā becomes ṣ after the prefix adhi (Pāṇini 8.3.65) and th becomes ṭh next to ṣ (8.4.41 ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya), as a feminine epithet. (1) mithyā-jagat 'the unreal world': the indeclinable mithyā 'falsely' qualifies jagat. (2) adhiṣṭhāna 'ground, substratum' is the head, taken in the feminine as an epithet of the Goddess, with the world in the genitive: 'the substratum of the unreal world'.

Analysis मिथ्या जगत् मिथ्याजगत्; मिथ्याजगतः अधिष्ठाना मिथ्याजगदधिष्ठाना
mithyā jagat mithyājagat; mithyājagataḥ adhiṣṭhānā mithyājagadadhiṣṭhānā

Significance In Advaita the world appears on Brahman as a snake appears on a rope: the appearance is false, the ground is real. She is that ground.

736 मुक्तिदा mukti-dā

She who gives liberation

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. -dā 'giving' from √dā is the head and mukti 'liberation' its object, as in name 669.

Analysis मुक्तिम् ददाति इति मुक्तिदा
muktim dadāti iti muktidā

Significance Liberation is Her gift; no effort alone wins it without Her grace.

737 मुक्तिरूपिणी mukti-rūpiṇī

She who is in the form of liberation

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya with the possessive suffix -in (Pāṇini 5.2.115 ata iniṭhanau). (1) mukti 'liberation' is identified with rūpa 'form' (karmadhāraya). (2) The possessive -in: 'She whose form is liberation'.

Analysis मुक्तिः एव रूपम् मुक्तिरूपम्; तत् अस्याः अस्ति इति मुक्तिरूपिणी
muktiḥ eva rūpam muktirūpam; tat asyāḥ asti iti muktirūpiṇī

Significance She does not only give liberation (736); She is liberation itself — the freedom that is the Self's own nature.

738 लास्यप्रिया lāsya-priyā

She who is fond of the lāsya dance

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. priya 'dear' and lāsya 'graceful dance' form a bahuvrīhi with priya placed second: 'She to whom the lāsya dance is dear'.

Analysis लास्यम् प्रियम् यस्याः सा लास्यप्रिया
lāsyam priyam yasyāḥ sā lāsyapriyā

Significance Śiva's tāṇḍava and the Goddess's lāsya together are the dance of the universe: vigor and grace, dissolution and creation.

739 लयकरी laya-karī

She who causes absorption

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. -kara 'making' from √kṛ (feminine -ī) is the head and laya 'dissolution, absorption' its object, as in name 682.

Analysis लयम् करोति इति लयकरी
layam karoti iti layakarī

Significance She brings about the dissolution of the worlds at the end of an age, and in the yogin the absorption of the mind (laya) into its source.

740 लज्जा lajjā

She who exists as modesty in living beings

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance 'To the Goddess who abides in all beings in the form of modesty' (yā devī sarvabhūteṣu lajjārūpeṇa saṃsthitā) is one of the salutations of the Devī Māhātmya (ch. 5). The seed-syllable hrīṃ is called the lajjā-bīja.

741 रम्भादिवन्दिता rambhādi-vanditā

She who is adored by the celestial damsels such as Rambhā

Sandhi रम्भादि = रम्भा + आदि (rambhā + ādi) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner bahuvrīhi). (1) rambhā-ādi 'those of whom Rambhā is the first' (bahuvrīhi): the apsarases. (2) The participle vanditā 'saluted, adored' is the head and takes them in the instrumental of agent.

Analysis रम्भा आदिः यासाम् ताः रम्भादयः; रम्भादिभिः वन्दिता रम्भादिवन्दिता
rambhā ādiḥ yāsām tāḥ rambhādayaḥ; rambhādibhiḥ vanditā rambhādivanditā

Significance The apsarases, famed for their beauty, bow to Her, whose beauty is the source of all beauty.

Śloka 143names 742–745

भवदावसुधावृष्टिः पापारण्यदवानला ।
दौर्भाग्यतूलवातूला जराध्वान्तरविप्रभा ॥ १४३ ॥

bhavadāvasudhāvṛṣṭiḥ pāpāraṇyadavānalā |
daurbhāgyatūlavātūlā jarādhvāntaraviprabhā || 143 ||

Where the names meet

Names 742–749 are a run of eight metaphors (rūpaka): each names an evil as fire, forest, cotton, darkness, ocean, mountain or timber, and Her as what quenches, burns, scatters, dispels or cuts it.

The names

742 भवदावसुधावृष्टिः bhava-dāva-sudhā-vṛṣṭiḥ

She who is the rain of nectar falling on the forest fire of worldly existence

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound saptamī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner rūpaka-karmadhāraya and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) bhava-dāva 'the forest fire that is worldly existence': a karmadhāraya of identification (rūpaka). (2) sudhā-vṛṣṭi 'a rain of nectar' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) The rain is the head, falling on that fire (locative): 'a rain of nectar on the forest fire of worldly existence'. vṛṣṭi keeps its own feminine i-stem.

Analysis भवः एव दावः भवदावः; सुधायाः वृष्टिः सुधावृष्टिः; भवदावे सुधावृष्टिः भवदावसुधावृष्टिः
bhavaḥ eva dāvaḥ bhavadāvaḥ; sudhāyāḥ vṛṣṭiḥ sudhāvṛṣṭiḥ; bhavadāve sudhāvṛṣṭiḥ bhavadāvasudhāvṛṣṭiḥ

Significance Saṃsāra burns like a forest fire; Her grace falls on it like a shower of nectar, quenching it. This begins a run of eight metaphor names (742–749).

743 पापारण्यदवानला pāpāraṇya-davānalā

She who is the forest fire that consumes the forest of sins

Sandhi पापारण्य = पाप + अरण्य (pāpa + araṇya) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); दवानला = दव + अनला (dava + analā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner rūpaka-karmadhāraya and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) pāpa-araṇya 'the forest that is sin' (rūpaka). (2) dava-anala 'forest fire', literally 'the fire of the forest' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) The fire is the head, taken in the feminine as Her epithet, with the forest of sin in the genitive: 'the forest fire to the forest of sins'.

Analysis पापम् एव अरण्यम् पापारण्यम्; दवस्य अनलः दवानलः; पापारण्यस्य दवानला पापारण्यदवानला
pāpam eva araṇyam pāpāraṇyam; davasya analaḥ davānalaḥ; pāpāraṇyasya davānalā pāpāraṇyadavānalā

Significance As a wildfire leaves nothing of a forest, Her grace burns away the accumulated sins of the devotee.

744 दौर्भाग्यतूलवातूला daurbhāgya-tūla-vātūlā

She who is the gale that drives away the cotton wisps of misfortune

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner rūpaka-karmadhāraya). (1) daurbhāgya-tūla 'the cotton that is misfortune' (rūpaka). (2) vātūlā 'whirlwind, gale' is the head and takes it in the genitive: 'the gale to the cotton of misfortune'.

Analysis दौर्भाग्यम् एव तूलम् दौर्भाग्यतूलम्; दौर्भाग्यतूलस्य वातूला दौर्भाग्यतूलवातूला
daurbhāgyam eva tūlam daurbhāgyatūlam; daurbhāgyatūlasya vātūlā daurbhāgyatūlavātūlā

Significance Misfortune, however heaped up, is as light as cotton before the wind of Her grace.

745 जराध्वान्तरविप्रभा jarādhvānta-ravi-prabhā

She who is the sunlight that dispels the darkness of old age

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner rūpaka-karmadhāraya and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) jarā-dhvānta 'the darkness that is old age' (rūpaka). (2) ravi-prabhā 'the light of the sun' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) The sunlight is the head and the darkness stands to it in the genitive: 'the sunlight to the darkness of old age'.

Analysis जरा एव ध्वान्तम् जराध्वान्तम्; रवेः प्रभा रविप्रभा; जराध्वान्तस्य रविप्रभा जराध्वान्तरविप्रभा
jarā eva dhvāntam jarādhvāntam; raveḥ prabhā raviprabhā; jarādhvāntasya raviprabhā jarādhvāntaraviprabhā

Significance Old age and decay vanish before Her as darkness before the sun; traditionally She grants lasting vigor, and the inner youth of the Self that never ages.

Śloka 144names 746–749

भाग्याब्धिचन्द्रिका भक्तचित्तकेकिघनाघना ।
रोगपर्वतदम्भोलिर् मृत्युदारुकुठारिका ॥ १४४ ॥

bhāgyābdhicandrikā bhaktacittakekighanāghanā |
rogaparvatadambholir mṛtyudārukuṭhārikā || 144 ||

Translation

748She who is the thunderbolt that shatters the mountain of disease; 749She who is the axe that cuts down the tree of death.

भाग्यbhāgyagood fortune

Where the names meet

दम्भोलिर्मृत्यु = दम्भोलिः + मृत्यु… (dambholiḥ + mṛtyu…) — visarga becomes r before a vowel or voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ)

The r of -dambholir- is the visarga of rogaparvatadambholiḥ (748); name 749 begins mṛtyu-.

The names

746 भाग्याब्धिचन्द्रिका bhāgyābdhi-candrikā

She who is the moonlight that swells the ocean of good fortune

Sandhi भाग्याब्धि = भाग्य + अब्धि (bhāgya + abdhi) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); अब्धि = अप् + धि (ap + dhi) — jaśtva: p becomes b before the voiced dh (Pāṇini 8.2.39 jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte), inside the lexicalised compound abdhi 'ocean' ('holder of the waters')

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner rūpaka-karmadhāraya). (1) bhāgya-abdhi 'the ocean that is good fortune' (rūpaka). (2) candrikā 'moonlight' is the head and takes that ocean in the genitive: 'the moonlight to the ocean of good fortune'.

Analysis भाग्यम् एव अब्धिः भाग्याब्धिः; भाग्याब्धेः चन्द्रिका भाग्याब्धिचन्द्रिका
bhāgyam eva abdhiḥ bhāgyābdhiḥ; bhāgyābdheḥ candrikā bhāgyābdhicandrikā

Significance As moonlight raises the tide, Her grace makes the devotee's fortune rise and overflow.

747 भक्तचित्तकेकिघनाघना bhakta-citta-keki-ghanāghanā

She who is the cloud that gladdens the peacocks who are the hearts of Her devotees

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner rūpaka-karmadhāraya and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) bhakta-citta 'the hearts of the devotees' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) bhaktacitta-kekin 'the peacocks that are those hearts' (rūpaka; kekin loses its n). (3) ghanāghanā 'dense rain-cloud' is the head and takes the peacocks in the genitive: 'the rain-cloud to the peacocks that are the devotees' hearts'.

Analysis भक्तानाम् चित्तानि भक्तचित्तानि; भक्तचित्तानि एव केकिनः भक्तचित्तकेकिनः; भक्तचित्तकेकिनाम् घनाघना भक्तचित्तकेकिघनाघना
bhaktānām cittāni bhaktacittāni; bhaktacittāni eva kekinaḥ bhaktacittakekinaḥ; bhaktacittakekinām ghanāghanā bhaktacittakekighanāghanā

Significance Peacocks dance with joy when rain-clouds gather; so the devotee's heart dances at the sight of Her.

748 रोगपर्वतदम्भोलिः roga-parvata-dambholiḥ

She who is the thunderbolt that shatters the mountain of disease

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner rūpaka-karmadhāraya). (1) roga-parvata 'the mountain that is disease' (rūpaka). (2) dambholi 'thunderbolt' is the head and takes it in the genitive.

Analysis रोगः एव पर्वतः रोगपर्वतः; रोगपर्वतस्य दम्भोलिः रोगपर्वतदम्भोलिः
rogaḥ eva parvataḥ rogaparvataḥ; rogaparvatasya dambholiḥ rogaparvatadambholiḥ

Significance As Indra's thunderbolt struck the mountains, Her grace shatters disease however massive, of body and of mind.

749 मृत्युदारुकुठारिका mṛtyu-dāru-kuṭhārikā

She who is the axe that cuts down the tree of death

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner rūpaka-karmadhāraya). (1) mṛtyu-dāru 'the timber that is death' (rūpaka). (2) kuṭhārikā 'axe' is the head and takes it in the genitive.

Analysis मृत्युः एव दारु मृत्युदारु; मृत्युदारुणः कुठारिका मृत्युदारुकुठारिका
mṛtyuḥ eva dāru mṛtyudāru; mṛtyudāruṇaḥ kuṭhārikā mṛtyudārukuṭhārikā

Significance Death, rooted as a great tree, is felled by Her; She grants immortality, the knowledge of the deathless Self.

Śloka 145names 750–756

महेश्वरी महाकाली महाग्रासा महाशना ।
अपर्णा चण्डिका चण्डमुण्डासुरनिषूदिनी ॥ १४५ ॥

maheśvarī mahākālī mahāgrāsā mahāśanā |
aparṇā caṇḍikā caṇḍamuṇḍāsuraniṣūdinī || 145 ||

The names, separated

750महेश्वरीmaheśvarī751महा-कालीmahā-kālī752महा-ग्रासाmahā-grāsā753महाशनाmahāśanā

750She who is the great Sovereign (Maheśvarī); 751She who is the great Kālī; 752She who is the great devourer, swallowing all at the dissolution; 753She whose eating is great, who consumes all that is;

754She who owes no debt; 755She who is Caṇḍikā, fierce against the wicked; 756She who slew the demons Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa.

Where the names meet

Names 750–753 all begin with mahā-; 753 is mahā + aśanā 'whose eating is great', not mahā + śanā. Names 751 and 755–756 recall the Devī Māhātmya.

The names

750 महेश्वरी maheśvarī

She who is the great Sovereign (Maheśvarī)

Sandhi महेश्वरी = महा + ईश्वरी (mahā + īśvarī) — guṇa: ā + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound karmadhāraya. mahatī 'great' qualifies īśvarī 'sovereign', the head. The feminine adjective takes its masculine stem (puṃvadbhāva) and mahat becomes mahā- (a morphological replacement); mahā + īśvarī then fuse by guṇa. The name is also the feminine of Maheśvara, 'the consort of the Great Lord'.

Analysis महती ईश्वरी महेश्वरी
mahatī īśvarī maheśvarī

Significance Maheśvarī is the consort and power of Maheśvara (Śiva), and one of the Mothers; She is the supreme ruler of all.

751 महाकाली mahā-kālī

She who is the great Kālī

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya. mahatī 'great' qualifies kālī; as in name 750 it appears as mahā- (mahat 'great' becomes mahā- before a co-referential member (Pāṇini 6.3.46 ān mahataḥ samānādhikaraṇajātīyayoḥ)). The members meet without sound change.

Analysis महती काली महाकाली
mahatī kālī mahākālī

Significance Mahākālī is the fierce form who withdraws all into Herself at the end of time; the Devī Māhātmya invokes Her as the first of its three great forms.

752 महाग्रासा mahā-grāsā

She who is the great devourer, swallowing all at the dissolution

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. mahat 'great' qualifies grāsa 'mouthful, devouring', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She whose devouring is great'. mahat appears as mahā- before a co-referential member (Pāṇini 6.3.46).

Analysis महान् ग्रासः यस्याः सा महाग्रासा
mahān grāsaḥ yasyāḥ sā mahāgrāsā

Significance At the end of an age the whole universe is a single mouthful for Her.

753 महाशना mahāśanā

She whose eating is great, who consumes all that is

Sandhi महाशना = महा + अशना (mahā + aśanā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi. mahat 'great' qualifies aśana 'eating, food', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She whose eating is great', i.e. who consumes the universe. mahat becomes mahā- (Pāṇini 6.3.46), and mahā + aśana fuse by savarṇa-dīrgha.

Analysis महत् अशनम् यस्याः सा महाशना
mahat aśanam yasyāḥ sā mahāśanā

Significance The Kaṭha Upaniṣad (1.2.25) speaks of the One for whom the priest and the warrior are food and death only the sauce; She takes back the whole creation into Herself.

754 अपर्णा aparṇā

She who owes no debt

Sandhi अपर्णा = अप + ऋणा (apa + ṛṇā) — guṇa: a + ṛ → ar (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ), on the reading apa + ṛṇa 'free of debt'; on the reading a + parṇa there is no sandhi

Compound prādi-bahuvrīhi (alternatively nañ-bahuvrīhi). Two analyses give the same word. (1) apa 'away' stands for apagata 'gone', with ṛṇa 'debt': 'She whose debt is gone', who owes nothing and frees others from their debts. (2) a- 'not' with parṇa 'leaf': 'She who had not even a leaf (to eat)', Pārvatī in Her penance for Śiva.

Analysis अपगतम् ऋणम् यस्याः सा अपर्णा; अथवा न पर्णम् (भक्ष्यम्) यस्याः सा अपर्णा
apagatam ṛṇam yasyāḥ sā aparṇā; athavā na parṇam (bhakṣyam) yasyāḥ sā aparṇā

Significance She owes nothing to anyone and releases Her devotees from their debts, the three debts to gods, sages and ancestors among them. Aparṇā is also Pārvatī, who in Her penance gave up even fallen leaves as food (Kālidāsa, Kumārasambhava 5.28).

Uncertain The name has two analyses: apa + ṛṇa 'free of debt' (the meaning given) and a + parṇa 'without (even) a leaf', the classical name of Pārvatī.

755 चण्डिका caṇḍikā

She who is Caṇḍikā, fierce against the wicked

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Caṇḍikā is the Goddess of the Devī Māhātmya (Caṇḍī), whose fierceness is turned against the demons for the protection of the worlds.

756 चण्डमुण्डासुरनिषूदिनी caṇḍa-muṇḍāsura-niṣūdinī

She who slew the demons Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa

Sandhi मुण्डासुर = मुण्ड + असुर (muṇḍa + asura) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); निषूदिनी = नि + सूदिनी (ni + sūdinī) — the s of √sūd becomes retroflex ṣ after the i of the prefix ni (ṣatva)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya and dvandva). (1) caṇḍa-muṇḍa 'Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa' (itaretara-dvandva). (2) caṇḍamuṇḍa-asura 'the demons Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa' (karmadhāraya, the names in apposition to asura). (3) niṣūdinī 'slayer' (agent noun in -in from ni + √sūd) is the head and takes the pair in the genitive.

Analysis चण्डः च मुण्डः च चण्डमुण्डौ; चण्डमुण्डौ असुरौ चण्डमुण्डासुरौ; चण्डमुण्डासुरयोः निषूदिनी चण्डमुण्डासुरनिषूदिनी
caṇḍaḥ ca muṇḍaḥ ca caṇḍamuṇḍau; caṇḍamuṇḍau asurau caṇḍamuṇḍāsurau; caṇḍamuṇḍāsurayoḥ niṣūdinī caṇḍamuṇḍāsuraniṣūdinī

Significance In the Devī Māhātmya (ch. 7) Kālī, springing from the Goddess's brow, slays Caṇḍa and Muṇḍa, and is then named Cāmuṇḍā.

क्षराक्षरात्मिका सर्वलोकेशी विश्वधारिणी ।
त्रिवर्गदात्री सुभगा त्र्यम्बका त्रिगुणात्मिका ॥ १४६ ॥

kṣarākṣarātmikā sarvalokeśī viśvadhāriṇī |

Where the names meet

tryambakā (762) is tri + ambaka 'three-eyed', not tri + ambā.

The names

757 क्षराक्षरात्मिका kṣarākṣarātmikā

She whose nature is both the perishable and the imperishable

Sandhi क्षराक्षर = क्षर + अक्षर (kṣara + akṣara) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); अक्षरात्मिका = अक्षर + आत्मिका (akṣara + ātmikā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner dvandva and nañ-tatpuruṣa). (1) a-kṣara 'imperishable' (nañ-tatpuruṣa). (2) kṣara-akṣara 'the perishable and the imperishable' (dvandva). (3) Both are identified with ātman 'self, nature', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She whose self is both'. ātman with the suffix -ka in a bahuvrīhi gives -ātmikā.

Analysis न क्षरः अक्षरः; क्षरः च अक्षरः च क्षराक्षरौ; क्षराक्षरौ आत्मा यस्याः सा क्षराक्षरात्मिका
na kṣaraḥ akṣaraḥ; kṣaraḥ ca akṣaraḥ ca kṣarākṣarau; kṣarākṣarau ātmā yasyāḥ sā kṣarākṣarātmikā

Significance The Bhagavad Gītā (15.16) names two puruṣas, the perishable (all beings) and the imperishable (the unchanging); She is both. Akṣara also means 'letter', so She is the perishable spoken sound and the imperishable syllable.

758 सर्वलोकेशी sarva-lokeśī

She who is the ruler of all worlds

Sandhi लोकेशी = लोक + ईशी (loka + īśī) — guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) sarva-loka 'all the worlds' (karmadhāraya). (2) īśī 'sovereign' is the head and takes them in the genitive.

Analysis सर्वे लोकाः सर्वलोकाः; सर्वलोकानाम् ईशी सर्वलोकेशी
sarve lokāḥ sarvalokāḥ; sarvalokānām īśī sarvalokeśī

Significance Every world, from the highest heaven to the lowest, is under Her rule.

759 विश्वधारिणी viśva-dhāriṇī

She who supports the universe

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. dhāriṇī 'bearing, supporting' (agent noun in -in from the causative of √dhṛ, feminine) is the head and governs viśva 'the universe' as its object.

Analysis विश्वम् धारयति इति विश्वधारिणी
viśvam dhārayati iti viśvadhāriṇī

Significance She holds up the universe as its ground and sustains it at every moment.

760 त्रिवर्गदात्री tri-varga-dātrī

She who bestows the three goals of life

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner dvigu). (1) tri-varga 'the group of three' (a numeral compound, dvigu): dharma, artha and kāma. (2) dātrī 'giver' is the head and takes the triad in the genitive.

Analysis त्रयाणाम् वर्गः त्रिवर्गः; त्रिवर्गस्य दात्री त्रिवर्गदात्री
trayāṇām vargaḥ trivargaḥ; trivargasya dātrī trivargadātrī

Significance The trivarga is right living (dharma), wealth (artha) and fulfilment of desire (kāma); with liberation (apavarga, name 764) they make the four aims of life.

761 सुभगा subhagā

She who is supremely fortunate and lovely, the seat of all prosperity

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound prādi-bahuvrīhi. su 'well, good' qualifies bhaga 'fortune, excellence, loveliness', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She whose fortune is excellent'. The members meet without sound change.

Analysis शोभनः भगः यस्याः सा सुभगा
śobhanaḥ bhagaḥ yasyāḥ sā subhagā

Significance Bhaga traditionally names the six excellences — sovereignty, strength, fame, prosperity, knowledge and dispassion — and She has them all; Subhagā is also a name of the beloved wife. Her worship is called saubhāgya.

762 त्र्यम्बका tryambakā

She who has three eyes

Sandhi त्र्यम्बका = त्रि + अम्बका (tri + ambakā) — yaṇ: i becomes y before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci)

Compound bahuvrīhi. tri 'three' qualifies ambaka 'eye', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She who has three eyes'.

Analysis त्रीणि अम्बकानि यस्याः सा त्र्यम्बका
trīṇi ambakāni yasyāḥ sā tryambakā

Significance Her three eyes are traditionally the sun, the moon and fire; Tryambaka is also Śiva, and She is His consort.

763 त्रिगुणात्मिका tri-guṇātmikā

She whose nature is the three guṇas

Sandhi गुणात्मिका = गुण + आत्मिका (guṇa + ātmikā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner dvigu). (1) tri-guṇa 'the three guṇas' (numeral karmadhāraya, dvigu). (2) They are identified with ātman 'nature', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She whose nature is the three guṇas'. ātman with -ka gives -ātmikā.

Analysis त्रयः गुणाः त्रिगुणाः; त्रिगुणाः आत्मा यस्याः सा त्रिगुणात्मिका
trayaḥ guṇāḥ triguṇāḥ; triguṇāḥ ātmā yasyāḥ sā triguṇātmikā

Significance As Prakṛti She is made of sattva, rajas and tamas, appearing as the three goddesses and the three functions; name 789 says that She is also beyond them.

व्रताvratāvow, religious observancevrata, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

The names

764 स्वर्गापवर्गदा svargāpavarga-dā

She who bestows heaven and liberation

Sandhi स्वर्गापवर्ग = स्वर्ग + अपवर्ग (svarga + apavarga) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner dvandva). (1) svarga-apavarga 'heaven and liberation' (itaretara-dvandva). (2) -dā 'giving' from √dā is the head and governs the pair as its object.

Analysis स्वर्गः च अपवर्गः च स्वर्गापवर्गौ; स्वर्गापवर्गौ ददाति इति स्वर्गापवर्गदा
svargaḥ ca apavargaḥ ca svargāpavargau; svargāpavargau dadāti iti svargāpavargadā

Significance She gives both enjoyment (bhukti) and release (mukti): heaven to those who seek it and liberation to those who seek that.

765 शुद्धा śuddhā

She who is pure

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance No impurity of ignorance or its effects touches Her; She purifies all who approach Her.

766 जपापुष्पनिभाकृतिः japā-puṣpa-nibhākṛtiḥ

She whose form is red like the hibiscus flower

Sandhi निभाकृतिः = निभ + आकृतिः (nibha + ākṛtiḥ) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner tṛtīyā- and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) japā-puṣpa 'the hibiscus flower' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) …-nibha 'resembling' takes the flower as its standard (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (3) This qualifies ākṛti 'form, figure', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She whose form resembles the hibiscus flower'. Inside the compound nibhā takes its masculine stem nibha (puṃvadbhāva); ākṛti keeps its own feminine i-stem.

Analysis जपायाः पुष्पम् जपापुष्पम्; जपापुष्पेण निभा जपापुष्पनिभा; जपापुष्पनिभा आकृतिः यस्याः सा जपापुष्पनिभाकृतिः
japāyāḥ puṣpam japāpuṣpam; japāpuṣpeṇa nibhā japāpuṣpanibhā; japāpuṣpanibhā ākṛtiḥ yasyāḥ sā japāpuṣpanibhākṛtiḥ

Significance The meditation verses describe Her as red (aruṇā) like vermilion and the rising sun; the red of compassion and of the creative power.

767 ओजोवती ojovatī

She who is full of vitality

Sandhi ओजोवती = ओजस् + वती (ojas + vatī) — -as becomes -o before a voiced consonant: s → r(u) → u, which combines with a to o (Pāṇini 6.1.114 haśi ca)

Compound not a compound

Significance Ojas is the essence of vigor and splendor; She possesses it fully and imparts it to Her devotees.

768 द्युतिधरा dyuti-dharā

She who bears radiance, full of light and splendor

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. -dhara 'bearing, holding' from √dhṛ (feminine -ā) is the head and governs dyuti 'radiance' as its object.

Analysis द्युतिम् धरति इति द्युतिधरा
dyutim dharati iti dyutidharā

Significance Her own light is the light by which all lights shine (tasya bhāsā sarvam idaṃ vibhāti).

769 यज्ञरूपा yajña-rūpā

She who is in the form of sacrifice

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. rūpa 'form' is identified with yajña 'sacrifice', and the whole points to the Goddess.

Analysis यज्ञः रूपम् यस्याः सा यज्ञरूपा
yajñaḥ rūpam yasyāḥ sā yajñarūpā

Significance The Veda identifies the sacrifice with the Lord Himself; She is the rite, the offering and its fruit.

770 प्रियव्रता priya-vratā

She who is fond of vows

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. priya 'dear' qualifies vrata 'vow, observance', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She to whom vows are dear'.

Analysis प्रियाणि व्रतानि यस्याः सा प्रियव्रता
priyāṇi vratāni yasyāḥ sā priyavratā

Significance She is pleased by vows kept for Her, such as fasts and observances on Her sacred days.

Śloka 148names 771–776

दुराराध्या दुराधर्षा पाटलीकुसुमप्रिया ।
महती मेरुनिलया मन्दारकुसुमप्रिया ॥ १४८ ॥

durārādhyā durādharṣā pāṭalīkusumapriyā |
mahatī merunilayā mandārakusumapriyā || 148 ||

The names, separated

771दुर्-आराध्याdur-ārādhyā772दुर्-आधर्षाdur-ādharṣā773पाटली-कुसुम-प्रियाpāṭalī-kusuma-priyā

774महतीmahatī775मेरु-निलयाmeru-nilayā776मन्दार-कुसुम-प्रियाmandāra-kusuma-priyā

Translation

771She who is difficult to worship; 772She who cannot be assailed or overpowered; 773She who is fond of the pāṭalī flower (the pale red trumpet flower);

774She who is great (Mahatī); 775She whose abode is Mount Meru; 776She who is fond of the mandāra flowers.

Word by word

आराध्याārādhyāto be worshippedā + √rādh, gerundive, feminine
772 दुराधर्षा dur-ādharṣā
दुस्duswith difficulty, hardprefix; dur- before a vowel
आधर्षाādharṣāto be assailed, overpoweredā + √dhṛṣ 'to dare, attack' + -a (khal), feminine
773 पाटलीकुसुमप्रिया pāṭalī-kusuma-priyā
पाटलीpāṭalīthe pāṭalī tree, trumpet-flower (Stereospermum), with pale red blossoms
कुसुमkusumaflower
प्रियाpriyādear; fond ofpriya, with the feminine -ā

महतीmahatīgreatfeminine of mahat; also the name of Nārada's vīṇā

मेरुmeruMeru, the golden mountain at the center of the world
निलयाnilayāabode, dwellingnilaya, from ni + √lī 'to settle', with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

मन्दारmandārathe mandāra tree, one of the five trees of heaven (coral tree)
कुसुमkusumaflower
प्रियाpriyādear; fond ofpriya, with the feminine -ā

Where the names meet

durārādhyā (771) answers sukhārādhyā (681): easy to worship for the devoted, hard for the undisciplined.

The names

771 दुराराध्या dur-ārādhyā

She who is difficult to worship

Sandhi दुराराध्या = दुस् + आराध्या (dus + ārādhyā) — the final s of dus becomes r before a vowel (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ)

Compound prādi-tatpuruṣa. The gerundive ārādhyā 'to be worshipped' is the head; the prefix dus 'with difficulty' qualifies it: 'to be worshipped only with difficulty'.

Analysis दुःखेन आराध्या दुराराध्या
duḥkhena ārādhyā durārādhyā

Significance The counterpart of name 681 (sukhārādhyā): easy for those who love Her, She is hard to reach for those whose senses and mind are unrestrained.

772 दुराधर्षा dur-ādharṣā

She who cannot be assailed or overpowered

Sandhi दुराधर्षा = दुस् + आधर्षा (dus + ādharṣā) — the final s of dus becomes r before a vowel (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ)

Compound prādi-tatpuruṣa (with a khal formation). ādharṣa 'being assailed' is formed from ā + √dhṛṣ with the suffix khal, which is used after dus, su and īṣat in the sense 'hard / easy to be done' (Pāṇini 3.3.126 īṣadduḥsuṣu kṛcchrākṛcchrārtheṣu khal); dus is fused with it: 'hard to assail'.

Analysis दुःखेन आधर्ष्यते इति दुराधर्षा
duḥkhena ādharṣyate iti durādharṣā

Significance No power can attack or overcome Her, and none can overcome those She protects.

773 पाटलीकुसुमप्रिया pāṭalī-kusuma-priyā

She who is fond of the pāṭalī flower (the pale red trumpet flower)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) pāṭalī-kusuma 'the flower of the pāṭalī tree' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) A bahuvrīhi with priya 'dear' placed second: 'She to whom the pāṭalī flower is dear'.

Analysis पाटल्याः कुसुमम् पाटलीकुसुमम्; पाटलीकुसुमम् प्रियम् यस्याः सा पाटलीकुसुमप्रिया
pāṭalyāḥ kusumam pāṭalīkusumam; pāṭalīkusumam priyam yasyāḥ sā pāṭalīkusumapriyā

Significance The fragrant pāṭalī blossom is among the flowers offered in Her worship.

774 महती mahatī

She who is great (Mahatī)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance She is great beyond measure. Mahatī is also the name of the sage Nārada's vīṇā, so the name is read as Her presence in that instrument and in music.

775 मेरुनिलया meru-nilayā

She whose abode is Mount Meru

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. nilaya 'abode' is identified with Meru, and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She whose abode is Meru'.

Analysis मेरुः निलयः यस्याः सा मेरुनिलया
meruḥ nilayaḥ yasyāḥ sā merunilayā

Significance Her city stands on the central peak of Meru (compare name 55, sumerumadhyaśṛṅgasthā); inwardly Meru is the spinal axis, and the three-dimensional Śrīcakra is called Meru.

776 मन्दारकुसुमप्रिया mandāra-kusuma-priyā

She who is fond of the mandāra flowers

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). As in name 773: mandāra-kusuma 'the flower of the mandāra tree' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa), then a bahuvrīhi with priya placed second.

Analysis मन्दारस्य कुसुमम् मन्दारकुसुमम्; मन्दारकुसुमम् प्रियम् यस्याः सा मन्दारकुसुमप्रिया
mandārasya kusumam mandārakusumam; mandārakusumam priyam yasyāḥ sā mandārakusumapriyā

Significance Mandāra is one of the five wish-fulfilling trees of Indra's heaven; its flowers please Her.

Śloka 149names 777–784

वीराराध्या विराड्रूपा विरजा विश्वतोमुखी ।
प्रत्यग्रूपा पराकाशा प्राणदा प्राणरूपिणी ॥ १४९ ॥

vīrārādhyā virāḍrūpā virajā viśvatomukhī |
pratyagrūpā parākāśā prāṇadā prāṇarūpiṇī || 149 ||

The names, separated

777वीराराध्याvīrārādhyā778विराड्-रूपाvirāḍ-rūpā779विरजाvirajā780विश्वतो-मुखीviśvato-mukhī

781प्रत्यग्-रूपाpratyag-rūpā782पराकाशाparākāśā783प्राण-दाprāṇa-dā784प्राण-रूपिणीprāṇa-rūpiṇī

Translation

777She who is worshipped by heroic persons; 778She whose form is Virāj, the cosmic whole; 779She who is without rajas (desire and anger); 780She who faces all directions;

781She who is the indwelling Self; 782She who is the supreme space (ākāśa); 783She who is the giver of life; 784She whose form is prāṇa, the breath of life.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish
777 वीराराध्या vīrārādhyā
वीरvīrahero; in Tantra, the practitioner of the heroic disposition (vīra-bhāva)
आराध्याārādhyāto be worshippedā + √rādh, gerundive, feminine
778 विराड्रूपा virāḍ-rūpā
विराज्virājVirāj, the cosmic whole, the universe as one bodyvi + √rāj 'to shine, rule'
रूपाrūpāhaving the formrūpa, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi
779 विरजा virajā
विviaway, apartprefix
रजाrajārajas: the guṇa of passion and activity; dust, impurityraja(s), with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi
780 विश्वतोमुखी viśvato-mukhī
विश्वतस्viśvatason all sides, everywhereviśva 'all' + the suffix -tas
मुखीmukhīface, mouthmukha, with the feminine -ī of the bahuvrīhi
781 प्रत्यग्रूपा pratyag-rūpā
प्रत्यञ्च्pratyañcturned inward, inner; the inner Selfprati + √añc 'to turn'; pratyak at the end of a member
रूपाrūpāhaving the formrūpa, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi
782 पराकाशा parākāśā
परparasupreme, highest
आकाशाākāśāspace, etherākāśa, with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi
783 प्राणदा prāṇa-dā
प्राणprāṇalife-breath, lifepra + √an 'to breathe'
दाdāgiving, giver√dā + -a, feminine
784 प्राणरूपिणी prāṇa-rūpiṇī
प्राणprāṇalife-breath, the vital force
रूपिणीrūpiṇīhaving the formrūpa + -in, feminine

Where the names meet

Spelling traps: virāḍrūpā has ḍ for the j of virāj, pratyagrūpā g for the k of pratyak; parākāśā is para + ākāśa 'space', not parā + kāśā.

The names

777 वीराराध्या vīrārādhyā

She who is worshipped by heroic persons

Sandhi वीराराध्या = वीर + आराध्या (vīra + ārādhyā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa. The gerundive ārādhyā is the head; vīra 'hero' stands to it in the instrumental of agent.

Analysis वीरैः आराध्या वीराराध्या
vīraiḥ ārādhyā vīrārādhyā

Significance In the Tantras the vīra is the practitioner of the heroic disposition, between the paśu and the divya; traditionally also the one who has conquered the inner enemies.

778 विराड्रूपा virāḍ-rūpā

She whose form is Virāj, the cosmic whole

Sandhi विराड्रूपा = विराज् + रूपा (virāj + rūpā) — the final j of virāj becomes ṣ at the end of a member (Pāṇini 8.2.36, which names rāj) and then the voiced ḍ before r (jaśtva, 8.2.39)

Compound bahuvrīhi. rūpa 'form' is identified with Virāj, the cosmic body, and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She whose form is Virāj'.

Analysis विराट् रूपम् यस्याः सा विराड्रूपा
virāṭ rūpam yasyāḥ sā virāḍrūpā

Significance In Vedānta Virāj is the Lord as the gross universe taken as one body; all that is seen is Her form.

779 विरजा virajā

She who is without rajas (desire and anger)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound prādi-bahuvrīhi. vi 'away' stands for vigata 'gone', with rajas 'passion; dust': 'She from whom rajas has gone'. rajas is treated as an a-stem (raja) and takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis विगतम् रजः यस्याः सा विरजा
vigatam rajaḥ yasyāḥ sā virajā

Significance Desire and anger are born of rajas (Bhagavad Gītā 3.37); She is untouched by them and by all impurity. Virajā is also the name of a sacred river and a goddess of a famous shrine.

780 विश्वतोमुखी viśvato-mukhī

She who faces all directions

Sandhi विश्वतोमुखी = विश्वतस् + मुखी (viśvatas + mukhī) — -as becomes -o before a voiced consonant (Pāṇini 6.1.114 haśi ca)

Compound bahuvrīhi. The adverb viśvatas 'on all sides' qualifies mukha 'face', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She whose faces are on every side'. A bahuvrīhi ending in a word for a body part forms its feminine in -ī.

Analysis विश्वतः मुखानि यस्याः सा विश्वतोमुखी
viśvataḥ mukhāni yasyāḥ sā viśvatomukhī

Significance The Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad (3.3) praises the One whose eyes and faces are everywhere (viśvataś cakṣur uta viśvatomukhaḥ); She sees and is present in every direction.

781 प्रत्यग्रूपा pratyag-rūpā

She who is the indwelling Self

Sandhi प्रत्यग्रूपा = प्रत्यक् + रूपा (pratyak + rūpā) — jaśtva: a final k becomes g before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.39 jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte)

Compound bahuvrīhi. pratyak 'turned inward' qualifies rūpa 'form', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She whose form is inward', the inner Self. The stem pratyañc 'inward' appears as pratyak at the end of a member.

Analysis प्रत्यक् रूपम् यस्याः सा प्रत्यग्रूपा
pratyak rūpam yasyāḥ sā pratyagrūpā

Significance 'A wise one, seeking immortality, turned the eye inward and saw the inner Self (pratyagātman)' (Kaṭha Upaniṣad 2.1.1). She is that inner Self, found by turning within.

782 पराकाशा parākāśā

She who is the supreme space (ākāśa)

Sandhi पराकाशा = पर + आकाशा (para + ākāśā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) para-ākāśa 'the supreme space' (karmadhāraya). (2) As a bahuvrīhi with the feminine -ā: 'She whose own nature is the supreme space'. ākāśa is masculine or neuter, so the -ā shows the name is an epithet; para then appears in its masculine stem.

Analysis परम् आकाशम् पराकाशम्; पराकाशम् स्वरूपम् यस्याः सा पराकाशा
param ākāśam parākāśam; parākāśam svarūpam yasyāḥ sā parākāśā

Significance In the Chāndogya Upaniṣad (1.9.1) all beings arise from space (ākāśa) and return into it, and the Brahma Sūtra (1.1.22) reads that ākāśa as Brahman. She is that supreme space of consciousness, the material cause of cosmic and individual bodies.

783 प्राणदा prāṇa-dā

She who is the giver of life

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. -dā 'giving' from √dā is the head and prāṇa 'life-breath' its object.

Analysis प्राणान् ददाति इति प्राणदा
prāṇān dadāti iti prāṇadā

Significance Every breath of every creature is Her gift; She also gives the sensory powers, which the Upaniṣads call prāṇas.

784 प्राणरूपिणी prāṇa-rūpiṇī

She whose form is prāṇa, the breath of life

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya with the possessive suffix -in (Pāṇini 5.2.115 ata iniṭhanau). (1) prāṇa 'life-breath' is identified with rūpa 'form' (karmadhāraya). (2) The possessive -in: 'She whose form is prāṇa'.

Analysis प्राणः एव रूपम् प्राणरूपम्; तत् अस्याः अस्ति इति प्राणरूपिणी
prāṇaḥ eva rūpam prāṇarūpam; tat asyāḥ asti iti prāṇarūpiṇī

Significance After giving life (783) She is life itself; the Brahma Sūtra (1.1.28) shows that the prāṇa praised in the Upaniṣads is Brahman.

Śloka 150names 785–790

मार्ताण्डभैरवाराध्या मन्त्रिणीन्यस्तराज्यधूः ।
त्रिपुरेशी जयत्सेना निस्त्रैगुण्या परापरा ॥ १५० ॥

mārtāṇḍabhairavārādhyā mantriṇīnyastarājyadhūḥ |
tripureśī jayatsenā nistraiguṇyā parāparā || 150 ||

The names, separated

785मार्ताण्ड-भैरवाराध्याmārtāṇḍa-bhairavārādhyā786मन्त्रिणी-न्यस्त-राज्य-धूःmantriṇī-nyasta-rājya-dhūḥ

787त्रिपुरेशीtripureśī788जयत्-सेनाjayat-senā789निस्-त्रैगुण्याnis-traiguṇyā790परापराparāparā

Translation

785She who is worshipped by Mārtāṇḍa Bhairava; 786She who has entrusted the burden of Her kingdom to Her minister, Mantriṇī;

787She who is the sovereign of Tripura (the three cities); 788She whose army is ever victorious; 789She who is beyond the three guṇas; 790She who is both the supreme (parā) and the non-supreme (aparā).

Word by word

SanskritEnglish
785 मार्ताण्डभैरवाराध्या mārtāṇḍa-bhairavārādhyā
मार्ताण्डmārtāṇḍathe Sun
भैरवbhairavaBhairava, a fierce form of Śiva
आराध्याārādhyāto be worshippedā + √rādh, gerundive, feminine

मन्त्रिणीmantriṇīthe woman minister; Mantriṇī (Śyāmalā), Her chief counselor
न्यस्तnyastaplaced, entrustedni + √as 'to throw, put', past participle
राज्यrājyakingdom, rule
धूःdhūḥyoke, burden, responsibilitynominative of dhur; the vowel is lengthened before the final r (Pāṇini 8.2.76 rvor upadhāyā dīrgha ikaḥ)

त्रिtrithree

जयत्jayatconquering, victorious√ji 'to conquer', present participle

निस्niswithout, beyondprefix

Where the names meet

jayatsenā (788) is jayat + senā, not jaya + tsenā; mantriṇīnyastarājyadhūḥ (786) ends in dhūḥ, the nominative of dhur 'burden'.

The names

785 मार्ताण्डभैरवाराध्या mārtāṇḍa-bhairavārādhyā

She who is worshipped by Mārtāṇḍa Bhairava

Sandhi भैरवाराध्या = भैरव + आराध्या (bhairava + ārādhyā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) mārtāṇḍa-bhairava 'Bhairava who is the Sun' (karmadhāraya of apposition). (2) The gerundive ārādhyā is the head and takes him in the instrumental of agent.

Analysis मार्ताण्डः च असौ भैरवः च मार्ताण्डभैरवः; मार्ताण्डभैरवेण आराध्या मार्ताण्डभैरवाराध्या
mārtāṇḍaḥ ca asau bhairavaḥ ca mārtāṇḍabhairavaḥ; mārtāṇḍabhairaveṇa ārādhyā mārtāṇḍabhairavārādhyā

Significance Traditionally Mārtāṇḍa Bhairava, Śiva in the form of the Sun, dwells with his consort in one of the enclosures of Her city and worships Her there.

Uncertain The place of Mārtāṇḍa Bhairava in Her city follows the usual account; the exact enclosure could not be confirmed against a printed text.

786 मन्त्रिणीन्यस्तराज्यधूः mantriṇī-nyasta-rājya-dhūḥ

She who has entrusted the burden of Her kingdom to Her minister, Mantriṇī

Sandhi न्यस्त = नि + अस्त (ni + asta) — yaṇ: i becomes y before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over inner ṣaṣṭhī- and saptamī-tatpuruṣas). (1) rājya-dhur 'the yoke of the kingdom' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) mantriṇī-nyasta 'placed on the Mantriṇī' (saptamī-tatpuruṣa with the participle; mantriṇī keeps its ī because this is not a karmadhāraya). (3) The whole is a bahuvrīhi with the instrumental yayā: 'She by whom the burden of the kingdom has been placed on the Mantriṇī'. The participle stands first, as is usual in a bahuvrīhi.

Analysis राज्यस्य धूः राज्यधूः; मन्त्रिण्याम् न्यस्ता मन्त्रिणीन्यस्ता; मन्त्रिणीन्यस्ता राज्यधूः यया सा मन्त्रिणीन्यस्तराज्यधूः
rājyasya dhūḥ rājyadhūḥ; mantriṇyām nyastā mantriṇīnyastā; mantriṇīnyastā rājyadhūḥ yayā sā mantriṇīnyastarājyadhūḥ

Significance In the Lalitopākhyāna Mantriṇī (Śyāmalā, Rājaśyāmalā) is Her prime minister and Daṇḍanāthā (Vārāhī) Her commander; the Empress rules through them. Inwardly, the counsel of the mantra governs the devotee's life.

Uncertain Pāṇini 5.4.74 adds the compound-final -a to a compound ending in dhur (…-dhura); the name keeps the bare dhūḥ, a usage also found in epic and Purāṇic Sanskrit. Noted, not a text concern: the verse and the metre support dhūḥ.

787 त्रिपुरेशी tripureśī

She who is the sovereign of Tripura (the three cities)

Sandhi त्रिपुरेशी = त्रिपुर + ईशी (tripura + īśī) — guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner dvigu). (1) tri-pura 'the three cities' taken as one whole (samāhāra-dvigu). (2) īśī 'sovereign' is the head and takes it in the genitive.

Analysis त्रयाणाम् पुराणाम् समाहारः त्रिपुरम्; त्रिपुरस्य ईशी त्रिपुरेशी
trayāṇām purāṇām samāhāraḥ tripuram; tripurasya īśī tripureśī

Significance The three cities are read as every triad — the three bodies, the three states of waking, dream and sleep, the three worlds. In Śrīcakra worship Tripureśī is the presiding goddess of one of the enclosures.

788 जयत्सेना jayat-senā

She whose army is ever victorious

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. The present participle jayat 'conquering' qualifies senā 'army', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She whose army is conquering'. The feminine jayantī takes its masculine stem jayat inside the bahuvrīhi (puṃvadbhāva); t and s meet with no change.

Analysis जयन्ती सेना यस्याः सा जयत्सेना
jayantī senā yasyāḥ sā jayatsenā

Significance Her hosts of śaktis never know defeat; in the Lalitopākhyāna they overthrow Bhaṇḍāsura's armies.

789 निस्त्रैगुण्या nis-traiguṇyā

She who is beyond the three guṇas

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound prādi-bahuvrīhi. nis 'out, away' stands for nirgata 'gone', and the whole points to the Goddess: 'She from whom the three guṇas have gone'. The s of nis stays s before the voiceless t.

Analysis निर्गतम् त्रैगुण्यम् यस्याः सा निस्त्रैगुण्या
nirgatam traiguṇyam yasyāḥ sā nistraiguṇyā

Significance 'The Vedas deal with the three guṇas; be free of the three guṇas (nistraiguṇya), Arjuna' (Bhagavad Gītā 2.45). As Prakṛti She is made of the guṇas (763); as pure consciousness She is beyond them.

790 परापरा parāparā

She who is both the supreme (parā) and the non-supreme (aparā)

Sandhi परापरा = पर + अपरा (para + aparā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound karmadhāraya (of two co-referential adjectives). parā 'supreme' and aparā 'not supreme' both describe the one Goddess: 'She who is both the higher and the lower'. Inside the compound parā takes its masculine stem para (puṃvadbhāva), which fuses with aparā by savarṇa-dīrgha.

Analysis परा च असौ अपरा च परापरा
parā ca asau aparā ca parāparā

Significance The Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad (1.1.4) speaks of two knowledges, the higher (parā) and the lower (aparā); She is both, the transcendent and the manifest. In the Tantras Parāparā is also the middle of three levels (parā, parāparā, aparā).

Uncertain Read as 'both supreme and non-supreme' (karmadhāraya) or as 'the intermediate, Parāparā' (the middle of the Tantric triad).

Śloka 151names 791–796

सत्यज्ञानानन्दरूपा सामरस्यपरायणा ।
कपर्दिनी कलामाला कामधुक् कामरूपिणी ॥ १५१ ॥

satyajñānānandarūpā sāmarasyaparāyaṇā |
kapardinī kalāmālā kāmadhuk kāmarūpiṇī || 151 ||

The names, separated

791सत्य-ज्ञानानन्द-रूपाsatya-jñānānanda-rūpā792सामरस्य-परायणाsāmarasya-parāyaṇā

793कपर्दिनीkapardinī794कला-मालाkalā-mālā795काम-धुक्kāma-dhuk796काम-रूपिणीkāma-rūpiṇī

Translation

791She who is truth, knowledge and bliss; 792She who is wholly intent on sāmarasya, the perfect equipoise of Śiva and Śakti;

793She who is the consort of Kapardin, Śiva of the matted locks; 794She who wears the arts as a garland; 795She who fulfills all desires; 796She who assumes any form at will.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish
791 सत्यज्ञानानन्दरूपा satya-jñānānanda-rūpā
सत्यsatyatruth, the realfrom sat 'being' + -ya
ज्ञानjñānaknowledge, consciousness√jñā 'to know' + -ana
आनन्दānandabliss
रूपाrūpāhaving the form ofrūpa 'form', with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi
792 सामरस्यपरायणा sāmarasya-parāyaṇā
सामरस्यsāmarasyaoneness of flavor, perfect equipoiseabstract noun from samarasa 'of the same flavor' (sama + rasa), with vṛddhi of the first vowel
परparahighest, supreme
अयनाayanāresort, goal (lit. 'going')ayana from √i 'to go'; feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi; ayana → -āyaṇa in the compound
793 कपर्दिनी kapardinī
कपर्दिनीkapardinīconsort of Kapardin; also, wearing braided lockskaparda 'braided, matted hair' + the possessive suffix -in gives kapardin, an epithet of Śiva; feminine -ī
794 कलामाला kalā-mālā
कलाkalāart, skill; also a digit of the moon, a portion of power
मालाmālāgarland, string, series
795 कामधुक् kāma-dhuk
कामkāmadesire, wish
धुक्dhukmilking out, yielding√duh + zero suffix; at the word's end h becomes gh and then k, and the initial d is aspirated to dh because the aspiration of h is lost (nominative duh → dhuk)
796 कामरूपिणी kāma-rūpiṇī
कामkāmawill, wish; also Kāma (Kāmeśvara, the god of love)
रूपिणीrūpiṇīhaving the form ofrūpa 'form' + the possessive suffix -in (ṇ by ṇatva after r), feminine -ī

Where the names meet

Name 791 gives the Vedāntic definition sat-cit-ānanda; 792 sāmarasya is the technical term for the 'one flavor' of Śiva and Śakti.

The names

791 सत्यज्ञानानन्दरूपा satya-jñānānanda-rūpā

She who is truth, knowledge and bliss

Sandhi ज्ञानानन्द = ज्ञान + आनन्द (jñāna + ānanda) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner dvandva). (1) satya-jñāna-ānanda 'truth, knowledge and bliss' is a dvandva of three equal members. (2) The whole is a bahuvrīhi describing Her: 'She whose form (rūpa) is truth, knowledge and bliss'; rūpa takes the feminine -ā to agree with Her. The three are not three qualities She possesses but Her very nature, which is why rūpa is used.

Analysis सत्यम् च ज्ञानम् च आनन्दः च सत्यज्ञानानन्दाः; सत्यज्ञानानन्दाः रूपम् यस्याः सा सत्यज्ञानानन्दरूपा
satyam ca jñānam ca ānandaḥ ca satyajñānānandāḥ; satyajñānānandāḥ rūpam yasyāḥ sā satyajñānānandarūpā

Significance The Taittirīya Upaniṣad defines Brahman as satyaṃ jñānam anantam and teaches that bliss (ānanda) is Brahman; the name gives the Goddess the Vedāntic svarūpa-lakṣaṇa, sat-cit-ānanda.

792 सामरस्यपरायणा sāmarasya-parāyaṇā

She who is wholly intent on sāmarasya, the perfect equipoise of Śiva and Śakti

Sandhi परायणा = पर + अयना (para + ayanā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ), inside the lexicalised compound parāyaṇa; the n of ayana then becomes ṇ after the r (ṇatva)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over the lexicalised karmadhāraya parāyaṇa). (1) para-ayana 'the highest resort, final goal' (karmadhāraya; as a lexical word, 'wholly devoted to'). (2) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose highest resort is sāmarasya', i.e. who is wholly intent on it. Sāmarasya, 'the state of having one flavor', is an abstract noun from sama-rasa 'of equal flavor'.

Analysis परम् अयनम् परायणम्; सामरस्यम् परायणम् यस्याः सा सामरस्यपरायणा
param ayanam parāyaṇam; sāmarasyam parāyaṇam yasyāḥ sā sāmarasyaparāyaṇā

Significance In Śrīvidyā and Kashmir Śaivism sāmarasya is the 'single flavor' of Śiva and Śakti in union, where consciousness and its power are tasted as one; the Goddess abides in that state and leads the devotee into it.

793 कपर्दिनी kapardinī

She who is the consort of Kapardin, Śiva of the matted locks

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Śiva is Kapardin, 'the one with the braided coil of hair'; as His inseparable power She bears the same name in the feminine. The feminine can also describe Her own braided hair.

Uncertain The feminine of kapardin can mean 'wife of Kapardin' (the usual reading) or 'She who herself wears the kaparda braid'.

794 कलामाला kalā-mālā

She who wears the arts as a garland

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (alternatively bahuvrīhi). As a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa mālā 'garland' is the head: 'the garland of the arts', She herself being that garland. As a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose garland is the arts', i.e. who wears them. Both readings are current; the second matches the traditional paraphrase.

Analysis कलानाम् माला कलामाला; अथवा कलाः माला यस्याः सा कलामाला
kalānām mālā kalāmālā; athavā kalāḥ mālā yasyāḥ sā kalāmālā

Significance Traditionally the sixty-four arts (catuḥṣaṣṭi kalāḥ) are meant, strung together as Her ornament; kalā can also be read as the digits of the moon or the subtle portions of Her power.

Uncertain Ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa ('the garland of the arts') and bahuvrīhi ('whose garland is the arts') readings are both current.

795 कामधुक् kāma-dhuk

She who fulfills all desires

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. The final member dhuk is a root-noun from √duh 'to milk' with the zero suffix kvip, which can stand only at the end of a compound with its object as the upapada: 'one who milks out desires', i.e. yields what is wished for.

Analysis कामान् दोग्धि इति कामधुक्
kāmān dogdhi iti kāmadhuk

Significance The name calls up Kāmadhenu, the wish-yielding cow; as the cow gives milk freely to her calf, She yields to Her devotees whatever they seek, worldly and spiritual.

796 कामरूपिणी kāma-rūpiṇī

She who assumes any form at will

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa, made possessive by the suffix -in (alternatively ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) kāma-rūpa 'form (taken) at will' — kāma here means 'free choice', the instrumental relation of a tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa. (2) The possessive suffix -in, feminine -iṇī, makes it 'She who has forms at will', i.e. takes any form She wishes. Read as a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, kāmarūpa is 'the form of Kāma (Kāmeśvara or the god of love)', and the name becomes 'She who has the form of Kāma'.

Analysis कामेन रूपम् कामरूपम्; कामरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति कामरूपिणी; अथवा कामस्य रूपम् कामरूपम्
kāmena rūpam kāmarūpam; kāmarūpam asyāḥ asti iti kāmarūpiṇī; athavā kāmasya rūpam kāmarūpam

Significance Traditionally also read as the presiding Goddess of Kāmarūpa, the Śakti-pīṭha of Kāmākhyā, and as She whose form is one with Kāmeśvara.

Uncertain Three readings are current: 'taking form at will', 'having the form of Kāma/Kāmeśvara', and 'Goddess of Kāmarūpa'.

Śloka 152names 797–805

कलानिधिः काव्यकला रसज्ञा रसशेवधिः ।
पुष्टा पुरातना पूज्या पुष्करा पुष्करेक्षणा ॥ १५२ ॥

kalānidhiḥ kāvyakalā rasajñā rasaśevadhiḥ |
puṣṭā purātanā pūjyā puṣkarā puṣkarekṣaṇā || 152 ||

The names, separated

797कला-निधिःkalā-nidhiḥ798काव्य-कलाkāvya-kalā799रस-ज्ञाrasa-jñā800रस-शेवधिःrasa-śevadhiḥ

801पुष्टाpuṣṭā802पुरातनाpurātanā803पूज्याpūjyā804पुष्कराpuṣkarā805पुष्करेक्षणाpuṣkarekṣaṇā

797She who is the treasure-house of all arts; 798She who is the art of poetry; 799She who knows all the rasas; 800She who is the treasure-house of rasa;

Word by word

SanskritEnglish

रसrasataste, essence; aesthetic emotion

रसrasaessence, bliss, aesthetic flavor
शेवधिःśevadhiḥtreasure, treasury
801 पुष्टा puṣṭā
पुष्टाpuṣṭānourished, full, thriving√puṣ 'to nourish, thrive', past participle, feminine

पुरातनाpurātanāancient, of oldthe indeclinable purā 'formerly' + the suffix -tana, feminine

Where the names meet

Names 801–805 all begin with pu-/pū-; 804 puṣkarā and 805 puṣkarekṣaṇā are separate names.

The names

797 कलानिधिः kalā-nidhiḥ

She who is the treasure-house of all arts

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. nidhi 'treasury, store' is the head and kalā stands to it in the genitive: 'the treasury of the arts'. The masculine noun nidhi keeps its own gender as Her name.

Analysis कलानाम् निधिः कलानिधिः
kalānām nidhiḥ kalānidhiḥ

Significance Kalānidhi is also a name of the moon, the 'store of digits'; traditionally She is the moon that holds all sixteen kalās, and the source of every art.

798 काव्यकला kāvya-kalā

She who is the art of poetry

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya (alternatively ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). kalā is the head. As a karmadhāraya: 'the art that is poetry'; as a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa: 'the art of poetry'. The sense is the same.

Analysis काव्यम् एव कला काव्यकला; अथवा काव्यस्य कला काव्यकला
kāvyam eva kalā kāvyakalā; athavā kāvyasya kalā kāvyakalā

Significance Traditionally all poetry and song are Her form, and She grants the gift of poetic speech to Her devotees.

799 रसज्ञा rasa-jñā

She who knows all the rasas

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. jña 'knowing' is formed from √jñā with the suffix -a and stands only at the end of a compound, with its object (rasa) as the upapada: 'one who knows rasa'; feminine -ā.

Analysis रसम् जानाति इति रसज्ञा
rasam jānāti iti rasajñā

Significance Rasa is both the flavor of things and the aesthetic emotion of poetry and drama; She knows every rasa. Rasajñā is also a word for the tongue, the organ that knows taste.

800 रसशेवधिः rasa-śevadhiḥ

She who is the treasure-house of rasa

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. śevadhi 'treasure' is the head and rasa stands to it in the genitive: 'the treasure of rasa'. The masculine noun keeps its gender as Her name.

Analysis रसस्य शेवधिः रसशेवधिः
rasasya śevadhiḥ rasaśevadhiḥ

Significance The Taittirīya Upaniṣad says of the Self raso vai saḥ, 'He is rasa; obtaining rasa one becomes blissful'; She is the store of that bliss.

801 पुष्टा puṣṭā

She who is full of vigor and abundantly nourished

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Traditionally She is the fullness that nourishes every being; Puṣṭi, 'nourishment', is counted among Her powers.

802 पुरातना purātanā

She who is ancient

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance She is the primordial one, existing before all that was created.

803 पूज्या pūjyā

She who is worthy of worship by all

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance As the gerundive says, worship is Her due; traditionally even the gods worship Her.

804 पुष्करा puṣkarā

She who is whole and gives nourishment to all

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Traditionally read as She who nourishes all, connecting the name with puṣṭā (801); puṣkara also names the lotus, the sky and the holy lake Puṣkara.

Uncertain puṣkara has many senses (lotus, water, sky, the tīrtha Puṣkara); the gloss 'nourishing' rests on a traditional etymology from √puṣ rather than on regular grammar.

805 पुष्करेक्षणा puṣkarekṣaṇā

She who has eyes like lotus petals

Sandhi पुष्करेक्षणा = पुष्कर + ईक्षणा (puṣkara + īkṣaṇā) — guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (with an upamāna comparison). A comparison folded into a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose eyes (īkṣaṇa) are like lotuses (puṣkara)'. īkṣaṇa takes the feminine -ā to agree with Her.

Analysis पुष्करे इव ईक्षणे यस्याः सा पुष्करेक्षणा
puṣkare iva īkṣaṇe yasyāḥ sā puṣkarekṣaṇā

Significance Lotus eyes are the classical sign of grace: wide, cool and compassionate, they rest on the devotee as a lotus opens to the sun.

Śloka 153names 806–812

परञ्ज्योतिः परन्धाम परमाणुः परात्परा ।
पाशहस्ता पाशहन्त्री परमन्त्रविभेदिनी ॥ १५३ ॥

parañjyotiḥ parandhāma paramāṇuḥ parātparā |
pāśahastā pāśahantrī paramantravibhedinī || 153 ||

The names, separated

806परञ्-ज्योतिःparañ-jyotiḥ807परन्-धामparan-dhāma808परमाणुःparamāṇuḥ809परात्-पराparāt-parā

810पाश-हस्ताpāśa-hastā811पाश-हन्त्रीpāśa-hantrī812पर-मन्त्र-विभेदिनीpara-mantra-vibhedinī

806She who is the supreme light; 807She who is the supreme abode; 808She who is the subtlest particle; 809She who is the most supreme of the supreme ones;

810She who holds a noose in Her hand; 811She who destroys the bonds; 812She who shatters the mantras employed by enemies.

पाशpāśanoose
