Where the names meet

Names 806 and 807 are two-word phrases (param jyotiḥ, param dhāma) whose m has become ñ and n before the next consonant; they are not compounds of para.

The names

806 परञ्ज्योतिः parañ-jyotiḥ

She who is the supreme light

Sandhi परञ्ज्योतिः = परम् + ज्योतिः (param + jyotiḥ) — a word-final m becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ), which here takes the nasal of the following palatal, ñ (optional, 8.4.59 vā padāntasya)

Compound not a compound

Significance The Chāndogya Upaniṣad speaks of the self that, 'reaching the supreme light (paraṃ jyotir upasampadya)', appears in its own form; She is that light, by which sun, moon and fire shine.

807 परन्धाम paran-dhāma

She who is the supreme abode

Sandhi परन्धाम = परम् + धाम (param + dhāma) — a word-final m becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ), which here takes the nasal of the following dental, n (optional, 8.4.59 vā padāntasya)

Compound not a compound

Significance The Bhagavad Gītā (10.12) calls the Lord paraṃ brahma paraṃ dhāma, 'the supreme Brahman, the supreme abode'; She is the final resting place from which there is no return.

808 परमाणुः paramāṇuḥ

She who is the subtlest particle

Sandhi परमाणुः = परम + अणुः (parama + aṇuḥ) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound karmadhāraya. parama 'utmost' qualifies aṇu 'minute particle', the head: 'the utmost-minute one', the subtlest particle. The masculine aṇu keeps its gender as Her name.

Analysis परमः अणुः परमाणुः
paramaḥ aṇuḥ paramāṇuḥ

Significance The Kaṭha Upaniṣad describes the Self as aṇor aṇīyān, 'subtler than the subtle'; She pervades even the smallest thing and is too fine to be grasped by the senses.

809 परात्परा parāt-parā

She who is the most supreme of the supreme ones

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound pañcamī-tatpuruṣa of the aluk kind (the first member keeps its ablative ending). parā 'higher, supreme' is the head; parāt 'than the high' is an ablative of comparison and keeps its case ending inside the compound (aluk): 'higher than the highest'. It can equally be taken as a fixed two-word phrase.

Analysis परात् परा परात्परा
parāt parā parātparā

Significance Nothing stands beyond Her: She transcends even what is called supreme, such as the deities of creation, preservation and dissolution.

Uncertain Whether parātparā is an aluk compound or a two-word phrase written together is a matter of analysis; the meaning is the same.

810 पाशहस्ता pāśa-hastā

She who holds a noose in Her hand

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (vyadhikaraṇa: the members are in different cases). 'She in whose hand (hasta) is the noose (pāśa)': the noose is nominative, the hand locative, so the bahuvrīhi joins members that do not agree. hasta takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis पाशः हस्ते यस्याः सा पाशहस्ता
pāśaḥ haste yasyāḥ sā pāśahastā

Significance The noose is one of Her four emblems (name 8 describes it as the power of attachment); holding it She binds, and the next name says She also cuts every bond.

811 पाशहन्त्री pāśa-hantrī

She who destroys the bonds

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. hantrī 'destroyer' (agent noun from √han) is the head and the nooses stand to it in the genitive. Pāṇini restricts such compounds of an object with a -tṛ agent noun (2.2.15), but names of this shape are admitted as compounds of general relation (śeṣa-ṣaṣṭhī).

Analysis पाशानाम् हन्त्री पाशहन्त्री
pāśānām hantrī pāśahantrī

Significance In Śaiva doctrine the soul in bondage is the paśu, held by the pāśa of impurity, karma and māyā; She who holds the noose (810) is also the one who severs it.

812 परमन्त्रविभेदिनी para-mantra-vibhedinī

She who shatters the mantras employed by enemies

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) para-mantra 'the mantras of others', i.e. of enemies (para here is 'other, hostile', not 'supreme'). (2) vibhedinī 'one who breaks apart' is the head, with those mantras in the genitive.

Analysis परेषाम् मन्त्राः परमन्त्राः; परमन्त्राणाम् विभेदिनी परमन्त्रविभेदिनी
pareṣām mantrāḥ paramantrāḥ; paramantrāṇām vibhedinī paramantravibhedinī

Significance Traditionally She protects the devotee from hostile spells and rites; mantra can also mean an enemy's counsel, which She brings to nothing.

Śloka 154names 813–820

मूर्ता ऽमूर्ता ऽनित्यतृप्ता मुनिमानसहंसिका ।
सत्यव्रता सत्यरूपा सर्वान्तर्यामिनी सती ॥ १५४ ॥

mūrtā 'mūrtā 'nityatṛptā munimānasahaṃsikā |
satyavratā satyarūpā sarvāntaryāminī satī || 154 ||

The names, separated ° form as a name on its own; in the recitation above it joins its neighbour

817सत्य-व्रताsatya-vratā818सत्य-रूपाsatya-rūpā819सर्वान्तर्-यामिनीsarvāntar-yāminī820सतीsatī

Translation

813She who has forms; 814She who has no definite form; 815She who is satisfied even by our perishable offerings; 816She who is the swan in the Mānasa lake that is the minds of sages;

817She whose vow is truth, who abides firmly in truth; 818She who is truth itself; 819She who is the inner ruler dwelling within all; 820She who is Being itself, the Real; She who is Satī.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish
813 मूर्ता mūrtā

अanotthe negative particle na in composition

अनित्यanityaimpermanent, perishablea- 'not' + nitya 'lasting'

मुनिmunisage, silent contemplative
मानसmānasamind; also Lake Mānasafrom manas 'mind'
हंसिकाhaṃsikāfemale swanhaṃsī 'female swan' with the suffix -ka (affectionate); ī shortened before it

सत्यsatyatruth

सत्यsatyatruth, the real
रूपाrūpāform, naturerūpa with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

अन्तर्antarwithin

820 सती satī
सतीsatībeing, real; virtuous; Satīpresent participle of √as 'to be' (sat), feminine -ī

Where the names meet

मूर्ताऽमूर्ता = मूर्ता + अमूर्ता (mūrtā + amūrtā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); the avagraha (ऽ) marks the absorbed initial a of the next name

अमूर्ताऽनित्यतृप्ता = अमूर्ता + अनित्यतृप्ता (amūrtā + anityatṛptā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); the avagraha (ऽ) marks the absorbed initial a of the next name

Three names hide in mūrtā'mūrtā'nityatṛptā: 813 mūrtā, 814 amūrtā, 815 anityatṛptā. Without the avagrahas the last could be misread as nityatṛptā.

The names

813 मूर्ता mūrtā

She who has forms

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance The Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad (2.3.1) says Brahman has two forms, the formed (mūrta) and the formless (amūrta); names 813 and 814 give Her both.

814 अमूर्ता amūrtā

She who has no definite form

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound nañ-tatpuruṣa. The negative particle na appears as a- before a consonant and negates the head mūrtā: 'not having form'.

Analysis न मूर्ता अमूर्ता
na mūrtā amūrtā

Significance Paired with 813: as the formless She is the unmanifest Brahman beyond the reach of the senses, and the formed and the formless are equally Her.

815 अनित्यतृप्ता anitya-tṛptā

She who is satisfied even by our perishable offerings

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner nañ-tatpuruṣa). (1) a-nitya 'not lasting, perishable' (nañ-tatpuruṣa). (2) The participle tṛptā 'satisfied' is the head and takes perishable things in the instrumental: 'satisfied with what is perishable'.

Analysis न नित्यम् अनित्यम्; अनित्यैः तृप्ता अनित्यतृप्ता
na nityam anityam; anityaiḥ tṛptā anityatṛptā

Significance Traditionally read as Her grace: the Eternal is pleased with transient offerings such as a flower, a leaf or water given with devotion.

Uncertain The śloka's continuous text mūrtāmūrtānitya… could also be divided amūrtā + nityatṛptā 'ever satisfied'; the edited text marks the a of anitya with an avagraha, following the traditional division.

816 मुनिमानसहंसिका muni-mānasa-haṃsikā

She who is the swan in the Mānasa lake that is the minds of sages

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound saptamī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) muni-mānasa 'the mind of sages' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) haṃsikā 'swan' is the head and the mind is its locative: 'the swan in the sages' mind'. mānasa is a double meaning: 'mind' and Lake Mānasa, the swans' home; the sages' mind is that lake.

Analysis मुनीनाम् मानसम् मुनिमानसम्; मुनिमानसे हंसिका मुनिमानसहंसिका
munīnām mānasam munimānasam; munimānase haṃsikā munimānasahaṃsikā

Significance As swans dwell on Lake Mānasa, She sports in the still minds of sages; the haṃsa is also the breath-mantra haṃsa/so 'ham and the soul's discrimination of the real from the unreal.

817 सत्यव्रता satya-vratā

She whose vow is truth, who abides firmly in truth

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. 'She whose vow (vrata) is truth (satya)': the two members agree and together describe Her; vrata takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis सत्यम् व्रतम् यस्याः सा सत्यव्रता
satyam vratam yasyāḥ sā satyavratā

Significance Traditionally She never departs from Her word, and She is reached by those whose observance is truthfulness.

818 सत्यरूपा satya-rūpā

She who is truth itself

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. 'She whose form (rūpa) is truth': rūpa takes the feminine -ā; She is truth itself, not a possessor of it.

Analysis सत्यम् रूपम् यस्याः सा सत्यरूपा
satyam rūpam yasyāḥ sā satyarūpā

Significance Traditionally connected with the Upaniṣadic satyasya satyam, 'the truth of truth': She is the reality on which all relative truths rest.

819 सर्वान्तर्यामिनी sarvāntar-yāminī

She who is the inner ruler dwelling within all

Sandhi सर्वान्तर् = सर्व + अन्तर् (sarva + antar) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (the final member itself an upapada compound). (1) antar-yāmin 'the one who controls from within' (antar 'within' + √yam 'to restrain, guide' + -in). (2) It is the head of a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa with sarva 'all': 'the inner controller of all'.

Analysis अन्तः यच्छति इति अन्तर्यामिनी; सर्वेषाम् अन्तर्यामिनी सर्वान्तर्यामिनी
antaḥ yacchati iti antaryāminī; sarveṣām antaryāminī sarvāntaryāminī

Significance The Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad's antaryāmin teaching describes the Self that dwells in every being and rules it from within, unknown to it; She is that inner controller.

820 सती satī

She who is Being itself, the Real; She who is Satī

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance As sat She is pure existence, the ground of all that is; She is also Satī, the daughter of Dakṣa who gave up Her body rather than hear Śiva reviled, and from whose limbs the Śakti-pīṭhas arose.

Śloka 155names 821–830

ब्रह्माणी ब्रह्म जननी बहुरूपा बुधार्चिता ।
प्रसवित्री प्रचण्डा ऽऽज्ञा प्रतिष्ठा प्रकटाकृतिः ॥ १५५ ॥

brahmāṇī brahma jananī bahurūpā budhārcitā |
prasavitrī pracaṇḍā ''jñā pratiṣṭhā prakaṭākṛtiḥ || 155 ||

The names

821 ब्रह्माणी brahmāṇī

She who is Brahmāṇī, the creative power of Brahmā

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Brahmāṇī is one of the mother-goddesses (Mātṛkās). Traditionally the name is also connected with the Taittirīya Upaniṣad's brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā, 'Brahman is the tail, the support', which lies behind the older rendering.

Uncertain The traditional interpretation through 'brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā' rests on a derivation that could not be confirmed; the plain grammatical sense is given as the meaning.

822 ब्रह्म brahma

She who is Brahman

Sandhi ब्रह्मजननी = ब्रह्म + जननी (brahma + jananī) — No sound change: the śloka's ब्रह्मजननी is divided by Bhāskararāya into two names, ब्रह्म (822) and जननी (823). brahma is the neuter nominative singular of brahman (the final n is lost at the end of the word), so the two words simply stand side by side.

Compound not a compound

Significance The Goddess is identified with the Absolute of the Upaniṣads, without attributes and beyond all names; the neuter noun keeps its own gender as Her name.

Variants Read as one word, ब्रह्मजननी would be the single name 'Mother of Brahmā (or of Brahman)', as some popular lists take it; Bhāskararāya's count of a thousand requires two names here.

823 जननी jananī

She who is the Mother

Sandhi ब्रह्मजननी = ब्रह्म + जननी (brahma + jananī) — No sound change: jananī is the second of the two names into which Bhāskararāya divides the śloka's ब्रह्मजननी (see 822).

Compound not a compound

Significance Standing on its own, the name makes Her the mother of all without limit; read with 822, the Absolute itself is the one who gives birth.

Variants See 822: some lists read ब्रह्मजननी as one name.

824 बहुरूपा bahu-rūpā

She who has a multitude of forms

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. 'She whose forms are many': bahu 'many' and rūpa 'form' agree and together describe Her; rūpa takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis बहूनि रूपाणि यस्याः सा बहुरूपा
bahūni rūpāṇi yasyāḥ sā bahurūpā

Significance The Kaṭha Upaniṣad speaks of the one who 'makes the one form manifold' (ekaṃ rūpaṃ bahudhā yaḥ karoti); every form in the universe is Hers.

825 बुधार्चिता budhārcitā

She who is worshipped by the wise

Sandhi बुधार्चिता = बुध + अर्चिता (budha + arcitā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa. The participle arcitā 'worshipped' is the head and the wise are the agents in the instrumental: 'worshipped by the wise'.

Analysis बुधैः अर्चिता बुधार्चिता
budhaiḥ arcitā budhārcitā

Significance Traditionally the wise are those who know Her true nature; budha can also be the planet Mercury or the gods, all of whom worship Her.

826 प्रसवित्री prasavitrī

She who is mother of the universe

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Traditionally the name is connected with Savitṛ, the impeller of the Gāyatrī mantra: She is the one who brings the whole universe forth.

827 प्रचण्डा pracaṇḍā

She who is full of awe-inspiring wrath

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound prādi-tatpuruṣa. The prefix pra 'forth, exceedingly' intensifies the head caṇḍā 'fierce': 'exceedingly fierce'.

Analysis प्रकर्षेण चण्डा प्रचण्डा
prakarṣeṇa caṇḍā pracaṇḍā

Significance The Taittirīya Upaniṣad says that from fear of the Absolute the wind blows and the sun rises; Her fierceness is that awe which keeps the cosmic order, and it is turned against the devotee's foes.

828 आज्ञा ājñā

She who is the divine command Herself

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Her command is the law of the universe, which even the gods obey; ājñā is also the cakra between the eyebrows, the 'command' center, where She is meditated upon.

829 प्रतिष्ठा pratiṣṭhā

She who is the foundation

Sandhi प्रतिष्ठा = प्रति + स्था (prati + sthā) — after the i of the prefix prati the s of sthā becomes ṣ (Pāṇini 8.3.65), and th then becomes ṭh next to ṣ (ṣṭutva, Pāṇini 8.4.41 ṣṭunā ṣṭuḥ)

Compound not a compound

Significance She is the ground on which everything stands (the Taittirīya Upaniṣad's brahma pucchaṃ pratiṣṭhā). Pratiṣṭhā is also the second of the five kalās of Śaiva doctrine, which name 853 brings to its summit.

830 प्रकटाकृतिः prakaṭākṛtiḥ

She whose form is manifest

Sandhi प्रकटाकृतिः = प्रकट + आकृतिः (prakaṭa + ākṛtiḥ) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi. 'She whose form (ākṛti) is manifest (prakaṭā)'. The feminine adjective prakaṭā takes its masculine stem prakaṭa in the compound (puṃvadbhāva, Pāṇini 6.3.34). The final member ākṛti is already feminine and keeps its nominative -iḥ.

Analysis प्रकटा आकृतिः यस्याः सा प्रकटाकृतिः
prakaṭā ākṛtiḥ yasyāḥ sā prakaṭākṛtiḥ

Significance Traditionally She is manifest to everyone as the sense 'I am'. In Śrīvidyā the yoginīs of the outermost enclosure of the Śrīcakra are called prakaṭa 'manifest', and the name is also read as Her having them for Her form.

Śloka 156names 831–837

प्राणेश्वरी प्राणदात्री पञ्चाशत्पीठरूपिणी ।
विशृङ्खला विविक्तस्था वीरमाता वियत्प्रसूः ॥ १५६ ॥

prāṇeśvarī prāṇadātrī pañcāśatpīṭharūpiṇī |
viśṛṅkhalā viviktasthā vīramātā viyatprasūḥ || 156 ||

The names, separated

831She who rules over the prāṇas and the senses; 832She who is the giver of life; 833She whose form is the fifty sacred seats (pīṭhas);

834She who is unfettered, free in every way; 835She who abides in secluded places; 836She who is the mother of the valiant; 837She who is the mother of the ether (space).

The names

831 प्राणेश्वरी prāṇeśvarī

She who rules over the prāṇas and the senses

Sandhi प्राणेश्वरी = प्राण + ईश्वरी (prāṇa + īśvarī) — guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. īśvarī 'ruler' is the head and the prāṇas stand to it in the genitive: 'the ruler of the vital breaths'. In the Upaniṣads prāṇāḥ (plural) also means the senses.

Analysis प्राणानाम् ईश्वरी प्राणेश्वरी
prāṇānām īśvarī prāṇeśvarī

Significance Traditionally also 'Queen of life' in the sense of beloved: She is the life-breath of Śiva, and of every living being.

832 प्राणदात्री prāṇa-dātrī

She who is the giver of life

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. dātrī 'giver' (agent noun from √dā) is the head and the prāṇas stand to it in the genitive: 'the giver of life-breath' (on such compounds with -tṛ see name 811).

Analysis प्राणानाम् दात्री प्राणदात्री
prāṇānām dātrī prāṇadātrī

Significance She gives breath to every creature; the Kauṣītaki and other Upaniṣads identify prāṇa with consciousness, so She gives both life and awareness.

833 पञ्चाशत्पीठरूपिणी pañcāśat-pīṭha-rūpiṇī

She whose form is the fifty sacred seats (pīṭhas)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound dvigu (numeral karmadhāraya), made possessive by the suffix -in. (1) pañcāśat-pīṭha 'the fifty seats': a numeral qualifying a noun, i.e. a dvigu, allowed because a further member follows. (2) That compound with rūpa 'form' takes the possessive suffix -in (feminine -iṇī): 'She whose form is the fifty seats'. The final t of pañcāśat is unchanged before p.

Analysis पञ्चाशत् पीठानि पञ्चाशत्पीठानि; पञ्चाशत्पीठानि रूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति पञ्चाशत्पीठरूपिणी
pañcāśat pīṭhāni pañcāśatpīṭhāni; pañcāśatpīṭhāni rūpam asyāḥ asti iti pañcāśatpīṭharūpiṇī

Significance Traditionally the fifty pīṭhas correspond to the fifty letters of the Sanskrit alphabet (the mātṛkās), placed on the body in nyāsa; the sacred places of the land and the sounds of speech are both Her body.

834 विशृङ्खला vi-śṛṅkhalā

She who is unfettered, free in every way

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound prādi-bahuvrīhi. The prefix vi stands for vigata 'gone': 'She from whom fetters (śṛṅkhala) are gone', i.e. who is bound by nothing. The final member takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis विगतानि शृङ्खलानि यस्याः सा विशृङ्खला
vigatāni śṛṅkhalāni yasyāḥ sā viśṛṅkhalā

Significance Traditionally She is bound by no rule, karma or injunction, being the source of all laws; She also frees Her devotees from every chain.

Corrected विश‍ृङ्खला → विशृङ्खला. Removed a zero-width joiner inside शृ; the IAST had become "viśa‍ṛṅkhalā".

835 विविक्तस्था vivikta-sthā

She who abides in secluded places

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. stha 'standing, dwelling' is formed from √sthā with the suffix -a after a word in the locative (Pāṇini 3.2.4 supi sthaḥ): 'one who dwells in a secluded place'; feminine -ā.

Analysis विविक्ते तिष्ठति इति विविक्तस्था
vivikte tiṣṭhati iti viviktasthā

Significance Traditionally She dwells in solitary, pure places and in the discerning mind (viveka) of those who sift the real from the unreal.

836 वीरमाता vīra-mātā

She who is the mother of the valiant

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. mātā 'mother' is the head and the heroes stand to it in the genitive.

Analysis वीराणाम् माता वीरमाता
vīrāṇām mātā vīramātā

Significance In Tantra the vīra is the adept of the heroic disposition (vīrabhāva); She is mother to the courageous in battle and in sādhana.

837 वियत्प्रसूः viyat-prasūḥ

She who is the mother of the ether (space)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. prasū 'mother, one who brings forth' is the head and the sky stands to it in the genitive: 'mother of space'. prasū is a root-noun (pra + √sū), so its nominative ends in -ūḥ.

Analysis वियतः प्रसूः वियत्प्रसूः
viyataḥ prasūḥ viyatprasūḥ

Significance The Taittirīya Upaniṣad says that from the Self space (ākāśa) first arose; She is the source of space, the first of the elements, and so of all the rest.

Śloka 157names 838–843

मुकुन्दा मुक्तिनिलया मूलविग्रहरूपिणी ।
भावज्ञा भवरोगघ्नी भवचक्रप्रवर्तिनी ॥ १५७ ॥

mukundā muktinilayā mūlavigraharūpiṇī |
bhāvajñā bhavarogaghnī bhavacakrapravartinī || 157 ||

The names, separated

838मुकुन्दाmukundā839मुक्ति-निलयाmukti-nilayā840मूल-विग्रह-रूपिणीmūla-vigraha-rūpiṇī

841भाव-ज्ञाbhāva-jñā842भव-रोग-घ्नीbhava-roga-ghnī843भव-चक्र-प्रवर्तिनीbhava-cakra-pravartinī

838She who grants liberation; She who is Mukundā, one with Viṣṇu; 839She who is the abode of liberation; 840She who is the root form of everything;

841She who is the knower of all thoughts and sentiments; 842She who destroys the disease of worldly existence, the round of birth and death; 843She who turns the wheel of the cycle of birth and death.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish

मुक्तिmuktiliberation√muc 'to release' + -ti
निलयाnilayāabode, dwellingni + √lī 'to rest in'; nilaya with the feminine -ā

मूलmūlaroot, original, source
विग्रहvigrahaform, embodiment, image
रूपिणीrūpiṇīhaving the form ofrūpa 'form' + the possessive suffix -in (ṇ by ṇatva after r), feminine -ī

भावbhāvainner state, feeling, intention; being√bhū 'to be' + -a, with vṛddhi

Where the names meet

Names 842–843 face each other: She destroys the disease of existence and also turns its wheel.

The names

838 मुकुन्दा mukundā

She who grants liberation; She who is Mukundā, one with Viṣṇu

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Mukunda is Viṣṇu, and She is His feminine counterpart (the Goddess as Viṣṇu's own power); the traditional etymology 'giver of muku, liberation' gives the older rendering.

Uncertain The derivation muku 'liberation' + dā 'giving' is a traditional etymology (nirukti), not regular grammar.

839 मुक्तिनिलया mukti-nilayā

She who is the abode of liberation

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, used adjectivally (alternatively bahuvrīhi). (1) mukti-nilaya 'the dwelling-place of liberation' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, nilaya the head). The compound is used of Her as an epithet and so takes the feminine -ā; traditionally this is explained by the possessive suffix ac of the arśa-ādi class ('having, being X'). As a bahuvrīhi it reads 'She whose dwelling is liberation'. Either way She and liberation are found in one place.

Analysis मुक्तेः निलयः मुक्तिनिलयः; मुक्तिनिलयः अस्याः अस्ति इति मुक्तिनिलया; अथवा मुक्तिः निलयः यस्याः सा मुक्तिनिलया
mukteḥ nilayaḥ muktinilayaḥ; muktinilayaḥ asyāḥ asti iti muktinilayā; athavā muktiḥ nilayaḥ yasyāḥ sā muktinilayā

Significance Traditionally the four kinds of liberation (sālokya, sāmīpya, sārūpya, sāyujya) reside in Her, and She is reached in the state of liberation itself.

Uncertain The feminine ending admits two analyses: an adjectival ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa ('the abode of liberation') and a bahuvrīhi ('whose abode is liberation').

840 मूलविग्रहरूपिणी mūla-vigraha-rūpiṇī

She who is the root form of everything

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya, made possessive by the suffix -in. (1) mūla-vigraha 'the root form' (karmadhāraya: mūla 'root, original' qualifies vigraha 'form, embodiment'). (2) With rūpa and the possessive suffix -in: 'She whose form is the root form'.

Analysis मूलम् विग्रहः मूलविग्रहः; मूलविग्रहः रूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति मूलविग्रहरूपिणी
mūlam vigrahaḥ mūlavigrahaḥ; mūlavigrahaḥ rūpam asyāḥ asti iti mūlavigraharūpiṇī

Significance In Śrīvidyā She is the original form from which the other forms of the Goddess, such as Bālā and the attendant powers of the Śrīcakra, issue; mūla also recalls the mūlādhāra and the root mantra (mūla-mantra).

841 भावज्ञा bhāva-jñā

She who is the knower of all thoughts and sentiments

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. jña 'knowing' (√jñā + -a) stands at the end of the compound with its object bhāva as the upapada: 'one who knows (inner) states'; feminine -ā.

Analysis भावम् जानाति इति भावज्ञा
bhāvam jānāti iti bhāvajñā

Significance She knows the intention behind every act of devotion, and so accepts even an imperfect offering made with a true heart; bhāva also means existence, all of which She knows.

842 भवरोगघ्नी bhava-roga-ghnī

She who destroys the disease of worldly existence, the round of birth and death

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya of identification). (1) bhava-roga 'the disease that is worldly existence': a karmadhāraya of identification (rūpaka) — existence itself is the disease. (2) ghnī 'destroying' (from √han) stands at the end with the disease as its object (upapada-tatpuruṣa).

Analysis भवः एव रोगः भवरोगः; भवरोगम् हन्ति इति भवरोगघ्नी
bhavaḥ eva rogaḥ bhavarogaḥ; bhavarogam hanti iti bhavarogaghnī

Significance Traditionally saṃsāra is the disease and knowledge of Her the remedy; She is the physician of the soul.

843 भवचक्रप्रवर्तिनी bhava-cakra-pravartinī

She who turns the wheel of the cycle of birth and death

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya of identification). (1) bhava-cakra 'the wheel that is worldly existence' (rūpaka karmadhāraya). (2) pravartinī 'she who sets in motion' is the head, with the wheel in the genitive.

Analysis भवः एव चक्रम् भवचक्रम्; भवचक्रस्य प्रवर्तिनी भवचक्रप्रवर्तिनी
bhavaḥ eva cakram bhavacakram; bhavacakrasya pravartinī bhavacakrapravartinī

Significance The same Power that frees (842) also keeps the wheel of existence turning, by Her will, for the ripening of every soul's karma.

छन्दःसारा शास्त्रसारा मन्त्रसारा तलोदरी ।

Word by word

SanskritEnglish
844 छन्दःसारा chandaḥ-sārā
छन्दस्chandasVedic hymn, the Veda; meter
साराsārāessence, coresāra with the feminine -ā
845 शास्त्रसारा śāstra-sārā
शास्त्रśāstrascripture, authoritative teaching√śās 'to instruct' + -tra
साराsārāessencesāra with the feminine -ā
846 मन्त्रसारा mantra-sārā
मन्त्रmantramantra, sacred formula
साराsārāessencesāra with the feminine -ā
847 तलोदरी talodarī
तलtalaflat surface, palm; also the nether worlds (atala, vitala …)
उदरीudarībelly, waistudara with the feminine -ī of the bahuvrīhi
848 उदारकीर्तिः udāra-kīrtiḥ
उदारudāraexalted, noble, generous
कीर्तिःkīrtiḥfame, glory√kṝt 'to proclaim' + -ti
849 उद्दामवैभवा uddāma-vaibhavā
उद्udup, out, away (prefix)
दामdāmarope, bonddāman, n lost in composition
वैभवाvaibhavāmight, glory, magnificencevaibhava (from vibhu 'pervading, mighty'), with the feminine -ā
850 वर्णरूपिणी varṇa-rūpiṇī
वर्णvarṇaletter, sound of the alphabet; also color, class
रूपिणीrūpiṇīhaving the form ofrūpa 'form' + the possessive suffix -in (ṇ by ṇatva after r), feminine -ī

Where the names meet

उदारकीर्तिरुद्दामवैभवा = उदारकीर्तिः + उद्दामवैभवा (udārakīrtiḥ + uddāmavaibhavā) — visarga after a vowel other than a or ā becomes r before a voiced sound, here the vowel u

Divide udārakīrtir uddāmavaibhavā (848, 849): the r belongs to the visarga of kīrtiḥ, not to the next name (not udārakīrti ruddāma).

The names

844 छन्दःसारा chandaḥ-sārā

She who is the essence of the Vedas

Sandhi छन्दःसारा = छन्दस् + सारा (chandas + sārā) — the final s of chandas becomes visarga at the end of a member and, before s, may stay as visarga instead of s (optional, Pāṇini 8.3.36 vā śari)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, used adjectivally. (1) chandaḥ-sāra 'the essence of the Vedas' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, sāra the head). The compound is used of Her as an epithet and so takes the feminine -ā; traditionally this is explained by the possessive suffix ac of the arśa-ādi class ('having, being X').

Analysis छन्दसाम् सारः छन्दःसारः; छन्दःसारः अस्याः अस्ति इति छन्दःसारा
chandasām sāraḥ chandaḥsāraḥ; chandaḥsāraḥ asyāḥ asti iti chandaḥsārā

Significance Chandas is the Veda as metrical hymn; traditionally the Gāyatrī, the 'mother of the Vedas', is their essence and is Her form.

845 शास्त्रसारा śāstra-sārā

She who is the essence of all scriptures

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, used adjectivally. (1) śāstra-sāra 'the essence of the scriptures' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). The compound is used of Her as an epithet and so takes the feminine -ā; traditionally this is explained by the possessive suffix ac of the arśa-ādi class ('having, being X').

Analysis शास्त्राणाम् सारः शास्त्रसारः; शास्त्रसारः अस्याः अस्ति इति शास्त्रसारा
śāstrāṇām sāraḥ śāstrasāraḥ; śāstrasāraḥ asyāḥ asti iti śāstrasārā

Significance Every śāstra, from the Vedas and Upaniṣads to the Tantras and Purāṇas, has Her as its final import.

846 मन्त्रसारा mantra-sārā

She who is the essence of all mantras

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, used adjectivally. (1) mantra-sāra 'the essence of mantras' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). The compound is used of Her as an epithet and so takes the feminine -ā; traditionally this is explained by the possessive suffix ac of the arśa-ādi class ('having, being X').

Analysis मन्त्राणाम् सारः मन्त्रसारः; मन्त्रसारः अस्याः अस्ति इति मन्त्रसारा
mantrāṇām sāraḥ mantrasāraḥ; mantrasāraḥ asyāḥ asti iti mantrasārā

Significance In Śrīvidyā the fifteen-syllabled Pañcadaśī (and its sixteen-syllabled form) is regarded as the crown of all mantras, and it is Her very form.

847 तलोदरी talodarī

She who is slender-waisted

Sandhi तलोदरी = तल + उदरी (tala + udarī) — guṇa: a + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (with an upamāna comparison). 'She whose belly (udara) is like a flat surface (tala)', i.e. slender-waisted. A bahuvrīhi ending in a word for a body part may take the feminine -ī (Pāṇini 4.1.54).

Analysis तलम् इव उदरम् यस्याः सा तलोदरी
talam iva udaram yasyāḥ sā talodarī

Significance The slender waist is a classical mark of beauty; traditionally the name is also read as She in whose belly lie the lower worlds (talas), the cosmic form containing all regions.

Uncertain Two readings are current: 'whose waist is flat (slender)' and 'in whose belly are the talas, the lower worlds'.

848 उदारकीर्तिः udāra-kīrtiḥ

She who possesses exalted fame

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. 'She whose fame (kīrti) is exalted (udārā)'. The feminine adjective takes its masculine stem udāra in the compound (puṃvadbhāva, Pāṇini 6.3.34); kīrti is already feminine and keeps its nominative -iḥ.

Analysis उदारा कीर्तिः यस्याः सा उदारकीर्तिः
udārā kīrtiḥ yasyāḥ sā udārakīrtiḥ

Significance Her glory is sung everywhere and Her fame is generous: it is sung by those whom She has blessed.

849 उद्दामवैभवा uddāma-vaibhavā

She whose prowess is unlimited

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner prādi-bahuvrīhi). (1) ud-dāman 'from which the rope has gone', i.e. unbound, unrestrained (prādi-bahuvrīhi; ud stands for udgata). (2) 'She whose might (vaibhava) is unbounded' (bahuvrīhi); vaibhava takes the feminine -ā. The d of ud meets the d of dāma without change.

Analysis उद्गतम् दाम यस्मात् तत् उद्दाम; उद्दाम वैभवम् यस्याः सा उद्दामवैभवा
udgatam dāma yasmāt tat uddāma; uddāma vaibhavam yasyāḥ sā uddāmavaibhavā

Significance Her power is bound by nothing; the whole creation is only a fraction of Her glory.

850 वर्णरूपिणी varṇa-rūpiṇī

She whose form is the letters of the alphabet

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya of identification, made possessive by the suffix -in. (1) varṇa-rūpa 'the form that is the letters' (karmadhāraya of identification). (2) The possessive suffix -in (feminine -iṇī) makes it 'She whose form is the letters'.

Analysis वर्णाः एव रूपम् वर्णरूपम्; वर्णरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति वर्णरूपिणी
varṇāḥ eva rūpam varṇarūpam; varṇarūpam asyāḥ asti iti varṇarūpiṇī

Significance The fifty letters (mātṛkā), from a to kṣa, are traditionally Her body; all speech and all mantras are woven from them.

Śloka 159names 851–853

जन्ममृत्युजरातप्तजनविश्रान्तिदायिनी ।
सर्वोपनिषदुद्घुष्टा शान्त्यतीतकलात्मिका ॥ १५९ ॥

janmamṛtyujarātaptajanaviśrāntidāyinī |
sarvopaniṣadudghuṣṭā śāntyatītakalātmikā || 159 ||

The names, separated

851जन्म-मृत्यु-जरा-तप्त-जन-विश्रान्ति-दायिनीjanma-mṛtyu-jarā-tapta-jana-viśrānti-dāyinī

852सर्वोपनिषद्-उद्घुष्टाsarvopaniṣad-udghuṣṭā853शान्त्यतीत-कलात्मिकाśāntyatīta-kalātmikā

Translation

851She who gives peace and repose to those who are afflicted by birth, death and decrepitude;

852She who is proclaimed by all the Upaniṣads; 853She whose very nature is the kalā beyond peace (śāntyatītā).

Word by word

SanskritEnglish
851 जन्ममृत्युजरातप्तजनविश्रान्तिदायिनी janma-mṛtyu-jarā-tapta-jana-viśrānti-dāyinī
जन्मन्janmanbirthappears as janma- in the compound

जराjarāold age, decay

जनjanapeople, beings

दायिनीdāyinīgiver√dā 'to give' + -in, feminine -ī
852 सर्वोपनिषदुद्घुष्टा sarvopaniṣad-udghuṣṭā
सर्वsarvaall
उपनिषद्upaniṣadUpaniṣad, secret teachingupa + ni + √sad 'to sit'
उद्घुष्टाudghuṣṭāproclaimed aloud, declaredud + √ghuṣ 'to sound', past participle, feminine

शान्तिśāntipeace; the fourth kalā
अतीतatītagone beyondati + √i 'to go', past participle
कलाkalākalā, a phase or power of manifestation
आत्मिकाātmikāhaving the nature ofātman + -ka, feminine -ikā

Where the names meet

Name 851 fills the whole first half. Name 853 names the fifth of the five kalās (nivṛtti, pratiṣṭhā, vidyā, śānti, śāntyatītā); pratiṣṭhā (829) is the second.

The names

851 जन्ममृत्युजरातप्तजनविश्रान्तिदायिनी janma-mṛtyu-jarā-tapta-jana-viśrānti-dāyinī

She who gives peace and repose to those who are afflicted by birth, death and decrepitude

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over a dvandva, a tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa, a karmadhāraya and a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) janma-mṛtyu-jarā 'birth, death and old age' (dvandva). (2) …-tapta 'scorched by them' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (3) …tapta-jana 'people so scorched' (karmadhāraya). (4) …jana-viśrānti 'their rest' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (5) dāyinī 'giver' is the head, with the rest as its object (upapada-tatpuruṣa). janman appears as janma- in composition (loss of final n).

Analysis जन्म च मृत्युः च जरा च जन्ममृत्युजराः; जन्ममृत्युजराभिः तप्ताः जन्ममृत्युजरातप्ताः; जन्ममृत्युजरातप्ताः जनाः जन्ममृत्युजरातप्तजनाः; जन्ममृत्युजरातप्तजनानाम् विश्रान्तिः जन्ममृत्युजरातप्तजनविश्रान्तिः; ताम् ददाति इति जन्ममृत्युजरातप्तजनविश्रान्तिदायिनी
janma ca mṛtyuḥ ca jarā ca janmamṛtyujarāḥ; janmamṛtyujarābhiḥ taptāḥ janmamṛtyujarātaptāḥ; janmamṛtyujarātaptāḥ janāḥ janmamṛtyujarātaptajanāḥ; janmamṛtyujarātaptajanānām viśrāntiḥ janmamṛtyujarātaptajanaviśrāntiḥ; tām dadāti iti janmamṛtyujarātaptajanaviśrāntidāyinī

Significance Birth, death and old age are the threefold heat of saṃsāra; traditionally She is the shade in which the scorched traveler rests, the final repose of liberation.

852 सर्वोपनिषदुद्घुष्टा sarvopaniṣad-udghuṣṭā

She who is proclaimed by all the Upaniṣads

Sandhi सर्वोपनिषद् = सर्व + उपनिषद् (sarva + upaniṣad) — guṇa: a + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) sarva-upaniṣad 'all the Upaniṣads' (karmadhāraya; sarva is the qualifier). (2) The participle udghuṣṭā 'proclaimed aloud' is the head and the Upaniṣads are its agents in the instrumental. The stem-final d of upaniṣad simply stands before the vowel u.

Analysis सर्वाः उपनिषदः सर्वोपनिषदः; सर्वोपनिषद्भिः उद्घुष्टा सर्वोपनिषदुद्घुष्टा
sarvāḥ upaniṣadaḥ sarvopaniṣadaḥ; sarvopaniṣadbhiḥ udghuṣṭā sarvopaniṣadudghuṣṭā

Significance All the Upaniṣads declare the one Brahman, and in Śrīvidyā that Brahman is the Goddess; their teaching proclaims Her.

853 शान्त्यतीतकलात्मिका śāntyatīta-kalātmikā

She whose very nature is the kalā beyond peace (śāntyatītā)

Sandhi शान्त्यतीत = शान्ति + अतीत (śānti + atīta) — yaṇ: i becomes y before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci); कलात्मिका = कला + आत्मिका (kalā + ātmikā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya and a dvitīyā-tatpuruṣa). (1) śānti-atītā 'gone beyond śānti' (dvitīyā-tatpuruṣa with atīta, Pāṇini 2.1.24). (2) It qualifies kalā (karmadhāraya); the feminine first member takes its masculine stem (puṃvadbhāva, Pāṇini 6.3.42). (3) The whole is a bahuvrīhi with ātman 'self, nature', which in this position appears as -ātmaka, feminine -ātmikā: 'She whose very nature is the kalā beyond śānti'.

Analysis शान्तिम् अतीता शान्त्यतीता; शान्त्यतीता कला शान्त्यतीतकला; शान्त्यतीतकला आत्मा यस्याः सा शान्त्यतीतकलात्मिका
śāntim atītā śāntyatītā; śāntyatītā kalā śāntyatītakalā; śāntyatītakalā ātmā yasyāḥ sā śāntyatītakalātmikā

Significance In Śaiva and Śākta doctrine the five kalās (nivṛtti, pratiṣṭhā, vidyā, śānti, śāntyatītā) are the phases through which consciousness descends into the world; the fifth, beyond peace, is the subtlest, and it is Her nature.

Śloka 160names 854–861

गम्भीरा गगनान्तस्था गर्विता गानलोलुपा ।
कल्पनारहिता काष्ठा ऽकान्ता कान्तार्धविग्रहा ॥ १६० ॥

gambhīrā gaganāntasthā garvitā gānalolupā |
kalpanārahitā kāṣṭhā 'kāntā kāntārdhavigrahā || 160 ||

The names, separated ° form as a name on its own; in the recitation above it joins its neighbour

854गम्भीराgambhīrā855गगनान्त-स्थाgaganānta-sthā856गर्विताgarvitā857गान-लोलुपाgāna-lolupā

858कल्पना-रहिताkalpanā-rahitā859काष्ठाkāṣṭhā860अकान्ता°akāntā861कान्तार्ध-विग्रहाkāntārdha-vigrahā

Translation

854She who is unfathomable; 855She who dwells at the farthest bound of space, and within it; 856She who is proud; 857She who delights in music;

858She who is free from imaginary attributes; 859She who is the highest goal, beyond which there is nothing; 860She who ends all sins and sorrows; 861She who is half the body of Her husband.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish

गम्भीराgambhīrādeep, profound, unfathomable

856 गर्विता garvitā
गर्विताgarvitāproud, in whom pride has arisengarva 'pride' + the suffix -ita, feminine
857 गानलोलुपा gāna-lolupā
गानgānasong, music√gai 'to sing' + -ana
लोलुपाlolupāeager for, delighting infrom the intensive of √lup, feminine

रहिताrahitāfree from, devoid of√rah 'to abandon', past participle, feminine

काष्ठाkāṣṭhālimit, goal; direction; a unit of time

अर्धardhahalf
विग्रहाvigrahābody, formvigraha with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi

Where the names meet

काष्ठाऽकान्ता = काष्ठा + अकान्ता (kāṣṭhā + akāntā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); the avagraha (ऽ) marks the absorbed initial a of the next name

kāṣṭhā'kāntā is 859 kāṣṭhā + 860 akāntā; the avagraha shows that the second name begins with a.

The names

854 गम्भीरा gambhīrā

She who is unfathomable

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Like a deep lake whose bottom cannot be seen, She cannot be measured by the mind or by speech.

855 गगनान्तस्था gaganānta-sthā

She who dwells at the farthest bound of space, and within it

Sandhi गगनान्त = गगन + अन्त (gagana + anta) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) gagana-anta 'the end (or interior) of the sky' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) stha 'dwelling' (√sthā + -a after a locative, Pāṇini 3.2.4) is the head: 'one who dwells there'; feminine -ā. anta can mean both 'limit' and 'inside'.

Analysis गगनस्य अन्तः गगनान्तः; गगनान्ते तिष्ठति इति गगनान्तस्था
gaganasya antaḥ gaganāntaḥ; gaganānte tiṣṭhati iti gaganāntasthā

Significance Traditionally the space meant is also the small space (dahara ākāśa) within the heart, of which the Chāndogya Upaniṣad speaks; She dwells there as pure consciousness.

Uncertain anta can be read as 'limit' (beyond the sky) or 'interior' (within space); both readings are current.

856 गर्विता garvitā

She who is proud

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Traditionally Her pride is the full self-awareness of the sole sovereign of all, who has no equal; it is not the vanity of the limited ego.

857 गानलोलुपा gāna-lolupā

She who delights in music

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound saptamī-tatpuruṣa. lolupā 'eager, longing' is the head and music is the object of its longing, in the locative.

Analysis गाने लोलुपा गानलोलुपा
gāne lolupā gānalolupā

Significance Traditionally She is pleased by music offered in devotion; nāda, sound itself, is Her form.

858 कल्पनारहिता kalpanā-rahitā

She who is free from imaginary attributes

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa. The participle rahitā 'free from, devoid of' is the head and takes kalpanā in the instrumental.

Analysis कल्पनया रहिता कल्पनारहिता
kalpanayā rahitā kalpanārahitā

Significance Traditionally kalpanā is the superimposition by which the mind imagines name, form and distinction on the Real; She is free of it, being pure consciousness.

859 काष्ठा kāṣṭhā

She who is the highest goal, beyond which there is nothing

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance The Kaṭha Upaniṣad says of the Puruṣa, 'beyond Him there is nothing; He is the limit (kāṣṭhā), He the highest goal'. Kāṣṭhā is also a direction and a small unit of time, all of which are Her.

860 अकान्ता akāntā

She who ends all sins and sorrows

Sandhi अकान्ता = अक + अन्ता (aka + antā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (traditional analysis). aka 'pain, sin' is the object and antā 'one who brings to an end' (from anta 'end') is the head: 'She who ends sorrow and sin'.

Analysis अकम् अन्तयति इति अकान्ता
akam antayati iti akāntā

Significance Traditionally read as She who puts an end to the pain and sin of those who turn to Her.

Uncertain aka 'pain, sin' is a rare word and the analysis aka + antā is the traditional one; the śloka's sandhi kāṣṭhā'kāntā fixes the initial a, so a reading kāntā 'beloved' is not available here.

861 कान्तार्धविग्रहा kāntārdha-vigrahā

She who is half the body of Her husband

Sandhi कान्तार्ध = कान्त + अर्ध (kānta + ardha) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) kānta-ardha 'half of the beloved' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose body (vigraha) is half of the Beloved'; vigraha takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis कान्तस्य अर्धम् कान्तार्धम्; कान्तार्धम् विग्रहः यस्याः सा कान्तार्धविग्रहा
kāntasya ardham kāntārdham; kāntārdham vigrahaḥ yasyāḥ sā kāntārdhavigrahā

Significance The name evokes Ardhanārīśvara, the Lord who is half woman: Śiva and Śakti share one body, as consciousness and its power are one.

kanatkanakatāṭaṅkā līlāvigrahadhāriṇī || 161 ||

kārya in name 862 is 'effect', paired with kāraṇa 'cause'.

The names

862 कार्यकारणनिर्मुक्ता kārya-kāraṇa-nirmuktā

She who is free from the bond of cause and effect

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound pañcamī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner dvandva). (1) kārya-kāraṇa 'effect and cause' (dvandva). (2) The participle nirmuktā 'released, free' is the head and takes the pair in the ablative: 'free from effect and cause'.

Analysis कार्यम् च कारणम् च कार्यकारणे; कार्यकारणाभ्याम् निर्मुक्ता कार्यकारणनिर्मुक्ता
kāryam ca kāraṇam ca kāryakāraṇe; kāryakāraṇābhyām nirmuktā kāryakāraṇanirmuktā

Significance Traditionally She is the Absolute, which is neither an effect of anything nor, in its own nature, a cause; causality belongs to the world She projects, not to Her.

863 कामकेलितरङ्गिता kāma-keli-taraṅgitā

She who surges in waves of joy in Her love-play with Kāmeśvara

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) kāma-keli 'the love-play of Kāma (Kāmeśvara)' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) taraṅgitā 'made to surge in waves' is the head, with that play as its instrument.

Analysis कामस्य केलिः कामकेलिः; कामकेलिभिः तरङ्गिता कामकेलितरङ्गिता
kāmasya keliḥ kāmakeliḥ; kāmakelibhiḥ taraṅgitā kāmakelitaraṅgitā

Significance Traditionally the play of Kāmeśvara and Kāmeśvarī is the bliss of Śiva and Śakti in union, and the waves of that bliss are the worlds that arise from it.

864 कनत्कनकताटङ्का kanat-kanaka-tāṭaṅkā

She who wears glittering gold ear ornaments

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya and an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) kanaka-tāṭaṅka 'earrings of gold' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa of material). (2) The present participle kanat 'shining' qualifies them (karmadhāraya). (3) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose earrings are of shining gold'; tāṭaṅka takes the feminine -ā. The t of kanat is unchanged before k.

Analysis कनकस्य ताटङ्कौ कनकताटङ्कौ; कनन्तौ कनकताटङ्कौ कनत्कनकताटङ्कौ; कनत्कनकताटङ्कौ यस्याः सा कनत्कनकताटङ्का
kanakasya tāṭaṅkau kanakatāṭaṅkau; kanantau kanakatāṭaṅkau kanatkanakatāṭaṅkau; kanatkanakatāṭaṅkau yasyāḥ sā kanatkanakatāṭaṅkā

Significance Her earrings are a sign of Her auspicious wifehood: the Saundaryalaharī (verse 28) ascribes Śiva's survival of the poison He swallowed to the power of Her tāṭaṅkas.

865 लीलाविग्रहधारिणी līlā-vigraha-dhāriṇī

She who takes on forms in play

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (1) līlā-vigraha 'forms taken in play' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (2) dhāriṇī 'bearing, assuming' (causative of √dhṛ + -in) is the head, with the forms as its object.

Analysis लीलया विग्रहाः लीलाविग्रहाः; लीलाविग्रहान् धारयति इति लीलाविग्रहधारिणी
līlayā vigrahāḥ līlāvigrahāḥ; līlāvigrahān dhārayati iti līlāvigrahadhāriṇī

Significance She has no need to take a body; Her incarnations and manifestations are play (līlā), undertaken freely for the good of the worlds.

Śloka 162names 866–871

अन्तर्मुखसमाराध्या बहिर्मुखसुदुर्लभा ॥ १६२ ॥

ajā kṣayavinirmuktā mugdhā kṣipraprasādinī |
antarmukhasamārādhyā bahirmukhasudurlabhā || 162 ||

Where the names meet

Names 870 and 871 form a pair: to be worshipped by those turned within, very hard to reach for those turned outward.

The names

866 अजा ajā

She who has no birth

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa with the negative particle. The negative a- is joined to ja 'born' (from √jan, which occurs only at the end of a compound): 'not born'; feminine -ā.

Analysis न जायते इति अजा
na jāyate iti ajā

Significance The Śvetāśvatara Upaniṣad speaks of the one unborn (ajā), red, white and black, who brings forth many offspring like herself: Prakṛti with its three guṇas. Ajā also means 'she-goat', the image that verse plays on.

867 क्षयविनिर्मुक्ता kṣaya-vinirmuktā

She who is free from decay

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound pañcamī-tatpuruṣa. The participle vinirmuktā 'wholly released' is the head and kṣaya 'decay' stands to it in the ablative.

Analysis क्षयात् विनिर्मुक्ता क्षयविनिर्मुक्ता
kṣayāt vinirmuktā kṣayavinirmuktā

Significance Being unborn (866) She does not decay; time, which wastes all things, has no hold on Her.

868 मुग्धा mugdhā

She who is captivating in Her beauty

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance The participle also means 'innocent, artless': Her beauty is that of simplicity, and it bewilders even Śiva.

869 क्षिप्रप्रसादिनी kṣipra-prasādinī

She who is quickly pleased

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. prasādinī is an agent noun in -in of habit (Pāṇini 3.2.78 supy ajātau ṇinis tācchīlye) from pra + √sad 'to become clear, gracious'; the adverb kṣipra 'quickly' is the upapada: 'one who is quickly gracious'.

Analysis क्षिप्रम् प्रसीदति इति क्षिप्रप्रसादिनी
kṣipram prasīdati iti kṣipraprasādinī

Significance Traditionally She is easily and swiftly moved to grace, even by a little devotion.

870 अन्तर्मुखसमाराध्या antar-mukha-samārādhyā

She who is to be worshipped by those whose gaze is turned within

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner bahuvrīhi). (1) antar-mukha 'those whose face is turned within' (bahuvrīhi). (2) The gerundive samārādhyā 'to be worshipped fully' is the head, with those people as its agents in the instrumental. The r of antar is original.

Analysis अन्तः मुखम् येषाम् ते अन्तर्मुखाः; अन्तर्मुखैः समाराध्या अन्तर्मुखसमाराध्या
antaḥ mukham yeṣām te antarmukhāḥ; antarmukhaiḥ samārādhyā antarmukhasamārādhyā

Significance Traditionally inward worship (antar-yāga), with the mind withdrawn from the senses, is the highest form of Her worship.

871 बहिर्मुखसुदुर्लभा bahir-mukha-su-dur-labhā

She who is difficult to attain by those whose attention is directed outwards

Sandhi बहिर्मुख = बहिस् + मुख (bahis + mukha) — final s becomes ru (Pāṇini 8.2.66 sasajuṣo ruḥ), which stands as r before a voiced consonant

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner bahuvrīhi and a prādi compound). (1) bahir-mukha 'those whose face is turned outward' (bahuvrīhi). (2) dur-labha 'hard to obtain' (the suffix -a after dur, Pāṇini 3.3.126), intensified by su 'very' (prādi). (3) The whole: 'very hard to obtain for those turned outward' (instrumental of agent). The counterpart of name 870.

Analysis बहिः मुखम् येषाम् ते बहिर्मुखाः; दुःखेन लभ्यते इति दुर्लभा; सुतराम् दुर्लभा सुदुर्लभा; बहिर्मुखैः सुदुर्लभा बहिर्मुखसुदुर्लभा
bahiḥ mukham yeṣām te bahirmukhāḥ; duḥkhena labhyate iti durlabhā; sutarām durlabhā sudurlabhā; bahirmukhaiḥ sudurlabhā bahirmukhasudurlabhā

Significance Those whose minds run outward through the senses do not find Her, though She is nearest of all; the Kaṭha Upaniṣad says the Self-born pierced the senses outward, and only the one who turns the gaze within sees the Self.

Śloka 163names 872–879

निरामया निरालम्बा स्वात्मारामा सुधासृतिः ॥ १६३ ॥

trayī trivarganilayā tristhā tripuramālinī |

Where the names meet

Names 872–875 each begin with tri-: the three Vedas, the three aims of life, the triads She abides in, and Tripuramālinī of the Śrīcakra. Name 878 is sva + ātma + ārāmā (not svātmā + rāmā); 879 reads sudhāsṛtiḥ (variant sudhāsrutiḥ).

The names

872 त्रयी trayī

She who is the three Vedas

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Trayī is the old name for the Ṛg, Yajur and Sāma Vedas together; the name also covers every triad — the three guṇas, three states, three worlds — that She comprises.

873 त्रिवर्गनिलया tri-varga-nilayā

She who is the abode of the threefold aims of human life

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, used adjectivally (over an inner dvigu). (1) tri-varga 'the group of three', i.e. dharma, artha and kāma (a numeral compound, dvigu). (2) …-nilaya 'abode of that group' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). The compound is used of Her as an epithet and so takes the feminine -ā; traditionally this is explained by the possessive suffix ac of the arśa-ādi class ('having, being X').

Analysis त्रयाणाम् वर्गः त्रिवर्गः; त्रिवर्गस्य निलयः त्रिवर्गनिलयः; त्रिवर्गनिलयः अस्याः अस्ति इति त्रिवर्गनिलया
trayāṇām vargaḥ trivargaḥ; trivargasya nilayaḥ trivarganilayaḥ; trivarganilayaḥ asyāḥ asti iti trivarganilayā

Significance The trivarga is dharma, artha and kāma, the three aims of life in the world; She is their ground, and beyond them She grants the fourth, mokṣa.

874 त्रिस्था tri-sthā

She who abides in the three worlds, the three times and the three states

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. stha 'abiding' (√sthā + -a after a locative, Pāṇini 3.2.4) with tri 'three' in the locative plural as the upapada: 'abiding in the three'; feminine -ā.

Analysis त्रिषु तिष्ठति इति त्रिस्था
triṣu tiṣṭhati iti tristhā

Significance The name leaves 'three' open; traditionally it covers the three worlds, the three times (past, present, future), the three states (waking, dream, sleep) and the three deities of creation, preservation and dissolution.

875 त्रिपुरमालिनी tripura-mālinī

She who is Tripuramālinī, the presiding Goddess of the inner ten-triangle enclosure (antardaśāra) of the Śrīcakra

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound dvigu (samāhāra), followed by a possessive in -in. (1) tri-pura 'the three cities' (a numeral compound denoting the group, dvigu). (2) mālinī 'garlanded' (mālā + the possessive -in): 'She who has the three cities as Her garland'. As the proper name of a Śrīcakra deity the name is not usually analysed further.

Analysis त्रयाणाम् पुराणाम् समाहारः त्रिपुरम्; त्रिपुरम् माला अस्याः अस्ति इति त्रिपुरमालिनी
trayāṇām purāṇām samāhāraḥ tripuram; tripuram mālā asyāḥ asti iti tripuramālinī

Significance In the Śrīcakra each enclosure has a presiding Goddess whose name begins with Tripura-; Tripuramālinī rules the sixth, the inner ten triangles.

Uncertain As a proper name its internal analysis is not fixed; the vigraha given is grammatical, not a traditional gloss.

876 निरामया nir-āmayā

She who is free from diseases of all kinds

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound prādi-bahuvrīhi. The prefix nir stands for nirgata 'gone out': 'She from whom disease (āmaya) is gone'; āmaya takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis निर्गतः आमयः यस्याः सा निरामया
nirgataḥ āmayaḥ yasyāḥ sā nirāmayā

Significance Free of every affliction of body and mind, She also frees Her devotees from them.

877 निरालम्बा nir-ālambā

She who depends on none

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound prādi-bahuvrīhi. 'She from whom support (ālamba) is gone', i.e. who rests on nothing; ālamba takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis निर्गतः आलम्बः यस्याः सा निरालम्बा
nirgataḥ ālambaḥ yasyāḥ sā nirālambā

Significance She is the support of all and is Herself supported by nothing.

878 स्वात्मारामा svātmārāmā

She who rejoices in Her own self

Sandhi स्वात्म = स्व + आत्म (sva + ātma) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); आत्मारामा = आत्म + आरामा (ātma + ārāmā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya and a saptamī-tatpuruṣa). (1) sva-ātman 'one's own self' (karmadhāraya; ātman appears as ātma- with loss of the final n). (2) svātma-ārāma 'delight in one's own self' (saptamī-tatpuruṣa). (3) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose delight is in Her own self'.

Analysis स्वः आत्मा स्वात्मा; स्वात्मनि आरामः स्वात्मारामः; स्वात्मारामः यस्याः सा स्वात्मारामा
svaḥ ātmā svātmā; svātmani ārāmaḥ svātmārāmaḥ; svātmārāmaḥ yasyāḥ sā svātmārāmā

Significance She needs nothing outside Herself for joy; the Upaniṣads call such a one ātmārāma, 'delighting in the Self'.

879 सुधासृतिः sudhā-sṛtiḥ

She who is the stream of nectar

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. sṛti 'flowing, course' is the head and nectar stands to it in the genitive: 'the stream of nectar'. The feminine noun sṛti keeps its nominative -iḥ.

Analysis सुधायाः सृतिः सुधासृतिः
sudhāyāḥ sṛtiḥ sudhāsṛtiḥ

Significance In the kuṇḍalinī practice nectar flows from the moon in the thousand-petalled lotus once the power reaches it; She is that stream, which drenches the subtle body.

Variants Some editions read सुधास्रुतिः sudhāsrutiḥ (√sru 'to flow'), with the same sense.

Corrected सुधास्रुतिः / सृतिः → सुधासृतिः. "सुधास्रुतिः / सृतिः" → सुधासृतिः: the verse reads सुधासृतिः; the slash alternative was an editorial note left in the name (sudhāsrutiḥ is a recorded variant).

Śloka 164names 880–883

यज्ञप्रिया यज्ञकर्त्री यजमानस्वरूपिणी ॥ १६४ ॥

saṃsārapaṅkanirmagnasamuddharaṇapaṇḍitā |

880She who is skilled in raising those who are immersed in the mire of transmigratory life;

881She who is fond of sacrifices and other rites; 882She who is the doer of sacrificial rites; 883She who has the form of the yajamāna, the patron who offers the sacrifice.

Where the names meet

Name 880 fills the whole first half; names 881–883 turn to the Vedic sacrifice.

The names

880 संसारपङ्कनिर्मग्नसमुद्धरणपण्डिता saṃsāra-paṅka-nirmagna-samuddharaṇa-paṇḍitā

She who is skilled in raising those who are immersed in the mire of transmigratory life

Sandhi संसार = सम् + सार (sam + sāra) — the final m of the prefix sam becomes anusvāra before s (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ), inside the lexicalised saṃsāra; उद्धरण = उद् + हरण (ud + haraṇa) — after d, h becomes dh, the aspirate of the preceding stop (optional, Pāṇini 8.4.62 jhayo ho 'nyatarasyām)

Compound saptamī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, a saptamī-tatpuruṣa and a karmadhāraya of identification). (1) saṃsāra-paṅka 'the mire that is saṃsāra' (rūpaka karmadhāraya). (2) …-nirmagna 'sunk in that mire' (saptamī-tatpuruṣa). (3) …-samuddharaṇa 'the lifting out of those so sunk' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (4) paṇḍitā 'skilled' is the head, with the rescue as the field of skill in the locative.

Analysis संसारः एव पङ्कः संसारपङ्कः; संसारपङ्के निर्मग्नाः संसारपङ्कनिर्मग्नाः; संसारपङ्कनिर्मग्नानाम् समुद्धरणम् संसारपङ्कनिर्मग्नसमुद्धरणम्; संसारपङ्कनिर्मग्नसमुद्धरणे पण्डिता संसारपङ्कनिर्मग्नसमुद्धरणपण्डिता
saṃsāraḥ eva paṅkaḥ saṃsārapaṅkaḥ; saṃsārapaṅke nirmagnāḥ saṃsārapaṅkanirmagnāḥ; saṃsārapaṅkanirmagnānām samuddharaṇam saṃsārapaṅkanirmagnasamuddharaṇam; saṃsārapaṅkanirmagnasamuddharaṇe paṇḍitā saṃsārapaṅkanirmagnasamuddharaṇapaṇḍitā

Significance Traditionally saṃsāra is a mire in which the soul sinks deeper the more it struggles; She, standing outside it, is expert at lifting the soul out.

881 यज्ञप्रिया yajña-priyā

She who is fond of sacrifices and other rites

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. 'She to whom sacrifice (yajña) is dear (priya)'; priya takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis यज्ञः प्रियः यस्याः सा यज्ञप्रिया
yajñaḥ priyaḥ yasyāḥ sā yajñapriyā

Significance Every sacrifice, outer or inner, reaches Her; in Śrīvidyā the inner sacrifice of offering the mind into consciousness is the dearest of all.

882 यज्ञकर्त्री yajña-kartrī

She who is the doer of sacrificial rites

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. kartrī 'doer, performer' (agent noun from √kṛ) is the head and the sacrifice stands to it in the genitive (on compounds with -tṛ see name 811).

Analysis यज्ञस्य कर्त्री यज्ञकर्त्री
yajñasya kartrī yajñakartrī

Significance Traditionally She is the real agent in every rite; the priest and the patron act by Her power.

883 यजमानस्वरूपिणी yajamāna-svarūpiṇī

She who has the form of the yajamāna, the patron who offers the sacrifice

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya of identification, made possessive by the suffix -in. (1) yajamāna-svarūpa 'the nature that is the yajamāna' (karmadhāraya of identification). (2) The possessive suffix -in makes it 'She whose own form is the yajamāna'.

Analysis यजमानः एव स्वरूपम् यजमानस्वरूपम्; यजमानस्वरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति यजमानस्वरूपिणी
yajamānaḥ eva svarūpam yajamānasvarūpam; yajamānasvarūpam asyāḥ asti iti yajamānasvarūpiṇī

Significance The yajamāna is one of the eight forms (aṣṭamūrti) of Śiva, with the five elements, the sun and the moon; She bears that form as His power.

विप्रप्रिया विप्ररूपा विश्वभ्रमणकारिणी ॥ १६५ ॥

dharmādhārā dhanādhyakṣā dhanadhānyavivardhinī |
viprapriyā viprarūpā viśvabhramaṇakāriṇī || 165 ||

The names, separated

The names

884 धर्माधारा dharmādhārā

She who is the support of dharma

Sandhi धर्माधारा = धर्म + आधारा (dharma + ādhārā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, used adjectivally. (1) dharma-ādhāra 'the support of dharma' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, ādhāra the head). The compound is used of Her as an epithet and so takes the feminine -ā; traditionally this is explained by the possessive suffix ac of the arśa-ādi class ('having, being X').

Analysis धर्मस्य आधारः धर्माधारः; धर्माधारः अस्याः अस्ति इति धर्माधारा
dharmasya ādhāraḥ dharmādhāraḥ; dharmādhāraḥ asyāḥ asti iti dharmādhārā

Significance Dharma upholds the world, and She upholds dharma: She is the ground on which right order stands, as both its source and its protector.

885 धनाध्यक्षा dhanādhyakṣā

She who oversees wealth

Sandhi धनाध्यक्षा = धन + अध्यक्षा (dhana + adhyakṣā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); अध्यक्षा = अधि + अक्षा (adhi + akṣā) — yaṇ: i becomes y before a dissimilar vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci), inside the lexicalised adhyakṣa 'overseer'

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. adhyakṣā 'overseer, presiding lady' is the head and wealth stands to it in the genitive.

Analysis धनस्य अध्यक्षा धनाध्यक्षा
dhanasya adhyakṣā dhanādhyakṣā

Significance Dhanādhyakṣa is a title of Kubera, lord of riches; traditionally She is the power behind Kubera and the giver of wealth to those who worship Her.

886 धनधान्यविवर्धिनी dhana-dhānya-vivardhinī

She who increases wealth and harvests

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner dvandva). (1) dhana-dhānya 'wealth and grain' (dvandva). (2) vivardhinī 'one who increases' is the head, with the pair in the genitive.

Analysis धनम् च धान्यम् च धनधान्ये; धनधान्ययोः विवर्धिनी धनधान्यविवर्धिनी
dhanam ca dhānyam ca dhanadhānye; dhanadhānyayoḥ vivardhinī dhanadhānyavivardhinī

Significance Traditionally She gives prosperity in money and in food to the householder who worships Her.

887 विप्रप्रिया vipra-priyā

She who is fond of the learned

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. 'She to whom the learned (vipra) are dear (priya)'; priya takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis विप्राः प्रियाः यस्याः सा विप्रप्रिया
viprāḥ priyāḥ yasyāḥ sā viprapriyā

Significance Traditionally the vipra is one who knows the Veda and Brahman; such knowers are dear to Her.

888 विप्ररूपा vipra-rūpā

She who has the form of the vipra, the knower of the Self

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. 'She whose form (rūpa) is the vipra'; rūpa takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis विप्रः रूपम् यस्याः सा विप्ररूपा
vipraḥ rūpam yasyāḥ sā viprarūpā

Significance Traditionally She is present in the sage who knows Brahman, and Her worship is completed by honoring such a one.

889 विश्वभ्रमणकारिणी viśva-bhramaṇa-kāriṇī

She who makes the universe go around through Her power of illusion

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) viśva-bhramaṇa 'the revolving of the universe' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) kāriṇī 'one who causes' (√kṛ + -in) is the head, with that revolving as its object.

Analysis विश्वस्य भ्रमणम् विश्वभ्रमणम्; विश्वभ्रमणम् करोति इति विश्वभ्रमणकारिणी
viśvasya bhramaṇam viśvabhramaṇam; viśvabhramaṇam karoti iti viśvabhramaṇakāriṇī

Significance The Bhagavad Gītā (18.61) says the Lord dwells in the heart of all beings, 'causing them to revolve by māyā as if mounted on a machine'; She turns the worlds and the wandering of souls.

Śloka 166names 890–897

ayonir yoninilayā kūṭasthā kularūpiṇī || 166 ||

Where the names meet

अयोनिर्योनिनिलया = अयोनिः + योनिनिलया (ayoniḥ + yoninilayā) — visarga after a vowel other than a or ā becomes r before a voiced sound, here y

Divide ayonir yoninilayā (894, 895): the r is the visarga of ayoniḥ. The two names are a deliberate paradox: without source, yet the abode of all sources.

The names

890 विश्वग्रासा viśva-grāsā

She who devours the universe

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (alternatively upapada-tatpuruṣa). As a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose morsel (grāsa) is the universe'. As an upapada-tatpuruṣa: 'She who swallows the universe' (grāsa from √gras with vṛddhi). The sense is the same.

Analysis विश्वम् ग्रासः यस्याः सा विश्वग्रासा; अथवा विश्वम् ग्रसते इति विश्वग्रासा
viśvam grāsaḥ yasyāḥ sā viśvagrāsā; athavā viśvam grasate iti viśvagrāsā

Significance At dissolution the whole universe is a mouthful to Her; the Kaṭha Upaniṣad speaks of the one for whom priest and warrior are food and death itself the sauce.

891 विद्रुमाभा vidrumābhā

She who shines like coral (with Her red complexion)

Sandhi विद्रुमाभा = विद्रुम + आभा (vidruma + ābhā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (with an upamāna comparison). 'She whose radiance (ābhā) is like that of coral (vidruma)'. ābhā is already feminine.

Analysis विद्रुमस्य इव आभा यस्याः सा विद्रुमाभा
vidrumasya iva ābhā yasyāḥ sā vidrumābhā

Significance Her complexion is red like coral, the color of compassion and of the rising sun in which She is meditated.

892 वैष्णवी vaiṣṇavī

She who is the power of Viṣṇu

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance The Devī Māhātmya hails Her as vaiṣṇavī śaktir anantavīryā, 'the power of Viṣṇu, of boundless might, the seed of the universe'; Vaiṣṇavī is also one of the Mātṛkās.

893 विष्णुरूपिणी viṣṇu-rūpiṇī

She who has the form of Viṣṇu, the all-pervading

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya of identification, made possessive by the suffix -in. (1) viṣṇu-rūpa 'the form that is Viṣṇu'. (2) With the possessive -in: 'She whose form is Viṣṇu'.

Analysis विष्णुः एव रूपम् विष्णुरूपम्; विष्णुरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति विष्णुरूपिणी
viṣṇuḥ eva rūpam viṣṇurūpam; viṣṇurūpam asyāḥ asti iti viṣṇurūpiṇī

Significance The older rendering, 'a form that extends over the whole universe', gives the traditional etymology of Viṣṇu as the pervader; She is that pervading presence.

894 अयोनिः ayoniḥ

She who is without origin

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound nañ-bahuvrīhi. 'She for whom there is no source (yoni)': the negative a- and yoni form a bahuvrīhi. The feminine i-stem keeps its nominative -iḥ.

Analysis न विद्यते योनिः यस्याः सा अयोनिः
na vidyate yoniḥ yasyāḥ sā ayoniḥ

Significance She is the uncaused source; nothing precedes Her. The next name turns this around: She is the abode of every source.

895 योनिनिलया yoni-nilayā

She who is the seat of all origins

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa, used adjectivally. (1) yoni-nilaya 'the abode of the sources' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). The compound is used of Her as an epithet and so takes the feminine -ā; traditionally this is explained by the possessive suffix ac of the arśa-ādi class ('having, being X'). A locative reading, 'She who dwells in the yoni', is also current.

Analysis योनीनाम् निलयः योनिनिलयः; योनिनिलयः अस्याः अस्ति इति योनिनिलया
yonīnām nilayaḥ yoninilayaḥ; yoninilayaḥ asyāḥ asti iti yoninilayā

Significance In Śrīvidyā the yoni is also the central triangle (trikoṇa) of the Śrīcakra, the womb of the worlds, in which She dwells.

Uncertain Read as 'the abode of all sources' or as 'She who dwells in the yoni (the central triangle)'.

896 कूटस्था kūṭa-sthā

She who remains unchanged like the anvil

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. stha 'standing' (√sthā + -a after a locative, Pāṇini 3.2.4) with kūṭa as the upapada: 'standing like (on) an anvil', i.e. immovable; feminine -ā.

Analysis कूटे तिष्ठति इति कूटस्था
kūṭe tiṣṭhati iti kūṭasthā

Significance The Bhagavad Gītā calls the imperishable Self kūṭastha, unchanging like the anvil on which everything is shaped. In Śrīvidyā the name is also read as She who abides in the three kūṭas (sections) of the Pañcadaśī mantra.

897 कुलरूपिणी kula-rūpiṇī

She whose form is kula, the deity of the Kaula path

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya of identification, made possessive by the suffix -in. (1) kula-rūpa 'the form that is kula'. (2) With the possessive -in: 'She whose form is kula'.

Analysis कुलम् एव रूपम् कुलरूपम्; कुलरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति कुलरूपिणी
kulam eva rūpam kularūpam; kularūpam asyāḥ asti iti kularūpiṇī

Significance In the Kaula tradition kula is Śakti and the whole manifest world, and also the triad of knower, knowing and known; She is all of these and is worshipped as the deity of the Kaula path.

Śloka 167names 898–905

वीरगोष्ठीप्रिया वीरा नैष्कर्म्या नादरूपिणी ।
विज्ञानकलना कल्या विदग्धा बैन्दवासना ॥ १६७ ॥

vīragoṣṭhīpriyā vīrā naiṣkarmyā nādarūpiṇī |
vijñānakalanā kalyā vidagdhā baindavāsanā || 167 ||

Where the names meet

Name 905 baindavāsanā: the baindava place is the bindu at the center of the Śrīcakra.

The names

898 वीरगोष्ठीप्रिया vīra-goṣṭhī-priyā

She who is fond of the assembly of warriors

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) vīra-goṣṭhī 'the assembly of heroes' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She to whom that assembly is dear'.

Analysis वीराणाम् गोष्ठी वीरगोष्ठी; वीरगोष्ठी प्रिया यस्याः सा वीरगोष्ठीप्रिया
vīrāṇām goṣṭhī vīragoṣṭhī; vīragoṣṭhī priyā yasyāḥ sā vīragoṣṭhīpriyā

Significance Traditionally both the gathering of warriors and the circle of Tantric adepts (vīras) who meet for Her worship.

899 वीरा vīrā

She who is heroic

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Her heroism is shown in the destruction of Bhaṇḍa and the demons; She is also the mother and refuge of heroes (836).

900 नैष्कर्म्या naiṣkarmyā

She who is beyond all action (naiṣkarmya)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance The Bhagavad Gītā speaks of naiṣkarmya-siddhi, the perfection of freedom from action; though all action flows from Her power, She is untouched by it, being Her own fulfillment.

901 नादरूपिणी nāda-rūpiṇī

She who is in the form of the primal sound

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya of identification, made possessive by the suffix -in. (1) nāda-rūpa 'the form that is nāda'. (2) With the possessive -in: 'She whose form is nāda'.

Analysis नादः एव रूपम् नादरूपम्; नादरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति नादरूपिणी
nādaḥ eva rūpam nādarūpam; nādarūpam asyāḥ asti iti nādarūpiṇī

Significance In the Tantric account of creation nāda is the first stirring of sound from the bindu, from which the letters and mantras arise; in the mantra it is the subtle resonance after the anusvāra.

902 विज्ञानकलना vijñāna-kalanā

She who is the realization of supreme knowledge (vijñāna)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. kalanā 'grasping, realizing' is the head and vijñāna stands to it in the genitive: 'the realizing of (supreme) knowledge'.

Analysis विज्ञानस्य कलना विज्ञानकलना
vijñānasya kalanā vijñānakalanā

Significance Traditionally vijñāna is the direct experience of Brahman as distinct from book-learning; She is that realization itself.

903 कल्या kalyā

She who is able, sound and auspicious

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Kalya means 'ready, capable' and 'whole, healthy', and also 'auspicious, of the dawn'; She is ever ready to grant what is sought.

Uncertain kalya has several senses (able, healthy, auspicious; also 'dawn'), and traditional glosses differ; the rendering combines the main ones.

904 विदग्धा vidagdhā

She who is expert in everything

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance She is the accomplished one, skilled in every art and in the conduct of the world.

905 बैन्दवासना baindavāsanā

She whose seat is the bindu, the central point of the Śrīcakra

Sandhi बैन्दवासना = बैन्दव + आसना (baindava + āsanā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi. 'She whose seat (āsana) is the baindava', the place of the bindu; āsana takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis बैन्दवम् आसनम् यस्याः सा बैन्दवासना
baindavam āsanam yasyāḥ sā baindavāsanā

Significance The baindava-sthāna is the innermost point of the Śrīcakra, the sarvānandamaya cakra, where She sits with Kāmeśvara.

Śloka 168names 906–911

तत्त्वाधिका तत्त्वमयी तत्त्वमर्थस्वरूपिणी ।
सामगानप्रिया सौम्या सदाशिवकुटुम्बिनी ॥ १६८ ॥

tattvādhikā tattvamayī tattvamarthasvarūpiṇī |
sāmagānapriyā saumyā sadāśivakuṭumbinī || 168 ||

The names, separated

906तत्त्वाधिकाtattvādhikā907तत्त्व-मयीtattva-mayī908तत्त्वम्-अर्थ-स्वरूपिणीtattvam-artha-svarūpiṇī

906She who transcends all cosmic categories; 907She who is Reality itself, consisting of the tattvas; 908She whose very nature is the meaning of tat and tvam, That and thou;

Where the names meet

Name 907 tattvamayī is a single name here (contrast 425–427 tat / tvam / ayī). Name 908 divides tat-tvam-artha ('the meaning of tat and tvam'), not tattva + martha.

The names

906 तत्त्वाधिका tattvādhikā

She who transcends all cosmic categories

Sandhi तत्त्वाधिका = तत्त्व + अधिका (tattva + adhikā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound pañcamī-tatpuruṣa. adhikā 'exceeding, beyond' is the head and the tattvas stand to it in the ablative of comparison: 'beyond the tattvas'.

Analysis तत्त्वेभ्यः अधिका तत्त्वाधिका
tattvebhyaḥ adhikā tattvādhikā

Significance In Śaiva and Śākta doctrine the world is built of thirty-six tattvas, from earth up to Śiva; She is beyond them all, even the highest.

907 तत्त्वमयी tattva-mayī

She who is Reality itself, consisting of the tattvas

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Having gone beyond the tattvas (906), She is also made of them: every principle of the world is Her. Traditionally tattva is also read as Śiva, the highest principle, so that the name makes Her one with Him. Here tattvamayī is a single name; earlier in the hymn (425–427) Bhāskararāya divides the same letters into tat, tvam and ayī.

908 तत्त्वमर्थस्वरूपिणी tattvam-artha-svarūpiṇī

She whose very nature is the meaning of tat and tvam, That and thou

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa with quoted words as first member, inside a karmadhāraya made possessive by -in. (1) tat-tvam-artha 'the meaning of the words tat and tvam': the two pronouns are quoted from the mahāvākya, so they keep their own form (not the stems tad, yuṣmad), and artha 'meaning' is the head (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) That meaning is identified with svarūpa 'own nature'. (3) The possessive -in: 'She whose own nature is the meaning of tat and tvam'. The m of tvam simply stands before the a of artha; no sound changes.

Analysis तत् त्वम् इति पदयोः अर्थः तत्त्वमर्थः; तत्त्वमर्थः एव स्वरूपम् तत्त्वमर्थस्वरूपम्; तत्त्वमर्थस्वरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति तत्त्वमर्थस्वरूपिणी
tat tvam iti padayoḥ arthaḥ tattvamarthaḥ; tattvamarthaḥ eva svarūpam tattvamarthasvarūpam; tattvamarthasvarūpam asyāḥ asti iti tattvamarthasvarūpiṇī

Significance The Chāndogya Upaniṣad's tat tvam asi, 'That thou art', identifies the meaning of tat (Brahman) with the meaning of tvam (the inner Self); She is what both words finally denote, and their identity.

909 सामगानप्रिया sāma-gāna-priyā

She who is fond of the chanting of the Sāma Veda

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) sāma-gāna 'the singing of Sāman chants' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; sāman appears as sāma- with loss of the final n). (2) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She to whom the singing of the Sāmans is dear'.

Analysis साम्नाम् गानम् सामगानम्; सामगानम् प्रियम् यस्याः सा सामगानप्रिया
sāmnām gānam sāmagānam; sāmagānam priyam yasyāḥ sā sāmagānapriyā

Significance The Sāman chants are the Veda set to melody; the Bhagavad Gītā says 'among the Vedas I am the Sāma Veda'. She delights in this music of the Veda.

910 सौम्या saumyā

She who is gentle and benign, cool like the moon

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Saumya is the opposite of fierce: She is mild and pleasing like the moon (soma), though She can also be fierce (827).

911 सदाशिवकुटुम्बिनी sadāśiva-kuṭumbinī

She who is the consort of Sadāśiva

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) sadā-śiva 'ever auspicious', the name of the deity Sadāśiva (the indeclinable sadā qualifies śiva). (2) kuṭumbinī 'mistress of the household, wife' is the head, with Sadāśiva in the genitive.

Analysis सदा शिवः सदाशिवः; सदाशिवस्य कुटुम्बिनी सदाशिवकुटुम्बिनी
sadā śivaḥ sadāśivaḥ; sadāśivasya kuṭumbinī sadāśivakuṭumbinī

Significance Among the five cosmic functions Sadāśiva presides over grace (anugraha); as His household mistress She is the one who carries out that grace.

Śloka 169names 912–917

सव्यापसव्यमार्गस्था सर्वापद्विनिवारिणी ।
स्वस्था स्वभावमधुरा धीरा धीरसमर्चिता ॥ १६९ ॥

savyāpasavyamārgasthā sarvāpadvinivāriṇī |
svasthā svabhāvamadhurā dhīrā dhīrasamarcitā || 169 ||

The names, separated

914स्व-स्थाsva-sthā915स्वभाव-मधुराsvabhāva-madhurā916धीराdhīrā917धीर-समर्चिताdhīra-samarcitā

आपद्āpadcalamity, misfortuneā + √pad 'to fall'

धीरdhīrawise, steadfast
