The names

912 सव्यापसव्यमार्गस्था savyāpasavya-mārga-sthā

She who occupies (or can be reached by) both the left and right paths of worship

Sandhi सव्यापसव्य = सव्य + अपसव्य (savya + apasavya) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya and a dvandva). (1) savya-apasavya 'left and right' (dvandva). (2) They qualify mārga 'path' (karmadhāraya): 'the left and right paths'. (3) stha 'abiding' (√sthā + -a after a locative, Pāṇini 3.2.4) is the head: 'She who abides in both paths'.

Analysis सव्यम् च अपसव्यम् च सव्यापसव्ये; सव्यापसव्ये मार्गौ सव्यापसव्यमार्गौ; सव्यापसव्यमार्गयोः तिष्ठति इति सव्यापसव्यमार्गस्था
savyam ca apasavyam ca savyāpasavye; savyāpasavye mārgau savyāpasavyamārgau; savyāpasavyamārgayoḥ tiṣṭhati iti savyāpasavyamārgasthā

Significance Traditionally the left (vāma) and right (dakṣiṇa) modes of Tantric worship both lead to Her, and She abides in each.

Uncertain savya is mostly 'left' but is occasionally used for 'right' in ritual contexts; the name covers both paths either way.

913 सर्वापद्विनिवारिणी sarvāpad-vinivāriṇī

She who removes all dangers

Sandhi सर्वापद् = सर्व + आपद् (sarva + āpad) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) sarva-āpad 'all calamities' (karmadhāraya). (2) vinivāriṇī 'one who wards off' is the head, with the calamities in the genitive. The final d of āpad is unchanged before v.

Analysis सर्वाः आपदः सर्वापदः; सर्वापदाम् विनिवारिणी सर्वापद्विनिवारिणी
sarvāḥ āpadaḥ sarvāpadaḥ; sarvāpadām vinivāriṇī sarvāpadvinivāriṇī

Significance Traditionally remembering Her name is itself protection in every calamity.

914 स्वस्था sva-sthā

She who abides in Herself; She who is free from all afflictions

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. stha 'abiding' (√sthā + -a after a locative, Pāṇini 3.2.4) with sva 'oneself' as the upapada: 'abiding in Herself'; feminine -ā. As an ordinary adjective svastha also means 'healthy, at ease'.

Analysis स्वे तिष्ठति इति स्वस्था
sve tiṣṭhati iti svasthā

Significance Resting in Her own nature, She is never disturbed; the everyday sense 'healthy, at ease' gives the second half of the meaning.

915 स्वभावमधुरा svabhāva-madhurā

She who is sweet in Her inherent nature

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) sva-bhāva 'one's own nature' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) madhurā 'sweet' is the head, with svabhāva in the instrumental of respect: 'sweet by nature'.

Analysis स्वस्य भावः स्वभावः; स्वभावेन मधुरा स्वभावमधुरा
svasya bhāvaḥ svabhāvaḥ; svabhāvena madhurā svabhāvamadhurā

Significance Her sweetness is not put on for the devotee: it is Her very nature, the bliss of consciousness.

916 धीरा dhīrā

She who is wise; She who gives wisdom

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Dhīra also means 'steadfast, composed'. The second half of the meaning rests on a traditional etymology, dhiyaṃ rāti, 'She gives wisdom'.

Uncertain The sense 'giver of wisdom' depends on the traditional analysis dhī + √rā; the ordinary meanings are 'wise' and 'steadfast'.

917 धीरसमर्चिता dhīra-samarcitā

She who is worshipped by the wise

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa. The participle samarcitā 'well worshipped' is the head and the wise are its agents in the instrumental.

Analysis धीरैः समर्चिता धीरसमर्चिता
dhīraiḥ samarcitā dhīrasamarcitā

Significance The Kaṭha Upaniṣad calls the dhīra the one who turns the gaze within and sees the Self; such steadfast sages worship Her.

Śloka 170names 918–922

चैतन्यार्घ्यसमाराध्या चैतन्यकुसुमप्रिया ।

Where the names meet

Names 918–919 describe inner worship, with consciousness as the arghya and as the flower.

The names

918 चैतन्यार्घ्यसमाराध्या caitanyārghya-samārādhyā

She who is to be worshipped with consciousness as the arghya offering

Sandhi चैतन्यार्घ्य = चैतन्य + अर्घ्य (caitanya + arghya) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya of identification). (1) caitanya-arghya 'the arghya that is consciousness' (rūpaka karmadhāraya). (2) The gerundive samārādhyā 'to be worshipped' is the head, with that offering as its instrument.

Analysis चैतन्यम् एव अर्घ्यम् चैतन्यार्घ्यम्; चैतन्यार्घ्येण समाराध्या चैतन्यार्घ्यसमाराध्या
caitanyam eva arghyam caitanyārghyam; caitanyārghyeṇa samārādhyā caitanyārghyasamārādhyā

Significance In inner worship the arghya is not water but consciousness itself, offered back to its source.

919 चैतन्यकुसुमप्रिया caitanya-kusuma-priyā

She who is fond of the flower that is consciousness

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya of identification). (1) caitanya-kusuma 'the flower that is consciousness' (rūpaka). (2) The whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She to whom that flower is dear'.

Analysis चैतन्यम् एव कुसुमम् चैतन्यकुसुमम्; चैतन्यकुसुमम् प्रियम् यस्याः सा चैतन्यकुसुमप्रिया
caitanyam eva kusumam caitanyakusumam; caitanyakusumam priyam yasyāḥ sā caitanyakusumapriyā

Significance Traditionally inner virtues such as non-violence, self-control and compassion are the 'flowers' of mental worship; the flower of pure consciousness is the dearest to Her.

920 सदोदिता sadoditā

She who is ever risen, ever shining

Sandhi सदोदिता = सदा + उदिता (sadā + uditā) — guṇa: ā + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound tatpuruṣa of an indeclinable with a participle (sup-supā samāsa). The indeclinable sadā 'always' qualifies the participle uditā 'risen', the head: 'ever risen'.

Analysis सदा उदिता सदोदिता
sadā uditā sadoditā

Significance Unlike the sun She never sets: consciousness is always present, in waking, dream and sleep alike.

921 सदातुष्टा sadā-tuṣṭā

She who is ever pleased

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tatpuruṣa of an indeclinable with a participle (sup-supā samāsa). The indeclinable sadā 'always' qualifies the participle tuṣṭā 'pleased', the head.

Analysis सदा तुष्टा सदातुष्टा
sadā tuṣṭā sadātuṣṭā

Significance Being full in Herself She is always content, and so is easily pleased by Her devotees.

922 तरुणादित्यपाटला taruṇāditya-pāṭalā

She who is rosy like the morning sun

Sandhi तरुणादित्य = तरुण + आदित्य (taruṇa + āditya) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound upamāna-karmadhāraya (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) taruṇa-āditya 'the young (rising) sun' (karmadhāraya). (2) The standard of comparison is compounded with the word for the shared quality, pāṭalā 'rosy' (upamāna-karmadhāraya, Pāṇini 2.1.55): 'rosy as the rising sun'.

Analysis तरुणः आदित्यः तरुणादित्यः; तरुणादित्यः इव पाटला तरुणादित्यपाटला
taruṇaḥ ādityaḥ taruṇādityaḥ; taruṇādityaḥ iva pāṭalā taruṇādityapāṭalā

Significance Her meditation-form is rosy-red like the rising sun, the color of compassion and of the dawn of knowledge.

Śloka 171names 923–926

दक्षिणादक्षिणाराध्या दरस्मेरमुखाम्बुजा ।
कौलिनीकेवला ऽनर्घ्यकैवल्यपददायिनी ॥ १७१ ॥

dakṣiṇādakṣiṇārādhyā darasmeramukhāmbujā |
kaulinīkevalā 'narghyakaivalyapadadāyinī || 171 ||

The names, separated ° form as a name on its own; in the recitation above it joins its neighbour

923दक्षिणादक्षिणाराध्याdakṣiṇādakṣiṇārādhyā924दर-स्मेर-मुखाम्बुजाdara-smera-mukhāmbujā

925कौलिनी-केवलाkaulinī-kevalā926अनर्घ्य-कैवल्य-पद-दायिनी°anarghya-kaivalya-pada-dāyinī

Translation

923She who is worshipped by those of the right-hand path and those of the left; 924She whose lotus-face wears a gentle smile;

925She who, for the followers of the Kaula way, is the Absolute, pure consciousness; 926She who bestows the priceless state of final liberation (kaivalya).

Word by word

दक्षिणdakṣiṇaright; of the right-hand (dakṣiṇa) way of worship; also skillful, learned
अदक्षिणadakṣiṇanot of the right: of the left-hand (vāma) way; also unskilled, simplenañ (a- 'not') + dakṣiṇa
आराध्याārādhyāto be worshipped, to be propitiatedā + √rādh 'to propitiate', gerundive (-ya), feminine
924 दरस्मेरमुखाम्बुजा dara-smera-mukhāmbujā
दरdaraslightly, a littlean indeclinable used adverbially
स्मेरsmerasmiling√smi 'to smile' + the suffix -ra

Where the names meet

कौलिनीकेवलाऽनर्घ्य = कौलिनीकेवला + अनर्घ्य… (kaulinīkevalā + anarghya…) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101); the avagraha marks the absorbed a of anarghya

Name 925 kaulinīkevalā is a single name (some printings write it as two words, which breaks the count); name 926 begins with an-arghya 'priceless', whose initial a is hidden in the long ā (avagraha). In 923 the long ā after the first dakṣiṇa hides the a- of a-dakṣiṇa: right-hand and left-hand worshipers.

The names

923 दक्षिणादक्षिणाराध्या dakṣiṇādakṣiṇārādhyā

She who is worshipped by those of the right-hand path and those of the left

Sandhi दक्षिणादक्षिण = दक्षिण + अदक्षिण (dakṣiṇa + adakṣiṇa) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); दक्षिणादक्षिणाराध्या = दक्षिणादक्षिण + आराध्या (dakṣiṇādakṣiṇa + ārādhyā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner itaretara-dvandva, whose second member is a nañ-tatpuruṣa). (1) a-dakṣiṇa 'not of the right' (nañ-tatpuruṣa). (2) dakṣiṇa and adakṣiṇa are joined as a dvandva, 'those of the right and those not of the right'. (3) The gerundive ārādhyā 'to be worshipped' is the head and takes the dvandva in the instrumental of the agent: 'to be worshipped by both'. The long ā after the first dakṣiṇa hides the negative a- of the second member, which is why the name is easily misread as dakṣiṇā + dakṣiṇa.

Analysis न दक्षिणाः अदक्षिणाः; दक्षिणाः च अदक्षिणाः च दक्षिणादक्षिणाः; दक्षिणादक्षिणैः आराध्या दक्षिणादक्षिणाराध्या
na dakṣiṇāḥ adakṣiṇāḥ; dakṣiṇāḥ ca adakṣiṇāḥ ca dakṣiṇādakṣiṇāḥ; dakṣiṇādakṣiṇaiḥ ārādhyā dakṣiṇādakṣiṇārādhyā

Significance Traditionally dakṣiṇa and adakṣiṇa are the right-hand (Vedic, samaya) and left-hand (vāma) modes of worship, and She receives both; the pair is also read as the learned and the unlearned, both of whom reach Her.

Uncertain Besides right-hand / left-hand ways, the pair is also read as the skillful and the unskillful (learned and unlearned); both readings rest on the same dvandva.

924 दरस्मेरमुखाम्बुजा dara-smera-mukhāmbujā

She whose lotus-face wears a gentle smile

Sandhi मुखाम्बुजा = मुख + अम्बुजा (mukha + ambujā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya and an upamita-karmadhāraya). (1) dara-smera 'slightly smiling': the indeclinable dara 'a little' qualifies smera 'smiling'. (2) mukha-ambuja 'the face that is like a lotus': an upamita compound, the face compared to the lotus with the comparison word iva understood. (3) (1) qualifies (2), and the whole is a bahuvrīhi describing Her: 'She whose lotus-face is gently smiling'; ambuja takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis दरम् स्मेरम् दरस्मेरम्; मुखम् अम्बुजम् इव मुखाम्बुजम्; दरस्मेरम् मुखाम्बुजम् यस्याः सा दरस्मेरमुखाम्बुजा
daram smeram darasmeram; mukham ambujam iva mukhāmbujam; darasmeram mukhāmbujam yasyāḥ sā darasmeramukhāmbujā

Significance The slight smile is traditionally read as the outward sign of Her grace: it reassures the devotee and, in the Purāṇic account, is enough to destroy the demons.

925 कौलिनीकेवला kaulinī-kevalā

She who, for the followers of the Kaula way, is the Absolute, pure consciousness

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya (one name made of two co-referential words); a tatpuruṣa reading is also given. Read as one name, kaulinī 'She of the Kula (the Kaula tradition)' and kevalā 'the Absolute, unmixed, alone' stand in apposition: 'the Kaula Goddess who is the Absolute'. A genitive reading, 'the Absolute for the Kaulas', underlies the traditional gloss that the followers of the Kaula way worship Her as pure consciousness. The words meet without sound change.

Analysis कौलिनी च असौ केवला च कौलिनीकेवला; अथवा कौलिनीनाम् केवला कौलिनीकेवला
kaulinī ca asau kevalā ca kaulinīkevalā; athavā kaulinīnām kevalā kaulinīkevalā

Significance Kula is the whole of manifest reality held together in Śakti; for the Kaula practitioner the Goddess of the Kula is herself kevala, the one consciousness without a second.

Uncertain The internal relation (apposition, or a genitive 'the Absolute for the Kaulas') is not settled; both are traditional and the meaning combines them.

Variants Some printings write कौलिनी केवला as two words; the 1,000-name count requires one name here (see the correction log).

Corrected कौलिनी केवला → कौलिनीकेवला. "कौलिनी केवला" → कौलिनीकेवला: counted as one name (925) in the 1,000; written as two words it reads as two names and breaks the count.

926 अनर्घ्यकैवल्यपददायिनी anarghya-kaivalya-pada-dāyinī

She who bestows the priceless state of final liberation (kaivalya)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya, itself over a nañ-tatpuruṣa and a karmadhāraya). (1) an-arghya 'beyond price' (nañ-tatpuruṣa; na becomes an- before a vowel). (2) kaivalya-pada 'the state that is kaivalya' (karmadhāraya of identity). (3) (1) qualifies (2). (4) dāyinī 'giver' is the head and takes (3) as its object: 'She who gives the priceless state of liberation'.

Analysis न अर्घ्यम् अनर्घ्यम्; कैवल्यम् एव पदम् कैवल्यपदम्; अनर्घ्यम् कैवल्यपदम् अनर्घ्यकैवल्यपदम्; अनर्घ्यकैवल्यपदम् ददाति इति अनर्घ्यकैवल्यपददायिनी
na arghyam anarghyam; kaivalyam eva padam kaivalyapadam; anarghyam kaivalyapadam anarghyakaivalyapadam; anarghyakaivalyapadam dadāti iti anarghyakaivalyapadadāyinī

Significance Kaivalya, the isolation of the Self from all that is not the Self, is the highest goal; nothing can be paid for it, so it is Her gift alone.

Śloka 172names 927–933

स्तोत्रप्रिया स्तुतिमती श्रुतिसंस्तुतवैभवा ।
मनस्विनी मानवती महेशी मङ्गलाकृतिः ॥ १७२ ॥

stotrapriyā stutimatī śrutisaṃstutavaibhavā |

आकृतिःākṛtiḥform, shape, appearanceā + √kṛ, feminine noun in -ti

Where the names meet

Name 928 stutimatī is stuti + the possessive suffix -matī ('possessed of praise'), not mati 'mind'; 930 manasvinī and 931 mānavatī are likewise possessive derivatives.

The names

927 स्तोत्रप्रिया stotra-priyā

She who is fond of hymns in Her praise

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. stotra 'hymns' and priya 'dear' are co-referential and the compound describes Her: 'She to whom hymns are dear'. priya takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis स्तोत्राणि प्रियाणि यस्याः सा स्तोत्रप्रिया
stotrāṇi priyāṇi yasyāḥ sā stotrapriyā

Significance Traditionally the name assures the reciter that the hymn itself, this Sahasranāma included, is an offering She loves.

928 स्तुतिमती stutimatī

She who is rich in praise, the true object of all praises

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Every hymn, wherever it is addressed, finally reaches Her; so all praise is Hers.

929 श्रुतिसंस्तुतवैभवा śruti-saṃstuta-vaibhavā

She whose glory is extolled by the Śrutis (the Vedas)

Sandhi संस्तुत = सम् + स्तुत (sam + stuta) — the final m of the prefix sam becomes anusvāra before a consonant (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa). (1) śruti-saṃstuta 'well praised by the Śrutis' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa; the participle is the head, the Vedas its agents). (2) This qualifies vaibhava 'glory', and the whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose glory is extolled by the Śrutis'; vaibhava takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis श्रुतिभिः संस्तुतम् श्रुतिसंस्तुतम्; श्रुतिसंस्तुतम् वैभवम् यस्याः सा श्रुतिसंस्तुतवैभवा
śrutibhiḥ saṃstutam śrutisaṃstutam; śrutisaṃstutam vaibhavam yasyāḥ sā śrutisaṃstutavaibhavā

Significance The Upaniṣads praise Her greatness as the supreme Brahman even where they do not name Her.

930 मनस्विनी manasvinī

She who is high-minded, of strong and independent mind

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Traditionally: Her mind depends on nothing outside Herself; She is self-determined and steadfast.

931 मानवती mānavatī

She who is high-minded, full of dignity and honor

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Traditionally māna is also the proud indignation of love, so the name recalls Her loving pride toward Kāmeśvara; She is also the one honored by all.

932 महेशी maheśī

She who is the consort of Maheśa (Śiva), the great sovereign Goddess

Sandhi महेशी = महा + ईशी (mahā + īśī) — guṇa: ā + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound karmadhāraya (maheśa), with the feminine of association; or karmadhāraya on the feminine directly. Two analyses give the same form. (1) mahā-īśa 'the great Lord', Maheśa (Śiva), whose wife is called Maheśī by the feminine of association. (2) mahatī īśī 'the great sovereign Lady' directly, mahatī becoming mahā- in a karmadhāraya (Pāṇini 6.3.42, 6.3.46).

Analysis महान् ईशः महेशः; महेशस्य पत्नी महेशी; अथवा महती ईशी महेशी
mahān īśaḥ maheśaḥ; maheśasya patnī maheśī; athavā mahatī īśī maheśī

Significance As Maheśī She is Śiva's own power, inseparable from Maheśvara; in Her own right She is the supreme ruler.

933 मङ्गलाकृतिः maṅgalākṛtiḥ

She who is of auspicious form

Sandhi मङ्गलाकृतिः = मङ्गल + आकृतिः (maṅgala + ākṛtiḥ) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi. maṅgala 'auspicious' qualifies ākṛti 'form' and the whole describes Her: 'She whose form is auspicious'. ākṛti is already feminine and keeps its ending; the adjective stands in its basic stem maṅgala.

Analysis मङ्गला आकृतिः यस्याः सा मङ्गलाकृतिः
maṅgalā ākṛtiḥ yasyāḥ sā maṅgalākṛtiḥ

Significance To see or meditate on Her form is itself auspicious; whatever is auspicious in the world is a reflection of Her.

Śloka 173names 934–941

विश्वमाता जगद्धात्री विशालाक्षी विरागिणी ।
प्रगल्भा परमोदारा परामोदा मनोमयी ॥ १७३ ॥

viśvamātā jagaddhātrī viśālākṣī virāgiṇī |
pragalbhā paramodārā parāmodā manomayī || 173 ||

The names, separated

934विश्व-माताviśva-mātā935जगद्-धात्रीjagad-dhātrī936विशालाक्षीviśālākṣī937विरागिणीvirāgiṇī

934She who is the Mother of the universe; 935She who is the nurse and sustainer of the world; 936She who has large eyes; 937She who is dispassionate;

938She who is skillful and confident; 939She who is supremely generous; 940She who is supremely joyful; 941She who is in the form of the mind.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish

विशालviśālawide, large, broad
अक्षीakṣīeyeakṣi, as akṣa at the end of a bahuvrīhi, with the feminine -ī

उदाराudārāgenerous, noble, munificentfeminine of udāra

परparasupreme, highest

मनस्manasmind
मयीmayīconsisting of, made ofthe suffix -maya (mayaṭ), feminine -ī

Where the names meet

Names 939 and 940 play on the same syllables and must be divided differently: param-odārā (parama + udārā) and parām-odā (para + āmodā).

The names

934 विश्वमाता viśva-mātā

She who is the Mother of the universe

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. mātā 'mother' is the head; viśva 'the universe' stands to it in the genitive: 'the Mother of the universe'.

Analysis विश्वस्य माता विश्वमाता
viśvasya mātā viśvamātā

Significance She brings forth the universe and cares for it as a mother cares for her child.

935 जगद्धात्री jagad-dhātrī

She who is the nurse and sustainer of the world

Sandhi जगद्धात्री = जगत् + धात्री (jagat + dhātrī) — jaśtva: a final t becomes d before a voiced sound (Pāṇini 8.2.39 jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. dhātrī 'nurse, supporter' is the head; jagat 'the world' stands to it in the genitive: 'the nurse and sustainer of the world'.

Analysis जगतः धात्री जगद्धात्री
jagataḥ dhātrī jagaddhātrī

Significance After name 934 has called Her Mother, this name calls Her the nurse who feeds and protects what She has brought forth.

936 विशालाक्षी viśālākṣī

She who has large eyes

Sandhi विशालाक्षी = विशाल + अक्षी (viśāla + akṣī) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi. viśāla 'wide, large' qualifies akṣi 'eye', and the whole describes Her: 'She whose eyes are large'. At the end of a bahuvrīhi akṣi becomes akṣa (Pāṇini 5.4.113 bahuvrīhau sakthyakṣṇoḥ svāṅgāt ṣac), and the feminine is akṣī.

Analysis विशाले अक्षिणी यस्याः सा विशालाक्षी
viśāle akṣiṇī yasyāḥ sā viśālākṣī

Significance Wide eyes are a classical mark of beauty and also of the all-seeing; Viśālākṣī is the name under which the Goddess is worshipped at Kāśī.

937 विरागिणी virāgiṇī

She who is dispassionate

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Though She enjoys the play of the worlds, nothing in them binds Her; She is the model of the vairāgya the seeker must cultivate.

938 प्रगल्भा pragalbhā

She who is skillful and confident

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Traditionally: She is accomplished in every art and acts with complete assurance in creating and governing the worlds.

939 परमोदारा paramodārā

She who is supremely generous

Sandhi परमोदारा = परम + उदारा (parama + udārā) — guṇa: a + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound karmadhāraya. parama 'supreme' qualifies udārā 'generous, noble' (both refer to Her; parama takes its masculine stem by puṃvadbhāva): 'supremely generous'.

Analysis परमा उदारा परमोदारा
paramā udārā paramodārā

Significance Her generosity has no limit: She gives even Herself to the devotee.

940 परामोदा parāmodā

She who is supremely joyful

Sandhi परामोदा = पर + आमोदा (para + āmodā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi. para 'supreme' qualifies āmoda 'joy, delight', and the whole describes Her: 'She whose joy is supreme'; āmoda takes the feminine -ā. The string could also be cut parā + modā (moda 'joy'), with the same sense.

Analysis परः आमोदः यस्याः सा परामोदा
paraḥ āmodaḥ yasyāḥ sā parāmodā

Significance Her joy is the bliss (ānanda) that is Her very nature, not a joy dependent on anything; āmoda also means fragrance, the 'scent' of that bliss. With 939 it plays on the same syllables: param-odārā, parām-odā.

Uncertain The usual division is para + āmodā; parā + modā is also possible, with the same sense.

941 मनोमयी manomayī

She who is in the form of the mind

Sandhi मनोमयी = मनस् + मयी (manas + mayī) — the final s of manas becomes u after a and before a voiced consonant, and a + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.114 haśi ca, with 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound not a compound

Significance In the Taittirīya Upaniṣad the manomaya kośa is the sheath made of mind; She pervades it and is also the power by which the mind thinks.

Śloka 174names 942–947

व्योमकेशी विमानस्था वज्रिणी वामकेश्वरी ।
पञ्चयज्ञप्रिया पञ्चप्रेतमञ्चाधिशायिनी ॥ १७४ ॥

vyomakeśī vimānasthā vajriṇī vāmakeśvarī |
pañcayajñapriyā pañcapretamañcādhiśāyinī || 174 ||

The names, separated

942व्योम-केशीvyoma-keśī943विमान-स्थाvimāna-sthā944वज्रिणीvajriṇī945वामकेश्वरीvāmakeśvarī

946पञ्च-यज्ञ-प्रियाpañca-yajña-priyā947पञ्च-प्रेत-मञ्चाधिशायिनीpañca-preta-mañcādhiśāyinī

Translation

942She who has the sky as Her hair; 943She who is seated in Her celestial chariot; 944She who bears the thunderbolt (vajra); 945She who is Vāmakeśvarī, the sovereign Goddess of the Vāmakeśvara Tantra;

946She who is fond of the five forms of sacrifice; 947She who reclines on a couch made of the five corpses.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish
942 व्योमकेशी vyoma-keśī
व्योमन्vyomansky, spaceappears as vyoma- (final n dropped, Pāṇini 8.2.7 nalopaḥ prātipadikāntasya)
केशीkeśīhairkeśa, with the feminine -ī of the bahuvrīhi
943 विमानस्था vimāna-sthā
विमानvimānacelestial car or palace; also the towered shrine of a temple
स्थाsthāstanding, abiding, seated√sthā 'to stand', feminine
944 वज्रिणी vajriṇī
वज्रvajrathunderbolt; diamond
इणीiṇīpossessingthe possessive suffix -in, feminine -ī; n becomes ṇ after the r
945 वामकेश्वरी vāmakeśvarī
वामकvāmakavāmaka: 'the left' or 'the beautiful'; the vāma wayfrom vāma 'left; lovely'
ईश्वरीīśvarīsovereign ladyfeminine of īśvara, from √īś 'to rule'
946 पञ्चयज्ञप्रिया pañca-yajña-priyā
पञ्चन्pañcanfiveappears as pañca- (final n dropped, Pāṇini 8.2.7)
यज्ञyajñasacrifice, worship

पञ्चन्pañcanfiveappears as pañca-
प्रेतpretacorpse; lit. 'departed'pra + √i 'to go', past participle
मञ्चmañcacouch, bedstead
अधिशायिनीadhiśāyinīreclining uponadhi + √śī 'to lie' + -in, feminine

Where the names meet

Name 945 recalls the Vāmakeśvara Tantra, a root text of Śrīvidyā. From 946 a run of names begins on pañca 'five' (946–950).

The names

942 व्योमकेशी vyoma-keśī

She who has the sky as Her hair

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. vyoman 'sky' is identified with keśa 'hair' (the sky is Her hair), and the whole describes Her; keśa, a body part, takes the feminine -ī (Pāṇini 4.1.54). vyoman drops its final n in the compound.

Analysis व्योम केशाः यस्याः सा व्योमकेशी
vyoma keśāḥ yasyāḥ sā vyomakeśī

Significance Her cosmic form fills space, its tresses being the sky. Vyomakeśa is also a name of Śiva, so the name is read as well as 'consort of Vyomakeśa'.

943 विमानस्था vimāna-sthā

She who is seated in Her celestial chariot

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. -sthā 'standing, abiding' (√sthā with the suffix -a, Pāṇini 3.2.4 supi sthaḥ) is the head and takes vimāna in the locative: 'abiding in the celestial car'.

Analysis विमाने तिष्ठति इति विमानस्था
vimāne tiṣṭhati iti vimānasthā

Significance Traditionally She is enthroned in Her aerial car, travelling with the gods; vimāna is also the temple tower over the sanctum, where She dwells as the presiding deity.

944 वज्रिणी vajriṇī

She who bears the thunderbolt (vajra)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Traditionally read also as Indrāṇī, the power of Indra the vajra-bearer (vajrin), and as 'She who is adorned with diamonds'.

945 वामकेश्वरी vāmakeśvarī

She who is Vāmakeśvarī, the sovereign Goddess of the Vāmakeśvara Tantra

Sandhi वामकेश्वरी = वामक + ईश्वरी (vāmaka + īśvarī) — guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; as a name, the feminine of Vāmakeśvara. Vāmakeśvara, 'the Lord of the vāmaka', is a name of Śiva; Vāmakeśvarī is his consort, or directly 'the Sovereign of the vāmaka'. īśvarī is the head. The name also recalls the Vāmakeśvara Tantra, a root text of Śrīvidyā.

Analysis वामकस्य ईश्वरी वामकेश्वरी; अथवा वामकेश्वरस्य पत्नी वामकेश्वरी
vāmakasya īśvarī vāmakeśvarī; athavā vāmakeśvarasya patnī vāmakeśvarī

Significance The Vāmakeśvara Tantra (with the Nityāṣoḍaśikārṇava) is a foundational text of Śrīvidyā, and She is its presiding deity, the consort of Vāmakeśvara (Śiva).

Uncertain The sense of vāmaka (the left-hand way, or 'beauty') is variously explained.

946 पञ्चयज्ञप्रिया pañca-yajña-priyā

She who is fond of the five forms of sacrifice

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner dvigu). (1) pañca-yajña 'the five sacrifices': a numeral compound (dvigu), formed because another member follows (Pāṇini 2.1.51). (2) priyā 'dear' is co-referential, and the whole describes Her: 'She to whom the five sacrifices are dear'.

Analysis पञ्च यज्ञाः पञ्चयज्ञाः; पञ्चयज्ञाः प्रियाः यस्याः सा पञ्चयज्ञप्रिया
pañca yajñāḥ pañcayajñāḥ; pañcayajñāḥ priyāḥ yasyāḥ sā pañcayajñapriyā

Significance The five are traditionally the śrauta rites agnihotra, darśapūrṇamāsa, cāturmāsya, paśu (animal) and soma sacrifices; they are also read as the five daily mahāyajñas (to the gods, sages, ancestors, beings and humans).

Uncertain Which five sacrifices are meant (śrauta rites, the five mahāyajñas, or Āgamic five) differs between explanations.

947 पञ्चप्रेतमञ्चाधिशायिनी pañca-preta-mañcādhiśāyinī

She who reclines on a couch made of the five corpses

Sandhi मञ्चाधिशायिनी = मञ्च + अधिशायिनी (mañca + adhiśāyinī) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and dvigu). (1) pañca-preta 'the five corpses' (dvigu). (2) pañcapreta-mañca 'the couch of (made of) the five corpses' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) adhiśāyinī 'reclining upon' is the head and takes the couch as its object: with adhi, √śī governs the accusative of the place (Pāṇini 1.4.46 adhiśīṅsthāsāṃ karma).

Analysis पञ्च प्रेताः पञ्चप्रेताः; पञ्चप्रेतानाम् मञ्चः पञ्चप्रेतमञ्चः; पञ्चप्रेतमञ्चम् अधिशेते इति पञ्चप्रेतमञ्चाधिशायिनी
pañca pretāḥ pañcapretāḥ; pañcapretānām mañcaḥ pañcapretamañcaḥ; pañcapretamañcam adhiśete iti pañcapretamañcādhiśāyinī

Significance The five are Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra, Īśvara and Sadāśiva: four form the legs and Sadāśiva the plank. Without Her power even these gods are lifeless (preta); compare name 249, pañcapretāsanāsīnā.

Śloka 175names 948–954

पञ्चमी पञ्चभूतेशी पञ्चसङ्ख्योपचारिणी ।
शाश्वती शाश्वतैश्वर्या शर्मदा शम्भुमोहिनी ॥ १७५ ॥

pañcamī pañcabhūteśī pañcasaṅkhyopacāriṇī |

951 शाश्वती śāśvatī
शाश्वतीśāśvatīeternal, everlastingśāśvata (from śaśvat 'perpetually'), feminine
952 शाश्वतैश्वर्या śāśvataiśvaryā
शाश्वतśāśvataeternal
ऐश्वर्याaiśvaryāsovereignty, lordshipaiśvarya (abstract noun from īśvara), with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi
953 शर्मदा śarma-dā
शर्मन्śarmanhappiness, shelter, well-beingappears as śarma- (final n dropped)
दाdāgiving, giver√dā 'to give', feminine

शम्भुśambhuŚambhu, Śiva ('source of happiness')
मोहिनीmohinīenchantress, she who bewilderscausative of √muh 'to be bewildered' + -in, feminine

Where the names meet

The run on 'five' ends with 950 (the five offerings of worship); 951–952 then pair śāśvatī 'eternal' with śāśvataiśvaryā 'whose sovereignty is eternal'.

The names

948 पञ्चमी pañcamī

She who is the fifth, beyond Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Rudra and Īśvara

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Traditionally She is the power of Sadāśiva, the fifth beyond the four gods of creation, maintenance, dissolution and veiling; Pañcamī is also one of the twelve names of Vārāhī, Her commander.

949 पञ्चभूतेशी pañca-bhūteśī

She who is the sovereign of the five elements

Sandhi भूतेशी = भूत + ईशी (bhūta + īśī) — guṇa: a + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner dvigu). (1) pañca-bhūta 'the five elements' (dvigu). (2) īśī 'sovereign lady' is the head and the elements stand to it in the genitive: 'the sovereign of the five elements'.

Analysis पञ्च भूतानि पञ्चभूतानि; पञ्चभूतानाम् ईशी पञ्चभूतेशी
pañca bhūtāni pañcabhūtāni; pañcabhūtānām īśī pañcabhūteśī

Significance Earth, water, fire, air and space arise from Her and obey Her; inwardly the five elements are mastered in the five lower cakras, which She rules.

950 पञ्चसङ्ख्योपचारिणी pañca-saṅkhyopacāriṇī

She who is worshipped with the fivefold offerings (fragrance, flowers, incense, lamp and food)

Sandhi सङ्ख्या = सम् + ख्या (sam + khyā) — the final m of the prefix sam becomes anusvāra and then the nasal of the following k-row, ṅ (Pāṇini 8.3.23, 8.4.59); सङ्ख्योपचारिणी = सङ्ख्या + उपचारिणी (saṅkhyā + upacāriṇī) — guṇa: ā + u → o (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner bahuvrīhi), completed by the possessive suffix -in. (1) pañca-saṅkhya 'whose number is five' (bahuvrīhi), qualifying (2) upacāra 'service, offering of worship'. (3) The possessive -in (feminine -iṇī) makes the whole describe Her: 'She who has (receives) the services numbering five'.

Analysis पञ्च सङ्ख्या येषाम् ते पञ्चसङ्ख्याः; पञ्चसङ्ख्याः उपचाराः पञ्चसङ्ख्योपचाराः; पञ्चसङ्ख्योपचाराः अस्याः सन्ति इति पञ्चसङ्ख्योपचारिणी
pañca saṅkhyā yeṣām te pañcasaṅkhyāḥ; pañcasaṅkhyāḥ upacārāḥ pañcasaṅkhyopacārāḥ; pañcasaṅkhyopacārāḥ asyāḥ santi iti pañcasaṅkhyopacāriṇī

Significance The pañcopacāra pūjā, the simplest complete worship, offers gandha, puṣpa, dhūpa, dīpa and naivedya; traditionally these also stand for the five elements offered back to Her.

951 शाश्वती śāśvatī

She who is eternal

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Everything with a beginning has an end; She alone has neither.

952 शाश्वतैश्वर्या śāśvataiśvaryā

She who holds eternal sovereignty

Sandhi शाश्वतैश्वर्या = शाश्वत + ऐश्वर्या (śāśvata + aiśvaryā) — vṛddhi: a + ai → ai (Pāṇini 6.1.88 vṛddhir eci)

Compound bahuvrīhi. śāśvata 'eternal' qualifies aiśvarya 'sovereignty', and the whole describes Her: 'She whose sovereignty is eternal'; aiśvarya takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis शाश्वतम् ऐश्वर्यम् यस्याः सा शाश्वतैश्वर्या
śāśvatam aiśvaryam yasyāḥ sā śāśvataiśvaryā

Significance Her rule over the worlds is not acquired and cannot be lost; the powers (aiśvarya) sought by others are Hers by nature.

953 शर्मदा śarma-dā

She who is the giver of happiness

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. -dā 'giving' (√dā with the suffix -a, Pāṇini 3.2.3 āto 'nupasarge kaḥ) is the head and takes śarman as its object: 'giver of happiness'.

Analysis शर्म ददाति इति शर्मदा
śarma dadāti iti śarmadā

Significance Śarman is both happiness and refuge: She gives the lasting well-being that comes from shelter in Her.

954 शम्भुमोहिनी śambhu-mohinī

She who enchants Śambhu (Śiva)

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. mohinī 'enchantress' (causative of √muh with -in) is the head and takes Śambhu as its object: 'She who enchants Śambhu'.

Analysis शम्भुम् मोहयति इति शम्भुमोहिनी
śambhum mohayati iti śambhumohinī

Significance Śiva, absorbed in himself, is drawn by Her beauty into union with Her, and from that union creation proceeds.

Śloka 176names 955–963

धरा धरसुता धन्या धर्मिणी धर्मवर्धिनी ।
लोकातीता गुणातीता सर्वातीता शमात्मिका ॥ १७६ ॥

dharā dharasutā dhanyā dharmiṇī dharmavardhinī |
lokātītā guṇātītā sarvātītā śamātmikā || 176 ||

955धराdharā956धर-सुताdhara-sutā957धन्याdhanyā958धर्मिणीdharmiṇī959धर्म-वर्धिनीdharma-vardhinī

955She who is the Earth, the bearer of all; 956She who is the daughter of the mountain (Himavat); 957She who possesses great wealth; She who is supremely blessed; 958She who is righteous; 959She who promotes righteousness;

Word by word

अतीताatītāgone beyond, transcendingati + √i 'to go', past participle, feminine

Where the names meet

धराधरसुता is divided by Bhāskararāya into two names, dharā 'the Earth' (955) and dharasutā 'daughter of the mountain' (956); there is no sound change at the cut. Read as one word (dharādhara-sutā) it would be a single name and the count of 1,000 would fall short. Names 960–962 form a rising series on atītā 'gone beyond'.

The names

955 धरा dharā

She who is the Earth, the bearer of all

Sandhi धराधरसुता = धरा + धरसुता (dharā + dharasutā) — no sound change: a name boundary, not a sandhi. Bhāskararāya divides the verse's धराधरसुता into two names, dharā (955) and dharasutā (956); read as one word, dharādhara-sutā, it would be a single name 'daughter of the mountain', and the count of 1,000 needs two

Compound not a compound

Significance As the earth bears all beings patiently, She bears the whole universe.

956 धरसुता dhara-sutā

She who is the daughter of the mountain (Himavat)

Sandhi धराधरसुता = धरा + धरसुता (dharā + dharasutā) — no sound change: a name boundary, not a sandhi. Bhāskararāya divides the verse's धराधरसुता into two names, dharā (955) and dharasutā (956); read as one word, dharādhara-sutā, it would be a single name 'daughter of the mountain', and the count of 1,000 needs two

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. sutā 'daughter' is the head; dhara 'the mountain' stands to it in the genitive: 'the daughter of the mountain', Pārvatī, daughter of Himavat.

Analysis धरस्य सुता धरसुता
dharasya sutā dharasutā

Significance As Pārvatī She is born as the daughter of Himavat, king of mountains, to become Śiva's bride.

957 धन्या dhanyā

She who possesses great wealth; She who is supremely blessed

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Every kind of fortune is Hers, and those who worship Her become blessed (dhanya) too.

958 धर्मिणी dharmiṇī

She who is righteous

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance Dharma is Her own nature; She is also the one who upholds it in the world.

959 धर्मवर्धिनी dharma-vardhinī

She who promotes righteousness

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. vardhinī 'increaser' (causative of √vṛdh with -in) is the head and takes dharma as its object: 'She who makes dharma grow'.

Analysis धर्मम् वर्धयति इति धर्मवर्धिनी
dharmam vardhayati iti dharmavardhinī

Significance She strengthens dharma in the world and in the life of the devotee.

960 लोकातीता lokātītā

She who transcends the worlds

Sandhi लोकातीता = लोक + अतीता (loka + atītā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound dvitīyā-tatpuruṣa. The participle atītā 'gone beyond' is the head and takes the first member as its object in the accusative; atīta is one of the words that form such compounds (Pāṇini 2.1.24 dvitīyā śrita-atīta-patita-gata-atyasta-prāpta-āpannaiḥ).

Analysis लोकान् अतीता लोकातीता
lokān atītā lokātītā

Significance She pervades all the worlds and yet is not contained by them.

961 गुणातीता guṇātītā

She who transcends the guṇas

Sandhi गुणातीता = गुण + अतीता (guṇa + atītā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound dvitīyā-tatpuruṣa. The participle atītā 'gone beyond' is the head and takes the first member as its object in the accusative; atīta is one of the words that form such compounds (Pāṇini 2.1.24 dvitīyā śrita-atīta-patita-gata-atyasta-prāpta-āpannaiḥ).

Analysis गुणान् अतीता गुणातीता
guṇān atītā guṇātītā

Significance As nirguṇa Brahman She stands beyond sattva, rajas and tamas, though She wields them in creation (name 984).

962 सर्वातीता sarvātītā

She who transcends everything

Sandhi सर्वातीता = सर्व + अतीता (sarva + atītā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound dvitīyā-tatpuruṣa. The participle atītā 'gone beyond' is the head and takes the first member as its object in the accusative; atīta is one of the words that form such compounds (Pāṇini 2.1.24 dvitīyā śrita-atīta-patita-gata-atyasta-prāpta-āpannaiḥ).

Analysis सर्वम् अतीता सर्वातीता
sarvam atītā sarvātītā

Significance The three names 960–962 widen step by step: beyond the worlds, beyond the qualities that make them, beyond all that is.

963 शमात्मिका śamātmikā

She whose very nature is tranquility

Sandhi शमात्मिका = शम + आत्मिका (śama + ātmikā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound bahuvrīhi. śama 'tranquility' is identified with ātman 'self, nature', and the whole describes Her: 'She whose very nature is tranquility'. The bahuvrīhi takes the suffix -ka, whose a becomes i before the feminine -ā (ātmikā).

Analysis शमः आत्मा यस्याः सा शमात्मिका
śamaḥ ātmā yasyāḥ sā śamātmikā

Significance Śama, the stilling of the mind, heads the Vedāntic disciplines; She is that peace itself, and grants it.

Śloka 177names 964–970

964बन्धूक-कुसुम-प्रख्याbandhūka-kusuma-prakhyā965बालाbālā966लीला-विनोदिनीlīlā-vinodinī

Where the names meet

The second half is a run of su- names (967–970), on auspicious married life; it leads into 971.

The names

964 बन्धूककुसुमप्रख्या bandhūka-kusuma-prakhyā

She whose radiance resembles the red bandhūka flower

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi of resemblance (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) bandhūka-kusuma 'the bandhūka flower' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (2) prakhyā 'appearance, brightness' at the end of a compound means 'resembling': the whole is a bahuvrīhi, 'She whose radiance is like the bandhūka flower's'.

Analysis बन्धूकस्य कुसुमम् बन्धूककुसुमम्; बन्धूककुसुमस्य प्रख्या इव प्रख्या यस्याः सा बन्धूककुसुमप्रख्या
bandhūkasya kusumam bandhūkakusumam; bandhūkakusumasya prakhyā iva prakhyā yasyāḥ sā bandhūkakusumaprakhyā

Significance Her complexion is the red of dawn and of the bandhūka blossom, the color of compassion (anurāga) in Her dhyāna.

965 बाला bālā

She who is Bālā, the ever-young girl

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound not a compound

Significance In Śrīvidyā, Bālā Tripurasundarī is the Goddess as a girl, worshipped with the three-syllable Bālā mantra, often the first initiation; traditionally She never leaves the innocence and playfulness of a child.

966 लीलाविनोदिनी līlā-vinodinī

She who delights in Her sport

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa. vinodinī 'one who amuses herself, takes delight' is the head; līlā 'play' stands to it in the instrumental: 'She who delights Herself with play'.

Analysis लीलया विनोदिनी लीलाविनोदिनी
līlayā vinodinī līlāvinodinī

Significance Creation, preservation and dissolution are Her play (līlā), undertaken not from need but from the fullness of delight; the name echoes Lalitā, 'She who plays'.

967 सुमङ्गली su-maṅgalī

She who is eternally auspicious; She who is never widowed

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound prādi-bahuvrīhi. su 'good, well' qualifies maṅgala 'auspiciousness', and the whole describes Her: 'She whose auspiciousness is perfect'. The feminine is formed with -ī.

Analysis शोभनम् मङ्गलम् यस्याः सा सुमङ्गली
śobhanam maṅgalam yasyāḥ sā sumaṅgalī

Significance A sumaṅgalī is a married woman whose husband lives; since Her Lord Kāmeśvara is eternal, Her auspiciousness never ends.

968 सुखकरी sukha-karī

She who gives happiness

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. -karī 'making' (√kṛ with the suffix -a, feminine -ī) is the head and takes sukha as its object: 'She who makes happiness'.

Analysis सुखम् करोति इति सुखकरी
sukham karoti iti sukhakarī

Significance She causes happiness in this world and the bliss of liberation beyond it.

969 सुवेषाढ्या su-veṣāḍhyā

She who is rich in beautiful attire and adornment

Sandhi सुवेषाढ्या = सुवेष + आढ्या (suveṣa + āḍhyā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner prādi-tatpuruṣa). (1) su-veṣa 'beautiful attire' (prādi-tatpuruṣa). (2) āḍhyā 'rich, abounding' is the head and takes (1) in the instrumental: 'rich in beautiful attire'.

Analysis शोभनः वेषः सुवेषः; सुवेषेण आढ्या सुवेषाढ्या
śobhanaḥ veṣaḥ suveṣaḥ; suveṣeṇa āḍhyā suveṣāḍhyā

Significance Her splendid dress and ornaments are the sign of the auspicious married state (names 967 and 970).

970 सुवासिनी suvāsinī

She who is ever auspiciously married

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (lexicalised). su 'well' + vāsinī 'dwelling' (√vas with -in): 'she who dwells well', the established word for a married woman whose husband is living.

Analysis सुष्ठु वसति इति सुवासिनी
suṣṭhu vasati iti suvāsinī

Significance A suvāsinī lives in the auspicious married state; Her union with Kāmeśvara is eternal. The next name speaks of the worship of suvāsinīs.

Where the names meet

प्रीताऽऽशोभना = प्रीता + आशोभना (prītā + āśobhanā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101); the doubled avagraha marks the absorbed long ā

Name 972 is āśobhanā (Bhāskararāya's division of prītā + āśobhanā); the sound would be the same with prītā + śobhanā, so the doubled avagraha records the reading. Name 976 Tripurāmbikā is the presiding deity of the eighth enclosure of the Śrīcakra.

The names

971 सुवासिन्यर्चनप्रीता suvāsiny-arcana-prītā

She who is pleased by the worship of suvāsinīs (auspicious married women)

Sandhi सुवासिन्यर्चन = सुवासिनी + अर्चन (suvāsinī + arcana) — yaṇ: ī → y before an unlike vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) suvāsinī-arcana 'the worship of suvāsinīs' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; the genitive is read as objective: the suvāsinīs are honored). (2) prītā 'pleased' is the head and takes (1) in the instrumental of cause: 'pleased by the worship of suvāsinīs'. The genitive could also be subjective, 'worship performed by suvāsinīs'.

Analysis सुवासिनीनाम् अर्चनम् सुवासिन्यर्चनम्; सुवासिन्यर्चनेन प्रीता सुवासिन्यर्चनप्रीता
suvāsinīnām arcanam suvāsinyarcanam; suvāsinyarcanena prītā suvāsinyarcanaprītā

Significance In Śrīvidyā practice suvāsinī-pūjā honors married women as living forms of the Goddess; She takes that honor as given to Herself.

Uncertain suvāsinī-arcana may mean worship OF suvāsinīs (the Śrīvidyā rite of suvāsinī-pūjā) or worship BY them; the first is followed.

972 आशोभना āśobhanā

She who is radiant through and through

Sandhi प्रीताऽऽशोभना = प्रीता + आशोभना (prītā + āśobhanā) — savarṇa-dīrgha across the name boundary: ā + ā → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101); the doubled avagraha marks the absorbed long ā. Bhāskararāya reads the name as ā-śobhanā; the sounds would be the same if one cut prītā + śobhanā, so the division is his reading, not a sound change inside the name

Compound prādi-tatpuruṣa. The preposition ā 'all around, fully' qualifies śobhanā 'radiant, beautiful': 'radiant on every side, entirely beautiful'. Read without ā (śobhanā), the sense would be simply 'the beautiful one'.

Analysis आ समन्तात् शोभना आशोभना
ā samantāt śobhanā āśobhanā

Significance Her beauty has no flaw or side that is not radiant; it shines inwardly as purity of mind (name 973) as well as outwardly.

Uncertain The verse string can be cut prītā + āśobhanā or prītā + śobhanā with identical sound; Bhāskararāya's division (āśobhanā) is followed.

973 शुद्धमानसा śuddha-mānasā

She whose mind is pure; She who purifies the minds of Her worshipers

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. śuddha 'pure' qualifies mānasa 'mind', and the whole describes Her: 'She whose mind is pure'; mānasa takes the feminine -ā. Read as an instrumental bahuvrīhi (śuddhaṃ mānasaṃ yayā), it means 'She by whom the mind is purified'.

Analysis शुद्धम् मानसम् यस्याः सा शुद्धमानसा
śuddham mānasam yasyāḥ sā śuddhamānasā

Significance Her own awareness is untouched by any impurity, and meditation on Her purifies the devotee's mind.

974 बिन्दुतर्पणसन्तुष्टा bindu-tarpaṇa-santuṣṭā

She who is pleased by the libations offered at the bindu of the Śrīcakra

Sandhi सन्तुष्टा = सम् + तुष्टा (sam + tuṣṭā) — the final m of the prefix sam becomes anusvāra and then the nasal of the following t-row, n (Pāṇini 8.3.23, 8.4.59)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner saptamī-tatpuruṣa). (1) bindu-tarpaṇa 'the libation offered at the bindu' (saptamī-tatpuruṣa). (2) santuṣṭā 'fully satisfied' is the head and takes (1) in the instrumental: 'satisfied by the libations at the bindu'.

Analysis बिन्दौ तर्पणम् बिन्दुतर्पणम्; बिन्दुतर्पणेन सन्तुष्टा बिन्दुतर्पणसन्तुष्टा
bindau tarpaṇam bindutarpaṇam; bindutarpaṇena santuṣṭā bindutarpaṇasantuṣṭā

Significance In Śrīcakra worship tarpaṇa is offered to Her at the central bindu; inwardly the bindu is in the sahasrāra, where the nectar of union satisfies Her.

975 पूर्वजा pūrva-jā

She who is the first-born, preceding all

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. -jā 'born' (√jan with the suffix -a) is the head; pūrva 'before, first' qualifies it adverbially: 'born first'.

Analysis पूर्वम् जाता पूर्वजा
pūrvam jātā pūrvajā

Significance Before the gods and the worlds came to be, She was; She is the primordial power from which all else is born.

976 त्रिपुराम्बिका tripurāmbikā

She who is the Mother of the three cities (tripuras)

Sandhi त्रिपुराम्बिका = त्रिपुर + अम्बिका (tripura + ambikā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner dvigu); or karmadhāraya. (1) tri-pura 'the three cities' (dvigu). (2) ambikā 'mother' is the head and the cities stand to it in the genitive: 'the Mother of the three cities'. As a karmadhāraya, Tripurā (the Goddess) and Ambikā are one: 'Tripurā the Mother' (then tripurā + ambikā, ā + a → ā).

Analysis त्रयाणाम् पुराणाम् समाहारः त्रिपुरम्; त्रिपुराणाम् अम्बिका त्रिपुराम्बिका; अथवा त्रिपुरा च असौ अम्बिका च त्रिपुराम्बिका
trayāṇām purāṇām samāhāraḥ tripuram; tripurāṇām ambikā tripurāmbikā; athavā tripurā ca asau ambikā ca tripurāmbikā

Significance Tripurāmbā is the presiding deity (cakreśvarī) of the eighth enclosure of the Śrīcakra, the inner triangle; the three cities are read as every triad: the three worlds, bodies, states and powers.

Uncertain Genitive ('Mother of the three cities') and appositional ('Tripurā the Mother') analyses are both current.

Śloka 179names 977–981

ज्ञानमुद्रा ज्ञानगम्या ज्ञानज्ञेयस्वरूपिणी ॥ १७९ ॥

The names, separated

977दश-मुद्रा-समाराध्याdaśa-mudrā-samārādhyā978त्रिपुराश्री-वशङ्करीtripurāśrī-vaśaṅkarī

977She who is worshipped with the ten mudrās; 978She who holds Tripurāśrī under Her sway;

979She who is in the form of the jñāna mudrā; 980She who is to be reached through knowledge; 981She who is both knowledge and the known.

Where the names meet

Names 977–983 concern the ten mudrās of Śrīcakra worship and the deities of its enclosures: 978 Tripurāśrī presides over the fifth enclosure; 982 yonimudrā and 983 trikhaṇḍā (in the next śloka) are the ninth and tenth mudrās. Tripurāśrī is one deity's name: divide tripurāśrī-vaśaṅkarī.

The names

977 दशमुद्रासमाराध्या daśa-mudrā-samārādhyā

She who is worshipped with the ten mudrās

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner dvigu). (1) daśa-mudrā 'the ten mudrās' (dvigu). (2) samārādhyā 'to be worshipped fully' is the head and takes (1) in the instrumental: 'to be worshipped with the ten mudrās'.

Analysis दश मुद्राः दशमुद्राः; दशमुद्राभिः समाराध्या दशमुद्रासमाराध्या
daśa mudrāḥ daśamudrāḥ; daśamudrābhiḥ samārādhyā daśamudrāsamārādhyā

Significance The ten mudrās of Śrīcakra worship are Sarvasaṅkṣobhiṇī, Sarvavidrāviṇī, Sarvākarṣiṇī, Sarvavaśaṅkarī, Sarvonmādinī, Sarvamahāṅkuśā, Sarvakhecarī, Sarvabījā, Sarvayoni and Sarvatrikhaṇḍā; each is both a gesture and a goddess of an enclosure.

978 त्रिपुराश्रीवशङ्करी tripurāśrī-vaśaṅkarī

She who holds Tripurāśrī under Her sway

Sandhi वशङ्करी = वशम् + करी (vaśam + karī) — the m of vaśam becomes anusvāra and then the nasal of the following k-row, ṅ (Pāṇini 8.3.23, 8.4.59)

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa. vaśaṅkarī 'one who brings under control' (vaśa + √kṛ, with the augment m that keeps vaśam's form, Pāṇini 6.3.67) is the head, and Tripurāśrī is the one brought under Her sway.

Analysis त्रिपुराश्रियम् वशम् करोति इति त्रिपुराश्रीवशङ्करी
tripurāśriyam vaśam karoti iti tripurāśrīvaśaṅkarī

Significance Tripurāśrī is the cakreśvarī of the fifth enclosure (sarvārthasādhaka cakra); traditionally Tripurāśrī is also read as the fortune (śrī) of the three worlds, which She commands.

Uncertain Tripurāśrī as the fifth-enclosure deity and as 'the fortune of the three worlds' are both traditional readings.

979 ज्ञानमुद्रा jñāna-mudrā

She who is in the form of the jñāna mudrā

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. mudrā 'gesture' is the head; jñāna stands to it in the genitive: 'the gesture of knowledge'.

Analysis ज्ञानस्य मुद्रा ज्ञानमुद्रा
jñānasya mudrā jñānamudrā

Significance In the jñāna (cin) mudrā the index finger, the individual self, bows to join the thumb, the supreme: She is the knowledge that gesture teaches.

980 ज्ञानगम्या jñāna-gamyā

She who is to be reached through knowledge

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa. The gerundive gamyā 'to be reached' is the head and takes jñāna in the instrumental: 'to be reached through knowledge'.

Analysis ज्ञानेन गम्या ज्ञानगम्या
jñānena gamyā jñānagamyā

Significance Traditionally the knowledge is the realization of identity with Her, the path of jñāna.

981 ज्ञानज्ञेयस्वरूपिणी jñāna-jñeya-svarūpiṇī

She who is both knowledge and the known

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound dvandva and karmadhāraya, completed by the possessive suffix -in. (1) jñāna-jñeya 'knowledge and the knowable' (itaretara-dvandva). (2) That pair is identified with svarūpa 'own form, nature'. (3) The possessive -in (feminine -iṇī) makes the whole describe Her: 'She whose own nature is both knowledge and the known'.

Analysis ज्ञानम् च ज्ञेयम् च ज्ञानज्ञेये; ज्ञानज्ञेये एव स्वरूपम् ज्ञानज्ञेयस्वरूपम्; ज्ञानज्ञेयस्वरूपम् अस्याः अस्ति इति ज्ञानज्ञेयस्वरूपिणी
jñānam ca jñeyam ca jñānajñeye; jñānajñeye eva svarūpam jñānajñeyasvarūpam; jñānajñeyasvarūpam asyāḥ asti iti jñānajñeyasvarūpiṇī

Significance In the non-dual view the knower, knowing and known are one consciousness; She is both the knowing and its object.

Where the names meet

त्रिगुणाम्बा = त्रिगुणा + अम्बा (triguṇā + ambā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101); Bhāskararāya reads two names here, triguṇā (984) and ambā (985)

अनघाऽद्भुत = अनघा + अद्भुत… (anaghā + adbhuta…) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101); the avagraha marks the absorbed a of adbhuta

त्रिगुणाम्बा holds two names, triguṇā and ambā; and 988 begins with adbhuta, its initial a hidden after anaghā (avagraha).

The names

982 योनिमुद्रा yoni-mudrā

She who is in the form of the yoni mudrā

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa. mudrā 'gesture' is the head; yoni 'source, womb' stands to it in the genitive: 'the gesture of the yoni'.

Analysis योनेः मुद्रा योनिमुद्रा
yoneḥ mudrā yonimudrā

Significance The yoni mudrā is the ninth of the ten mudrās of Śrīcakra worship (Sarvayoni); it shows Her as the source of all.

983 त्रिखण्डेशी tri-khaṇḍeśī

She who is the sovereign of the Trikhaṇḍā, the tenth mudrā

Sandhi त्रिखण्डेशी = त्रिखण्डा + ईशी (trikhaṇḍā + īśī) — guṇa: ā + ī → e (Pāṇini 6.1.87 ād guṇaḥ)

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner bahuvrīhi). (1) tri-khaṇḍā 'that which has three parts', the name of the tenth mudrā (bahuvrīhi). (2) īśī 'sovereign lady' is the head and the mudrā stands to it in the genitive: 'the sovereign of the Trikhaṇḍā'.

Analysis त्रयः खण्डाः यस्याः सा त्रिखण्डा; त्रिखण्डायाः ईशी त्रिखण्डेशी
trayaḥ khaṇḍāḥ yasyāḥ sā trikhaṇḍā; trikhaṇḍāyāḥ īśī trikhaṇḍeśī

Significance Trikhaṇḍā (Sarvatrikhaṇḍā) is the tenth mudrā, used in invoking Her; traditionally the three parts are also the three kūṭas (sections) of the Pañcadaśī mantra, so She rules the mantra itself.

Uncertain Trikhaṇḍā as the tenth mudrā, or the three kūṭas of the Pañcadaśī mantra: both are traditional.

984 त्रिगुणा tri-guṇā

She who is endowed with the three guṇas of sattva, rajas and tamas

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. tri 'three' qualifies guṇa 'quality', and the whole describes Her: 'She who has the three guṇas'; guṇa takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis त्रयः गुणाः यस्याः सा त्रिगुणा
trayaḥ guṇāḥ yasyāḥ sā triguṇā

Significance As Prakṛti She wields the three qualities in creating, sustaining and dissolving, though Herself beyond them (name 961). Her final ā absorbs the a of the next name, ambā.

985 अम्बा ambā

She who is the Mother of all beings, the Mother of the universe

Sandhi त्रिगुणाम्बा = त्रिगुणा + अम्बा (triguṇā + ambā) — savarṇa-dīrgha across the name boundary: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101). Bhāskararāya reads the verse's त्रिगुणाम्बा as two names, triguṇā (984) and ambā (985); the initial a of ambā is absorbed into the long ā

Compound not a compound

Significance The simplest of Her names, the child's word for mother; traditionally the triad triguṇā-ambā is read as the Mother who works through the three guṇas.

Uncertain triguṇāmbā can also be read as one word, 'the Mother of the three guṇas'; the 1,000-name count follows Bhāskararāya's two names.

986 त्रिकोणगा tri-koṇa-gā

She who resides in the triangle

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner bahuvrīhi). (1) tri-koṇa 'that which has three angles', a triangle (bahuvrīhi). (2) -gā 'going, abiding' (√gam with the suffix -a) is the head and takes the triangle in the locative: 'She who abides in the triangle'.

Analysis त्रयः कोणाः यस्य तत् त्रिकोणम्; त्रिकोणे गच्छति इति त्रिकोणगा
trayaḥ koṇāḥ yasya tat trikoṇam; trikoṇe gacchati iti trikoṇagā

Significance The inner triangle of the Śrīcakra surrounds the bindu and is Her seat (the eighth enclosure); inwardly it is the triangle in the mūlādhāra and the kāmakalā.

987 अनघा anaghā

She who is sinless

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound nañ-bahuvrīhi. nañ 'not' with agha 'sin': 'She in whom there is no sin'. na becomes an- before a vowel; the members meet without further sound change.

Analysis न विद्यते अघम् यस्याः सा अनघा
na vidyate agham yasyāḥ sā anaghā

Significance No sin or impurity touches Her, and She removes the sins of those who remember Her.

988 अद्भुतचारित्रा adbhuta-cāritrā

She whose deeds are marvelous

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi. adbhuta 'wondrous' qualifies cāritra 'conduct, deeds', and the whole describes Her: 'She whose deeds are wondrous'; cāritra takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis अद्भुतम् चारित्रम् यस्याः सा अद्भुतचारित्रा
adbhutam cāritram yasyāḥ sā adbhutacāritrā

Significance Her deeds, from slaying Bhaṇḍa to granting liberation, surpass anything the mind can measure.

989 वाञ्छितार्थप्रदायिनी vāñchitārtha-pradāyinī

She who grants what is desired

Sandhi वाञ्छितार्थ = वाञ्छित + अर्थ (vāñchita + artha) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound upapada-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya). (1) vāñchita-artha 'desired objects' (karmadhāraya). (2) pradāyinī 'giver' is the head and takes (1) as its object: 'She who gives the desired objects'.

Analysis वाञ्छिताः अर्थाः वाञ्छितार्थाः; वाञ्छितार्थान् प्रददाति इति वाञ्छितार्थप्रदायिनी
vāñchitāḥ arthāḥ vāñchitārthāḥ; vāñchitārthān pradadāti iti vāñchitārthapradāyinī

Significance Traditionally She grants each worshiper what they seek, and in the end leads them to desire only Her.

Śloka 181names 990–993

अभ्यासातिशयज्ञाता षडध्वातीतरूपिणी ।
अव्याजकरुणामूर्तिर् अज्ञानध्वान्तदीपिका ॥ १८१ ॥

abhyāsātiśayajñātā ṣaḍadhvātītarūpiṇī |
avyājakaruṇāmūrtir ajñānadhvāntadīpikā || 181 ||

The names, separated ° form as a name on its own; in the recitation above it joins its neighbour

990अभ्यासातिशय-ज्ञाताabhyāsātiśaya-jñātā991षडध्वातीत-रूपिणीṣaḍadhvātīta-rūpiṇī

992अव्याज-करुणा-मूर्तिः°avyāja-karuṇā-mūrtiḥ993अज्ञान-ध्वान्त-दीपिकाajñāna-dhvānta-dīpikā

Translation

990She who is known through intense and sustained spiritual practice; 991She whose form transcends the six paths;

992She who is the embodiment of compassion that asks for no reason; 993She who is the bright lamp that dispels the darkness of ignorance.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish

अभ्यासabhyāsarepeated practice, spiritual disciplineabhi + √as 'to throw, apply'
अतिशयatiśayaexcess, intensity, pre-eminenceati + √śī
ज्ञाताjñātāknown√jñā 'to know', past participle, feminine
991 षडध्वातीतरूपिणी ṣaḍadhvātīta-rūpiṇī
षष्ṣaṣsixṣaṭ as a word; ḍ before the vowel by jaśtva
अध्वन्adhvanpath, way; in Tantra one of the six adhvansappears as adhva- (final n dropped)
अतीतatītagone beyondati + √i 'to go', past participle

अanot, withoutnañ

ध्वान्तdhvāntadarkness√dhvan, past participle used as a noun

Where the names meet

मूर्तिरज्ञान = मूर्तिः + अज्ञान… (mūrtiḥ + ajñāna…) — visarga after a vowel other than a/ā becomes r before a voiced sound (here the vowel a)

The r before ajñāna belongs to name 992 (mūrtiḥ); name 993 begins ajñāna. Name 991's 'six paths' are the six adhvans of the Āgamas.

The names

990 अभ्यासातिशयज्ञाता abhyāsātiśaya-jñātā

She who is known through intense and sustained spiritual practice

Sandhi अभ्यास = अभि + आस (abhi + āsa) — yaṇ: i → y before an unlike vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci), at the prefix junction of abhi + āsa; अभ्यासातिशय = अभ्यास + अतिशय (abhyāsa + atiśaya) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa (over an inner ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) abhyāsa-atiśaya 'the intensity (excess) of practice' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; atiśaya is the head). (2) The participle jñātā 'known' is the head of the whole and takes (1) in the instrumental of means: 'known through intense practice'.

Analysis अभ्यासस्य अतिशयः अभ्यासातिशयः; अभ्यासातिशयेन ज्ञाता अभ्यासातिशयज्ञाता
abhyāsasya atiśayaḥ abhyāsātiśayaḥ; abhyāsātiśayena jñātā abhyāsātiśayajñātā

Significance The Bhagavad Gītā (6.35) teaches that the restless mind is held by practice (abhyāsa) and dispassion; She is realized when that practice becomes wholehearted and continuous.

991 षडध्वातीतरूपिणी ṣaḍadhvātīta-rūpiṇī

She whose form transcends the six paths

Sandhi षडध्व = षष् + अध्व (ṣaṣ + adhva) — jaśtva: the final ṣ of ṣaṣ 'six' becomes the voiced stop ḍ at the word boundary before a vowel (Pāṇini 8.2.39 jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte); षडध्वातीत = षडध्व + अतीत (ṣaḍadhva + atīta) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound possessive in -in over a karmadhāraya, with an inner dvitīyā-tatpuruṣa and dvigu. (1) ṣaḍ-adhvan 'the six paths' (dvigu; adhvan drops its n). (2) ṣaḍadhva-atīta 'gone beyond the six paths' (dvitīyā-tatpuruṣa with atīta, Pāṇini 2.1.24). (3) This qualifies rūpa 'form' (karmadhāraya), and the possessive -in (feminine -iṇī) makes the whole describe Her: 'She whose form transcends the six paths'.

Analysis षट् अध्वानः षडध्वानः; षडध्वनः अतीतम् षडध्वातीतम्; षडध्वातीतम् रूपम् षडध्वातीतरूपम्; तत् अस्याः अस्ति इति षडध्वातीतरूपिणी
ṣaṭ adhvānaḥ ṣaḍadhvānaḥ; ṣaḍadhvanaḥ atītam ṣaḍadhvātītam; ṣaḍadhvātītam rūpam ṣaḍadhvātītarūpam; tat asyāḥ asti iti ṣaḍadhvātītarūpiṇī

Significance In the Āgamas the six adhvans are the six 'paths' by which the cosmos unfolds: varṇa, pada and mantra on the side of sound, and kalā, tattva and bhuvana on the side of objects. Her true form lies beyond all six.

992 अव्याजकरुणामूर्तिः avyāja-karuṇā-mūrtiḥ

She who is the embodiment of compassion that asks for no reason

Sandhi व्याज = वि + आज (vi + āja) — yaṇ: i → y before an unlike vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci), at the prefix junction of vi + āja

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner karmadhāraya and a nañ-bahuvrīhi). (1) a-vyāja 'without pretext or motive' (nañ-bahuvrīhi). (2) It qualifies karuṇā 'compassion' (karmadhāraya; puṃvadbhāva gives avyāja-): 'compassion that needs no reason'. (3) mūrti 'embodiment' is the head and the compassion stands to it in the genitive: 'the embodiment of unconditional compassion'. A karmadhāraya reading ('the form that is itself such compassion') gives the same sense.

Analysis न विद्यते व्याजः यस्याः सा अव्याजा; अव्याजा करुणा अव्याजकरुणा; अव्याजकरुणायाः मूर्तिः अव्याजकरुणामूर्तिः
na vidyate vyājaḥ yasyāḥ sā avyājā; avyājā karuṇā avyājakaruṇā; avyājakaruṇāyāḥ mūrtiḥ avyājakaruṇāmūrtiḥ

Significance Her compassion does not wait for merit or devotion; it is Her nature, as a mother's love precedes the child's deserving.

993 अज्ञानध्वान्तदीपिका ajñāna-dhvānta-dīpikā

She who is the bright lamp that dispels the darkness of ignorance

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa (over an inner rūpaka-karmadhāraya and a nañ-tatpuruṣa). (1) a-jñāna 'ignorance' (nañ-tatpuruṣa). (2) ajñāna-dhvānta 'the darkness that is ignorance' (karmadhāraya of identification, rūpaka). (3) dīpikā 'lamp' is the head and the darkness stands to it in the genitive: 'the lamp for the darkness of ignorance', i.e. the lamp that dispels it.

Analysis न ज्ञानम् अज्ञानम्; अज्ञानम् एव ध्वान्तम् अज्ञानध्वान्तम्; अज्ञानध्वान्तस्य दीपिका अज्ञानध्वान्तदीपिका
na jñānam ajñānam; ajñānam eva dhvāntam ajñānadhvāntam; ajñānadhvāntasya dīpikā ajñānadhvāntadīpikā

Significance As one lamp ends the darkness of a room at once, knowledge of Her ends ignorance, however long it has lasted.

Śloka 182names 994–997

आबालगोपविदिता सर्वानुल्लङ्घ्यशासना ।
श्रीचक्रराजनिलया श्रीमत्त्रिपुरसुन्दरी ॥ १८२ ॥

ābālagopaviditā sarvānullaṅghyaśāsanā |
śrīcakrarājanilayā śrīmattripurasundarī || 182 ||

The names, separated

994आबाल-गोप-विदिताābāla-gopa-viditā995सर्वानुल्लङ्घ्य-शासनाsarvānullaṅghya-śāsanā

996श्री-चक्र-राज-निलयाśrī-cakra-rāja-nilayā997श्रीमत्-त्रिपुर-सुन्दरीśrīmat-tripura-sundarī

Translation

994She who is known by all, even by children and cowherds; 995She whose command no one can transgress;

996She who abides in the Śrīcakra, the king of cakras; 997She who is the glorious Tripurasundarī.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish
994 आबालगोपविदिता ābāla-gopa-viditā
आāup to, includingpreposition (āṅ) in the inclusive sense
बालbālachild
गोपgopacowherd
विदिताviditāknown√vid 'to know', past participle, feminine
995 सर्वानुल्लङ्घ्यशासना sarvānullaṅghya-śāsanā
सर्वsarvaall, everyone
अनुल्लङ्घ्यanullaṅghyanot to be transgressednañ (an-) + ud + √laṅgh 'to leap over', gerundive
शासनाśāsanācommand, ruleśāsana (from √śās 'to command'), with the feminine -ā of the bahuvrīhi
996 श्रीचक्रराजनिलया śrī-cakra-rāja-nilayā
श्रीśrīauspicious, glorious; Śrī
चक्रcakracakra: wheel, diagram (yantra)
राजन्rājankingappears as rāja at the end of a tatpuruṣa

श्रीमत्śrīmatglorious, auspiciousśrī + the possessive suffix -mat
त्रिtrithree
पुरpuracity, world
सुन्दरीsundarībeautiful woman, the beautiful one

Where the names meet

Name 994: gopa is 'cowherd' (not 'beetle'), and ā- is inclusive, 'down to'. Names 996–997 name the Śrīcakra and Tripurasundarī, the yantra and the presiding deity of Śrīvidyā, as the hymn closes; 997 is spelled with tt (śrīmat + tripura).

The names

994 आबालगोपविदिता ābāla-gopa-viditā

She who is known by all, even by children and cowherds

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound avyayībhāva over an itaretara-dvandva, joined to the participle. (1) bāla-gopa 'children and cowherds' (dvandva). (2) ā 'up to, including' with it forms an avyayībhāva, ābālagopam 'down to children and cowherds' (Pāṇini 2.1.13 āṅ maryādābhividhyoḥ; here inclusive). (3) This qualifies the participle viditā 'known': 'known to all, down to children and cowherds'.

Analysis बालाः च गोपाः च बालगोपाः; आ बालगोपेभ्यः आबालगोपम्; आबालगोपम् विदिता आबालगोपविदिता
bālāḥ ca gopāḥ ca bālagopāḥ; ā bālagopebhyaḥ ābālagopam; ābālagopam viditā ābālagopaviditā

Significance No learning is needed to know Her: even children and cowherds know Her as the Mother, present in every heart.

Uncertain The outer link of the avyayībhāva to the participle viditā is loose; it may also be read as an instrumental, 'known by (all) down to children and cowherds'.

995 सर्वानुल्लङ्घ्यशासना sarvānullaṅghya-śāsanā

She whose command no one can transgress

Sandhi सर्वानुल्लङ्घ्य = सर्व + अनुल्लङ्घ्य (sarva + anullaṅghya) — savarṇa-dīrgha: a + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ); उल्लङ्घ्य = उद् + लङ्घ्य (ud + laṅghya) — the prefix ud assimilates to the following l: d becomes l (Pāṇini 8.4.60 tor li)

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa and a nañ-tatpuruṣa). (1) an-ullaṅghya 'not to be transgressed' (nañ-tatpuruṣa; na becomes an- before a vowel). (2) sarva-anullaṅghya 'not to be transgressed by anyone' (tṛtīyā-tatpuruṣa, the instrumental of the agent with the gerundive). (3) This qualifies śāsana 'command', and the whole is a bahuvrīhi: 'She whose command no one can transgress'.

Analysis न उल्लङ्घ्यम् अनुल्लङ्घ्यम्; सर्वैः अनुल्लङ्घ्यम् सर्वानुल्लङ्घ्यम्; सर्वानुल्लङ्घ्यम् शासनम् यस्याः सा सर्वानुल्लङ्घ्यशासना
na ullaṅghyam anullaṅghyam; sarvaiḥ anullaṅghyam sarvānullaṅghyam; sarvānullaṅghyam śāsanam yasyāḥ sā sarvānullaṅghyaśāsanā

Significance Even the gods, the sun, fire and wind act under Her command; the order of the cosmos is Her unbroken law.

996 श्रीचक्रराजनिलया śrī-cakra-rāja-nilayā

She who abides in the Śrīcakra, the king of cakras

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound bahuvrīhi (over an inner karmadhāraya and ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (1) cakra-rāja 'the king of cakras' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa; rājan becomes rāja at the end of a tatpuruṣa, Pāṇini 5.4.91 rājāhaḥsakhibhyaṣ ṭac). (2) śrī qualifies it: 'the glorious king of cakras', the Śrīcakra. (3) nilaya 'abode' is identified with it, and the whole describes Her: 'She whose abode is the Śrīcakra, king of cakras'; nilaya takes the feminine -ā.

Analysis चक्राणाम् राजा चक्रराजः; श्रीयुक्तः चक्रराजः श्रीचक्रराजः; श्रीचक्रराजः निलयः यस्याः सा श्रीचक्रराजनिलया
cakrāṇām rājā cakrarājaḥ; śrīyuktaḥ cakrarājaḥ śrīcakrarājaḥ; śrīcakrarājaḥ nilayaḥ yasyāḥ sā śrīcakrarājanilayā

Significance The Śrīcakra is Her own form as yantra and the supreme diagram of Śrīvidyā worship; the hymn now names it as Her dwelling as it draws to a close.

Uncertain The compound can also be read śrī + cakrarāja, 'the glorious king of cakras'; both name the Śrīcakra.

997 श्रीमत्त्रिपुरसुन्दरी śrīmat-tripura-sundarī

She who is the glorious Tripurasundarī

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya (over an inner saptamī- or ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and a dvigu). (1) tri-pura 'the three cities, the three worlds' (dvigu). (2) tripura-sundarī 'the beauty of the three worlds', i.e. the most beautiful in them (saptamī-tatpuruṣa; a genitive reading gives the same sense). (3) śrīmatī 'glorious' qualifies her, reduced to śrīmat by puṃvadbhāva in the karmadhāraya: 'the glorious Tripurasundarī'.

Analysis त्रयाणाम् पुराणाम् समाहारः त्रिपुरम्; त्रिपुरे सुन्दरी त्रिपुरसुन्दरी; श्रीमती त्रिपुरसुन्दरी श्रीमत्त्रिपुरसुन्दरी
trayāṇām purāṇām samāhāraḥ tripuram; tripure sundarī tripurasundarī; śrīmatī tripurasundarī śrīmattripurasundarī

Significance Tripurasundarī is the presiding name of the Goddess in Śrīvidyā, the most beautiful in the three worlds and beyond the three states of waking, dream and sleep.

Śloka 183names 998–1000

श्रीशिवा शिवशक्त्यैक्यरूपिणी ललिताम्बिका ।
एवं श्रीललितादेव्या नाम्नां साहस्रकं जगुः ॥ १८३ ॥

śrīśivā śivaśaktyaikyarūpiṇī lalitāmbikā |
evaṃ śrīlalitādevyā nāmnāṃ sāhasrakaṃ jaguḥ || 183 ||

The names, separated

998श्री-शिवाśrī-śivā999शिव-शक्त्य्-ऐक्य-रूपिणीśiva-śakty-aikya-rūpiṇī1000ललिताम्बिकाlalitāmbikā

The closing line — no name; its words, separated:

·एवम्°evam·श्री-ललिता-देव्याः°śrī-lalitā-devyāḥ·नाम्नाम्°nāmnām·साहस्रकम्°sāhasrakam·जगुःjaguḥ

Translation

998She who is the auspicious and divine Śivā; 999She who is the union of Śiva and Śakti in one form; 1000She who is the divine Mother Lalitā;

Thus the goddesses of speech sang the thousand names of Śrī Lalitā Devī.

Word by word

SanskritEnglish
998 श्रीशिवा śrī-śivā
श्रीśrīauspicious, glorious; Śrī
शिवाśivāŚivā: the auspicious one, the consort of Śivafeminine of śiva 'auspicious'
999 शिवशक्त्यैक्यरूपिणी śiva-śakty-aikya-rūpiṇī
शिवśivaŚiva
शक्तिśaktiŚakti, power
ऐक्यaikyaoneness, unionabstract noun from eka 'one'
रूपिणीrūpiṇīhaving the formrūpa 'form' + -in, feminine
1000 ललिताम्बिका lalitāmbikā
ललिताlalitāLalitā: 'She who plays', the lovely one√lal 'to play, sport', past participle, feminine
अम्बिकाambikāmotherambā + -ka, feminine
Closing line · एवं evaṃ — thus, in this way
एवम्evamthus, in this wayan indeclinable
· श्रीललितादेव्या śrīlalitādevyā — of the Goddess Śrī Lalitā (karmadhāraya: śrī-lalitā-devī, "the Goddess Śrī Lalitā", in the genitive singular)
श्रीśrīauspicious (honorific)
ललिताlalitāLalitā, "She who plays"
देव्याःdevyāḥof the Goddessdevī "goddess", genitive singular
· नाम्नां nāmnāṃ — of the names
नाम्नाम्nāmnāmof the namesnāman "name", genitive plural
· साहस्रकं sāhasrakaṃ — the thousand, the set of a thousand
साहस्रकम्sāhasrakama set of a thousandfrom sahasra "thousand"; neuter, accusative singular — the object of jaguḥ
· जगुः jaguḥ — they sang
जगुःjaguḥthey sang√gai "to sing", perfect, third person plural

Where the words meet

एवं = एवम् (evaṃ = evam) — m becomes anusvāra (ṃ) before the consonant ś (Pāṇini 8.3.23 mo 'nusvāraḥ)

श्रीललितादेव्या = श्रीललितादेव्याः (śrīlalitādevyā = śrīlalitādevyāḥ) — devyāḥ loses its visarga before the n of nāmnām: after ā, visarga before a voiced sound drops (Pāṇini 8.3.17, 8.3.22)

नाम्नां = नाम्नाम् (nāmnāṃ = nāmnām) — m becomes anusvāra before s

साहस्रकं = साहस्रकम् (sāhasrakaṃ = sāhasrakam) — m becomes anusvāra before j

The first half holds the last three names, 998–1000, ending on Her own name, Lalitāmbikā. The second half is not a name but the closing line (its words are analysed below). Traditionally the singers are the Vāgdevīs (Vaśinī and the others), who composed the hymn at Her command.

The names

998 श्रीशिवा śrī-śivā

She who is the auspicious and divine Śivā

Sandhi none inside the name; the parts stand as written

Compound karmadhāraya. śrī 'auspicious, glorious' stands in apposition to śivā 'the auspicious one, Śiva's consort': 'the auspicious Śivā'. The members meet without sound change.

Analysis श्रीः शिवा श्रीशिवा
śrīḥ śivā śrīśivā

Significance She is Śivā, the power of Śiva and auspiciousness itself; the next name declares Śiva and Śakti to be one.

999 शिवशक्त्यैक्यरूपिणी śiva-śakty-aikya-rūpiṇī

She who is the union of Śiva and Śakti in one form

Sandhi शक्त्यैक्य = शक्ति + ऐक्य (śakti + aikya) — yaṇ: i → y before an unlike vowel (Pāṇini 6.1.77 iko yaṇ aci)

Compound possessive in -in over a karmadhāraya, a ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa and an itaretara-dvandva. (1) śiva-śakti 'Śiva and Śakti' (itaretara-dvandva). (2) śivaśakti-aikya 'the oneness of Śiva and Śakti' (ṣaṣṭhī-tatpuruṣa). (3) That oneness is identified with rūpa 'form', and the possessive -in (feminine -iṇī) makes the whole describe Her: 'She whose form is the union of Śiva and Śakti'.

Analysis शिवः च शक्तिः च शिवशक्ती; शिवशक्त्योः ऐक्यम् शिवशक्त्यैक्यम्; शिवशक्त्यैक्यम् एव रूपम् शिवशक्त्यैक्यरूपम्; तत् अस्याः अस्ति इति शिवशक्त्यैक्यरूपिणी
śivaḥ ca śaktiḥ ca śivaśaktī; śivaśaktyoḥ aikyam śivaśaktyaikyam; śivaśaktyaikyam eva rūpam śivaśaktyaikyarūpam; tat asyāḥ asti iti śivaśaktyaikyarūpiṇī

Significance The whole of Śrīvidyā rests on this non-duality: Śiva without Śakti cannot act, Śakti without Śiva has no ground; Kāmeśvara and Kāmeśvarī are one.

Corrected शिवशक्तैक्यरूपिणी → शिवशक्त्यैक्यरूपिणी. शिवशक्तैक्य → शिवशक्त्यैक्य: śakti + aikya gives śakty-aikya (yaṇ sandhi); the y was missing.

1000 ललिताम्बिका lalitāmbikā

She who is the divine Mother Lalitā

Sandhi ललिताम्बिका = ललिता + अम्बिका (lalitā + ambikā) — savarṇa-dīrgha: ā + a → ā (Pāṇini 6.1.101 akaḥ savarṇe dīrghaḥ)

Compound karmadhāraya. Lalitā and ambikā 'Mother' are co-referential: 'Lalitā, the Mother'. ambikā is the head; the two simply meet in savarṇa-dīrgha.

Analysis ललिता च असौ अम्बिका च ललिताम्बिका
lalitā ca asau ambikā ca lalitāmbikā

Significance The thousand names end with Her own name: Lalitā, whose play is the universe, and Ambikā, the Mother to whom every name has been addressed.

Colophon

इति श्रीब्रह्माण्डपुराणे उत्तरखण्डे श्रीहयग्रीवागस्त्यसंवादे श्रीललितासहस्रनामस्तोत्रकथनं सम्पूर्णम् ॥

iti śrībrahmāṇḍapurāṇe uttarakhaṇḍe śrīhayagrīvāgastyasaṃvāde śrīlalitāsahasranāmastotrakathanaṃ sampūrṇam ||

Thus ends the narration of the Śrī Lalitā Sahasranāma Stotra, in the dialogue of Śrī Hayagrīva and Agastya, in the Uttara-khaṇḍa of the Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa.

Found by aligning every name against the śloka text; the śloka-to-name table is now generated from the text instead of typed.
